questions.explain: The card splits the title into अष्ट, अङ्ग and संग्रहे.

questions.q: Which statements about this unit are right?
options: It is a heading and not a full sentence with a verb
The ending -ए is locative singular: in
It names the work as a compendium of eight limbs
It is a command to the reader
optionExplain: No verb occurs.
The data labels it m. loc. sg.
That is the meaning of the compound.
No limb is named in this unit.
There is no imperative verb.
questions.explain: The unit is a title in the locative; it names the work but does not list the limbs.
questions.rule: A title fragment: in the Compendium of the Eight Limbs; no list.

questions.q: An invented title is षडङ्गसंग्रहे (षट् means six), built like अष्टांगसंग्रहे. What does it say?
options: In the Compendium of the Eight Limbs
To the Compendium of the Six Limbs
In the Compendium of the Six Limbs
The Compendium is of six sages
optionExplain: Eight is अष्ट, not षट्.
A dative would end in -आय.
Right: षट् is six, and -ए locative gives in.
अङ्ग is limb, and no sages are named.
questions.explain: Number + अङ्ग + संग्रहे reads: in the compendium of that many limbs.
questions.rule: Number + अङ्ग + संग्रहे (loc.) = in the compendium of n limbs.
questions.teaches: A number before अङ्ग counts the limbs, and the locative -ए on संग्रहे gives in the compendium.

questions.q: What does the heading सूत्रस्थानम् १ name?
options: The Section on Treatment of the sick, number 1
The Section on Diseases and causes, number 1
The Section of Remedies and drugs, number 8
optionExplain: Treatment is चिकित्सा, which is not in the heading.
Disease is रोग, which is not in the heading.
The numeral is १, one, and the first word is not about remedies.
Right: सूत्रस्थानम् is the Section of Aphorisms, and १ is one.
questions.explain: The heading gives the section and the number one.

questions.q: Match each part of the heading to its meaning.
pairs: one, read as the chapter number
questions.explain: The heading has an aphorism-part, a section-part and a number.
questions.rule: सूत्र = aphorism; स्थानम् = section, place; १ = one.

questions.q: The first part of the heading, meaning aphorism, is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: सूत्र means aphorism and opens the compound सूत्रस्थानम्.
questions.teaches: In a compound the first member qualifies the second: सूत्र + स्थान = the section of aphorisms.

questions.q: Which is the right split of सूत्रस्थानम्?
options: सूत्र + स्थानम्, with no change at the join
सूत्रः + स्थानम्, with a visarga after सूत्र
सूत्र + अस्थानम्, with a negative prefix on the second word
सूत् + रस्थानम्, cutting the word inside सूत्र
optionExplain: Right: The two words stand side by side unchanged.
A visarga would show in the written word.
अस्थानम् would mean no place, which the card does not give.
Neither part is a word on the card.
questions.explain: The card gives सूत्र and स्थानम् as the two members.

questions.q: Which statements about this unit are right?
options: The numeral १ is read as the chapter number
The word सूत्रस्थानम् is neuter, nominative singular
It names the section of the work
The numeral १ means the first verse
optionExplain: The card's note says so.
The data labels it n. nom. sg.
It is the section heading.
The card reads it as the chapter number.
No verb occurs here.
questions.explain: The heading names the section and gives the chapter number; it has no verb.
questions.rule: A section name plus the chapter number; no verb.

questions.q: An invented heading is चिकित्सास्थानम् ३ (चिकित्सा means treatment), built like सूत्रस्थानम् १. What does it say?
optionExplain: Aphorism is सूत्र, which is not in this word.
Right: Number three, and चिकित्सा treatment plus स्थान section.
The numeral is ३, three, and the compound reads treatment first.
The word is चिकित्सा, treatment, and the number is three.
questions.explain: X-स्थानम् names the section about X, and the numeral follows.
questions.rule: X + स्थानम् + number = the section on X, number n.
questions.teaches: A compound X + स्थानम् names the section on X, and a numeral after it is the chapter number.

questions.q: Unit 4 is a line of homage. To whom is it addressed?
optionExplain: He is honoured in the next unit, not here.
The teachers are honoured in unit 8.
Right: The word गणेशाय names him in the dative.
The Buddha is honoured in unit 10.
questions.explain: The line pays homage to Śrī Gaṇeśa.
questions.rule: श्रीगणेशाय नमः = homage to Śrī Gaṇeśa.

questions.q: Match each word of the line to its meaning.
questions.explain: The three words are honorific, the one honoured and homage.
questions.rule: श्री = revered; गणेशाय = to Gaṇeśa; नमः = homage.

questions.q: The word for homage is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: नमः means homage; it stands at the end of the line.
questions.teaches: नमः is a noun meaning homage; the one honoured stands in the dative before it.

questions.q: What does the ending of गणेशाय show?
optionExplain: A locative would end in -ए.
A genitive would end in -स्य.
A plural would not end in -आय.
Right: -आय is the dative singular of a name in -अ.
questions.explain: The one honoured stands in the dative: to Gaṇeśa.

questions.q: Put the words of the line in the order of the text.
questions.explain: The honorific comes first, then the one honoured, then homage.

questions.q: An invented line is श्रीगुरवे नमः, built like श्रीगणेशाय नमः. What does it say?
options: Homage to the revered teacher, one person
Homage to the revered teachers, several
The revered teacher bows in homage
Homage comes from the revered teacher
optionExplain: Right: -ave is the dative singular of गुरु, so the line says to the teacher.
A plural would be गुरुभ्यः, as in unit 8.
गुरवे is dative, so he is the one honoured.
From would be an ablative, which this ending is not.
questions.explain: Dative + नमः means homage to the one named; गुरु takes -अवे in the dative singular.
questions.teaches: Whoever is honoured stands in the dative before नमः; a name in -उ takes -अवे, as in गुरवे.

questions.q: Unit 5 pays homage to a second figure. Who is named?
optionExplain: He is honoured in unit 4.
Right: धन्वन्तरये is his name in the dative.
He appears in unit 11, in a different sentence.
He appears in unit 13, among the sages who spoke.
questions.explain: The line is homage to Śrī Dhanvantari.
questions.rule: श्रीधन्वन्तरये नमः = homage to Śrī Dhanvantari.

questions.q: Match each word of the line to its meaning.
questions.explain: The three words are honorific, the one honoured and homage.
questions.rule: श्री = revered; धन्वन्तरये = to Dhanvantari; नमः = homage.

questions.q: The word meaning to Dhanvantari is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: धन्वन्तरये is the dative singular of धन्वन्तरि.
questions.teaches: A name in -इ ends in -अये in the dative singular: धन्वन्तरि gives धन्वन्तरये.

questions.q: Which is the stem (base form) of धन्वन्तरये?
optionExplain: A stem in -अ would give -आय, as with गणेशाय.
A stem in long -ई would give a different dative.
Right: The name ends in -इ, and -ये is its dative singular.
-अय is part of the ending and not of the stem.
questions.explain: The dative -ये (with -अ- before it) belongs to a stem in -इ.

questions.q: Which statements about this unit are right?
options: It names Dhanvantari in the dative
It gives no description of Dhanvantari
It contains the verb I bow
optionExplain: The data labels धन्वन्तरये m. dat. sg.
नमः closes the line.
Only his name appears.
No such statement is in the line.
नमः is a noun; there is no verb.
questions.explain: The unit is a name in the dative plus नमः, with no description and no verb.
questions.rule: Dhanvantari is only named; no description, no verb.

questions.q: An invented line is श्रीमुनये नमः, built like श्रीधन्वन्तरये नमः. What does it say?
options: Homage to the revered sages, several
The revered sage bows in homage
Homage comes from the revered sage
Homage to the revered sage, one person
optionExplain: A plural would be मुनिभ्यः.
मुनये is dative, so he is the one honoured.
From would be an ablative, which this ending is not.
Right: मुनये is the dative singular of मुनि, a stem in -इ.
questions.explain: A stem in -इ gives -अये in the dative singular, so मुनये means to the sage.
questions.teaches: A name or noun in -इ takes -अये in the dative singular (धन्वन्तरये, मुनये), and नमः then means homage to him.

questions.q: Unit 6 is another line of homage. Whom does the card say it names?
optionExplain: Right: The long word contains Sītā and Rāmacandra.
He is honoured in unit 4.
He is honoured in unit 5.
They are honoured in unit 8.
questions.explain: The line pays homage to Śrī Sītā-Rāmacandra.
questions.rule: श्रीसीतारामचंद्राय नमः = homage to Śrī Sītā-Rāmacandra.

questions.q: Match each element of the line to its meaning.
questions.explain: The ending -आय shows the dative, श्री is the honorific and नमः is homage.

questions.q: The word for homage is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: नमः closes the line, as in units 4 to 8.
questions.teaches: Each homage line ends with नमः after the dative of the one honoured.

questions.q: Which part of श्रीसीतारामचंद्राय carries the dative ending?
options: The part सीता, in the middle
optionExplain: श्री is the honorific and has no ending.
Right: -आय stands on the final member of the compound.
A non-final member stays bare.
A compound takes one ending.
questions.explain: The dative -आय is on the last member.
questions.rule: One ending, on the last member.

questions.q: Put the parts of the line in the order of the text.
questions.explain: The honorific, then the names, then homage.

questions.q: In an invented line श्रीज्ञानदेवाय नमः, which member carries the dative ending?
optionExplain: श्री here is the honorific and has no ending.
A middle member stays in its bare form.
Right: In a compound the case ending stands on the last member.
A compound takes one ending, on its last member.
questions.explain: As in चंद्राय above, only the last member of a compound shows the ending, and it is the dative here: homage to Jñānadeva.
questions.rule: One ending, on the last member.
questions.teaches: A long compound of names takes one case ending, on its last member, so श्रीज्ञानदेवाय नमः is homage to the revered Jñānadeva.

questions.q: What does the line श्रीशं वंदे say?
options: They bowed to the Lord of Śrī (Lakṣmī)
The Lord of Śrī (Lakṣmī) bows to me
I bow to the revered teachers of old
I bow to the Lord of Śrī (Lakṣmī)
optionExplain: वंदे is first person singular, I, and not they.
He is the object (accusative), not the one who bows.
Teachers are honoured in unit 8, with नमः.
Right: वंदे is I bow, and श्रीशम् is its object.
questions.explain: The speaker says I bow, and the object is the Lord of Śrī.
questions.rule: श्रीशं वंदे = I bow to the Lord of Śrī.

questions.q: Match each word of the line to its meaning.
questions.explain: The object, the verb and the first member of the compound.
questions.rule: श्रीशम् = Lord of Śrī; वंदे = I bow; श्री = Śrī (Lakṣmī).

questions.q: The word, printed वंदे, meaning I bow is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: वन्दे (printed वंदे) is the first person singular present of √वन्द्.
questions.teaches: Unlike the noun नमः, वन्दे is a verb: it says I bow and takes its object in the accusative.

questions.q: Which is the right split of श्रीशम्?
options: श्री + ईशम्, where ई + ई gives ई
श्र + ईशम्, dropping the vowel of श्री
श्री + शम्, with a second word शम्
श्रीश + अम्, with a bare accusative ending
optionExplain: Right: The two long vowels merge into one.
श्र would drop the vowel of श्री, which the card keeps.
The card gives the second member as ईशम्, lord, with its ई.
-अम् is the accusative ending, and the word for lord is ईश.
questions.explain: श्री and ईशम् meet with ई + ई, so one long ई is written.

questions.q: Which statements about this unit are right?
options: वंदे is first person singular present
श्रीशम् is accusative: it is the one bowed to
The Sanskrit does not name the deity
The Sanskrit says the name Viṣṇu
optionExplain: The data labels it 1 sg. pres.
The data labels it m. acc. sg.
Only the title Lord of Śrī is given.
Only the book's Hindi says so, not the Sanskrit.
The card gives it as singular.
questions.explain: The unit has a verb I bow and an accusative object, with the god unnamed in the Sanskrit.
questions.rule: I bow + Lord of Śrī (accusative); the deity is not named.

questions.q: An invented line is गुरुं वन्दे, built like श्रीशं वंदे. What does it say?
optionExplain: The teacher is the object, so he is the one bowed to.
Right: गुरुम् is the accusative object, and वन्दे is I bow.
वन्दे is I, and गुरुम् is singular.
From would be an ablative, which -म् is not.
questions.explain: A noun in the accusative before वन्दे is the one bowed to.
questions.teaches: The one bowed to stands in the accusative before the verb वन्दे, I bow, as in श्रीशं वंदे.

questions.q: Unit 8 pays homage to a group. Who are they?
options: The knowers of the medical tradition
optionExplain: They are the speakers in unit 13.
They appear in unit 11, in a verse of bowing.
Right: गुरुभ्यः is the dative plural of गुरु.
He is honoured in unit 10.
questions.explain: The line pays homage to the revered teachers.
questions.rule: श्रीगुरुभ्यो नमः = homage to the revered teachers.

questions.q: Match each word of the line to its meaning.
questions.explain: Teacher, to the teachers, homage and the honorific.
questions.rule: गुरु = teacher; गुरुभ्यः = to the teachers; नमः = homage; श्री = revered.

questions.q: The word for teacher is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: गुरु is the stem; गुरुभ्यः is its dative plural.
questions.teaches: The stem गुरु becomes गुरुभ्यः in the dative plural.

questions.q: Which explains गुरुभ्यो नमः?
options: गुरुभ्यर् + नमः: the visarga becomes र् before न
गुरुभ्य + ओनमः: an ओ is added before नमः
गुरुभ्यस् + नमः: the visarga stays as स्
गुरुभ्यः + नमः: the visarga after अ becomes ओ before the voiced न
optionExplain: र् appears after vowels other than अ or आ, not after the अ of भ्यः.
Nothing is added; the visarga itself changes.
The visarga changes before a voiced sound.
Right: A visarga after अ turns into ओ before a voiced sound.
questions.explain: The visarga of गुरुभ्यः follows the अ of भ्य and meets the voiced न, so it becomes ओ.

questions.q: Which statements about this unit are right?
options: गुरुभ्यः is dative: the teachers are the ones honoured
The final ओ of गुरुभ्यो comes from a visarga
The line names the teachers one by one
optionExplain: -भ्यः is the dative plural ending.
Dative plus नमः means homage to them.
Before the voiced न the visarga became ओ.
No teacher is named.
The ending -भ्यः is plural.
questions.explain: The line honours teachers as a plural group, and its ओ is the changed visarga.
questions.rule: Dative plural + नमः; no names; ओ from a visarga.

questions.q: An invented line is श्रीमुनिभ्यो नमः, built like श्रीगुरुभ्यो नमः. What does it say?
options: Homage to the revered sages, several
Homage to the revered sage, one
The revered sages bow in homage
Homage comes from the revered sages
optionExplain: Right: -भ्यः is the dative plural, and the ओ comes from its visarga.
A singular dative would be मुनये.
मुनिभ्यः is dative, so they are the ones honoured.
मुनिभ्यः is the same form in dative and ablative plural; नमः takes the dative, so it is to, not from.
questions.explain: Plural dative -भ्यः plus नमः gives homage to them, and the visarga turns into ओ before न.
questions.teaches: A dative plural in -भ्यः before नमः is written -भ्यो नमः, because a visarga after अ becomes ओ before a voiced sound.

questions.q: What fills this unit?
options: Six verbs, each saying I bow
Six describing words, all accusative singular
optionExplain: No verb occurs in this unit.
Right: They share one case and wait for the noun they describe.
No teacher is named here.
Body parts appear only as parts of a picture, and the words are descriptions.
questions.explain: The unit is a chain of six accusative descriptions with no verb; the noun comes in unit 10.

questions.q: Put the six describing words in the order of the text.
questions.explain: The text runs craving, imaginings, hatred, desire and anger, reasonings, passion.
questions.rule: तृष्णा · असद्विकल्प · प्रद्वेष · कामक्रोध · वितर्क · राग.

questions.q: Match each part of the picture to what the text puts there.
questions.explain: Each compound says having X as the part: the head is false imaginings, and so on.
questions.rule: head = false imaginings; hood = hatred; poison = desire and anger; eyes = passion.
questions.teaches: Each compound of the unit has the form X-part: the second member is the body part and the first is what it is made of.

questions.q: Which is the right split of रागप्रचंडेक्षणम्?
options: राग + प्रचण्ड + ईक्षणम्, where अ + ई gives ए
optionExplain: Neither part is a word on the card.
The card gives eyes as ईक्षणम्, and not क्षणम्, a moment.
Right: The final अ of प्रचण्ड and the ई of ईक्षण merge into ए.
इक्षणम् is not the word on the card, which gives ईक्षणम्.
questions.explain: प्रचण्ड and ईक्षणम् meet with अ + ई, which gives ए.

questions.q: Which feature is NOT in this unit?
optionExplain: प्रद्वेषचंचत्फणम् is in this unit.
रागप्रचंडेक्षणम् is in this unit.
कामक्रोधविषम् is in this unit.
Right: That is मोहास्यम्, in the next unit.
questions.explain: The mouth of delusion belongs to unit 10; the six features of this unit are craving, imaginings, hatred, poison, reasonings and passion.
questions.rule: Mouth = delusion is in unit 10, not here.

questions.q: Two invented words, दीर्घबाहुं रक्तनेत्रं, are masculine accusative singular. Which noun agrees with them?
optionExplain: Right: Masculine, accusative, singular: it agrees in all three.
That is nominative, not accusative.
That is feminine, and the words are masculine.
That is plural, and the words are singular.
questions.explain: Descriptive words agree with their noun in case, number and gender, as these six will with the noun of unit 10.
questions.rule: Describing words agree in case, number and gender.
questions.teaches: Descriptive compounds must agree with the noun they describe, so six accusative singular masculine words wait for a noun of that same form.

questions.q: Who is honoured in unit 10?
options: The mind-serpent, which calmed the Buddha
The Buddha, who calmed the mind-serpent
The Buddha, who was calmed by the serpent
The mantra of wisdom, which spoke to him
optionExplain: The serpent is the object, and he is the one who acts.
Right: बुद्धाय is the one honoured, and he is the one who calmed it.
The serpent is calmed, and does not calm.
The mantra is only the means.
questions.explain: The Buddha is honoured because, by the power of the mantra of wisdom, he calmed the dreadful mind-serpent.
questions.rule: Homage to the Buddha who calmed the mind-serpent.

questions.q: Put the phrases in the order of the text.
questions.explain: The serpent is described, then the means, the deed and the homage follow.
questions.rule: मोहास्यम् · स्वशरीरकोटरशयम् · चित्तोरगं दारुणम् · प्रज्ञामंत्रबलेन · यः शमितवान् · बुद्धाय तस्मै नमः.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
pairs: by the power of the mantra of wisdom
questions.explain: These are the key words of the unit.
questions.rule: चित्तोरगम् = mind-serpent; दारुणम् = dreadful; प्रज्ञामंत्रबलेन = by the power of the mantra of wisdom; शमितवान् = has calmed; बुद्धाय = to the Buddha.
questions.teaches: Key words of unit 10: the serpent is चित्तोरगम्, the means is the power of the mantra of wisdom, and the one honoured is बुद्धाय.

questions.q: Which is the right split of चित्तोरगम्?
options: चित्त + उरगम्, where अ + उ gives ओ
optionExplain: A visarga before उ would leave चित्त उरगम्, and not चित्तोरगम्.
रगम् is not a word on the card.
Right: The final अ of चित्त and the उ of उरगम् merge into ओ.
ऊरगम् is not the word on the card, which gives उरगम्.
questions.explain: चित्त (mind) and उरगम् (serpent) join by अ + उ → ओ.

questions.q: Which features of the serpent does this unit itself state?
options: It has delusion as its mouth
It lies in the hollow of its own body
It has a quivering hood of hatred
It has fierce eyes of passion
optionExplain: मोहास्यम्.
स्वशरीरकोटरशयम्.
दारुणम्.
That is in unit 9, not here.
That is in unit 9, not here.
questions.explain: Mouth, hollow and dreadful are in this unit; hood and eyes are in the previous one.

questions.q: An invented line is यः सत्यवान् तस्मै नमः. What does it say?
options: Homage to him who is a liar
He who is truthful bows to me
Homage to whom he is truthful
Homage to him who is truthful
optionExplain: सत्यवान् means possessing truth.
तस्मै is dative, so he is the one honoured.
यः is the subject, and he is the one being described.
Right: यः is who and तस्मै is to him.
questions.explain: यः … तस्मै pairs a who with a to him, as in unit 10.
questions.rule: यः … तस्मै = he who … to him.
questions.teaches: A relative यः (who) is picked up later by तस्मै (to him): the clause says what he did, and the homage goes to him.

questions.q: What is said to have been cast out, roots and all?
options: The innate diseases beginning with attachment
The books of the medical tradition
optionExplain: Right: रागादिरोगाः सहजाः समूलाः.
No pupils are named in this unit.
Those are what the sages know, not what was cast out.
The verse names attachment and the like, not these.
questions.explain: The first line says the innate diseases beginning with attachment (rāga) were cast out.
questions.rule: Cast out: the innate diseases beginning with attachment.

questions.q: Put the phrases in the order of the text.
questions.explain: The text first says what was cast out, then bows to the physician and to the knowers.
questions.rule: रागादिरोगाः · येनाशु सर्वे · जगतोऽप्यपास्ताः · तमेकवैद्यं · शिरसा नमामि · वैद्यागमज्ञांश्च पितामहादीन्.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are the words that carry the sense of the first line.
questions.rule: सहज = innate; समूल = with roots; आशु = quickly; अपास्त = cast out; एकवैद्य = the sole physician.
questions.teaches: The first line is built from five small words: innate, with roots, quickly, cast out and the sole physician.

questions.q: Which is the right split of जगतोऽप्यपास्ताः?
optionExplain: ओऽपि is not a word on the card.
Right: A visarga after अ before अ becomes ओ, and the ऽ marks the dropped अ.
पास्ताः is not a word, and the card gives अपास्ताः.
उपि is not a word on the card.
questions.explain: जगतः, अपि and अपास्ताः are the three words; the visarga before अ turns into ओ and the following अ is shown by ऽ.

questions.q: Whom does the speaker bow to in this unit?
options: The knowers of the medical tradition
optionExplain: तमेकवैद्यम् is the first object of नमामि.
वैद्यागमज्ञान् is the second object.
पितामहादीन् is named with them.
They are what was cast out, not what is bowed to.
The world only appears in the phrase even of the world.
questions.explain: The accusatives तम्, ज्ञान् and आदीन् are the ones bowed to.
questions.rule: Bowed to: the one physician, the knowers of the tradition, Pitāmaha and others.

questions.q: An invented line is वेदार्थज्ञान् मुनीन् शिरसा नमामि. What does it say?
options: The sages bow with the head to those who know the Veda
I bow to the head of the sages who know the Veda
I bow with my head to the sages who know the meaning of the Veda
I know the meaning of the Veda by bowing to sages
optionExplain: The verb नमामि is I bow, not they bow.
शिरसा is instrumental, with the head, and not the thing bowed to.
Right: शिरसा is with the head and the accusatives are the ones bowed to.
ज्ञान् is an accusative describing the sages and not my knowing.
questions.explain: Accusative plural objects + शिरसा + नमामि = I bow with my head to them.
questions.rule: Objects in the accusative + शिरसा नमामि.
questions.teaches: Those bowed to stand in the accusative (here plural) before नमामि, and शिरसा adds with my head.

questions.q: What does this opening line announce?
options: That the authors have finished the chapter
That a pupil asks for the chapter Āyuṣyakāmīya
That the chapter lists the sages by name
That the authors will explain a chapter named Āyuṣyakāmīya
optionExplain: The verb is future, so nothing has yet been done.
No pupil or question appears in the line.
The line says nothing of its contents.
Right: व्याख्यास्यामः says we shall explain, and the chapter name is given.
questions.explain: The line is the standard formula announcing the chapter named Āyuṣyakāmīya.
questions.rule: अथात … व्याख्यास्यामः = now, therefore, we shall explain.
questions.section: आयुर्वेद की परम्परा: ब्रह्मा से इन्द्र

questions.q: Put the words of the formula in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Now, therefore, the title, chapter, we shall explain.
questions.section: आयुर्वेद की परम्परा: ब्रह्मा से इन्द्र

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: The formula is these four elements plus the title.
questions.rule: अथ = now; अतः = therefore; अध्यायम् = chapter; व्याख्यास्यामः = we shall explain.
questions.teaches: The formula opens with now (अथ) and therefore (अतः), names the chapter, and ends with the future verb we shall explain.
questions.section: आयुर्वेद की परम्परा: ब्रह्मा से इन्द्र

questions.q: Which split of अथात fits the card?
options: अथ + अतः, where अ + अ gives आ
अथा + तः, with a long आ standing alone
अथ + आतः, with आतः as a second word
अथात् + अ, ending in a plain त्
optionExplain: Right: The two words are now and therefore, and the two अ merge.
Neither part is a word on the card.
आतः is not a word on the card, which gives अतः.
Neither part is a word on the card.
questions.explain: The card splits the opening into अथ (now) and अतः (therefore).
questions.section: आयुर्वेद की परम्परा: ब्रह्मा से इन्द्र

questions.q: What does the verb व्याख्यास्यामः tell about who speaks and when?
options: He spoke, in the past: he explained
We speak, in the future: we shall explain
You must act now: explain it
optionExplain: A third person past would look different.
Right: The data labels it 1 pl. fut.
A command would not have the future sign -स्य-.
The ending is plural, we, and the tense is future.
questions.explain: First person plural future: we (the authors) shall explain.
questions.section: आयुर्वेद की परम्परा: ब्रह्मा से इन्द्र

questions.q: An invented line is अथातः शयनीयमध्यायं व्याख्यास्यामः. What does it say?
options: Now, therefore, we have explained the chapter named Śayanīya
Now, therefore, you explain the chapter named Śayanīya
Now, therefore, we shall explain the chapter named Śayanīya
Therefore, then, the chapter named Śayanīya explains us
optionExplain: The verb is future, not past.
The verb is we, not you.
Right: Same formula, with a new title.
The chapter is the object, not the one who explains.
questions.explain: The formula stays the same and only the chapter title changes.
questions.teaches: A chapter opens with अथातः, the chapter's name, अध्यायं and व्याख्यास्यामः, and only the name changes.
questions.section: आयुर्वेद की परम्परा: ब्रह्मा से इन्द्र

questions.q: Who is said to have spoken in this unit?
options: Pitāmaha and the knowers of the tradition
The Buddha, in praise of wisdom and mind
Ātreya and the other great sages
optionExplain: He appears only as 'by one desiring life', not as a speaker.
They appear in unit 11, as those bowed to.
He appears in unit 10, not here.
Right: आत्रेयादयो महर्षयः is the subject of आहुः.
questions.explain: The great sages, Ātreya and the others, are the ones who said it.
questions.rule: Speakers: Ātreya and other great sages.
questions.section: आयुर्वेद की परम्परा: ब्रह्मा से इन्द्र

questions.q: Put the phrases in the order of the text.
questions.explain: The saying is introduced, the sages are named, then comes the one who desires life and the means.
questions.rule: इति ह स्म · आहुः · आत्रेयादयः · महर्षयः · आयुःकामयमानेन · धर्मार्थसुखसाधनम्.
questions.section: आयुर्वेद की परम्परा: ब्रह्मा से इन्द्र

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words give the speakers, the saying and the one who desires life.
questions.rule: आहुः = they said; महर्षयः = great sages; आत्रेयादयः = Ātreya and others; आयुः = life; कामयमानेन = by one desiring.
questions.teaches: The unit's words answer who spoke (they said, great sages, Ātreya and others) and about whom (one desiring life).
questions.section: आयुर्वेद की परम्परा: ब्रह्मा से इन्द्र

questions.q: Which is the right split of स्माहुरात्रेयादयः?
optionExplain: Right: The visarga of आहुः becomes र् before the vowel आ, and अ + आ gives आ.
हुः and रात्रेय are not words on the card.
The card gives the name as आत्रेय.
उः is not a word on the card.
questions.explain: The words are स्म, आहुः, आत्रेय and आदयः; the visarga turns into र् before a vowel after उ.
questions.section: आयुर्वेद की परम्परा: ब्रह्मा से इन्द्र

questions.q: What does the card say about the end of this unit?
options: The sentence is finished: it names what is to be done at once
The sentence is unfinished: what is to be done comes in unit 14
The sentence ends with a command that is given to the sages
The sentence lists all the different means to dharma and wealth
optionExplain: The task of the one desiring life is not given here.
Right: The unit stops at the means to dharma, wealth and happiness.
The sages are the speakers, not the ones commanded.
No means are listed in this unit.
questions.explain: The unit gives the speakers and the one who desires life; the rest follows.
questions.section: आयुर्वेद की परम्परा: ब्रह्मा से इन्द्र

questions.q: In the invented words विद्याकामयमानेन शिष्येण, who is meant?
options: By a pupil desired by knowledge
By knowledge that desires a pupil
By a pupil who desires knowledge
optionExplain: कामयमान says the pupil desires; he is not desired.
विद्या is the thing wished for.
Right: Both words are instrumental singular: by one desiring, by a pupil.
शिष्येण is singular.
questions.explain: Like आयुःकामयमानेन, the participle agrees with the person who desires: here by a pupil who desires knowledge.
questions.rule: Object + कामयमानेन = by one desiring that.
questions.teaches: A participle in -कामयमानेन names the one who desires something, and agrees in case with that person.
questions.section: आयुर्वेद की परम्परा: ब्रह्मा से इन्द्र

questions.q: What attitude toward the teachings of Āyurveda does the first line urge?
optionExplain: The line does not ask for doubt.
The line does not speak of pride.
The line does not speak of fear.
Right: आदर is regard, and परम makes it the highest.
questions.explain: The line says supreme regard is to be paid to the teachings of Āyurveda.
questions.rule: आयुर्वेदोपदेशेषु विधेयः परमादरः = supreme regard is to be paid.
questions.section: आयुर्वेद की परम्परा: ब्रह्मा से इन्द्र

questions.q: Match each part of the first line to its meaning.
pairs: to be paid, to be done
questions.explain: These words carry the whole instruction of the line.
questions.rule: उपदेशेषु = in the teachings; विधेयः = to be done; परम = supreme; आदरः = regard.
questions.section: आयुर्वेद की परम्परा: ब्रह्मा से इन्द्र

questions.q: Put the three words of the first line in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The line names where (in the teachings), then what is to be done, then what: supreme regard.
questions.teaches: A short instruction can be held as three steps: where it applies, what is to be done, and the thing to do.
questions.section: आयुर्वेद की परम्परा: ब्रह्मा से इन्द्र

questions.q: Which is the right split of आयुर्वेदोपदेशेषु?
optionExplain: Right: अ + उ joins as ओ, so आयुर्वेद + उपदेशेषु is written आयुर्वेदोपदेशेषु.
This would be written आयुर्वेद उपदेशेषु.
This would be written आयुर्वेदयुपदेशेषु.
This would be written आयुर्वेदावुपदेशेषु.
questions.explain: आयुर्वेदोपदेशेषु = आयुर्वेद (Āyurveda) + उपदेशेषु (in the teachings).
questions.section: आयुर्वेद की परम्परा: ब्रह्मा से इन्द्र

questions.q: In विधेयः परमादरः, which word names what is to be paid?
optionExplain: It is the first member of the compound in the first word, not the thing to be paid.
Right: विधेयः agrees with it: supreme regard is the thing to be done.
It names where, in the teachings, not what is paid.
It says 'to be done'; it is not the thing paid.
questions.explain: विधेयः is a 'to be done' form agreeing with आदरः.
questions.rule: विधेयः + noun = that noun is to be done.
questions.section: आयुर्वेद की परम्परा: ब्रह्मा से इन्द्र

questions.q: Join नव (new) and उपदेशेषु (in the teachings) by the same sandhi. Which spelling results?
optionExplain: The two vowels do not simply merge into उ.
अ + उ does not give ऊ.
Right: अ + उ gives ओ, as in आयुर्वेदोपदेशेषु.
औ comes from अ + ओ or अ + औ, not from अ + उ.
questions.explain: The rule of the verse works on any word ending in अ that meets उ.
questions.teaches: When a word ending in अ meets a word beginning with उ, the two vowels join as ओ: नव + उपदेशेषु → नवोपदेशेषु.
questions.section: आयुर्वेद की परम्परा: ब्रह्मा से इन्द्र

questions.q: The teaching is handed down a chain. Who is the first receiver named in this verse?
optionExplain: They receive it second.
He is the last receiver in the line.
He is not named in this verse.
Right: ददौ दक्षाय: he gave to Dakṣa.
questions.explain: The chain opens with Dakṣa, then the Aśvins, then Indra.
questions.section: आयुर्वेद की परम्परा: ब्रह्मा से इन्द्र

questions.q: Match each word of the first line to its meaning.
questions.explain: Three receivers, each in the 'to' form, and the verb 'gave'.
questions.rule: ददौ = gave; दक्षाय = to Dakṣa; अश्विभ्याम् = to the two Aśvins; शतक्रतवे = to Śatakratu.
questions.section: आयुर्वेद की परम्परा: ब्रह्मा से इन्द्र

questions.q: Put the receivers in the order the verse hands the teaching on.
questions.explain: Dakṣa first, then the two Aśvins, then Śatakratu (Indra).
questions.teaches: A line of teaching can be held as a chain of receivers: Dakṣa, the two Aśvins, Śatakratu.
questions.section: आयुर्वेद की परम्परा: ब्रह्मा से इन्द्र

questions.q: Which is the right split of सोऽश्विभ्याम्?
optionExplain: Right: A visarga after अ before अ becomes ओ, and the अ is marked by ऽ: सोऽश्विभ्याम्.
This would be written साश्विभ्याम्.
This would be written सावश्विभ्याम्.
श्विभ्याम् is not a word.
questions.explain: सोऽश्विभ्याम् = सः (he) + अश्विभ्याम् (to the two Aśvins).
questions.section: आयुर्वेद की परम्परा: ब्रह्मा से इन्द्र

questions.q: Which four aims does the second line name? Choose all that apply.
optionExplain: Named: first in the compound.
Named: second.
Named: third.
Named: fourth.
Life is not one of the four in this line.
Fame is not named here.
questions.explain: धर्मार्थकाममोक्षाणाम् is a list of four, in the 'of' form: of dharma, wealth, desire and liberation.
questions.rule: The four: धर्म, अर्थ, काम, मोक्ष.
questions.section: आयुर्वेद की परम्परा: ब्रह्मा से इन्द्र

questions.q: In an invented line ददौ शिष्याय स गुरुः, who receives what is given?
optionExplain: गुरुः is the one who gives (ending -ः).
Right: The ending -आय marks the receiver.
ददौ means gave.
Only one receiver is named.
questions.explain: As in ददौ दक्षाय, the 'to' form names the receiver of a gift.
questions.rule: Receiver of ददौ = the word in -आय.
questions.teaches: After ददौ ('gave') the receiver stands in the -आय form: दक्षाय 'to Dakṣa', शिष्याय 'to the pupil'.
questions.section: आयुर्वेद की परम्परा: ब्रह्मा से इन्द्र

questions.q: Men are suffering. Which name does the verse put at the head?
optionExplain: Indra is not named in this verse.
Brahmā is not named in this verse.
Right: पुरस्कृत्य पुनर्वसुम्: having put Punarvasu in front.
Dakṣa is not named in this verse.
questions.explain: Punarvasu is placed in front; the other names follow in the list.
questions.rule: पुरस्कृत्य पुनर्वसुम् = putting Punarvasu at the head.
questions.section: ऋषि इन्द्र के पास: आठ अङ्ग

questions.q: Match each word of the first line to its meaning.
questions.explain: The first line is a condition plus an act of putting someone in front.
questions.rule: नरेषु = among men; पीड्यमानेषु = being afflicted; पुरस्कृत्य = having put in front; पुनर्वसुम् = Punarvasu.
questions.section: ऋषि इन्द्र के पास: आठ अङ्ग

questions.q: Put the four words of the first line in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Men, afflicted, putting in front, Punarvasu.
questions.teaches: The line reads as: when men are afflicted (two words), putting Punarvasu in front (two words).
questions.section: ऋषि इन्द्र के पास: आठ अङ्ग

questions.q: पुरस्कृत्य means having put in front. Why does it end in -य and not -त्वा?
options: The verb is in the plural, not singular
The act is still going on right now
-त्वा is used only after roots ending in ध
A word, पुरस्, comes before the root
optionExplain: Number does not decide between -य and -त्वा.
A 'having done' word names a finished act.
-त्वा is not limited to roots in ध.
Right: A 'having done' word takes -य when something is joined before the root.
questions.explain: A 'having done' word has -त्वा after a plain root (बुद्ध्वा) and -य when a word or prefix is joined before it (पुरस्कृत्य).
questions.rule: Plain root + -त्वा; word or prefix + root + -य.
questions.section: ऋषि इन्द्र के पास: आठ अङ्ग

questions.q: Which of these names appear in this verse? Choose all that apply.
optionExplain: Named in the second line.
Named in the second line.
Named in the second line.
Not named in this verse.
Not named in this verse.
questions.explain: The second line begins with Dhanvantari, Bharadvāja and Nimi; the last two names of the list are uncertain in the print.
questions.section: ऋषि इन्द्र के पास: आठ अङ्ग

questions.q: An invented phrase जनेषु रुग्णेषु (रुग्ण = sick) follows नरेषु पीड्यमानेषु. What does it mean?
optionExplain: Right: Two words in -एषु that agree give 'when (they are) so and so'.
That would end in -नाम्, not -एषु.
That would end in -ऐः, not -एषु.
That would end in -भ्यः, not -एषु.
questions.explain: As नरेषु पीड्यमानेषु = when men are afflicted, जनेषु रुग्णेषु = when the people are sick.
questions.rule: Noun + describing word, both in -एषु = 'when (they are) so'.
questions.teaches: Two agreeing words in -एषु, a noun and its describing word, tell the situation: जनेषु रुग्णेषु 'when the people are sick'.
questions.section: ऋषि इन्द्र के पास: आठ अङ्ग

questions.q: How is Śatakratu described as the sages come to him?
options: A king of men, lord of the earth
A refuge, the lord of the immortals
A pupil of the great sages
optionExplain: The verse calls him lord of the immortals.
Right: शरण्यम् अमरेश्वरम्: a refuge, lord of the immortals.
He is the one approached, not their pupil.
No such guard is named here.
questions.explain: The two titles are शरण्य (giving refuge) and अमरेश्वर (lord of the immortals).
questions.section: ऋषि इन्द्र के पास: आठ अङ्ग

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: Doers, a quality of the doers, the act, and a title of the one approached.
questions.rule: महर्षयः = great sages; महात्मानः = high-souled; उपाजग्मुः = approached; शरण्यम् = refuge.
questions.section: ऋषि इन्द्र के पास: आठ अङ्ग

questions.q: Put the words of the second line in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The one approached, the act, then his two titles.
questions.teaches: The second line names the one approached, what was done, then two titles of the one approached.
questions.section: ऋषि इन्द्र के पास: आठ अङ्ग

questions.q: Which is the right split of शतक्रतुमुपाजग्मुः?
optionExplain: This would be written शतक्रतुरुपाजग्मुः.
मुपाजग्मुः is not a word.
Right: A final म् joins the vowel that follows: म् + उ is written मु.
पाजग्मुः is not a word.
questions.explain: शतक्रतुमुपाजग्मुः = शतक्रतुम् (Śatakratu, the one approached) + उपाजग्मुः (they approached).
questions.rule: म् + vowel: the म् is written with the vowel.
questions.section: ऋषि इन्द्र के पास: आठ अङ्ग

questions.q: Who approached Śatakratu according to this verse? Choose all that apply.
optionExplain: Named: महर्षयः.
Named: आलम्बायनादयः.
Dakṣa is named in unit 15, not here.
Brahmā is not named in this verse.
questions.explain: The doers are the sages and Alambāyana with others; Śatakratu is the one approached.
questions.section: ऋषि इन्द्र के पास: आठ अङ्ग

questions.q: In the invented line ऋषयो विष्णुमुपाजग्मुः, who is approached?
optionExplain: ऋषयः are the doers.
Only one is approached.
उपाजग्मुः means they approached.
Right: The -म् form marks the one approached, as in शतक्रतुम्.
questions.explain: The same pattern as the verse: doers + one approached in -म् + उपाजग्मुः.
questions.teaches: With उपाजग्मुः ('approached') the one approached stands in the -म् form, and a doer's -ः turns to ओ before a voiced sound: ऋषयः + विष्णुम् → ऋषयो विष्णुम्.
questions.section: ऋषि इन्द्र के पास: आठ अङ्ग

questions.q: The sages have come to Indra for refuge. What does he do on seeing them?
optionExplain: Right: निजगाद: he spoke, declared.
Nothing of the kind is said.
The verb says he spoke.
No gift is mentioned here.
questions.explain: Indra speaks out a teaching as soon as he sees them.
questions.rule: तान् दृष्ट्वा निजगाद = having seen them, he declared.
questions.section: ऋषि इन्द्र के पास: आठ अङ्ग

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: The doer, the act, the manner, and the 'of life' that qualifies the Veda.
questions.rule: सहस्राक्षः = thousand-eyed; निजगाद = declared; यथागमम् = according to tradition; आयुषः = of life.
questions.section: ऋषि इन्द्र के पास: आठ अङ्ग

questions.q: Put the words of the second line in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Of life, protector, Veda, subsidiary Veda, of Atharvan.
questions.teaches: The second line builds up the thing declared: of life, a protector, a Veda, a subsidiary Veda, of Atharvan.
questions.section: ऋषि इन्द्र के पास: आठ अङ्ग

questions.q: Which is the right split of तान्दृष्ट्वैव?
optionExplain: ताः is feminine; the sages are masculine, तान्.
Right: आ + ए joins as ऐ, so दृष्ट्वा + एव is written दृष्ट्वैव.
व alone is not a word here.
This would be written दृष्ट एव.
questions.explain: तान्दृष्ट्वैव = तान् (them) + दृष्ट्वा (having seen) + एव (at once).
questions.section: ऋषि इन्द्र के पास: आठ अङ्ग

questions.q: दृष्ट्वा means 'having seen'. What does it tell us about the order of events?
options: Two persons did these two acts
optionExplain: That would reverse the order.
Both acts have the same doer.
Right: A 'having done' word names the act before the main verb.
It is stated as done.
questions.explain: Indra saw, then spoke: दृष्ट्वा precedes निजगाद, and the doer is the same.
questions.rule: -त्वा word: its act comes before the main verb, same doer.
questions.section: ऋषि इन्द्र के पास: आठ अङ्ग

questions.q: Join गत्वा (having gone) and एव by the same sandhi. Which spelling results?
optionExplain: That would come from गत्व + इव (अ + इ → ए), not from आ + ए.
The ए does not vanish.
औ comes from आ + ओ or आ + औ.
Right: आ + ए gives ऐ, as in दृष्ट्वैव.
questions.explain: The rule that gave दृष्ट्वैव works for any word ending in आ that meets ए.
questions.teaches: A word ending in आ followed by ए joins as ऐ: दृष्ट्वा + एव → दृष्ट्वैव, गत्वा + एव → गत्वैव.
questions.section: ऋषि इन्द्र के पास: आठ अङ्ग

questions.q: A Veda has attained the state of eight limbs. Who understood it, according to the verse?
optionExplain: Right: यं पितामहः बुबुधे: which the Grandfather understood.
Indra declared it in unit 18; the verse says the Grandfather understood it.
Dakṣa is not named in this verse.
Punarvasu is not named in this verse.
questions.explain: बुबुधे means understood, and its doer is पितामहः.
questions.section: ऋषि इन्द्र के पास: आठ अङ्ग

questions.q: Match each term of the first line to its literal meaning.
questions.explain: Five of the eight terms; the verse does not explain how they are used.
questions.rule: काय = body; बाल = child; ग्रह = seizers; शल्य = dart; जरा = old age.
questions.section: ऋषि इन्द्र के पास: आठ अङ्ग

questions.q: The first term is काय. Put the other seven terms in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The line runs: body, child, seizers, upper part, dart, fang, old age, bull.
questions.rule: काय → बाल → ग्रह → ऊर्ध्वांग → शल्य → दंष्ट्रा → जरा → वृष (काय पहला है).
questions.teaches: The eight terms are a fixed list; saying them in order is the way to hold them.
questions.section: ऋषि इन्द्र के पास: आठ अङ्ग

questions.q: Which is the right split of ग्रहोर्ध्वांग?
optionExplain: This would be written ग्रह ऊर्ध्वांग.
Right: अ + ऊ joins as ओ, so ग्रह + ऊर्ध्वांग is written ग्रहोर्ध्वांग.
This would be written ग्रहयूर्ध्वांग.
This would be written ग्रह्यूर्ध्वांग.
questions.explain: ग्रहोर्ध्वांग = ग्रह (seizers) + ऊर्ध्वांग (upper part).
questions.section: ऋषि इन्द्र के पास: आठ अङ्ग

questions.q: In यं पितामहः बुबुधे, what does यम् stand for?
optionExplain: He is the doer, पितामहः.
They are in the 'by' form, वृषैः.
Right: यम् is 'which'; its noun, the Veda, is supplied from unit 18.
अष्टांगताम् is what the Veda attained, not what was understood.
questions.explain: यम् points back to the Veda, the one the Grandfather understood.
questions.rule: यम् = which: it repeats the supplied Veda.
questions.section: ऋषि इन्द्र के पास: आठ अङ्ग

questions.q: Join वन (forest) and ऊर्ध्वम् (upward) by the same sandhi. Which spelling results?
optionExplain: अ + ऊ does not give ऊ.
आ is for अ + अ.
औ is for अ + ओ or अ + औ.
Right: अ + ऊ gives ओ, as in ग्रहोर्ध्वांग.
questions.explain: The sandhi in ग्रहोर्ध्वांग works the same on any word ending in अ.
questions.teaches: A word ending in अ followed by ऊ joins as ओ: ग्रह + ऊर्ध्व → ग्रहोर्ध्व, वन + ऊर्ध्वम् → वनोर्ध्वम्.
questions.section: ऋषि इन्द्र के पास: आठ अङ्ग

questions.q: After the sages take it up, what is it that they receive, per the first line?
optionExplain: Right: तम् आम्नायम् is what they received.
No king or gift is named.
No weapon is named here.
No naming is mentioned.
questions.explain: The first line says they received that traditional teaching.
questions.rule: गृहीत्वा ते तमाम्नायम् = having received that teaching, they.
questions.section: ऋषि इन्द्र के पास: आठ अङ्ग

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: The act, what was received, how, and the doers.
questions.rule: गृहीत्वा = having received; आम्नायम् = traditional teaching; परस्परम् = mutually; ते = they.
questions.section: ऋषि इन्द्र के पास: आठ अङ्ग

questions.q: Put the first three words of the unit in order.
questions.explain: Having received, they, that teaching.
questions.teaches: The unit opens with the act of receiving, then the receivers (ते), then what they received.
questions.section: ऋषि इन्द्र के पास: आठ अङ्ग

questions.q: Which is the right split of तमाम्नायम्?
optionExplain: This would be written तस्याम्नायम्.
Right: A final म् joins the next vowel: तम् + आम्नायम् is written तमाम्नायम्.
This would be written तानाम्नायम्.
नायम् is not a word here.
questions.explain: तमाम्नायम् = तम् (that) + आम्नायम् (traditional teaching).
questions.rule: म् + vowel: the म् is written with the vowel.
questions.section: ऋषि इन्द्र के पास: आठ अङ्ग

questions.q: In गृहीत्वा ते तमाम्नायम्, which word is the doer of the receiving?
optionExplain: तम् is 'that', in the -म् form with the thing received.
आम्नायम् is the thing received.
Right: ते is 'they', the doers; गृहीत्वा names their act.
परस्परम् says how: mutually.
questions.explain: ते names the doers; तम् आम्नायम् is what they received.
questions.rule: Doer ते + गृहीत्वा; the -म् words are what is received.
questions.section: ऋषि इन्द्र के पास: आठ अङ्ग

questions.q: In the invented line शिष्याः पाठं गृहीत्वा मुदिता अभवन् (became), who is delighted, and when?
options: The lesson, after the pupils receive it
The pupils, before receiving the lesson
The teacher, after giving the lesson
The pupils, after receiving the lesson
optionExplain: पाठम् is what was received.
गृहीत्वा names the earlier act.
No teacher is named.
Right: गृहीत्वा comes first; मुदिताः goes with शिष्याः.
questions.explain: As in the verse: a -त्वा word, then a describing word in -आः that agrees with the doers.
questions.rule: -त्वा act first; -आः describing word agrees with the plural doers.
questions.teaches: A 'having done' word (-त्वा) names the earlier act, and a plural describing word like मुदिताः goes with the plural doers (शिष्याः).
questions.section: ऋषि इन्द्र के पास: आठ अङ्ग

questions.q: For what purpose do they compose treatises, according to the first line?
options: To end the teaching of Āyurveda
optionExplain: Right: स्थित्यर्थम् आयुर्वेदस्य: for the sake of its continuance.
The line states no such purpose.
The line says the opposite: its continuance.
No king is mentioned.
questions.explain: The purpose is स्थिति, the staying on, of Āyurveda.
questions.rule: स्थित्यर्थम् = for the sake of continuance.

questions.q: Match each word of the first line to its meaning.
questions.explain: The purpose, whose, what, and the act.
questions.rule: स्थित्यर्थम् = for continuance; आयुर्वेदस्य = of Āyurveda; तंत्राणि = treatises; चक्रिरे = they composed.

questions.q: Put the words of the first line in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Purpose, of Āyurveda, they then, treatises, composed.
questions.teaches: The line puts the purpose first and the act last: for continuance, of Āyurveda, they then, treatises, composed.

questions.q: Which is the right split of स्थित्यर्थम्?
optionExplain: This would be written स्थित्यार्थम्.
Right: इ before a different vowel becomes य्: स्थिति + अर्थम् is written स्थित्यर्थम्.
This would be written स्थितिरर्थम्.
This would be written स्थितेऽर्थम्.
questions.explain: स्थित्यर्थम् = स्थिति (continuance) + अर्थम् (for the sake of).

questions.q: तंत्राणि is neuter plural and चक्रिरे is past. How many treatises, and when?
options: Treatises are still to be composed
optionExplain: Plural -आणि does not mean one.
चक्रिरे is past, not future.
Right: Plural noun and a past act.
तंत्राणि is the thing made, not the doers.
questions.explain: तंत्राणि is plural, so several treatises, and चक्रिरे says it was done.
questions.rule: Neuter plural -आणि = several; चक्रिरे = they made (past).

questions.q: Join ते and अपि by the same sandhi as ते + अथ → तेऽथ. Which spelling results?
optionExplain: ए becomes अय् before other vowels, not before अ.
ए does not turn into आ.
ए does not turn into औ.
Right: ए stays before अ, and the lost अ is marked by ऽ.
questions.explain: As ते + अथ gives तेऽथ, ते + अपि gives तेऽपि.
questions.teaches: After ए an initial अ is dropped and marked by ऽ: ते + अथ → तेऽथ, ते + अपि → तेऽपि.

questions.q: Karāla and others are called good disciples. What is done for them?
options: They are made to learn it
They are asked to be silent
optionExplain: Right: ग्राहयामासुः: they caused to learn.
Nothing of the kind is said.
No kingship is mentioned.
The verb is about learning.
questions.explain: The good disciples are made to learn the teaching.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: The learners, the causing, the 'own', and the making.
questions.rule: सच्छिष्यान् = good disciples; ग्राहयामासुः = caused to learn; स्वंस्वम् = each his own; चक्रुः = they made.

questions.q: Put the phrases of the second line in the verse's order (joined words shown split).
questions.explain: Each his own treatise, then, they too, made, and those made.
questions.rule: स्वंस्वं तंत्रं → ततः → तेऽपि → चक्रुः → तानि कृतानि च.
questions.teaches: The second line goes: each his own treatise, then they too made (it), and those that were made.

questions.q: Which is the right split of सच्छिष्यान्?
optionExplain: This would be written स शिष्यान्.
Right: त् before श joins as च्छ: सत् + शिष्यान् is written सच्छिष्यान्.
This would be written सत्यशिष्यान्, keeping the य्.
This would be written सा शिष्यान्.
questions.explain: सच्छिष्यान् = सत् (good) + शिष्यान् (disciples).

questions.q: ग्राहयामासुः means 'they caused to learn'. Who learns?
optionExplain: They are the subject of ग्राहयामासुः, the causers, not the learners.
The point of the act is that someone learns.
Right: The causing is done to the disciples, who are in -आन् form.
Treatises are things, not learners.
questions.explain: The sages are the doers of the causing; Karāla and the other disciples are the learners.
questions.rule: Causing verb: one makes another learn.

questions.q: Join ऋषयः and ते as in ततः + ते → ततस्ते. Which spelling results?
optionExplain: ओ is for a voiced sound; त is not voiced.
The consonant स् is not dropped.
श् is for च or छ, not for त.
Right: A visarga before त becomes स्.
questions.explain: ततः + ते gave ततस्ते; the same rule works here.
questions.teaches: A visarga before त becomes स्: ततः + ते → ततस्ते, चक्रुः + तानि → चक्रुस्तानि, ऋषयः + ते → ऋषयस्ते.

questions.q: To whom do the intelligent ones recite the treatises?
optionExplain: Right: गुरून् सर्षिसंघान्: teachers together with groups of sages.
No king is mentioned.
No such listeners are named.
They are not named here.
questions.explain: The works are recited to the teachers, who sit with groups of sages.
questions.rule: गुरून् संश्रावयामासुः = they made the teachers hear.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five words that carry the sequence: recited, praised, obtained.
questions.rule: गुरून् = teachers; संश्रावयामासुः = recited; सुमेधसः = of good intelligence; प्रशस्तानि = praised; लेभिरे = obtained.

questions.q: Put the words of the second line in the verse's order.
questions.explain: By them, praised, those of theirs, standing, on earth, obtained.
questions.rule: तैः → प्रशस्तानि → तान्येषाम् → प्रतिष्ठाम् → भुवि → लेभिरे.
questions.teaches: The second line runs: by them, praised, those works of theirs, standing, on earth, they obtained.

questions.q: Which is the right split of तान्येषाम्?
optionExplain: This would be written तानैषाम्.
Right: इ before a different vowel becomes य्: तानि + एषाम् is written तान्येषाम्.
This would be written तान्यैषाम्.
This would be written तान एषाम्.
questions.explain: तान्येषाम् = तानि (those) + एषाम् (of them).

questions.q: Which statements agree with this unit? Choose all that apply.
options: The treatises were recited to the teachers
The treatises gained standing on earth
The treatises were kept secret from the sages
optionExplain: Stated in the first line.
Stated: प्रशस्तानि.
Stated: प्रतिष्ठां भुवि लेभिरे.
The opposite: they were recited before groups of sages.
questions.explain: The unit gives the order: recited, praised, standing gained.

questions.q: Join पुस्तकानि and अपि by the same sandhi as तानि + एषाम् → तान्येषाम्. Which spelling results?
optionExplain: The इ is not simply dropped.
The य् must join the consonant न्: न्य.
Right: इ before a different vowel becomes य्.
इ does not lengthen here.
questions.explain: तानि + एषाम् gave तान्येषाम्; the same rule works here.
questions.teaches: A final इ before a different vowel becomes य्: तानि + एषाम् → तान्येषाम्, पुस्तकानि + अपि → पुस्तकान्यपि.

questions.q: Does the verse say that each single treatise is all-embracing?
options: Yes, but only the first one
optionExplain: That is the opposite of अव्यापि.
The word तेषाम् refers to the treatises.
No treatise is singled out.
Right: अव्यापि means not all-embracing.
questions.explain: तेषाम् एकैकम् अव्यापि: of those, each one is not all-embracing.
questions.rule: एकैकम् अव्यापि = each one is not all-embracing.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: Three words of the first claim and the word तु that turns it.
questions.rule: तेषाम् = of those; एकैकम् = each one; अव्यापि = not all-embracing; तु = but.

questions.q: Put these five phrases of the verse in their order.
questions.explain: Of those, each one, not all-embracing; then, in pursuit of each treatise, loss of a man's life.
questions.teaches: The two lines are held as two halves: each one is not all-embracing; pursuing each in turn wastes a man's life.

questions.q: Which is the right split of प्रतितंत्राभियोगे?
optionExplain: Right: अ + अ joins as आ: प्रतितंत्र + अभियोगे is written प्रतितंत्राभियोगे.
This would be written प्रतितंत्र्यभियोगे.
This would be written प्रतितंत्रेऽभियोगे.
भियोगे is not a word.
questions.explain: प्रतितंत्राभियोगे = प्रतितंत्र (each treatise) + अभियोगे (in the pursuit).

questions.q: What does the verse say happens if each treatise is taken up in turn?
options: A man gains a long life
A complete wasting of a man's life
optionExplain: The verse says the reverse.
Right: पुरुषायुषसंक्षयः: total loss of a man's life.
The first line says each one is not all-embracing.
Nothing like that is said.
questions.explain: तु ('but') turns the argument: pursuing each in turn uses up a man's whole life.
questions.rule: प्रतितंत्राभियोगे तु = but in pursuing each treatise; result: loss of life.

questions.q: On the pattern of प्रतितंत्र (for each treatise), what does प्रतिगृहम् mean?
optionExplain: प्रति does not mean 'many together'.
प्रति does not name an owner.
Right: प्रति before a noun gives 'each, every'.
प्रति does not mean 'best'.
questions.explain: प्रति + noun names each one of them: प्रतितंत्र each treatise, प्रतिगृहम् each house.
questions.teaches: प्रति before a noun gives 'each, every': प्रतितंत्र 'each treatise', प्रतिगृहम् 'each house'.

questions.q: Do the authors of the treatises state different matters, or the same matter?
options: Nothing at all, they are silent
The same matter, again and again
optionExplain: The verse says the very same matter.
No clash is mentioned.
The verse says it was stated.
Right: स एवार्थः प्रोक्तः पुनःपुनः: that very matter, stated again and again.
questions.explain: The verse says the matter is the same, with some special point here and there.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: The means, the repetition, the authors, and the added point.
questions.rule: अध्ययनेन = by study; पुनःपुनः = again and again; तंत्रकारैः = by the authors; विशेषतः = in particular.

questions.q: Put the phrases of the second line in the verse's order.
questions.explain: By the authors, that very matter, somewhere, some, in particular.
questions.rule: तंत्रकारैः → स एवार्थः → क्वचित् → कश्चित् → विशेषतः.
questions.teaches: The second line says who, what, and then how it varies: somewhere some special point.

questions.q: Which is the right split of एवार्थः?
optionExplain: Right: अ + अ joins as आ: एव + अर्थः is written एवार्थः.
This would be written एवोऽर्थः.
This would be written एवेऽर्थः.
This would be written एवावर्थः.
questions.explain: एवार्थः = एव (the very) + अर्थः (matter).

questions.q: प्रोक्तः means 'stated'. Which noun of the second line does it go with?
optionExplain: This is 'by the authors', the ones who state.
Right: Both end in -ः: the matter is what is stated.
This is 'some'; it ends in -त्, not in -ः like प्रोक्तः.
This is 'in particular', an adverb, not a noun.
questions.explain: प्रोक्तः and अर्थः agree: the matter has been stated by the authors.
questions.rule: Describing word and noun agree in form: प्रोक्तः ~ अर्थः.

questions.q: On the pattern of तंत्रकारैः (by the authors of treatises), which word means by the authors of poems?
optionExplain: This is one author, as the doer.
This is 'by one author'.
Right: काव्य (poem) + कार (maker) + the 'by, many' ending -ऐः.
This is one author, the one acted on.
questions.explain: तंत्र + कारैः gives 'by the makers of treatises'; काव्य + कारैः gives 'by the makers of poems'.
questions.rule: Work + कार + ऐः = by the makers of that work (many).
questions.teaches: A word for a work plus कार ('maker') names its author, and -ऐः means 'by (many)': तंत्रकारैः, काव्यकारैः.

questions.q: What is the Aṣṭāṅgasaṃgraha said to be, in relation to the earlier treatises?
options: A refutation of all the treatises that came before it
A copy of one single treatise, word for word
A commentary that explains one treatise line by line
A condensing of all the treatises
optionExplain: Nothing in the line speaks of refuting.
The line says all the treatises, and condensed.
The line says it condenses them; it does not call itself a commentary.
Right: सर्वतंत्राणि संहृत्य: having condensed all the treatises.
questions.explain: संहृत्य means having condensed, and सर्वतंत्राणि is all the treatises.
questions.rule: सर्वतंत्राणि संहृत्य = having condensed all the treatises.

questions.q: Match each word of line 2 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words carry the whole claim of the second line.
questions.rule: सर्वतंत्राणि = all treatises; अतः = therefore; संहृत्य = having condensed.

questions.q: The word for 'therefore' is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: अतः means therefore: it links the claim to what came before.
questions.teaches: अतः ('from this, therefore') begins a result: the earlier texts are the reason, the compendium is the result.

questions.q: Which is the right split of सर्वतंत्राण्यतः?
optionExplain: Right: इ before a different vowel becomes य्: णि + अ gives ण्य.
यतः is not what stands here, and the first part would end in -अ.
-ए + अ would give -ए with an avagraha, not ण्य.
A visarga before अ would give -ओऽ, not ण्य.
questions.explain: सर्वतंत्राणि (all treatises, neuter plural) + अतः (therefore).
questions.rule: इ + different vowel → य् + vowel: णि + अतः = ण्यतः.

questions.q: Put these parts of line 2 in the order of the verse (leaving out the unclear word).
questions.explain: The line runs: all treatises, therefore, having condensed, the Aṣṭāṅgasaṃgraha.

questions.q: Which form meaning having collected, from सं + ग्रह्, is built like संहृत्य, 'having condensed'?
optionExplain: -त्वा goes on a verb without prefix; with a prefix it becomes -य.
Right: A verb with a prefix forms its 'having done' form in -य, as संहृत्य does.
This is a noun, 'a collection', not a 'having done' form.
This is 'collected' (a past participle), not 'having collected'.
questions.explain: संहृत्य (सं + हृ) is a 'having done' form with a prefix: it ends in -य (here -त्य).
questions.teaches: A verb with a prefix forms its 'having done' word in -य (संहृत्य, संगृह्य); without a prefix it takes -त्वा.

questions.q: On which three branches (स्कंध) does the work rest, according to this unit?
optionExplain: These come later, in unit 31, as the doṣas.
Nothing like this is in the unit.
Right: हेतु, लिंग, औषध are the three branches in the second line.
These are not named here.
questions.explain: The second line names हेतु, लिंग and औषध as the three branches.

questions.q: Put the three branches in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The line runs हेतु, लिंग, औषध.

questions.q: Which is the right split of हेतुलिंगौषध-?
optionExplain: षध is not a word.
गौषध is not a word.
That would be written लिंगोषध, with ओ, not औ.
Right: अ + औ gives औ, so लिंग + औषध is written लिंगौषध.
questions.explain: Three words are joined: हेतु (cause), लिंग (sign), औषध (medicine).
questions.rule: अ/आ + औ → औ: लिंग + औषध = लिंगौषध.
questions.teaches: When a word ending in -अ meets a word beginning with औ, the two join as औ (लिंग + औषध = लिंगौषध).

questions.q: Match each part of the compound to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words build the two descriptions of the work.
questions.rule: वर्जितः = free from; त्रय = group of three; मात्र = only; निबंधनः = resting on.

questions.q: Which two of these does the unit say the work is free from?
optionExplain: Right: it is the first item of the list.
Right: it is named in the list.
Cause is one of the three branches the work rests on.
Sign is one of the three branches the work rests on.
Medicine is one of the three branches the work rests on.
questions.explain: वर्जित means free from: the work is free from misplaced elaboration and repetition (and ākṣepa). The three branches are what it rests on.
questions.rule: Free from: अस्थानविस्तर, पुनरुक्त. Rests on: हेतु, लिंग, औषध.

questions.q: An invented phrase says भयवर्जितः, like पुनरुक्तादिवर्जितः. What does it mean?
optionExplain: Right: -वर्जित at the end of a compound means free from what comes before.
वर्जित means free from, not full of.
'Born of' would be -ज, not -वर्जित.
Nothing in the word means measuring.
questions.explain: X-वर्जित = free from X: अस्थान…आदिवर्जितः is 'free from … and the like'.
questions.teaches: A compound ending in -वर्जित means 'free from' the first part (पुनरुक्तादिवर्जितः; भयवर्जितः).

questions.q: The work is the illuminator of what kind of passages?
options: Passages that repeat what was said before
Passages whose meaning and essence are deeply hidden
Passages that are easy to understand
Passages that other treatises leave out altogether
optionExplain: Repetition is what unit 27 says the work avoids.
Right: विनिगूढार्थतत्त्वानां प्रदेशानां प्रकाशकः.
The verse says the hidden ones, not the easy ones.
Nothing in the verse speaks of missing passages.
questions.explain: विनिगूढ = deeply hidden; अर्थतत्त्व = meaning and essence; प्रदेश = passage, topic.
questions.rule: प्रकाशकः illuminates passages of hidden meaning.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: The two doers (प्रकाशक, विनिवर्तक) and the two words about their object and extent.
questions.rule: प्रकाशकः = illuminator; विनिवर्तकः = remover; विरोध = contradiction; भूयिष्ठम् = for the most part.

questions.q: The word for 'illuminator' is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: प्रकाशकः = the one who makes something shine.
questions.teaches: A word ending in -क, like प्रकाशक and विनिवर्तक, names the doer of the action: one who illuminates, one who removes.

questions.q: Which pairing matches the verse?
options: Remover of hidden passages; illuminator of contradictions
Illuminator of hidden passages and illuminator of contradictions
Illuminator of hidden passages; remover of contradictions
Remover of hidden passages and remover of contradictions
optionExplain: The two doers are swapped.
The second doer is विनिवर्तकः, a remover.
Right: प्रकाशकः goes with the hidden passages and विनिवर्तकः with the contradictions.
The first doer is प्रकाशकः, an illuminator.
questions.explain: प्रकाशक goes with the hidden passages, विनिवर्तक with the contradictions.

questions.q: Put these parts of the verse in order.
questions.explain: The verse first names the hidden passages and their illuminator, then the contradictions, 'for the most part', and their remover.
questions.rule: Hidden passages → illuminator → contradictions → for the most part → remover.

questions.q: Join ग्रंथ + अर्थ in the way स्व + अन्य is joined. Which is right?
optionExplain: -ओ comes from a visarga, which is not there.
-ऐ comes from अ + ए/ऐ, not from अ + अ.
The अ + अ do not drop out.
Right: अ + अ gives आ, as in स्व + अन्य = स्वान्य.
questions.explain: In स्वान्य both short अ meet and make one long आ.
questions.teaches: Two short अ side by side join as one long आ: स्व + अन्य = स्वान्य, ग्रंथ + अर्थ = ग्रंथार्थ.

questions.q: What does line 1 say will be done by divisions?
options: A presentation suited to the age
A refutation of the other treatises
A list of all the drugs of the earth
A translation into the common speech
optionExplain: Right: युगानुरूपसंदर्शः विभागेन करिष्यते.
Nothing in line 1 speaks of refuting.
No drugs are named in line 1.
Nothing in line 1 speaks of translating.
questions.explain: संदर्शः is the presentation; युगानुरूप says it is suited to the age.
questions.rule: Line 1: a presentation suited to the age will be made by divisions.

questions.q: Match each word of line 1 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are the four pieces of the announcement.
questions.rule: युगानुरूप = suited to the age; संदर्शः = presentation; विभागेन = by division; करिष्यते = will be made.

questions.q: The word for 'will be made' is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: करिष्यते is future, third person singular, middle voice, with a passive sense.
questions.teaches: The -ष्य- in करिष्यते marks the future ('will'); the ending -ते with the passive sense gives 'will be made'.
questions.rule: करिष्यते = will be made (future, passive sense).

questions.q: One word is wrong in: 'A presentation suited to the book will be made, by division.' Which?
optionExplain: संदर्शः is a presentation.
Right: युग means age, not book.
करिष्यते is future: will be made.
विभागेन means by division.
questions.explain: The line says suited to the age (युग), not suited to a book.

questions.q: Put these parts of line 1 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The line runs: presentation suited to the age, by division, will be made.

questions.q: An invented line says क्रमेण वक्ष्यते, like विभागेन करिष्यते. What does it say?
options: It will be hidden by the order
It will be told in order
optionExplain: वक्ष्यते is future, not past; क्रमेण is not disorder.
वक्ष्यते means told, not hidden.
Right: क्रमेण = in order (a word in -एन gives the manner); वक्ष्यते = will be told.
The verb is passive: it will be told, it does not tell.
questions.explain: A noun in -एन says how (by what means); a verb in -ष्यते is a future passive.
questions.rule: -एन = by, in the manner of; -ष्य- = future.
questions.teaches: A noun ending in -एन says how the action is done (विभागेन, क्रमेण); -ष्य- marks the future, so करिष्यते and वक्ष्यते read 'will be made', 'will be told'.

questions.q: What does the unit say is collected in particular?
optionExplain: Grammar is not named.
No drugs are named here.
The unit does not speak of earlier verses in this way.
Right: संगृहीतं विशेषेण यत्र कायचिकित्सितम्.
questions.explain: कायचिकित्सित is the treatment of the body; विशेषेण says it is collected especially.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words give the two statements of the unit.
questions.rule: संगृहीतम् = collected; विशेषेण = especially; यत्र = where; वर्जितम् = devoid of.

questions.q: Which is the right split of किंचिदागमवर्जितम्?
optionExplain: Right: Final त् becomes voiced द् before a vowel, so किंचित् + आगम is written किंचिदागम.
गम is not the word here, and किंचिदा is not a word.
A visarga would give a different join, and किंचिः is not a word.
किंचिद is not a word; the word is किंचित्.
questions.explain: किंचित् (anything) + आगम (āgama) + वर्जितम् (devoid of).
questions.rule: Final त् → द् before a vowel.
questions.teaches: A final त् is voiced to द् when a vowel or voiced sound follows (किंचित् + आगम = किंचिदागम).

questions.q: Which reading of line 2 fits the Sanskrit?
options: Here not the slightest thing is contrary to āgama
Here not the slightest thing is devoid of āgama
Here something is devoid of āgama
Here not the slightest thing is collected from āgama
optionExplain: Contrary would need a word like विरुद्ध; वर्जित means devoid of.
Right: वर्जित means devoid of.
The न (not) makes it 'nothing'.
संगृहीत is in line 1 and says something else.
questions.explain: न … किंचित् … आगमवर्जितम्: nothing at all is devoid of āgama.

questions.q: Put these parts of line 1 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The line runs: collected, especially, where, treatment of the body.

questions.q: An invented line says न किंचिदत्र भयवर्जितम्, like न किंचिदागमवर्जितम्. What does it say?
options: Here everything is free from fear
Here something is free from fear
Here nothing is free from fear
optionExplain: The न reverses that.
न किंचित् means not anything.
Right: न … किंचित् … वर्जितम् says nothing at all is free from that.
The line says nothing is free from it; it does speak of fear.
questions.explain: Not anything is free from fear.
questions.rule: न किंचित् … वर्जितम् = nothing at all is devoid of …
questions.teaches: न किंचित् with an adjective negates it for every item: न किंचिदागमवर्जितम् = nothing is devoid of āgama.

questions.q: Which three doṣas does the unit name?
options: Pitta, Kapha and the digestive fire
optionExplain: Blood is not named as a doṣa here.
The digestive fire (agni) is in unit 34, not a doṣa here.
The belly (koṣṭha) is in unit 35, not a doṣa here.
Right: वायुः पित्तं कफश्चेति त्रयो दोषाः.
questions.explain: The second line names the three in order: वायुः, पित्तम्, कफः.

questions.q: Put the three doṣas in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The verse runs वायुः, पित्तम्, कफः.

questions.q: Why is कफः + च written कफश्च?
options: A visarga before च becomes श्
A visarga before a voiced sound becomes ओ
A visarga before a vowel becomes र्
optionExplain: Right: Before च or छ the visarga turns into श्.
That is the rule after अ before a voiced sound; च is not voiced.
च is not a vowel.
It does not drop here; it changes to श्.
questions.explain: कफः + च + इति joins as कफश्चेति: visarga + च → श्च, and च + इ → चे.
questions.teaches: A visarga before च or छ becomes श् (कफः + च = कफश्च).

questions.q: Why is it त्रयो दोषाः and not त्रयः दोषाः?
options: A visarga before द becomes श्
A visarga after अ before a voiced consonant becomes ओ
A visarga after अ always drops
The visarga turns to र् because दोषाः is long
optionExplain: श् comes before च or छ.
Right: त्रयः ends in अः and द is voiced, so अः becomes ओ.
It does not drop before a voiced consonant; it turns to ओ.
र् comes after other vowels, not after अ.
questions.explain: त्रयः + दोषाः = त्रयो दोषाः.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words are in the two lines.
questions.rule: संक्षेपाय = for brevity; समासतः = in brief; वायुः = Vāyu; क्रमः = order.

questions.q: Join बालः + गच्छति by the rule of त्रयः + दोषाः. Which is right?
optionExplain: र् is after other vowels, not after अ.
श् comes before च or छ.
Right: अः before a voiced consonant (ग) becomes ओ.
The sound does not vanish.
questions.explain: बालः ends in अः and ग is voiced, so ओ.
questions.teaches: After अ, a visarga before a voiced consonant becomes ओ (त्रयः + दोषाः = त्रयो दोषाः, बालः + गच्छति = बालो गच्छति).

questions.q: By which three states is each doṣa said to be threefold?
options: Birth, youth and old age, as in a life
Morning, noon and night, as in a day
High, middling and low, as in grades
optionExplain: These are not named in this unit.
These are not named in this unit.
These are the grades of increase and decrease, not the three states.
Right: वृद्धिक्षयसाम्यविभेदतः.
questions.explain: The first line names वृद्धि, क्षय and साम्य.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: The first three are the states of line 1; उत्कृष्ट is the first grade of line 2.
questions.rule: वृद्धि = increase; क्षय = decrease; साम्य = equilibrium; उत्कृष्ट = high.

questions.q: Which is the right split of वृद्धिक्षयावपि?
optionExplain: Right: -औ before a vowel becomes आव्, so वृद्धिक्षयौ + अपि is written वृद्धिक्षयावपि.
वपि is not a word.
आवपि is not a word.
वृद्धिक्षयाव् is not a word; the आव् is the join itself.
questions.explain: वृद्धिक्षयौ is a pair, increase and decrease; अपि means also.
questions.teaches: The sound औ turns into आव् before a vowel (वृद्धिक्षयौ + अपि = वृद्धिक्षयावपि); here -औ is the dual of the joined pair.

questions.q: Which does the verse say are graded high, middling and low?
optionExplain: Equilibrium is not graded in this unit.
Right: वृद्धिक्षयावपि: increase and decrease, too, are threefold.
Only increase and decrease are graded.
Decrease is named with it.
questions.explain: The second line grades वृद्धि and क्षय only.

questions.q: Put the three grades in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The compound runs उत्कृष्ट, मध्य, अल्प.

questions.q: An invented line says प्रत्येकं ते द्विधा, like प्रत्येकं ते त्रिधा. What does it say?
optionExplain: त्रिधा is threefold; द्विधा is twofold.
प्रत्येकम् means each, not together.
Right: द्वि is two and -धा means in that many ways, as त्रि-धा is threefold.
द्वि is two, not one.
questions.explain: A number + -धा gives 'in that many ways'.
questions.teaches: A number + -धा means 'in that many ways': द्विधा twofold, त्रिधा threefold.

questions.q: What do the doṣas do to the body when they are deranged?
optionExplain: That is what they do when unaltered.
The verse gives an effect for each state.
Protecting is not what the verse says.
Right: विकृताः देहं घ्नन्ति: deranged, they strike the body down.
questions.explain: घ्नन्ति means they destroy; it goes with विकृताः.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: The two states and the two results of line 1.
questions.rule: विकृताः = deranged; अविकृताः = unaltered; घ्नन्ति = they destroy; वर्द्धयन्ति = they make grow.

questions.q: What does अविकृताः mean, built from the prefix अ- and विकृताः?
optionExplain: Right: अ- negates: अ + विकृताः = not deranged.
अ- does not strengthen; it negates.
'Born of' would end in -ज.
The word is about the state, not about being destroyed.
questions.explain: अ-विकृत is the opposite of विकृत.
questions.rule: अ- before a word negates it.
questions.teaches: The prefix अ- makes the opposite of a word (विकृत deranged, अविकृत unaltered).

questions.q: Which pairing matches the unit?
options: Deranged and unaltered both make it grow
optionExplain: The two results are swapped.
Right: The first half says विकृत → घ्नन्ति, the second अविकृत → वर्द्धयन्ति.
Unaltered ones make the body grow.
Deranged ones destroy it.
questions.explain: The verse reads in parallel: deranged with destroy, unaltered with make grow.

questions.q: Put the three places of the doṣas in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The compound runs below, middle, above.

questions.q: Join व्यापिनः + अपि the way the verse does. Which is right?
optionExplain: A visarga after अ does not give आ.
The visarga does change before अ.
Right: अः + अ becomes ओऽ: the ऽ marks the dropped अ.
ऐ comes from other sounds, not from अः.
questions.explain: अः + अ gives ओऽ.
questions.teaches: A final अः meeting an अ joins as ओऽ (व्यापिनः + अपि = व्यापिनोऽपि).

questions.q: What is the digestive fire (अग्नि) when the doṣas are even?
optionExplain: Sharp is one of the three irregular states.
Slow is one of the three irregular states.
Irregular is one of the three irregular states.
Right: समैः समः: with even ones, even.
questions.explain: The last words are समैः समः: even doṣas, even fire.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four are the states of the fire in line 2.
questions.rule: विषमः = irregular; तीक्ष्णः = sharp; मंदः = slow; समः = even.

questions.q: Why is तैः + भवेत् written तैर्भवेत्?
options: A visarga after ऐ before a voiced sound becomes र्
A visarga after ऐ before a voiced sound becomes ओ
A visarga before भ becomes श्
optionExplain: Right: After any vowel except अ and आ, a visarga turns into र् before a voiced sound.
ओ is the result only after अ.
श् comes before च or छ.
It does not drop here; it becomes र्.
questions.explain: तैः (by them) + भवेत् (becomes): the visarga turns into र्.
questions.rule: Visarga after ऐ + voiced sound → र्.
questions.teaches: After a vowel other than अ or आ, a visarga before a voiced sound becomes र् (तैः + भवेत् = तैर्भवेत्).

questions.q: In the end, middle and beginning of which of these are the doṣas said to be?
optionExplain: No season is named in line 1.
Right: भुक्तानाम् ends the list: age, day, night, meal.
No journey is named in line 1.
No month is named in line 1.
questions.explain: Line 1 lists वयः, अहः, रात्रि and भुक्त.
questions.rule: भुक्त = meal: one of the four.

questions.q: Put the states of the fire in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The verse runs irregular, sharp, slow, then even for the even doṣas.

questions.q: Join दोषैः + भवति the way तैः + भवेत् is joined. Which is right?
optionExplain: ओ is the result after अ, not after ऐ.
श् comes before च or छ.
Right: A visarga after ऐ before a voiced sound (भ) becomes र्.
The visarga does not drop.
questions.explain: दोषैः ends in ऐः and भ is voiced, so र्.
