questions.section: अंजन, नस्य, गण्डूष, कवल और धूम

questions.q: Match each word of unit 32 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words carry the unit's terms.
questions.rule: अञ्जन = collyrium; नस्य = nasal remedy; कवल = mouthful; उत्क्लेशित = stirred up.
questions.teaches: उत्क्लेशित is the participle of ut-√kliś, stirred up.
questions.section: अंजन, नस्य, गण्डूष, कवल और धूम

questions.q: Which split of नावनेरितम् is right?
optionExplain: इ + ई would give ई, not ए.
रितम् is not a word.
Right: अ + ई gives ए, so नावन + ईरितम् is written नावनेरितम्: set in motion by nasal administration.
एरितम् is not a word of the card.
questions.explain: नावनेरितम् = नावन (nasal administration) + ईरितम् (set in motion).
questions.section: अंजन, नस्य, गण्डूष, कवल और धूम

questions.q: Which two words of unit 32 are instrumental plurals?
optionExplain: Right: n. inst. pl., by nasyas.
Right: m. inst. pl., by mouthfuls.
This is a neuter accusative singular participle.
This is also a neuter accusative singular participle.
questions.explain: The -ऐः endings mark the two instrumental plurals.
questions.section: अंजन, नस्य, गण्डूष, कवल और धूम

questions.q: Which is the instrumental plural of फल (fruit), meaning by fruits?
optionExplain: That is the instrumental singular, by a fruit.
That is the nominative plural, fruits.
That is the locative plural, in fruits.
Right: A stem in -अ takes -ऐः in the instrumental plural, like नस्यैः and कवलैः.
questions.explain: The pattern of नस्यैः and कवलैः gives फलैः.
questions.teaches: A stem in -अ forms the instrumental plural in -ऐः (by Xs).
questions.section: अंजन, नस्य, गण्डूष, कवल और धूम

questions.q: What does unit 33 say perfumes, garlands and the like do?
options: They stir up vāta and kapha
They are to be given up
optionExplain: Right: गन्धमाल्यादिकम् ... अलक्ष्मीघ्नम्: destroying misfortune.
Nothing like this is said.
Nothing like this is said.
The unit calls them an adornment.
questions.explain: The unit calls them promoting virility, destroying misfortune, and an adornment.
questions.section: अंजन, नस्य, गण्डूष, कवल और धूम

questions.q: Put the subject and three descriptions of statement (b) in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Perfumes and garlands come first, then virility-promoting, misfortune-destroying, adornment.
questions.section: अंजन, नस्य, गण्डूष, कवल और धूम

questions.q: Match each word of unit 33 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words carry the unit's key terms.
questions.rule: वृष्य = promoting virility; अलक्ष्मीघ्न = destroying misfortune; प्रसाधन = adornment; क्रमात् = in order.
questions.teaches: अलक्ष्मीघ्न is a compound: अलक्ष्मी (misfortune) + घ्न (destroying).
questions.section: अंजन, नस्य, गण्डूष, कवल और धूम

questions.q: Which split of कवलोत्क्लिष्टम् is right?
optionExplain: The word is कवल, the base ends in अ.
Right: अ + उ gives ओ, so कवल + उत्क्लिष्टम् is written कवलोत्क्लिष्टम्: stirred up by mouthfuls.
त्क्लिष्टम् is not a word.
ओत्क्लिष्टम् is not a word of the card.
questions.explain: कवलोत्क्लिष्टम् = कवल (mouthful) + उत्क्लिष्टम् (stirred up).
questions.section: अंजन, नस्य, गण्डूष, कवल और धूम

questions.q: In statement (a) of unit 33, what is one to overcome in order?
optionExplain: Pitta is not named in the unit.
Pitta is not named in the unit.
Right: वातकफं जयेत्: one should overcome vāta and kapha.
Neither is named in the unit.
questions.explain: जयेत् has वातकफम् as its object, and क्रमात् means in order.
questions.section: अंजन, नस्य, गण्डूष, कवल और धूम

questions.q: What would शोकघ्नम् (like अलक्ष्मीघ्नम्) mean?
optionExplain: -घ्न does not mean born of.
That is the opposite of destroying.
That would be a word like शोकरहित.
Right: X-घ्न means destroying X.
questions.explain: अलक्ष्मीघ्नम् is destroying misfortune, so शोकघ्नम् is destroying sorrow.
questions.teaches: The ending -घ्न after a noun means destroying that thing.
questions.section: अंजन, नस्य, गण्डूष, कवल और धूम

questions.q: Which garment does unit 34 say one should not wear?
optionExplain: Right: मलिनम्: dirty.
The unit forbids the dirty, not the clean.
The unit forbids the worn-out, not the new.
The unit forbids the showy, not the plain.
questions.explain: The garment faults are worn out, dirty, red, showy.
questions.rule: Not worn out, dirty, red or showy.

questions.q: Put the four faults of the garment in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Line 1 lists worn out, dirty, red, showy.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 34 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words carry the faults of the garment.
questions.rule: जीर्ण = worn out; मलिन = dirty; रक्त = red; उल्बण = showy.
questions.teaches: Four adjectives in one line list the faults of the garment, all in the accusative singular neuter.

questions.q: Which split of जलजादृते is right?
optionExplain: The card's word is जलजात्, in the ablative with ऋते.
Right: त् before a vowel becomes द्: जलजात् + ऋते → जलजादृते, 'except water-born'.
जलजान् is not a word of the card.
अदृते is not a word of the card.
questions.explain: जलजादृते = जलजात् (from the water-born) + ऋते (except).
questions.rule: ऋते takes the ablative: जलजात् ऋते.

questions.q: Which are named in unit 34 as faults?
optionExplain: Right: जीर्णम्.
Right: मलिनम्.
Right: उल्बणम्.
Silk is not mentioned.
questions.explain: Three garment faults are named; silk is not.

questions.q: How is नरः + गच्छेत् written when joined?
optionExplain: A visarga after अ does not stay before a voiced consonant.
आ does not replace अः here.
Right: अः before a voiced consonant becomes ओ, as in वासो न.
The visarga becomes ओ; it is not dropped.
questions.explain: The same rule that gives वासो न gives नरो गच्छेत्.
questions.teaches: The visarga after अ becomes ओ before a voiced consonant; use it for any new phrase.

questions.q: Unit 35 says one should not wear cloth, a flower or sandals in what condition?
options: Not yet washed clean by water
Torn at the edge of the cloth
optionExplain: Washing is not mentioned in the unit.
Tearing is not mentioned in the unit.
Buying is not mentioned in the unit.
Right: अन्येन विधृतम्: worn by another.
questions.explain: The prohibition is of things already worn by another.
questions.rule: Not cloth, flower or sandals worn by another.

questions.q: Put the three things not to wear, as listed in line 1, in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Line 1 reads cloth, flower, pair of sandals.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 35 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words carry the unit's two sentences.
questions.rule: अन्येन = by another; विधृतम् = worn; उपानहौ = pair of sandals; इच्छन् = desiring.
questions.teaches: उपानहौ is dual (a pair); इच्छन् is a present participle, desiring.

questions.q: Which split of नैव is right?
optionExplain: Right: अ + ए gives ऐ, so न + एव is written नैव: not indeed.
इ + ए would give ये, not ऐ.
व is not a word.
ऐव is not a word of the card.
questions.explain: नैव = न (not) + एव (indeed).

questions.q: Which does the one in line 2 of unit 35 desire?
optionExplain: Right: रुचि.
Right: वैशद्य.
Right: सौगन्ध्य.
Wealth is not named in the unit.
questions.explain: The three desired things are relish, clarity and fragrance.

questions.q: How is सदा + एव (ever, indeed) written when joined?
optionExplain: ए alone would drop the long vowel; the join gives ऐ.
Right: आ + ए gives ऐ, as अ + ए does in नैव.
The two vowels join; they do not stand apart.
ओ comes from अ/आ + उ/ऊ, not from अ/आ + ए.
questions.explain: The same rule that gives नैव gives सदैव.
questions.teaches: अ or आ followed by ए joins into ऐ; use it for any new phrase.

questions.q: What does line 2 of unit 36 call pleasing and accompanied by pūga-fruit?
optionExplain: Garlands are in unit 34.
Sandals are in unit 35, line 1.
Right: ताम्बूलीनां किसलयं हृद्यं पूगफलान्वितम्.
Warm water is in unit 30.
questions.explain: The leaf is the subject: tender, pleasing, with pūga-fruit.

questions.q: Put the four phrases of line 2 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Line 2 reads of the tāmbūlī, tender leaf, pleasing, with pūga-fruit.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 36 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words carry the structure of the unit.
questions.rule: किसलयम् = tender leaf; हृद्यम् = pleasing; अन्वितम् = accompanied by; सह = together with.
questions.teaches: अन्वित at the end of a compound means accompanied by the first part.

questions.q: Which split of पूगफलान्वितम् is right?
optionExplain: इ + अ would give य, not आ.
Neither part is a word.
एन्वितम् is not a word of the card.
Right: अ + अ gives आ, so पूगफल + अन्वितम् is written पूगफलान्वितम्.
questions.explain: पूगफलान्वितम् = पूगफल (pūga-fruit) + अन्वितम् (accompanied by).

questions.q: Where does the verb of unit 36 (hold in the mouth) come from?
optionExplain: Right: Unit 36 has no verb; the card notes that 35.2 and 36 form one sentence.
Line 1 has only names and सह.
जयेत् means one should overcome.
आचरेत् means one should practise, and it belongs to unit 31.
questions.explain: 35.2 gives धारयेत्, and unit 36 gives what is held.

questions.q: Which form means accompanied by fruit?
optionExplain: That means devoid of fruit.
Right: X + अन्वितम् means accompanied by X; अ + अ gives आ.
That means without fruit.
That means born of fruit.
questions.explain: The pattern of पूगफलान्वितम् gives फलान्वितम्.
questions.teaches: A compound ending in अन्वित means accompanied by the first member.

questions.q: Unit 37 calls that thing (तत्) what, for the persons it lists?
optionExplain: Unit 38 calls it suitable for other persons.
The unit limits it to the listed persons.
Right: अपथ्यं शोषिणां च तत्: that is unsuitable.
हृद्यम् is said of the leaf in unit 36, not here.
questions.explain: The unit says अपथ्यम्, unsuitable.
questions.rule: तत् = unsuitable for the listed persons.

questions.q: Put the four afflictions of line 2 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Line 2 reads poison, fainting, intoxication, and then wasting (śoṣa).

questions.q: Match each word of unit 37 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words carry line 2.
questions.rule: विष = poison; मूर्च्छा = fainting; मद = intoxication; शोष = wasting.
questions.teaches: These are the afflictions of line 2; the unit gives them as terms, without cause or treatment.

questions.q: Which split of विषमूर्च्छामदार्त्तानाम् is right?
optionExplain: विषम would mean uneven, and ऊर्च्छा is not a word.
आमद is not a word of the card.
Neither of the last two parts is a word.
Right: अ + आ gives आ: मद + आर्त्तानाम् → मदार्त्तानाम्: of those afflicted by poison, fainting, intoxication.
questions.explain: The compound is poison, fainting, intoxication, afflicted.

questions.q: For which persons does unit 37 call that unsuitable?
optionExplain: Right: विष...आर्त्तानाम्.
Right: कुपितचक्षुषाम्.
Right: शोषिणाम्.
Unit 38 calls it suitable for such a person.
questions.explain: Poison, irritated eyes and śoṣa are named in unit 37; the bathed person is in unit 38.
questions.rule: Unit 37: unsuitable for the listed persons; unit 38: suitable after sleep, eating, bathing, vomiting.

questions.q: What does ज्वरार्त्तानाम् (like मदार्त्तानाम्) mean?
optionExplain: Right: X-आर्त्त means afflicted by X, and -आनाम् is the genitive plural.
-आनाम् is the genitive plural, not the instrumental.
-आर्त्त means afflicted, not overcoming.
The compound puts fever first: afflicted by fever.
questions.explain: The pattern of मदार्त्तानाम् gives 'of those afflicted by fever'.
questions.rule: X-आर्त्त + आनाम् = of those afflicted by X.
questions.teaches: X-आर्त्त means afflicted by X; the ending -आनाम् is the genitive plural (of those).

questions.q: For which person does unit 38 call that thing suitable (पथ्यम्)?
options: One who has run a long way
One who has risen from sleep
One who has kept a fast
One who has gone to sleep at night
optionExplain: Running is not mentioned in the unit.
Right: सुप्तोत्थिते: for one who has risen from sleep.
Fasting is not mentioned in the unit.
The unit says risen from sleep.
questions.explain: Unit 38 names four states: risen from sleep, eaten, bathed, vomited.
questions.rule: पथ्य after sleep, eating, bathing, vomiting.

questions.q: Put the four states of the person in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Line 1 reads risen from sleep, eaten, bathed, vomited.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 38 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Each state is a locative singular, 'in the case of'.
questions.rule: सुप्तोत्थिते, भुक्ते, स्नाते, वान्ते are four locatives.
questions.teaches: A past participle in the locative, with a noun, means in the case of a person who has done it.

questions.q: Which split of सुप्तोत्थिते is right?
optionExplain: The first part is सुप्त, ending in अ.
ए is not what joins here.
Right: अ + उ gives ओ, so सुप्त + उत्थिते is written सुप्तोत्थिते: risen from sleep.
ओत्थिते is not a word of the card.
questions.explain: सुप्तोत्थिते = सुप्त (asleep) + उत्थिते (risen).

questions.q: Which are named in line 2 of unit 38?
optionExplain: Right: द्विपत्रम्.
Right: एकं पूगम्.
Right: सचूर्णखदिरम्.
Honey is not named in the unit.
questions.explain: Line 2 names a pair of leaves, one pūga, and powder with khadira.

questions.q: Which phrase means in the case of a person who has gone?
optionExplain: That is accusative: a person who has gone, as an object.
That is nominative: the person who has gone, as subject.
That is dative: for the person gone.
Right: A participle in the locative with a noun in the locative, as भुक्ते मानवे.
questions.explain: The pattern of भुक्ते मानवे gives गते मानवे.
questions.rule: Locative participle + locative noun = in the case of X.
questions.teaches: Participle and noun both in the locative mean in the case of a person who has done it.

questions.q: Line 2 of unit 39 calls even a long life censured when what is lacking?
options: The means are not at hand
Children are not near at hand
Friends are not near at hand
Health is not near at hand
optionExplain: Right: असन्निहितसाधनम्: having no means at hand.
Children are not mentioned in the line.
Friends are not mentioned in the line.
Health is not mentioned in the line.
questions.explain: The line says a long life is censured if the means are not at hand.
questions.rule: दीर्घ आयु also निन्दित without साधन.

questions.q: Put the five parts of line 2 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The line reads censured, long, even, life, having no means at hand.

questions.q: Match each word of line 2 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words carry the sentence.
questions.rule: निन्दित = censured; दीर्घ = long; आयुः = life; साधन = means.
questions.teaches: साधन is the means; असन्निहित-साधन is a bahuvrīhi: having no means at hand.

questions.q: Which split of दीर्घमप्यायुः is right?
optionExplain: मप्य is not a word.
Right: म् joins the next vowel, and इ + आ gives या: अपि + आयुः → अप्यायुः.
अप्य is not a word of the card.
यायुः is not a word.
questions.explain: दीर्घमप्यायुः = दीर्घम् (long) + अपि (even) + आयुः (life).

questions.q: The word for 'life' in line 2 of unit 39 is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: आयुः, the last member of दीर्घमप्यायुः, means life.
questions.teaches: आयुः = life.

questions.q: What does अप्राप्तधनः (like असन्निहितसाधनम्) mean?
options: One who has already obtained wealth
One whose wealth is not obtained
optionExplain: The prefix अ- negates, so it is the opposite.
That would be प्राप्तधनम्.
Right: अ- negates: अप्राप्त + धन, a bahuvrīhi, one whose wealth is not obtained.
No giving is in the word.
questions.explain: असन्निहितसाधनम् = a-sannihita-sādhanam, having no means at hand; अप्राप्तधनः has the same shape.
questions.rule: अ- + participle + noun = one whose X is not ... .
questions.teaches: A bahuvrīhi with negative अ- describes one whose thing is not present or obtained.

questions.q: Which of these does the verse name for one who desires wealth?
optionExplain: Not named in the verse.
Not named in the verse.
Not named in the verse.
Right: कृषिम् is the first item of the list.
questions.explain: The list begins with कृषिं वणिज्यां गोरक्षाम्: agriculture, trade, cattle-keeping.
questions.rule: धनार्थी resorts to कृषि, वणिज्या, गोरक्षा, a virtuous king.

questions.q: Put the four things to resort to in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The verse runs: agriculture, trade, cattle-keeping, a virtuous king.

questions.q: The verse's word for 'agriculture' is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters)?
questions.explain: कृषिम् (accusative) is the first thing the wealth-seeker resorts to.
questions.teaches: Each item of the list stands in the accusative (कृषिम्, वणिज्याम्, गोरक्षाम्) because it is what one resorts to (संश्रयेत्).

questions.q: Which is the right split of गोरक्षामुपायैः?
optionExplain: Right: Final म् takes the next vowel: म् + उ gives मु.
मुपायैः is not a word.
आमुपायैः is not a word.
A visarga would not turn into म.
questions.explain: गोरक्षाम् (cattle-keeping, accusative) + उपायैः (by means).
questions.rule: Final म् + vowel: the म् joins the vowel (गोरक्षाम् + उपायैः = गोरक्षामुपायैः).

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words carry the sense of the verse: who, what he does, and the two objects described.
questions.rule: धनार्थी = one desiring wealth; संश्रयेत् = should resort to; गुणिनम् = virtuous; क्रियाम् = activity, occupation.

questions.q: Built like धनार्थी, what does विद्यार्थी mean?
optionExplain: The ending -अर्थी is about wanting, not giving.
Right: -अर्थी at the end of a compound means one who desires the first part.
That would not name a person who wants something.
Nothing in the ending means 'without'.
questions.explain: धन-अर्थी is 'one desiring wealth'; विद्या-अर्थी in the same way is 'one desiring knowledge'.
questions.teaches: A compound ending in -अर्थी names the person who desires the first part (धनार्थी, विद्यार्थी).

questions.q: What does मुक्तवेगः say about the person?
options: He is carried by the urges
optionExplain: मुक्त does not mean hidden.
Nothing like this is in the word.
Right: मुक्त = released and वेग = urge.
मुक्त means freed from, not carried by.
questions.explain: मुक्तवेगः is a compound: the one who has released the urges.
questions.rule: मुक्त-वेगः = one who has released the urges.

questions.q: Match each readable word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words are readable in the print.
questions.rule: मुक्तवेगः = having released the urges; पाणिना = with the hand; निष्क्रामेत् = should go out; वेग = urge.

questions.q: Which part of this unit does the card mark as unreadable?
optionExplain: This is clear: should go out.
This is clear: with the hand.
This is clear: having released the urges.
Right: गमनखमाहारसमास्त्रियः has no reading.
questions.explain: Only the second word of line 1 is garbled; the card builds on the clear words only.
questions.rule: Where the print is garbled, the card says so and nothing is built on it.
questions.teaches: When a word is garbled in the print, the card marks it and the questions use only the readable words.

questions.q: Which is the right split of निष्क्रामेद्देव-?
optionExplain: Right: Final त् becomes द् before the voiced द: त् + द gives द्द.
A visarga would not give द्द.
That would not end the verb in -एत्.
द्देव is not a word.
questions.explain: निष्क्रामेत् (should go out) + देव- (the first member of the last compound).
questions.rule: त् + voiced consonant → द्: निष्क्रामेत् + देव = निष्क्रामेद्देव.

questions.q: Put these three readable parts in the order of the unit.
questions.explain: Line 1 begins with the released urges; line 2 has the hand and then the going out.

questions.q: Built like मुक्तवेगः, what does मुक्तक्रोधः mean?
options: One who is full of anger
One who has let go of anger
One who is about to be angry
optionExplain: मुक्त means released, not filled.
Right: मुक्त-X at the start of a bahuvrīhi names one who has released X.
A bahuvrīhi names the person, not the anger.
Nothing like 'about to' is in the word.
questions.explain: Like मुक्त-वेगः, one who has released the urges, मुक्त-क्रोधः is one who has released anger.
questions.rule: मुक्त-X = one who has released X.
questions.teaches: A bahuvrīhi that begins with मुक्त names the one who has released the second member (मुक्तवेगः, मुक्तक्रोधः).

questions.q: How far ahead does the verse say one should look while walking?
optionExplain: The verse limits the sight, it does not extend it.
The verse names a measure, a yoke's length, not the ground.
Right: युगमात्रदृक् means looking a yoke's length ahead.
Nothing like this is in the verse.
questions.explain: युगमात्र-दृक् is looking only a yoke's length ahead.
questions.rule: युगमात्रदृक् = looking a yoke's length ahead.

questions.q: Put the three things for the night walk in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Line 2 gives the staff, the head-dress and the companion in this order.

questions.q: Which is the right split of चात्यधिके?
optionExplain: त्यधिके is not a word.
आति is not a word in the verse; the verse has अति.
यधिके is not a word.
Right: अ + अ gives आ in चाति; इ before अ becomes य् in त्यधि.
questions.explain: च (and) + अति (exceedingly) + अधिके (pressing, in a task).
questions.rule: अ + अ → आ (च + अति = चाति); इ + अ → य (ति + अधि = त्यधि).
questions.teaches: Two sandhi meet here: अ + अ gives आ, and इ before a different vowel becomes य्.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Each word is a describing word for the walker.
questions.rule: सातपत्रपदत्राणः, युगमात्रदृक्, दंडी and सहायवान् all describe the walker.

questions.q: A task at night is exceedingly pressing. What does the verse give the walker?
options: A lamp, a drum and a dog
A staff alone, going without company
optionExplain: Right: That is line 2.
That is line 1, not the night rule.
None of these is named.
The verse names a companion.
questions.explain: At night, when the business is exceedingly pressing, the verse names a staff, a head-dress and a companion.
questions.rule: रात्रि + अत्यधिक कार्य: दंडी, मौली, सहायवान्.

questions.q: Built like सातपत्र (with an umbrella), what does सपुस्तकः छात्रः mean?
options: A student who gives a book
optionExplain: स- means with, not without.
Right: स- at the start of a bahuvrīhi means 'with'.
A bahuvrīhi describes the person, not a book.
Nothing in स- means giving.
questions.explain: स-पुस्तकः is 'with a book', as सातपत्र is 'with an umbrella'.
questions.teaches: A bahuvrīhi that begins with स- (सातपत्र…) describes someone who has X with him.

questions.q: When does the verse say one should go about covered?
optionExplain: By day the verse says not with the head covered.
Midday is not named in this unit.
Right: रात्रौ पर्यटेत् is paired with प्रावृत्य.
Dawn is not named in this unit.
questions.explain: The verse says to go about covered at night, and by day not with the head covered.
questions.rule: रात्रौ प्रावृत्य; अहनि न प्रावृत्य शिरः.

questions.q: Put these phrases of line 1 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The line runs: having covered, one should roam, at night, not having covered the head, by day.
questions.rule: प्रावृत्य पर्यटेत् · रात्रौ · न प्रावृत्य शिरः · अहनि.

questions.q: Which gives the join in शिरोऽहनि?
optionExplain: ए + अ would give शिरेऽहनि.
आ + अ would give शिराहनि.
हनि is not the word here; the word is अहनि.
Right: अः + अ gives ओ followed by an avagraha (ऽ).
questions.explain: शिरः (head) + अहनि (by day).
questions.teaches: A visarga after अ, before अ, becomes ओ and the following अ is shown by ऽ (शिरः + अहनि = शिरोऽहनि).

questions.q: A translation says: 'At night go about covered; by day, with the head covered.' What is wrong?
options: By day the verse says not
At night the verse says uncovered
The verse speaks of evening, not night
optionExplain: Right: न प्रावृत्य शिरः अहनि.
The verse says covered at night.
पर्यटेत् is a verb of going about.
The word is रात्रौ, at night.
questions.explain: The day rule has न: by day one should not go with the head covered.
questions.rule: अहनि = by day; न प्रावृत्य शिरः = not with the head covered.

questions.q: Which does line 2 of this unit name?
optionExplain: भस्म.
तुष.
अशुचि.
That is in unit 44.
Not named.
questions.explain: Line 2 names ashes, husks and impure things (after the shadows); gravel is in the next unit.

questions.q: Built like प्रावृत्य, which form means having sat down (from उप + विश्)?
optionExplain: -त्वा goes on a verb without a prefix.
Right: A prefixed verb forms its 'having done' word in -य.
This means 'should sit down'.
This means 'sits down'.
questions.explain: प्रावृत्य (प्र + आ + वृ) ends in -य; the prefixed उप + विश् does likewise: उपविश्य.
questions.teaches: A verb with a prefix forms its 'having done' word in -य (प्रावृत्य, उपविश्य); a plain verb takes -त्वा.

questions.q: What must one not do to the ground of gravel, clods, offerings and bathing?
optionExplain: The verb is आक्रमेत्, step upon.
Nothing like sweeping is in the verse.
Right: न आक्रमेत् = should not step upon.
Nothing like digging is in the verse.
questions.explain: आक्रमेत् is should step upon, and न forbids it.
questions.rule: न आक्रमेत् = should not step upon.

questions.q: Put the times of line 2 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Line 2 names midday, the two twilights, night and midnight.

questions.q: In नाक्रमेच्छर्करा-, what happens to the final त् of आक्रमेत् before श?
optionExplain: That is not how this sandhi works.
द् stands before voiced sounds; श is unvoiced.
न् is for a following nasal.
Right: The त् is replaced by च् and the श by छ.
questions.explain: न + आक्रमेत् + शर्करा joins as नाक्रमेच्छर्करा.
questions.teaches: Final त् before श becomes च् and the श becomes छ (आक्रमेत् + शर्करा = आक्रमेच्छर्करा).

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are the nouns of the unit.
questions.rule: शर्करा = gravel; लोष्ट = clod; बलि = offering; चतुष्पथम् = crossroads.

questions.q: Which times does line 2 name?
optionExplain: मध्याह्ने.
संध्ययोः.
अर्धरात्रे.
Not named.
Not named.
questions.explain: Line 2 names midday, the two twilights, night and midnight; neither the full-moon day nor the rainy season.

questions.q: Built like रात्रौ (at night), what form means in the fire, from अग्नि?
optionExplain: Right: Some -इ nouns, like अग्नि, take -औ in the locative singular.
This is the dative, 'to the fire'.
This is the instrumental, 'by the fire'.
This is 'of/from the fire'.
questions.explain: रात्रि → रात्रौ (locative); अग्नि → अग्नौ.
questions.teaches: Some -इ nouns (अग्नि, रात्रि) have the locative singular in -औ (रात्रौ, अग्नौ).

questions.q: Which places does the verse say not to resort to even by day?
options: Rivers, gardens, markets, temples and open fields nearby
Slaughterhouse, forest, empty house, cremation ground
Trees, shrines and courtyards, which are in line 1
Roads, fields, wells, bridges, ferries and market squares
optionExplain: None of these is named.
Right: Line 2 lists these after दिवाऽपि न.
These are in line 1.
None of these is named.
questions.explain: Line 2 lists सूना, अटवी, शून्यगृह and श्मशान, with 'even by day'.
questions.rule: दिवाऽपि न: सूना, अटवी, शून्यगृह, श्मशान.

questions.q: Put the places of line 2 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Line 2 lists slaughterhouse, forest, empty house, cremation ground.

questions.q: Which is the right split of दिवाऽपि?
optionExplain: That would be written दिवोऽपि.
आपि is not a word here; the verse has अपि.
Right: आ before अ stays आ; the printed ऽ only marks the dropped अ.
The word is दिवा, without a visarga.
questions.explain: दिवा (by day) + अपि (even): दिवाऽपि, even by day.
questions.rule: आ + अ → आ; ऽ marks the dropped अ.
questions.teaches: आ before अ stays आ; the printed ऽ only marks the elided अ (दिवा + अपि = दिवाऽपि).

questions.q: Which does line 1 name?
optionExplain: वृक्ष.
चैत्य.
चत्वर.
That is in line 2.
That is in line 2.
questions.explain: Line 1 names trees, shrines and the courtyard; the cremation ground and slaughterhouse are in line 2.

questions.q: Asha is at an empty house at noon. What does this unit say?
options: Only at night is it forbidden
Not to be resorted to, even by day
optionExplain: The line says even by day.
Midnight is in unit 44, not here.
The verse says even by day not.
Right: शून्यगृह is in line 2 with दिवाऽपि न.

questions.q: Built like शून्यगृह (empty house), what does शून्यनगर mean?
optionExplain: Right: शून्य- at the start of a compound says 'empty'.
The first member describes the second as empty.
शून्य does not mean full.
Nothing in शून्य means new.
questions.explain: शून्य-गृह is an empty house; शून्य-नगर is an empty city.
questions.teaches: A compound that begins with शून्य- names an empty X (शून्यगृह, शून्यनगर).

questions.q: What does the verse say one should not utter at Śiva, the venerable and auspicious things?

Nothing about a name is in the verse.
Nothing about a blessing is in the verse.

questions.rule: न हुंकुर्यात् = should not utter huṃ.

questions.q: Put the four objects of the first line in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The line runs: Śiva, the venerable, the praised, auspicious things.

questions.q: Which is the right split of नापसव्यम्?
optionExplain: पसव्यम् is not a word.
That word is not in the verse.
Right: न + अ gives ना.
The word is अपसव्यम्, left-wise, not सव्यम् alone.

questions.teaches: A न before a word that begins with अ joins with it as ना (नापसव्यम्).

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words carry the two prohibitions.
questions.rule: हुंकुर्यात् = should utter huṃ; पूज्यम् = the venerable; प्रशस्तान् = the praised; अपसव्यम् = left-wise.

questions.q: Ravi says huṃ aloud at a venerable one (पूज्यम्). What does this unit say?

It is allowed: only auspicious things are named

It is forbidden: the venerable is named
optionExplain: पूज्यम् is also named.
पूज्यम् is also named.
The verse forbids it.
Right: न हुंकुर्यात् … पूज्यम्.

questions.rule: न हुंकुर्यात् + शिवम्, पूज्यम्, प्रशस्तान्, मङ्गलानि.

questions.q: Built like न हुंकुर्यात्, which phrase means one should not speak?
optionExplain: Right: न with an optative says 'should not'.
This says 'should speak'.
This is a past form, 'spoke'.
This is a future form, 'will speak'.

questions.q: What does the verse say one should do to a crossroads?
optionExplain: Nothing like this is in the verse.
Right: चतुष्पथं नमस्कुर्यात्.

Nothing like this is in the verse.

questions.rule: चतुष्पथं नमस्कुर्यात् = one should bow to a crossroads.

questions.q: Put the six names of line 2 in the order of the verse.

questions.rule: व्याल · व्याधित · अशस्त · अदान्त · क्षुत् · पिपासित.

questions.q: Which is the right split of नादान्त-?
optionExplain: The verse has the particle न, not ना.
आदान्त is not the word of the verse.
Right: न + अ gives ना.
That does not give अदान्त (untamed).

questions.rule: अ + अ → आ: न + अदान्त = नादान्त.
questions.teaches: न + a word beginning with अ joins as ना, and the अ- is the 'not' of the word itself (अदान्त = untamed).

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words are in line 2.
questions.rule: व्याल = fierce; व्याधित = sick; अदान्त = untamed; पिपासित = thirsty.

questions.q: Which does line 2 name?
optionExplain: व्याधित.
क्षुत्.
पिपासित.
Not named in line 2.
Not named in line 2.
questions.explain: Line 2 names the sick, the hungry and the thirsty; not the aged or the learned.
questions.rule: Line 2: व्याल, व्याधित, अशस्त, अदान्त, क्षुत्, पिपासित.

questions.q: Built like अशस्तैः (with the ill-regarded), which form means with good people?
optionExplain: This is the singular, 'with a good person'.
This is the accusative plural, 'good people' as objects.
This is the nominative plural, 'good people' as doers.
Right: A masculine -अ noun takes -ऐः in the instrumental plural.
questions.explain: अशस्तैः is the instrumental plural of an -अ noun; सज्जनैः is the same form of सज्जन.
questions.teaches: The instrumental plural of a masculine -अ noun ends in -ऐः (अशस्तैः, सज्जनैः) and means 'with several …'.

questions.q: What does the verse say about the time when the sun is in mid-sky?

optionExplain: Right: न नभोमध्यगे रवौ, with न व्रजेत् carried over.
The verse forbids going, it does not urge haste.
Bathing is not mentioned.
Prayer is not mentioned.
questions.explain: The line ends with न नभोमध्यगे रवौ: not when the sun has gone to mid-sky.
questions.rule: न नभोमध्यगे रवौ = not when the sun is in mid-sky.

questions.q: Put the three conditions of line 2 in the order of the verse.

questions.q: What does अति- add in अतिसायम् and अतिपङ्के?
optionExplain: The negative here is the separate न.
Right: अति-सायम् is very late in the evening; अति-पङ्के is in deep mud.
Nothing in the glosses says 'before'.
Nothing in the glosses says 'near'.
questions.explain: अति- means very or excessively: deep mud, very late evening.
questions.teaches: The prefix अति- at the start of a word adds 'very, too much' (अतिपङ्के, अतिसायम्).

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.

questions.q: Raju plans to go on a cow's back. What does this unit say?
options: It is fine by day but not at night
It is fine unless the cow's tail is cut
One should not go on a cow's back
It is fine in deep mud
optionExplain: The verse gives no such limit.

questions.q: Built like नभोमध्यगे रवौ (when the sun is in mid-sky), which phrase means when the sun has risen?
optionExplain: Both are accusative, 'the risen sun' as an object.
Both are instrumental, 'by the risen sun'.
Both are nominative, 'the sun is risen' as a statement.
Right: Noun and describing word both in the locative: 'when …'.
questions.explain: नभोमध्यगे रवौ has noun and describing word in the locative singular; उदिते सूर्ये does the same.
questions.rule: Noun + describing word both in the locative = 'when …'.
questions.teaches: A noun and a describing word in the locative together mean 'when X is …' (रवौ नभोमध्यगे, सूर्ये उदिते).

questions.q: With whom does the verse say one should not go?
optionExplain: Right: न शत्रुणा सह.
Not named.
Not named.
Not named in this unit.

questions.q: Put the four items of line 2 in the order of the verse.

questions.q: Which is the right split of नैकः?
optionExplain: The word is न, not ना.
Right: अ + ए gives ऐ: न + एकः = नैकः.
ए + ए does not give नै.
ऐकः is not the word here.
questions.explain: न (not) + एकः (alone).
questions.teaches: A short अ meeting ए joins as ऐ (न + एकः = नैकः).

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.

questions.q: Which does line 1 say one should not do?
optionExplain: असन्निहितपानीयः.
अतितूर्णम्.
संततम्.
Not named.
Not named.
questions.explain: The first line names no water at hand, too hurried, and continuous going; rain and a dog are not named.

questions.q: Built like असन्निहितपानीयः, what does असन्निहितदीपः mean?

One who carries a lamp far away
One who has no lamp at hand
optionExplain: A bahuvrīhi names the person, not the lamp.
Nothing about carrying is in the word.
Right: A bahuvrīhi with अ- names the person who lacks X at hand.

questions.explain: असन्निहित-पानीयः is 'one for whom water is not at hand'; असन्निहित-दीपः is the same with a lamp.
questions.rule: अ-सन्निहित-X = one without X at hand.
questions.teaches: A bahuvrīhi with असन्निहित- names the person who has no X at hand (असन्निहितपानीयः, असन्निहितदीपः).

questions.q: What does the verse say one should not do before outsiders?

questions.q: Which is the right split of नाचरेत्पुरः?
optionExplain: Right: न + आ gives ना; the verb ends in -एत्.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.

optionExplain: Drinking is named too.

Not named.

Right: नदीं तरेन्न बाहुभ्याम्.

questions.q: Put the five things in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The verse runs: river, mass of fire, rugged mountain, doubtful boat, tree.
questions.rule: नदी · अग्निस्कन्ध · विषम शैल · संशयिता नौका · तरु.

questions.q: In नाग्निस्कंधमभिब्रजेत्, which is the right split of ...स्कंधमभि-?
optionExplain: Right: Final म् takes the next vowel: स्कंधम् + अभि = स्कंधमभि.
A visarga would not give म.
भि is not the prefix; it is अभि.
मभि is not a word.
questions.explain: अग्निस्कन्धम् (mass of fire) + अभिव्रजेत् (should approach).
questions.rule: Final म् + vowel: the म् joins the vowel.
questions.teaches: A word ending in म् joins the next word's first vowel (अग्निस्कन्धम् + अभि = अग्निस्कन्धमभि).

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words carry the nouns and one describing word.
questions.rule: नदी = river; बाहुभ्याम् = with the two arms; शैल = mountain; विषम = rugged.

questions.q: Which does the verse say one should not do?
options: Cross a river with the arms
optionExplain: नदीं तरेन्न बाहुभ्याम्.
नाग्निस्कंधमभिब्रजेत्.
नारोहेद्विषमं शैलम्.
Not named.
Not named; only climbing a tree is.
questions.explain: The first three are named; lighting a lamp and cutting a tree are not.
questions.rule: River with arms, fire mass, rugged mountain.

questions.q: Built like संशयितां नावम्, which phrase means a hard-to-cross river?
optionExplain: -अम् would agree with a masculine or neuter noun.
Right: The describing word takes the same gender, number and case as the noun.
-अः is nominative masculine; नदीम् is accusative feminine.
-आः is plural; नदीम् is singular.
questions.explain: संशयिताम् (f. acc. sg.) agrees with नावम् (f. acc. sg.); दुर्गमाम् does the same with नदीम्.
questions.rule: Adjective and noun agree in gender, number and case.
questions.teaches: A describing word takes the gender, number and case of its noun (संशयितां नावम्, दुर्गमां नदीम्).

questions.q: With what does the verse say one should not bring fruit down from a tree?
optionExplain: Not named.
Not named.
Right: निपातयेन्न लोष्टेन.
Not named.
questions.explain: लोष्टेन is with a clod, and न forbids it; a fruit is also named.

questions.q: Put these parts of line 1 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Line 1 runs: should bring down, not with a clod, not with a fruit, fruit from the tree.
questions.rule: निपातयेत् · न लोष्टेन · न फलेन · फलं द्रुमात्.

questions.q: Which is the right split of निपातयेन्नलोष्टेन?
optionExplain: न्न is not a word.
A visarga would not give न्न.
The verb ends in -एत्, not -एन्.
Right: Final त् becomes न् before न.
questions.explain: निपातयेत् (should bring down) + न (not) + लोष्टेन (with a clod).
questions.teaches: Final त् before a nasal (न) becomes न् (निपातयेत् + न = निपातयेन्न).

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are the key words of the two lines.
questions.rule: द्रुमात् = from a tree; लोष्टेन = with a clod; अद्वारेण = through a non-door; प्रविशेत् = should enter.

questions.q: Which two ways of entering does the unit say are not to be used?
options: When forbidden, and by a non-door
At night, and alone, without a guide
With a companion, and with a staff
When ill, and when hungry or thirsty
optionExplain: Right: वार्यमाणः and अद्वारेण.
Neither is named.
Neither is named.
Neither is named.
questions.explain: Line 2 forbids entering when forbidden (वार्यमाणः) and through a non-door (अद्वारेण).

questions.q: Built like अद्वारेण (through a non-door), what does अपथेन mean?
optionExplain: That would be पथा, without the अ-.
Right: अ- before a noun makes 'not X'.
That is a locative, पथि.
That is an ablative, पथात्.
questions.explain: अद्वार is 'not a door'; अपथ is 'not a path', and the -एन ending is the instrumental.
questions.teaches: अ- before a noun says 'not that' (अद्वारेण, अपथेन).

questions.q: Whom does this verse say one should not wake?
options: A person who is ill and rather weak
A person who is keeping a long watch
A person who is properly asleep
A person who is eating a full meal
optionExplain: Illness is not mentioned in the verse.
Keeping watch is not mentioned; the verse speaks of sleep.
Right: युक्तनिद्रं न बोधयेत्: one should not wake the properly asleep.
Eating is not mentioned in this verse.
questions.explain: युक्तनिद्र = one duly (properly) asleep; न बोधयेत् = one should not wake.
questions.rule: युक्तनिद्रं न बोधयेत् = one should not wake a person properly asleep.

questions.q: Match each part of the body or faculty in line 2 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are five of the six items whose restlessness (चापल) is forbidden.
questions.rule: पाणि = hand; वाक् = speech; पाद = foot; नेत्र = eye; उदर = belly.

questions.q: In पाणिवाक्पाददण्डनेत्रोदरचापलम्, which items does the last word चापलम् (restlessness) apply to?
options: Only the belly, the item next to it
Only the hands and speech, the first two
Only the eyes and the belly, the last two
optionExplain: The last word is shared, not limited to its neighbour.
Nothing in the compound stops after the first two.
The compound has no break before the last two.
Right: In a long compound the last member is shared by every earlier member.
questions.explain: The six items stand in one compound, so चापलम् belongs to each of them.
questions.rule: In a compound, the final word is shared by all earlier members.
questions.teaches: In a long compound the last word (here चापलम्, restlessness) is shared by every earlier member.

questions.q: Which is the right split of नाचरेत्?
optionExplain: Right: अ + आ gives आ: न + आचरेत् is written नाचरेत्.
That would drop the prefix आ and change the word.
रेत् is not a verb form here.
ओ before आ would give अव्, written नवाचरेत्, not नाचरेत्.
questions.explain: The line is a prohibition: न (not) + आचरेत् (should indulge in).
questions.rule: अ + आ → आ: न + आचरेत् = नाचरेत्.

questions.q: Put the six items of line 2 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The compound runs: hand, speech, foot, stick, eye, belly.
questions.rule: पाणि · वाक् · पाद · दण्ड · नेत्र · उदर.

questions.q: Join न + आदद्यात् (should not take) in the way न + आचरेत् is joined. Which is right?
optionExplain: That drops the long vowel; the two vowels become one long आ.
Right: अ + आ gives आ, as in नाचरेत्.
ए is the result of अ + इ, not of अ + आ.
औ is the result of अ + औ or आ + औ, not of अ + आ.
questions.explain: अ + आ → आ: न + आदद्यात् = नादद्यात्.
questions.teaches: When a word ending in -अ meets a word beginning with आ, the two join as long आ (न + आचरेत् = नाचरेत्; न + आदद्यात् = नादद्यात्).

questions.q: How many times in the fortnight does line 1 say?
optionExplain: त्रिः means thrice, not twice.
त्रिः means thrice, not once.
Right: त्रिः पक्षस्य: three times of the fortnight.
The verse speaks of the fortnight, not of every day.
questions.explain: त्रिः is the adverb 'three times'; पक्षस्य is 'of the fortnight'.
questions.rule: त्रिः पक्षस्य = three times in a fortnight.

questions.q: Match each item of line 1 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are the four items and the frequency of line 1.
questions.rule: कच = hair; श्मश्रु = beard; नख = nails; रोम = body-hair; त्रिः = three times.

questions.q: In स्वहस्तेन, what does the ending -एन add to स्वहस्त?
options: 'one's own hand' as the thing done
optionExplain: 'Of' would be the ending -स्य, as in पक्षस्य.
'In' would be the ending -ए.
That would be the ending -म्, as in स्नानम्.
Right: -एन on a masculine a-word marks the instrument: with, by.
questions.explain: स्वहस्तेन = with one's own hand (instrumental singular).
questions.teaches: A masculine a-word with the ending -एन names the instrument: 'with, by' (स्वहस्तेन = with one's own hand).

questions.q: Which is the right split of स्नानं चानुसमाचरेत्?
optionExplain: Right: च + अनु: अ + अ gives आ, written चानु.
नुसमाचरेत् is not a word.
That breaks the verb अनुसमाचरेत् apart.
The verb begins with अ (अनु-), not आ.
questions.explain: Three words: स्नानम् (bathing), च (and), अनुसमाचरेत् (should practise regularly).
questions.rule: अ + अ → आ: च + अनु = चानु.

questions.q: Line 2 says 'not' about which two means?
optionExplain: Right: स्वहस्तेन.
Right: दन्तैः.
No razor is named in the verse.
No comb is named in the verse.
questions.explain: न स्वहस्तेन दन्तैर्वा: not with one's own hand or with the teeth.

questions.q: A new phrase says स्वपादेन गच्छेत्. What does स्वपादेन mean?
optionExplain: 'Of' would be -स्य: स्वपादस्य.
Right: -एन marks the instrument, as in स्वहस्तेन.
'In' would be -ए: स्वपादे.
A dual would end in -औ.
questions.explain: स्वपादेन is built like स्वहस्तेन: with one's own foot.
questions.teaches: The ending -एन on a masculine a-word means 'with, by' (स्वहस्तेन, स्वपादेन).

questions.q: According to this verse, when is the oil massage to be practised?
options: Right after the whole meal has been taken and finished
Only when the oil has first been gently warmed up
When the wish for food and drink has arisen
Only at the very end of the day, at night
optionExplain: The verse speaks of the wish for food, not of the meal being over.
Warming is not mentioned in the verse.
Right: अथ जातान्नपानेच्छः: then, one in whom desire for food and drink has arisen.
The verse gives no time of day.
questions.explain: जात = arisen; अन्न-पान = food and drink; इच्छा = wish.
questions.rule: जातान्नपानेच्छः = (one) in whom the wish for food and drink has arisen.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are the key words of the unit.
questions.rule: मारुतघ्न = wind-destroying; सुगन्धि = fragrant; तैल = oil; अभ्यङ्ग = oil massage; इच्छा = wish.

questions.q: मारुतघ्नैः, सुगन्धिभिः and तैलैः all end in plural instrument endings. Why do they match?
options: Each names a different tool for the massage
Each names a different person who gives the massage
They match only by a chance of sound, nothing more
They describe the oils, so they agree with them
optionExplain: They name qualities of one thing, the oils.
No person is named; the words describe the oils.
The match is grammatical agreement.
Right: A describing word agrees with its noun in case and number.
questions.explain: मारुतघ्नैः and सुगन्धिभिः describe तैलैः, so all three are instrumental plural.
questions.rule: A describing word agrees with its noun in case, number and gender.
questions.teaches: A describing word takes the case and number of the noun it describes (मारुतघ्नैः सुगन्धिभिः तैलैः, all instrumental plural).

questions.q: Which is the right split of यथर्तु?
optionExplain: Right: आ + ऋ gives अर्, so यथा + ऋतु is written यथर्तु.
The word is यथा (according to), not यथ.
रतु is not a word.
ओ before ऋ would give a different spelling.
questions.explain: यथा (according to) + ऋतु (season): according to the season.
questions.rule: अ/आ + ऋ → अर्: यथा + ऋतु = यथर्तु.

questions.q: Put these parts of the verse in order.
questions.explain: The verse names the time first, then the three qualities of the oils, then the oils, then abhyaṅga.
questions.rule: Wish for food and drink → wind-destroying → fragrant → season-pleasant → oils → abhyaṅga.

questions.q: A new phrase describes pots: ____ घटैः, with cool pots. Which word agrees with घटैः?
optionExplain: This is singular and in a different case.
Right: घटैः is instrumental plural, so the describing word is शीतलैः.
This is singular; घटैः is plural.
This is a neuter plural nominative or accusative, not instrumental.
questions.explain: Describing words agree with the noun: घटैः (instr. pl.) takes शीतलैः.
questions.rule: Describing word = same case and number as its noun.
questions.teaches: Choose the describing word that agrees with its noun in case and number, as मारुतघ्नैः agrees with तैलैः.

questions.q: In the first words of this unit, what is abhyaṅga called with regard to vāta?
options: A feeder and increaser of vāta
A measurer and weigher of vāta
A hider and keeper of vāta
optionExplain: -हा means one who destroys, not feeds.
Nothing in the word means measuring.
Right: वातहा: वात + हा, destroyer of vāta.
Nothing in the word means hiding.
questions.explain: वातहा = वात + हा: destroyer of vāta.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are the clear words of the unit.
questions.rule: वातहा = destroyer of vāta; क्लम = fatigue; श्रम = exertion; जरा = old age; अपहः = remover.

questions.q: In जरापहः, what do जरा and अपहः together mean?
options: Giver and bringer of old age
optionExplain: अपह means remover, not giver.
'Born of' would end in -ज.
Nothing in the word means equal.
Right: जरा + अपहः: आ + अ gives आ; अपह is 'remover' of what comes before.
questions.explain: जरा + अपहः = जरापहः: remover of old age.
questions.rule: X + अपहः = remover of X; आ + अ → आ.
questions.teaches: A compound ending in -अपह means 'remover of' the first part (जरापहः = remover of old age; आ + अ joins as आ).

questions.q: Which is the right split of वातहा?
optionExplain: Right: Two parts: वात (vāta) and -हा (destroyer).
That would join to वाताहा, not वातहा.
तहा is not a word.
-आ here is part of the word -हा, not a separate ending.
questions.explain: वात (vāta) + हा (destroyer): a compound with a doer word at the end.

questions.q: Put these three items of line 2 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The end of line 2 runs: fatigue, exertion, old age, then the remover.

questions.q: A new word is ज्वरहा. Built like वातहा, what does it mean?
optionExplain: -हा destroys; it does not give.
Right: X-हा = destroyer of X.
'Born of' would be -ज.
Nothing in the word means equal.
questions.explain: ज्वर + हा = destroyer of fever, as वात + हा = destroyer of vāta.
questions.teaches: A compound ending in -हा names the destroyer of the first part (वातहा, ज्वरहा).

questions.q: In touch (स्पर्शन), which is said to be predominant?
optionExplain: Fire is not named in the verse.
Water is not named in the verse.
Right: स्पर्शने अभ्यधिको वायुः: in touch, wind is predominant.
Pitta is not named in this verse.
questions.explain: अभ्यधिकः = predominant; वायुः = wind.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are the key words of the two lines.
questions.rule: चर्म = leather; घट = pot; वायु = wind; त्वक् = skin; स्पर्शन = sense of touch.

questions.q: What does -वत् add in रथाक्षचर्मघटवत्?
options: It means 'because of', giving a reason
It means 'without', denying the three things
It means 'many', counting the three things
It means 'like': like an axle, leather and a pot
optionExplain: A reason would need a word such as यस्मात्.
'Without' is not what -वत् adds.
-वत् is not a counting word here.
Right: -वत् at the end of a word makes a comparison: 'like'.
questions.explain: The simile compares the benefits with those of an axle, leather and a pot.
questions.teaches: The ending -वत् makes a comparison: 'like' (घटवत् = like a pot).

questions.q: Why is it written अभ्यधिको वायुः and not अभ्यधिकः वायुः?
options: A final -अः becomes -ओ before a voiced consonant
The word अभ्यधिकः changes its meaning before वायुः
The visarga drops with no change before वायुः
The visarga turns to र् before वायुः
optionExplain: Right: अभ्यधिकः + वायुः: ः after अ turns to ओ before व.
Only the spelling changes, not the meaning.
After अ it becomes ओ; it does not simply drop.
र् stands after other vowels, not after अ.
questions.explain: Sandhi: अः + voiced sound → ओ.

questions.q: Which two statements does line 2 make?
options: The sense of touch rests on the skin
The skin rests on the sense of touch
optionExplain: Right: स्पर्शने अभ्यधिको वायुः.
Right: स्पर्शनं त्वगाश्रयम्.
The verse says the reverse.
The verse does not say that; the skin is the seat of touch.
questions.explain: Wind is predominant in touch; touch has the skin as its seat.
questions.rule: वायु in touch; touch on the skin.

questions.q: A new phrase says सिंहवत् तिष्ठेत्. What does सिंहवत् mean?
optionExplain: 'From' would be the ending -आत् or -तः.
Right: -वत् makes 'like', as in घटवत्.
-वत् does not mean without.
'Of' would be -स्य: सिंहस्य.
questions.explain: सिंहवत् = like a lion, built like घटवत्.
questions.teaches: A word plus -वत् means 'like' it (घटवत्, सिंहवत्).

questions.q: On which three parts does the verse say abhyaṅga is to be practised especially?
optionExplain: These are not the three named.
These are not the three named.
Right: शिरःश्रवणपादेषु: on the head, ears and feet.
These are not the three named.
questions.explain: शिरः = head; श्रवण = ear; पाद = foot; विशेषेण = especially.
questions.rule: शिरःश्रवणपादेषु = on the head, ears and feet.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words carry the reasoning and the stress of the unit.
questions.rule: त्वच्य = good for the skin; परम् = supremely; यस्मात् = because; अतः = therefore; विशेषेण = especially.

questions.q: In the pair यस्मात् … अतः, what does each word do?
options: यस्मात् gives the result; अतः gives the reason
Both give reasons, one for each body part
यस्मात् gives the reason; अतः gives the result
optionExplain: The roles are swapped.
The pair links one reason to one result.
Especially is विशेषेण.
Right: 'Because … therefore': the reason comes first and the result follows.
questions.explain: यस्मात् = because (the skin); अतः = therefore (practise it).
questions.teaches: यस्मात् (because) and अतः (therefore) pair a reason with its result.

questions.q: Which is the right split of त्वच्यश्च?
optionExplain: Right: A visarga before च becomes श्: त्वच्यः + च = त्वच्यश्च.
श्च is not a word.
ओ would come before a voiced sound, not before च.
The visarga before च becomes श्, not स्.
questions.explain: त्वच्यः (good for the skin) + च (and).

questions.q: Put the parts of line 2 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Line 2 names the places first, then 'it', 'especially', and the verb.
questions.rule: शिरः · श्रवण · पादेषु · तम् · विशेषेण · शीलयेत्.

questions.q: In the new sentence यस्मात् दीपः तेजस्वी, अतः तं पश्येत्, which part states the reason?
optionExplain: This follows अतः and is the result.
Right: The clause with यस्मात् states the reason.
This is the result, not the reason.
This names the lamp but not the whole reason clause दीपः तेजस्वी.
questions.explain: The clause with यस्मात् gives the reason: because the lamp is bright.
questions.rule: यस्मात् clause = reason; अतः clause = result.
questions.teaches: In a यस्मात् … अतः sentence, the यस्मात् clause states the reason and the अतः clause the result.

questions.q: Practised on the head, what is abhyaṅga said to be good for?
optionExplain: Teeth are not named in this verse.
Nails are not named in this verse.
Right: स केश्यः शीलितो मूर्ध्नि: good for the hair when practised on the head.
The voice is not named in this verse.
questions.explain: केश्य = good for the hair; मूर्ध्नि = on the head.
questions.rule: मूर्ध्नि शीलितः केश्यः = on the head, good for the hair.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words give the sense of the two lines.
questions.rule: केश्य = good for the hair; कपाल = skull; इन्द्रिय = sense organ; तर्पण = nourishing; शूल = pain.

questions.q: In शूलघ्नम्, what does the ending -घ्न add to शूल?
options: It names a giver of pain
It names the place of the pain
It names the cause of the pain
It names a destroyer of pain
optionExplain: -घ्न destroys; it does not give.
A place would be shown by an ending such as -ए.
A cause would be shown by -ज or a word like कारण.
Right: -घ्न at the end of a compound means 'destroying' what comes before.
questions.explain: शूल + घ्न = destroying pain; the word agrees with कर्णपूरणम्.
questions.teaches: A compound ending in -घ्न means 'destroying' the first part (शूलघ्नम् = destroying pain).

questions.q: Which is the right split of कपालेन्द्रिय-?
optionExplain: Right: अ + इ gives ए: कपाल + इन्द्रिय = कपालेन्द्रिय.
न्द्रिय is not a word.

questions.q: Join गज + इन्द्र (lord of elephants) in the way कपाल + इन्द्रिय is joined. Which is right?

questions.q: Which three things does line 1 say foot abhyaṅga produces?
options: Hunger, thirst and strength of the whole body
Warmth of the skin, speech and good hearing
Steadiness, sleep and clearness of sight

optionExplain: None of these is named in line 1.
None of these is named in line 1.

None of these is named in line 1.

questions.q: Match each item of the verse to its meaning.

questions.q: In प्रसादकृत्, what does -कृत् add to प्रसाद?

questions.teaches: A compound ending in -कृत् means 'maker of' the first part (दृक्प्रसादकृत् = maker of clearness of sight).

questions.q: Which is the right split of पादाभ्यंगः?

ओ + अ would stay as ओऽ.
इ + अ would give य, not आ.

questions.q: Put these five items dispelled in line 2 in the order of the verse.

questions.q: A new word is तमःप्रणुत्, like स्फुटनप्रणुत्. What does it mean?

'Born of' would end in -ज.

questions.q: What is activity called which produces exertion of the body, according to line 2?

Bathing is not defined here.
Right: शरीरायासजननं कर्म व्यायाम उच्यते.

questions.q: In शरीरायासजननम्, what does -जनन add to शरीरायास?

It names the person who feels the exertion of the body

questions.teaches: A compound ending in -जनन means 'producing' the first part (शरीरायासजननम् = producing exertion of the body).

ओऽभ्यंगः is not a word.
भ्यंगः is not a word.

Right: X-जनन = producing X.
A cause would be shown by -तः or -ज.
Nothing in the word means measuring.

questions.teaches: A compound ending in -जनन means 'producing' the first part (शरीरायासजननम्, भयजननम्).

questions.q: From what do these five results arise, according to line 2?

questions.q: What does the ending -आत् show in व्यायामात्?

'In' would be the ending -ए.

questions.teaches: The ending -आत् on a masculine a-word means 'from' (व्यायामात् = from exercise).

दुपजायतेः is not a word.
आदुपजायतेः is not a word.
questions.explain: व्यायामात् (from exercise) + उपजायते (arises).

questions.q: Put the five results in the order of the verse.

questions.rule: लाघव · कर्मसामर्थ्य · दीप्त अग्नि · मेदःक्षय · विभक्तघनगात्रत्व.

questions.q: Built like व्यायामात्, which word means from study (पाठ, masculine)?

questions.q: With how much strength is it to be practised by the strong who eat unctuous food?

optionExplain: The verse says half, not full.

questions.q: Put the six fields of rash excess in the order of the verse.

questions.q: Which is the right rendering of the second line, गजं सिंह इवाकर्षन् भजन्नति विनश्यति?

questions.rule: गजम् = elephant (object), सिंहः = lion, आकर्षन् = dragging.

questions.q: Which two of these does the verse name among the fields of rash excess?

Right: it stands in the compound.

questions.q: The visarga of सिंहः drops before इव. How is the invented बालः + इव written?
optionExplain: Right: अः before a vowel other than अ: the visarga drops and the vowels stay apart.

questions.teaches: Visarga after अ is lost before a vowel other than अ, and the two vowels are not joined: सिंहः + इव = सिंह इव.

questions.q: Which of these does the verse say udvartana does?

questions.q: Which two of these does the verse say udvartana does?

Right: त्वक्प्रसादकरम्.

questions.q: Like कफहरम् (remover of kapha), what does the invented शोकहरम् mean?

questions.q: Which pair does the verse say bathing gives?

questions.rule: कण्डू = itching, मल = dirt, श्रम = exertion, स्वेद = sweat, दाह = burning.
questions.teaches: The members of the long compound before -जित् are the things bathing conquers; each is read alone: कण्डू itching, मल dirt, श्रम exertion, स्वेद sweat, दाह burning.

questions.q: What does the ending -जित् in पाप्मजित् say about bathing?
options: It is overcome by the listed things
It brings about the listed things
It is born from the listed things
optionExplain: जित् is active here: bathing is the conqueror.
Right: जित् means conquering: the compound lists what bathing conquers.
जित् means conquering, not bringing about.
Born from would be -ज; -जित् is conquering.
questions.explain: The last member -जित् governs the whole compound: bathing conquers all those.

questions.q: Which two does the verse say bathing overcomes?
optionExplain: Right: it is in the compound.
Right: it is in the compound.
Hunger is not in the list.
Cold is not in the list.
Fear is not in the list.
questions.explain: Sweat and itching are named in line 2; hunger, cold and fear are not.
questions.rule: The compound lists कण्डू, मल, श्रम, स्वेद, तन्द्रा, तृट्, दाह, पाप्मन्.

questions.q: Like पाप्मजित्, what does the invented शत्रुजित् mean?
optionExplain: -जित् is not 'born of'.
Nothing in -जित् means friend.
Right: A noun + जित् at the end: the conqueror of that noun.
In this pattern the noun is what is conquered.
questions.explain: शत्रुजित् is the conqueror of enemies.
questions.teaches: At the end of a compound, -जित् means conquering what the first part names.

questions.q: What does the verse say hot-water pouring over the lower body does?
optionExplain: That is the result said of the head.
The eyes are mentioned only for the head.
Nothing is said of lengthening hair.
Right: बलावहः: bringing strength.
questions.explain: Line 1: pouring hot water over the lower body is बलावहः.

questions.q: Put the words of line 1 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Line 1: with hot water, of the lower body, the pouring, strength-bringing.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse with its meaning.
questions.explain: Each is a word of the two lines.
questions.rule: उष्ण + अम्बु = hot water; अधःकाय = lower body; उत्तमाङ्ग = the head; परिषेक = pouring; चक्षुस् = eye.
questions.teaches: Case endings carry the sense: -ना marks the means (उष्णाम्बुना), -स्य marks 'of' (अधःकायस्य, उत्तमाङ्गस्य), -षाम् marks 'of the many' (चक्षुषाम्).

questions.q: Which translation of line 2 has no wrong word?
options: By the same, on the head, it takes away the strength of hair and eyes
By the same, on the head, it brings the strength of hair and eyes
By the same, on the feet, it takes away the strength of hair and eyes
By the same, on the head, it takes away the strength of hair and ears
optionExplain: Right: बलहृत् is taking away strength; केशचक्षुषाम् is of the hair and eyes.
बलहृत् is taking away, the opposite of bringing.
उत्तमाङ्ग is the head.
The verse says eyes (चक्षुषाम्), not ears.
questions.explain: Line 2 keeps the same pouring but at the head, with the opposite result.
questions.rule: उत्तमाङ्ग = head; बलहृत् = taking away strength.

questions.q: What does तेन in तेनैव चोत्तमांगस्य point back to?
optionExplain: परिषेक is the act in the nominative; तेन is the means, the water.
Right: तेन is the instrumental 'with that': the water used for the pouring.
बल is the result, not the means.
These come later in line 2.
questions.explain: तेन एव means with that very (hot) water, now used on the head.

questions.q: Like बलहृत्, 'taking away strength', what does the invented सुखहृत् mean?
options: Born of happiness in the mind
Full of happiness in the mind
optionExplain: That would be -आवह as in बलावहः.
-हृत् is not 'born of'.
Right: A noun + हृत् at the end: what takes that noun away.
-हृत् is not 'full of'.
questions.explain: सुखहृत् is the opposite of सुखावहः, as बलहृत् is of बलावहः.
questions.rule: X + हृत् = taking away X; X + आवह = bringing X.
questions.teaches: -आवह at the end of a compound brings, -हृत् takes away: बलावहः and बलहृत्, सुखावहः and सुखहृत्.

questions.q: What does the clear start of line 1 say about bathing and the head?
options: Do not bathe after the head has been wetted
Bathe only the head and nothing else of the body
Do not wet the head at all while bathing
Do not bathe without wetting the head first
optionExplain: The verse forbids bathing without wetting the head first.
No such restriction is said.
The reverse: the head is wetted first.
Right: नानाप्लुत्य शिरः स्नायात्: not bathing without having wetted the head.
questions.explain: The head is wetted first; bathing without that is what the words forbid.
questions.rule: ना + अनाप्लुत्य शिरः स्नायात्: should not bathe without wetting the head.

questions.q: Put these clear parts of line 1 in verse order (leaving out the doubtful word अल्पे).
questions.explain: The line runs: not without wetting, the head, should bathe, in water, ... not in cold.
questions.rule: नानाप्लुत्य · शिरः · स्नायात् · जले · (अल्पे) · न शीतले.

questions.q: Match each clear word of line 1 with its meaning.
questions.explain: Four words of the line are plain.
questions.rule: स्नायात् = should bathe (optative); शिरः = head; जले = in water; शीतले = in cold (water).
questions.teaches: Verbs in -यात् mean 'should' (स्नायात् = should bathe) and nouns in -ए name the place (जले in water, शीतले in cold water).

questions.q: Which is the right split of नानाप्लुत्य?
optionExplain: Right: न + अ gives ना; the second half is अनाप्लुत्य, without having wetted.
That would join as नाप्लुत्य, with one ना.
That would give नाप्लुत्य, not नानाप्लुत्य.
No word नान begins it; the join does not fit.
questions.explain: नानाप्लुत्य is न + अनाप्लुत्य: a + a → ā.
questions.rule: अ + अ → आ: न + अनाप्लुत्य = नानाप्लुत्य.

questions.q: Which two does the clear part of line 1 say?
options: not bathing without first wetting the head
bathing only with the head wetted last
optionExplain: Right: नानाप्लुत्य शिरः स्नायात्.
Right: न शीतले.
Night is not mentioned.
A meal is not mentioned in this unit.
The head is wetted first.
questions.explain: The two plain statements are: head wetted first, not in cold water.

questions.q: Following न + अनाप्लुत्य, how is the invented न + अपठित्वा (not without reading) written?
optionExplain: The two a's join; they do not stay apart.
Right: न + अ joins into ना, as in नानाप्लुत्य.
A + a does not make ए; it makes आ.
A + a does not make ओ; it makes आ.
questions.explain: Short a + short a = long ā: नापठित्वा.
questions.teaches: Two short a's join into long ā: न + अपठित्वा = नापठित्वा.

questions.q: What does the verse say about looking at oneself in water?
options: One should look at oneself in water
One should look only at the water's surface
One should not look at oneself in water
One should look at oneself only in cold water
optionExplain: The word न forbids it.
Nothing like that is said.
Right: नात्मानमीक्षेत जले: not oneself should look in water.
Cold water is not mentioned in this unit.
questions.explain: Line 2 begins with a prohibition: न + आत्मानम् + ईक्षेत जले.

questions.q: Put the four phrases of line 2 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Line 2 runs: not oneself should look, in water, not standing on the bank, the reservoir.

questions.q: Match each word of the unit with its meaning.
questions.explain: Each is a plain word of the two lines.
questions.rule: आत्मा = self; ईक्षेत = should look at; जल = water; परवारि = another's water; तटस्थ = standing on the bank.
questions.teaches: A verb in -एत means 'should' (ईक्षेत = should look at); आत्मानम् in -अम् is the thing looked at; nouns in -ए / -इ name the place (जले, परवारिणि).

questions.q: Which is the right split of नात्मानमीक्षेत?
optionExplain: There is no word अत्मानम्; it is आत्मानम्.
There is no such word-break; the word is आत्मानम्.
The negative is the short न; ना is not the word न here, and न + आत्मानम् already gives नात्मानम्.
Right: न + आ gives ना; the m of आत्मानम् then meets ई.
questions.explain: आत्मानम् is the object of ईक्षेत; the negative is the initial न.

questions.q: In नात्मानमीक्षेत जले, which word is the object of ईक्षेत?
optionExplain: Right: आत्मानम् is accusative: oneself is what is looked at.
It is locative: where one looks, not what.
It is the negative word.
It is the verb itself.
questions.explain: One looks at oneself (accusative) in the water (locative).

questions.q: In the invented line न वदेत् मिथ्या, what does the verb वदेत् with न mean?
optionExplain: The optative with न says should not, not a plain statement.
Right: न + optative (-एत्, -यात्) is a prohibition, as in न स्नायात्, नेक्षेत.
It is not past.
It is not future.
questions.explain: The optative ending (-एत्, -यात्) with न forbids: should not.
questions.teaches: The optative (-एत्, -यात्) with न is a prohibition: न वदेत् मिथ्या, 'one should not speak falsely'.

questions.q: What does line 1 say about the water?
options: It should be splashed with both hands together
It should be drunk from the cupped hand
It should not be splashed with the hand or foot
It should be kept away from the feet always
optionExplain: The verse forbids splashing and says hand or foot.
Drinking is not mentioned.
Right: न प्रतिस्फालयेत् अम्बु पाणिना चरणेन वा.
Keeping from the feet is not said.
questions.explain: Line 1 forbids striking the water back with the hand or foot.

questions.q: Put these phrases in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Line 1 gives the water prohibition; line 2 the two after-bathing ones.
questions.rule: न प्रतिस्फालयेदम्बु · पाणिना चरणेन वा · स्नात्वा न मृज्याद्गात्राणि · धुनुयान्न शिरोरुहान्.

questions.q: Match each word with its meaning.
questions.explain: Five words of the verse.
questions.rule: पाणि = hand; चरण = foot; गात्र = limb; शिरोरुह = (what grows on the head) hair; स्नात्वा = having bathed.
questions.teaches: The ending -ना / -एन marks the tool (पाणिना with the hand, चरणेन with the foot); -त्वा marks 'having done' (स्नात्वा); -आणि marks the many limbs (गात्राणि).

questions.q: What kind of form is स्नात्वा?
optionExplain: That is स्नायात्.
It is not future.
It is a verb form, not a noun.
Right: -त्वा on a verb without prefix means having done.
questions.explain: स्नात्वा = having bathed, the action before the two prohibitions.

questions.q: Which two does the verse say not to do after bathing?
optionExplain: Right: स्नात्वा न मृज्याद्गात्राणि.
Right: धुनुयान्न शिरोरुहान्.
A turban is not mentioned in this verse.
Not mentioned in this verse.
Not mentioned in this verse.
questions.explain: The two after-bathing prohibitions are wiping the limbs and shaking the hair.

questions.q: Using स्नात्वा न, what does the invented दृष्ट्वा न वदेत् mean?
options: Having seen, one should not speak
Having seen, one does not speak
Having spoken, one should not see
optionExplain: Right: -त्वा gives 'having done'; न + optative forbids.
The optative with न forbids; it is not a plain statement.
The roles are swapped.
दृष्ट्वा is 'having seen', and there is no future.
questions.explain: Both rules together: absolutive + न + optative.
questions.rule: -त्वा = having done (दृश् + त्वा → दृष्ट्वा); न + optative = should not.
questions.teaches: A 'having done' form followed by न and an optative gives 'having done, one should not ...': स्नात्वा न मृज्यात्.

questions.q: What does धौत in धौतवाससी mean?
optionExplain: Dyeing is not said.
Right: धौत is the past participle of धाव्, washed; वाससी is the two garments.
Tearing is not said.
Newness is not said.
questions.explain: धौतवाससी = the two washed garments.

questions.q: Put these clear words in the order of the verse (leaving out the doubtful ones).
questions.explain: Line 1 ends with the turban and the two washed garments; line 2 has the garment worn before.

questions.q: Match each clear word with its meaning.
questions.explain: Plain words of the unit.
questions.rule: स + उष्णीष = with turban; धौत = washed; पूर्व + धृत = worn before; अम्बर = garment; स्पृशेत् = should touch.
questions.teaches: A bahuvrīhi with स- means 'with' (सोष्णीषे), and a participle first member names the state: धौत washed, पूर्वधृत worn before.

questions.q: Which is the right split of सोष्णीषे, 'together with the turban'?
optionExplain: That would stay as सोउष्णीषे.
That would give स उष्णीषे, with a dropped visarga.
Right: अ + उ → ओ: स + उष्णीषे = सोष्णीषे.
That would give सूष्णीषे (उ + उ → ऊ).
questions.explain: स- means with; अ + उ → ओ.
questions.rule: अ + उ → ओ: स + उष्णीष = सोष्णीष.

questions.q: Which two words of the unit name clothing?
optionExplain: Right: garment.
Right: turban.
A verb: should touch.
Not named in this unit.
Not named in this unit.
questions.explain: Garment and turban are clothing; the other words are a verb or things not named.

questions.q: Like सोष्णीषे, 'with a turban', what does the invented सपुस्तकः शिष्यः mean?
options: A pupil who is a book
optionExplain: That would be अ- or निः-.
स- does not make 'is'.
स- is not 'of'.
Right: स- + noun = with that noun.
questions.explain: स- + पुस्तक = with a book.
questions.rule: स- + noun = with that noun (a bahuvrīhi).
questions.teaches: The prefix स- in a compound means 'with': सोष्णीषे with a turban, सपुस्तकः with a book.

questions.q: What does line 1 say about garments?
options: A different garment for each of three occasions
One garment for all three occasions together
Two garments shared by all three occasions
A new garment for each day of the week
optionExplain: Right: वासः अन्यत् अन्यत्: one garment, another, another, for sleeping, going out and worship.
The line says different ones.
No such count is stated.
Days are not mentioned.
questions.explain: Sleeping, going out and worship each get a different garment.

questions.q: Put the three occasions in the order of line 1.
questions.explain: The line: for sleeping, for going out, for worship of the deity.

questions.q: Match each word with its meaning.
questions.explain: Five words of line 1.
questions.rule: शयन = sleeping; निर्गम = going out; देवतार्चन = worship of the deity; वासस् = garment; अन्य = other.
questions.teaches: The three locatives in -ए name occasions (शयने sleeping, निर्गमे going out, देवतार्चने worship); वासः is the garment and अन्यत् 'another'.

questions.q: Which is the right split of वासोऽन्यत्?
optionExplain: The o here comes from a visarga; the base is वासः.
Right: अः + अ → ओऽ: वासः + अन्यत् = वासोऽन्यत्.
That would join into वासान्यत्.
That would give वासेऽन्यत्.
questions.explain: A visarga after अ becomes ओ before अ, and the अ is dropped (ऽ).

questions.q: For which of these does line 1 NOT name a separate garment?
optionExplain: शयने is named.
निर्गमे is named.
Right: Bathing is not named in line 1 (unit 74 line 2 only begins a sentence about it).
देवतार्चने is named.
questions.explain: Line 1 names three occasions only.

questions.q: Like शयने (for sleeping), what is the invented form for reading, from पठन?
optionExplain: That is a masculine nominative ending.
That is the nominative/accusative.
That is the instrumental, 'by reading'.
Right: Stems in -अ end in -ए in the locative, used for 'for/at'.
questions.explain: शयन → शयने; पठन → पठने.
questions.rule: -अ stem (masculine or neuter), locative -ए: शयने, निर्गमे, पठने.
questions.teaches: The locative in -ए names the occasion 'for/at': शयने for sleeping, देवतार्चने for worship, पठने for reading.

questions.q: Which word of line 1 says what is done to the listed people?
optionExplain: Right: गर्हितम् is the predicate of line 1.
The verse says censured.
Not the word used.
Opposite of गर्हितम्.
questions.explain: Line 1 ends with गर्हितम्: censured.

questions.q: Put the four kinds of person of line 1 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Line 1: distension, pīnasa, indigestion, those who have eaten.

questions.q: Match each word with its meaning.
questions.explain: Five words of the unit.
questions.rule: आध्मान = distension; अजीर्ण = indigestion; भुक्तवत् = one who has eaten; गर्हित = censured; भुञ्जीत = should eat.
questions.teaches: An अ- prefix negates (अजीर्ण = not digested), -वत् marks one who has done (भुक्तवत् = who has eaten), and -ईत is the verb ending 'should' (भुञ्जीत).

questions.q: Which is the right split of भुंजीतान्नं?
optionExplain: A visarga would give भुञ्जीतोऽन्नम्.
Right: अ + अ → आ: भुञ्जीत + अन्नम् = भुञ्जीतान्नम्.
तान्नम् is not a word.
That would give भुञ्जीतेऽन्नम्, ending in -ए, not the printed भुञ्जीतान्नम्.
questions.explain: The verb भुञ्जीत (should eat) comes first, then the object अन्नम्.

questions.q: Which three of these kinds of person does line 1 list?
optionExplain: Right: आध्मान.
Right: अजीर्ण.
Right: भुक्तवत्.
Fever is not named in this unit.
Hunger is not named in this unit.
questions.explain: Line 1 names distension, pīnasa, indigestion and those who have eaten.

questions.q: Like भुक्तवत्सु (in those who have eaten), what is the invented form for in those who have read, from पठितवत्?
optionExplain: That would mean 'in the things read'.
That is the nominative singular.
Right: -वत् stems end in -वत्सु in the locative plural.
That is a genitive/ablative singular.
questions.explain: भुक्तवत् → भुक्तवत्सु; पठितवत् → पठितवत्सु.
questions.teaches: A -वत् participle names one who has done: भुक्तवत्सु, in those who have eaten; पठितवत्सु, in those who have read.

questions.q: With what state of mind does line 1 say the welcoming and offering are done?
optionExplain: Anger is not said.
Fear is not said.
Hunger is not said.
Right: प्रसन्नात्मा: whose mind is cheerful.
questions.explain: प्रसन्न means cheerful; आत्मा is mind or self.

questions.q: Put these acts in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Welcoming, offering oblation, giving; then the cooked food with water; then the place.
questions.rule: अभिनन्द्य · हुत्वा · दत्वा · पाकं सजलम् · एकान्ते.

questions.q: Match each word with its meaning.
questions.explain: Five words of the two lines.
questions.rule: हुत्वा = having offered oblation; दत्वा = having given; शक्तितः = according to ability; सजल = with water; एकान्ते = in a secluded place.
questions.teaches: -त्वा words mean 'having done' (हुत्वा, दत्वा), -तः means 'according to' (शक्तितः), स- means 'with' (सजल) and a locative in -ए names the place (एकान्ते).

questions.q: Why does अभिनंद्य end in -य while हुत्वा ends in -त्वा?
options: The two forms have different tenses
optionExplain: Right: A 'having done' form takes -य after a prefix, -त्वा without one.
It is a 'having done' form, like हुत्वा.
√हु has no prefix here.
Both mean 'having done'.
questions.explain: Prefix → -य; no prefix → -त्वा.

questions.q: Which three acts does the verse name before the eating?
optionExplain: Right.
Right.
Right.
Fasting is not named.
Bathing is not named in this unit.
questions.explain: The three 'having done' forms are the acts; the other two are not named here.

questions.q: Which is the form meaning having bowed, from प्र + नम्, as अभि + नन्द् gives अभिनन्द्य?
optionExplain: -त्वा goes on a verb without prefix.
Right: With a prefix the ending is -य.
-त्वा does not go on a verb with a prefix, and the ण is missing.
This is not a 'having done' form; that ends in -य after a prefix.
questions.explain: प्र + नम् + य = प्रणम्य (the न becomes ण after र).
questions.teaches: A 'having done' form of a prefixed verb ends in -य (अभिनन्द्य, प्रणम्य); an unprefixed verb takes -त्वा (हुत्वा, नत्वा).

questions.q: What does line 1 say about cooking food?
options: One should cook food only for oneself
One should cook food for the dead
One should not cook food for oneself
One should not cook food for others
optionExplain: The verse says the reverse.
The dead are mentioned only in line 2.
Right: पाचयेत् न अन्नम् आत्मने: should not have food cooked for oneself.
The verse says to give, not to refuse.
questions.explain: Line 1 pairs giving (to all) with not cooking for oneself.

questions.q: Put the three groups whose food is not to be eaten in the order of line 2.
questions.explain: Line 2: of those about to die, of the dead, of those living in misery.

questions.q: Match each word with its meaning.
questions.explain: Five words of the two lines.
questions.rule: मुमूर्षु = wishing to die, about to die; मृत = dead; दुःखजीविन् = living in misery; आत्मने = for oneself; प्रयच्छेत् = should give.
questions.teaches: Genitive plurals in -आम् name whose food: मुमूर्षूणाम्, मृतानाम्, दुःखजीविनाम्; the dative -ने in आत्मने means 'for oneself'.

questions.q: Which is the right split of पाचयेन्नान्नमात्मने?
optionExplain: पाचयेन् is not a word; the verb is पाचयेत्, ending in त्.
The negative न would be lost.
There is no word आन्नम्; the word is अन्नम्, joined with न into नान्नम्.
Right: त् before न becomes न्; न + अ joins into ना.
questions.explain: Four words: should cause to cook, not, food, for oneself.
questions.rule: त् + न → न्न; न + अ → ना.

questions.q: Whose food does line 2 say not to eat? Choose three.
optionExplain: Right: मुमूर्षूणाम्.
Right: मृतानाम्.
Right: दुःखजीविनाम्.
Not named in this verse.
Not named in this verse.
questions.explain: The three groups of line 2 are named; learned people and guests are not.

questions.q: Like मृतानाम्, 'of the dead', what does शिष्याणाम् in the invented शिष्याणामन्नम् mean?
