optionExplain: Right: -आणाम् is the genitive plural of a-stems: 'of the ...'.
That would be a dative, शिष्येभ्यः.
That would be an instrumental, शिष्यैः.
That would be singular, शिष्यस्य.
questions.explain: Genitive plural ends in -नाम्/-णाम्.
questions.teaches: The genitive plural ending -आनाम्/-आणाम् means 'of the ...': मृतानाम् of the dead, शिष्याणाम् of the pupils.

questions.q: Which of these kinds of person does line 1 name?
optionExplain: No physician is named.
Right: पतित is the third member of the list.
No teacher is named.
No king is named.
questions.explain: Line 1 is a list of kinds of person, the third member being the outcast.

questions.q: Put the members of the line-1 compound in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The line: one conquered by women, eunuch, outcast, cruel, doer of evil deeds.

questions.q: Match each word of line 1 with its meaning.
questions.explain: Five members of the list.
questions.rule: स्त्रीजित = conquered by women; क्लीब = eunuch; पतित = fallen; क्रूर = cruel; दुष्कृतकारिन् = doer of evil deeds.
questions.teaches: A long compound is read member by member; each member names one kind of person: स्त्रीजित, क्लीब, पतित, क्रूर, दुष्कृतकारिन्.

questions.q: Which translation of line 1 has no wrong word?
options: Of one ruled by women, a eunuch, an outcast, a kind one, evildoers
Of one ruled by women, a eunuch, a king, a cruel one, evildoers
Of one ruled by women, a eunuch, an outcast, a cruel one, evildoers
Of one ruled by women, a eunuch, an outcast, a cruel one, saints
optionExplain: क्रूर is cruel, not kind.
पतित is an outcast, not a king.
Right: स्त्रीजित, क्लीब, पतित, क्रूर, दुष्कृतकारिन् in that order.
दुष्कृत is evil deed, not saint.
questions.explain: Each member corresponds to one word of the print.
questions.rule: पतित = fallen; क्रूर = cruel; दुष्कृत = evil deed.

questions.q: Which member of the line-1 compound names one who does evil deeds?
optionExplain: That is a eunuch.
That is fallen, an outcast.
That is one conquered by women.
Right: दुष्कृत (evil deed) + कारिन् (doer).
questions.explain: The last member is the doer of evil deeds.

questions.q: Like दुष्कृतकारिणाम् (of doers of evil deeds), what is the invented form for of doers of good deeds?
optionExplain: Right: सु- is the good counterpart of दुः-; the ending -णाम् stays.
That is a nominative plural.
That is a dative singular.
That keeps the evil prefix.
questions.explain: दुः- → सु-, the rest unchanged.
questions.teaches: -कारिन् names a doer, and the genitive plural is -कारिणाम्; सु- and दुः- turn the deed good or evil: सुकृतकारिणाम्, दुष्कृतकारिणाम्.

questions.q: What does the verse say about things connected with sesame?
options: They are not to be eaten while the sun is rising
They are not to be eaten when the sun has set
They are to be eaten only after the sun has set
They are to be eaten at any hour
optionExplain: The verse names the setting of the sun, not the rising.
Right: सर्वं च तिलसंबद्धं नाद्यादस्तमिते रवौ: not eaten once the sun has set.
The verb is negated: नाद्यात् means one should not eat.
The verse bars them once the sun has set.
questions.explain: The verse ties the sesame prohibition to the time when the sun has set.
questions.rule: तिलसंबद्धं नाद्यादस्तमिते रवौ = nothing connected with sesame to be eaten at sunset.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words carry the three prohibitions.
questions.rule: उत्संगे = on the lap; भक्ष्यान् = edibles; अंजलिना = with the joined palms; अस्तमिते = when set.

questions.q: Which is the right split of नोत्संगे?
optionExplain: त्संगे is not a word.
That would leave out the उ of उत्संगे.
Right: अ + उ join as ओ, so न + उत्संगे gives नोत्संगे.
The ओ is the result of the joining, so it is not a separate part.
questions.explain: नोत्संगे is न (not) + उत्संगे (on the lap).
questions.rule: अ + उ → ओ: न + उत्संगे = नोत्संगे.
questions.teaches: Short अ followed by उ joins as ओ (न + उत्संगे = नोत्संगे).

questions.q: With what is water not to be drunk, according to the verse?
optionExplain: No vessel is mentioned.
The lap belongs to the edibles, not to the water.
Sunset is mentioned only for sesame things.
Right: जलं नांजलिना पिवेत्: not with the joined palms.
questions.explain: अंजलिना is the instrumental of अंजलि: by means of the joined palms.
questions.rule: जलं नांजलिना पिवेत् = water not with the joined palms.

questions.q: Put the three prohibitions in the order of the verse.
items: eating edibles placed on the lap
drinking water with the joined palms
questions.explain: The first line gives the lap and the palms; the second line gives sesame at sunset.
questions.rule: Lap · joined palms · sesame at sunset.

questions.q: Following अंजलिना, which means by the sage (मुनि, masculine)?
optionExplain: Right: Masculine words in -इ take -ना in the instrumental singular, as अंजलिना.
This is the locative, 'in the sage'.
This is genitive or ablative, 'of / from the sage'.
This is the nominative plural, 'sages'.
questions.explain: अंजलि → अंजलिना; मुनि → मुनिना.
questions.teaches: A masculine noun in -इ forms the instrumental singular in -इना (अंजलिना, मुनिना): 'by / with'.

questions.q: What is one not to do right after eating, according to the first line?
optionExplain: Speaking is not forbidden in the first line.
Right: भुक्तमात्र आयस्येत् with न: one should not exert oneself just after eating.
No gift is mentioned.
No washing is mentioned.
questions.explain: भुक्तमात्रः means just after eating; आयस्येत् means one should exert oneself, here negated.
questions.rule: न भुक्तमात्र आयस्येत् = not to exert oneself just after eating.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words carry the two prohibitions and one description of the talks.
questions.rule: भुक्तमात्रः = just after eating; आयस्येत् = should exert oneself; निषिद्धम् = forbidden; अर्थ्याभिः = with purposeful ones.

questions.q: In भुक्तमात्रआयस्येत् the visarga of भुक्तमात्रः is dropped before आ. What is the rule?
options: Visarga after अ always becomes ओ
Visarga becomes र् before any vowel
Visarga after अ drops before a vowel other than अ, and the two vowels stay apart
Visarga stays and the आ is dropped
optionExplain: That happens before a voiced consonant, not before आ.
That is for visarga after other vowels, not after अ.
Right: भुक्तमात्रः + आयस्येत् gives भुक्तमात्र आयस्येत्.
Here the visarga is dropped and आ stays.
questions.explain: The printed भुक्तमात्रआयस्येत् is regular, not a typo.
questions.rule: अः + vowel other than अ → अ (visarga dropped), no joining.
questions.teaches: After अ, a visarga drops before any vowel other than अ and the vowels stay apart (भुक्तमात्रः + आयस्येत् → भुक्तमात्र आयस्येत्).

questions.q: Which pair of descriptions of the talks (कथाभिः) does the verse give?
optionExplain: Neither is said.
Neither is said.
Dharma is foremost here, not wealth.
Right: धर्मोत्तराभिः and अर्थ्याभिः.
questions.explain: धर्म-उत्तर means with dharma foremost; अर्थ्य means purposeful.
questions.rule: धर्मोत्तराभिः अर्थ्याभिः कथाभिः = with talks with dharma foremost, purposeful.

questions.q: Put these words of the first line in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The line runs: just after eating, should exert oneself, (not) forbidden, should resort to.

questions.q: Following कथाभिः, which means with the maidens (कन्या, feminine)?
optionExplain: Right: Feminine -आ nouns take -आभिः in the instrumental plural, like कथाभिः.
This is genitive plural, 'of the maidens'.
This is locative plural, 'among the maidens'.
This is nominative plural, 'the maidens'.
questions.explain: कथा → कथाभिः; कन्या → कन्याभिः.
questions.teaches: A feminine noun in -आ forms the instrumental plural in -आभिः (कथाभिः, कन्याभिः): 'with'.

questions.q: Which part of the day does the first line speak of?
optionExplain: The line says मध्य, middle.
Right: मध्यं दिनस्य: the middle of the day.
The line says मध्य, middle.
The line speaks of the day (दिन).
questions.explain: मध्यम् is the middle and दिनस्य is of the day.
questions.rule: मध्यं दिनस्य गमयेत् = one should pass the middle of the day.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words carry the main statements of the unit.
questions.rule: मध्यम् = middle; दिनस्य = of the day; गमयेत् = should pass; नास्तिकैः = with unbelievers.

questions.q: In लोकभूपविद्विष्टैर्न, what does the visarga of -ऐः become before न?
optionExplain: ओ is for visarga after short अ.
It is dropped before a vowel, not before a voiced consonant.
Right: A visarga after ऐ becomes र् before a voiced consonant.
श् stands before च or छ, not before न.
questions.explain: लोकभूपविद्विष्टैः + न = लोकभूपविद्विष्टैर्न.
questions.teaches: A visarga after ऐ becomes र् before a voiced sound (विद्विष्टैः + न → विद्विष्टैर्न).

questions.q: Which two does the verse say one should not keep company with?
options: those hated by the people and the king
optionExplain: Right: लोकभूपविद्विष्टैः.
Right: नास्तिकैः.
These are the companions one is to have.
Only those hated by the king are named, not the king.
questions.explain: Line 2 negates संगच्छेत with two groups: the hated ones and the unbelievers.

questions.q: Put these parts of the unit in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The unit first gives the middle of the day and the companions, then the two groups to avoid.

questions.q: Following नास्तिकैः, which means with friends (मित्र, masculine)?
optionExplain: This is locative plural, 'among friends'.
This is genitive plural, 'of friends'.
This is accusative singular, 'a friend'.
Right: Masculine -अ nouns take -ऐः in the instrumental plural.
questions.explain: नास्तिक → नास्तिकैः; मित्र → मित्रैः.
questions.teaches: A masculine noun in -अ forms the instrumental plural in -ऐः (नास्तिकैः, मित्रैः): 'with'.

questions.q: In which two things is he not to be fond, according to the first line?
optionExplain: Right: कलिवैररुचिर्न स्यात्: he is not fond of quarrel and enmity.
Neither is named in the line.
Neither is named in the line.
Neither is named in the line.
questions.explain: The compound कलिवैररुचिः means fond of quarrel and enmity, and न स्यात् negates it.
questions.rule: कलिवैररुचिः न स्यात् = he should not be fond of quarrel and enmity.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words carry the first line and the end of the second.
questions.rule: संपद् = good fortune; विपत्ति = misfortune; धीरः = steady; कुतूहली = keenly interested.

questions.q: The word for 'steady' in line 1 is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: धीरः is steady, wise: he stays so in both fortune and misfortune.
questions.teaches: धीरः (nominative singular) describes the person who stays steady.

questions.q: Which statement matches line 2?
options: Content in learning alone, and keen in everything else besides
Content apart from learning, keen in that alone
Content and keen in everything alike
Content in nothing, keen in learning
optionExplain: This reverses the line.
Right: श्रुतादन्यत्र संतुष्टः, तत्रैव च कुतूहली.
The line makes a split.
The line says content everywhere except learning.
questions.explain: श्रुतात् अन्यत्र = apart from learning; तत्र एव = in that alone.
questions.rule: Content apart from श्रुत; keen in it alone.

questions.q: Put these four statements in the order of the verse.
items: not fond of quarrel and enmity
steady in good fortune and misfortune
questions.explain: The first line gives the first two; the second line gives the last two.
questions.rule: Quarrel · fortune and misfortune · content apart from learning · keen in it.

questions.q: Following तत्र + एव = तत्रैव, how is अत्र + एव (only here) written?
optionExplain: That would be अ + इ → ए.
That would be अ + उ → ओ.
Right: अ + ए joins as ऐ.
The two vowels do join.
questions.explain: अत्र + एव = अत्रैव, just as तत्र + एव = तत्रैव.
questions.teaches: Short अ followed by ए joins as ऐ (तत्र + एव = तत्रैव; अत्र + एव = अत्रैव).

questions.q: Which quality does the second line name?
optionExplain: Not named in this unit.
Not named in this unit.
Not named in this unit.
Right: संविभागी is in the second line.
questions.explain: संविभागी means one who shares with others.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are five of the qualities listed.
questions.rule: क्षान्तिमान् = patient; दक्षः = skilful; ह्रीमान् = modest; धीमान् = intelligent; संविभागी = one who shares.

questions.q: In क्षान्तिमान्, ह्रीमान्, धीमान्, what does the ending -मान् add?
optionExplain: Right: -मान् is the 'having' suffix (matup); क्षान्ति-मान् = having patience.
That would be a negative like अ- or -हीन.
That is not what the suffix means here.
That would be -ज.
questions.explain: -मान् makes a word meaning one who has the first part.
questions.teaches: The ending -मान् / -वान् means 'possessing' (क्षान्तिमान् = having patience, ह्रीमान् = modest).

questions.q: Which quality is NOT named in this unit?
optionExplain: ह्रीमान् is in line 2.
Right: No such word is in the unit.
दक्षः is in line 1.
प्रियातिथिः is in line 2.
questions.explain: The unit lists patience, courtesy, skill, consideration, modesty, intelligence, energy, sharing, love of guests.
questions.rule: Truthfulness is not in the list.

questions.q: Put these qualities in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Line 1 gives patience and skill; line 2 gives modesty, intelligence, sharing.

questions.q: Following धीमान्, which is the word for one who has strength (बल)?
optionExplain: This is 'by strength' (instrumental).
This is 'from strength' (ablative).
Right: A noun in -अ takes -वान् for 'possessing'.
This is 'strength' itself.
questions.explain: बल + वान् = बलवान्, one who has strength.
questions.teaches: -वान् or -मान् added to a noun gives 'one who has it' (धीमान्, बलवान्).

questions.q: To whom is he a giver of the piṇḍa offering, according to line 2?
optionExplain: Guests are in unit 83, not here.
No teachers are named.
The king is not named in this unit.
Right: दाता पितृभ्यः पिंडस्य: giver of the piṇḍa to the ancestors.
questions.explain: पितृभ्यः means to the ancestors.
questions.rule: दाता पितृभ्यः पिंडस्य = giver of the piṇḍa to the ancestors.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are the words of the second line.
questions.rule: पितृभ्यः = to the ancestors; पिंडस्य = of the piṇḍa; यष्टा = sacrificer; होता = offerer of oblations.

questions.q: According to the card, what case is पितृभ्यः, and so what does it mean here?
optionExplain: Right: The card marks it as m. dat. pl.
The genitive plural would be पितॄणाम्.
That would be पित्रा.
That would be पितृषु.
questions.explain: -भ्यः marks the dative plural here: the piṇḍa is given to the ancestors.
questions.teaches: The ending -भ्यः (dative plural) means 'to' several persons (पितृभ्यः = to the ancestors).

questions.q: What does आश्रितवत्सलः mean?
optionExplain: The order is the other way round.
Right: आश्रित = dependant, वत्सल = affectionate.
आश्रित means dependant, not teacher.
वत्सल means affectionate.
questions.explain: The compound is a tat-puruṣa: affectionate to those who depend on him.

questions.q: Put these qualities in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Line 1 gives grave and affectionate to dependants; line 2 gives giver, sacrificer, offerer.

questions.q: Like दाता 'giver' (from √दा), what is 'doer' (from √कृ)?
optionExplain: This is 'having done'.
This is 'the act of doing'.
Right: The agent noun ends in -ता in the nominative singular.
This is 'done'.
questions.explain: दाता, यष्टा, होता, कर्ता are all agent nouns in -ता.
questions.teaches: An agent noun ('one who does') ends in -ता in the nominative singular (दाता, यष्टा, होता, कर्ता).

questions.q: Towards the wretched (दीन), what is he to be?
optionExplain: The comforter is for the frightened.
That is for the angry.
No gift is named for the wretched.
Right: दीनानामनुकंपकः.
questions.explain: दीनानाम् अनुकंपकः = compassionate to the wretched.

questions.q: Match each group of people to what he is towards them.
questions.explain: Each group is paired with one response.
questions.rule: wretched → compassionate; frightened → comforter; angry → one who pacifies.

questions.q: What ending marks दीनानाम् and भीतानाम् as 'of the wretched', 'of the frightened'?
optionExplain: Right: Both words are masculine genitive plural (-आनाम्).
That is -आभिः for feminine nouns, meaning 'with'.
That would mean 'with'.
That would mean 'among'.
questions.explain: -आनाम् is the genitive plural.
questions.teaches: A masculine noun in -अ forms the genitive plural in -आनाम् (दीनानाम्, भीतानाम्): 'of the ...'.

questions.q: Which rendering of the second line is right?
options: A comforter of the angry, one who pacifies the frightened
A comforter of the frightened, one who pacifies the angry
A frightener of the angry, a comforter of the wretched
A pacifier of the wretched, compassionate to the frightened
optionExplain: The two groups are swapped.
Right: आश्वासकारी भीतानाम्; अनुनायकः for the angry.
आश्वास is comfort and the wretched are in line 1.
The groups and acts are mixed up.
questions.explain: Line 2 pairs the frightened with comforting and the angry with pacifying.

questions.q: Put these three responses in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The verse runs: wretched, frightened, angry.

questions.q: Following दीनानाम्, which means of the sick (रुग्ण, masculine)?
optionExplain: This is 'by the sick man'.
This is 'the sick' (nominative plural).
Right: Masculine -अ nouns take -आनाम् in the genitive plural.
This is 'among the sick'.
questions.explain: दीन → दीनानाम्; रुग्ण → रुग्णानाम्.
questions.teaches: Genitive plural of masculine -अ nouns ends in -आनाम् (दीनानाम्, रुग्णानाम्).

questions.q: Which of the five grounds of honour comes last, and so counts most?
optionExplain: Wealth is first, so it counts least.
Age is the middle one, not the last.
Kinship is second.
Right: वृत्त is the last in the list, and यथोत्तरम् makes each later one weightier.
questions.explain: यथोत्तरम् = each later one more so, and conduct is last.
questions.rule: वित्त · बंधु · वयस् · विद्या · वृत्त, rising.

questions.q: Put the five grounds of honour in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The compound lists wealth, kinship, age, learning, conduct.

questions.q: Match each quality of line 1 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are the four qualities of the first line.
questions.rule: पूर्वाभिभाषी = speaks first; सुमुखः = pleasant-faced; सुशीलः = of good character; पूज्यपूजकः = honourer of the honourable.
questions.teaches: पूर्वाभिभाषी, सुमुखः, सुशीलः, पूज्यपूजकः are four qualities named in line 1 of unit 86.

questions.q: What does यथोत्तरम् say about the five grounds?
options: Each later one makes a person more worthy of honour
Each earlier one makes a person more worthy
optionExplain: Right: यथोत्तरम् = each later one more so.
This reverses the order.
The word is about ascending order.
The verse says each later one is more, not only the last.
questions.explain: Later in the list means weightier.

questions.q: By the verse, which weighs more as a ground of honour, age or learning?
options: Age, since it is more natural
Learning, since it comes later in the list
optionExplain: The verse ranks by position, not by this.
Right: विद्या follows वयस्.
यथोत्तरम् ranks them.
Wealth is the first and lowest.
questions.explain: वयस् is third and विद्या fourth, so learning ranks higher.

questions.q: Following यथा + उत्तरम् = यथोत्तरम्, how is यथा + उक्तम् (as said) joined?
optionExplain: औ is the result of आ + ओ or आ + औ, not आ + उ.
The आ does not simply vanish.
Right: आ + उ joins as ओ.
The two vowels do join.
questions.explain: यथा + उक्तम् = यथोक्तम्.
questions.teaches: A long आ followed by उ joins as ओ (यथा + उत्तरम् = यथोत्तरम्; यथा + उक्तम् = यथोक्तम्).

questions.q: What is one to do with the person described, according to the verse?
optionExplain: The verb is about disregarding.
No instruction is mentioned.
The verse says the opposite.
Right: सुतरामभ्युपेक्षेत: all the more, one should disregard.
questions.explain: सुतराम् means all the more, especially; अभ्युपेक्षेत means one should disregard.
questions.rule: सुतराम् अभ्युपेक्षेत = one should especially disregard.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
pairs: who has abandoned the good path
questions.explain: These are the four descriptions of the person.
questions.rule: आत्मद्रुहम् = injuring himself; अमर्यादम् = without limits; मूढम् = foolish; उज्झितसत्पथम् = has abandoned the good path.

questions.q: What does सुतराम् add to the verb?
optionExplain: Right: सुतराम् means 'all the more, especially'.
That would be a negative like न.
Nothing in the word means slowly.
Nothing in the word means together.
questions.explain: सुतराम् strengthens the verb: one should especially disregard.
questions.teaches: सुतराम् is an adverb meaning 'all the more, especially', placed before the verb it strengthens.

questions.q: How does the verse describe the person at its end?
options: As a lamp for the path
As fuel for the blazing fire of hell
As a guest to be fed
As the king of the people
optionExplain: The verse speaks of hell's fire, not of a lamp.
Right: नरकार्चिष्मदिंधनम्.
No guest is mentioned.
No king is mentioned.
questions.explain: The last compound is naraka-arciṣmat-indhana: fuel for hell's blazing fire.
questions.rule: नरकार्चिष्मदिंधनम् = fuel for the blazing fire of hell.

questions.q: Put the four descriptions in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Line 1 gives the four descriptions in this order.

questions.q: Following अमर्यादम् 'without limits', what does अधनः mean?
optionExplain: That would be बहुधनः or धनवान्.
That would be धनदः.
Right: The prefix अ- (अन्- before a vowel) means 'without'.
The ending -ः marks a nominative, not 'of'.
questions.explain: अ + धन = अधन, one without wealth, as अ + मर्याद = अमर्याद, without limits.
questions.teaches: The prefix अ- before a noun gives 'without' it (अमर्याद = without limits, अधन = without wealth).

questions.q: Which of these is one of the qualities of speech in line 1?
optionExplain: Not in the list.
Not in the list.
Not in the list.
Right: मितम् is in the list.
questions.explain: The six are धर्म्य, अर्थ्य, प्रिय, तथ्य, मित, पथ्य.

questions.q: Put the six qualities of speech in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Line 1 runs: in accord with dharma, purposeful, pleasing, true, measured, wholesome.
questions.rule: धर्म्यम् · अर्थ्यम् · प्रियम् · तथ्यम् · मितम् · पथ्यम्.

questions.q: Match each quality of speech to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are five of the six qualities.
questions.rule: धर्म्यम् = in accord with dharma; अर्थ्यम् = purposeful; तथ्यम् = true; मितम् = measured; पथ्यम् = wholesome.
questions.teaches: The six qualities of speech include धर्म्यम्, अर्थ्यम्, तथ्यम्, मितम्, पथ्यम्.

questions.q: What does the verse say about whom one is not to praise or oppress?
options: It does not state the object
optionExplain: Right: स्तूयात् and पीडयेत् have no object in the verse.
No king is named.
No teachers are named.
No enemies are named.
questions.explain: आत्मानम् is the object of अवजानीयात्; the verse names no object for the other two (whether आत्मानम् carries over is left open).
questions.rule: Objects of स्तूयात् and पीडयेत् are not stated.

questions.q: Which two are among the six qualities of speech?
optionExplain: Right: तथ्यम्.
Right: पथ्यम्.
Not in the list.
Not in the list.
questions.explain: The list is धर्म्य, अर्थ्य, प्रिय, तथ्य, मित, पथ्य.
questions.rule: Six qualities; तथ्य and पथ्य among them.

questions.q: Following धर्म्य 'in accord with dharma', what means in accord with justice (न्याय)?
optionExplain: This means 'possessing justice'.
Right: The suffix -य makes 'in accord with / fit for' (धर्म्य, अर्थ्य, पथ्य).
This is 'by justice'.
This is 'justice' itself.
questions.explain: न्याय + य = न्याय्य, in accord with justice, as धर्म + य = धर्म्य.
questions.teaches: The ending -य on a noun gives 'in accord with / fit for' it (धर्म्य, अर्थ्य, पथ्य, न्याय्य).

questions.q: Whom is one not to look down on, according to line 1?
options: Those superior to him in learning or in strength
Those who are angry with him or turn against him
The inferior in livelihood, limb, strength or learning
Those who are guests or who come to him for shelter
optionExplain: The verse speaks of the inferior.
Anger is not mentioned in this unit.
Right: हीनान् वृत्त्यंगबलश्रुतैः.
Guests are not mentioned in this unit.
questions.explain: हीनान् is the inferior; the instrumental names the four respects.
questions.rule: न हीनान् अवमन्येत = not to look down on the inferior.

questions.q: Put the four respects of inferiority in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The compound runs वृत्ति, अंग, बल, श्रुत.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Three of these are what he is not to be; the fourth names those not to be despised.
questions.rule: क्रूरः = cruel; तीक्ष्णः = harsh; उपतापवान् = causing distress; हीनान् = the inferior.
questions.teaches: क्रूरः, तीक्ष्णः and उपतापवान् are what he is not to be; हीनान् are those he is not to despise.

questions.q: Which is the right split of हीना नवमन्येत?
optionExplain: नवमन्येत is not a word.
आनवमन्येत is not a word.
That would join as हीनावमन्येत; the न् of हीनान् is still there.
Right: The final न् of हीनान् is written with the next word's अ.
questions.explain: हीनान् (the inferior) + अवमन्येत (should look down on).
questions.rule: A final consonant is written with the following vowel.

questions.q: Which two does the verse say he is not to be?
optionExplain: Right: न क्रूरः.
Right: न तीक्ष्णः.
Not said here; श्रुत appears as a respect of inferiority.
Not said here; बल appears as a respect of inferiority.
questions.explain: Line 2 negates क्रूर, तीक्ष्ण and उपतापवान् (and one damaged word).
questions.rule: Not cruel, not harsh, not causing distress.

questions.q: Following हीनान् वृत्त्यंगबलश्रुतैः, what does an invented विद्यया हीनः mean?
optionExplain: Right: हीन with an instrumental names the respect in which one is lacking.
हीन does not mean made.
हीन means lacking, the opposite.
Nothing in the phrase means afraid.
questions.explain: विद्यया (instrumental) says in what respect; हीनः says lacking.
questions.rule: हीन + instrumental = lacking in that respect.
questions.teaches: हीन with an instrumental names the respect in which one is lacking (बलश्रुतैः हीनान्; विद्यया हीनः).

questions.q: What is one not to raise against another, according to line 2?
optionExplain: The verse names the rod.
Right: परस्य दंडं नोद्यच्छेत्.
No blessing is mentioned.
No banner is mentioned.
questions.explain: दंडम् is the rod, punishment; नोद्यच्छेत् is should not raise.
questions.rule: परस्य दंडं न उद्यच्छेत् = not raise the rod against another.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words carry the prohibitions.
questions.rule: पापम् = evil; पापे = in the evil person; दंडम् = rod; निपातयेत् = should strike down.

questions.q: What happens in पापे + अपि = पापेऽपि?
options: The अ after ए is dropped and marked with the sign ऽ
optionExplain: That happens before other vowels, not before अ.
ऐ results from अ + ए.
Right: ए before अ stays and the अ is replaced by ऽ.
The अ of अपि is dropped.
questions.explain: पापेऽपि is written for पापे अपि.
questions.rule: ए / ओ + अ → ए / ओ + ऽ.
questions.teaches: After a final ए or ओ, a following अ is dropped and shown with ऽ (पापे + अपि = पापेऽपि).

questions.q: What does the verse say about the evil person (पापे)?
options: Toward him alone one may do evil
Toward him one should do evil only when angry
He should be given a gift
Even toward him one should not do evil
optionExplain: The verse says the opposite.
No condition of anger is given here.
Nothing is said about gifts.
Right: पापं पापेऽपि नाचरेत्.
questions.explain: पापे अपि = even toward the evil one; नाचरेत् = one should not do.
questions.rule: पापं पापेऽपि नाचरेत् = evil is not done even to the evil.

questions.q: Put these three prohibitions in the order of the verse.
items: not doing evil even toward the evil
not raising the rod against another
questions.explain: Line 1 ends with evil toward the evil; line 2 gives the rod and then the striking down.
questions.rule: Evil toward the evil · raising the rod · striking down.

questions.q: Following पापेऽपि, how is ग्रामे + अपि (even in the village) written?
optionExplain: Right: ए before अ stays, the अ becomes ऽ.
ए becomes अय् before other vowels, not before अ.
ऐ is not the result of ए + अ.
The ए does not become आ.
questions.explain: ग्रामे + अपि = ग्रामेऽपि, like पापे + अपि = पापेऽपि.
questions.teaches: Final ए + अ is written ए and ऽ (पापेऽपि, ग्रामेऽपि).

questions.q: Against whom does line 1 allow the exception to not raising the rod?
options: A son or a pupil who deserves correction
optionExplain: No guest is named.
Right: अन्यत्र पुत्रात् शिष्याद्वा शासनार्हात्.
No king is named.
The exception is limited to a son or pupil.
questions.explain: अन्यत्र means except; the exception is a son or a pupil deserving correction.
questions.rule: अन्यत्र पुत्रात् शिष्याद्वा शासनार्हात् = except a son or pupil deserving correction.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words carry the exception and the second prohibition.
questions.rule: अन्यत्र = except; शासनार्हात् = deserving correction; हिताय = for (his) good; उल्बणाम् = excessive.

questions.q: Which is the right split of पुत्राच्छिष्याद्वा?
optionExplain: च्छिष्यात् is not a word.
The word is शिष्य, not छिष्य.
Right: त् + श joins as च्छ; शिष्यात् + वा gives शिष्याद्वा.
That would be nominative plurals, but the words are ablatives (-आत्).
questions.explain: Three words are joined: पुत्रात् (than a son), शिष्यात् (than a pupil), वा (or).
questions.rule: त् + श → च्छ; त् + voiced sound → द्.
questions.teaches: A final त् before श joins as च्छ (पुत्रात् + शिष्यात् = पुत्राच्छिष्यात्), and before a voiced sound becomes द् (शिष्यात् + वा = शिष्याद्वा).

questions.q: What is the second line's prohibition about?
options: Dancing and singing of any kind
Giving the rod to a pupil
Excessive activity of the kind of dancing, music and singing
optionExplain: उल्बणाम् limits it to excessive activity.
No study is mentioned.
The rod belongs to line 1.
Right: नृत्यवादित्रगीतादिनोल्बणां क्रियां.
questions.explain: उल्बणा क्रिया = excessive activity; नृत्य-वादित्र-गीत-आदि says of what kind.
questions.rule: उल्बणां क्रियां न आचरेत् = not carry on excessive activity.

questions.q: Put these parts of the unit in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Line 1 runs: except, son, pupil, deserving correction, for good.

questions.q: Following पुत्रात् 'than a son', which means than a friend (मित्र)?
optionExplain: Right: Masculine -अ nouns end in -आत् in the ablative singular.
This is 'by a friend'.
This is 'of a friend'.
This is 'in a friend'.
questions.explain: पुत्र → पुत्रात्; मित्र → मित्रात्. The word अन्यत्र takes the ablative here.
questions.teaches: The ablative singular of masculine -अ nouns ends in -आत् (पुत्रात्, मित्रात्); here with अन्यत्र it means 'than'.

questions.q: What does line 2 say the lower garment must not touch?
optionExplain: The line says ऊर्ध्वम्, above, not below.
Right: ऊर्ध्वं नाभेः शरीरस्य: the part of the body above the navel.
The ground is not mentioned in the line.
No other person or clothing is named.
questions.explain: The line forbids touching the part of the body above the navel with the lower garment.
questions.rule: ऊर्ध्वं नाभेः शरीरस्य + अधरवाससा + न स्पृशेत्.

questions.q: Match each thing line 1 names to its meaning.
questions.explain: These five are the things the person is devoted to in line 1.
questions.rule: केश = hair; वाक् = speech; वेष = dress; शम = calm; सांत्व = conciliation.

questions.q: Which is the right split of स्पृशेन्नाधरवाससा?
optionExplain: The first word is स्पृशेत्, whose त् changes before न; it is not स्पृशेन्.
धरवासस् is not the word; the word is अधरवासस्.
Right: Final त् before न becomes न्; न + अ gives ना.
न्ना is not a word.
questions.explain: स्पृशेत् (should touch) + न (not) + अधरवाससा (with the lower garment).
questions.rule: त् + न → न्न; न + अ → ना.
questions.teaches: A final त् before न joins as न्न (स्पृशेत् + न = स्पृशेन्न); न followed by अ gives ना.

questions.q: Which does line 1 name as things he is devoted to? Choose all that apply.
optionExplain: Right: the first item.
Right: the second item.
Right: the fourth item.
Food is not in the line.
Sleep is not in the line.
questions.explain: Line 1 names hair, speech, dress, calm and conciliation; food and sleep do not occur.
questions.rule: परायण list: केश, वाक्, वेष, शम, सांत्व.

questions.q: Put the five things of line 1 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The compound runs केश, वाक्, वेष, शम, सांत्व, then परायणः.

questions.q: Take the compound धर्मपरायणः, built like शमसांत्वपरायणः. What does it mean?
optionExplain: परायण means devoted, not hostile.
'Born of' would be -ज.
'Free from' would be -वर्जित.
Right: X-परायण means devoted to X.
questions.explain: X-परायणः = one who is devoted to X.
questions.teaches: A compound ending in -परायण means 'devoted to' the first part (शमसांत्वपरायणः; धर्मपरायणः).

questions.q: What does line 1 say one should not delay after intercourse?
optionExplain: Right: शौचंप्रति विलंबनं: delay regarding cleansing.
Sleep is not named in the line.
Eating is not named in the line.
Speech is not named in the line.
questions.explain: The line forbids delay regarding cleansing after intercourse.

questions.q: Match each of the four acts in line 2 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four make the dvandva list that the uncovered mouth is attached to.
questions.rule: हास्य = laughing; क्षव = sneezing; उद्गार = belching; विजृंभण = yawning.

questions.q: Which is the right split of नासंवृतमुखो हास्य-?
optionExplain: आस्य (mouth) is a different word; it would leave the ह of हास्य unexplained.
Right: अ + अ gives आ; the visarga of -मुखः becomes ओ before a voiced sound.
The word is असंवृत (uncovered), not संवृत.
-मुखा would not give -मुखो.
questions.explain: न (not) + असंवृतमुखः (with mouth uncovered) + हास्य (laughing…).
questions.teaches: After -अ a visarga becomes ओ before a voiced sound (असंवृतमुखः + हास्य = असंवृतमुखो हास्य).

questions.q: Which translation of line 2 is right?
options: With the mouth covered one should not laugh, sneeze, belch or yawn.
With the mouth uncovered one should laugh, sneeze, belch or yawn.
With the mouth uncovered one should not laugh, sneeze, belch or yawn.
With the mouth uncovered one should not laugh, sneeze, cough or yawn.
optionExplain: असंवृत means not covered.
The न forbids them.
Right: असंवृतमुख: uncovered mouth; the four acts are all prohibited.
The list has belching (उद्गार), not coughing.
questions.explain: The line prohibits laughing, sneezing, belching and yawning when the mouth is uncovered.

questions.q: Put the four acts of line 2 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The list runs laughing, sneezing, belching, yawning.

questions.q: An invented word says शुचीभूय, built like मिथुनीभूय. What does it mean?
optionExplain: Nothing in -भूय means wishing.
-भूय is a 'having done' form, not a future.
भू here is 'become', not 'make' another clean.
Right: X-ī-bhūya means having become X.
questions.explain: मिथुनीभूय = having become a pair; शुचीभूय follows the same build: having become clean.
questions.rule: X + ई + भूय = having become X.
questions.teaches: X + ई + भूय is a 'having become X' form (मिथुनीभूय; शुचीभूय).

questions.q: What does line 1 say about scratching one's own head?
options: Not with both hands at once
Not with the left hand alone
Not on any day before noon
Not with a comb or a stick
optionExplain: Right: पाणिद्वयेन युगपत् … न कंडूयेत्: not with both hands together.
Left and right hands are not mentioned.
No time of day is given.
A comb or stick is not named.
questions.explain: Line 1 forbids scratching the head with both hands at the same time.
questions.rule: पाणिद्वयेन + युगपत् + न कंडूयेत् + आत्मनः शिरः.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These five words carry the three prohibitions.
questions.rule: पाणिद्वयेन = with both hands; युगपत् = at once; शिरसा = on the head; भारम् = load.

questions.q: Which is the right split of वहेन्न भारं?
optionExplain: The verb is वहेत् (should carry), not वहेन.
Right: Final त् before न becomes न्: वहेत् + न = वहेन्न.
ना is not a word here; the word is न.
न्न is not a word.
questions.explain: वहेत् (should carry) + न (not) + भारम् (load).
questions.teaches: A final त् before न becomes न्न (वहेत् + न = वहेन्न); the same joins कंडूयेत् + न.

questions.q: Which does the unit name as things not to do? Choose all that apply.
options: scratch the head with both hands at once
carry a load on the head
optionExplain: Right: line 1.
Right: line 2.
Right: line 2.
Not in the verse.
Not in the verse.
questions.explain: The verse names exactly these three prohibitions; the other two are not in it.
questions.rule: Three: both hands scratching, load on head, fire and water together.

questions.q: Put the three prohibitions in the order of the verse.
items: सिर को दोनों हाथों से एक साथ खुजलाना
आग और पानी को एक साथ ढोना
questions.explain: The verse gives scratching the head first, then the load on the head, then fire and water.

questions.q: How is तत् + च written when joined?
optionExplain: त् changes before च.
The त् becomes the unvoiced च्, not ज्.
Right: A final त् before च becomes च्, as in युगपत् + च = युगपच्च.
No स् is formed.
questions.explain: युगपच्चाग्निवारिणी is युगपत् + च + अग्निवारिणी; in the same way तत् + च = तच्च.
questions.teaches: A final त् before च becomes च् (युगपत् + च = युगपच्च; तत् + च = तच्च).

questions.q: Which body part does line 1 name first?
optionExplain: No ear is named.
No eye or brow is named.
No hair is named in this unit.
Right: नासिकां is the first word, accusative: the nose.
questions.explain: Line 1 begins with नासिकाम्, the nose; दशनान् (teeth) follows.
questions.rule: नासिकाम् = the nose; दशनान् = the teeth.

questions.q: Match each clear word of the unit to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words are clear in the print, though the verbs around them are doubtful.
questions.rule: नासिका = nose; दशन = tooth; छेद = cutting; भेद = splitting; मर्दन = rubbing.

questions.q: Which case and number is नासिकाम् in line 1?
optionExplain: Right: The -ाम् ending of a feminine noun marks the object, one thing.
The nominative would be नासिका.
The instrumental would be नासिकया.
The genitive plural would be नासिकानाम्.
questions.explain: नासिकाम् is feminine accusative singular, the thing acted on.
questions.teaches: A feminine noun in -ा has accusative singular in -ाम् (नासिका: नासिकाम्).

questions.q: Which word of line 1 means 'teeth'?
optionExplain: नासिका is the nose.
Right: दशन = tooth; -आन् is the accusative plural.
This is the verb (a form of 'tear at').
न is 'not'.
questions.explain: दशनान् is 'teeth', accusative plural.

questions.q: Put the four clear list words at the end of line 2 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The list runs cutting, splitting, snapping, rubbing.

questions.q: Taken as a dvandva, what does छेदभेद mean?
optionExplain: A dvandva lists both items; it does not make one belong to the other.
Nothing in the compound is negative.
Right: A dvandva joins items with 'and'.
The compound names acts, not two kinds of persons.
questions.explain: छेद + भेद in a dvandva = cutting and splitting, like the list छेद-भेद-आस्फोटन-मर्दन.
questions.teaches: A dvandva compound names several items side by side, 'A and B' (छेदभेद = cutting and splitting).

questions.q: What does line 1 say about making sounds with mouth, limbs or nails?
options: Forbidden only when there is no purpose at all
Allowed whenever there is some purpose to it
Forbidden only when it is done with the nails
Not without purpose, and not even with a purpose
optionExplain: The line adds 'even with purpose' (कार्येऽपि).
The line forbids it even then.
Mouth and limbs are named too.
Right: नाकार्ये न च कार्येऽपि: neither in the purposeless nor even in the purposeful.
questions.explain: Line 1 forbids the sounds in both cases: without purpose and even with a purpose.
questions.rule: न अकार्ये + न च कार्ये अपि.

questions.q: Match each word of line 1 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words make the pair 'without purpose / with purpose' and the three sound-makers.
questions.rule: अकार्य = without purpose; कार्य = a purposeful matter; मुख = mouth; अङ्ग = limb; नख = nail.

questions.q: Which is the right split of नाकार्ये?
optionExplain: Right: न + अ gives ना.
That would mean 'not in a purposeful matter', losing the अ of अकार्य.
नाक is not what stands here.
A long आ would give नाकार्ये only if आकार्ये were a word; it is not.
questions.explain: न (not) + अकार्ये (in what is without purpose).
questions.teaches: न followed by a word that begins with अ joins as ना (न + अकार्ये = नाकार्ये).

questions.q: The first word of line 2, meaning 'foot', is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: पादम् is the accusative of पाद, foot: 'one foot'.
questions.teaches: पाद is the foot; पादम् is the accusative, पादेन the instrumental ('with the foot').
questions.rule: पादं पादेन = (one) foot with (the other) foot.

questions.q: Put the three acts done to a foot, in line 2, in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Line 2 says: press, scratch, clean.

questions.q: How is न + अशुचि (न meaning not, अशुचि unclean) written when joined?
optionExplain: The अ would be lost, which sandhi does not do here.
Right: न + अ gives ना.
ऐ comes from न + ए, not न + अ.
ओ comes from न + उ, not न + अ.
questions.explain: As न + अकार्ये = नाकार्ये, न + अशुचि = नाशुचि.
questions.teaches: न + अ- gives ना- (नाकार्ये; नाशुचि).

questions.q: What does line 2 say to do repeatedly?
options: Oil the hair, the face, the hands and the ears
Cover the nails, the feet and the ears with cloth
Keep the nails, feet and seats of impurity clean
Cut the nails and the teeth, and bind the feet
optionExplain: None of these is named.
Covering is not mentioned.
Right: अभीक्ष्णं निर्मलान् दध्यात्: repeatedly keep clean.
Cutting is not mentioned.
questions.explain: The line tells one to repeatedly keep the nails, the feet and the seats of impurity clean.

questions.q: Match each word of line 2 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words carry the instruction of line 2.
questions.rule: अभीक्ष्णम् = repeatedly; निर्मलान् = clean; दध्यात् = should keep; नख = nail; पाद = foot.

questions.q: Which is the right split of नोपविष्टः?
optionExplain: न + उ does not give ना.
पविष्ट is not the word; it is उपविष्ट (seated).
There is no नु here.
Right: अ + उ gives ओ.
questions.explain: न (not) + उपविष्टः (seated).
questions.teaches: A word ending in -अ meets उ- and they join as ओ (न + उपविष्टः = नोपविष्टः).

questions.q: Which word of line 2 means 'repeatedly'?
optionExplain: Right: It means repeatedly, often.
निर्मल is clean.
दध्यात् is 'should keep'.
नख is nail.
questions.explain: अभीक्ष्णम् is 'repeatedly'.

questions.q: Put the three things kept clean in line 2 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The compound runs nails, feet, seats of impurity.

questions.q: How is न + उक्तम् (न meaning not, उक्तम् said) written when joined?
optionExplain: The vowel would not stay उ.
Right: अ + उ gives ओ.
ना would come from न + अ.
औ comes from न + औ.
questions.explain: As न + उपविष्टः = नोपविष्टः, न + उक्तम् = नोक्तम्.
questions.teaches: न + उ- gives नो- (नोपविष्टः; नोक्तम्).

questions.q: What does line 1 say about tending a fire that is unkindled?
options: One should tend it only at night
One should tend it with water
optionExplain: The न forbids it.
No time of day is given.
Right: नासमिद्धमुपासीत: not tend the unkindled.
Water is not mentioned.
questions.explain: असमिद्ध means not kindled; with न उपासीत the verse says one should not tend such a fire.

questions.q: Match each condition to its meaning.
questions.explain: These six conditions fill the two lines, one after another.
questions.rule: असमिद्ध = not kindled; अशुचि = unclean; अनुवातम् = along the wind; विवृत = uncovered; क्लान्त = weary.

questions.q: What does अन्यमानसः mean?
optionExplain: That would be an ordinary genitive, not a person described by it.
अन्य means 'other', not 'free from'.
The compound names the person, not a thought.
Right: A bahuvrīhi describes a person by what he has: अन्य-मानस, 'other mind'.
questions.explain: The compound describes the person: he whose mind (मानस) is elsewhere (अन्य).
questions.rule: A bahuvrīhi names the owner of the parts: अन्यमानसः = whose mind is elsewhere.
questions.teaches: A bahuvrīhi describes a person by what he has (अन्यमानसः = one whose mind is elsewhere; असंवृतमुखः = with mouth uncovered).

questions.q: Which does the verse name as conditions in which not to tend the fire? Choose all that apply.
optionExplain: Right: असमिद्ध.
Right: क्लान्त.
Right: अन्यमानस.
Anger is not in this verse.
Hunger is not in this verse.
questions.explain: Unkindled, weary and mind elsewhere are in the verse; anger and hunger are not.
questions.rule: Six conditions: unkindled, unclean, along the wind, uncovered, weary, mind elsewhere.

questions.q: Put the six conditions in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Line 1 gives unkindled and unclean; line 2 gives along the wind, uncovered, weary, mind elsewhere.
questions.rule: असमिद्ध · अशुचि · अनुवात · विवृत · क्लान्त · अन्यमानस.

questions.q: How is न + एकम् (न meaning not, एकम् one) written when joined?
optionExplain: Right: अ + ए gives ऐ, as in न + एव = नैव.
अ + ए does not stay ए.
No इ is inserted.
ओ comes from अ + उ.
questions.explain: The verse has नैव from न + एव; in the same way न + एकम् = नैकम्.
questions.teaches: न + ए- gives नै- (नैव, from न + एव; नैकम्, from न + एकम्).

questions.q: What does line 2 say one should not do constantly?
options: Walk about in crowded, noisy places for long
Gaze at moving, minute or unpleasant things
Speak of unpleasant things to other people
Handle small tools for a long time at a stretch
optionExplain: Walking is not in the line.
Right: सततं न निरीक्षेत चलसूक्ष्माप्रियाणि.
The verb is gazing, not speaking.
Handling is not in the line.
questions.explain: Line 2 forbids constant gazing at things that are moving, minute or unpleasant.

questions.q: Match each word of the unit to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words carry the two clear instructions.
questions.rule: आस्य = mouth; सततम् = constantly; चल = moving; सूक्ष्म = minute; अप्रिय = unpleasant.

questions.q: Which is the right split of चलसूक्ष्माप्रियाणि?
optionExplain: That loses the negative अ of अप्रिय, 'dear' instead of 'unpleasant'.
The first part has no long आ.
Right: आ here is अ + अ: सूक्ष्म + अप्रियाणि.
आप्रिय is not a word.
questions.explain: Three words are joined: moving, minute, unpleasant (अ-प्रिय, 'not dear').
questions.rule: अ + अ → आ: सूक्ष्म + अप्रिय = सूक्ष्माप्रिय.
questions.teaches: Two short अ meeting join as आ (सूक्ष्म + अप्रिय = सूक्ष्माप्रिय; न + अकार्ये = नाकार्ये).

questions.q: Which translation of धमेन्नास्येन is right?
options: One should not blow with the foot
One should blow with the mouth
One should not eat with the mouth
One should not blow with the mouth
optionExplain: पाद, foot, is not in this word.
The न forbids it.
The verb is धमेत्, blow, not eat.
Right: धमेत् + न + आस्येन: not blow with the mouth.
questions.explain: आस्येन is 'with the mouth'; धमेत् is 'should blow'; न forbids it.

questions.q: Put the three kinds of thing in line 2 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The list runs moving, minute, unpleasant.

questions.q: Taken as a dvandva, what does the invented neuter plural मधुरशीतानि mean?
options: One thing both sweet and cold
optionExplain: Right: A neuter plural ending -ानि lists adjectives, as चलसूक्ष्माप्रियाणि does.
-ानि is plural: several things.
No negative is in it.
The compound lists qualities of things, not an abstract noun.
questions.explain: Like चल-सूक्ष्म-अप्रियाणि (moving, minute, unpleasant things), मधुरशीतानि means sweet and cold things.
questions.teaches: A neuter plural adjective list ending in -ाणि/-ानि means 'things that are A, B' (चलसूक्ष्माप्रियाणि; मधुरशीतानि).

questions.q: Which of these does line 1 name among things not to gaze at?
optionExplain: The line says अमार्जित, not wiped.
Right: दर्पणममार्जितं: a mirror that has not been wiped.
No lamp is named.
No river is named.
questions.explain: Line 1 lists the inauspicious, faeces and urine, and an unwiped mirror.
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are the clear words of the two lines.
questions.rule: अप्रशस्त = inauspicious; विण्मूत्र = faeces and urine; अमार्जित = unwiped; उद्यन्तम् = rising; तपन्तम् = blazing.
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: What kind of compound is विण्मूत्रं?
options: A bahuvrīhi: one who has urine
optionExplain: That would be a genitive tatpuruṣa, which the pair does not need.
There is no negative prefix in it.
Right: Two nouns side by side joined by 'and' make a dvandva.
The compound names the two things themselves, not a person.
questions.explain: विष् (faeces) and मूत्र (urine) stand side by side, 'faeces and urine'.
questions.teaches: A dvandva puts two or more nouns side by side meaning 'A and B' (विण्मूत्रम्; हास्यक्षवोद्गारविजृंभणम्).
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: By this card's reading, where is the noun that the participles उद्यन्तम्, आयान्तम्, तपन्तम् describe?
options: In line 1 of this unit, as दर्पणम्
It is the word प्रतिभागतम् itself
optionExplain: दर्पणम् is a mirror and does not fit 'rising'.
चल is an adjective, not a noun for these.
That is another participle, and is doubtful.
Right: Unit 100 has no noun for them; this card joins them with the 'shining one' (भास्वन्तम्) of unit 101.
questions.explain: The participles are accusative masculine and wait for भास्वन्तम् in the next unit.
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: Put the three things of line 1 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Line 1 gives the inauspicious, faeces and urine, then the unwiped mirror.
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: Which phrase agrees with अग्निम् (fire, masculine accusative) to say blazing fire?
optionExplain: Right: A masculine accusative noun takes -न्तम्, like तपन्तम्.
-न्ती is feminine.
-न्तः is nominative.
-न्तीम् is feminine accusative.
questions.explain: A participle agrees with its noun: masculine accusative singular तपन्तम्.
questions.rule: Participle agrees in case, number and gender.
questions.teaches: A participle agrees with its noun in case, number and gender (तपन्तम्, masculine accusative, with a masculine noun).
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: Whose face does line 2 say one should not gaze at?
optionExplain: No child is named.
Right: न क्रुद्धस्य (मुद्रित: कुद्धस्य) गुरोर्मुखं: not the face of an angry teacher.
No guest is named.
No king is named.
questions.explain: Line 2 ends with the face of an angry (क्रुद्ध) teacher (गुरु).
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words carry the four sights of the unit.
questions.rule: उपरक्त = eclipsed; भास्वन्तम् = the shining one; तिरोहित = covered; अतितेजस्वि = excessively bright.
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: Which is the right split of नान्यदप्यतितेजस्वि?
optionExplain: दपि is not a word; the word is अपि.
अति is part of the adjective अतितेजस्वि.
Right: Each junction is a plain vowel sandhi; final त् becomes द् before the vowel.
तितेजस्वि is not a word; the prefix is अति.
questions.explain: न (not) + अन्यत् (other) + अपि (even) + अतितेजस्वि (excessively bright).
questions.rule: Final त् + vowel → द्: अन्यत् + अपि = अन्यदपि.
questions.teaches: A final त् before a vowel is written द् (अन्यत् + अपि = अन्यदपि).
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: The card reads भास्वन्तम् as which body?
optionExplain: The moon is called तुहिनांशु in unit 104; भास्वत् ('shining') is the card's word for the sun.
The unit speaks of being eclipsed, which does not suit a lamp.
The teacher is named separately as गुरु.
Right: भास्वत् is a common word for the sun; the card reads it so.
questions.explain: भास्वन्तम् is 'the shining one', taken as the sun; eclipse and cloth fit it.
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: Put the four sights of the unit in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The unit gives the eclipsed one, the one covered by a cloth, anything else too bright, the angry teacher's face.
questions.rule: उपरक्त · वाससा तिरोहित · अन्य अतितेजस्वि · क्रुद्ध गुरु का मुख.
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: How is तत् + अपि written when joined?
optionExplain: Right: A final त् before a vowel becomes द्.
The अ of अपि does not disappear.
The त् does not double.
थ is a different sound.
questions.explain: As अन्यत् + अपि = अन्यदपि, तत् + अपि = तदपि.
questions.teaches: A final त् before a vowel is written द् (अन्यदपि; तदपि).
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: Which of these states of a woman does line 1 list?
optionExplain: Sleep is not in the list.
Right: नग्नां is in the list: naked.
Weeping is not in the list.
Travel is not in the list.
questions.explain: The four states of line 1 are discharging, menstruating, naked and united with another.
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: Match each word of line 1 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words are the states listed for the woman.
questions.rule: स्रवन्ती = discharging; उदक्या = menstruating woman; नग्ना = naked; अन्यसंगता = united with another.
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: Which is the right split of नोदक्यां?
optionExplain: ना would come from न + अ.
The word is उदक्या, not दक्या.
Right: अ + उ gives ओ.
There is no ओ in the word.
questions.explain: न (not) + उदक्याम् (a menstruating woman).
questions.teaches: न + उ- joins as नो- (नोदक्याम्, like नोपविष्टः).
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: Which states of a woman does line 1 name? Choose all that apply.
optionExplain: Right: the first item.
Right: the second item.
Right: the third item.
Not in the line.
Not in the line.
questions.explain: Line 1 names discharging, menstruating, naked and united with another; asleep and weeping do not occur.
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: Put the four states of line 1 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Line 1 runs discharging, menstruating, naked, united with another.
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: Which word agrees with the noun बालाम् (a girl, accusative) to say 'naked'?
optionExplain: -म् is neuter or masculine.
-ः is masculine nominative.
-ा is feminine nominative.
Right: A feminine accusative singular adjective ends in -ाम्, like नग्नाम्.
questions.explain: An adjective takes the gender, number and case of its noun: feminine accusative singular नग्नाम्.
questions.teaches: An adjective agrees with its noun in gender, number and case: feminine accusative singular is -ाम् (नग्नाम्) or -ीम् (स्रवन्तीम्).
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: What does line 1 say about sleeping?
options: Not on the same bed with her
Only when lying on the ground
Not at all, in any place
optionExplain: Right: शयीत नैकशयने: not on one (the same) bed.
The ground is not mentioned.
No time of day is given.
It forbids the same bed, not all sleep.
questions.explain: Line 1 says one should not sleep on the same bed (एकशयने) with her.
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: Match each word of line 1 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These five words carry both prohibitions of line 1.
questions.rule: शयीत = should sleep; एकशयने = on the same bed; अश्नीयात् = should eat; तया = with her; सह = together.
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: Which is the right split of नैकशयने?
optionExplain: ऐकशयन is not the word; the word is एकशयन.
Right: अ + ए gives ऐ.
ना would come from न + अ, and then the ए would stay separate.
कशयन is not a word.
questions.explain: न (not) + एकशयने (on one bed, on the same bed).
questions.teaches: न + ए- joins as नै- (नैकशयने; नैव).
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: Which is right for न चाश्नीयात्तया सह?
options: And one should eat together with her
And one should not eat before her
And one should not eat together with her
And one should not sleep beside her
optionExplain: The न forbids it.
तया सह is 'together with her', not 'before'.
Right: न च अश्नीयात् तया सह: not eat with her.
The verb is अश्नीयात्, eat; sleeping was line 1.
questions.explain: अश्नीयात् is 'should eat', तया सह is 'together with her', and न forbids it.
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: Put the main words of line 1 in the order of the verse (leaving out न).
questions.explain: Line 1 runs: should sleep, on one bed, should eat, with her, together.
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: What does the invented compound एकासने mean?
optionExplain: एक is 'one', not 'every'.
There is no negative.
Nothing like 'higher' is in it.
Right: एक in such a compound means 'one, the same', as in एकशयने.
questions.explain: Like एकशयने (on the same bed), एकासने is एक + आसने: on the same seat.
questions.teaches: एक at the start of a compound can mean 'the same' (एकशयने = on the same bed; एकासने = on the same seat).
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: Which state does this unit make the condition for its prohibitions?
optionExplain: Right: नोच्छिष्टः: not (to do these) while ucchiṣṭa.
Weariness belongs to unit 98.
Nakedness belongs to unit 102.
Anger belongs to unit 101, and concerns the teacher.
questions.explain: The unit begins with उच्छिष्टः, one who has eaten and not yet cleansed.
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words carry the condition and the objects of the unit.
questions.rule: उच्छिष्ट = unpurified from food; तारका = star; तुहिनांशु = moon; दिवाकर = sun; शिरः = head.
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: Which is the right split of स्पृशेच्छिरः?
optionExplain: च्छिर is not a word.
Right: Final त् before श joins as च्छ.
The verb is स्पृशेत्, not स्पृशेच्.
There is no word छिरः; the word is शिरः.
questions.explain: स्पृशेत् (should touch) + शिरः (head).
questions.teaches: A final त् before श becomes च्छ (स्पृशेत् + शिरः = स्पृशेच्छिरः).
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: Which word names the sun in line 1?
optionExplain: तारका is a star.
तुहिनांशु, 'cool-rayed', is the moon.
Right: दिवाकर, 'day-maker', is the sun.
उच्छिष्ट is a state of the person.
questions.explain: The compound lists stars, then the moon (तुहिनांशु), then the sun (दिवाकर).
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: Put the five prohibited acts of line 2 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Line 2 runs: look, go, recite, sleep, touch the head.
questions.rule: पश्येत् · यायात् · पठेत् · स्वप्यात् · स्पृशेत् शिरः.
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: How is तत् + शरीरम् written when joined?
optionExplain: त् changes before श.
त् does not become श्.
The त् becomes च् and the श becomes छ; the sound is च्छ.
Right: A final त् before श becomes च्छ.
questions.explain: As स्पृशेत् + शिरः = स्पृशेच्छिरः, तत् + शरीरम् = तच्छरीरम्.
questions.teaches: A final त् before श becomes च्छ (स्पृशेच्छिरः; तच्छरीरम्).
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: The verse says one should not point out to another a cow in which state?
options: A cow that is being sold
A cow that is tied up
optionExplain: Right: चरंतीं: grazing, moving about, is named in line 1.
Sleeping is not named.
Selling is not mentioned.
Being tied is not mentioned.
questions.explain: Line 1 names two states of the cow: पाययंतीं (making someone drink) and चरंतीं (grazing).
questions.rule: Not to point out to another: a cow that is making (someone) drink or grazing.
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: Match each word of line 1 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words carry the whole command of line 1.
questions.rule: चरंतीं = grazing; गां = cow; निवेदयेत् = should point out; अन्यस्मै = to another.
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: Which is the right split of नान्यस्मै?
optionExplain: The card's word split has न (not) and अन्यस्मै; ना is not a word in this line.
Right: न + अ gives ना: the two short a-sounds join into a long ā.
आन्यस्मै is not a word in this line.
Neither part is a word here.
questions.explain: नान्यस्मै is न (not) + अन्यस्मै (to another): अ + अ → आ.
questions.rule: अ + अ → आ: न + अन्यस्मै = नान्यस्मै.
questions.teaches: When न meets a word beginning with short अ, the two join as ना (न + अन्य = नान्य).
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: Put these three in the order in which the verse names them.
questions.explain: The verse names the cow first (line 1), then, in line 2, the meteor and then Indra's bows.
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: Which of these are named in line 2 of the unit?
options: the halo of sun and moon
optionExplain: Right: it opens line 2.
Right: it is the second item.
Right: it is the last item.
Lightning is not named.
An eclipse is not named.
questions.explain: The three items are the halo, the meteor and Indra's bows; lightning and an eclipse are not in the verse.
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: By the same rule as नान्यस्मै, how is न + अग्निम् (not fire, accusative) written when joined?
optionExplain: The two a-sounds must join, not stay apart.
ए is the result of अ + इ, not अ + अ.
Right: न + अ joins as ना, so the अ of अग्निम् is absorbed.
ओ is the result of अ + उ, not अ + अ.
questions.explain: अ + अ → आ, as in नान्यस्मै.
questions.teaches: न + a word beginning with अ joins as ना (नान्यस्मै, नाग्निम्).
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: Line 2 says one should not state which thing of the fortnight?
optionExplain: No length is spoken of.
Rain is not in line 2.
A month name is not given.
Right: तिथिं पक्षस्य: the lunar day of the fortnight.
questions.explain: The first words of line 2 are तिथिं पक्षस्य न ब्रूयात्.
questions.rule: Not to state: तिथि of the पक्ष.
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: Match each word of line 2 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words make up the two commands of line 2.
questions.rule: तिथि = lunar day; पक्षस्य = of the fortnight; नक्षत्राणि = stars; ब्रूयात् = should tell.
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: Which is the right split of ब्रूयान्नक्षत्राणि?
optionExplain: Right: Final त् before न becomes न्: ब्रूयात् + न → ब्रूयान्न.
The verb is ब्रूयात्, ending in त्, not न्.
That would drop the final consonant of the verb.
A visarga would not turn into न्न.
questions.explain: ब्रूयात् (should tell) + नक्षत्राणि (stars): त् + न → न्न.
questions.teaches: A final त् before a word beginning with न changes to न्: ब्रूयात् + नक्षत्राणि = ब्रूयान्नक्षत्राणि.
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: Put the four parts of line 2 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Line 2: तिथिं पक्षस्य न ब्रूयात् | नक्षत्राणि न निर्दिशेत्.
questions.rule: तिथि न ब्रूयात् · नक्षत्र न निर्दिशेत्.
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: Which two things does line 2 say one should not state or point out?
options: the lunar day of the fortnight
optionExplain: Right: तिथिं पक्षस्य.
Right: नक्षत्राणि.
No month name is mentioned.
Planets are not mentioned.
questions.explain: Only the tithi and the nakṣatras are named in line 2.
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: By the model पक्षस्य (of the fortnight), how do you say of the month, for मास?
optionExplain: -एन is the 'by' ending.
Right: A masculine word in -अ takes -स्य for 'of'.
-ए is the 'in' ending.
-अम् is the object ending.
questions.explain: पक्ष → पक्षस्य; मास → मासस्य.
questions.teaches: A masculine word in -अ forms 'of …' with -स्य (पक्षस्य, मासस्य).
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: What does the verse say one should not do with an insult (अपमान)?
optionExplain: Nothing about revenge is said.
Nothing about forgiving is said.
Right: प्रकाशयेत् is 'should reveal'; with न it is a prohibition.
Nothing about forgetting is said.
questions.explain: The verb of the verse is प्रकाशयेत्, 'should reveal', with न.
questions.rule: न प्रकाशयेत् = one should not reveal.
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: Put the things not to be revealed in the order of the verse.
items: जन्म-लग्न, जन्म-नक्षत्र और धन का सार
questions.explain: Line 1 gives birth details and wealth, then the house fault; line 2 gives the insult and the master's lack of affection.
questions.rule: जन्म-लग्न… · गृहे मल · अपमान · प्रभु की निःस्नेहता.
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Three of these words name items of the verse; the fourth names the master.
questions.rule: मल = fault; अपमान = insult; निःस्नेहता = lack of affection; प्रभोः = of the master.
questions.teaches: मल, अपमान, निःस्नेहता name the faults; प्रभोः (of the master) ends in the 'of' form of a word in -उ.
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: Why does नात्मनो end in -ओ, from न + आत्मनः?
options: Two short अ sounds join to give ओ here
न always changes to नो before a vowel
The ending marks a dual number of the noun
Visarga after अ becomes ओ before ज
optionExplain: अ + अ gives आ, not ओ.
न does not change like this.
The ending shows a case, not a dual.
Right: आत्मनः + जन्म: अः before the voiced ज turns into ओ.
questions.explain: आत्मनः before जन्म- (a voiced sound) loses its visarga and gets ओ: आत्मनो.
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: Which of these does the verse say one should not reveal?
optionExplain: Right: गृहे मलं.
Right: अपमानं.
Right: निःस्नेहतां प्रभोः.
The master's age is not in the verse.
Not in the verse.
questions.explain: The verse names the house fault, the insult and the master's lack of affection; the master's age and a neighbour's quarrel are not there.
questions.rule: Not to reveal: गृहे मल, अपमान, प्रभु की निःस्नेहता.
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: By the model प्रभोः (of the master, from प्रभु), what is of the teacher, for गुरु?
optionExplain: Right: Words in -उ take -ओः for 'of', as प्रभु → प्रभोः.
This is the plain naming form.
-अवे is the 'to, for' form.
-औ is the 'in' form.
questions.explain: प्रभु → प्रभोः (of the master); गुरु → गुरोः (of the teacher).
questions.teaches: A masculine word in -उ forms 'of …' in -ओः (प्रभोः, गुरोः).
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: Which of these is named in line 1 of the list?
optionExplain: Rain is not named.
Right: रज (dust) is the third item of line 1.
Thunder is not named.
Lightning is not named.
questions.explain: Line 1 names front or east wind, sun-heat, dust, frost and harsh winds.
questions.rule: Line 1: पुरोवात, आतप, रज, तुषार, परुष अनिल.
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: Put the five items of line 1 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Line 1: पुरोवात, आतप, रज, तुषार, परुष अनिल.
questions.rule: पुरोवात · आतप · रज · तुषार · परुष अनिल.
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: Which is the right split of क्षवथूद्गार?
optionExplain: That would keep a long ऊ and lose a vowel in the join.
ऊद्गार is not a word here.
Right: उ + उ joins as ऊ.
Neither part is a word.
questions.explain: क्षवथु (sneezing) + उद्गार (belching): उ + उ → ऊ.
questions.teaches: Short उ followed by उ joins as ऊ (क्षवथु + उद्गार = क्षवथूद्गार).
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: Match each word of the list to its meaning.
questions.explain: Words from both lines of this open list.
questions.rule: पुरोवात = front/east wind; आतप = sun-heat; तुषार = frost; कास = cough.
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: Which of these are named in line 2 of the unit?
optionExplain: Right: उद्गार.
Right: स्वप्न.
Right: मैथुन.
Bathing is not named.
Speaking is not named in this line.
questions.explain: Line 2 lists sneezing, belching, coughing, sleep, eating and sexual union.
questions.rule: Line 2: क्षवथु, उद्गार, कास, स्वप्न, अन्न, मैथुन.
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: By the same rule as क्षवथूद्गार, how is गुरु + उपदेश joined?
optionExplain: The two vowels must join into one long ऊ.
ओ is the result of अ + उ, not उ + उ.
व् appears when उ meets a different vowel, not उ.
Right: उ + उ → ऊ.
questions.explain: गुरु + उपदेश: उ + उ gives ऊ, so गुरूपदेश.
questions.teaches: Short उ + उ always joins as ऊ (क्षवथूद्गार, गुरूपदेश).
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: Which activity does the list name in its second line?
optionExplain: Right: सुरापानं is named in line 2.
Gambling is not named.
Bathing is not named; only shade on a bank is.
Singing is not named.
questions.explain: Line 2 names shade on a riverbank, drinking liquor, and beasts of prey, fanged and horned animals.
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: Put the items of the list in the order of the verse.
items: हिंसक, दाढ़ वाले और सींग वाले प्राणी
questions.explain: Line 1: noisy wind, talk with tossing. Line 2: bank shade, liquor, beasts.
questions.rule: सशब्द वायु · उत्क्षेपवादिता · कूले छाया · सुरापान · व्याल-दंष्ट्रि-विषाणिन्.
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words build the second item of line 1.
questions.rule: हस्त = hand; भ्रू = brow; नेत्र = eye; उत्क्षेप = tossing.
questions.teaches: हस्त, भ्रू, नेत्र are body parts and उत्क्षेप is tossing; they build one compound word.
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: Which translation of हस्तभ्रूनेत्रोत्क्षेपवादितां is right?
options: Talk with folded hands, lowered brows and closed eyes
Talk with tossing of hands, brows and eyes
Talk with the hands, feet and eyes of a beast
Silence of hands, brows and eyes
optionExplain: That is the opposite of tossing.
Right: उत्क्षेप is tossing; हस्त, भ्रू, नेत्र are hands, brows and eyes.
Feet and beasts are not in this word.
वादिता is talking, not silence.
questions.explain: The word joins the three parts of the body with उत्क्षेप (tossing) and वादिता (talking).
questions.rule: हस्त-भ्रू-नेत्र-उत्क्षेप-वादिता = talk with tossing of hands, brows, eyes.
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: Which of these are named in the list of this unit?
optionExplain: Right: सशब्दमनिलं.
Right: सुरापानं.
Right: दंष्ट्रिन् is in the last word.
The verse speaks of shade on a riverbank, not a forest tree.
The wind is noisy (सशब्द), not quiet.
questions.explain: The list has noisy wind, liquor and fanged animals; the forest-tree shade and the quiet breeze are wrong.
questions.rule: In the list: सशब्द वायु, सुरापान, दंष्ट्रिन्.
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: By the model दंष्ट्रिन् (fanged, from दंष्ट्रा, fang), what does केशिन् (from केश, hair) mean?
optionExplain: Without is expressed by a negative word, not by -इन्.
Nothing in -इन् means cutting.
Right: -इन् added to a noun means 'having that noun'.
'Of' would be -स्य.
questions.explain: दंष्ट्रा → दंष्ट्रिन् (having fangs); विषाण → विषाणिन् (having horns); केश → केशिन् (having hair).
questions.teaches: A word ending in -इन् added to a noun means 'having it' (दंष्ट्रिन् fanged, विषाणिन् horned, केशिन् having hair).
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: With whom does the list name strife (विग्रह)?
optionExplain: Servants are not named.
Neighbours are not named.
Relatives are not named.
Right: विग्रहमुत्तमैः: strife with the best, the superiors (उत्तमैः).
questions.explain: Line 1 says विग्रहं उत्तमैः: strife with superiors.
questions.rule: Line 1: service of the low…; strife with superiors.
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: Put the five items said to be 'at the twilights' in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Line 2 after संध्यासु: eating, women, sleep, study, thinking.
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: Which is the right split of संध्यास्वभ्यवहार-?
optionExplain: Right: उ + a different vowel joins as व् + that vowel: सु + अ → स्व.
वभ्यवहार is not a word.
The locative ending is short -सु, not -सू.
स्वभ्यवहार is not a word.
questions.explain: संध्यासु (at the twilights) + अभ्यवहार (eating): उ + अ → व्.
questions.teaches: Short उ before a different vowel changes to व् (संध्यासु + अभ्यवहार = संध्यास्वभ्यवहार).
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: Match each word of line 1 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words make up the two items of line 1.
questions.rule: हीन = low; अनार्य = ignoble; अतिनिपुण = over-clever; विग्रह = strife.
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: Which of these are named in line 1 of the unit?
optionExplain: Right: हीन.
Right: अतिनिपुण.
Right: विग्रहमुत्तमैः.
Strife with them is named, not service.
Service of the low is named, not strife.
questions.explain: Service goes with the low, ignoble and over-clever; strife goes with the superiors.
questions.rule: सेवा: हीन, अनार्य, अतिनिपुण; विग्रह: उत्तम.
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: By the same rule as संध्यास्वभ्यवहार, how is मधु + अत्र joined?
optionExplain: ऊ comes only from उ + उ.
Right: उ before a different vowel becomes व्.
ओ comes from अ + उ.
The vowels must join.
questions.explain: मधु + अत्र: उ → व्, so मध्वत्र.
questions.teaches: Short उ before a different vowel becomes व् (संध्यासु + अभ्यवहार, मधु + अत्र = मध्वत्र).
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: Line 2 speaks of passing through the midst of which group?
optionExplain: No animals are in this compound.
None of these is in this compound.
Right: तोय, अग्नि, पूज्य are the three in the compound before मध्येन.
None of these is in this compound.
questions.explain: तोयाग्निपूज्यमध्येन यानं: going through the midst of water, fire and the venerable.
questions.rule: यान through the middle of तोय, अग्नि, पूज्य.
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: Put the three in the compound in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The compound runs तोय-अग्नि-पूज्य-मध्येन.
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: Which is the right split of तोयाग्नि-?
optionExplain: The card's split has तोय with short अ; तोया is not the member here.
आग्नि is not a word.
Neither part is a word.
Right: अ + अ joins as आ.
questions.explain: तोय (water) + अग्नि (fire): अ + अ → आ.
questions.teaches: Short अ + अ joins as आ (तोय + अग्नि = तोयाग्नि).
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words make up the phrase.
questions.rule: तोय = water; अग्नि = fire; पूज्य = venerable; मध्येन = through the midst of.
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: Which of these are named in the phrase before मध्येन?
optionExplain: Right: तोय.
Right: अग्नि.
Right: पूज्य.
No cow is in this phrase.
A bank is not in this phrase.
questions.explain: The phrase has water, fire and the venerable; a cow and a river bank are not in it.
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: By the rule that gave तोयाग्नि, how is जल + अग्नि joined?
optionExplain: Right: अ + अ → आ.
The vowels must join.
ए comes from अ + इ.
ओ comes from अ + उ.
questions.explain: जल + अग्नि: अ + अ gives आ.
questions.teaches: Short अ + अ joins as आ (तोयाग्नि, जलाग्नि).
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: What does line 1 say one should avoid, besides attachment to liquor?
optionExplain: These are not named.
Right: विस्रंभस्वातंत्र्ये स्त्रीषु: trust and independence towards women.
These are not named.
These are not named.
questions.explain: Line 1 has two objects of त्यजेत्: excessive attachment to liquor, and trust and independence towards women.
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: Put the four parts of line 1 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Line 1 runs: मद्यातिसक्तिं | विस्रंभस्वातंत्र्ये | स्त्रीषु च | त्यजेत्.
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: The verb meaning 'should avoid' in line 1 is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters).
questions.explain: त्यजेत् is the optative of √त्यज्, 'give up, avoid'.
questions.teaches: त्यजेत् = should avoid, give up.
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: One key word of line 1, and the verb and two key words of line 2.
questions.rule: विस्रंभ = trust; अधिवसेत् = should dwell in; वास्तु = dwelling site; गर्हित = condemned.
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: Which reading of line 2 is right?
options: One may live there for one day only, not longer
One should live in a site that its treatise praises
Not even one day in a site its treatise condemns
One should build a new site for a single day only
optionExplain: अपि with न means not even one day.
The treatise condemns it (गर्हित).
Right: नैकाहमपि अधिवसेत् वास्तु तच्छास्त्रगर्हितम्.
Building is not in the line.
questions.explain: न + एकाहम् + अपि + अधिवसेत्: not even for one day should one dwell.
questions.rule: Not even one day in a condemned site.
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: By the rule that gave नैकाहम्, how is न + एकम् joined?
optionExplain: A single ए would come from अ + इ.
आ comes from अ + अ.
ओ comes from अ + उ.
Right: अ + ए → ऐ.
questions.explain: न + एकाहम् gives नैकाहम्; likewise न + एकम् gives नैकम्.
questions.teaches: Short अ + ए joins as ऐ (न + एकाहम् = नैकाहम्, न + एकम् = नैकम्).
questions.section: क्या न देखे, क्या न करे

questions.q: Which kind of region does the unit name as one not to live in?
optionExplain: Right: नावैद्यं: not one without a physician.
Temples are not named.
Markets are not named.
Rivers are not named.
questions.explain: Six kinds of region are named; one is the physician-less region.
questions.rule: Not to live: व्याधिबहुल, अवैद्य, अनायक, अधर्मिजनभूयिष्ठ, उपसृष्ट, पर्वत.
questions.section: निवास और दस पाप-कर्मों का त्याग

questions.q: Put the six kinds of region in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Line 1: disease, no physician, no leader. Line 2: unrighteous people, afflicted, mountain.
questions.rule: व्याधिबहुल · अवैद्य · अनायक · अधर्मिजनभूयिष्ठ · उपसृष्ट · पर्वत.
questions.section: निवास और दस पाप-कर्मों का त्याग

questions.q: Which is the right split of नाप्यनायकं?
optionExplain: नायकं is not what the verse has; the word is अनायक.
Right: न + अ → ना, and अपि + अ → अप्य, giving नाप्यनायकं.
आपि is not a word here.
Neither part is a word.
questions.explain: न (not) + अपि (also) + अनायकं (without a leader).
questions.teaches: Several small words can join in one written word: न + अपि + अनायकम् = नाप्यनायकम्.
questions.section: निवास और दस पाप-कर्मों का त्याग

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four of the six regions.
questions.rule: व्याधिबहुल = abounding in disease; अवैद्य = without a physician; अनायक = without a leader; उपसृष्ट = afflicted.
questions.section: निवास और दस पाप-कर्मों का त्याग

questions.q: Which of these regions does the unit name?
optionExplain: Right: व्याधिबहुलं.
Right: नावैद्यं.
Right: पर्वतं.
No desert is named.
No coast is named.
questions.explain: Disease-ridden, physician-less and mountain regions are named; desert and coast are not.
