optionExplain: Visarga is not named in this unit.
Only ādāna gets the label here.
The label is given to ādāna.
Right: तयोः आदानम् आग्नेयम्: of the two, ādāna is āgneya.
questions.explain: आदानम् is the subject and आग्नेयम् says what it is.
questions.rule: तयोः आदानम् आग्नेयम् = of the two, ādāna is āgneya.

questions.q: Match each word of the sentence to its meaning.
questions.explain: These three words are the whole sentence.
questions.rule: तयोः = of those two; आदानम् = ādāna; आग्नेयम् = fiery, belonging to Agni.

questions.q: The word for 'fiery, belonging to Agni' is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: आग्नेयम् is the neuter form agreeing with आदानम्.
questions.teaches: आग्नेय is made from अग्नि; in the sentence it is neuter, like आदानम्.

questions.q: Which is the right split of तयोरादानमाग्नेयम्?
optionExplain: Right: A visarga after ओ turns into र् before a vowel.
That would be written तयोर्दानम्, without the long आ.
Dropping the visarga leaves no र् to join the words.
अग्नेयम् is not the word; the word is आग्नेयम्.
questions.explain: तयोः (of those two) + आदानम् + आग्नेयम्.
questions.rule: Visarga after a vowel other than अ/आ, before a vowel → र्.

questions.q: Put the words of the sentence in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The sentence runs: of those two, ādāna, fiery.

questions.q: Which word completes the invented line तयोः जलं ____, meaning the water of the two is cool, agreeing like आग्नेयम्?
optionExplain: This is masculine; जलम् is neuter.
Right: जलम् is neuter, so the describing word is neuter: -म्.
This is feminine; जलम् is neuter.
This is masculine plural; जलम् is singular neuter.
questions.explain: A describing word agrees with its noun: neuter आदानम् → neuter आग्नेयम्; neuter जलम् → neuter शीतलम्.
questions.rule: Describing word agrees with its noun in gender, number and case.
questions.teaches: A word that says what something is (आग्नेयम्) takes the gender and number of its noun (आदानम्, neuter singular).

questions.q: According to this sentence, what do the sun and the winds bring to men in ādāna?
optionExplain: Strength being built up is said of visarga, in the later unit.
Sleep is not mentioned in this sentence.
Right: नृणां दौर्बल्यमावहन्ति: they bring weakness to men.
Hunger is not mentioned in this sentence.
questions.explain: The last clause says they bring weakness to men.
questions.rule: आदान: the sun and the winds bring दौर्बल्य to men.

questions.q: Match each word of the sentence to its meaning.
questions.explain: The sentence names three tastes that are strengthened and one thing that is taken away.
questions.rule: तिक्त = bitter; कषाय = astringent; कटु = pungent; स्नेह = moisture.

questions.q: The word for 'sun' in this sentence is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: अर्कः is the sun, the first subject of the sentence.
questions.teaches: अर्क is one of the words for the sun; here it is the subject with the winds (वायवः).

questions.q: Which is the right split of अत्यर्थोष्ण-?
optionExplain: That would join as अत्यर्थौष्ण, and ओष्ण is not a word here.
अष्ण is not a word, and the उ would be lost.
ए + उ would give अत्यर्थयुष्ण, not अत्यर्थोष्ण.
Right: अ + उ joins as ओ: अत्यर्थ + उष्ण = अत्यर्थोष्ण.
questions.explain: अत्यर्थ (very) + उष्ण (hot): very hot.

questions.q: Put these parts of the sentence in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The two subjects come first, then the three things they do as participles, then the main verb: they bring weakness.
questions.rule: अर्कः · तत्संपर्काद्वायवः · सोमजं गुणमुपशोषयंतः · जगतः स्नेहमाददानाः · रूक्षान् रसांस्तिक्तकषायकटुकानभिप्रबलयंतः · दौर्बल्यमावहंति.

questions.q: In the invented line बालाः गायन्तः गच्छन्ति, what does गायन्तः say, like उपशोषयन्तः?
options: The place the boys go to
optionExplain: Right: A -न्तः present participle says what the subject does at the same time.
गायन्तः is plural and present, not past.
A participle in -न्तः is not a place word.
It is a present participle, not a future.
questions.explain: उपशोषयन्तः (drying up) goes with the plural subjects and says what they do while the main verb happens.
questions.rule: Present participle masculine plural in -न्तः = 'doing X' with a plural subject.
questions.teaches: A present participle in -न्तः (masculine plural) describes what the plural subject is doing at the same time as the main verb, as in उपशोषयन्तः.

questions.q: Which of the two, ādāna or visarga, is called saumya here?
optionExplain: Ādāna was called āgneya in unit 17.
Right: विसर्गः तु सौम्यः: visarga, however, is saumya.
Only visarga gets the label in this sentence.
Visarga is called saumya.
questions.explain: विसर्गः is the subject and सौम्यः tells what it is.
questions.rule: विसर्गः तु सौम्यः = visarga, however, is saumya.

questions.q: Match each word of the sentence to its meaning.
questions.explain: These three words are the whole sentence.
questions.rule: विसर्गः = release; तु = but, however; सौम्यः = gentle, of Soma.

questions.q: The word for 'but, however' is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: तु sets this sentence against the one before it.
questions.teaches: तु is a small word meaning but or however; it comes after the first word of its clause.

questions.q: Which is the right split of विसर्गस्तु?
optionExplain: ओ appears before a voiced sound; त is not voiced.
च would give विसर्गश्च; the word here is तु.
Right: A visarga before त turns into स्.
That would be written विसर्गात्तु, with त्, not स्.
questions.explain: विसर्गः (visarga) + तु (but).

questions.q: Put the words of the sentence in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The sentence runs: visarga, however, saumya.

questions.q: In the invented pair दिनं उष्णम्; रात्रिः तु शीतला, what does तु signal?
options: A contrast with the sentence before
optionExplain: तु marks a contrast, not a repetition.
तु does not make a question.
तु says nothing about time.
Right: तु marks 'but, however': the second sentence is set against the first.
questions.explain: तु sets रात्रिः against दिनम्, as विसर्गः तु is set against आदान.
questions.rule: तु = but, however: contrast with what came before.
questions.teaches: तु, after the first word of a sentence, sets that sentence against the one before it (विसर्गस्तु after आदानम् आग्नेयम्).

questions.q: What does the sentence say happens to men's strength in visarga?
optionExplain: Right: बलं चोपचीयते नृणाम्: the strength of men is built up.
Weakness is the word of the ādāna sentence (unit 18).
The sentence says it is built up.
Nothing like this is said.
questions.explain: The last clause says men's strength is built up.
questions.rule: visarga: non-dry tastes increase; strength is built up.

questions.q: Match each word of the sentence to its meaning.
questions.explain: The sentence names three tastes and calls them not dry.
questions.rule: अम्ल = sour; लवण = salty; मधुर = sweet; अरूक्षाः = not dry.

questions.q: The word for 'strength' is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: बलम् is strength, the second thing that increases.
questions.teaches: बल is strength; in the sentence it is the subject of उपचीयते (is built up).

questions.q: Which tastes does this sentence say increase in visarga? Select all.
optionExplain: Right: it is the first of the three.
Right: it is the second of the three.
Right: it is the third of the three.
Bitter is one of the dry tastes of the ādāna sentence (unit 18).
Astringent is a dry taste of the ādāna sentence (unit 18).
Pungent is a dry taste of the ādāna sentence (unit 18).
questions.explain: Visarga: sour, salty and sweet increase; bitter, astringent and pungent are the ādāna tastes.
questions.rule: Visarga: अम्ल, लवण, मधुर. Ādāna: तिक्त, कषाय, कटु.

questions.q: Put these phrases of the sentence in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The sentence gives the sun, the moon and the refreshed world first, then the tastes increase and strength is built up.
questions.rule: दक्षिणायनगेऽर्के · शशिनि चाव्याहतबले · शिशिराभिर्भाभिः शश्वदाप्यायमाने · अरूक्षा रसाः प्रवर्द्धंते · बलं चोपचीयते.

questions.q: What does the invented line मेघे गर्जति मयूराः नृत्यन्ति mean, with a locative phrase like अर्के?
options: When the cloud thunders, peacocks dance
The cloud thunders for the peacocks
After the peacocks dance, it thunders
optionExplain: मेघे गर्जति is a phrase with its own verb form, not just a place.
Right: मेघे गर्जति (locative) sets the circumstance, as अर्के … does.
Nothing marks the peacocks as the aim.
The locative phrase is the circumstance, not a later event.
questions.explain: In the verse, locative phrases like अर्के, शशिनि, जगति give the circumstances, then the main clause follows.
questions.rule: Locative noun + locative participle = 'when X is so'.
questions.teaches: A noun with a participle, both in the locative (अर्के दक्षिणायनगे), sets the circumstance 'when X is so' before the main clause.

questions.q: What does भवति चात्र do in the text?
optionExplain: The chapter continues after this line.
No season is named in this line.
Right: 'And on this matter there is the following': then verses come.
No food is named in this line.
questions.explain: The line points ahead to what is said next.
questions.rule: भवति चात्र = and on this there is (the following).

questions.q: Match each word of the line to its meaning.
questions.explain: These three words are the whole line.
questions.rule: भवति = there is; च = and; अत्र = here, on this.

questions.q: The word for 'here, on this' is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: अत्र means here or on this matter.
questions.teaches: अत्र is a small word of place: here; with a matter it means on this.

questions.q: Which is the right split of चात्र?
optionExplain: चा is not a word.
आत्र is not a word.
A visarga here would not give चात्र.
Right: अ + अ joins as आ: च + अत्र = चात्र.
questions.explain: च (and) + अत्र (here).

questions.q: Put the words of the line in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The line runs: there is, and, here.

questions.q: Which is the correct joining of तथा + अत्र?
optionExplain: Right: आ + अ joins as आ, like च + अत्र = चात्र.
The long आ stays long; it is not shortened.
ऐ would come from आ + ए or ऐ, not from आ + अ.
ओ would come from आ + उ, not from आ + अ.
questions.explain: Same rule as चात्र: a or ā meeting a or ā gives ā.
questions.teaches: When अ or आ meets अ or आ, the two become one long आ (च + अत्र = चात्र; तथा + अत्र = तथात्र).

questions.q: In Śarad and Vasanta, how is the strength of visarga and ādāna graded?
optionExplain: Low is the grade of Varṣā and Nidāgha.
Right: शरद्वसन्तयोः मध्यम्: in Śarad and Vasanta, middling.
No season is said to have none.
Varṣā goes with Nidāgha and is low.
questions.explain: The second line gives Śarad and Vasanta as middling.
questions.rule: Śarad, Vasanta: middling; Varṣā, Nidāgha: low.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words carry the grades, the strength and a season name.
questions.rule: मध्यम् = middling; हीनम् = low, poor; बलम् = strength; निदाघः = hot season.

questions.q: The word for 'low, poor' is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: हीनम् is the grade given to Varṣā and Nidāgha.
questions.teaches: हीन means lacking, low; it is neuter to agree with बलम्.

questions.q: Which two seasons does the verse pair together with the grade 'low'?
optionExplain: That pair is middling, not low.
The verse does not pair these two.
Right: वर्षा निदाघयोः are joined and given हीनम्.
The verse does not pair these two.
questions.explain: The verse gives its pairs as: Hemanta-Śiśira, Śarad-Vasanta, Varṣā-Nidāgha.

questions.q: Put the three pairs of seasons in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The verse takes Hemanta and Śiśira first, then Śarad and Vasanta, then Varṣā and Nidāgha.
questions.rule: हेमंते शिशिरे च · शरद्वसंतयोः · वर्षा निदाघयोः.

questions.q: What does the invented word ग्रीष्मवसन्तयोः mean, built like शरद्वसन्तयोः?
options: In the many seasons from Grīṣma
Of or in the two, Grīṣma and Vasanta
optionExplain: A joined pair names two things, not one.
-योः is dual, not many.
The ending does not mean after.
Right: A joined pair with the dual ending -योः names both together.
questions.explain: शरद्वसन्तयोः = Śarad and Vasanta, the two; ग्रीष्मवसन्तयोः works the same way.
questions.rule: Joined pair + -योः = the two named, together.
questions.teaches: Two nouns joined into one word with the dual ending -योः name both together (शरद्वसन्तयोः, 'of or in Śarad and Vasanta').

questions.q: Because of the wind's coldness, what does the north do in this verse?
options: Makes the hair stand on end
optionExplain: Right: मरुच्छैत्यादुत्तरो रोमहर्षणः: from the wind's coldness the north causes horripilation.
Steaming rivers are in a later verse.
Flowering plants are in the verse after this one.
The verse says the opposite: dim and clouded.
questions.explain: The second line ends with रोमहर्षणः, causing the hair to stand on end.
questions.rule: उत्तरः + रोमहर्षणः: the north makes the hair stand on end.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
pairs: causing the hair to stand on end
questions.explain: These four words describe what the verse shows.
questions.rule: धूमधूम्राः = smoke-grey; रजोमन्दाः = dim with dust; तुषाराविलमण्डलाः = discs clouded by frost; रोमहर्षणः = hair-raising.

questions.q: The word for 'frost' (as in तुषार-आविल) is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: तुषार is frost, the cause of the cloudy discs.
questions.teaches: तुषार names frost; in the compound it is the first member: clouded by frost.

questions.q: Which is the right split of मरुच्छैत्यादुत्तरो?
optionExplain: A visarga before श would give मरुश्शैत्यात्.
Right: त् before श joins as च्छ; शैत्यात् + उत्तरः gives शैत्यादुत्तरः.
सैत्यात् is not a word; the word is शैत्यात्.
त् + च gives च्च, not च्छ, and चैत्य is not coldness.
questions.explain: मरुत् (wind) + शैत्यात् (from coldness) + उत्तरः (north).
questions.rule: त् + श → च्छ; त् before a vowel-led word → द्.

questions.q: Put these words of the verse in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The verse gives the three descriptions first, then the cold wind and the hair-raising north.

questions.q: Built like तुषाराविलमण्डलाः, what does the invented मेघावृतशिखराः describe?
options: Things that cover peaks with clouds
Things whose peaks are covered by clouds
Peaks that are made of cloud
optionExplain: आवृत is passive: covered, not covering.
The clouds are the covering, not the owners of the peaks.
Right: First part says by what, then the state, then whose: मेघ + आवृत + शिखराः.
आवृत means covered, not made of.
questions.explain: तुषार-आविल-मण्डलाः = those with discs clouded by frost; मेघ-आवृत-शिखराः = those with peaks covered by clouds.
questions.rule: By-what + state + whose, all in one word.
questions.teaches: A compound can say 'by what, in what state, whose': तुषार (frost) + आविल (clouded) + मण्डल (disc) = those whose discs are clouded by frost.

questions.q: Which of these creatures does the verse name among the spirited (दृप्त) ones?
optionExplain: Cows are not named in the verse.
Deer are not named in the verse.
Dogs are not named in the verse.
Right: वायस is the fifth of the six animals named.
questions.explain: The six are elephants, goats, buffaloes, horses, crows and pigs.
questions.rule: दृप्त: गज, अज, महिष, वाजि, वायस, सूकर.

questions.q: Match each animal word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These five of the six animal words are in the second line.
questions.rule: गज = elephant; अज = goat; महिष = buffalo; वायस = crow; सूकर = pig.

questions.q: The word for spirited or proud, as in the second line, is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: दृप्ताः says what the six animals are.
questions.teaches: दृप्त describes the animals in the plural; the print drops the final visarga before the voiced ग.

questions.q: Which is the right split of कुसुमोज्ज्वलाः?
optionExplain: Right: अ + उ joins as ओ: कुसुम + उज्ज्वलाः = कुसुमोज्ज्वलाः.
That would join as कुसुमौज्ज्वलाः, with औ.
That would be written कुसुम उज्ज्वलाः.
The उ would be lost, and the word is उज्ज्वल.
questions.explain: कुसुम (blossom) + उज्ज्वलाः (bright): bright with blossoms.

questions.q: Put the six animals in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The second line runs: elephants, goats, buffaloes, horses, crows, pigs.
questions.rule: गज · अज · महिष · वाजि · वायस · सूकर.

questions.q: What does the invented word मृगसिंहव्याघ्राः mean, with one plural ending at the end, like गजाज…सूकराः?
options: The tiger of the lion's deer
optionExplain: A dvandva joins separate kinds; it does not say 'like'.
Right: In a dvandva list, the members are joined without 'and' and one ending closes them.
No link of 'of' joins the members.
The members are different kinds, not names of one.
questions.explain: गजाजमहिषवाजिवायससूकराः is a list of six kinds joined into one word; the new word lists three.
questions.rule: Dvandva = members joined with 'and'; the ending sits on the last.
questions.teaches: In a dvandva list the members are joined with no 'and' and the shared plural ending sits on the last word (गजाजमहिषवाजिवायससूकराः).

questions.q: At the coming of the cold, what is said of the rivers?
optionExplain: Nothing in the verse says the rivers dry up.
Nothing in the verse speaks of flood.
Right: नद्यः सबाष्पाः सोष्माणः: the rivers have vapour and warmth.
The verse says warm and steaming.
questions.explain: The second line says the rivers are with vapour and with warmth.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These five words name what the verse describes.
questions.rule: मीन = fish; विहंगम = bird; नद्यः = rivers; कूप = well; आपः = waters.

questions.q: The word for 'rivers' is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: नद्यः is the plural of नदी, river.
questions.teaches: नदी (river) has the plural नद्यः, the subject of the second line.

questions.q: Which is the right split of कूपापश्च?
optionExplain: श्च is not a word; the श् comes from a visarga.
श्च is not a word; the word is च.
That would be written कूप आपश्च, with the visarga lost.
Right: अ + आ joins as आ, and a visarga before च turns into श्.
questions.explain: कूप (well) + आपः (waters) + च (and).
questions.rule: अ + आ → आ; visarga + च → श्च.

questions.q: Put these phrases of the verse in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The verse gives the two descriptions, then the rivers, steaming and warm, then the well waters and the time.
questions.rule: हिमानीपटलच्छन्नाः · लीनमीनविहंगमाः · नद्यः · सबाष्पाः सोष्माणः · कूपापश्च · हिमागमे.

questions.q: What does the invented word सजलाः mean, with the prefix स- as in सबाष्पाः?
optionExplain: Right: स- at the start of such a word means with, having.
स- gives 'with'; 'without' would be निर्- or अ-.
'Born of' would end in -ज.
'Like' would end in -वत् or -सम.
questions.explain: सबाष्पाः = with vapour; सजलाः = with water.
questions.teaches: स- at the start of a compound means 'with, having' what the next word names (सबाष्पाः 'with vapour', सोष्माणः 'with warmth').

questions.q: In the cold, struck by cold wind, what do the heats of the body do?
optionExplain: The verse says inside, not out.
Right: देहोष्माणः विशन्तः अन्तः: the heats of the body enter inside (अन्तः).
Nothing of the kind is in the verse.
The verse says they go inside.
questions.explain: The first line says the heats of the body enter inside.
questions.rule: शीत + ठंडी वायु → देह की ऊष्माएँ भीतर.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These five words carry the sequence of the verse.
questions.rule: देहोष्माणः = heats of the body; विशन्तः = entering; जठरे = in the belly; अनलम् = fire; प्रबलम् = strong.

questions.q: The word for 'fire', the thing made strong, in the second line is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: अनलम् is the fire made strong, the object of कुर्वते.
questions.teaches: अनल is a word for fire; in the print the अ is the avagraha after कुर्वते.

questions.q: Which is the right split of पिंडितोष्माणं?
optionExplain: That would join as पिण्डितौष्माणम्, with औ.
That would be written पिण्डित ऊष्माणम्.
Right: अ + ऊ joins as ओ: पिण्डित + ऊष्माणम् = पिण्डितोष्माणम्.
The ऊ would be lost, and the word is ऊष्माण.
questions.explain: पिण्डित (massed) + ऊष्माणम् (heat): with heat massed together.

questions.q: Put these phrases of the verse in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The verse goes from the heats of the body, entering, struck by cold wind, to the belly and the fire made strong.
questions.rule: देहोष्माणः · विशंतः · शीते शीतानिलाहताः · जठरे · पिंडितोष्माणं प्रबलं · कुर्वते अनलम्.

questions.q: Built like अनलं प्रबलं कुर्वते, which invented line means they make the water cool?
optionExplain: जलस्य is 'of the water', not the thing made.
शीतलेन is 'by the cool one', not the result.
जले is 'in the water', not the thing made.
Right: 'Make X Y': both X and Y stand in the accusative, then the verb.
questions.explain: अनलम् and प्रबलम् both stand in the accusative with कुर्वते: make the fire strong.
questions.rule: Make X Y: X and Y in the accusative + the verb of making.
questions.teaches: With 'make' (कृ), the thing made and what it becomes both stand in the accusative: अनलं प्रबलं कुर्वते, 'they make the fire strong'.

questions.q: Line 1 of this unit speaks of the strong in which period?
optionExplain: Right: विसर्गे बलिनाम्: in visarga, of the strong.
Ādāna is not named in this unit.
Only visarga is named here.
विसर्गे names the period.
questions.explain: The first word of the unit, विसर्गे, names the period.
questions.rule: विसर्गे बलिनाम् = in visarga, of the strong.

questions.q: Match each word of line 1 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words are the clear ones in the first line.
questions.rule: विसर्गे = in visarga; बलिनाम् = of the strong; प्रायः = generally; क्षमम् = capable.

questions.q: The word for 'generally' is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: प्रायः means generally, for the most part.
questions.teaches: प्रायः is a small word that softens a claim: generally, mostly.

questions.q: Which is the right split of बृंहणान्यन्नपानानि?
optionExplain: ए + अ would give ए with an avagraha, not ण्य.
Right: इ before a different vowel becomes य्: णि + अ gives ण्य.
A word ending in -य does not join as -ण्य + अ.
न्यन्नपानानि is not a word.
questions.explain: बृंहणानि (nourishing) + अन्नपानानि (foods and drinks), both neuter plural.
questions.rule: इ + a different vowel → य् + that vowel.

questions.q: Put the parts of line 2 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The line runs: nourishing, foods and drinks, one should apply, for the right use of that.

questions.q: Built like योजयेत् (one should apply), which invented form means one should go?
optionExplain: This is the plain present: he goes.
This is a past form: he went.
Right: The ending -एत् marks 'one should' or 'may'.
This is a future form: he will go.
questions.explain: योजयेत् ends in -एत्, the 'should' form; गच्छेत् ends the same way.
questions.teaches: The ending -एत् on a verb (योजयेत्, गच्छेत्) says 'one should' or 'may', for one person.

questions.q: What does the unit say the fire would do without fuel (अनिंधनः)?
optionExplain: The unit says it would subside, not blaze up.
That is the other alternative, introduced by 'or else' and tied to excess.
The wind (marut) is named only after the dhātus are depleted.
Right: सीदेत् is 'would subside'; अनिंधनः is 'without fuel'.
questions.explain: अनिंधनः = without fuel; सीदेत् = would subside.
questions.rule: अनिंधनः ... सीदेत् = without fuel it would subside.

questions.q: Match each word of the unit to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words carry the two alternatives and the step after them.
questions.rule: अनिंधनः = without fuel; सीदेत् = would subside; धातून् = dhātus; क्षयात् = from depletion.

questions.q: Put these words of the unit in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The unit runs: without fuel, would subside; the dhātus, would digest; from depletion, the wind.
questions.rule: अनिंधनः · सीदेत् · धातून् · पचेत् · क्षयात् · मरुत्.
questions.teaches: The unit's chain is: no fuel, subsiding; or digesting the dhātus; then depletion; then the wind.

questions.q: Which is the right split of सीदेदत्युदीर्णतया?
optionExplain: Right: त् becomes द् before a vowel, and इ + उ gives य् + उ: अत्युदीर्णतया.
These pieces are not words.
A visarga after ए would become र् before a vowel (सीदेर्), not द्; and अत्य is not a word.
अतु is not the word; the form is अति (excessively).
questions.explain: सीदेत् (would subside) + अति-उदीर्णतया (through excess of intensity).
questions.rule: त् → द् before a vowel; इ + उ → यु: अति + उदीर्णतया = अत्युदीर्णतया.

questions.q: Where does the unit place the wind (marut) in its sequence?
options: Before the fire loses its fuel
After the depletion of the dhātus
At the same time as the digestion of the dhātus
Instead of the dhātus being digested
optionExplain: The first line speaks of fuel; the wind comes at the end.
Right: ततः तेषां क्षयात् मरुत्: then, from their depletion, the wind.
The wind follows the depletion (ततः), it is not simultaneous.
The depletion follows the digesting of the dhātus.
questions.explain: ततः = then; the wind comes from (after) the depletion of the dhātus. What the wind does is in the next unit.
questions.rule: ततः तेषां क्षयात् मरुत् = then, from their depletion, the wind.

questions.q: Like पचेत् (would digest), which form means it would burn (√दह्)?
optionExplain: This is 'it burns', a plain statement, not 'would'.
This is 'burnt', a past participle.
Right: A 3rd-person singular optative of √दह् ends in -एत्, like पचेत् and सीदेत्.
This is the noun 'burning'.
questions.explain: पचेत् and सीदेत् are 3 sg optative, 'would digest/subside'; दहेत् is built the same way.
questions.teaches: A 3rd-person singular optative ends in -एत् (पचेत्, सीदेत्, दहेत्) and means 'would / should'.

questions.q: Which tastes (रस) does the unit ask for in the cold season (हिम)?
options: Bitter, pungent and astringent, with plain food
Bitter, sour and pungent, with dry food
Only sweet, with nothing else added to it
optionExplain: These three tastes are not named in the unit.
Bitter and pungent are not named, and the unit says unctuous, not dry.
Sour and salty are named too.
Right: स्वादु-अम्ल-लवण: sweet, sour, salty; also unctuous (स्निग्ध).
questions.explain: भजेत् स्निग्धान् स्वाद्वम्ललवणान् रसान्: one should use unctuous, sweet, sour and salty tastes.
questions.rule: Cold season: स्निग्ध + स्वादु + अम्ल + लवण.

questions.q: Put these words of line 2 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The line runs स्निग्ध, then sweet, sour, salty.

questions.q: Match each word of line 1 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words state when and why the disturbance is described.
questions.rule: कुप्येत् = would be disturbed; शीतः = cold; विशेषतः = especially; शीते = in cold weather.
questions.teaches: Line 1 says: it is cold and so it would be disturbed, especially in cold weather.

questions.q: Which is the right split of स्वाद्वम्ललवणान्?
optionExplain: Right: उ before a different vowel becomes व्: स्वादु + अम्ल = स्वाद्वम्ल.
वम्ल is not a word.
ओ + अ would give -ोऽ, not द्व.
A long ऊ would also turn into व्, but the word is स्वादु, short.
questions.explain: Three tastes: स्वादु (sweet), अम्ल (sour), लवण (salty).
questions.rule: उ + different vowel → व् + vowel: स्वादु + अम्ल = स्वाद्वम्ल.

questions.q: According to the unit, why is the instruction given (अतः, 'therefore')?
options: The fire has no fuel in the hot season
The cold one is disturbed, especially in cold weather
The tastes named are light and dry
Cold weather makes everyone hungry early
optionExplain: Nothing about a hot season is in the unit.
Right: अतः points back to line 1: being cold, it is disturbed, most in cold weather.
The unit says the tastes are unctuous.
Hunger is not mentioned.
questions.explain: अतः means 'therefore': the use of the tastes follows from the disturbance in cold.
questions.rule: शीते विशेषतः · अतो हिमे भजेत् = especially in cold; therefore, in the cold season, use ...

questions.q: Join a new example, मधु + अम्ल, as one word. Which is right?
optionExplain: The vowels would not simply drop.
ओ is not made from उ + अ.
Right: उ + a different vowel → व् + vowel, as in स्वाद्वम्ल.
A long ऊ needs उ + उ, not उ + अ.
questions.explain: Same rule as स्वादु + अम्ल = स्वाद्वम्ल.
questions.teaches: Final उ before a different vowel becomes व् (स्वादु + अम्ल = स्वाद्वम्ल; मधु + अम्ल = मध्वम्ल).

questions.q: What does the unit say about the wines (मद्यानि)?
optionExplain: Aged is not said; the word is अभिनव, fresh.
Dilution is not mentioned.
Boiling is not mentioned.
Right: Right: अभिनवानि = fresh.

A cloak is not named.
questions.explain: स्रग्वी = wearing a garland (the print has स्त्रग्वी).

questions.q: Match each word of line 1 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words describe the person.
questions.rule: स्नातः = bathed; स्वलंकृतः = well adorned; स्रग्वी = wearing a garland; रूषितः = anointed.

questions.q: Put these descriptions in the order of line 1.
questions.explain: Bathed, well adorned, garland, anointed with sandal and aguru.
questions.teaches: Line 1 lists four states of the person, ending with the anointing with sandal and aguru.

questions.q: Which is the right split of स्वलंकृतः?
optionExplain: That would give स्वालंकृतः, with a long आ.
लंकृतः is not a word.
सो + अलंकृतः would give सोऽलंकृतः, not स्वलंकृतः.
Right: उ + a different vowel → व् + vowel: सु + अलंकृतः = स्वलंकृतः.
questions.explain: सु (well) + अलंकृतः (adorned).

questions.q: The words विन्यस्तान् and अंकितान् end in -आन्. What does this show?
options: They qualify a plural noun elsewhere
They are verbs saying what is done
They name the garland of line 1
optionExplain: Right: Right: -आन् is masculine accusative plural; the noun is in the next unit.
The person is nominative singular (-ः).
They are participles, not verbs.
The garland is named by स्रग्वी in line 1.
questions.explain: The noun they qualify comes in the next unit.
questions.rule: -आन् = masc. acc. pl.; the noun is elsewhere.

questions.q: Join invented पुष्प + उत्पल as one word. Which is right?
optionExplain: The अ does not turn into उ.
Right: अ + उ → ओ, as in सहकार + उत्पल = सहकारोत्पल.
औ comes from अ + ओ, not अ + उ.
The vowels would be joined.
questions.explain: Same rule as in सहकारोत्पलांकितान्.
questions.teaches: A final अ/आ before उ gives ओ (सहकार + उत्पल = सहकारोत्पल; पुष्प + उत्पल = पुष्पोत्पल).

questions.q: Which of these is a drink named in line 1 of this unit?
optionExplain: पानक (a drink) is named in a later unit, not in this one.
शर्करा (sugar) belongs to a later unit.
Right: Line 1 names आसव, अरिष्ट, सीधु, मार्द्वीक and माधव.
घृत (ghee) belongs to a later unit.
questions.explain: The five names in line 1 are आसव, अरिष्ट, सीधु, मार्द्वीक and माधव.
questions.rule: Line 1: आसव · अरिष्ट · सीधु · मार्द्वीक · माधव.

questions.q: Put the five drinks of line 1 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The line runs आसव, अरिष्ट, सीधु, मार्द्वीक, माधव.

questions.q: Match each word of the unit to its meaning.
questions.explain: These five words carry the sense of the two lines: the drinks, the 'and' of line 1 and the 'or' of line 2.
questions.rule: च = and; वा = or; क्षौद्र = honey; वारि = water.
questions.teaches: च joins things together ('and') and वा offers alternatives ('or'); क्षौद्रवारि is 'honey-water', a compound of two nouns.

questions.q: Which is the right split of निर्गदांश्चासव-?
optionExplain: A visarga would give निर्गदाश्चासव, with no anusvara.
श्च is not a word; the श् comes from the joining.
अंश्च is not a word here.
Right: -ान् before च becomes -ांश्च; च + आ gives चा.
questions.explain: निर्गदान् (accusative plural) + च (and) + आसव: न् before च turns into ंश्.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT named in this unit?
optionExplain: Right: Coconut water is named in a later unit, not here.
क्षौद्रवारि is in line 2.
सारांभः is in line 2.
This is the first water of line 2.
questions.explain: Line 2 names three waters: with musta and śuṇṭhī, sāra-water and honey-water. Coconut water is not among them.
questions.rule: Line 2: three waters, joined by वा.

questions.q: In the style of क्षौद्रवारि, which compound means sugar-water?
optionExplain: Here वारि comes first: the compound would read 'water-sugar'.
Right: X + वारि means the water of X, as क्षौद्रवारि is honey-water.
The ending -ता would make an abstract noun, not 'sugar-water'.
The prefix अ- would negate it: 'water without sugar'.
questions.explain: In क्षौद्रवारि the first part says which water: honey-water. शर्करावारि is built the same way.
questions.teaches: A compound X-वारि (or X-अम्बु) names the water of X, with the first part telling which (क्षौद्रवारि = honey-water).

questions.q: Which of these does line 1 say one should avoid?
optionExplain: Exercise is avoided in a later unit, not in this one.
Wine is dealt with in a later unit.
Right: दिवास्वप्न is in line 1.
Bathing is not named here.
questions.explain: दिवास्वप्न (day-sleep) is the third item of the list.
questions.rule: Avoid: गुरु, शीत, दिवास्वप्न, स्निग्ध, अम्ल, मधुर.

questions.q: Put the six things of line 1 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The line runs heavy, cold, day-sleep, unctuous, sour, sweet.
questions.rule: गुरु · शीत · दिवास्वप्न · स्निग्ध · अम्ल · मधुर.

questions.q: Match each word of line 1 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These five words are five of the six things listed for avoiding.
questions.rule: गुरु = heavy; स्निग्ध = unctuous; अम्ल = sour; मधुर = sweet; दिवा = by day.
questions.teaches: दिवास्वप्न is दिवा 'by day' + स्वप्न 'sleep': a compound of two words.

questions.q: Which is the right split of मधुरांस्त्यजेत्?
optionExplain: A visarga before त would give मधुरास्त्यजेत्, with no anusvara.
स्त्यजेत् is not a word; the स् comes from the joining.
There is no word स्त्यजेत्; the verb is त्यजेत्.
Right: -ान् before त becomes -ांस्; त्यजेत् is the verb.
questions.explain: मधुरान् (sweet things, accusative plural) + त्यजेत् (should avoid).

questions.q: Which phrase does line 2 give together with 'in summer' (ग्रीष्मे)?
optionExplain: Right: तीक्ष्णांशुः means sharp-rayed.
The word is तीक्ष्ण (sharp), not cold.
The line says kindled by forest fire, not veiled by cloud.
The word is तीक्ष्ण (sharp), the opposite of soft.
questions.explain: Line 2 describes summer with: like the atasī flower, sharp-rayed (तीक्ष्णांशुः), kindled by forest fire.

questions.q: In the style of त्यजेत्, what does शिष्यः आलस्यं त्यजेत् say?
options: A student should give up laziness
optionExplain: A past act would use a past form, not -एत्.
Right: -एत् is the 'should' form, as in त्यजेत्.
A plain present would be त्यजति.
Nothing in the sentence says he has none.
questions.explain: त्यजेत् is the 'should' form of the verb त्यज् (give up); the invented sentence uses it the same way.
questions.teaches: The ending -एत् (त्यजेत्) says what one 'should' do; शिष्यः आलस्यं त्यजेत् = a student should give up laziness.

questions.q: What does line 1 say of the directions (दिशः)?
optionExplain: Nothing about darkness is said.
No cloud is mentioned in the unit.
Right: दिशः ज्वलन्ति: the directions blaze.
The unit speaks of blazing heat.
questions.explain: The first words say दिशः ज्वलन्ति, and the earth too.

questions.q: Put these parts of the unit in the order of the verse.
items: the wind is not pleasant from any side
questions.explain: Line 1 gives directions, earth and wind; line 2 ends with the creatures.

questions.q: Match each word of the unit to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words name what burns, what blows and who is affected.
questions.rule: दिशः = directions; ज्वलन्ति = blaze; मारुतः = wind; जन्तवः = creatures; ज्वरिताः = feverish.
questions.teaches: ज्वलन्ति ('they blaze') is a plural verb agreeing with the plural दिशः; भूमिः च is added to it.

questions.q: Which is the right split of नैकतः?
optionExplain: ऐकतः is not a word; the word is एकतः (from one side).
The 'not' here is the short न, not ना.
A visarga would not leave a bare न.
Right: अ + ए joins as ऐ: न + एकतः = नैकतः.
questions.explain: नैकतः is न (not) + एकतः (from one side), so 'not from one side'.

questions.q: What does the unit say about the wind (मारुतः)?
options: It is not pleasant from any side
It is pleasant from every side
It is pleasant only from the north
optionExplain: Right: मारुतो नैकतः सुखः.
The line says it is not pleasant.
No rain is mentioned in this unit.
No direction is singled out.
questions.explain: Line 1 says the wind is not pleasant (सुखः) from one side, read as from no side.

questions.q: Which is the right joining of सदा + एव?
optionExplain: That would drop the ā without a reason.
Right: आ + ए joins as ऐ, as अ + ए does in नैकतः.
ए does not become औ.
Sandhi joins the two vowels; they do not stand side by side.
questions.explain: आ (and अ) before ए join as ऐ: सदा + एव = सदैव, like न + एकतः = नैकतः.
questions.teaches: When a word ending in -अ or -आ meets ए, the two join as ऐ (न + एकतः = नैकतः; सदा + एव = सदैव).

questions.q: Which animals does line 1 name?
optionExplain: Deer and birds belong to a later unit about food.
Neither is named.
Right: मातङ्ग and महिष are the two animals of line 1.
Neither is named.
questions.explain: Line 1 names tall elephants (तुङ्ग मातङ्ग) and buffaloes (महिष).

questions.q: Put the parts of the compound in line 2 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The compound runs: sun, ray, ember, heap, consumed, waters.
questions.rule: दिवाकर · कर · अंगार · निकर · क्षपित · अंभस्.

questions.q: Match each word of the unit to its meaning.
questions.explain: These five words carry the picture of the two lines: the animals and the burning heap.
questions.rule: तुंग = tall; मातंग = elephant; महिष = buffalo; अंगार = ember; निकर = heap.
questions.teaches: In a compound like अंगारनिकर the parts follow one another: 'a heap of embers'.

questions.q: Which is the right split of तापार्त-?
optionExplain: अर्त is not a word here.
ताप is the word, with a short final vowel.
A visarga would not vanish inside a compound.
Right: अ + आ joins as आ: ताप + आर्त = तापार्त.
questions.explain: तापार्त = ताप (heat) + आर्त (distressed): 'distressed by heat'.

questions.q: What does line 2 say consumed the waters?
optionExplain: Right: दिवाकरकरांगारनिकर.
Leaves are mentioned in unit 45, not here.
The wind is not named in this line.
The animals are in line 1 and only make the water turbid.
questions.explain: Line 2: the waters are consumed by a heap (निकर) of embers (अङ्गार) that are the sun's rays (दिवाकर-कर).
questions.rule: दिवाकरकरांगारनिकर = heap of embers that are the sun's rays.

questions.q: In the style of कलुषीकृत, which word means made dirty?
optionExplain: -हीन means devoid of: 'devoid of dirt'.
Right: X-ई-कृत means made X: कलुषी-कृत is made turbid.
-स्थित means standing or kept in it.
-दीपित means kindled.
questions.explain: The pattern X-ई-कृत turns a quality into 'made X'; मलिन (dirty) gives मलिनीकृत.
questions.teaches: The form X-ई-कृत means 'made X' (कलुषीकृत = made turbid; मलिनीकृत = made dirty).

questions.q: What does line 1 say the trees (महीरुहाः) are devoid of?
optionExplain: Fruit is not mentioned.
Birds are not mentioned.
Right: छायाहीनाः: devoid of shade.
Roots are not mentioned.
questions.explain: छाया-हीनाः means devoid of shade.

questions.q: Put these descriptions in the order of the verse.
items: marked by dry bark and creepers
questions.explain: Line 1 gives the rivers and the shadeless trees; line 2 gives the leaves and the dry bark.

questions.q: Match each word of the unit to its meaning.
questions.explain: These five words are the things the two lines describe.
questions.rule: नद्यः = rivers; महीरुहाः = trees; पर्ण = leaf; वल्कल = bark; लता = creeper.
questions.teaches: In a compound the first part tells the kind: पर्ण 'leaf', वल्कल 'bark' and लता 'creeper' appear as parts of the compounds विशीर्णजीर्णपर्णाः and शुष्कवल्कललताङ्किताः.

questions.q: Which is the right split of नद्यश्छाया-?
optionExplain: ओ is made only before a voiced sound; छ is unvoiced.
नद्या would be a different case, not the plural subject.
श्छाया is not a word; the श् comes from the joining.
Right: A visarga before छ becomes श्: नद्यः + छाया = नद्यश्छाया.
questions.explain: नद्यः (rivers) + छाया... : the visarga changes to श् before the छ of छाया.

questions.q: What kind of leaves does line 2 give the trees?
optionExplain: Right: विशीर्णजीर्णपर्णाः.
The line says fallen and old.
Nothing says wet or heavy.
The line says fallen and old.
questions.explain: विशीर्ण (fallen) and जीर्ण (old) both describe the leaves (पर्ण).

questions.q: Which phrase means trees devoid of fruit, in the style of छायाहीनाः महीरुहाः?
optionExplain: -युक्त means joined with: 'with fruit'.
Right: X-हीन means devoid of X.
This is 'devoid of shade', not of fruit.
This is singular and in the wrong case.
questions.explain: फल (fruit) + हीन (devoid) gives फलहीन; it agrees with the plural trees: फलहीनाः वृक्षाः.
questions.teaches: A compound ending in -हीन means 'devoid of' the first part, and it agrees with the noun it describes.

questions.q: What does the sun do in line 1, according to the unit?
options: It gives back the world's moisture
It draws away the world's moisture
optionExplain: The verb आदत्ते means draws away, not gives.
The verse says the world's moisture, not only rivers.
Right: आदत्ते जगतः स्नेहं भृशम्.
No cloud is mentioned.
questions.explain: Line 1: the sun strongly (भृशम्) draws away (आदत्ते) the moisture (स्नेहम्) of the world (जगतः).
questions.rule: आदत्ते जगतः स्नेहं भृशम् — the sun draws away moisture.

questions.q: Put the six things of line 2 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The line runs exercise, sun, pungent, sour, salty, hot.
questions.rule: व्यायाम · आतप · कटु · अम्ल · लवण · उष्ण.

questions.q: The word for 'therefore' in line 2 is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: अतः means therefore: it brings the result of the reason given in line 1.
questions.teaches: अतः ('from this, therefore') begins the result; यतः ('because') begins the reason.

questions.q: Which is the right split of त्यजेदतः?
optionExplain: तः is not a word here.
दतः is not the word; the 'therefore' is अतः.
त्यजेः is a different person of the verb.
Right: A final त् becomes द् before a vowel: त्यजेत् + अतः = त्यजेदतः.
questions.explain: त्यजेत् (should avoid) + अतः (therefore).

questions.q: Which reason does the unit give for the avoidance?
options: the sun draws away the world's moisture
the wind blows pleasantly from every side
the rivers have banks grown high
the earth is cold and still
optionExplain: Right: यतः … आदित्यो भृशम्.
Unit 43 says the wind is not pleasant.
That is in unit 45; it is not the stated reason here.
The units speak of blazing heat.
questions.explain: The word यतः (because) introduces the sun's drawing away moisture; अतः (therefore) leads to the avoiding.

questions.q: In यतः मेघो गर्जति, अतः जनाः गृहं विशेयुः, which word introduces the result?
optionExplain: यतः means because: it begins the reason.
Right: अतः means therefore: it begins the result.
जनाः is the subject, 'the people'.
गृहम् is 'the house', the thing entered.
questions.explain: As in the verse, यतः gives the reason (the cloud thunders) and अतः the result (the people should enter the house).
questions.teaches: यतः ('because') opens the reason and अतः ('therefore') opens the result that follows from it.

questions.q: Which of these does line 1 give as a way to use wine?
optionExplain: Honey is not named in line 1.
Heating is not mentioned.
Right: सुबहुवारि is in line 1.
No time of day is named.
questions.explain: The line allows wine in small amount, or with much water (सुबहुवारि).
questions.rule: मद्यं न सेव्यं, स्वल्पं वा, सुबहुवारि वा.

questions.q: Put the four results named in line 2 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The line runs śoṣa, slackness, burning, bewilderment.

questions.q: Match each word of line 2 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The four results and the word that introduces them.
questions.rule: शोष = drying-up; शैथिल्य = slackness; दाह = burning; मोह = bewilderment; अन्यथा = otherwise.
questions.teaches: अन्यथा ('otherwise') says what happens if the condition just given is not kept.

questions.q: What does अन्यथा do in line 2?
options: it adds a further allowed use of wine
it gives the reason for line 1
it names the amount of wine
optionExplain: It does not allow anything; it begins the results.
A reason would be introduced by यतः.
No amount is given in the unit.
Right: अन्यथा means otherwise.
questions.explain: अन्यथा (otherwise) turns from the conditions of line 1 to what follows if they are not kept.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT named in line 2 as a result?
optionExplain: Right: Swelling is not named in the unit.
दाह is the third result.
शोष is the first result.
मोह is the fourth result.
questions.explain: Line 2 names four: śoṣa, slackness, burning, bewilderment. Swelling is not among them.
questions.rule: Four results: शोष, शैथिल्य, दाह, मोह.

questions.q: In the style of सेव्यम्, what does वन्द्यः गुरुः mean?
optionExplain: That would be a past form.
Right: -य after a verb root says 'to be done': वन्द्य = to be honoured.
That would be a present participle.
Nothing says this.
questions.explain: सेव्य is 'to be used', from √सेव्. In the same way वन्द्य is 'to be honoured', from √वन्द्.
questions.teaches: A word in -य made from a verb root (सेव्य, वन्द्य) means 'to be done': it says what should be used or honoured.

questions.q: In line 2, which word means 'cold'?
optionExplain: This means rich in sugar.
This means with mantha.
Right: हिम means cold.
This means drinks.
questions.explain: हिमानि is the word for cold; it stands at the end of line 2.

questions.q: Match each word of line 2 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are the five words of line 2.
questions.rule: पानक = drink; समन्थ = with mantha; सिताढ्य = rich in sugar; हिम = cold.

questions.q: Put the words of line 2 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The line runs पानकानि, समन्थानि, सिताढ्यानि, हिमानि, च.
questions.teaches: A line can be learned as a row of describing words after its noun: पानकानि first, then the three that describe it.

questions.q: Which is the right split of समन्थानि?
optionExplain: न्थानि is not a word.
थानि is not a word.
सा + म would stay long: सामन्थानि.
Right: स- 'with' + मन्थानि: with mantha.
questions.explain: स (with) + मन्थानि: with mantha.

questions.q: What gender and number do पानकानि, समन्थानि, सिताढ्यानि and हिमानि share?
optionExplain: Right: The data marks all four as neuter nominative plural.
A masculine singular would not end in -आनि.
A feminine plural would end differently, as in -आः.
A neuter singular would end in -म्, as पानकम्.
questions.explain: All four end in -नि, the neuter plural, so they belong together.

questions.q: Which phrase means sweet fruits? फल is neuter.
optionExplain: मधुरः is masculine singular; it does not agree.
Right: Neuter plural describing word and noun, like हिमानि पानकानि.
The noun फलम् is singular here.
मधुराः is masculine plural; it does not agree with a neuter noun.
questions.explain: A neuter plural noun (फलानि) takes neuter plural describing words (मधुराणि), as पानकानि takes हिमानि.
questions.rule: Describing word and noun agree in gender and number.
questions.teaches: A describing word agrees with its noun: a neuter plural noun takes a neuter plural describing word (-आणि/-आनि).

questions.q: Which of these is named in line 2?
optionExplain: Honey-water is in unit 41, not here.
Not named; the unit names sugar (शर्करा), not juice.
Right: नारिकेरांबु is in line 2.
Not named; the grain is śāli rice.
questions.explain: Line 2 names śāli, milk, ghee, grapes, coconut water and sugar.
questions.rule: शालि · क्षीर · घृत · द्राक्षा · नारिकेराम्बु · शर्करा.

questions.q: Put the six items of line 2 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The line runs śāli, milk, ghee, grapes, coconut water, sugar.
questions.rule: शालि · क्षीर · घृत · द्राक्षा · नारिकेराम्बु · शर्करा.

questions.q: Match each item of line 2 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five of the six items of line 2.
questions.rule: क्षीर = milk; घृत = ghee; द्राक्षा = grapes; नारिकेर = coconut; अम्बु = water; शर्करा = sugar.
questions.teaches: नारिकेराम्बु is नारिकेर 'coconut' + अम्बु 'water': the first part says which water.

questions.q: Which is the right split of नारिकेरांबु?
optionExplain: आम्बु is not a word.
रांबु is not a word.
A visarga would change into ओ before अ, not vanish.
Right: अ + अ joins as आ: नारिकेर + अम्बु = नारिकेराम्बु.
questions.explain: नारिकेर (coconut) + अम्बु (water).

questions.q: Which animals and birds does line 1 name?
optionExplain: Right: जाङ्गलान् मृगपक्षिणः.
The line says dry-land, not water-dwelling.
The line says dry-land, not marsh.
The line says dry-land (जाङ्गल).
questions.explain: Line 1 says जाङ्गल animals and birds, with the data's gloss 'dry-land'.

questions.q: Which is the right joining of द्राक्षा + अम्बु, grape-water?
optionExplain: The two vowels do not stand side by side.
Right: आ + अ joins as आ, like अ + अ in नारिकेराम्बु.
आ + अ does not become ओ.
आ + अ does not become ऐ.
questions.explain: When a word ending in -आ meets अ, the two join as one long आ: द्राक्षा + अम्बु = द्राक्षाम्बु.
questions.teaches: A word ending in -अ or -आ before अ joins into one long आ (नारिकेर + अम्बु; द्राक्षा + अम्बु = द्राक्षाम्बु).

questions.q: With what are the garlands of line 1 said to come?
optionExplain: Neither is named.
Neither is named; the necklaces are a separate item.
Right: स्रजः सकमलोत्पलाः.
Sandal is in line 2, applied to the women.
questions.explain: The garlands come with (स) lotuses (कमल) and water-lilies (उत्पल).

questions.q: Put the four listed things in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Line 1 gives fan-breezes, necklaces and garlands; line 2 gives the women.

questions.q: Match each word of the unit to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five of the things named in the two lines.
questions.rule: तालवृन्त = palm-leaf fan; हार = necklace; स्रज् = garland; मृणाल = lotus-stalk.
questions.teaches: कान्ता is a woman who is loved (a beloved); it is feminine, and the plural is कान्ताः.

questions.q: Which is the right split of सकमलोत्पलाः?
optionExplain: कमला is not the word here; the lotus is कमल.
ओत्पल is not a word.
A visarga would not show here.
Right: अ + उ joins as ओ: कमल + उत्पल = कमलोत्पल.
questions.explain: सकमलोत्पलाः = स (with) + कमल (lotus) + उत्पल (water-lily).

questions.q: How does line 2 describe the beloved women?
options: with gold bracelets, smeared with camphor paste
with lotus garlands, smeared with musk
with pearl bracelets, strewn with petals
optionExplain: Right: मृणालवलयाः, चन्दनरूषिताः.
The line says lotus-stalk and sandal.
The line says lotus-stalk bracelets and sandal.
The line says lotus-stalk and sandal.
questions.explain: Line 2: slender, with lotus-stalk (मृणाल) bracelets (वलय), beloved, smeared with sandal (चन्दन).

questions.q: What does रत्नवलयाः कान्ताः mean, in the style of मृणालवलयाः?
options: women who are bracelets of jewels
jewels that are the bracelets of women
optionExplain: The compound describes the women; they are not bracelets.
Right: A compound like X-वलयाः describes those who have X-bracelets.
The jewels are not the described subject.
Nothing in the compound negates the bracelets.
questions.explain: The compound रत्नवलयाः says 'having bracelets of jewels' and describes the women, as मृणालवलयाः does.
questions.teaches: A compound like मृणालवलयाः describes a person as 'having lotus-stalk bracelets'; it agrees with the noun it describes (कान्ताः).

questions.q: Which of these does the unit say to resort to?
optionExplain: Mountains are not named.
Deserts are not named.
Right: काननानि is in line 1.
Markets are not named.
questions.explain: Line 1 names lakes, tanks, rivers and groves.

questions.q: Put the four places of line 1 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The line runs lakes, tanks, rivers, groves.

questions.q: Match each word of the unit to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five things the unit names.
questions.rule: सरांसि = lakes; वापीः = tanks; सरितः = rivers; काननानि = groves; वासांसि = garments.
questions.teaches: Nouns in the accusative plural name the things resorted to; the verb निषेवेत tells what is done to them.

questions.q: The verb 'should resort to' in line 2 is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: निषेवेत is the 3rd person singular optative of नि-सेव्: 'should resort to'.
questions.teaches: निषेवेत: the 'should' form (-एत) of ni-sev, in the middle voice.

questions.q: Which two words are feminine plural (accusative) in line 1?
optionExplain: Right: tanks, feminine accusative plural.
Right: rivers, feminine accusative plural.
This is neuter plural.
This is neuter plural.
This is neuter plural, and it stands in line 2.
questions.explain: The data marks वापीः and सरितः as feminine accusative plural; सरांसि and काननानि are neuter.

questions.q: Which sentence means a student should serve the teacher?
optionExplain: सेवते is a plain present: 'serves'.
असेवत is a past form: 'served'.
सेविष्यते is a future form: 'will serve'.
Right: -एत is the 'should' form, as in निषेवेत.
questions.explain: सेवेत has the same -एत ending as निषेवेत, so it says 'should serve'.
questions.teaches: The ending -एत (निषेवेत, सेवेत) says what one 'should' do; the plain present, past and future have other endings.

questions.q: Where does the unit say one should sleep by day (दिवा)?
optionExplain: Right: धारागृहे: in a shower-house.
The open roof is for the night.
No cellar is named.
No tree is named here.
questions.explain: दिवा (by day) goes with the shower-house where water falls from a contrivance.

questions.q: Put these words of the unit in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The unit runs: where water falls from a contrivance, should sleep, in the shower-house, by day, at night, on the open roof.
questions.rule: निष्पतद्यन्त्रसलिले · स्वप्यात् · धारागृहे · दिवा · रात्रौ · आकाशतलके.

questions.q: The word for 'by day' is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: दिवा means by day, and it is paired with रात्रौ, at night.
questions.teaches: दिवा 'by day' and रात्रौ 'at night' set the two times of the unit against each other.

questions.q: Which is the right split of स्वप्याद्धारागृहे?
optionExplain: आरागृहे is not a word.
Right: A final त् becomes द् before a voiced sound: स्वप्यात् + धारा- = स्वप्याद्धारा-.
द्धारागृहे is not a word.
The verb ends in त्, not in a vowel.
questions.explain: स्वप्यात् (should sleep) + धारागृहे (in the shower-house).

questions.q: What does the unit say of the night place?
options: a closed room smeared with sandal
an open roof strewn with flowers
optionExplain: This is the day place.
No closed room is named.
Right: आकाशतलके सुगन्धिकुसुमास्तृते.
River banks are in unit 45, not here.
questions.explain: At night (रात्रौ) one sleeps on the open roof (आकाशतलक) strewn with fragrant flowers.

questions.q: Which sentence means one should sleep in the garden?
optionExplain: -आत् says 'from the garden'.
-स्य says 'of the garden'.
-म् makes the garden the thing slept, not the place.
Right: The locative -ए says 'in', as in धारागृहे.
questions.explain: A noun in the locative (धारागृहे, आकाशतलके) tells where; उद्याने is the locative of उद्यान.
questions.teaches: The locative ending -ए (धारागृहे, उद्याने) tells the place where something is done.

questions.q: With what are the limbs moistened, according to line 1?
optionExplain: Right: कर्पूरचन्दनार्द्राङ्गः.
Neither is named.
Water and flowers are in the earlier unit, not here.
Neither is named.
questions.explain: आर्द्र (moist) अङ्ग (limbs) with camphor (कर्पूर) and sandal (चन्दन).

questions.q: Put these parts of the unit in the order of the verse.
items: limbs moistened with camphor and sandal
questions.explain: Line 1 gives the two descriptions; line 2 gives the rains, the wind and the crops.
questions.rule: कर्पूरचन्दनार्द्राङ्गः · विरलानङ्गसङ्गमः · वर्षासु · वारुणो वायुः · सर्वसस्यसमुद्गमः.

questions.q: Match each word of line 2 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five words that carry the sense of line 2.
questions.rule: वर्षासु = in the rains; वायुः = wind; सर्व = all; सस्य = crop; समुद्गम = springing up.
questions.teaches: वर्षासु is the locative plural of the feminine वर्षा, used for the rainy months: 'in the rains'.

questions.q: Which is the right split of वारुणो वायुः?
optionExplain: That would join as वारुणा वायुः, with a long vowel.
Right: -अः before a voiced sound (व) becomes ओ.
ए does not turn into ओ.
-म् would stay as -म् or -ं, not become ओ.
questions.explain: वारुणः (Vāruṇa, kept untranslated) + वायुः (wind): the visarga becomes ओ before the voiced व.

questions.q: What does line 2 say springs up in the rains?
optionExplain: The line says all crops.
Lotuses are named in unit 50; the line says all crops.
Right: सर्वसस्यसमुद्गमः.
The line does not speak of rivers.
questions.explain: Line 2: in the rains the wind is Vāruṇa, and all crops (सर्वसस्य) spring up (समुद्गम).
questions.rule: सर्वसस्यसमुद्गमः = springing up of all crops.

questions.q: Which means in the garlands? माला is feminine, like वर्षा.
optionExplain: This is the locative singular, 'in the garland'.
This is the instrumental plural, 'by the garlands'.
This is the genitive plural, 'of the garlands'.
Right: -आसु is the locative plural of feminine -आ nouns, as वर्षासु.
questions.explain: वर्षा gives वर्षासु; माला is declined the same way, so 'in the garlands' is मालासु.
questions.teaches: Feminine nouns in -आ form the locative plural in -आसु (वर्षासु = in the rains; मालासु = in the garlands).

questions.q: In line 1, what is said to be dimmed by clouds blue like cut sapphire?
optionExplain: Right: नभः is the noun of line 1: the sky.
No river is named in line 1.
No sun is named in line 1.
No forest is named in line 1.
questions.explain: The last word of line 1, नभः, is the sky; the long compound before it describes it.
questions.rule: नभः = sky; the clouds are blue like cut sapphire.

questions.q: Match each word of line 1 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These pieces carry the picture: blue clouds, sapphire-like, over the sky.
questions.rule: इंद्रनील = sapphire; नील = blue; अभ्र = cloud; नभः = sky.

questions.q: The word for 'sky' in line 1 is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: नभः is the sky, the thing that the compound describes.
questions.teaches: नभः is a neuter noun, nominative singular; the long compound before it describes it.

questions.q: Which is the right translation of line 1?
options: The sky brightened by white clouds like moonstone
The sky dimmed by clouds blue like cut sapphire
The earth dimmed by clouds blue like cut sapphire
The sky dimmed by clouds red like cut ruby
optionExplain: The clouds are blue (नील), not white.
Right: भिन्नेंद्रनील = like cut sapphire; नीलाभ्र = blue clouds; आविल = dimmed.
The noun is नभः, sky, not earth.
The stone is इंद्रनील, sapphire, and the clouds are blue.
questions.explain: Sky (नभः), dimmed (आविलं), by clouds that are blue like cut sapphire.
questions.rule: नभः + आविल + नीलाभ्र: the dimmed sky has blue clouds.

questions.q: Put these pieces of the line 1 compound in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The compound runs: cut, sapphire, blue, cloud.

questions.q: Which is the correct joined form of नील + अंबुज (blue lotus)?
optionExplain: Two vowels meeting inside a compound are joined, not left apart.
अ + अ does not give ओ.
Right: अ + अ gives आ: नील + अंबुज = नीलांबुज, as in नील + अभ्र = नीलाभ्र.
अ + अ does not give ऐ.
questions.explain: The same rule joins नील + अभ्र into नीलाभ्र: a short अ meeting अ gives a long आ.
questions.teaches: When a word ending in अ is joined to a word beginning with अ, they merge into long आ (नील + अभ्र = नीलाभ्र).

questions.q: Which is said to be ocean-shaped in line 2?
optionExplain: Lotuses belong to line 1 and are not called ocean-shaped.
No clouds are named in this unit.
No hills are named in this unit.
Right: सरितः सागराकाराः: the rivers are ocean-shaped.
questions.explain: Line 2 begins सरितः सागराकारा: the rivers are ocean-shaped.

questions.q: Match each word of line 2 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words carry the whole of line 2.
questions.rule: सरितः = rivers; सागर = ocean; भूः = earth; अव्यक्त = indistinct.

questions.q: Which is the right sandhi result of भूः + अव्यक्त?
optionExplain: Right: A visarga after ऊ before a vowel becomes र्.
The visarga does not simply vanish here.
A visarga before a vowel does not become स्.
ओ appears only after अ + visarga, not after ऊ.
questions.explain: भूः + अव्यक्त joins as भूरव्यक्त: the visarga after ऊ turns to र् before a vowel.
questions.rule: Visarga after a vowel other than अ/आ + vowel → र्.
questions.teaches: A visarga after a vowel other than अ or आ turns into र् before a vowel (भूः + अ… = भूर्…).

questions.q: Which is the right translation of line 2?
options: The rivers are dry; the earth has water and land clear
Rivers look like oceans; earth shows no clear water-land line
The rivers are ocean-shaped; the earth has only dry land everywhere
The oceans are river-shaped; the earth has water and land clear
optionExplain: Neither part matches: अव्यक्त is indistinct.
Right: Both parts follow the words सागराकाराः and अव्यक्तजलस्थला.
जलस्थला names water and land together, indistinct.
सागर is in the comparison: rivers look like oceans.
questions.explain: Line 2 says the rivers look like oceans and the earth has no clear line between water and land.

questions.q: Put these parts of line 2 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Line 2 runs: rivers, ocean-shaped, earth, with water and land indistinct.

questions.q: In an invented phrase पर्वताकारः गजः, what is the elephant like?
options: It is the lord of mountains
It is shaped like a mountain
It is far from the mountain
optionExplain: The word says shape, not dwelling.
Nothing in -आकार means lord.
Right: X-आकार at the end of a compound means shaped like X.
Nothing in the word speaks of distance.
questions.explain: सागराकाराः (ocean-shaped) is सागर + आकार; the same pattern gives पर्वताकार, mountain-shaped.
questions.teaches: A compound ending in -आकार means 'shaped like' the first part (सागराकाराः, पर्वताकारः).

questions.q: By which three does line 1 say the earth resounds?
optionExplain: None of these is named in line 1.
None of these is named in line 1.
None of these is named in line 1.
Right: जीमूत, शिखी, दर्दुर: clouds, peacocks, frogs.
questions.explain: Line 1 names the deep thunder of clouds and the sounds of peacocks and frogs.
questions.rule: जीमूत (cloud) · शिखी (peacock) · दर्दुर (frog) sound; the earth is नादिता.

questions.q: Match each word of the unit to its meaning.
questions.explain: मंद्र (deep) and the cloud and frog belong to line 1; lightning is the last item of line 2.
questions.rule: जीमूत = cloud; मंद्र = deep; दर्दुर = frog; विद्युत् = lightning.

questions.q: The word for 'peacock' in line 1 is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: शिखी is the peacock, the second sound-maker of line 1.
questions.teaches: शिखी names the peacock; with the cloud and the frog it makes the three sound-makers.

questions.q: Which three does line 2 say light up the earth?
optionExplain: Peacocks belong to line 1 and are among the sounds.
Right: the first item of line 2.
Frogs belong to line 1 and are among the sounds.
Right: the second item of line 2.
Right: the third item of line 2.
questions.explain: Line 2 lists indragopa insects, bow-fragments and lightning flashes as what lights the earth.

questions.q: Put the three things that light the earth in the order of line 2.
questions.explain: Line 2 runs: indragopa, bow-fragments, lightning flashes.

questions.q: In an invented phrase भ्रमरनादिता वनभूः, what does the forest ground do?
options: It is lit up by the bees
It is stung by many bees
It is entirely free from bees
optionExplain: Right: -नादिता is feminine, 'resounding with', like मंद्र…नादिता.
Lit would be -दीपिता, as in line 2.
Nothing in -नादिता means stung.
Free from would be -वर्जिता or -रहिता.
questions.explain: नादिता means resounding; the first part of the compound names what makes the sound, as दर्दुर does.
questions.rule: X-नादिता = resounding with X; X-दीपिता = lit by X.
questions.teaches: A feminine compound ending in -नादिता means 'resounding with' the first part, and -दीपिता means 'lit by' it.

questions.q: What grass does line 1 say the earth has all around?
optionExplain: श्यामल is dark-green, not yellow or dry.
Right: श्यामल = dark-green, तृण = grass.
तृणा names grass the earth has.
No white flowers are mentioned here.
questions.explain: परितः श्यामलतृणा: all around, with dark-green grass.
questions.rule: परितः = all around; श्यामल = dark-green; तृण = grass.

questions.q: Match each word of line 1 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words build line 1.
questions.rule: परितः = all around; श्यामल = dark-green; तृण = grass; उज्ज्वल = bright.

questions.q: In line 2, which group contains only locative forms?
optionExplain: तदा and पुनः are indeclinables, not locative forms.
पुनः and तदा are indeclinables.
Right: Each ends in a locative sign (-ए, -औ): in the body, the fire dull, afflicted.
तदा and पुनः are indeclinables.
questions.explain: देहे (in the body), मंदे and अग्नौ (in the fire, dull), बाधिते (afflicted) are locative, and so is आदानाबले; तदा and पुनः are indeclinables.
questions.rule: Locative absolute: noun + participle both locative = 'when X is Y'.
questions.teaches: Two or more words in the locative can together mean 'when X is Y' (a locative absolute); the main verb comes later.

questions.q: Which is the right sandhi result of मंदे + अग्नौ?
optionExplain: Final ए before a short अ keeps ए (the अ is dropped and marked ऽ); it is not changed to य्.
ए + अ does not give long आ.
ए + अ does not give ऐ.
Right: -ए before अ keeps ए and drops the अ, marked by ऽ.
questions.explain: Final -ए followed by a short अ stays ए, and the अ is shown by the avagraha mark ऽ.

questions.q: Put these parts of line 2 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Line 2 runs: at that time, weak from ādāna, in the body, in the dull fire, afflicted, again.
questions.rule: तदा · आदानाबले · देहे · मंदेऽग्नौ · बाधिते · पुनः.

questions.q: Which invented phrase means: when the sun has risen?
optionExplain: Right: Noun and participle both in the locative: 'the sun being risen'.
Both nominative: 'the sun has risen', a plain statement.
Both accusative: a different construction.
Both instrumental: 'by the risen sun'.
questions.explain: Like देहे ... बाधिते in line 2, two locatives together give 'when ... being ...'.
questions.rule: Locative + locative participle = 'when X has done/been Y'.
questions.teaches: A noun and a past participle both in the locative state a circumstance: सूर्ये उदिते = 'when the sun has risen'.

questions.q: Which procedure does line 2 say one should resort to?
optionExplain: Not named in line 2.
Right: बस्तिकर्म निषेवेत: one should resort to the basti procedure.
Not named in line 2.
Not named in line 2.
questions.explain: Line 2 gives the instruction बस्तिकर्म निषेवेत.
questions.rule: बस्तिकर्म + निषेवेत = one should resort to the basti procedure.

questions.q: Match each word of line 2 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The words of line 2 say what to resort to and what must be done first.
questions.rule: बस्तिकर्म = basti procedure; निषेवेत = should resort to; कृत = completed; संशोधन = cleansing.

questions.q: Which word means one should dwell?
optionExplain: This is the plain present: 'dwells'.
This is a past form: 'dwelt'.
Right: -एत् marks 'should', as -एत in निषेवेत.
This is a noun: 'a dwelling'.
questions.explain: निषेवेत is a 'should' form (3rd person singular optative); वसेत् is built the same way.
questions.teaches: A verb ending in -एत् (or -एत in the middle voice) says what one should do (निषेवेत, वसेत्).

questions.q: Which is the right translation of line 2?
options: One should avoid the basti procedure, having completed the whole course of cleansing
One should resort to cleansing, having completed the basti procedure
One should resort to the basti procedure before any cleansing
One should resort to basti, having completed the course of cleansing
optionExplain: निषेवेत means resort to, not avoid.
The completed course is the cleansing, and basti is what follows.
कृत says the cleansing is already completed.
Right: बस्तिकर्म निषेवेत; कृतसंशोधनक्रमः = one who has completed the course of cleansing.
questions.explain: The order given is: cleansing completed first, then the basti procedure.

questions.q: Put these parts of line 2 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Line 2 runs: basti procedure, should resort to, one who has completed the course of cleansing.

questions.q: Which phrase means one should read the book?
optionExplain: Right: An accusative object plus a -एत् verb: 'should read the book'.
This is the plain present: 'reads the book'.
This is a past form: 'read the book'.
Two nouns: 'book, reading', no verb.
questions.explain: Like बस्तिकर्म निषेवेत, the object stands in the accusative and the verb ends in -एत्.
questions.teaches: A command in the verse is an object plus a verb in -एत्: ग्रंथं पठेत् = 'one should read the book'.

questions.q: Which three grains does line 1 list?
options: Old śāli rice, wheat and barley
Old śāli rice, lentils and sesame
optionExplain: None of these is named in the unit.
Right: पुराणशालि, गोधूम, यव.
Lentils and sesame are not named in line 1.
Mustard is not named in line 1.
questions.explain: Line 1 names old śāli rice, wheat and barley.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Three words name the grains; अंबु is the water of the last words.
questions.rule: शालि = rice; गोधूम = wheat; यव = barley; अंबु = water.

questions.q: The word for 'barley' in line 1 is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: यव is barley, the third grain of the list.
questions.teaches: In the printed गोधूमयवान् the two grains are joined as a pair (wheat and barley).

questions.q: Which three prepared drinks does line 2 name, not counting the water at the end?
optionExplain: Right: the first drink of line 2.
Yūṣa is taken with the grains in line 1.
Right: the second drink of line 2.
Rasa (broth) is taken with the grains in line 1.
Right: the third drink of line 2.
questions.explain: Line 2 lists madirā, ariṣṭa and mārdvīka, and then 'or a very small amount of water'.

questions.q: Put the three prepared drinks in the order of line 2.
questions.explain: Line 2 runs: madirā, ariṣṭa, mārdvīka, then a small amount of water.

questions.q: In an invented phrase तिलमुद्गान्, what are the two items?
optionExplain: A pair-compound lists items; it does not mean 'of'.
The two items stay separate.
Right: Two items joined in one word form a pair, as in गोधूमयवान्.
Nothing in the compound means 'without'.
questions.explain: गोधूमयवान् is 'wheat and barley'; a compound of this kind (dvandva) means 'A and B'.
questions.teaches: Items joined in one word, each in the same case, mean 'A and B' (गोधूमयवान् = wheat and barley).

questions.q: What does line 2 say the food should overcome?
optionExplain: These are not named in the line.
These are not named in the line.
These are not named in the line.
Right: भोजनं क्लेदवातजित्: food overcoming kleda and Vāta.
questions.explain: Line 2 says the food is क्लेदवातजित्: overcoming dampness and Vāta.

questions.q: Match each word of line 1 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Each word tells where the water comes from or how it is treated.
questions.rule: दिव्यम् = from the sky; कथित = boiled; कूप = well; सारसम् = of a lake.

questions.q: Which is the right sandhi result of तु + अह्नि?
optionExplain: Right: उ before a different vowel turns into व्.
The vowels are not left apart.
उ + अ does not give ओ.
उ + अ does not give आ.
questions.explain: तु + अह्नि = त्वह्नि: a short उ before a different vowel becomes व्.
questions.teaches: A final उ before a different vowel turns into व् (तु + अह्नि = त्वह्नि).

questions.q: Which phrase describes the day in line 2?
options: Hot and dry with no rain at all
Cold and dark with heavy frost
Clear and calm all day long
optionExplain: Nothing in the words speaks of heat or dryness.
Right: वृष्टिवाताकुले: troubled by rain and wind.
Nothing in the words speaks of cold or darkness.
आकुल means troubled, the opposite of calm.
questions.explain: वृष्टिवाताकुले अह्नि is 'on a day troubled by rain and wind'.
questions.rule: आकुल = troubled; वृष्टि = rain; वात = wind.

questions.q: Put these waters in the order of line 1.
questions.explain: Line 1 runs: rainwater, boiled well-water, cauṇḍya, lake water.

questions.q: In an invented phrase शत्रुजित् नृपः, what does the king do?
optionExplain: 'Born of' would be -ज.
Nothing in -जित् means loved.
Right: -जित् at the end means overcoming the first part.
Nothing in -जित् means fearing.
questions.explain: क्लेदवातजित् is क्लेद-वात-जित्, overcoming dampness and Vāta; शत्रुजित् is overcoming enemies.
questions.teaches: A compound ending in -जित् means 'overcoming' the first part (क्लेदवातजित्, शत्रुजित्).

questions.q: With what does line 2 say food and drink are taken when dense clouds rise?
optionExplain: Not named in the line.
Not named in the line.
Not named in the line.
Right: सक्षौद्रं: with honey.
questions.explain: Line 2 says अन्नपानं सक्षौद्रम्: food and drink with honey.

questions.q: Match each quality of line 1 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Line 1 lists six qualities; these are four of them.
questions.rule: परिशुष्क = well dried; लघु = light; उष्ण = hot; लवण = salty.

questions.q: The word for 'unctuous' in line 1 is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: स्निग्ध is unctuous, the third quality of line 1.
questions.teaches: स्निग्ध is neuter accusative singular (printed स्निग्धम्), agreeing with the understood 'food' (भोजन) of line 1.

questions.q: Which three of these does line 1 name among the qualities?
optionExplain: Sweet is not named in line 1.
Right: named in line 1.
Right: named in line 1.
Bitter is not named in line 1.
Right: named in line 1.
questions.explain: Line 1 names well dried, light, unctuous, hot, sour and salty; light, sour and unctuous are among them.

questions.q: Put the six qualities in the order of line 1.
questions.explain: Line 1 runs: well dried, light, unctuous, hot, sour, salty.
questions.rule: परिशुष्कम् · लघु · स्निग्धम् · उष्ण · अम्ल · लवणम्.

questions.q: Which is the correct joined form of नील + उत्पल (blue lotus)?
optionExplain: Right: अ + उ gives ओ, as in घन + उदये = घनोदये.
अ + उ is not simply shortened to उ.
अ + उ does not give औ.
अ + उ does not give आ.
questions.explain: घन + उदये joins as घनोदये: a short अ meeting उ gives ओ.
questions.teaches: A final अ before उ merges into ओ (घन + उदये = घनोदये, नील + उत्पल = नीलोत्पल).

questions.q: Which three does line 2 say the dwelling is free from?
options: Heavy dust, smoke and loud noise
Cold rain, hail and strong winds
optionExplain: These are not named in line 2.
Right: निर्दंश-मशक-उन्दुर: free from these three.
These are not named in line 2.
These are not named in line 2.
questions.explain: Line 2 ends with the compound read as निर्दंशमशकोन्दुरं (printed निर्दशमशकोंदुरं): free from biting flies, mosquitoes and rats.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Line 2 names the dwelling and the three things it is free from.
questions.rule: भवनम् = dwelling; दंश = biting fly; मशक = mosquito; उन्दुर = rat.

questions.q: Which is the right sandhi result of निः + दंश (printed निर्दश)?
optionExplain: The visarga does not simply vanish.
The visarga is not kept before द.
Right: A visarga before a voiced consonant turns into र् after इ.
A visarga before द does not become स्.
questions.explain: निः + दंश = निर्दंश: after इ the visarga becomes र् before the voiced द.
questions.rule: Visarga after इ/उ + voiced sound → र्.
questions.teaches: A visarga after इ or उ turns into र् before a voiced sound (निः + दंश = निर्दंश).

questions.q: Which pair of words in line 2 stand as opposites, with and without?
options: भवनं and च side by side
मशक and उन्दुर side by side
च and उन्दुर side by side
optionExplain: Neither word means with or without.
Both are things the dwelling is free from.
च means 'and'; उन्दुर is rat.
Right: स- means with and निर्- means without, whatever अग्नियान exactly is.
questions.explain: स- (with) + अग्नियान begin the first compound; निर्- (without) begins the second.

questions.q: Put the three things the dwelling is free from in the order of line 2.
questions.explain: Line 2 ends: biting flies, mosquitoes, rats.

questions.q: In an invented phrase निर्जलं सरः, what is the lake?
optionExplain: Right: निर्- at the start means without, as in निर्दंश…
Full of would be a word like जलपूर्ण.
Nothing in निर्- means beside.
Nothing in निर्- means made of.
questions.explain: निर्- (from निः) means without: निर्जल = without water, as निर्दंश… = without biting flies.
questions.teaches: The prefix निः / निर् means 'without' (निर्दंश…, निर्जलम्).

questions.q: With whom does line 2 say the person should go?
options: With the foremost horses of the guard
With the foremost servants of the house
With the foremost teachers of the school
optionExplain: Horses are not named in line 2.
Right: यायात् करेणुमुख्याभिः: should go with the foremost she-elephants.
Servants are not named in line 2.
Teachers are not named in line 2.
questions.explain: Line 2 says यायात् करेणुमुख्याभिः: should go with the foremost she-elephants.
questions.rule: करेणु = she-elephant; मुख्या = foremost; यायात् = should go.

questions.q: Match each word of the unit to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words give the person's tastes and dress.
questions.rule: स्नान = bathing; उद्वर्तन = ointment-rubbing; करेणु = she-elephant; चित्रवस्त्र = colourful clothes.

questions.q: Which phrase means one should go to the village?
optionExplain: This is the plain present: 'goes to the village'.
This is a past form: 'went to the village'.
Right: यायात् is the 'should go' form of the verb √या.
यातः is a participle, 'gone'; it is not a 'should' form.
questions.explain: यायात् in line 2 is 'should go', so ग्रामं यायात् is 'should go to the village'.
questions.teaches: The 'should go' form of √या is यायात्; the plain present is याति.

questions.q: Which list is the person said to be fond of in line 1?
options: Singing, dancing, dice-play, wine-drinking and music-making
Hunting, riding, archery, wrestling and other sports
Reading, writing, speech, silence and daily prayers
optionExplain: None of these is in line 1.
None of these is in line 1.
None of these is in line 1.
Right: प्रघर्ष, उद्वर्तन, स्नान and धूमगंधागुरु are the items of line 1.
questions.explain: Line 1 ends with …प्रियः, 'fond of', after the list of tastes.

questions.q: Put these four parts of line 1 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Line 1 runs: rubbing, ointment-rubbing, bathing, smoke-scent-agaru.

questions.q: In an invented phrase वनविहारप्रियः, what is the person?
options: Fond of walking in the forest
