questions.q: Match each word of unit 55 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Three ailments of the list and the place named after them.
questions.rule: गर = concocted poison; गुल्म = abdominal lump; कास = cough; श्लेष्म-आशय = seat of phlegm.
questions.teaches: Unit 55: गर = concocted poison, गुल्म = abdominal lump, कास = cough, श्लेष्माशय = the seat of phlegm.

questions.q: Which is the right split of गुल्मोदर in unit 55?
optionExplain: Final म् before a vowel stays: that would give गुल्ममुदर.
Right: अ + उ → ओ: गुल्म + उदर → गुल्मोदर.
उ + उ would give ऊ: गुल्मूदर.
अः before उ drops the visarga: गुल्म उदर, unjoined.
questions.explain: गुल्म (abdominal lump) + उदर (belly-ailment): अ + उ join as ओ.

questions.q: A patient has Vāta-Kapha lodged in the throat. Does unit 55 name its drug for him?
options: No: only belly ailments are named
Only if it is light and mobile
Yes: the last item names that state
No: the throat comes in a later unit
optionExplain: The list goes on to the seat of phlegm and the throat.
The unit names firm and heavy ailments, not light ones.
Right: वातश्लेष्मणि च कण्ठाश्रये = and in Vāta-Kapha seated in the throat.
The throat is named in this very unit.
questions.explain: The unit closes with Vāta-Kapha whose seat is the throat.
questions.rule: कण्ठ-आश्रय = having the throat as seat.

questions.q: श्लेष्माशयस्थ means located in the seat of phlegm. What does a new word हृदयस्थ mean?
optionExplain: Removing would need -हर; -स्थ means located in.
Arising would need -उत्थ, as in कफसंचयोत्थ.
Good for would need -हित or -हृद्य; -स्थ is located.
Right: हृदय (heart) + स्थ (located in), as in श्लेष्माशय-स्थ.
questions.explain: -स्थ after a place = located in it.
questions.rule: X + स्थ = located in X; X + उत्थ = arising from X.
questions.teaches: -स्थ = located in (श्लेष्माशयस्थ, हृदयस्थ); -उत्थ = arising from (कफसंचयोत्थ).

questions.q: What kind of preparation does unit 56 prescribe?
options: Oils to be put into the nose
Pastes to be rubbed on skin
optionExplain: Right: लेहान् = lehas (licked preparations), accusative plural.
No pill (गुटिका) is named in this unit.
No oil or nasal use is named in this unit.
No external paste is named in this unit.
questions.explain: The unit prepares lehas and prescribes them.
questions.rule: लेह = a licked preparation; विदध्यात् = should prescribe.

questions.q: Put these parts of unit 56 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Having prepared, joined with jīvanīya powder, with honey and sugar, with their decoctions, lehas, in phlegm with Pitta secondary.
questions.rule: प्रकल्प्य · …चूर्णसंयुक्तान् · समधुशर्करान् · तत्कषायैः · लेहान् · पित्तोपसर्जने श्लेष्मणि.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 56 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The action, the choice from the group, one added sweet, and the rank of Pitta.
questions.rule: प्रकल्प्य = having prepared; अन्यतम = any one; शर्करा = sugar; उपसर्जन = secondary.
questions.teaches: Unit 56: प्रकल्प्य = having prepared, अन्यतम = any one of several, शर्करा = sugar, उपसर्जन = secondary.

questions.q: In पित्तोपसर्जने श्लेष्मणि, what is the place of Pitta?
options: The only doṣa that is present
optionExplain: उपसर्जन is subordinate, the opposite of dominant.
Right: पित्त-उपसर्जन (bahuvrīhi): the phlegm state in which Pitta is secondary.
Absent would need a word like हीन; Pitta is present but secondary.
श्लेष्मणि names phlegm as the main state.
questions.explain: Kapha is the main state; Pitta goes along with it as the lesser partner.

questions.q: Besides the jīvanīya powder, what two things go into the lehas of unit 56?
optionExplain: Neither ghee nor salt is named in this unit.
Neither milk nor jaggery is named in this unit.
Right: समधुशर्करान् = with honey (मधु) and sugar (शर्करा).
Neither is named in this unit.
questions.explain: The lehas are made with honey and sugar, and with the decoctions of the same drugs.

questions.q: पित्तोपसर्जने means in which Pitta is secondary. What does a new word वातोपसर्जने mean?
optionExplain: उपसर्जन is secondary, not dominant.
Removal would be -हर or -शमन, not उपसर्जन.
The new word names Vāta, not Pitta.
Right: Same bahuvrīhi: वात + उपसर्जन, with अ + उ → ओ.
questions.explain: doṣa + उपसर्जन (bahuvrīhi) = the state in which that doṣa is secondary.
questions.rule: X-उपसर्जन = with X secondary; अ + उ → ओ.
questions.teaches: doṣa + उपसर्जन = in which that doṣa is secondary: पित्तोपसर्जन, वातोपसर्जन (अ + उ → ओ).

questions.q: In what form is dhāmārgava taken in unit 57?
optionExplain: Right: धामार्गवकल्कम् = dhāmārgava paste.
No powder is named in this unit.
No juice is named in this unit.
Ghee comes in line 05.01.64.
questions.explain: The drug is taken as kalka, a ground paste.

questions.q: Put these parts of unit 57 in the order of the text (leave out the last word).
questions.explain: Dhāmārgava paste, with the broth of tumbaru and dhānya.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 57 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The form of the drug, the liquid, and the two things the broth is made of.
questions.rule: कल्क = paste; यूष = broth; तुम्बरु = Zanthoxylum armatum (probable); धान्य = literally grain.
questions.teaches: Unit 57: कल्क = paste, यूष = broth, तुम्बरु = tumbaru (Zanthoxylum armatum, probable), धान्य = literally grain.

questions.q: In तुम्बरुधान्ययूषेण, which member is the head that the others describe?
optionExplain: तुम्बरु names what the broth is made of.
Right: The last member of a tatpuruṣa is its head: a broth of tumbaru and dhānya.
धान्य names what the broth is made of.
Only तुम्बरु and धान्य are paired; यूष is the head.
questions.explain: तुम्बरु-धान्य (a pair) + यूष (head): the broth of tumbaru and dhānya.
questions.rule: Tatpuruṣa: the last member is the head.

questions.q: A student meets तुम्बरु in unit 57. What identification does the card give?
optionExplain: Coriander is the disputed reading of dhānya, not of tumbaru.
Sponge gourd is one candidate for dhāmārgava.
Right: The data: tumbaru = Zanthoxylum armatum (Hindi tejbal, timur), probable.
Turmeric (haridrā) is named in line 05.01.63.
questions.explain: Tumbaru is probably Zanthoxylum armatum, tejbal or timur in Hindi.

questions.q: यूषेण (with broth) has ण because ष comes before it. Which new form means with milk (क्षीर)?
optionExplain: Here र is followed only by a vowel, so the न of the ending becomes ण: क्षीरेण.
क्षीराय is dative: for milk.
क्षीरात् is ablative: from milk.
Right: र before the ending also turns न into ण: क्षीर + इन → क्षीरेण.
questions.explain: Instrumental singular of an अ-stem ends in -एन; it becomes -एण after ऋ, र or ष in the word when no blocking consonant (a dental, palatal or cerebral stop, or ल, श, स) stands between (यूषेण, क्षीरेण; but रथेन).
questions.rule: -एन → -एण after र/ष when nothing blocks it: यूषेण, क्षीरेण; but रथेन.
questions.teaches: The instrumental -एन becomes -एण after र or ष when nothing blocks it: यूष → यूषेण, क्षीर → क्षीरेण (but रथ → रथेन).

questions.q: For which disorders is the preparation of unit 58 used?
optionExplain: Right: मनोविकारेषु = in disorders of the mind.
The eye is not named in this unit.
Skin diseases are named in line 05.01.66, not here.
Belly-ailments are named in line 05.01.60, not here.
questions.explain: The unit ends with मनोविकारेषु: in disorders of the mind.

questions.q: Put these four clearer names of unit 58 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: In the long compound, yavānī and haridrā stand early, punarnavā and kāsamarda near its end.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 58 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Three identified drugs and the word that says how many are used.
questions.rule: यवानी = ajwain; हरिद्रा = turmeric; पुनर्नवा = spreading hogweed; अन्यतम = any one.
questions.teaches: Unit 58: यवानी = ajwain, हरिद्रा = turmeric, पुनर्नवा = spreading hogweed (all standard); अन्यतम = any one.

questions.q: Which is the right split of मनोविकारेषु?
optionExplain: There is no word ओविकार; the ओ comes from मनः.
Right: The stem मनस् ends in -अः; अः → ओ before a voiced sound (व).
मनु is a different word; उ would not become ओ here.
आ before व stays आ: that would give मनाविकारेषु.
questions.explain: मनः (mind) + विकारेषु (in disorders): अः → ओ before व.
questions.rule: अः + voiced consonant → ओ (मनः + विकार → मनोविकार).

questions.q: A physician follows unit 58. How many drugs of the long list go into one decoction?
optionExplain: अन्यतम means any one, not all.
The text says any one, without naming which.
Right: अन्यतमकषायेण = with the decoction of any one of them.
Haridrā is one choice among many, not the only one.
questions.explain: अन्यतम: one drug chosen from the list makes the decoction.

questions.q: मनोविकार is a disorder of the mind. What does a new word नेत्रविकारेषु mean?
options: In the eyes of the mind
optionExplain: A remedy would need a word like औषध; विकार is a disorder.
मनस् is not in the new word.
नेत्र is the eye, not the face.
Right: Same tatpuruṣa: नेत्र (eye) + विकार (disorder), locative plural.
questions.explain: X-विकार = a disorder of X; -एषु = in (locative plural).
questions.rule: Tatpuruṣa: मनो-विकार, नेत्र-विकार = disorder of the mind / eye.
questions.teaches: X-विकार (tatpuruṣa) = disorder of X: मनोविकार (of the mind), नेत्रविकार (of the eye).

questions.q: What does unit 59 prepare for disorders of the mind?
optionExplain: Right: सर्पिः = ghee, the main word of the unit.
Lehas come in line 05.01.61.
The paste comes in line 05.01.62.
A broth comes in line 05.01.62.
questions.explain: Both options of the unit are ghees.

questions.q: Put the words of unit 59 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Produced from milk cooked with dhāmārgava root, ghee, or cooked with the six from phala, in disorders of the mind.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 59 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The part of the drug, the process, the liquid and how the ghee comes from it.
questions.rule: मूल = root; सिद्ध = cooked; क्षीर = milk; संभव = produced (from).
questions.teaches: Unit 59: मूल = root, सिद्ध = cooked, क्षीर = milk, संभव = produced from: ghee from milk cooked with the root.

questions.q: Which is the right split of फलादि in unit 59?
optionExplain: Final म् before a vowel stays: that would give फलमादि.
Right: अ + आ → आ: फल + आदि → फलादि.
अः before आ drops the visarga: फल आदि, unjoined.
ए before आ becomes अय्: फलयादि, or फल आदि.
questions.explain: फल + आदि (beginning with): two अ-sounds join as आ.

questions.q: In unit 59 the milk is cooked with dhāmārgava ____ (root). Type it in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: धामार्गवमूलसिद्धक्षीर = milk cooked with the root (मूल) of dhāmārgava.
questions.teaches: In unit 59 the root (मूल) of dhāmārgava is cooked in milk, and ghee is produced from that milk.

questions.q: फलादि means the group beginning with phala. What does a new word पिप्पल्यादि mean?
options: The end of the pippalī group
optionExplain: -आदि adds the others; it does not leave them out.
-आदि marks the first member, not the last.
Right: पिप्पली + आदि (ई + आ → या): beginning with pippalī.
No number is in the new word; षट् is not there.
questions.explain: X-आदि = (the items) beginning with X.
questions.rule: X + आदि = beginning with X: फलादि, पिप्पल्यादि.
questions.teaches: X-आदि = the group beginning with X: फलादि (from phala), पिप्पल्यादि (from pippalī, ई + आ → या).

questions.q: Which qualities does unit 60 give kṛtavedhana?
optionExplain: These are the opposites; none of them is named here.
Soft and cold are not named; कटु is pungent.
None of these is named in this unit.
Right: अत्यर्थकटुतीक्ष्णोष्णम् = exceedingly pungent, sharp and hot.
questions.explain: Kṛtavedhana is exceedingly (अत्यर्थ) pungent, sharp and hot.
questions.rule: कटु = pungent; तीक्ष्ण = sharp; उष्ण = hot.

questions.q: Put the ailments of unit 60 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: गरोदरगुल्मप्लीहपाण्डुरोगश्वयथुषु: concocted poison, belly-ailment, abdominal lump, spleen, pale-ailment, swelling.
questions.rule: गर · उदर · गुल्म · प्लीह · पाण्डुरोग · श्वयथु.

questions.q: Match each ailment of unit 60 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four members of the ailment list with the equivalents of the card.
questions.rule: प्लीह = spleen; पाण्डुरोग = anaemia; श्वयथु = swelling; गर = concocted poison.
questions.teaches: Unit 60: प्लीह = spleen (splenic enlargement), पाण्डुरोग = pale-ailment (anaemia), श्वयथु = swelling (oedema), गर = concocted poison.

questions.q: Which is the right split of तीक्ष्णोष्ण in unit 60?
optionExplain: Right: अ + उ → ओ: तीक्ष्ण + उष्ण → तीक्ष्णोष्ण.
Final म् before a vowel stays: that would give तीक्ष्णमुष्ण.
There is no word ष्ण; the ओ comes from अ + उ.
ए before उ becomes अय् or अ: तीक्ष्णयुष्ण or तीक्ष्ण उष्ण.
questions.explain: तीक्ष्ण (sharp) + उष्ण (hot): अ + उ join as ओ.

questions.q: Which two of these ailments does unit 60 name for kṛtavedhana?
optionExplain: Wrong: cough is named for dhāmārgava in line 05.01.60, not here.
Right: प्लीह stands in the list.
Wrong: fever is not named in this unit.
Right: श्वयथु closes the list.
questions.explain: Plīha and śvayathu are in the list; cough and fever are not.
questions.rule: गर, उदर, गुल्म, प्लीह, पाण्डुरोग, श्वयथु.

questions.q: अत्यर्थकटु means exceedingly pungent. What does a new word अत्यर्थशीत mean?
optionExplain: अत्यर्थ is beyond measure, not slightly.
Right: अत्यर्थ (exceedingly) + शीत (cold).
अत्यर्थ intensifies; it does not deny.
Only one quality, शीत, is in the new word.
questions.explain: अत्यर्थ before a quality = that quality to an extreme degree.
questions.rule: अत्यर्थ + quality = exceedingly so: अत्यर्थकटु, अत्यर्थशीत.
questions.teaches: अत्यर्थ before a quality means 'exceedingly': अत्यर्थकटु (exceedingly pungent), अत्यर्थशीत (exceedingly cold).

questions.q: For what kind of persons does unit 61 name kuṭaja fruit?
optionExplain: Strength is not named in this unit.
Age is not named in this unit.
Right: सुकुमारेषु = in delicate persons.
Body size is not named in this unit.
questions.explain: Kuṭaja fruit is for the delicate, after the exceedingly sharp kṛtavedhana.

questions.q: Put these ailments of unit 61 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: वातशोणितविसर्पज्वरकुष्ठादिषु: vātaśoṇita, visarpa, fever, kuṣṭha and the rest.

questions.q: Match each ailment of unit 61 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The four named ailments with the standard equivalents of the card.
questions.rule: वातशोणित = vātarakta; विसर्प = erysipelas; ज्वर = fever; कुष्ठ = skin diseases.
questions.teaches: Unit 61: वातशोणित = vātarakta (gout-type), विसर्प = erysipelas-type infection, ज्वर = fever, कुष्ठ = skin diseases incl. leprosy.

questions.q: Which is the right split of सुकुमारेषूल्बण in unit 61?
optionExplain: There is no form सुकुमारेषः; the locative plural is -एषु.
ओ before उ becomes अव्: सुकुमारेषवुल्बण.
There is no word षूल्बण; ष belongs to -एषु.
Right: उ + उ → ऊ: सुकुमारेषु + उल्बण → सुकुमारेषूल्बण.
questions.explain: सुकुमारेषु (in delicate persons) + उल्बण (prominent): two उ join as ऊ.

questions.q: A delicate patient has visarpa. Which drug does the text name for him?
optionExplain: Right: कुटजफलं पुनः सुकुमारेषु … विसर्प…: kuṭaja fruit, for the delicate, in visarpa.
Kṛtavedhana is exceedingly sharp, and visarpa is not in its list.
Dhāmārgava root is for disorders of the mind (05.01.64).
Tumbaru broth goes with dhāmārgava paste (05.01.62).
questions.explain: The delicate person and visarpa both point to kuṭaja fruit.
questions.rule: कुटजफल: सुकुमार · वातशोणित, विसर्प, ज्वर, कुष्ठ.

questions.q: कुष्ठादिषु means in kuṣṭha and the rest. What does a new word कासादिषु mean?
optionExplain: -आदि adds the rest; it does not limit to one.
Right: कास (cough) + आदि (and the rest), locative plural.
-आदिषु is a locative of the list, not of time.
From would be the ablative -आदिभ्यः.
questions.explain: X-आदिषु = in X and the rest (locative plural).
questions.rule: X + आदि = X and the rest: कुष्ठादि, कासादि (अ + आ → आ).
questions.teaches: X-आदिषु = in X and the rest: कुष्ठादिषु, कासादिषु (अ + आ → आ).

questions.q: In what are the kuṭaja fruit powders of unit 62 first soaked?
optionExplain: Goat's milk belongs to line 05.01.48.
Cow's urine is not named in this unit.
Right: अर्कक्षीरेण = with the milk of arka (Calotropis), its latex.
Honey is not named in this unit.
questions.explain: The powders are soaked for seven days in the milk (latex) of arka.
questions.rule: अर्क = Calotropis (standard); क्षीर = milk, here latex.

questions.q: Put these parts of unit 62 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Soaked in arka milk for seven days, or with a decoction, or with water, then prepared for emesis.

questions.q: Match each drug of unit 62 to its identification.
questions.explain: Four drugs of the unit with the identifications the data gives.
questions.rule: अर्क = Calotropis; मदनफल = Randia dumetorum; मधूक = mahua; सर्षप = mustard.
questions.teaches: Unit 62: अर्क = Calotropis (आक), मदनफल = Randia dumetorum (मैनफल), मधूक = mahua (all standard); सर्षप = mustard (probable).

questions.q: Which is the right split of सप्ताहम् (for seven days)?
optionExplain: Final म् before a vowel stays: that would give सप्तमहम्.
ए before अ swallows it: that would give सप्तेऽहम्.
There is no word हम्, and no आ would arise.
Right: अ + अ → आ: सप्त (seven) + अह (day) → सप्ताह.
questions.explain: सप्त (seven) + अह (day): two short अ join as आ.

questions.q: Which of these give the water (अम्भस्) of unit 62, any one of them?
optionExplain: Right: लवण is the third of the three.
Wrong: haridrā is named in line 05.01.63, not here.
Wrong: jīvaka belongs to the decoction list, not the water.
Right: सर्षप is the first of the three.
questions.explain: सर्षपमधूकलवणान्यतमाम्भसा: with water of any one of mustard, mahua and salt.

questions.q: वमनाय means for emesis (dative of purpose). What does a new form विरेचनाय mean?
optionExplain: Right: विरेचन (purgation) + -आय, the dative of purpose.
By would be the instrumental विरेचनेन.
From would be the ablative विरेचनात्.
Of would be the genitive विरेचनस्य.
questions.explain: The dative -आय of an अ-stem states the purpose: for X.
questions.rule: X + आय = for X: वमनाय, विरेचनाय.
questions.teaches: The dative -आय states the purpose: वमनाय (for emesis), विरेचनाय (for purgation).

questions.q: What does अत्र mean in भवति चात्र?
optionExplain: There would be तत्र.
Right: अत्र = here, in this matter.
Now would be अधुना or इदानीम्.
Therefore would be अतः or तस्मात्.
questions.explain: भवति चात्र = and here (in this matter) there is (this).

questions.q: Match each word of unit 63 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The formula has three words: the verb, the joining word and the place word.
questions.rule: भवति = there is; च = and; अत्र = here.

questions.q: Put the three words hidden in भवति चात्र in the order of the text.
questions.explain: भवति, then च, then अत्र, the last two joined as चात्र.
questions.teaches: भवति चात्र = भवति + च + अत्र: there is, and, here.

questions.q: Which is the right split of चात्र?
optionExplain: अः before अ gives ओऽ: that would be चोऽत्र.
ए before अ gives एऽ: that would be चेऽत्र.
Right: अ + अ → आ: च + अत्र → चात्र.
There is no word त्र, and no आ would arise.
questions.explain: च (and) + अत्र (here): two short अ join as आ.

questions.q: What follows the formula of unit 63 in the text?
options: A new list of kuṭaja drugs
optionExplain: The colophon (05.01.71) comes after the verse.
The kuṭaja prose ended with iti in line 05.01.67.
Chapter two begins only after the colophon.
Right: The note: the formula introduces the verse of lines 05.01.69 and 05.01.70.
questions.explain: भवति चात्र introduces verse after prose.

questions.q: च + अत्र gives चात्र. Which is the joined form of a new pair तत्र + अपि (there also)?
optionExplain: Right: अ + अ → आ, as in च + अत्र → चात्र.
Two अ do not shrink to one short अ; they give आ.
ए would come from अ + इ.
ओ would come from अ + उ.
questions.explain: Same rule as चात्र: short अ + short अ = आ.
questions.teaches: Short अ + short अ join as आ: च + अत्र = चात्र, तत्र + अपि = तत्रापि.

questions.q: Who should devise further preparations, according to verse 64?
optionExplain: The patient is not named in this verse.
Right: मतिमान् … विकल्पयेत् = the wise one should devise.
No pupil is named in this verse.
No attendant is named in this verse.
questions.explain: The wise physician makes new preparations from the model given.

questions.q: Put these words of verse 64 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: An indication, of the especially useful ones; with this seed the wise one should devise.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 64 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The two words for what the chapter is, and the two for what the reader does.
questions.rule: दिक् = indication; बीज = seed, model; मतिमान् = wise; विकल्पयेत् = should devise.
questions.teaches: Verse 64: दिक् = indication, बीज = seed (the model), मतिमान् = the wise one, विकल्पयेत् = should vary, devise.

questions.q: Which is the right split of दिगित्येषा?
optionExplain: आ + ए would give ऐ: दिगित्यैषा.
Neither दिगि nor त्येषा is a word.
Right: क् → ग् before a vowel; इ + ए → ये: दिगित्येषा.
दिशः before इ would lose the visarga: दिश इत्येषा.
questions.explain: दिक् (indication) + इति (thus) + एषा (this): two sandhi joins.
questions.rule: क् → ग् before a vowel; इ + ए → ये.

questions.q: In verse 64, what is बीज (seed) used to mean?
options: A seed that is to be planted
The kernel of the madana fruit
The model to build variations on
optionExplain: Those were a drug; here बीज is figurative.
No sowing is meant; it is a figure of speech.
Kernel is majjā; here बीज is the model.
Right: The note: बीज is figurative, the model from which variations are made.
questions.explain: As a seed grows into many plants, the given recipes grow into new ones.
questions.rule: बीज (figurative) = the model, the starting point.

questions.q: मतिमान् is one possessing mati (understanding). What does a new word बलवान् mean?
optionExplain: Right: बल (strength) + -वान्, the same possessive suffix as -मान्.
Lacking would need -हीन; -वान् is possessing.
बलम् is strength itself; -वान् names its possessor.
Taking away would need -हर; -वान् is possessing.
questions.explain: -मान् / -वान् after a noun = one who possesses it.
questions.rule: X + मान्/वान् = possessing X: मतिमान्, बलवान्.
questions.teaches: -मान् / -वान् = one possessing: मतिमान् (understanding), बलवान् (strength).

questions.q: What is the name of the chapter closed by unit 65?
optionExplain: Purgation is the subject of the next chapter, not this one.
Right: वमनकल्पो नाम = named Vamanakalpa (preparations for emesis).
Enema is not the name given here.
Dinacaryā is a Sūtrasthāna chapter.
questions.explain: The colophon names the chapter: Vamanakalpa.

questions.q: Put the words of unit 65 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Thus, Vamanakalpa, named, the first, chapter.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 65 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The four words around the chapter's name.
questions.rule: इति = thus; नाम = named; प्रथम = first; अध्याय = chapter.
questions.teaches: Unit 65: इति = thus, नाम = named, प्रथम = first, अध्याय = chapter.

questions.q: Which is the right split of प्रथमोऽध्यायः?
optionExplain: अ + अ would give आ: प्रथमाध्यायः.
There is no word ध्यायः; the ओ comes from प्रथमः.
Right: अः + अ → ओऽ: the अ of अध्यायः is swallowed (avagraha).
Final म् before a vowel stays: प्रथमम् अध्यायः, or प्रथममध्यायः.
questions.explain: प्रथमः (first) + अध्यायः (chapter): अः before अ gives ओ, and ऽ marks the lost अ.

questions.q: The colophon calls this chapter the ____ (first) chapter. Type it in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: प्रथमोऽध्यायः = प्रथमः (first) + अध्यायः (chapter).
questions.teaches: Unit 65 names the chapter Vamanakalpa and calls it the first (प्रथम) chapter.

questions.q: प्रथमः + अध्यायः gives प्रथमोऽध्यायः. Which is the joined form of a new pair द्वितीयः + अध्यायः?
optionExplain: That joins द्वितीय + अध्याय without the visarga.
Visarga becomes र् only after a vowel other than अ or आ.
ए would belong to a locative द्वितीये; -अः before अ gives ओऽ.
Right: Same rule: अः + अ → ओऽ.
questions.explain: -अः before अ: ओ, with avagraha for the lost अ.
questions.teaches: -अः + अ- → -ओऽ-: प्रथमोऽध्यायः, द्वितीयोऽध्यायः.

questions.q: What does this unit say the chapter will explain?
options: The signs of a failed purgation
optionExplain: Right: विरेचनकल्पम् = the preparations of purgation (virecana-kalpa).
Emesis would be vamana; the word here is विरेचन, purgation.
No signs are named in this unit; it gives only the topic.
Collecting the root comes in unit 6, not in the opening line.
questions.explain: अथातो विरेचनकल्पं व्याख्यास्यामः = now, therefore, we shall explain the preparations of purgation.
questions.rule: Opening formula: अथ अतः + topic + व्याख्यास्यामः.
questions.section: विरेचनकल्प का आरम्भ और श्रेष्ठ द्रव्य

questions.q: Match each word of the opening line to its meaning.
questions.explain: The four words make the whole formula.
questions.rule: अथ = now; अतः = therefore; विरेचनकल्पम् = purgation preparations; व्याख्यास्यामः = we shall explain.
questions.section: विरेचनकल्प का आरम्भ और श्रेष्ठ द्रव्य

questions.q: Put these words of unit 1 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Now, therefore, the topic, and last the verb: we shall explain.
questions.teaches: The formula puts the topic in the accusative between अथातो and the verb व्याख्यास्यामः.
questions.section: विरेचनकल्प का आरम्भ और श्रेष्ठ द्रव्य

questions.q: Which is the right split of अथातो in this line?
optionExplain: Neither piece is a word; the words are अथ (now) and अतः (therefore).
Right: अ + अ gives आ; the visarga of अतः after अ becomes ओ before the voiced व of विरेचन.
आतो is not a word; the second word is अतः, therefore.
The first word is the particle अथ, without a visarga.
questions.explain: अथ (now) + अतः (therefore) = अथातो before a voiced sound.
questions.rule: अ + अ → आ; -अः → -ओ before a voiced consonant.
questions.section: विरेचनकल्प का आरम्भ और श्रेष्ठ द्रव्य

questions.q: What form is व्याख्यास्यामः, according to its grammar label?
options: Present, third person plural: they explain
Optative, third person singular: one should explain
Future, first person plural: we shall explain
Past, first person plural: we explained
optionExplain: The ending -स्यामः marks a future with we as subject, not they.
An optative would end in -एत्, like आहरेत् in unit 6.
Right: The data labels it 1 pl. fut. of vi-ā-√khyā.
The label says future; nothing here is past.
questions.explain: व्याख्यास्यामः = we shall explain (future, 1st plural).
questions.section: विरेचनकल्प का आरम्भ और श्रेष्ठ द्रव्य

questions.q: Built on the same formula, which line would open a chapter on emetic preparations (invented)?
optionExplain: The topic is the object of 'we shall explain', so it must be accusative (-म्/ं), not nominative.
व्याख्यास्यति is 'he will explain'; the formula says 'we'.
Before a voiced व the visarga of अतः after अ becomes ओ: अथातो.
Right: Same frame: अथातो + the topic in the accusative + व्याख्यास्यामः.
questions.explain: Only the topic word changes; case, verb and sandhi stay as in unit 1.
questions.teaches: The chapter formula is अथातो + topic in the accusative + व्याख्यास्यामः (we shall explain).
questions.section: विरेचनकल्प का आरम्भ और श्रेष्ठ द्रव्य

questions.q: Which drug does the text name as the foremost purgative among roots?
optionExplain: Right: मूलेषु त्रिवृत्: among roots, trivṛt.
tilvaka is foremost among barks (त्वक्षु).
snuhī is foremost among milks (क्षीरेषु).
kāśmarya is not named in this unit; it comes in unit 9.
questions.explain: Roots: trivṛt; barks: tilvaka; milks: snuhī; fruits: harītakī.
questions.section: विरेचनकल्प का आरम्भ और श्रेष्ठ द्रव्य

questions.q: Match each class of the unit to its foremost purgative.
questions.explain: Each locative names the class; the nominative after it names the foremost drug.
questions.rule: roots → trivṛt; barks → tilvaka; milks → snuhī. (The fruit, printed हरीलकी, is probably हरीतकी; it is left out here.)
questions.section: विरेचनकल्प का आरम्भ और श्रेष्ठ द्रव्य

questions.q: Put the four classes in the order the unit names them.
questions.explain: Roots, barks, milks, fruits: the order of the text.
questions.teaches: The unit runs root, bark, milk, fruit, and gives one foremost purgative for each.
questions.section: विरेचनकल्प का आरम्भ और श्रेष्ठ द्रव्य

questions.q: In the phrase मूलेषु त्रिवृत्, which word names the class and which the drug?
options: त्रिवृत् names the class; मूलेषु the drug
मूलेषु names the class; त्रिवृत् the drug
Both words name drugs of equal rank
Both words name classes of purgative substance
optionExplain: Reversed: the locative plural मूलेषु means among roots, the class.
Right: मूलेषु is locative plural (among roots); त्रिवृत् is nominative, the foremost one.
मूलेषु is not a drug; it means among roots.
त्रिवृत् is a single drug, turpeth, not a class.
questions.explain: Pattern of the whole unit: locative plural = class, nominative = foremost item.
questions.section: विरेचनकल्प का आरम्भ और श्रेष्ठ द्रव्य

questions.q: In which class does the unit place snuhī (a spurge)?
optionExplain: Among roots the unit names trivṛt.
Among barks the unit names tilvaka.
Right: क्षीरेषु स्नुही: among milks, snuhī.
Among fruits the unit names a fruit (printed हरीलकी), not snuhī.
questions.explain: snuhī is the foremost purgative among milks (kṣīra, possibly milky sap).
questions.section: विरेचनकल्प का आरम्भ और श्रेष्ठ द्रव्य

questions.q: Which form means among leaves (invented), in the same locative plural as फलेषु?
optionExplain: This is nominative/accusative plural, leaves, not among leaves.
This is dative/ablative plural, to or from leaves.
This is instrumental plural, with leaves.
Right: An -अ noun takes -एषु in the locative plural: फल → फलेषु, पत्र → पत्रेषु.
questions.explain: फलेषु, मूलेषु and क्षीरेषु all end in -एषु, among ...
questions.teaches: Nouns in -अ form the locative plural in -एषु (फलेषु, मूलेषु, पत्रेषु): among ...
questions.section: विरेचनकल्प का आरम्भ और श्रेष्ठ द्रव्य

questions.q: What two kinds of trivṛt root does the unit name?
optionExplain: Right: अरुणम् = reddish; श्यामम् = dark.
White is not named; the words are अरुण and श्याम.
The unit names colours, not thickness.
Length is not mentioned.
questions.explain: मूलमरुणं श्यामं च: the root is reddish and dark (two kinds).
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के दो भेद और संग्रह

questions.q: Match each word of the unit to its meaning.
questions.explain: These five words carry the whole statement.
questions.rule: त्रिवृतायाः = of trivṛt; द्विविधम् = of two kinds; मूलम् = root; अरुणम् = reddish; श्यामम् = dark.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के दो भेद और संग्रह

questions.q: Put these words of unit 3 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Whose root, indeed, of two kinds, the root, then the two colours.
questions.rule: त्रिवृतायाः · खलु · द्विविधम् · मूलम् · अरुणम् · श्यामम्.
questions.teaches: The unit first says the root is of two kinds, then names them: reddish first, dark second.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के दो भेद और संग्रह

questions.q: Which is the right split of मूलमरुणं?
optionExplain: मरुणम् is not a word; the colour word is अरुणम्.
Right: A final म् before a vowel is written joined to it: मूलम् + अरुणम् = मूलमरुणम्.
मूल is neuter here (मूलम्), and a visarga would not give म.
रुणम् is not a word.
questions.explain: Two neuter nominatives: मूलम् (root), अरुणम् (reddish).
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के दो भेद और संग्रह

questions.q: A student says this unit calls the dark root the better one. What does unit 3 itself say?
options: It calls the dark root the better one
It forbids the dark root for any use at all
It names the two kinds and ranks neither
It says both roots have one colour
optionExplain: No ranking or quality is stated in unit 3.
Nothing is forbidden in this unit.
Right: The unit names only the colours; qualities come in units 4 and 5.
It says the root is of two kinds, reddish and dark.
questions.explain: Unit 3 is a division only: two kinds, reddish and dark.
questions.rule: द्विविधम्: two kinds named, nothing more.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के दो भेद और संग्रह

questions.q: Like त्रिवृतायाः (of trivṛtā), which form means of śyāmā (invented)?
optionExplain: -अस्य is the masculine/neuter genitive, not feminine.
-आयै is the dative, for śyāmā.
-आम् is the accusative.
Right: A feminine -आ noun takes -आयाः in the genitive singular, like त्रिवृता → त्रिवृतायाः.
questions.explain: त्रिवृतायाः is genitive singular of the feminine त्रिवृता.
questions.teaches: Feminine nouns in -आ form the genitive singular in -आयाः (त्रिवृतायाः, श्यामायाः): of ...
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के दो भेद और संग्रह

questions.q: By which word does the text say the reddish root is denoted?
optionExplain: Right: त्रिवृच्छब्दवाच्यम् = denoted by the word trivṛt.
श्यामा is the name of the other, dark root (unit 5).
tilvaka is the foremost bark of unit 2, another drug.
snuhī is the foremost milk of unit 2, another drug.
questions.explain: The reddish root is the one called trivṛt in the narrow sense.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के दो भेद और संग्रह

questions.q: Match each quality word to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are the first four qualities of the reddish root.
questions.rule: कषायमधुरम् = astringent and sweet; विपाके कटुकम् = pungent in vipāka; रूक्षम् = dry; श्लेष्मपित्तहरम् = removes Kapha and Pitta.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के दो भेद और संग्रह

questions.q: Put the qualities of the reddish root in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Taste, vipāka, dryness, the doṣas removed, then all ailments calmed when specially prepared.
questions.rule: कषायमधुरम् · विपाके कटुकम् · रूक्षम् · श्लेष्मपित्तहरम् · सर्वव्याधिशमनम्.
questions.teaches: The unit gives taste and vipāka first, then action on the doṣas, then the wider effect of special preparation.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के दो भेद और संग्रह

questions.q: For what reason does the text call the reddish root recommended (प्रशस्त)?
options: Because it is sweet in vipāka
optionExplain: Sharpness (तीक्ष्ण) is said of the dark root, unit 5.
Right: सुखविरेचनत्वात् = because of easy purgation.
Its vipāka is pungent (कटुक), not sweet.
The unit says it removes Kapha and Pitta.
questions.explain: The ablative सुखविरेचनत्वात् gives the reason: it purges easily.
questions.rule: सुखविरेचनत्वात् ... प्रशस्तम्: easy purging, so recommended.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के दो भेद और संग्रह

questions.q: What does the text say the reddish root does when made by a particular preparation (कल्पनाविशेषात्)?
options: It is unfit for the delicate
optionExplain: Sharpness belongs to the dark root (unit 5).
Kapha and Pitta are named before, without the special preparation.
Right: कल्पनाविशेषात् पुनः सर्वव्याधिशमनम्.
The unit recommends it for the delicate.
questions.explain: With a particular (unnamed) preparation, the reddish root calms all ailments.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के दो भेद और संग्रह

questions.q: Join तत् + शरीरम् (invented) as one sandhi form. Which is right?
optionExplain: त् does not become ज् before श.
त् → द् happens before voiced sounds; श is unvoiced, and it changes too.
त् cannot stay unchanged before श; it becomes च्.
Right: त् + श → च्छ, as in त्रिवृत् + शब्द → त्रिवृच्छब्द.
questions.explain: त्रिवृच्छब्द and सुखविरेचनत्वाच्छिशु both show त् + श → च्छ.
questions.teaches: Final त् before श becomes च्, and the श usually becomes छ: त्रिवृत् + शब्द = त्रिवृच्छब्द.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के दो भेद और संग्रह

questions.q: How does the text compare the dark root with the reddish one in qualities?
options: Not compared with it at all
optionExplain: Right: तस्माद्गुणैः किंचिद्धीनम् = somewhat inferior to that in qualities.
The text says somewhat inferior (किंचिद्धीनम्).
A difference is stated: somewhat inferior.
तस्मात् (than that) is the comparison with the reddish root.
questions.explain: The dark root is somewhat inferior (किंचित् हीनम्) to the reddish in qualities.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के दो भेद और संग्रह

questions.q: Match each word about the dark root to its meaning.
questions.explain: Three qualities and the name of the dark root.
questions.rule: तीक्ष्णम् = sharp; कंठहृदयकर्षणम् = pulls throat and heart; मूर्च्छासंमोहकृत् = causes fainting and bewilderment; श्यामाशब्दवाच्यम् = called śyāmā.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के दो भेद और संग्रह

questions.q: Put these words about the dark root in the order of the text.
questions.explain: First the comparison, then sharpness, the pull on throat and heart, fainting, and last for whom it is recommended.
questions.teaches: The unit lists the dark root's drawbacks before saying for whom it is recommended.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के दो भेद और संग्रह

questions.q: Which patient does the text pair with the dark root?
options: One who is unable to bear distress
optionExplain: Soft koṣṭha is named for the reddish root, unit 4.
Right: क्रूरकोष्ठेषु प्रशस्तम्: recommended for those with hard koṣṭha.
The delicate are named for the reddish root, unit 4.
The text says able to bear distress (क्लेशक्षम).
questions.explain: Dark root: many doṣas, able to bear distress, hard koṣṭha.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के दो भेद और संग्रह

questions.q: Which of these effects does the text name for the dark root?
optionExplain: Right: कंठहृदयकर्षणम्.
Not named in this unit.
Right: in the same compound.
Right: मूर्च्छासंमोहकृत्.
Not named in this unit.
questions.explain: The unit names the pull on throat and heart, fainting and bewilderment.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के दो भेद और संग्रह

questions.q: Like मूर्च्छासंमोहकृत् (causing fainting and bewilderment), which compound means causing sleep (invented)?
optionExplain: With कृत first the compound means one who has slept, not causing sleep.
कृतम् is a past participle, made, done; it does not mean causing.
Right: -कृत् at the end of a compound means making, causing: निद्रा + कृत्.
कृतिः is a noun, a making or a work; it is not the agent ending -कृत्.
questions.explain: मूर्च्छासंमोहकृत् = that which causes fainting and bewilderment.
questions.teaches: A compound ending in -कृत् means causing what the first part names (मूर्च्छासंमोहकृत्, निद्राकृत्).
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के दो भेद और संग्रह

questions.q: Which trivṛt root does the unit say one should collect?
options: One spread sideways near the surface
One rough, thick, lying close to the soil surface
Any root, whichever is the largest
A deep, smooth root, not spread sideways
optionExplain: The unit asks for one not spread sideways (अ-तिर्यक्).
The unit asks for a smooth (श्लक्ष्ण) root that has gone deep.
Size is not mentioned; three qualities are.
Right: अतिर्यग्विस्तृतं गंभीरानुगतं श्लक्ष्णम्.
questions.explain: Three marks of the root to collect: not sideways, deep, smooth.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के दो भेद और संग्रह

questions.q: Match each word of the unit to its meaning.
questions.explain: Three marks of the root, and the verb.
questions.rule: अतिर्यग्विस्तृतम् = not spread sideways; गंभीरानुगतम् = gone deep; श्लक्ष्णम् = smooth; आहरेत् = one should collect.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के दो भेद और संग्रह

questions.q: Put these words of unit 6 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Of the two, the root, its three marks, and last the verb.
questions.rule: तयोः · मूलम् · अतिर्यग्विस्तृतम् · गंभीरानुगतम् · श्लक्ष्णम् · आहरेत्.
questions.teaches: The unit names the root, then its three marks in order, and ends with the verb आहरेत्.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के दो भेद और संग्रह

questions.q: Which is the right split of मूलमतिर्यग्विस्तृतम्?
optionExplain: Right: म् joins the vowel अ; क् becomes ग् before the voiced व.
This loses the negation अ-: it would mean spread sideways, the opposite.
यग्विस्तृतम् is not a word; the word is तिर्यक्, sideways.
Neither piece is a word.
questions.explain: मूलम् (root) + अतिर्यग्विस्तृतम् (not spread sideways).
questions.rule: म् + vowel → joined; क् → ग् before a voiced sound.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के दो भेद और संग्रह

questions.q: A gatherer finds a root spreading sideways under the soil. Should it be collected, by this unit?
options: No: it must not spread sideways
Yes, if it is dried first
optionExplain: The unit says the opposite: not sideways.
Right: अतिर्यग्विस्तृतम्: the root must not be spread sideways.
Smoothness alone is not enough; it must also not be sideways and must go deep.
Drying (unit 7) comes after collecting the right root.
questions.explain: The root to collect is not spread sideways, deep and smooth.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के दो भेद और संग्रह

questions.q: Like आहरेत् (one should collect), which form means one should dig (√खन्, invented)?
optionExplain: This is the present: he digs.
This is the future: he will dig.
Right: 3rd person singular optative: root + -एत्, like आहरेत्.
This is a past participle: dug.
questions.explain: आहरेत् is a 3 sg optative, one should collect.
questions.teaches: A 3rd-person singular optative in -एत् gives an instruction: आहरेत्, खनेत् = one should ...
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के दो भेद और संग्रह

questions.q: What does the unit say to do with the bark before keeping it?
optionExplain: Boiling is not mentioned.
Powdering and salt come in unit 8, not here.
Honey is not mentioned here.
Right: शोषयित्वा = having dried.
questions.explain: त्वचं शोषयित्वा सम्यक् स्थापयेत्: having dried the bark, keep it properly.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के दो भेद और संग्रह

questions.q: Match each word of the unit to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five words make the whole unit.
questions.rule: ततः = then; त्वचम् = bark; शोषयित्वा = having dried; सम्यक् = properly; स्थापयेत् = one should keep.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के दो भेद और संग्रह

questions.q: Put these words of unit 7 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Then, the bark, having dried, properly, one should keep.
questions.teaches: The unit ends with the main verb स्थापयेत्; the -त्वा form before it is the earlier action.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के दो भेद और संग्रह

questions.q: What kind of form is शोषयित्वा?
options: A noun of action: the drying
optionExplain: Right: -त्वा marks an action done before the main verb.
An optative would end in -एत्, like स्थापयेत्.
A noun of action would be शोषणम्; -त्वा is not a noun ending.
A future would have -स्य-, as in -स्यति.
questions.explain: शोषयित्वा = having dried (absolutive, causative of √शुष्).
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के दो भेद और संग्रह

questions.q: By the unit, which comes first: drying the bark or keeping it?
optionExplain: The order is the other way round.
Right: The -त्वा form (शोषयित्वा) is done before स्थापयेत्.
-त्वा marks an earlier action, not a simultaneous one.
शोषयित्वा ... स्थापयेत् fixes the order.
questions.explain: Absolutive first, main verb after: dry, then keep.
questions.rule: X-त्वा Y-एत् = having done X, one should do Y.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के दो भेद और संग्रह

questions.q: Join रामः + तत्र (invented) as one sandhi form, like ततः + त्वचम्. Which is right?
optionExplain: -अः → -ओ only before voiced sounds; त is unvoiced.
श् comes before च/छ, not before त.
Right: A visarga before त becomes स्: ततः + त्वचम् = ततस्त्वचम्.
ष् comes before ट/ठ, not before त.
questions.explain: ततस्त्वचम् shows the same rule: ततः + त्वचम्.
questions.teaches: A visarga before त or थ becomes स्: ततः + त्वचम् = ततस्त्वचम्; रामः + तत्र = रामस्तत्र.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के दो भेद और संग्रह

questions.q: In which kind of ailment does this unit prescribe the powder?
optionExplain: Pitta comes in unit 9 (पित्तोत्थेषु).
Kapha comes in unit 10 (कफजेषु).
This unit names Vāta ailments only.
Right: वातामयेषु = in ailments of Vāta.
questions.explain: पिबेद्वातामयेषु: one should drink (it) in Vāta ailments.
questions.section: दोष के अनुसार त्रिवृत् का प्रयोग

questions.q: Match each word of the unit to its meaning.
questions.explain: Two additions to the powder and two liquids to take it with.
questions.rule: शुंठी = dried ginger; सैंधव = rock salt; अम्लैः = with sour things; मांसरसेन = with meat juice.
questions.section: दोष के अनुसार त्रिवृत् का प्रयोग

questions.q: Put these words of unit 8 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: That powder, combined with ginger and rock salt, with sour things, with meat juice, one should drink.
questions.rule: तत् · चूर्णम् · शुंठीसैंधवयुक्तम् · अम्लैः · मांसरसेन · पिबेत्.
questions.teaches: The unit names the powder and what it is combined with, then the liquids, then the verb and the ailment.
questions.section: दोष के अनुसार त्रिवृत् का प्रयोग

questions.q: Which items does the unit say the powder is combined with (युक्तम्), as against drunk with?
options: Sour things and also meat juice
optionExplain: Right: शुंठीसैंधवयुक्तम्: combined with śuṇṭhī and saindhava.
These are the liquids it is drunk with (instrumental), not युक्तम्.
Milk and sugar belong to the Pitta use, unit 9.
Honey and urine belong to the Kapha use, unit 10.
questions.explain: युक्तम् = combined with: ginger and rock salt; अम्लैः, मांसरसेन = the liquids.
questions.section: दोष के अनुसार त्रिवृत् का प्रयोग

questions.q: A Vāta patient cannot take sour things. Which other liquid does the unit allow?
optionExplain: Milk is a Pitta vehicle (unit 9).
Right: मांसरसेनापि: or also with meat juice.
Urine is a Kapha vehicle (unit 10).
Sugarcane is in the Pitta list (unit 9).
questions.explain: For Vāta: sour things, or also meat juice.
questions.section: दोष के अनुसार त्रिवृत् का प्रयोग

questions.q: Like वात + आमयेषु = वातामयेषु, which is the joined form of पित्त + आमयेषु (invented)?
optionExplain: The long आ of आमय must remain: अ + आ gives आ.
ओ comes from अ + उ, not अ + आ.
Right: अ + आ → आ: पित्त + आमयेषु = पित्तामयेषु.
ए comes from अ + इ, not अ + आ.
questions.explain: Same join as in वातामयेषु.
questions.teaches: A final अ and an initial आ join as आ: वात + आमय = वातामय.
questions.section: दोष के अनुसार त्रिवृत् का प्रयोग

questions.q: Ailments of which doṣa does this unit address?
optionExplain: Vāta is unit 8 (वातामयेषु).
Kapha is unit 10 (कफजेषु).
This unit names Pitta only.
Right: पित्तोत्थेषु = in those arising from Pitta.
questions.explain: पित्तोत्थेषु: in (ailments) arisen from Pitta.
questions.section: दोष के अनुसार त्रिवृत् का प्रयोग

questions.q: Match each item of the list to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five of the items the powder is taken with in Pitta ailments.
questions.rule: क्षीर = milk; क्षौद्र = honey; द्राक्षा = grape; इक्षु = sugarcane; सर्पिः = ghee.
questions.section: दोष के अनुसार त्रिवृत् का प्रयोग

questions.q: Put these items in the order of the unit's list.
questions.explain: Milk, honey, grape, sugarcane, kāśmarya (its juice), ghee.
questions.rule: क्षीर · क्षौद्र · द्राक्षा · इक्षु · काश्मर्य · सर्पिः.
questions.teaches: The Pitta list runs milk, honey, grape, sugarcane, kāśmarya juice, ghee, then sweet decoctions and sugar.
questions.section: दोष के अनुसार त्रिवृत् का प्रयोग

questions.q: Which is the right split of द्राक्षेक्षु?
optionExplain: Right: आ + इ → ए: द्राक्षा + इक्षु = द्राक्षेक्षु.
क्षु is not a word; the word is इक्षु, sugarcane.
The word for sugarcane has a short इ, and the grape word is द्राक्षा.
ई + इ would give ई, not ए.
questions.explain: Two list items: grape (द्राक्षा) and sugarcane (इक्षु).
questions.section: दोष के अनुसार त्रिवृत् का प्रयोग

questions.q: Which of these may the powder be taken with in Pitta ailments, by this unit?
optionExplain: No: rock salt is in the Vāta use, unit 8.
Right: last item of the compound.
Right: in the list.
Right: first item of the compound.
No: urine is in the Kapha use, unit 10.
questions.explain: Pitta: milk, honey, grape, sugarcane, kāśmarya juice, ghee, sweet decoctions, sugar.
questions.rule: पित्त → क्षीर, क्षौद्र, द्राक्षा, इक्षु, काश्मर्यस्वरस, सर्पिः, स्वादुकाथ, शर्करा.
questions.section: दोष के अनुसार त्रिवृत् का प्रयोग

questions.q: Like पित्त + उत्थ = पित्तोत्थ, which is the joined form of कफ + उत्थ (invented)?
optionExplain: औ comes from अ + ओ or अ + औ, not अ + उ.
Right: अ + उ → ओ, as in पित्तोत्थ.
The vowels do not just drop the अ; they merge as ओ.
व् appears when उ comes first, not अ.
questions.explain: पित्तोत्थेषु = पित्त + उत्थेषु (arisen from Pitta).
questions.teaches: A final अ and an initial उ join as ओ: पित्त + उत्थ = पित्तोत्थ.
questions.section: दोष के अनुसार त्रिवृत् का प्रयोग

questions.q: Which liquid heads the list of this unit for Kapha ailments?
optionExplain: Milk heads the Pitta list, unit 9.
Meat juice is for Vāta, unit 8.
Right: The compound begins मूत्र-क्षौद्र-...
Ghee closes the Pitta compound, unit 9.
questions.explain: मूत्रक्षौद्रक्षारारिष्ट...: urine first.
questions.section: दोष के अनुसार त्रिवृत् का प्रयोग

questions.q: Match each item of the Kapha list to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four of the liquids of the Kapha list.
questions.rule: मूत्र = urine; क्षौद्र = honey; अरिष्ट = fermented medicinal liquor; पीलुरस = juice of pīlu.
questions.section: दोष के अनुसार त्रिवृत् का प्रयोग

questions.q: Put these items in the order of the unit's list.
questions.explain: Urine, honey, kṣāra, ariṣṭa, pīlu juice, then triphalā (and pañcakola).
questions.rule: मूत्र · क्षौद्र · क्षार · अरिष्ट · पीलुरस · त्रिफला.
questions.teaches: The Kapha list runs urine, honey, kṣāra, ariṣṭa, pīlu juice, triphalā, pañcakola, with (v)yoṣa powder added.
questions.section: दोष के अनुसार त्रिवृत् का प्रयोग

questions.q: Which item is in this Kapha list and also in the Pitta list of unit 9?
optionExplain: Urine is only in the Kapha list.
Pīlu juice is only in the Kapha list.
Milk is only in the Pitta list.
Right: क्षौद्र appears in both compounds.
questions.explain: Honey is the one item shared with the Pitta list of unit 9.
questions.section: दोष के अनुसार त्रिवृत् का प्रयोग

questions.q: Which group named in this unit is made of harītakī, bibhītaka and āmalaka?
optionExplain: pañcakola is five drugs: pippalī, its root, cavya, citraka, śuṇṭhī.
Right: triphalā = the three myrobalans: harītakī, bibhītaka, āmalaka.
trijātaka is named in unit 11: cinnamon bark, cardamom, bay leaf.
questions.explain: The data names the members of each group once.
questions.section: दोष के अनुसार त्रिवृत् का प्रयोग

questions.q: Like कफजेषु (in those born of Kapha), which form means in those born of Vāta (invented)?
optionExplain: This is nominative plural: those born of Vāta.
Right: -ज (born of) + locative plural -एषु: वात + ज + एषु.
This is locative singular: in one born of Vāta.
This is instrumental plural: by those born of Vāta.
questions.explain: कफजेषु = कफ + ज (born) + -एषु (in those).
questions.rule: X-ज = born of X; -एषु = in those (locative plural).
questions.teaches: A compound in -ज means born of: कफज, वातज; with -एषु it means in (ailments) born of ...
questions.section: दोष के अनुसार त्रिवृत् का प्रयोग

questions.q: Which of these does the unit say to prepare from the same substances?
optionExplain: Oils are not in this unit's list of forms.
No enema is named here.
Right: लेहगुटिकामोदक...: lehas, pills, modakas.
No nasal preparation is named here.
questions.explain: Five forms: lehas, pills, modakas, bhakṣya and bhojya foods.
questions.section: दोष के अनुसार त्रिवृत् का प्रयोग

questions.q: Match each fruit of the unit to its meaning.
questions.explain: Two fruits and buttermilk of the sour group, and the mango of the fragrant group.
questions.rule: मातुलुंग = citron; दाडिम = pomegranate; तक्र = buttermilk; सहकार = mango.
questions.section: दोष के अनुसार त्रिवृत् का प्रयोग

questions.q: Put the five forms in the order the unit names them.
questions.explain: Lehas, pills, modakas, bhakṣya, bhojya.
questions.teaches: The unit closes with the forms to make: लेह, गुटिका, मोदक, then the two food classes भक्ष्य and भोज्य.
questions.section: दोष के अनुसार त्रिवृत् का प्रयोग

questions.q: Which quality word goes with सैंधव (rock salt) in the unit?
optionExplain: अम्लानि closes the compound of fruit juices and buttermilk.
तीक्ष्णानि goes with vyoṣa.
सुरभीणि goes with mango juice, trijātaka and nāgakeśara.
Right: सैंधवलवणानि = salty with rock salt.
questions.explain: Each compound ends in its quality: -मधुराणि, -अम्लानि, -लवणानि, -तीक्ष्णानि, -पूरितानि, -सुरभीणि.
questions.section: दोष के अनुसार त्रिवृत् का प्रयोग

questions.q: A cook adds mango juice, cardamom and nāgakeśara to a modaka. Which quality of the unit is that?
optionExplain: Right: sahakāra juice, trijātaka (with cardamom) and nāgakeśara are in the -सुरभीणि compound.
The sour group is citron, pomegranate, āmalaka, kola, karamardaka, kapittha and buttermilk.
Sharp is made with vyoṣa.
Filled is with vesavāra.
questions.explain: सहकाररसत्रिजातकनागकेशरकपूरसुरभीणि = fragrant with these.
questions.section: दोष के अनुसार त्रिवृत् का प्रयोग

questions.q: Like एभिः + एव = एभिरेव, which is the joined form of द्रव्यैः + एव (invented)?
optionExplain: The visarga does not vanish here; after ऐ it becomes र्.
Right: A visarga after a vowel other than अ/आ becomes र् before a vowel.
स् appears before त/थ, not before a vowel.
य् is not made from a visarga.
questions.explain: एभिरेव and द्रव्यैर्यथास्वम् both show visarga → र्.
questions.rule: इः/ऐः + vowel or voiced sound → इर्/ऐर्.
questions.teaches: After a vowel other than अ or आ, a visarga becomes र् before a vowel or voiced sound: एभिः + एव = एभिरेव.
questions.section: दोष के अनुसार त्रिवृत् का प्रयोग

questions.q: What does भवति mean in this formula?
optionExplain: That is पिबेत् (unit 8).
That is व्याख्यास्यामः (unit 1).
Right: भवति = there is (3 sg present of √भू).
That is स्थापयेत् (unit 7).
questions.explain: भवति चात्र = and here there is (this).
questions.section: दोष के अनुसार त्रिवृत् का प्रयोग

questions.q: Match each word of the formula to its meaning.
questions.explain: Three words make the formula.
questions.rule: भवति = there is; च = and; अत्र = here.
questions.section: दोष के अनुसार त्रिवृत् का प्रयोग

questions.q: Put the words of the formula in the order of the text.
questions.explain: There is, and, here.
questions.teaches: The formula is the verb भवति followed by च and अत्र, joined as चात्र.
questions.section: दोष के अनुसार त्रिवृत् का प्रयोग

questions.q: Which is the right split of चात्र?
optionExplain: त्र is not a word here.
आत्र is not a word; the word is अत्र, here.
Neither piece is a word.
Right: अ + अ → आ: च + अत्र = चात्र.
questions.explain: च (and) + अत्र (here).
questions.section: दोष के अनुसार त्रिवृत् का प्रयोग

questions.q: After भवति चात्र, what kind of text does the data say follows?
optionExplain: Right: The note says the formula introduces the verses of lines 05.02.13-37.
The chapter goes on; verses follow.
This is still the purgation chapter.
The formula marks the move from prose to verse.
questions.explain: भवति चात्र introduces verses after a stretch of prose.
questions.section: दोष के अनुसार त्रिवृत् का प्रयोग

questions.q: Which is the joined form of च + अपि (and also, invented)?
optionExplain: The two अ do not drop to one short अ; they give आ.
Right: अ + अ → आ, as in च + अत्र = चात्र.
ए comes from अ + इ.
औ comes from अ + ओ or औ.
questions.explain: Same rule as चात्र.
questions.teaches: Two short अ join as a long आ: च + अत्र = चात्र, च + अपि = चापि.
questions.section: दोष के अनुसार त्रिवृत् का प्रयोग

questions.q: What does verse 13 call the lick (लेहः) at its end?
options: A strong emetic drink for Kapha
optionExplain: The verse says विरेचनम्, purgative; emesis is not named.
No ailment is named in this verse.
Right: लेहो हृद्यं विरेचनम् = the lick is a heart-pleasing purgative.
The verse calls it a purgative, not a daily food.
questions.explain: हृद्यम् = pleasing to the heart; विरेचनम् = purgative.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के हिम, लेह और चूर्ण-योग

questions.q: Match each word of verse 13 to its meaning.
pairs: with a decoction of trivṛt paste
questions.explain: These words carry the making of the preparation and its name.
questions.rule: त्रिवृत्कल्ककषायेण = with a decoction of trivṛt paste; साधितः = prepared; ससितः = with sugar; हिमः = cold preparation; लेहः = lick.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के हिम, लेह और चूर्ण-योग

questions.q: Put these words of verse 13 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: With what it is made, prepared, the hima with sugar, then (after the honey-trijāta word) the lick, and last what it is.
questions.rule: त्रिवृत्कल्ककषायेण · साधितः · ससितो हिमः · लेहो · हृद्यं विरेचनं.
questions.teaches: The verse first says how the hima is made, then what it is mixed with, and ends by naming it a heart-pleasing purgative.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के हिम, लेह और चूर्ण-योग

questions.q: What is the pausal (unjoined) form of ससितो in ससितो हिमः?
optionExplain: A final म् before ह would be written ससितं, not ससितो.
A final आ does not turn into ओ.
A final औ stays औ before a consonant; it would not be printed as ओ.
Right: -अः becomes -ओ before a voiced sound such as ह: ससितः + हिमः = ससितो हिमः.
questions.explain: ससितः (with sugar) agrees with हिमः (m. nom. sg.).
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के हिम, लेह और चूर्ण-योग

questions.q: By the data's reading, with what is the hima prepared (साधितः)?
options: A decoction made with trivṛt paste
Milk boiled together with the trivṛt root
Sesame oil and the trivṛt powder
Honey and ghee with the trivṛt
optionExplain: Right: त्रिवृत्कल्ककषायेण, read as a decoction made with trivṛt paste.
Milk is not named in this verse.
Oil and powder belong to the Kalyāṇaka recipe of line 05.02.31.
Honey comes in line 2 with trijāta; ghee is not named here.
questions.explain: The instrumental त्रिवृत्कल्ककषायेण says with what it is prepared.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के हिम, लेह और चूर्ण-योग

questions.q: Like ससितः (with sugar) said of हिमः, which word means with honey for the same masculine noun (invented)?
optionExplain: निर्- means without: without honey.
Right: स- + noun makes an adjective 'with ...'; masculine nominative like हिमः: समधुः.
This is the instrumental of the noun मधु, not a स- compound agreeing with हिमः.
This is accusative; हिमः is nominative, so the adjective must be nominative.
questions.explain: स + सित = ससित (with sugar), agreeing with हिमः.
questions.rule: स- + X = with X; the compound takes the case of its noun.
questions.teaches: A compound with स- in front means 'having X, with X' and agrees with its noun: ससितो हिमः, समधुर्हिमः.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के हिम, लेह और चूर्ण-योग

questions.q: What does verse 14 say happens once the powder has been licked?
optionExplain: The verse says विरिच्यते, is purged; vomiting is not named.
No fever or other ailment is named in this verse.
Right: साधु विरिच्यते = one is well purged.
Sleep is not named; the verse names purgation.
questions.explain: लीढ्वा साधु विरिच्यते: having licked, one is well purged.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के हिम, लेह और चूर्ण-योग

questions.q: Match each word of verse 14 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The words of the second line, and one drug of the first.
questions.rule: चूर्णितम् = powdered; लीढ्वा = having licked; साधु = well; विरिच्यते = one is purged; शर्करा = sugar.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के हिम, लेह और चूर्ण-योग

questions.q: Put the five drugs in the order verse 14 names them.
questions.explain: Ajagandhā, tavakṣīrī, vidārī, sugar, and trivṛt last.
questions.teaches: The first line is one long compound of five drugs, ending with trivṛt.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के हिम, लेह और चूर्ण-योग

questions.q: What kind of form is लीढ्वा?
optionExplain: An optative would end in -एत् or -यात्, like भक्षयेत्.
The noun lick is लेहः (line 05.02.14).
The present would be लेढि; लीढ्वा is not a finite verb.
Right: -त्वा (here -ढ्वा after √लिह्) marks an action done before the main verb विरिच्यते.
questions.explain: लीढ्वा = having licked (absolutive of √लिह्).
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के हिम, लेह और चूर्ण-योग

questions.q: Which of these does verse 14 put into the powder?
optionExplain: No: elā is named in line 05.02.20, not here.
No: viḍaṅga comes in the recipe of line 05.02.24.
Right: the third drug of the list.
Right: the last drug of the list.
Right: the fourth item.
questions.explain: Five items: ajagandhā, tavakṣīrī, vidārī, sugar, trivṛt.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के हिम, लेह और चूर्ण-योग

questions.q: Like विरिच्यते (one is purged), which form of √मुच् means one is released (invented)?
optionExplain: Right: Passive 3rd singular: root + -यते, like विरिच्यते from vi-√रिच्.
This is the active present: he releases.
This is a causative optative: one should cause to release.
This is an absolutive: having released.
questions.explain: विरिच्यते is a passive: the person is purged.
questions.teaches: A passive present in -यते says what is done to the subject: विरिच्यते (is purged), मुच्यते (is released).
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के हिम, लेह और चूर्ण-योग

questions.q: What does verse 15 say is smeared with trivṛt?
options: The whole belly of the suffering patient
The inside of a split sugarcane piece
A clay pot used for the cooking
The tongue of the suffering patient
optionExplain: No smearing of the body is named here.
Right: लिम्पेत् अन्तः त्रिवृतया द्विधाकृतेक्षुगण्डिकम्.
No pot is named in this verse.
The verse smears the sugarcane piece, not the tongue.
questions.explain: द्विधाकृत = made two-fold; इक्षुगण्डिक = piece of sugarcane; अन्तः = inside.
questions.rule: अन्तः त्रिवृतया लिम्पेत् = smear inside with trivṛt.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के हिम, लेह और चूर्ण-योग

questions.q: Match each name in the sufferer's compound to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are the troubles of the person for whom the preparation is made.
questions.rule: सन्निपात = derangement of all three doṣas together; ज्वर = fever; स्तंभ = stiffness; पिपासा = thirst; दाह = burning.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के हिम, लेह और चूर्ण-योग

questions.q: Put the sufferer's troubles in the order of verse 15.
questions.explain: Sannipāta, fever, stiffness, thirst, burning, and then पीडितः (afflicted).
questions.teaches: The first line is one compound: five troubles, closed by पीडितः, afflicted.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के हिम, लेह और चूर्ण-योग

questions.q: In लिंपेदंतस्त्रिवृतया, why is the verb लिम्पेत् printed as लिंपेद्?
options: द् is the verb's own last letter in the optative
It is a misprint for लिम्पेत्
Final त् becomes द् before the vowel of अन्तः
द् marks a past tense here
optionExplain: The optative ends in -एत्; द् comes only from sandhi.
This is regular sandhi, not a misprint.
Right: त् is voiced to द् before a vowel: लिम्पेत् + अन्तः = लिम्पेदन्तः.
The data labels लिम्पेत् an optative: one should smear.
questions.explain: The same token also shows अन्तः + त्रिवृतया → अन्तस्त्रिवृतया (visarga → स् before त).
questions.rule: त् → द् before a vowel; -ः → -स् before त.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के हिम, लेह और चूर्ण-योग

questions.q: A patient has fever, stiffness, thirst and burning. What does verse 15 itself say to do?
options: Lick trivṛt powder with honey and ghee
Drink trivṛt powder with sour things or with meat juice
Boil trivṛt in milk with sugar and honey
Split sugarcane and smear its inside with trivṛt
optionExplain: That is the recipe of verse 14, which names no patient.
That is the Vāta use of line 05.02.8.
No milk or boiling is named in this verse.
Right: This is the action of the verse; the next steps follow in line 05.02.19.
questions.explain: Verse 15: the patient described, then smearing a split sugarcane piece with trivṛt.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के हिम, लेह और चूर्ण-योग

questions.q: Like त्रिवृतया (with trivṛtā), which is the instrumental singular of the feminine एला, cardamom (invented use)?
optionExplain: Right: Feminine -आ nouns take -अया in the instrumental singular: त्रिवृता → त्रिवृतया.
-एन is the masculine/neuter instrumental.
-आम् is the accusative.
-आयाः is the genitive or ablative.
questions.explain: त्रिवृतया = with trivṛtā (f. inst. sg.).
questions.teaches: Feminine nouns in -आ form the instrumental singular in -अया: त्रिवृतया, एलया = with ...
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के हिम, लेह और चूर्ण-योग

questions.q: How does verse 16 say the joined sugarcane piece is cooked before eating?
options: Steamed by puṭa-cooking, in a wrapping
Roasted directly on bare open coals till dark
Dried in the sun for days
optionExplain: No milk or boiling is named here.
Right: तत्स्विन्नं पुटपाकेन: that, steamed by puṭa-cooking (puṭa = fold, wrapping).
The verse says steamed (स्विन्नम्) by puṭapāka.
No drying is named; it is steamed.
questions.explain: स्विन्नम् = steamed; पुटपाकेन = by cooking in a wrapped parcel.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के हिम, लेह और चूर्ण-योग

questions.q: Match each word of the first line to its meaning.

questions.rule: एकीकृत्य = having joined into one; स्विन्नम् = steamed; पुटपाकेन = by puṭa-cooking; भक्षयेत् = one should eat.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के हिम, लेह और चूर्ण-योग

questions.q: Put these words of the first line in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Having joined, and, that steamed, by puṭa-cooking, one should eat.
questions.teaches: The line goes from joining to steaming to eating, with the verb भक्षयेत् last.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के हिम, लेह और चूर्ण-योग

questions.q: What does पुटपाक mean, by the data's note?
optionExplain: Nothing in puṭa means twice.
पाक is cooking, not grinding.
Right: puṭa = fold, wrapping; pāka = cooking.
No soaking is meant; पाक is cooking.
questions.explain: पुटपाक = puṭa-cooking, cooking wrapped in a parcel.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के हिम, लेह और चूर्ण-योग

questions.q: Which items does the second line of verse 16 name?
optionExplain: No: viḍaṅga comes in line 05.02.24.
No: honey is not in this line.
Right: भृंगैलाभ्याम् = with bhṛṅga and elā.
Right: the last word of the line.
Right: समा नीली.
questions.explain: The line names bhṛṅga, elā, nīlī, trivṛt and sugar; how they are measured is unclear.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के हिम, लेह और चूर्ण-योग

questions.q: एकीकृत्य takes -त्य because एकी- stands before √कृ. With no first part, which absolutive of √कृ means having done?
optionExplain: -य / -त्य is used only when a prefix or similar first part stands before the root.
This is the past participle: done.
This is a future participle: about to do.
Right: A bare root takes -त्वा: कृत्वा.
questions.explain: एकी + कृ + त्य = एकीकृत्य (having made into one).
questions.rule: Bare root: -त्वा; with a prefix: -य (-त्य after a short vowel).
questions.teaches: The absolutive is -त्वा on a bare root (कृत्वा) but -य/-त्य when a first part stands before it (एकीकृत्य).
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के हिम, लेह और चूर्ण-योग

questions.q: In what form does verse 17 say the powder is drunk?
options: As a tarpaṇa, a satiating draught
As drops put into the nose
As a gargle, then spat out
optionExplain: Right: तर्पणं पिबेत् = one should drink (it as) a tarpaṇa.
No enema is named; the verb is पिबेत्, drink.
Nasal use is not named here.
The verse says drink, not gargle.
questions.explain: चूर्णं ... तर्पणं पिबेत्.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के हिम, लेह और चूर्ण-योग

questions.q: Match each word of verse 17 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Three things the powder is taken with, its form, and one group of users.
questions.rule: फलरस = fruit juice; क्षौद्र = honey; सक्तु = flour of roasted grain; तर्पणम् = satiating draught; अल्पानलेषु = in those with little fire.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के हिम, लेह और चूर्ण-योग

questions.q: Put these parts of verse 17 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: The powder, with what, as what, the verb, then in which ailments and in whom.
questions.rule: चूर्णं · फलरसक्षौद्रसक्तुभिः · तर्पणं · पिबेत् · वातपित्तकफोत्थेषु रोगेषु · अल्पानलेषु च.
questions.teaches: Line 1 says how to take the powder; line 2 says in whom, with locatives.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के हिम, लेह और चूर्ण-योग

questions.q: Which is the right split of रोगेष्वल्पानलेषु?
optionExplain: अल्पान and लेषु are not words; the word is अनलेषु, fire.
Right: उ + अ → व: रोगेषु + अल्प → रोगेष्वल्प; अ + अ → आ: अल्प + अनल → अल्पानल.
रोगेष्व is not a form; the locative plural is रोगेषु.
The locative plural ends in short -उ: रोगेषु.
questions.explain: Two locative plurals: in ailments, in those with little fire.
questions.rule: उ + unlike vowel → व्; अ + अ → आ.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के हिम, लेह और चूर्ण-योग

questions.q: Besides ailments of the three doṣas, in whom does verse 17 also give this powder?
options: In those whose fire is very strong
optionExplain: The verse says little (अल्प) fire, not strong.
Pregnancy is not named in this verse.
Right: अल्पानलेषु च = and in those with little fire.
Poison is not named in this verse.
questions.explain: अल्प = little; अनल = fire, probably the digestive fire.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के हिम, लेह और चूर्ण-योग

questions.q: Join अल्प + अन्नम् (little food, invented) like अल्प + अनल: ____. Type it in Devanagari or English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: अ + अ → आ: अल्प + अन्नम् = अल्पान्नम्, as अल्प + अनलेषु = अल्पानलेषु.
questions.teaches: Two short अ sounds join as a long आ: अल्प + अनल = अल्पानल.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के हिम, लेह और चूर्ण-योग

questions.q: For whom does verse 18 call the preceding preparation a harmless purgation?
optionExplain: The verse says delicate, not strong.
Age is not named in this verse.
Children are not named in this verse.
Right: नरेषु सुकुमारेषु निरपायं विरेचनम्.
questions.explain: सुकुमार = delicate; निरपाय = without harm.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के हिम, लेह और चूर्ण-योग

questions.q: Match each word of the first line to its meaning.

questions.rule: नरेषु = in men; सुकुमारेषु = delicate; निरपायम् = harmless; विरेचनम् = purgation.

questions.q: Put the items of the new list in the order of verse 18.

questions.teaches: The second line is a compound list of drugs closed by trivṛt.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के हिम, लेह और चूर्ण-योग

questions.q: What does निरपायम् mean, as the data renders it?
optionExplain: Right: निर् + अपाय: without loss or danger, rendered harmless.
अपाय is loss or danger, not delay.
No word for food is in निरपाय.
No word for water is in निरपाय.
questions.explain: निरपायं विरेचनम् = a harmless purgation.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के हिम, लेह और चूर्ण-योग

questions.q: What is कणा in this list, by the data?
optionExplain: Cardamom is एला (line 05.02.20).
Right: कणा = pippalī, long pepper (standard).
Black pepper is मरिच (line 05.02.29).
Dried ginger is शुंठी (line 05.02.8).
questions.explain: kaṇā literally grain, particle; used as a name of pippalī.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के हिम, लेह और चूर्ण-योग

questions.q: Like नरेषु सुकुमारेषु (in delicate men), which phrase means in firm men, with दृढ (invented)?
optionExplain: दृढाः is nominative plural; it does not agree with नरेषु.
दृढे is locative singular; नरेषु is plural.
Right: The adjective takes the same case and number as its noun: locative plural -एषु.

questions.explain: नरेषु and सुकुमारेषु are both locative plural.
questions.rule: Adjective agrees with its noun in case and number.
questions.teaches: An adjective agrees with its noun in case and number: नरेषु सुकुमारेषु, नरेषु दृढेषु.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के हिम, लेह और चूर्ण-योग

questions.q: With what does verse 19 say the preparation is taken?
options: Milk and sugar, or else water
Sour things, or else meat juice
Honey and ghee, or else jaggery
optionExplain: Milk and water are not named in this verse.

questions.q: Match each clear word of verse 19 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The vehicles of the first line and two ailments of the second.

questions.q: Put these words of verse 19 in the order of the text.

questions.q: Which is the right split of मध्वाज्येन?
optionExplain: Right: उ + आ → वा: मधु + आज्येन = मध्वाज्येन.
Neither piece is a word.
मध्व is not a word; the word is मधु, honey.
अज्येन is not a word; with short अ the join would be मध्वज्-.
questions.explain: मधु (honey) + आज्य (ghee), in the instrumental: with honey and ghee.

questions.section: त्रिवृत् के हिम, लेह और चूर्ण-योग

questions.q: What does प्लीहोदर denote, by the data?

A burning felt in the chest
A pain felt in the joints

Joint pain is not named in this verse.
