questions.q: मध्वाज्येन is the instrumental singular of the dvandva मध्वाज्य. Which is the instrumental singular of क्षीरघृत, milk and ghee (invented)?
optionExplain: This is nominative/accusative, not with ...
This is genitive: of milk and ghee.
Right: -अ stem, instrumental singular -एन, like मध्वाज्येन: with milk and ghee.
This is locative: in milk and ghee.
questions.explain: A dvandva of two liquids taken together can stand in the singular: मध्वाज्येन.
questions.teaches: A pair of substances can form one singular dvandva; its instrumental in -एन means 'with both': मध्वाज्येन, क्षीरघृतेन.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् के हिम, लेह और चूर्ण-योग

questions.q: What does verse 20 say the preparation does to many ailments (गदान् बहून्)?
optionExplain: The verse says wipes away, the opposite.
परिमार्ष्टि does not mean reveal.
No upward movement is named.
Right: परिमार्ष्टि = wipes away (pari-√मृज्).
questions.explain: परिमार्ष्टि गदान् बहून् = it wipes away many ailments.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 20 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The clear words of line 1 and two drugs of line 2.
questions.rule: परिमार्ष्टि = wipes away; गदान् = ailments; बहून् = many; त्रिफला = three myrobalans; चित्रक = leadwort.

questions.q: Put the drugs of the second line in the order of verse 20.
questions.explain: Viḍaṅga, pippalī root, triphalā, dhānya, citraka.
questions.teaches: The Kalyāṇaka list opens with five drugs in one compound; it continues in the next verse.

questions.q: In which case is विडंगपिप्पलीमूलत्रिफलाधान्यचित्रकान्?
optionExplain: Right: -आन् is the masculine accusative plural ending.
That would end in -आः (चित्रकाः).
That would end in -ऐः (चित्रकैः).
That would end in -एषु (चित्रकेषु).
questions.explain: The drug list is an accusative object; its verb comes later in the recipe.

questions.q: Which item of this list does the data take as coriander seed (probable)?
optionExplain: citraka is leadwort.
Right: dhānya = coriander seed (dhānyaka), probable; plain sense grain.
viḍaṅga is false black pepper.
triphalā is the three myrobalans.
questions.explain: dhānya in drug lists is usually dhānyaka, coriander (probable).

questions.q: Like गदान् बहून् (many ailments, accusative), which phrase means many ailments with रोग, in the accusative (invented)?
optionExplain: This is nominative plural.
This is instrumental plural: with many ailments.
Right: Masculine accusative plural: रोग → रोगान्; बहु → बहून्.
This is locative plural: in many ailments.
questions.explain: गदान् बहून् is the object of परिमार्ष्टि.
questions.teaches: The object of a verb is accusative; masculine plural -आन् / -ऊन्: गदान् बहून्, रोगान् बहून्.

questions.q: What amount does verse 21 give for each powdered item?
optionExplain: Eight palas is the measure of oil and trivṛt in line 05.02.31.
Three prasthas is the dhātrī juice of line 05.02.32.
Half a tulā goes with the jaggery of line 05.02.32.
Right: कार्षिकं पृथक् = of one karṣa, separately.
questions.explain: कार्षिकम् = of (one) karṣa; पृथक् = separately.

questions.q: Match each drug of verse 21 to its name in English.
questions.explain: Five of the items added to the Kalyāṇaka list.
questions.rule: मरिच = black pepper; इन्द्रयव = kuṭaja seeds; अजाजी = cumin; हस्तिपिप्पली = elephant pepper (probable); पंचलवण = the five salts.

questions.q: Put these drugs in the order of verse 21.
questions.explain: Marica, indrayava, ajājī, pippalī, hastipippalī, then dīpyaka in line 2.
questions.rule: मरिच · इन्द्रयव · अजाजी · पिप्पली · हस्तिपिप्पली · दीप्यक.
questions.teaches: Line 1 is one compound of five drugs; line 2 adds dīpyaka and the five salts and gives the measure.

questions.q: Which is the right split of मरिचेंद्रयवाजाजी?
optionExplain: Right: अ + इ → ए: मरिच + इन्द्र → मरिचेन्द्र; अ + अ → आ: इन्द्रयव + अजाजी → इन्द्रयवाजाजी.
न्द्रयव is not a word.
मरि and चेन्द्रयव are not words.
एन्द्रयव is not a word; and अ + ए would give ऐ, not ए.
questions.explain: Three drugs: black pepper, indrayava, cumin.
questions.rule: अ + इ → ए; अ + अ → आ.

questions.q: What does verse 21 say about the five salts (पंचलवण)?
options: They are left out of the powder
They are included, but not named here
Only rock salt is to be used, not five
They are to be drunk on their own
optionExplain: पंचलवणम् is in the list of items powdered.
Right: The data notes that the five salts are not named in this verse.
No single salt is named; the verse says five salts.
They are powdered with the other items.
questions.explain: पंचलवणम् = the five salts, as one group; the names are not given.

questions.q: Like कार्षिकम् (of one karṣa) from कर्ष, which word means of one pala, from पल (invented)?
optionExplain: The first vowel must be lengthened (vṛddhi): पा-, not प-.
This is the measure itself, not of one pala.
Right: -इक adds vṛddhi to the first vowel: कर्ष → कार्षिक, पल → पालिक.
This is the instrumental: by a pala.
questions.explain: कार्षिक = weighing one karṣa.
questions.teaches: The suffix -इक with vṛddhi of the first vowel makes 'of one ...' from a measure: कर्ष → कार्षिक, पल → पालिक.

questions.q: What measure does verse 22 give for the two portions of sesame oil and trivṛt powder?
optionExplain: One karṣa each is the measure of the spices of verse 21.
Three prasthas is the dhātrī juice of line 2.
Half a tulā goes with the jaggery.
Right: चाष्टपलोन्मितौ = and measured as eight palas.
questions.explain: अष्ट = eight; पल = a weight; उन्मितौ = measured (dual).

questions.q: Match each phrase of verse 22 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The ingredients and their counts in the verse.
questions.rule: तिलतैल = sesame oil; त्रिवृच्चूर्ण = trivṛt powder; भागौ = two portions; धात्रीफलरस = dhātrī (emblic) fruit juice; प्रस्थान् त्रीन् = three prasthas.

questions.q: Put these parts of verse 22 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Oil, trivṛt powder, their measure, then the dhātrī juice and its measure.
questions.rule: तिलतैल · त्रिवृच्चूर्ण · अष्टपल · धात्रीफलरस · प्रस्थान् त्रीन्.
questions.teaches: Each ingredient of the verse is followed by its measure: oil and powder by eight palas, the juice by three prasthas.

questions.q: Which is the right split of त्रिवृच्चूर्ण?
optionExplain: Right: त् + च → च्च: त्रिवृत् + चूर्ण = त्रिवृच्चूर्ण.
Neither piece is a word.
द् appears before voiced sounds; च is unvoiced, and द् would not give च्च.
The drug name ends in त्, not in a visarga.
questions.explain: त्रिवृत् (turpeth) + चूर्ण (powder).

questions.q: Why is भागौ in the dual?
options: It counts the three prasthas of the dhātrī juice
It counts two portions: oil and trivṛt powder
It counts the oil and the jaggery
It counts the five salts of verse 21
optionExplain: The prasthas are counted by त्रीन्, three, in the plural.
Right: तिलतैल-त्रिवृच्चूर्ण-भागौ = the two portions, of sesame oil and of trivṛt powder.
The jaggery is in line 2, not in this compound.
The salts belong to the spice list with one karṣa each.
questions.explain: Two members in the compound, so the dual: भागौ, उन्मितौ.

questions.q: Like प्रस्थान् त्रीन् (three prasthas, masculine accusative), which means three fruits with the neuter फल, accusative (invented)?
optionExplain: These are masculine forms; फल is neuter.
त्रीन् is masculine; with a neuter noun it is त्रीणि.
Right: The numeral three agrees in gender: masculine त्रीन्, neuter त्रीणि; फल takes फलानि.
त्रयः is masculine nominative.
questions.explain: प्रस्थान् त्रीन्: noun and numeral agree, both m. acc. pl.
questions.rule: त्रि agrees: m. acc. त्रीन्, n. nom./acc. त्रीणि.
questions.teaches: The numeral त्रि (three) takes its noun's gender and case: प्रस्थान् त्रीन् (m.), फलानि त्रीणि (n.).

questions.q: On what fire does verse 23 say the mixture is cooked?
options: No fire: it is mixed cold
optionExplain: मृदु means mild, the opposite of strong.
पक्त्वा says it is cooked.
The verse names a fire (अग्नि), not the sun.
Right: पक्त्वा मृद्वग्निना = having cooked on a mild fire.
questions.explain: मृदु = mild; अग्निना = with fire.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 23 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Three words of the method and two conditions of the list.
questions.rule: पक्त्वा = having cooked; मृद्वग्निना = on a mild fire; खादेत् = one should eat; मंदाग्नित्वम् = slowness of fire (weak digestion); ज्वरम् = fever.

questions.q: Put these words of verse 23 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Having cooked, on a mild fire, one should eat, then; and the list begins: weak digestion, fever.
questions.rule: पक्त्वा · मृद्वग्निना · खादेत् · ततः · मंदाग्नित्वं · ज्वरं.
questions.teaches: Line 1 gives the method (cook, then eat); line 2 opens the list of conditions, in the accusative.

questions.q: Which is the right split of मृद्वग्निना?
optionExplain: Right: उ + अ → व: मृदु + अग्निना = मृद्वग्निना.
Neither piece is a word.
वग्निना is not a word; the word is अग्निना, by fire.
The व comes from the उ of मृदु; the second word is अग्निना.
questions.explain: मृदु (mild) + अग्निना (with fire).

questions.q: Which of these conditions does verse 23 list (the verb destroys comes in verse 24)?
optionExplain: No: cough is in verse 19, another recipe.
Right: the second item.
Right: the first item of line 2.
No: thirst is in verse 15.
No: burning is in verse 15.
questions.explain: Line 2: weak digestion, fever, fainting, mūtrakṛcchra, arocaka.

questions.q: Join लघु + अन्नम् (light food, invented) like मृदु + अग्निना: ____. Type it in Devanagari or English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: उ + अ → व: लघु + अन्नम् = लघ्वन्नम्, as मृदु + अग्निना = मृद्वग्निना.
questions.teaches: A final उ before an unlike vowel becomes व्: मृदु + अग्निना = मृद्वग्निना.

questions.q: Besides destroying ailments, what else does verse 24 say the preparation is?
options: A daily food for the healthy
optionExplain: No emesis is named; it is a purgative recipe.
Right: पुंसवनश्च सः = and it is a puṃsavana.
The verse does not call it a food.
Poison is not named in this verse.
questions.explain: पुंसवन = male-begetting.

questions.q: Match each ailment of verse 24 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five of the seven names in the first line.
questions.rule: कुष्ठ = skin diseases incl. leprosy; अर्शस् = haemorrhoids; कामला = jaundice; मेह = prameha urinary disorders; भगंदर = anal fistula.

questions.q: Put these ailments in the order of verse 24.
questions.explain: Kuṣṭha, arśas, kāmalā, meha, gulma, udara, and bhagandara closes the compound.
questions.rule: कुष्ठ · अर्शः · कामला · मेह · गुल्म · उदर.
questions.teaches: The first line is one compound of seven ailments, from kuṣṭha to bhagandara.

questions.q: Why does the visarga stay in अर्शःकामला?
options: It is a misprint and should be removed
It marks अर्शः as a dual
A visarga stays before an unvoiced क
It should have become ओ here
optionExplain: This is regular sandhi, not a misprint.
The stem is अर्शस्; the visarga is its final s, not a dual.
Right: arśas + kāmalā: before the unvoiced क the visarga remains.
-अः → ओ happens before voiced sounds; अर्शस् is an -अस् stem and क is unvoiced.
questions.explain: The stem is अर्शस्; its final स् shows as visarga before क.

questions.q: By the data's note, what does सः (it) refer to?
optionExplain: सः is the subject of हन्ति, the one that destroys ailments.
The physician is not named in this verse.
The whole prepared guḍa, not trivṛt alone, is meant.
Right: The note says सः refers to the guḍa Kalyāṇaka named in line 05.02.37.
questions.explain: हन्ति ... सः: it destroys; it is the Kalyāṇaka guḍa.

questions.q: Like पुंसवनः + च → पुंसवनश्च, which is the joined form of रामः + च (invented)?
optionExplain: Right: A visarga before च becomes श्: पुंसवनः + च = पुंसवनश्च.
स् comes before त/थ, not before च.
-अः → ओ only before voiced sounds; च is unvoiced.
The visarga does not drop before च; it becomes श्.
questions.explain: पुंसवनश्च shows the rule: visarga + च → श्च.
questions.teaches: A visarga before च or छ becomes श्: पुंसवनः + च = पुंसवनश्च; रामः + च = रामश्च.

questions.q: In which seasons does verse 25 say the guḍa named Kalyāṇaka is fit for use?
optionExplain: The verse says सर्वेषु ऋतुषु, all seasons, not one.
Right: सर्वेष्वृतुषु यौगिकः = fit for use in all seasons.
No single season is named; it is all seasons.
The verse names no particular season.
questions.explain: सर्वेषु = in all; ऋतुषु = in the seasons; यौगिकः = fit for use.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् की गुटिका और ऋतु-अनुसार योग

questions.q: Match each word of verse 25 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The first line names and praises the guḍa; the second ends with trivṛt.
questions.rule: गुडः = guḍa; कल्याणकः = Kalyāṇaka; ऋतुषु = in the seasons; यौगिकः = fit for use; त्रिवृत् = turpeth.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् की गुटिका और ऋतु-अनुसार योग

questions.q: Put the drugs that go with trivṛt in the order of verse 25.
questions.explain: Vyoṣa, trijātaka, ambhoda, kṛmighna, āmalaka; trivṛt closes the line.
questions.teaches: The second line is one instrumental compound of five drug names (two of them sets of three), and त्रिवृत् stands last.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् की गुटिका और ऋतु-अनुसार योग

questions.q: Which split of सर्वेष्वृतुषु is right?
optionExplain: There is no word वृतुषु; the व् comes from the उ of सर्वेषु.
There is no form सर्वेष्व; the locative plural is सर्वेषु.
Right: उ before a vowel becomes व्: सर्वेषु + ऋतुषु → सर्वेष्वृतुषु.
ष्वृतुषु is not a word; सर्वेषु agrees with ऋतुषु.
questions.explain: सर्वेषु ऋतुषु: both locative plural, in all seasons.
questions.rule: उ / ऊ + unlike vowel → व् + vowel.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् की गुटिका और ऋतु-अनुसार योग

questions.q: By the card, which three drugs does the set name व्योष stand for?
options: Cinnamon bark, small cardamom, bay leaf
Dry ginger, long pepper, black pepper
optionExplain: That is trijātaka, the next name in the line.
That is triphalā, which this verse does not name.
These are the three single drugs after trijātaka.
Right: vyoṣa = śuṇṭhī, pippalī, marica (standard).
questions.explain: व्योष = the three pungents; त्रिजातक = the set of cinnamon bark, small cardamom and bay leaf.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् की गुटिका और ऋतु-अनुसार योग

questions.q: Like आमलकैः + त्रिवृत् → आमलकैस्त्रिवृत्, which is the joined form of फलैः + तैलम् (invented)?
optionExplain: Right: A visarga before त becomes स्: आमलकैः + त्रिवृत् → आमलकैस्त्रिवृत्.
The visarga does not drop before त; it becomes स्.
र् comes before voiced sounds, not before an unvoiced त.
श् comes before च/छ, not before त.
questions.explain: आमलकैस्त्रिवृत्: visarga → स् before त.
questions.teaches: A visarga before त or थ becomes स्: आमलकैस्त्रिवृत्, फलैस्तैलम्.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् की गुटिका और ऋतु-अनुसार योग

questions.q: With what does verse 26 say the pills are made?
optionExplain: Ghee is not named in this verse.
Right: क्षौद्रेण गुलिकाः कृताः = pills are made with honey.
The guḍa was the Kalyāṇaka preparation; these pills use honey.
Cow's urine comes in line 05.02.50, not here.
questions.explain: क्षौद्र = honey; गुलिका = pill; कृताः = made.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् की गुटिका और ऋतु-अनुसार योग

questions.q: Match each ailment of verse 26 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five of the seven conditions of the second line.
questions.rule: मूत्रकृच्छ्र = dysuria; ज्वर = fever; छर्दि = vomiting; कास = cough; भ्रम = giddiness.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् की गुटिका और ऋतु-अनुसार योग

questions.q: Put these conditions in the order of verse 26.
questions.explain: Urine-difficulty, fever, vomiting, cough, then śoṣa and giddiness; kṣaya closes the line.
questions.rule: मूत्रकृच्छ्र · ज्वर · छर्दि · कास · शोष · भ्रम.
questions.teaches: The second line is a compound of four names followed by three separate locatives: शोषे, भ्रमे, क्षये.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् की गुटिका और ऋतु-अनुसार योग

questions.q: Which split of ज्वरच्छर्दि is right?
optionExplain: There is no word च्छर्दि; the च् is added by sandhi.
A visarga before छ would give ज्वरश्छर्दि.
Right: छ after a short vowel is written च्छ: ज्वर + छर्दि → ज्वरच्छर्दि.
There is no word चर्दि; vomiting is छर्दि.
questions.explain: छर्दि = vomiting; the doubling च्छ is only spelling sandhi.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् की गुटिका और ऋतु-अनुसार योग

questions.q: Which of these conditions does verse 26 name for the pills?
optionExplain: Right: in the compound of the second line.
No: arśas is also in line 05.02.35, not here.
Right: in the compound, after fever.
Right: भ्रमे, in giddiness.
No: kāmalā is in the Kalyāṇaka list of line 05.02.35.
questions.explain: Seven conditions: mūtrakṛcchra, fever, vomiting, cough, śoṣa, giddiness, kṣaya.
questions.rule: मूत्रकृच्छ्र · ज्वर · छर्दि · कास · शोष · भ्रम · क्षय.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् की गुटिका और ऋतु-अनुसार योग

questions.q: Like गुलिकाः कृताः (pills are made, f. pl.), which phrase correctly says a lick is made, with लेहः (m. sg.)?
optionExplain: कृता is feminine singular.
कृताः is plural; लेहः is singular.
कृतम् is neuter; लेहः is masculine.
Right: The participle takes the gender and number of its noun: m. sg. कृतः.
questions.explain: कृताः agrees with गुलिकाः: feminine nominative plural.
questions.rule: Past participle = adjective: it agrees with its noun.
questions.teaches: A past participle such as कृत agrees with its noun: गुलिकाः कृताः (f. pl.), लेहः कृतः (m. sg.).
questions.section: त्रिवृत् की गुटिका और ऋतु-अनुसार योग

questions.q: Which of these does verse 27 name as a condition where the pills are approved?
optionExplain: Right: शस्ताः सर्वविषेषु च = approved in all poisons too.
Wounds are not named in this verse.
Worms are not named here.
Swelling is not named in this verse.
questions.explain: सर्वविषेषु = in all poisons (loc. pl. of विष).
questions.section: त्रिवृत् की गुटिका और ऋतु-अनुसार योग

questions.q: Match each word of verse 27 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Three words of the first line and two of the new list.
questions.rule: पाण्ड्वामय = pāṇḍu disease; अल्पाग्नि = weak digestion; शस्ताः = approved; कौटजं बीजम् = kuṭaja seed; विश्वभेषज = dry ginger.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् की गुटिका और ऋतु-अनुसार योग

questions.q: Put the drugs of the second line in the order of verse 27.
questions.explain: Trivṛt, kuṭaja seed, pippalī, viśvabheṣaja.
questions.teaches: The second line names four drugs of a new recipe, from trivṛt to dry ginger.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् की गुटिका और ऋतु-अनुसार योग

questions.q: Which split of पाण्ड्वामये is right?
optionExplain: There is no stem पाण्ड्व; the व् comes from the उ of पाण्डु.
Right: उ before the unlike vowel आ becomes व्: पाण्डु + आमये → पाण्ड्वामये.
There is no word वामये here; आमय means ailment.
ओ + आ would give पाण्डवामये, not पाण्ड्वामये.
questions.explain: पाण्डु = pale; आमय = ailment; together the pāṇḍu disease.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् की गुटिका और ऋतु-अनुसार योग

questions.q: What does the avagraha (ऽ) in पाण्ड्वामयेऽल्पाग्नौ show?
options: The first word is a dual form
The अ of अल्प merged after -ए
A broken letter in the old print
optionExplain: No visarga stands there; आमये ends in ए.
आमये is locative singular here; the ऽ says nothing of number.
Right: आमये + अल्पाग्नौ: after final ए an initial अ merges, marked ऽ.
It is regular sandhi, not damage.
questions.explain: -ए + अ- → -एऽ-: आमयेऽल्पाग्नौ.
questions.rule: ए / ओ + अ → ए / ओ + ऽ.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् की गुटिका और ऋतु-अनुसार योग

questions.q: Like आमये + अल्पाग्नौ → आमयेऽल्पाग्नौ, which is the joined form of वने + अस्ति (invented)?
optionExplain: ए does not turn into आ before अ.
ए → अय् happens before other vowels, not before अ.
ए + अ does not give ऐ.
Right: Final ए before अ keeps ए and the अ merges, shown by ऽ.
questions.explain: आमयेऽल्पाग्नौ shows the rule ए + अ → एऽ.
questions.rule: ए / ओ + अ → ए / ओ + ऽ.
questions.teaches: After a final ए or ओ an initial अ is merged and marked with ऽ: आमयेऽल्पाग्नौ, वनेऽस्ति.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् की गुटिका और ऋतु-अनुसार योग

questions.q: In which season does verse 28 say this purgation is given?
optionExplain: Right: वर्षाकाले विरेचनं = a purgation in the rainy season.
The cold season comes in line 05.02.47, not here.
The hot season comes in line 05.02.48.
Spring is not named in this verse.
questions.explain: वर्षा = the rains; काले = in the time (of).
questions.section: त्रिवृत् की गुटिका और ऋतु-अनुसार योग

questions.q: Match each word of the first line of verse 28 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The first line is one compound, a time word and the name of the purgation.
questions.rule: क्षौद्र = honey; द्राक्षा = grape or raisin; रस = juice; उपेतम् = joined with; विरेचनम् = purgation.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् की गुटिका और ऋतु-अनुसार योग

questions.q: Put these parts of the first line in the order of verse 28.
questions.explain: Honey, drākṣā juice, joined with, in the rains, a purgation.
questions.teaches: The line says first what the formula is joined with, then the season, and ends with विरेचनम्.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् की गुटिका और ऋतु-अनुसार योग

questions.q: Which split of रसोपेतं is right?
optionExplain: There is no word पेतम्; the ओ comes from अ + उ.
Right: अ + उ → ओ: रस + उपेतम् → रसोपेतम्.
A visarga before उ would drop and leave रस उपेतम्, two words.
There is no word ओपेतम्; joined with is उपेतम्.
questions.explain: उपेत = joined with (upa-√i).
questions.section: त्रिवृत् की गुटिका और ऋतु-अनुसार योग

questions.q: A physician gives the trivṛt, kuṭaja-seed, pippalī and dry-ginger purgation in the rains. With what does verse 28 join it?
optionExplain: Hot water is the vehicle of line 05.02.47; rock salt is not named here.
Cow's urine is in line 05.02.50.
Right: क्षौद्रद्राक्षारसोपेतम् = joined with honey and drākṣā juice.
Neither ghee nor milk is named in this verse.
questions.explain: The first line closes the formula begun in line 05.02.42.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् की गुटिका और ऋतु-अनुसार योग

questions.q: Like रस + उपेतम् → रसोपेतम्, which is the joined form of मधुघृत + उपेतम्, joined with honey and ghee (invented)?
optionExplain: अ + उ gives ओ, not औ.
अ + उ does not give ऊ.
व् arises from उ before a vowel, not from अ.
Right: अ + उ → ओ, as in रसोपेतम्.
questions.explain: रसोपेतम् shows the rule अ + उ → ओ.
questions.teaches: Final अ before उ makes ओ: रस + उपेतम् → रसोपेतम्, मधुघृत + उपेतम् → मधुघृतोपेतम्.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् की गुटिका और ऋतु-अनुसार योग

questions.q: What liquid does the clear first word of verse 29 name?
options: Cow's urine with rock salt in it
Hot water with sugar added to it
optionExplain: Right: द्राक्षाम्बुना = with drākṣā water.
Neither is named in this verse.
Hot water comes in line 05.02.47.
No sour gruel is named here.
questions.explain: द्राक्षा = grape or raisin; अम्बु = water; -ना = with.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् की गुटिका और ऋतु-अनुसार योग

questions.q: Match each drug of the second line to its identification on the card.
questions.explain: Five of the six drugs; trivṛt is the first.
questions.rule: चित्रक = leadwort; पाठा = velvet-leaf (probable); अजाजी = cumin (probable); सरल = chir pine (probable); वचा = sweet flag.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् की गुटिका और ऋतु-अनुसार योग

questions.q: Put the drugs of the second line in the order of verse 29.
questions.explain: Trivṛt, citraka, pāṭhā, ajājī, sarala, vacā.
questions.rule: त्रिवृता · चित्रकं · पाठाम् · अजाजीं · सरलं · वचां.
questions.teaches: The second line lists six drugs, five of them as objects (accusative), from trivṛt to vacā.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् की गुटिका और ऋतु-अनुसार योग

questions.q: Which split of पाठामजाजीं is right?
optionExplain: There is no drug मजाजी; the म् ends पाठाम्.
Right: Final म् before a vowel is joined to it: पाठाम् + अजाजीम् → पाठामजाजीम्.
There is no form पाठाम; the accusative is पाठाम्.
पाठः + अ would give पाठोऽजाजीम्.
questions.explain: पाठाम् and अजाजीम् are both accusative singular feminine.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् की गुटिका और ऋतु-अनुसार योग

questions.q: Which of these drugs does the second line of verse 29 name?
optionExplain: No: hiṅgu comes in line 05.02.55.
Right: the second item.
Right: the fifth item.
No: musta is in the list of line 05.02.44.
Right: the last item.
questions.explain: Six drugs: trivṛt, citraka, pāṭhā, ajājī, sarala, vacā.
questions.rule: त्रिवृता · चित्रकं · पाठाम् · अजाजीं · सरलं · वचां.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् की गुटिका और ऋतु-अनुसार योग

questions.q: Like पाठाम् and वचाम् (objects in the list), which is the accusative singular of एला, cardamom (invented use)?
optionExplain: -अया is the instrumental singular: with cardamom.
-आयाः is the genitive or ablative singular.
Right: Feminine -आ nouns take -आम् in the accusative singular: पाठाम्, वचाम्, एलाम्.
एले is the nominative dual or vocative, not the accusative singular.
questions.explain: पाठाम्, वचाम्: f. acc. sg. in -आम्.
questions.teaches: Feminine nouns in -आ take -आम् as object (accusative singular): पाठाम्, वचाम्, एलाम्.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् की गुटिका और ऋतु-अनुसार योग

questions.q: In which season does verse 30 make trivṛt equal to sugar the purgation?
optionExplain: The rainy season's formula is in line 05.02.43.
Spring is not named in this verse.
Autumn is not named in this verse.
Right: त्रिवृता शर्करातुल्या ग्रीष्मकाले विरेचनं.
questions.explain: ग्रीष्मकाले = in the hot season.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् की गुटिका और ऋतु-अनुसार योग

questions.q: Match each word of verse 30 to its meaning.
questions.explain: One drug, the powder and its vehicle, and the hot-season formula.
questions.rule: स्वर्णक्षीरी = svarṇakṣīrī; चूर्णम् = powder; उष्णाम्बुना = with hot water; शर्करातुल्या = equal to sugar; विरेचनम् = purgation.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् की गुटिका और ऋतु-अनुसार योग

questions.q: Put the words of the second line in the order of verse 30.
questions.explain: Trivṛt, equal to sugar, in the hot season, a purgation.
questions.teaches: The hot-season line names the drug, its sugar measure, the season, and ends with विरेचनम्, like the rainy-season line.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् की गुटिका और ऋतु-अनुसार योग

questions.q: Which split of चूर्णमुष्णांबुना is right?
optionExplain: Right: म् joins the vowel उ; अ + अ → आ in उष्णाम्बुना.
There is no word मुष्ण; the म् ends चूर्णम्.
बुना is not a word; water is अम्बु.
चूर्णः + उ would give चूर्ण उष्ण, not चूर्णमुष्ण.
questions.explain: चूर्णम् = powder (object); उष्णाम्बुना = with hot water.
questions.rule: म् + vowel joined; अ + अ → आ.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् की गुटिका और ऋतु-अनुसार योग

questions.q: A purgation is wanted in the hot season. By verse 30, which preparation is it?
options: Trivṛt joined with honey and drākṣā juice
Trivṛt with sugar in equal measure
Trivṛt powder soaked in cow's urine
Trivṛt cooked into a guḍa with oil
optionExplain: That is the rainy-season formula of line 05.02.43.
Right: त्रिवृता शर्करातुल्या ग्रीष्मकाले.
Soaking in cow's urine is line 05.02.50.
That is the Kalyāṇaka guḍa, for all seasons.
questions.explain: Hot season: trivṛt equal to sugar.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् की गुटिका और ऋतु-अनुसार योग

questions.q: शर्करातुल्या agrees with feminine त्रिवृता. Which form says jaggery equal to sugar, with masculine गुडः (invented)?
optionExplain: तुल्या is feminine, for त्रिवृता, not for गुडः.
तुल्यम् is neuter.
Right: तुल्य is an adjective: masculine nominative singular with गुडः.
तुल्याः is plural; गुडः is singular.
questions.explain: त्रिवृता शर्करातुल्या: f. with f.
questions.rule: X-तुल्य = equal to X; it agrees with its noun.
questions.teaches: A compound in -तुल्य (equal to ...) is an adjective that agrees with its noun: त्रिवृता शर्करातुल्या, गुडः शर्करातुल्यः.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् की गुटिका और ऋतु-अनुसार योग

questions.q: In what does verse 31 say the powder is saturated?
optionExplain: Āmalaka juice is the liquid of line 05.02.60.
Hot water is the vehicle of line 05.02.47.
Oil is not named in this verse.
Right: गोमूत्रे भावयेत् = one should saturate in cow's urine.
questions.explain: गो = cow; मूत्र = urine; -ए = in.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् की गुटिका और ऋतु-अनुसार योग

questions.q: Match each word of the second line to its meaning.
questions.explain: The second line carries the whole procedure.
questions.rule: संचूर्ण्य = having powdered; गोमूत्रे = in cow's urine; भावयेत् = one should saturate; त्र्यहम् = for three days; च = and.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् की गुटिका और ऋतु-अनुसार योग

questions.q: Put these words of the second line in the order of verse 31.
questions.explain: The last drug, then powdering, in cow's urine, saturate, for three days.
questions.rule: स्वर्णक्षीरीं च · संचूर्ण्य · गोमूत्रे · भावयेत् · त्र्यहं.
questions.teaches: The line goes from the last drug to powdering, then to saturating in cow's urine, and ends with the time, three days.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् की गुटिका और ऋतु-अनुसार योग

questions.q: Which split of भावयेत्र्यहं is right?
optionExplain: Right: The verb भावयेत् (one should saturate) is followed by त्र्यहम् (for three days); the print shows one त्.
There is no word र्यहम्; three days is त्र्यहम्.
There is no form भावयेत्रि; the verb ends in -एत्.
A visarga before त would give भावयेस्त्र्यहम्.
questions.explain: त्र्यहम् itself = त्रि + अहम् (इ + अ → य).
questions.rule: Optative -एत् + following word; इ + अ → य.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् की गुटिका और ऋतु-अनुसार योग

questions.q: A student soaks the powder of verse 31 in cow's urine for seven days. What does the verse say instead?
options: Seven days is right as it is
Hot water is used, not urine
It is drunk at once, unsoaked
optionExplain: Seven days belongs to the āmalaka recipe of line 05.02.60.
Right: त्र्यहम् = for three days.
The verse names गोमूत्रे, cow's urine.
The verse says भावयेत्, saturate, for three days.
questions.explain: Verse 31: cow's urine, three days.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् की गुटिका और ऋतु-अनुसार योग

questions.q: Join प्रति + अहम् (each day) as त्रि + अहम् gives त्र्यहम्: ____. Type it in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. tryaham).
questions.explain: इ before the unlike vowel अ becomes य्: प्रति + अहम् → प्रत्यहम्, like त्रि + अहम् → त्र्यहम्.
questions.teaches: इ / ई + unlike vowel → य्: त्रि + अहम् → त्र्यहम्; प्रति + अहम् → प्रत्यहम्.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् की गुटिका और ऋतु-अनुसार योग

questions.q: For whom does verse 32 say this all-season formula takes away mala and doṣa?
optionExplain: The dry ones (रूक्ष) are named in line 05.02.54, for the next formula.
Neither is named in this verse.
Right: स्निग्धानां मलदोषहृत् = takes away mala and doṣa of the unctuous ones.
No such persons are named here.
questions.explain: स्निग्ध = made unctuous (oiled); -आनाम् = of (them).
questions.section: त्रिवृत् की गुटिका और ऋतु-अनुसार योग

questions.q: Match each word of the first line of verse 32 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five words make the whole first line.
questions.rule: एषः = this; सर्वर्तुकः = for all seasons; योगः = formula; स्निग्धानाम् = of the unctuous; मलदोषहृत् = taking away mala and doṣa.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् की गुटिका और ऋतु-अनुसार योग

questions.q: Put the drugs of the second line in the order of verse 32.
questions.explain: Śyāmā, trivṛt, durālabhā, hastipippalī, vatsaka.
questions.teaches: The second line is one compound of five drugs, from śyāmā to vatsaka (kuṭaja).
questions.section: त्रिवृत् की गुटिका और ऋतु-अनुसार योग

questions.q: Which split of सर्वर्तुको is right?
optionExplain: There is no word तुकः; the र् comes from अ + ऋ.
A visarga would drop before ऋ and leave सर्व ऋतुकः, two words.
सर्वे + ऋ would give सर्व ऋतुकः, not सर्वर्तुको.
Right: अ + ऋ → अर्: सर्व + ऋतुकः → सर्वर्तुकः; then -अः → -ओ before य.
questions.explain: सर्वर्तुक = belonging to all seasons (ऋतु + -क).
questions.section: त्रिवृत् की गुटिका और ऋतु-अनुसार योग

questions.q: Verse 32 calls the formula सर्वर्तुकः. When may it be given, by the card?
options: In any season of the year
Only after the clouds have gone
optionExplain: Right: सर्व + ऋतु + -क: of all seasons.
The rainy-season formula is a different one (line 05.02.43).
The hot-season formula is trivṛt with sugar (line 05.02.48).
That conjectural season belongs to line 05.02.45.
questions.explain: Unlike the seasonal purgations of verses 28 and 30, this one is for all seasons.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् की गुटिका और ऋतु-अनुसार योग

questions.q: Like मलदोषहृत् (taking away mala and doṣa), which invented compound means taking away fever?
optionExplain: -कृत् means making: causing fever.
Right: -हृत् (from √हृ, take away) at the end of a compound means taking away X.
-भृत् means bearing: carrying fever.
-वत् means having: feverish.
questions.explain: मलदोषहृत् = mala-doṣa + -हृत्.
questions.teaches: A compound ending in -हृत् names what takes a thing away: मलदोषहृत्, ज्वरहृत्.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् की गुटिका और ऋतु-अनुसार योग

questions.q: For whom, besides others, does verse 33 say the powder is approved?
optionExplain: अपि (even) says the dry ones are included too; nothing says only.
Children are not named in this verse.
Right: रूक्षाणाम् अपि = even of (for) the dry ones.
No ailment is named in this verse.
questions.explain: रूक्ष = dry, rough; अपि = even.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् की गुटिका और ऋतु-अनुसार योग

questions.q: Match each word of verse 33 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The three liquids, the making and the time word.
questions.rule: रस = juice; आज्य = ghee; उष्णाम्बु = hot water; सुचूर्णितम् = well powdered; सर्वदा = always.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् की गुटिका और ऋतु-अनुसार योग

questions.q: Put these words of the second line in the order of verse 33.
questions.explain: With the liquids, approved, of the dry ones, even, always.
questions.teaches: The second line names the vehicles first, then the verdict शस्तम्, and ends with whom (even the dry) and when (always).
questions.section: त्रिवृत् की गुटिका और ऋतु-अनुसार योग

questions.q: Which split of रसाज्योष्ण in रसाज्योष्णांबुभिः is right?
optionExplain: There is no word ज्य; ghee is आज्य.
There is no word ओष्ण; hot is उष्ण.
रसाः before आ would lose its visarga and stay apart: रसा आज्य.
Right: अ + आ → आ (रसाज्य); अ + उ → ओ (आज्योष्ण).
questions.explain: रस (juice), आज्य (ghee), उष्ण-अम्बु (hot water).
questions.rule: अ + आ → आ; अ + उ → ओ.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् की गुटिका और ऋतु-अनुसार योग

questions.q: Verse 32's cow's-urine formula was for the unctuous ones. What does verse 33 say of the new śyāmā powder?
options: It is approved always, even for the dry
It is forbidden for the dry (rūkṣa) ones
It may be given in the rains alone
It is to be taken with no liquid
optionExplain: Right: शस्तं रूक्षाणामपि सर्वदा.
The verse says the opposite: even for the dry ones.
सर्वदा = always; no single season.
Rasa, ghee and hot water are named.
questions.explain: रूक्षाणामपि: the dry are included; सर्वदा: at all times.
questions.rule: स्निग्ध: the cow's-urine formula (verse 32) · रूक्ष अपि: the śyāmā powder (verses 32-33).
questions.section: त्रिवृत् की गुटिका और ऋतु-अनुसार योग

questions.q: Like रूक्षाणाम् and स्निग्धानाम् (of the dry, of the unctuous), which is the genitive plural of बाल, child (invented)?
optionExplain: न becomes ण only after र्, ष् or ऋ, as in रूक्षाणाम्; बाल has none.
Right: -अ stems take -आनाम् in the genitive plural; न stays न because no र् or ष् comes before it.
-एभ्यः is the dative or ablative plural.
-अस्य is the genitive singular.
questions.explain: रूक्षाणाम्: ण because of the ष् in रूक्ष; स्निग्धानाम्: न.
questions.teaches: The genitive plural of -अ stems ends in -आनाम्, written -आणाम् after र् or ष् in the word: रूक्षाणाम्, स्निग्धानाम्, बालानाम्.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् की गुटिका और ऋतु-अनुसार योग

questions.q: What measure does verse 34 give for trivṛt?
optionExplain: Prastha is the measure of the juice in line 05.02.32.
Droṇa is the water measure of line 05.02.64.
Right: त्रिवृता पलं = trivṛt, a pala.
Half a tulā of jaggery is the Kalyāṇaka measure (line 05.02.32); trivṛt here is a pala.
questions.explain: पल = a weight measure; given as the text gives it.

questions.q: Match each name of the first line to its meaning on the card.
pairs: dry ginger, long pepper, black pepper
questions.explain: Three drug names and two measure words.
questions.rule: त्र्यूषण = the three pungents; त्रिफला = the three myrobalans; हिङ्गु = asafoetida; कार्षिक = of a karṣa; पल = a pala.

questions.q: Put the words of the first line in the order of verse 34.
questions.explain: Tryūṣaṇa, triphalā, hiṅgu, of a karṣa; trivṛt, a pala.
questions.rule: त्र्यूषणं · त्रिफला · हिंगु · कार्षिकं · त्रिवृता · पलं.
questions.teaches: The clear line gives three drugs and a karṣa measure, then trivṛt with its own measure, a pala.

questions.q: Which split of त्र्यूषणं is right?
optionExplain: अ + ऊ would give त्रोषणम्.
There is no word त्र्य; अ + ऊ would also give ओ.
There is no word षणम्; the य् comes from इ.
Right: इ before the unlike vowel ऊ becomes य्: त्रि + ऊषणम् → त्र्यूषणम्.
questions.explain: त्र्यूषण = the three pungents (= vyoṣa).

questions.q: A recipe calls for the three pungents. Which name in verse 34 stands for them?
optionExplain: Right: tryūṣaṇa = dry ginger, long pepper, black pepper (= vyoṣa).
Triphalā is the three fruits, the myrobalans.
Trivṛt is one plant, turpeth; 'threefold' is only its literal sense.
Hiṅgu is asafoetida, a single drug.
questions.explain: त्रि- names: त्र्यूषण (pungents), त्रिफला (fruits); त्रिवृत् is a single plant.

questions.q: कार्षिक (of a karṣa) is कर्ष + -इक with the first vowel made long. Which word follows this pattern from धर्म (invented use)?
optionExplain: The first vowel must be lengthened, as in कार्षिक.
Right: कर्ष → कार्षिक; धर्म → धार्मिक: अ → आ in the first syllable, + -इक.
The ending is -इक, not -अक.
-वत् is a different suffix: having dharma.
questions.explain: कार्षिकम् = of a karṣa (कर्ष + इक).
questions.teaches: The suffix -इक with the first vowel strengthened makes 'of / measured by X': कर्ष → कार्षिक, धर्म → धार्मिक.

questions.q: With what does verse 35 say the powder is drunk?
options: With cow's urine, after three days
With maṇḍa or a sour liquid
optionExplain: Cow's urine was for soaking, in line 05.02.50.
Milk is not named in this verse.
Right: मण्डेनाम्लेन वा पिबेत् = drink with maṇḍa or with a sour (liquid).
That is the rainy-season vehicle of line 05.02.43.
questions.explain: मण्ड = clear liquid of gruel; अम्ल = sour (liquid); वा = or.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 35 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The vehicles, one complaint, and the after-meal.
questions.rule: मण्ड = clear gruel liquid; अम्ल = sour; पार्श्वार्ति = flank pain; जीर्णे = when digested; रसौदन = rice with rasa.

questions.q: Put these parts of verse 35 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: The powder, how to drink it, what it drives away, after digestion, the rice.
questions.rule: तच्चूर्णं · मण्डेनाम्लेन वा पिबेत् · गुल्मपार्श्वार्तिनुत् · जीर्णे चास्मिन् · रसौदनं.
questions.teaches: The verse runs as a small procedure: drink the powder, its effect, and the meal after it is digested.

questions.q: Which split of रसौदनं is right?
optionExplain: There is no word दनम्; rice is ओदन.
A visarga before ओ would drop and leave रस ओदनम्, two words.
आ + उ would give रसोदनम्, with ओ, not औ.
Right: अ + ओ → औ: रस + ओदनम् → रसौदनम्.
questions.explain: ओदन = boiled rice; रस = juice or broth.

questions.q: When does verse 35 say the boiled rice with rasa is taken?
options: Before the powder is drunk, as a base
Mixed into the same drink as the powder
Only on the third day of the course
optionExplain: Right: जीर्णे चास्मिन् = and when this has been digested.
The verse puts the rice after digestion.
The powder is drunk with maṇḍa or sour liquid, not rice.
No days are counted in this verse.
questions.explain: जीर्णे = when digested (locative of जीर्ण).

questions.q: जीर्णे चास्मिन् = when this has been digested. Which invented phrase says when the medicine (औषध) has been digested?
optionExplain: Nominative: the digested medicine, not 'when'.
Right: Locative absolute: participle and noun both in the locative, as in जीर्णे अस्मिन्.
Instrumental: by or with the digested medicine.
Genitive: of the digested medicine.
questions.explain: जीर्णे अस्मिन्: both locative, giving the time 'when'.
questions.rule: Locative absolute = participle + noun in the locative: when ...
questions.teaches: A participle and its noun in the locative give the time of an action: जीर्णे अस्मिन्, जीर्णे औषधे = when it (the medicine) is digested.

questions.q: For how long does verse 36 say the powder is saturated?
optionExplain: Three days is the cow's-urine recipe of line 05.02.50.
No single night is named.
Right: सप्ताहं भाव्यम् = to be saturated for seven days.
No fortnight is named.
questions.explain: सप्त = seven; अह = day.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 36 to its meaning.
pairs: dry ginger, long pepper, black pepper
questions.explain: Three drug names and the two verb forms of the procedure.
questions.rule: त्रिफला = three myrobalans; व्योष = three pungents; सैन्धव = rock salt; प्रकल्प्य = having prepared; भाव्यम् = to be saturated.

questions.q: Put the drugs in the order of verse 36.
questions.explain: Trivṛt, triphalā, dantī, sātalā, vyoṣa, saindhava.
questions.rule: त्रिवृता · त्रिफला · दन्ती · सातला · व्योष · सैन्धव.
questions.teaches: The first line is one instrumental compound of six drugs, closed by saindhava (rock salt).

questions.q: What kind of form is भाव्यम् in verse 36?
optionExplain: That would be like प्रकल्प्य; भाव्यम् is a neuter adjective.
The optative is भावयेत्, as in line 05.02.50.
The past participle is भावितम्.
Right: -य added to the causative stem makes a gerundive: what is to be done.
questions.explain: प्रकल्प्य (having prepared) and भाव्यम् (to be saturated) both end in -य but differ.

questions.q: Which of these drugs go into the powder of verse 36?
optionExplain: Right: the third item.
Right: the last item, rock salt.
Right: the second item.
No: hiṅgu belongs to the powder of line 05.02.55.
No: citraka is in the list of line 05.02.46.
questions.explain: Six drugs: trivṛt, triphalā, dantī, sātalā, vyoṣa, saindhava.
questions.rule: त्रिवृता · त्रिफला · दन्ती · सातला · व्योष · सैन्धव.

questions.q: Like प्रकल्प्य (प्र + √कॢप् + -य), which invented absolutive means having cooked, with the prefix सम्- and √पच्?
optionExplain: Right: With a prefix, the absolutive takes -य: प्रकल्प्य, संपच्य.
-त्वा is used without a prefix (पक्त्वा); with सम्- it is -य.
This is an adjective: ripe, cooked.
This is an optative: one should cook.
questions.explain: प्रकल्प्य = having prepared (prefix + -य).
questions.rule: Prefix + root → absolutive in -य; bare root → -त्वा.
questions.teaches: An absolutive with a prefix ends in -य, a bare root takes -त्वा: प्रकल्प्य, संपच्य; पक्त्वा.

questions.q: What does the trivṛt ghee of verse 37 take away?
optionExplain: Neither is named in this verse.
Right: गुल्महरं घृतं = ghee that takes away gulma.
These were in line 05.02.40, for the pills.
Poisons were in line 05.02.41.
questions.explain: गुल्म = abdominal lump; हर = taking away.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 37 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Three of the uses in the first line, and two words of the ghee recipe.
questions.rule: तर्पण = satiating drink; यूष = broth; पिशित = meat; कल्क = paste; घृत = ghee.

questions.q: Put the four locative words of the first line in the order of verse 37.
questions.explain: In tarpaṇa, in broth, in meat, in rāga-preparations.
questions.teaches: The first line lists four foods or drinks in the locative (in ...), ending with the plural रागयुक्तिषु.

questions.q: With what is the ghee of verse 37 cooked (सिद्धम्)?
options: A decoction of śyāmā and trivṛt
Trivṛt powder soaked for three days in urine
Trivṛt paste, with sour liquid in equal measure
Āmalaka juice kept for seven days, with salt
optionExplain: That ghee (or milk) is cooked so in line 05.02.63, the next verse.
That is the powder of line 05.02.50.
Right: तुल्याम्लं त्रिवृताकल्कसिद्धं घृतं.
That is the soaking of line 05.02.60.
questions.explain: कल्क = paste; सिद्ध = cooked; तुल्याम्ल = equal (measure of) sour liquid.

questions.q: Which word of verse 37 shows that the ghee is cooked with the trivṛt paste?
optionExplain: This says equal sour liquid, not the cooking.
This says what the ghee takes away.
This only names the ghee.
Right: सिद्ध = cooked: त्रिवृताकल्कसिद्धम् = cooked with trivṛt paste.
questions.explain: In this book's glossary siddha = cooked.

questions.q: Like गुल्महरं घृतं (neuter), which invented phrase says cough-removing oil, with neuter तैलम्?
optionExplain: Right: X-हर agrees with its noun: neuter nominative -म् / -ं, as गुल्महरं घृतं.
कासहरः is masculine; तैलम् is neuter.
कासहरा is feminine.
कासहरेण is instrumental; तैलम् is nominative.
questions.explain: गुल्महरम् agrees with घृतम्: n. nom. sg.
questions.rule: X-हर (taking away X) = adjective agreeing with its noun.
questions.teaches: A compound in -हर (taking away X) agrees with its noun: गुल्महरं घृतम्, कासहरं तैलम्.

questions.q: Besides ghee, what does verse 38 say may also be cooked with the śyāmā-trivṛt decoction?
optionExplain: Oil is not named in this verse.
Right: पयोऽपि वा = or milk also.
Honey is not named here; it comes in line 05.02.66.
Curd is not named in this verse.
questions.explain: सिद्धं सर्पिः पयोऽपि वा: ghee, or milk also, cooked with the decoction.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् का अरिष्ट, सुरा और सौवीरक

questions.q: Match each word of verse 38 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The first line names two cooked liquids; the second line ends with the verb पचेत्.
questions.rule: सर्पिः = ghee; पयः = milk; कषाय = decoction; सिद्ध = cooked; पचेत् = should boil.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् का अरिष्ट, सुरा और सौवीरक

questions.q: Put the words of the first line of verse 38 in their order.
questions.explain: With the decoction of śyāmā and trivṛt, cooked, ghee, milk also, or.
questions.teaches: The first line puts the means (instrumental) first, then सिद्धं and the two liquids joined by वा.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् का अरिष्ट, सुरा और सौवीरक

questions.q: Which split of द्रोणेऽम्भसः is right?
optionExplain: There is no word म्भसः; the अ of अम्भसः is hidden behind ऽ.
द्रोण + अम्भसः would give द्रोणाम्भसः, with आ.
Right: After a final ए an initial अ merges and is marked ऽ: द्रोणे + अम्भसः → द्रोणेऽम्भसः.
द्रोणो is not a form here, and ओ would stay ओ.
questions.explain: द्रोणे = in a droṇa (loc. sg.); अम्भसः = of water (gen. sg.).
questions.section: त्रिवृत् का अरिष्ट, सुरा और सौवीरक

questions.q: By verse 38, in what measure of water are the eight handfuls boiled?
optionExplain: prastha is not named in this verse.
āḍhaka is not named in this verse.
tulā is a weight; it measures the jaggery in line 05.02.65.
Right: द्रोणेऽम्भसः पचेत् = one should boil in a droṇa of water.
questions.explain: Eight handfuls, one droṇa of water; the measure stays a droṇa, unconverted.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् का अरिष्ट, सुरा और सौवीरक

questions.q: Like पयः + अपि → पयोऽपि, which is the joined form of मनः + अपि (invented)?
optionExplain: Right: अः before अ becomes ओ and the अ merges, marked ऽ: पयः + अपि → पयोऽपि.
The visarga does not drop with a lengthened vowel here.
The अ of अपि is not lost while the visarga stays.
र् would come only after a vowel other than अ/आ.
questions.explain: पयोऽपि shows अः + अ → ओऽ.
questions.teaches: A visarga after अ before an initial अ gives ओ, and the अ is marked ऽ: पयोऽपि, मनोऽपि.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् का अरिष्ट, सुरा और सौवीरक

questions.q: By verse 39, how much of the decoction remains after boiling?
optionExplain: The verse says पाद, a quarter, not half.
Right: पादशेषं कषायम् = the decoction with a quarter remaining.
No eighth is named; पाद is a quarter.
No third is named; पाद is a quarter.
questions.explain: पाद = a quarter; शेष = remaining.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् का अरिष्ट, सुरा और सौवीरक

questions.q: Match each word of verse 39 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The first line treats the decoction; the second line names the pot and what goes in with it.
questions.rule: पादशेष = a quarter left; पूत = strained; गुडतुला = a tulā of guḍa; स्निग्ध घट = greased pot; क्षौद्र = honey.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् का अरिष्ट, सुरा और सौवीरक

questions.q: Put the steps of verse 39 in the text's order.
items: स्निग्धे घटे स्थाप्यं (put in a greased pot)
questions.explain: Reduce to a quarter, strain, add a tulā of jaggery, place in a greased pot.
questions.rule: पादशेष · पूत · गुडतुलायुत · स्निग्धे घटे स्थाप्य.
questions.teaches: Verse 39 is a procedure in four steps, from the reduced decoction to the greased pot.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् का अरिष्ट, सुरा और सौवीरक

questions.q: What kind of form is स्थाप्यम् in verse 39?
optionExplain: An absolutive with -य needs a prefix and is indeclinable; here स्थाप्यम् is a gerundive.
The past participle would be स्थापितम्.
Right: The data gives gdv. √स्था: स्थाप्यम् = is to be placed.
The optative would be स्थापयेत्.
questions.explain: स्थाप्यं घटे = (it) is to be placed in a pot.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् का अरिष्ट, सुरा और सौवीरक

questions.q: Which of these does verse 39 say go into the pot with the decoction?
optionExplain: Right: the first member of the last compound.
No: ghee was the preparation of line 05.02.63, not a pot ingredient here.
No: cow's urine is not named in this verse.
Right: leadwort, the last member.
Right: read as the fruit of pippalī (long pepper).
questions.explain: क्षौद्रपिप्पलीफलचित्रकैः = with honey, pippalī fruit and citraka.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् का अरिष्ट, सुरा और सौवीरक

questions.q: Like स्थाप्यम् (is to be placed, from √स्था), which is the gerundive of √दा (give)?
optionExplain: दत्त्वा is the absolutive: 'having given'.
दत्तम् is the past participle: 'given'.
दद्यात् is the optative: 'one should give'.
Right: देयम् is the gerundive of √दा: 'is to be given', like स्थाप्यम्.
questions.explain: स्थाप्यम्, देयम्: both gerundives, 'is to be ...'.
questions.rule: Gerundive = what is to be done.
questions.teaches: A gerundive says what is to be done: स्थाप्यम् 'is to be placed', देयम् 'is to be given'.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् का अरिष्ट, सुरा और सौवीरक

questions.q: By verse 40, after how long is the preparation in the pot drunk?
optionExplain: Right: मासे गते = when a month has gone.
पक्ष is not named in this verse; it says मास.
No count of nights is given; it says मास.
वर्ष is not named; the verse says मास.
questions.explain: मासे गते: a locative absolute, 'when a month has gone'.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् का अरिष्ट, सुरा और सौवीरक

questions.q: Match each word of verse 40 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The first line gives the time and the result; सुरा opens the alternative.
questions.rule: लिप्ते = when smeared; मासे गते = a month gone; पीतम् = drunk; जित् = conquering; सुरा = spirituous drink.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् का अरिष्ट, सुरा और सौवीरक

questions.q: Put the conditions the drink conquers in the order of verse 40.
questions.explain: Pāṇḍu, then swelling, then gulma; -जित् closes the compound.
questions.teaches: One compound names three conditions and ends in -जित्, 'conquering'.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् का अरिष्ट, सुरा और सौवीरक

questions.q: In पाण्डुश्वयथुगुल्मजित्, what does the last member -जित् show?
options: That the three cause the drink to spoil
That the drink conquers these three
That the three are drugs added to it
That it is forbidden in these three
optionExplain: जित् means conquering, not causing or spoiling.
Right: -जित् = conquering: the drink overcomes pāṇḍu, swelling and gulma.
पाण्डु, श्वयथु, गुल्म are conditions, not drugs.
जित् is praise of the effect, not a prohibition.
questions.explain: A compound ending in -जित्, -हर, -नुत् names what a remedy overcomes.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् का अरिष्ट, सुरा और सौवीरक

questions.q: By verse 40, the surā alternative is joined with what?
options: With a tulā of jaggery added
optionExplain: These went into the pot in line 05.02.66, not with the surā.
The tulā of guḍa belongs to line 05.02.65.
Right: तत्क्वाथसंयुता = joined with its decoction.
Neither is named in this verse.
questions.explain: सुरा वा ... तत्क्वाथसंयुता: or surā joined with its decoction.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् का अरिष्ट, सुरा और सौवीरक

questions.q: Like मासे गते (when a month has passed), which phrase says when the food (अन्न) is digested?
optionExplain: This nominative says 'the food is digested', not 'when'.
The instrumental means 'with/by the digested food'.
The genitive means 'of the digested food'.
Right: Both noun and participle in the locative: a locative absolute, like मासे गते.
questions.explain: मासे गते: noun and participle agree in the locative to give the time.
questions.teaches: Noun + participle both in the locative give a time clause: मासे गते, अन्ने जीर्णे.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् का अरिष्ट, सुरा और सौवीरक

questions.q: By verse 41, for how many days is the preparation steeped?
optionExplain: Right: आसुतं षडहम् = steeped for six days.
Three days is the soaking of line 05.02.50, not this verse.
Seven days is the soaking of line 05.02.60, not this verse.
No ten days are named here.
questions.explain: षट् + अहन् = a period of six days.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् का अरिष्ट, सुरा और सौवीरक

questions.q: Match each word of verse 41 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Steamed barley, kulmāṣa, steeping and ripening lead to the drink.
questions.rule: यव = barley; स्विन्न = steamed; कुल्माष = grain preparation; आसुत = steeped; पक्के = when ripened.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् का अरिष्ट, सुरा और सौवीरक

questions.q: Put the stages of verse 41 in the text's order.
questions.explain: Steamed barley, kulmāṣa, six days of steeping, ripening, then the drink.
questions.rule: यव स्विन्न · कुल्माष · आसुत षडह · पक्के जात · सौवीरक पिबेत्.
questions.teaches: Verse 41 is a fermentation in five stages that ends in a drink to be taken.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् का अरिष्ट, सुरा और सौवीरक

questions.q: By verse 41, in what are the barley grains steamed?
options: In cow's urine for three days
In a decoction of śyāmā and trivṛt
In the juice of āmalaka fruit
In a sour liquid of equal measure
optionExplain: Cow's urine was the soaking of line 05.02.50.
Right: श्यामात्रिवृत्क्वाथस्विन्नैः = steamed in a decoction of śyāmā and trivṛt.
āmalaka juice was the soaking of line 05.02.60.
The equal sour liquid went with the ghee of line 05.02.62.
questions.explain: क्वाथ = decoction; स्विन्न = steamed.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् का अरिष्ट, सुरा और सौवीरक

questions.q: Which drink does verse 41 say one should drink?
optionExplain: Surā was the alternative of line 05.02.68.
An ariṣṭa comes in line 05.02.91, not here.
Right: जातं सौवीरकं पिबेत् = one should drink the sauvīraka that has arisen.
No madhvāsava is named in this verse.
questions.explain: sauvīraka = a sour fermented barley drink.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् का अरिष्ट, सुरा और सौवीरक

questions.q: Like पिबेत् (one should drink, from √पा), which is the matching optative of √खाद् (eat)?
optionExplain: खादति is the present: 'he eats'.
खादितुम् is the infinitive: 'to eat'.
खादित्वा is the absolutive: 'having eaten'.
Right: खादेत् is the optative third singular, 'one should eat', like पिबेत्.
questions.explain: पिबेत्, खादेत्: the optative gives the instruction 'one should ...'.
questions.teaches: Instructions in these recipes use the optative in -एत्: पिबेत्, पचेत्, खादेत्.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् का अरिष्ट, सुरा और सौवीरक

questions.q: Which two kinds of barley grain does verse 42 give as alternatives?
options: Fried, or fresh from the field
optionExplain: Right: भृष्टान् वा सतुषान् शुष्कान् = roasted, or dry with husk.
Neither boiling nor flour is named in this verse.
Neither sprouting nor milk is named here.
Neither frying nor fresh grain is named here.
questions.explain: भृष्ट = roasted; सतुष = with husk; शुष्क = dry.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् का अरिष्ट, सुरा और सौवीरक

questions.q: Match each word of verse 42 to its meaning.

questions.rule: भृष्ट = roasted; सतुष = with husk; शुष्क = dry; आसुत = steeped; तद्वत् = likewise.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् का अरिष्ट, सुरा और सौवीरक

questions.q: Put these words in the order of verse 42.
questions.explain: Roasted, with husk, dry; steeped; likewise one should drink.
questions.rule: भृष्टान् · सतुषान् · शुष्कान् · आसुतान् · तद्वत् · पिबेत्.
questions.teaches: The accusatives भृष्टान्, सतुषान्, शुष्कान्, आसुतान् all describe the barley grains (यवान्).
questions.section: त्रिवृत् का अरिष्ट, सुरा और सौवीरक

questions.q: Which split of पिबेज्जातम् is right?
optionExplain: There is no word ज्जातम्; the first ज् comes from the त् of पिबेत्.
Right: त् before ज becomes ज्: पिबेत् + जातम् → पिबेज्जातम्.
पिबेज्जा is not a word; the verb is पिबेत्.
Neither पिब nor इज्जातम् fits; the optative is पिबेत्.
questions.explain: पिबेत् = one should drink; जातम् = what has arisen.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् का अरिष्ट, सुरा और सौवीरक

questions.q: By verse 42, with what are the barley grains steeped?
optionExplain: No sour gruel is named in this verse.
Milk is not named in this verse.
Right: आसुतान् अम्भसा = steeped with water.
Cow's urine is not named in this verse.
questions.explain: आसुत = steeped; अम्भसा = with water (inst. sg.).
questions.section: त्रिवृत् का अरिष्ट, सुरा और सौवीरक

questions.q: Like पिबेत् + जातम् → पिबेज्जातम्, which is the joined form of तत् + जलम् (invented)?
optionExplain: Before ज the त् becomes ज्, not द्.
त् does not stay unchanged before ज.
च् comes before च/छ, not before ज.
Right: त् before ज becomes ज्: तत् + जलम् → तज्जलम्.
questions.explain: पिबेज्जातम्, तज्जलम्: त् + ज → ज्ज.
questions.teaches: A final त् before ज becomes ज्: पिबेज्जातम्, तज्जलम्.
questions.section: त्रिवृत् का अरिष्ट, सुरा और सौवीरक

questions.q: Which plant does verse 43 call especially suitable?
optionExplain: Right: राजवृक्षोऽधिकं पथ्यः = rājavṛkṣa is especially suitable.
Trivṛt was the subject of the earlier verses, not of this one.
Dantī is not named in this verse.
Snuhī is not named in this verse.
questions.explain: rājavṛkṣa, lit. 'king-tree' = āragvadha, Cassia fistula (standard).

questions.q: Match each word of verse 43 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Three conditions of the first line and two words of praise in the second.
questions.rule: ज्वर = fever; हृद्रोग = heart disease; उदावर्त = upward-turned Vāta; पथ्य = suitable; शीतल = cool.

questions.q: Put the words praising rājavṛkṣa in the order of verse 43.
questions.explain: Especially, suitable, mild, sweet, cool.
questions.teaches: The second line praises rājavṛkṣa: especially suitable, then three qualities, mild, sweet and cool.

questions.q: Which split of राजवृक्षोऽधिकम् is right?
optionExplain: There is no word धिकम्; the अ of अधिकम् is behind ऽ.
Right: अः before अ becomes ओ and the अ merges as ऽ.
अ + अ would give राजवृक्षाधिकम्, with आ.
There is no word धिकम्; अधिकम् = especially.
questions.explain: राजवृक्षः (nom. sg.) + अधिकम् (especially).

questions.q: Which ailments does verse 43 name for the patients?
optionExplain: Right: the next member of the compound.
No: gulma is in line 05.02.67, not in this verse.
No: pāṇḍu was conquered by the pot preparation of line 05.02.67.
Right: the first word of the line.
Right: named before 'and the like'.
questions.explain: ज्वर · हृद्रोग · वातासृक् · उदावर्त · आदि.
questions.rule: रोगिषु = in those who have these ailments.

questions.q: Like मृदुः + मधुर → मृदुर्मधुर, which is the joined form of गुरुः + भवति (invented)?
optionExplain: The visarga does not simply drop after उ.
स् comes before त/थ, not before भ.
Right: After उ a visarga before a voiced sound becomes र्.
ओ arises only from अः; here the vowel is उ.
questions.explain: मृदुर्मधुरशीतलः: उः + म → उर्म.
questions.teaches: A visarga after इ or उ becomes र् before a voiced sound: मृदुर्मधुर, गुरुर्भवति.

questions.q: Which of these persons does verse 44 name?
optionExplain: A pregnant woman is not named in this verse.
The list is of weak or delicate persons, not the strong.
A fasting person is not named here.
Right: वृद्धे = in an old person.
questions.explain: बाले · वृद्धे · क्षते · क्षीणे · सुकुमारे मानवे.

questions.q: Match each person of verse 44 to its meaning.
questions.explain: All five are in the locative: 'in a child', 'in an old person' ...
questions.rule: बाल = child; वृद्ध = old; क्षत = wounded; क्षीण = wasted; सुकुमार = delicate.

questions.q: Put the persons in the order of verse 44.
questions.explain: Child, old, wounded, wasted, delicate; मानवे closes the line.
questions.rule: बाले · वृद्धे · क्षते · क्षीणे · सुकुमारे · च मानवे.
questions.teaches: The first line is a row of five locatives, closed by सुकुमारे च मानवे.

questions.q: What does the name चतुरङ्गुल literally mean?
optionExplain: Right: चतुर् = four; अङ्गुल = finger(-breadth): 'four-finger'.
'King-tree' is rājavṛkṣa, the name in verse 43.
अङ्गुल is a finger, not a root.
अङ्गुल is a finger, not a seed.
questions.explain: caturaṅgula and rājavṛkṣa: two names of āragvadha (Cassia fistula).

questions.q: On which word do the locatives बाले ... मानवे depend?
optionExplain: पिबेत् is not in this verse.
Right: The data: the locatives are governed by योज्यः, 'is to be used (in them)'.
दद्यात् comes in line 05.02.81, not here.
पचेत् belongs to line 05.02.64.
questions.explain: बाले ... मानवे योज्यः चतुरङ्गुलः: caturaṅgula is to be used in these persons.
questions.rule: Locative of the person + योज्य = to be used in him.

questions.q: Like बाले (in a child, from बाल), which is the locative singular of अश्व (horse)?
optionExplain: अश्वेन is instrumental: 'by a horse'.
अश्वस्य is genitive: 'of a horse'.
Right: An अ-stem takes -ए in the locative singular: बाले, अश्वे.
अश्वाय is dative: 'for a horse'.
questions.explain: बाले, वृद्धे, मानवे: all locative singular in -ए.
questions.teaches: Masculine अ-stems take -ए in the locative singular: बाले, वृद्धे, अश्वे.

questions.q: By verse 45, when is the fruit gathered?
options: At night, once it has fallen
In winter, once it has dried
optionExplain: The verse says परिणत, ripened, and names no rainy season.
Neither night nor fallen fruit is named.
No winter or dry fruit is named here.
Right: फलकाले परिणतं फलं समाहरेत् = at fruiting time gather the ripened fruit.
questions.explain: फलकाल = fruiting time; परिणत = ripened.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 45 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The first line gathers the fruit; the second chooses the good ones and puts them in sand.
questions.rule: फलकाल = fruit-time; परिणत = ripened; समाहरेत् = should gather; गुणवत् = good; सिकता = sand.

questions.q: Put the steps of verse 45 in the text's order.
items: गुणवतां भारं (a load of the good ones)
questions.explain: Wait for the fruiting time, gather the ripe fruit, pick the good ones, put them in sand.
questions.rule: फलकाले · समाहरेत् · गुणवतां भारं · सिकतासु विनिक्षिपेत्.
questions.teaches: Verse 45 opens a collection procedure: time, gathering, choice, storing in sand.

questions.q: Into what does verse 45 say the load of fruit is put?
optionExplain: Right: सिकतासु विनिक्षिपेत् = one should put into sands.
The greased pot held the trivṛt decoction, line 05.02.66.
The clean vessel takes the kernel later, line 05.02.80.
Water is not named in this verse.
questions.explain: सिकता = sand; the loc. pl. सिकतासु = in sands.

questions.q: By verse 45, which fruits are put into the sand?
optionExplain: Only the good ones of the ripe fruit are chosen.
Right: तेषां गुणवतां भारम् = a load of those that have good qualities.
The fruit gathered is परिणत, ripened.
Fallen fruit is not named in this verse.
questions.explain: गुणवत् = having good qualities; the choice comes before the sand.

questions.q: Like सिकतासु (in sands, from सिकता), which is the locative plural of लता (creeper)?
optionExplain: लतायाम् is locative singular: 'in a creeper'.
लताभिः is instrumental plural: 'with creepers'.
Right: Feminine आ-stems take -आसु in the locative plural: सिकतासु, लतासु.
लतानाम् is genitive plural: 'of creepers'.
questions.explain: सिकतासु: f. आ-stem, locative plural.
questions.teaches: Feminine आ-stems take -आसु in the locative plural: सिकतासु, लतासु.

questions.q: Where does verse 46 say the fruits are dried?
optionExplain: Shade is not named; the verse says आतपे.
No fire is named in this verse.
Wind is not named in this verse.
Right: शोषयेद् आतपे = one should dry in the sun.
questions.explain: आतप = sunshine, heat.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 46 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Dry, take out the kernel, store it clean.
questions.rule: शोषयेत् = should dry; आतपे = in the sun; मज्जानम् = kernel; उद्धृत्य = having taken out; शुचौ पात्रे = clean vessel.

questions.q: Put the steps of verse 46 in the text's order.
items: शुचौ पात्रे निधापयेत् (place in a clean vessel)
questions.explain: Take out, dry in the sun, take out the kernel, place it in a clean vessel.
questions.teaches: Verse 46 has four steps, joined by ततः ... ततः ('then ... then').

questions.q: उद्धृत्य ends in -य. What kind of form is it here?
options: A gerundive: 'is to be taken out'
optionExplain: Right: A root with a prefix (उद्-) takes -य for the absolutive.
The data gives abs.; it is not 'to be done'.
The optative would be उद्धरेत्.
The past participle would be उद्धृतम्.
questions.explain: उद्धृत्य = having taken out; the main verb is निधापयेत्.
questions.rule: Prefix + root → absolutive in -य; plain root → -त्वा.

questions.q: Which split of शोषयेदातपे is right?
optionExplain: There is no word दातपे; the द् comes from the त् of शोषयेत्.
Right: त् before a vowel becomes द्: शोषयेत् + आतपे → शोषयेदातपे.
There is no form शोषयेद; the optative ends in -एत्.
There is no word दातपे; आतप = sun.
questions.explain: शोषयेत् = one should dry; आतपे = in the sun.

questions.q: Like उद्धृत्य (उद् + √हृ, 'having taken out'), which is the absolutive of the plain root √हृ?
optionExplain: -य is used only when a prefix stands before the root.
हृतम् is the past participle: 'taken'.
Right: Without a prefix the absolutive takes -त्वा: हृत्वा, 'having taken'.
हरेत् is the optative: 'one should take'.
questions.explain: उद्धृत्य (prefix, -य) against हृत्वा (no prefix, -त्वा).
questions.teaches: Absolutives: a plain root takes -त्वा (हृत्वा), a root with a prefix takes -य (उद्धृत्य, समुद्धृत्य).

questions.q: With what does verse 47 say it is given?
optionExplain: Honey water is not named in this verse.
Milk is not named in this verse.
Sour gruel is not named in this verse.
Right: द्राक्षारसेन = with drākṣā (grape) juice.
questions.explain: द्राक्षा = grape (Vitis vinifera; standard); रस = juice.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 47 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The vehicle, the complaint, and the age range of children.
questions.rule: द्राक्षा = grape; दाह = burning; पीडित = afflicted; चतुर्वर्ष = four-year-old; द्वादशवार्षिक = twelve-year-old.

questions.q: Put the phrases of verse 47 in their order.
questions.explain: With grape juice give it; to one afflicted by burning and udāvarta; to a four-year-old child; up to twelve.
questions.rule: द्राक्षारसेन · दाहोदावर्तपीडिते · चतुर्वर्षे बाले · यावद् द्वादशवार्षिके.
questions.teaches: The first line gives vehicle and patient, the second the age range of children.

questions.q: Which split of दाहोदावर्त is right?
optionExplain: Right: अ + उ → ओ: दाह + उदावर्त → दाहोदावर्त.
There is no word दावर्त; the ओ hides the उ of उदावर्त.
There is no word ओदावर्त; the name is उदावर्त.
There is no word दाहोद; the words are दाह and उदावर्त.
questions.explain: दाह = burning; उदावर्त = upward-turned Vāta.

questions.q: By verse 47, up to what age of child is it given?
optionExplain: Four years is where the range starts, चतुर्वर्षे.
Right: यावद् द्वादशवार्षिके = up to one of twelve years.
Sixteen is not named in this verse.
Eight is not named in this verse.
questions.explain: From four years (चतुर्वर्षे) up to twelve (द्वादशवार्षिके).

questions.q: Like दद्यात् + दाह → दद्याद्दाह, which is the joined form of तत् + दानम् (invented)?
optionExplain: त् does not stay unvoiced before the voiced द.
The final consonant is not lost; it doubles as द्द.
Right: त् before द becomes द्: तत् + दानम् → तद्दानम्.
The द of दानम् does not change to त.
questions.explain: दद्याद्दाह: त् + द → द्द.
questions.teaches: A final त् before a voiced consonant becomes द्: दद्याद्दाह, तद्दानम्.

questions.q: What kind of decoction does verse 48 say one should make him drink?
optionExplain: The verse says हिम, cold.
Thickness is not named in this verse.
Salt is not named in this verse.
Right: कषायं पाययेद् हिमम् = make (him) drink a cold decoction.
questions.explain: हिम = cold.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 48 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The kernel's cold decoction, made to be drunk, with vehicles taken separately.
questions.rule: मज्जा = kernel; हिम = cold; पाययेत् = should make drink; धात्री = āmalakī; पृथक् = separately.

questions.q: Put the three vehicles in the order of verse 48.
questions.explain: Curd-maṇḍa, surā-maṇḍa, then dhātrī fruit juice.
questions.teaches: The second line is one instrumental compound of three vehicles, closed by पृथक्.

questions.q: What does पृथक् tell about the three vehicles of verse 48?
options: Each one is used on its own
They are boiled into the kernel
Only the first one may be used
optionExplain: Right: पृथक् = separately: one vehicle at a time.
That would contradict पृथक्, 'separately'.
They go with the drink; पृथक् says nothing of boiling.
All three are offered; पृथक् makes them alternatives.
questions.explain: पृथक् = separately, apart.

questions.q: Which split of पाययेद्धिमम् is right?
optionExplain: There is no word धिमम्; the ध comes from the ह of हिमम्.
Right: त् before ह becomes द् and ह becomes ध्: पाययेत् + हिमम् → पाययेद्धिमम्.
There is no word द्धिमम्; the verb is पाययेत्.
There is no word धिमम्; cold = हिम.
questions.explain: पाययेत् = should make drink; हिमम् = cold.

questions.q: Like पाययेत् + हिमम् → पाययेद्धिमम्, which is the joined form of तत् + हि (invented)?
optionExplain: त् does not stay unchanged before ह.
The ह also changes: it becomes ध after द्.
Right: त् + ह → द्ध: तत् + हि → तद्धि.
The द् is not lost; the result is द्ध.
questions.explain: पाययेद्धिमम्, तद्धि: त् + ह → द्ध.
questions.teaches: A final त् before ह gives द्ध: पाययेद्धिमम्, तद्धि.

questions.q: From what does verse 49 say the ghee arises?
optionExplain: No curd or churning is named in this verse.
Neither butter nor honey is named here.
sauvīraka joins the decoction, not the milk.
Right: चतुरङ्गुलसिद्धात् क्षीरात् यद् उदियाद् घृतम्.
questions.explain: क्षीर = milk; सिद्ध = cooked; उदियात् = would arise.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 49 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Two vehicles for the decoction, then the milk and the ghee that arises.
questions.rule: सौवीरक = sour barley drink; कल्क = paste; त्रैवृत = of trivṛt; क्षीर = milk; उदियात् = would arise.

questions.q: Put the items of verse 49 in their order.
questions.explain: sauvīraka, the trivṛt paste, the milk cooked with caturaṅgula, the ghee.
questions.rule: सौवीरकेण · कल्केन त्रैवृतेन · चतुरङ्गुलसिद्धात् क्षीरात् · घृतम्.
questions.teaches: Each line has its own वा: two vehicles in the first line, the ghee from milk in the second.

questions.q: What does the form त्रैवृत (from त्रिवृत्) mean in verse 49?
options: A third part of the trivṛt
optionExplain: Right: The vṛddhi derivative त्रैवृत = relating to trivṛt.
The word is a drug derivative, not 'three turns'.
No three kinds are meant; ऐ marks a derivative.
No fraction is meant; it is 'of trivṛt'.
questions.explain: कल्केन त्रैवृतेन = with a trivṛt paste.
questions.rule: इ → ऐ in the first syllable: 'relating to'.

questions.q: Which split of उदियाद्घृतम् is right?
optionExplain: There is no word द्घृतम्; the द् comes from उदियात्.
Right: त् before the voiced घ becomes द्: उदियात् + घृतम् → उदियाद्घृतम्.
Neither उदि nor याद्घृतम् is a word here.
There is no word उदियाद्घ; the noun is घृतम्.
questions.explain: उदियात् = would arise (opt.); घृतम् = ghee.

questions.q: Like त्रिवृत् → त्रैवृत (of trivṛt), which is the matching derivative of शिव (of Śiva)?
optionExplain: The vṛddhi of इ is ऐ, not ए.
-य is not added here; the first vowel is raised.
Right: इ of the first syllable becomes ऐ: शिव → शैव, as त्रिवृत् → त्रैवृत.
Lengthening इ to ई is not vṛddhi.
questions.explain: त्रैवृत, शैव: vṛddhi ऐ in the first syllable.
questions.rule: Derivative 'relating to X': first vowel इ → ऐ.
questions.teaches: A derivative meaning 'relating to X' raises the first vowel (इ → ऐ): त्रैवृत, शैव.

questions.q: By verse 50, in the juice of which fruit is the ghee cooked?
optionExplain: Grape juice was the vehicle of line 05.02.81.
Bilva is not named in this verse.
Pomegranate is not named in this verse.
Right: धात्रीणां रसे = in the juice of dhātrīs.
questions.explain: dhātrī = āmalakī, emblic myrobalan (standard).

questions.q: Match each word of verse 50 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The first line prepares the ghee; the second lists other decoctions for the same.
questions.rule: मज्जकल्क = kernel paste; धात्री = āmalakī; साधित = cooked; दशमूल = ten roots; कुलत्थ = horse gram.

questions.q: Put the drugs of the second line in the order of verse 50.
questions.explain: Daśamūla, kulattha, yava; च closes the line.
questions.teaches: Three genitives in the second line; their noun (कषाये) stands in line 05.02.89.

questions.q: Where do the genitives दशमूलस्य, कुलत्थानाम्, यवस्य find their noun?
options: In रसे of the first line
optionExplain: Right: The data: they depend on कषाये, 'in the decoction (of ...)'.
रसे is the juice of the dhātrīs only.
The kernel paste is of caturaṅgula, not of these.
तदेव is 'that same'; it does not take these genitives.
questions.explain: दशमूलस्य कुलत्थानां यवस्य च ... कषाये: in the decoction of these.
questions.rule: A genitive may wait for its noun in the next line.

questions.q: By the card, what does दशमूल ('ten roots') stand for here?
options: A known group the verse doesn't list
Ten parts of root to one of ghee
optionExplain: No handfuls are named here; दशमूल is the group of ten roots.
Right: daśamūla is the standard group of ten roots; the text does not list them.
दश counts the roots, not the age of trees.
No proportion is stated in this verse.
questions.explain: दश = ten; मूल = root: a fixed group of ten roots.

questions.q: Like तत् + एव → तदेव, which is the joined form of तत् + अपि (invented)?
optionExplain: त् does not stay unvoiced before a vowel.
The अ of अपि is not lost, and त् does not stay unvoiced.
Right: त् before a vowel becomes द्: तत् + अपि → तदपि.
The अ of अपि is not lost.
questions.explain: तदेव, तदपि: त् + vowel → द्.
questions.teaches: A final त् before a vowel becomes द्: तदेव, तदपि, शोषयेदातपे.

questions.q: By verse 51, what is put into the decoction of dantī?
optionExplain: Those went into the pot of line 05.02.66.
The guḍa is जीर्ण, old, and no ghee is put in.
Neither is put into the dantī decoction here.
Right: तन्मज्जां गुडं जीर्णं च निक्षिपेत्.
questions.explain: मज्जा = kernel; गुड = unrefined sugar; जीर्ण = old.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 51 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The ghee line and the dantī line.
questions.rule: कषाये = in the decoction; साधित = cooked; कल्कैः = with pastes; जीर्ण = old; निक्षिपेत् = should put in.

questions.q: Put the words of the second line of verse 51 in their order.
questions.explain: In the dantī decoction, its kernel, guḍa, old, one should put in.
questions.rule: दन्तीकषाये · तन्मज्जां · गुडं जीर्णं च · निक्षिपेत्.
questions.teaches: The second line names the vessel liquid first, then the two things put in, then the verb.

questions.q: In verse 51, what does जीर्ण mean with गुड?
optionExplain: Right: The glossary fixes जीर्ण = old here: old guḍa.
जीर्ण means digested only of food in the body, as in line 05.02.58.
Melted would be द्रुत or विलीन.
Nothing about refining is said.
questions.explain: गुडं जीर्णम् = old guḍa.

questions.q: Which of these does verse 51 state?
options: Ghee cooked in the decoction is drunk
Old guḍa goes into the dantī decoction
The dantī mixture is kept for a month
Honey is added to the dantī decoction
It is drunk with pastes of śyāmā and the rest
optionExplain: Right: कषाये साधितं सर्पिः ... पिबेत्.
Right: गुडं जीर्णं च निक्षिपेत्.
No: keeping it comes in line 05.02.91.
No: honey is not named in this verse.
Right: कल्कैः श्यामादिभिः.
questions.explain: Two instructions: drink the ghee with pastes; put kernel and old guḍa into the dantī decoction.

questions.q: Like तत् + मज्जाम् → तन्मज्जाम्, which is the joined form of तत् + मुखम् (invented)?
optionExplain: त् does not stay unchanged before म.
Right: त् before a nasal becomes न्: तत् + मुखम् → तन्मुखम्.
Before a nasal the त् becomes the nasal न्, not द्.
The final consonant is not lost.
questions.explain: तन्मज्जाम्: त् + म → न्म.
questions.teaches: A final त् before a nasal becomes न्: तन्मज्जाम्, तन्मुखम्.

questions.q: By verse 52, after how long is the ariṣṭa given to drink?
options: After seven days, or three nights
After a year, or at least six months
After a month, or a fortnight
After ten days, or as soon as sour
optionExplain: No seven days or three nights are named in this verse.
No year or six months are named; the verse says मास and पक्ष.
Right: स्थितं मासं ... पक्षमेव वा = kept a month, or just a fortnight.
No ten days and no souring are named in this verse.
questions.explain: मास = a month; पक्ष = a fortnight; वा = or.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 52 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The first line gives the time of drinking; the second names the bark taken and the part thrown away.
questions.rule: पाययेत् = should make drink; पक्ष = fortnight; त्वच् = bark; मूल = root; त्यक्त्वा = having discarded.

questions.q: Put the words of the second line of verse 52 in their order.
questions.explain: The bark, of the tilvaka root, having discarded, the inner bark.
questions.teaches: The second line names what is taken (the root bark) before what is thrown away (the inner bark).

questions.q: By verse 52, which part of tilvaka is taken for the new recipe?
options: The inner bark of the root alone
The ripe fruit with its kernel
The fresh leaves of the young plant
The root bark, without the inner bark
optionExplain: The inner bark is the part discarded (त्यक्त्वा).
Fruit and kernel belong to the caturaṅgula recipes of lines 05.02.77-80.
No leaves are named in this verse.
Right: त्वचं तिल्वकमूलस्य त्यक्त्वा अभ्यंतरवल्कलम्: root bark, inner bark discarded.
questions.explain: त्वच् = bark (skin); अभ्यन्तरवल्कल = the inner bark, which is thrown away.

questions.q: Which of these does verse 52 state?
options: The bark of the tilvaka root is taken
The ariṣṭa is drunk after a year
The ariṣṭa may be drunk after a fortnight
The ariṣṭa may be drunk after a month
The inner bark is kept and powdered
optionExplain: Right: त्वचं तिल्वकमूलस्य.
No: the verse says a month (मास) or a fortnight (पक्ष).
Right: पक्षमेव वा, or just a fortnight.
Right: स्थितं मासं पाययेत्.
No: the inner bark is discarded (त्यक्त्वा).
questions.explain: Two times of drinking for the ariṣṭa, then the root bark of tilvaka without its inner bark.

questions.q: Like त्यक्त्वा (having discarded, from √त्यज्), which is the absolutive of √पा (drink)?
optionExplain: Right: पीत्वा is the absolutive in -त्वा: 'having drunk', like त्यक्त्वा.
पिबेत् is the optative: 'one should drink'.
पीतम् is the past participle: 'drunk'.
पाययेत् is the causative optative: 'one should make drink'.
questions.explain: त्यक्त्वा, पीत्वा: the -त्वा form says 'having done' before the main verb.
questions.teaches: A verb without a prefix forms its absolutive in -त्वा: त्यक्त्वा 'having discarded', पीत्वा 'having drunk'.

questions.q: By verse 53, with which decoction is the third part saturated?
optionExplain: tilvaka is the bark itself; its decoction comes in line 05.02.102.
Right: रोध्रस्यैव कषायेण = with the decoction of rodhra alone.
The daśamūla decoction is the second soaking, in line 05.02.95.
No triphalā is named in this verse.
questions.explain: रोध्र = lodhra (Symplocos racemosa, standard); कषाय = decoction.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 53 to its meaning.
