questions.explain: Drying, then two parts strained, then the third part saturated.
questions.rule: विशोष्य = having dried; द्वौ भागौ = two parts; गालयेत् = should strain; तृतीयम् = the third; भावयेत् = should saturate.

questions.q: Put the steps of verse 53 in the text's order.
items: तृतीयं रोध्रकषायेण भावयेत् (saturate the third with rodhra decoction)
questions.explain: First drying (and powdering), then two parts are strained, then the third is saturated.
questions.rule: विशोष्य · द्वौ भागौ गालयेत् · तृतीयं भावयेत्.
questions.teaches: The powdered bark is divided: two parts are strained, the third gets a separate saturation.

questions.q: Which split of रोध्रस्यैव is right?
optionExplain: अ + इ gives ए: that would be रोध्रस्येव, not ऐ.
रोध्रस्यै is not a form of रोध्र, and ऐ + ए would not give ऐव.
Right: अ + ए → ऐ: रोध्रस्य + एव → रोध्रस्यैव.
There is no word स्यैव; रोध्रस्य is the genitive.
questions.explain: रोध्रस्य = of rodhra (gen.); एव = alone, only.

questions.q: By verse 53, what is done to the two parts?
optionExplain: Only the third part is saturated (तृतीयं ... भावयेत्).
No boiling is named in this verse.
No honey is named in this verse.
Right: द्वौ भागौ गालयेत् = one should strain two parts.
questions.explain: Two parts strained; the third saturated with rodhra decoction.

questions.q: Like रोध्रस्य + एव → रोध्रस्यैव, which is the joined form of तस्य + एव (invented)?
optionExplain: Right: अ + ए → ऐ: तस्य + एव → तस्यैव.
तस्येव would be तस्य + इव (अ + इ → ए).
No rule gives आव from अ + ए.
Within a phrase अ + ए do not stand apart; they join as ऐ.
questions.explain: रोध्रस्यैव, तस्यैव: अ + ए → ऐ.
questions.teaches: अ before ए merges into ऐ: रोध्रस्य + एव → रोध्रस्यैव, तस्य + एव → तस्यैव.

questions.q: By verse 54, in which decoction is the part saturated once more?
optionExplain: rodhra gave the first saturation, in line 05.02.94.
Right: कषाये दशमूलस्य = in the decoction of the ten roots.
The tilvaka decoction belongs to line 05.02.102.
The dantī decoction belongs to line 05.02.90.
questions.explain: दशमूल = the ten roots; पुनः = again.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 54 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The first line gives the second saturation; the second line the dry powder and the measure.
questions.rule: दशमूल = ten roots; भावित = saturated; पुनः = again; शुष्कचूर्ण = dry powder; पाणितल = palmful.

questions.q: Verse 54: the part is saturated ____ (again) in the daśamūla decoction. Type it in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: पुनः = again: the part already saturated with rodhra is saturated once more.
questions.teaches: पुनः marks the second saturation of the same part.

questions.q: By verse 54, how much of the dry powder is drunk?
optionExplain: No añjali is named in this verse.
No karṣa is named in this verse.
Right: पाणितलं पिबेत् = one should drink a palmful (palm-surface).
No pala is named in this verse.
questions.explain: पाणितल = the surface of the palm, read as a palm-sized measure.

questions.q: Put the steps of verse 54 in the text's order.
items: दशमूलकषाये भावितं पुनः (saturated again in daśamūla)
questions.explain: Second saturation, then a dry powder, then a palmful is drunk.
questions.rule: भावितं पुनः · शुष्कचूर्णं कृत्वा · पाणितलं पिबेत्.

questions.q: Like भावितम् (saturated, from the causative भावयति), which is the past participle of स्थापयति (places)?
optionExplain: स्थापयित्वा is the absolutive: 'having placed'.
स्थापयेत् is the optative: 'one should place'.
स्थाप्यम् is the gerundive: 'is to be placed'.
Right: A causative in -अयति makes its past participle in -इत: भावितम्, स्थापितम्.
questions.explain: भावयति → भावितम्; स्थापयति → स्थापितम्.
questions.teaches: The past participle of a causative ends in -इत: भावयति → भावितम्, स्थापयति → स्थापितम्.

questions.q: In verse 55, what is abhayā?
optionExplain: Right: abhayā = harītakī, Terminalia chebula (standard).
Long pepper is kṛṣṇā, the next member of the compound.
Leadwort is citraka, the last member of the compound.
meṣaśṛṅgī is the first member, named before abhayā.
questions.explain: अभया = हरड़, Terminalia chebula (standard).

questions.q: Match each drug of verse 55 to its meaning on the card.
questions.explain: The first line lists liquids and fruits; the second line four drugs named with the water.
questions.rule: मस्तु = whey; कोल = jujube; धात्रीफल = āmalakī fruit; कृष्णा = long pepper; चित्रक = leadwort.

questions.q: Put the members of the first compound of verse 55 in their order.
questions.explain: Whey, urine, surā-maṇḍa, kola, dhātrī fruit; अम्बुभिः closes the compound.
questions.teaches: One long dvandva compound lists the liquids and fruits; its instrumental ending -भिः says 'with'.

questions.q: Which split of मेषशृंग्यभया is right?
optionExplain: There is no drug भया; the अ of अभया became part of य.
Right: ई before अ becomes य्: मेषशृङ्गी + अभया → मेषशृङ्ग्यभया.
अ + अ would give आ: that would be मेषशृङ्ग्याभया.
ए + अ would give एऽ (मेषशृङ्गेऽभया), not य.
questions.explain: मेषशृङ्गी (f.) + अभया (f.): ई + अ → य.

questions.q: Which drugs does the second compound of verse 55 (ending -चित्रकैः) name?
optionExplain: No: rodhra is not named in this verse.
No: dhātrī fruit is in the first compound of the first line.
Right: the second member, harītakī.
Right: the first member.
Right: the third member, long pepper.
questions.explain: मेषशृङ्ग्यभयाकृष्णाचित्रकैः = with meṣaśṛṅgī, abhayā, kṛṣṇā and citraka.

questions.q: Like मेषशृङ्गी + अभया → मेषशृङ्ग्यभया, which is the joined form of नदी + अत्र (invented)?
optionExplain: The अ of अत्र is not lost; it stays after य्.
ई + अ gives य + अ, not य + आ.
Right: ई before अ becomes य्: नदी + अत्र → नद्यत्र.
ई does not turn into ए before अ.
questions.explain: मेषशृङ्ग्यभया, नद्यत्र: ई + अ → य.
questions.teaches: A final इ or ई before an unlike vowel becomes य्: मेषशृङ्गी + अभया → मेषशृङ्ग्यभया, नदी + अत्र → नद्यत्र.

questions.q: By verse 56, what should one drink then (तदा)?
options: The ghee of the ten roots
optionExplain: The tilvaka decoction is named in line 05.02.102, not here.
daśamūla was a decoction for soaking, in line 05.02.95.
No ghee is named in this verse.
Right: रोध्रकल्कं पिबेत्तदा = then one should drink the paste of rodhra.
questions.explain: कल्क = paste; रोध्र = lodhra.
questions.rule: यदा सौवीरकं जातं → तदा रोध्रकल्कं पिबेत्.

questions.q: Match each clear word of verse 56 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Only the clear words of the verse are matched; mairujān and the measure word stay open.
questions.rule: पिबेत् = should drink; जातम् = become; यदा = when; तदा = then; कल्क = paste.

questions.q: Put these printed words of the first line of verse 56 in their order.
questions.explain: The printed first line after its unclear first word, word by word; its sense is tentative.
questions.teaches: The first line ends with यदा (when), the clause that the second line answers with तदा (then).

questions.q: Which split of पिबेत्तदा is right?
optionExplain: Right: त् before त stays त्: पिबेत् + तदा → पिबेत्तदा.
त् + अ would give द: पिबेददा.
That would be written पिबेतदा, with one त; the verb is पिबेत्.
There is no word पिबेत्त; the verb is पिबेत्.
questions.explain: पिबेत् = one should drink; तदा = then.

questions.q: By verse 56, when is the rodhra paste drunk?
options: After a month in a greased pot
After drying it on the embers
optionExplain: The pressing out (सुनुयात्) comes first.
Right: जातं सौवीरकं यदा ... तदा: when it has become sauvīraka, then.
The month in a pot belongs to line 05.02.67.
Drying on embers comes in line 05.02.113.
questions.explain: यदा ... तदा: the drink follows the forming of the sauvīraka.

questions.q: Invented: यदा ज्वरः शान्तो भवेत्, ____ अन्नं दद्यात्. Which word answers यदा here?
optionExplain: A second यदा would repeat 'when'; the answer needs 'then'.
कदा asks 'when?'; it does not answer a यदा clause.
Right: यदा (when) is answered by तदा (then), as in verse 56.
यथा means 'as', answered by तथा, not by a यदा clause.
questions.explain: यदा ... तदा: 'when ... then'.
questions.teaches: A clause with यदा (when) is answered by तदा (then): जातं सौवीरकं यदा ... पिबेत्तदा.

questions.q: By verse 57, how long is the rodhra surā kept before drinking?
optionExplain: A month was one choice for the ariṣṭa in line 05.02.91.
No seven days are named in this verse.
Six days was the steeping of line 05.02.70.
Right: पक्षस्थितां पिबेत् = one should drink it kept for a fortnight.
questions.explain: पक्षस्थिता = kept for a fortnight.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 57 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The first line describes the surā; the second line lists what goes into the next preparation.
questions.rule: सुरा = spirituous drink; जाता = produced; पक्षस्थिता = kept a fortnight; कल्क = paste; सशर्कर = with sugar.

questions.q: Put the words of the first line of verse 57 in their order.
questions.explain: Surā, with rodhra decoction, produced, kept a fortnight, one should drink.
questions.teaches: The feminine accusatives जातां and पक्षस्थितां both describe सुरां, the object of पिबेत्.

questions.q: Why is सशर्करः in verse 57 masculine?
options: It goes with लेहः of the next line
It goes with सुरां of the first line
It goes with कषायेण, the word before it
It is the plain noun शर्करा, sugar
optionExplain: Right: सशर्करः (m. nom. sg.) agrees with लेहः in line 05.02.103.
सुरां is feminine accusative; it does not agree.
कषायेण is instrumental; सशर्करः is nominative.
शर्करा is feminine; सशर्करः is a bahuvrīhi, 'having sugar'.
questions.explain: A bahuvrīhi takes the gender of the noun it describes: here the leha.

questions.q: Which of these go into the second-line preparation of verse 57?
optionExplain: Right: the first item of the second line.
No: whey is not named in this verse.
Right: कल्केन च, with the paste.
Right: with sugar.
No: the rodhra decoction produces the surā of the first line.
questions.explain: तिल्वकस्य कषायेण कल्केन च सशर्करः: decoction, paste, sugar.

questions.q: Like सशर्करः (having sugar), what does समधुः लेहः (invented) mean?
optionExplain: Without honey would be निर्मधुः, not स-.
Right: स- + मधु = having honey: a bahuvrīhi like सशर्करः.
समधुः describes the leha; it does not replace it.
स- means 'with', not 'like'.
questions.explain: स- = with: सशर्करः, समधुः.
questions.teaches: The prefix स- makes a bahuvrīhi 'having X' that agrees with its noun: सशर्करः लेहः, समधुः लेहः.

questions.q: By verse 58, what does sudhā do?
options: It calms the doṣas without moving them
It increases the doṣas in a weak patient
It splits even a great accumulation of doṣas
It dries the doṣas slowly over months
optionExplain: भिनत्ति = splits; the verse does not speak of calming.
Nothing about increasing doṣas is said here.
Right: सुधा भिनत्ति दोषाणां महान्तमपि संचयम्.
No drying and no months are named in this verse.
questions.explain: भिनत्ति = splits, breaks up; संचय = accumulation.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 58 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The first line praises the leha; the second line states the power of sudhā.
questions.rule: सघृत = with ghee; लेह = lick-preparation; विरेचन = purgation; भिनत्ति = splits; संचय = accumulation.

questions.q: Put the words of the second line of verse 58 in their order.
questions.explain: Sudhā splits, of the doṣas, even a great, accumulation.
questions.teaches: Subject, verb, then the object संचयम् with its genitive दोषाणाम् and adjective महान्तम्.

questions.q: Which split of साधितो लेहः is right?
optionExplain: A final म् would give साधितं लेहः, with anusvāra.
There is no word ओलेहः; the ओ is the changed visarga.
ए before ल stays ए: that would be साधिते लेहः.
Right: अः before a voiced consonant becomes ओ: साधितः + लेहः → साधितो लेहः.
questions.explain: साधितः (m. nom. sg.) agrees with लेहः.

questions.q: A student calls the leha of verse 58 an emetic. What does the verse call it?
options: A remedy to be avoided by all
optionExplain: Right: स च श्रेष्ठं विरेचनम् = and that is an excellent purgation.
विरेचन is purgation by the bowel, not vomiting.
The verse calls it श्रेष्ठं विरेचनम्; it says nothing of mildness or children.
The verse praises it as श्रेष्ठ, excellent.
questions.explain: विरेचन = purgation (evacuation by the bowel).

questions.q: Like साधितः + लेहः → साधितो लेहः, which is the joined form of रसः + मधुरः (invented)?
optionExplain: र् appears only after vowels other than अ/आ.
Right: अः before the voiced म becomes ओ: रसो मधुरः.
आ would come from आः, not from अः.
स् appears only before त/थ, not before म.
questions.explain: साधितो लेहः, रसो मधुरः: अः + voiced consonant → ओ.
questions.teaches: A visarga after अ becomes ओ before a voiced consonant: साधितो लेहः, रसो मधुरः.

questions.q: Which person does verse 59 name among those in whom sudhā is not employed?
optionExplain: Strength is the opposite of अबल; no young man is named.
The verse names a soft (मृदु) koṣṭha, not a hard one.
Right: स्थविरे = in an old person, one of the five listed.
gulma is where sudhā is employed, line 05.02.107.
questions.explain: The five: soft koṣṭha, weak, child, old, long diseased.
questions.rule: मृदुकोष्ठ · अबल · बाल · स्थविर · दीर्घरोगी → नैव कल्पयेत्.

questions.q: Match each person of verse 59 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five locatives name the persons in whom sudhā is not employed.
questions.rule: मृदु कोष्ठ = soft koṣṭha; अबल = weak; बाल = child; स्थविर = old; दीर्घरोगी = long diseased.

questions.q: Put the persons of verse 59 in the text's order.
questions.explain: Soft koṣṭha, weak, child, old, long diseased.
questions.rule: मृदौ कोष्ठे · अबले · बाले · स्थविरे · दीर्घरोगिणि.
questions.teaches: The second line is a list of five locatives: 'in one who is ...'.

questions.q: Which split of कोष्ठेऽबले is right?
optionExplain: अ + अ would give आ: कोष्ठाबले.
अः + अ would give ओऽ: कोष्ठोऽबले.
There is no word स्बले; ऽ marks a lost अ.
Right: ए before अ stays ए and the अ is marked ऽ: कोष्ठे + अबले → कोष्ठेऽबले.
questions.explain: कोष्ठे (loc.) + अबले (loc.): in the koṣṭha, in a weak one.

questions.q: A patient is old and weak. By verse 59, should sudhā be employed in him?
options: No: the old and the weak are excluded
Yes: sudhā suits the old and weak
Yes, if it is cooked with ghee first
Only if he also has a soft koṣṭha
optionExplain: Right: स्थविरे and अबले are in the list of those in whom it is not employed.
The verse names both among those excluded.
No such exception is given in this verse.
A soft koṣṭha is another reason to exclude, not a condition to use.
questions.explain: The five locatives all fall under the 'not' of the first line.

questions.q: Like बाले (in a child, from बाल), which is the locative singular of वृद्ध (aged)?
optionExplain: वृद्धः is the nominative: 'an aged one'.
Right: An अ-stem makes its locative singular in -ए: बाले, वृद्धे.
वृद्धेन is the instrumental: 'by an aged one'.
वृद्धस्य is the genitive: 'of an aged one'.
questions.explain: बाले, स्थविरे, वृद्धे: locative singular -ए.
questions.teaches: Masculine अ-stems take -ए in the locative singular: बाले, स्थविरे, वृद्धे 'in one who is ...'.

questions.q: What does कल्प्या, opening verse 60, say of sudhā?
options: It is to be avoided in these
It is to be boiled in these
It is to be employed (in these)
It is to be stored for these
optionExplain: Avoidance was line 05.02.105; कल्प्या turns to use.
कल्प्या is from √कॢप्, 'employ', not 'boil'.
Right: कल्प्या (gerundive) = is to be employed: a positive rule after line 05.02.105.
Nothing about storing is said in this verse.
questions.explain: कल्प्या = is to be employed (f., agreeing with सुधा).

questions.q: Match each condition of verse 60 to its meaning on the card.
questions.explain: Conditions from both lines in which sudhā is to be employed.
questions.rule: गुल्म = abdominal lump; पाण्डु = pallor; दूषीविष = lodged poison; शोफ = swelling; दोषविभ्रान्तचेतस् = bewildered mind.

questions.q: Put the conditions of the second line of verse 60 in their order.
questions.explain: Pāṇḍu, dūṣīviṣa, swelling, a mind bewildered by the doṣas.
questions.teaches: The second line lists four locatives in which sudhā is to be employed.

questions.q: In which of these is sudhā to be employed by verse 60?
optionExplain: A soft koṣṭha is excluded, line 05.02.106.
A child is excluded, line 05.02.106.
One long diseased is excluded, line 05.02.106.
Right: शोफे is in the list of verse 60, under कल्प्या.
questions.explain: Verse 59 lists who is excluded; verse 60 lists where it is used.
questions.rule: नैव: मृदुकोष्ठ, बाल, दीर्घरोगी · कल्प्या: शोफ आदि.

questions.q: A patient's mind is bewildered by the doṣas. Which phrase of verse 60 covers him?
optionExplain: Right: = in one whose mind is bewildered by the doṣas (bahuvrīhi, loc.).
दूषीविषे = in lodged poison, a different condition.
पाण्डौ = in pāṇḍu, the pallor disease.
शोफे = in swelling.
questions.explain: दोष-विभ्रान्त-चेतस् = whose mind (चेतस्) is bewildered (विभ्रान्त) by doṣas.

questions.q: Like कल्प्या (f., agreeing with सुधा), which gerundive of √दा (give) goes with त्रिवृत् (f.) in an invented line?
optionExplain: देयः is masculine; त्रिवृत् is feminine.
Right: The gerundive agrees with its noun: त्रिवृत् is feminine, so देया, like कल्प्या.
देयम् is neuter; त्रिवृत् is feminine.
दत्ता is the past participle 'given', not 'is to be given'.
questions.explain: कल्प्या सुधा, देया त्रिवृत्: feminine gerundives in -आ.
questions.rule: Gerundive agrees in gender with its noun.
questions.teaches: A gerundive ('is to be ...') agrees with its noun: कल्प्या (सुधा), देया (त्रिवृत्).

questions.q: By verse 61, which sudhā is the best?
options: One smooth and wholly without thorns
One with few, soft and short thorns
One covered with many sharp thorns
One with broad leaves and no milk
optionExplain: The verse praises thorns; it names no smooth plant.
The thorns are तीक्ष्ण (sharp) and बहु (many).
Right: कण्टकैस्तीक्ष्णैर्बहुभिश्च समाचिता = covered with sharp and many thorns.
Neither leaves nor lack of milk is named here.
questions.explain: श्रेष्ठा = best; समाचिता = covered.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 61 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The first line describes the best plant by its thorns.
questions.rule: श्रेष्ठा = best; कण्टक = thorn; तीक्ष्ण = sharp; बहु = many; समाचिता = covered.

questions.q: Put the words of the first line of verse 61 in their order.
questions.explain: That one, best, with sharp and many thorns, covered.
questions.teaches: The three instrumentals (thorns, sharp, many) all go with समाचिता, 'covered'.

questions.q: Which split of कंटकैस्तीक्ष्णैः is right?
optionExplain: There is no word स्तीक्ष्ण; the स् is the changed visarga.
म् before त would give कण्टकं तीक्ष्णैः.
ए before त stays ए: कण्टके तीक्ष्णैः.
Right: ः before त becomes स्: कण्टकैः + तीक्ष्णैः → कण्टकैस्तीक्ष्णैः.
questions.explain: कण्टकैः and तीक्ष्णैः: both instrumental plural.

questions.q: By verse 61, of what age should the sudhā plant be?
optionExplain: Right: द्विवर्षा वा त्रिवर्षा वा = two years or three years old.
No one-year plant is named; it says two or three.
The verse says द्वि and त्रि, two and three.
An age is given: two or three years.
questions.explain: द्विवर्षा = two years old; त्रिवर्षा = three years old.

questions.q: Like कण्टकैः + तीक्ष्णैः → कण्टकैस्तीक्ष्णैः, which is the joined form of रामः + तत्र (invented)?
optionExplain: ओ comes before voiced sounds; त is unvoiced.
Right: ः before त becomes स्: रामः + तत्र → रामस्तत्र.
र् never comes from अः; and not before त.
आ would come from आः, not अः.
questions.explain: कण्टकैस्तीक्ष्णैः, रामस्तत्र: ः + त → स्त.
questions.teaches: A visarga before त or थ becomes स्: कण्टकैस्तीक्ष्णैः, रामस्तत्र.

questions.q: By verse 62, with what is the plant split open?
optionExplain: No hands are named; the verse says शस्त्र.
No stone is named; the verse says शस्त्र.
Right: पाटयित्वा शस्त्रेण = having split it open with a blade.
Embers come in line 05.02.113, for drying.
questions.explain: शस्त्र = blade, cutting instrument.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 62 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The first line draws out the milk; the second gives the decoctions and how they are used.
questions.rule: पाटयित्वा = having split open; शस्त्र = blade; क्षीर = milk; उद्धारयेत् = should draw out; एकशः = singly.

questions.q: Put the words of the first line of verse 62 in their order.
questions.explain: It, having split open, with a blade, one should then draw out the milk.
questions.teaches: The absolutive पाटयित्वा (having split) comes before the main action उद्धारयेत् (draw out).

questions.q: In verse 62, what does the dual बृहत्योः mean?
optionExplain: A dual means two, not one.
Many would need the plural, बृहतीनाम्.
bilva is in the other choice; वा separates them.
Right: Dual genitive: the pair bṛhatī and kaṇṭakārī (pair standard).
questions.explain: बृहत्योः = f. gen. dual: of the two bṛhatī.

questions.q: By verse 62, which decoctions may be used with the milk?
options: Of bilva and the rest, or of the two bṛhatīs
Of rodhra, or of tilvaka bark
Of dhātrī fruit, or of kola
Of trivṛt, or of dantī roots
optionExplain: Right: बिल्वादीनां बृहत्योर्वा क्वाथेन: two choices joined by वा.
rodhra and tilvaka belong to lines 05.02.91-103.
These are in line 05.02.97, not this verse.
Neither trivṛt nor dantī is named in this verse.
questions.explain: बिल्वादि = bilva (bael) and the others; बृहत्यौ = the two bṛhatīs.

questions.q: Like पाटयित्वा (having split, from पाटयति), which is the absolutive of शोषयति (dries)?
optionExplain: शोषितम् is the past participle: 'dried'.
Right: A causative in -अयति makes the absolutive -अयित्वा: पाटयित्वा, शोषयित्वा.
शोषयेत् is the optative: 'one should dry'.
Not the form of the causative; the causative keeps -अय-.
questions.explain: पाटयति → पाटयित्वा; शोषयति → शोषयित्वा.
questions.teaches: A causative verb keeps -अय- in its absolutive: पाटयित्वा, शोषयित्वा, मिश्रयित्वा.

questions.q: By verse 63, where is the mixture dried?
optionExplain: Drying in the sun was line 05.02.79, not this verse.
No shade is named in this verse.
Right: ततोऽङ्गारेषु शोषयेत् = then one should dry it on embers.
Sand was for the fruit in line 05.02.78.
questions.explain: अङ्गार = ember; शोषयेत् = should dry.
questions.rule: मिश्रयित्वा → अङ्गारेषु शोषयेत् → गुलिकां कृत्वा पिबेत्.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 63 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The first line mixes and dries; the second makes the pill and names its vehicles.
questions.rule: मिश्रयित्वा = having mixed; अङ्गार = ember; शोषयेत् = should dry; गुलिका = pill; मस्तु = whey.

questions.q: Put the actions of verse 63 in the order they are done.
questions.explain: Mix, dry on embers, make the pill, drink it; the print puts पिबेत् before कृत्वा.
questions.teaches: The absolutive कृत्वा (having made) is done before the main verb पिबेत्, even though it is printed after it.

questions.q: Which split of ततोऽंगारेषु is right?
optionExplain: त् before a vowel becomes द्: that would be तदंगारेषु.
There is no word गारेषु; ऽ marks the lost अ of अंगारेषु.
ततौ is not the word here, and औ + अ would give आव.
Right: अः before अ becomes ओ and the अ is marked ऽ: ततः + अंगारेषु → ततोऽंगारेषु.
questions.explain: ततः = then; अंगारेषु = on embers (loc. pl.).

questions.q: By verse 63, with which of these is the pill drunk?
optionExplain: Right: the second member; the animal is not stated.
No: honey is not named in this verse.
No: oil is not named in this verse.
Right: whey, the first member.
Right: the third member, followed by आदि, 'and the like'.
questions.explain: मस्तुमूत्रसुरादिभिः = with mastu, urine, surā and the like.

questions.q: Like मस्तुमूत्रसुरादिभिः (with mastu, urine, surā and the like), what does दधिक्षीरादिभिः (invented) mean?
options: With curd, milk and the like
With the first of curd and milk
optionExplain: Right: -आदि closes a list with 'and the like'; -भिः = 'with'.
-आदि adds 'and the like'; the list is open.
-भिः is the instrumental 'with', not 'without'.
आदि here means 'and so on', not 'the first one'.
questions.explain: X-Y-आदिभिः = with X, Y and the like.
questions.teaches: A list compound ending in -आदि means 'X, Y and the like': मस्तुमूत्रसुरादिभिः, दधिक्षीरादिभिः.

questions.q: By verse 64, with what are the steeped drugs drunk?
optionExplain: No honey and no water are named in this verse.
Right: रसेनाज्येन वा पिबेत् = one should drink with juice or with ghee.
Urine and whey are vehicles of verse 63, not of this verse.
Madirā with salt belongs to line 05.02.127.
questions.explain: रस = juice; आज्य = ghee; वा = or.
questions.rule: स्नुक्पयःपीत द्रव्य → रसेन आज्येन वा पिबेत्.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 64 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Seven days in snuk milk; then drunk with juice or ghee.
questions.rule: सप्ताहम् = seven days; स्नुक् = spurge; पयः = milk; रसेन = with juice; आज्येन = with ghee.

questions.q: Put the phrases of verse 64 (after the trivṛt group) in the text's order.
questions.explain: First the further drugs, then the seven-day steeping, then the drinking.
questions.rule: वरा · स्वर्णक्षीरी · सातला → सप्ताहं स्नुक्पयःपीतान् → रसेनाज्येन वा पिबेत्.
questions.teaches: The object comes first, its steeping next, and the verb pibet closes the sentence.

questions.q: In verse 64, who or what is स्नुक्पयःपीतान्?
options: The patient, after drinking snuk milk
The snuk milk, boiled with the drugs
The drugs, steeped in snuk milk
The drugs, dried in the sun for a week
optionExplain: The patient would be nom. sg.; पीतान् is m. acc. pl.
No boiling is named; the milk is what the drugs absorb.
Right: पीतान् is m. acc. pl., agreeing with the drugs (त्रिवृतादीन्).
No drying in the sun is named in this verse.
questions.explain: पीत = lit. 'drunk', here 'having absorbed, steeped'.
questions.rule: स्नुक्पयःपीतान् (m. acc. pl.) ↔ त्रिवृतादीन् (m. acc. pl.).

questions.q: Which of these does verse 64 state?
options: The drugs of the trivṛt group are listed one by one
Ghee is one vehicle for the drink
The drugs have absorbed snuk milk
optionExplain: No: the group is named only by 'trivṛt and others'.
No: varā is disputed; triphalā is only a frequent reading.
Right: रसेन ... वा, with juice or.
Right: आज्येन, with ghee.
Right: स्नुक्पयःपीतान्, lit. 'having drunk snuk milk'.
questions.explain: Steeped in snuk milk, then drunk with juice or ghee; the group is not listed and varā stays disputed.

questions.q: Like सप्ताहम् (for seven days), what does मासम् express in the invented मासं पिबेत्?
optionExplain: 'In the month' would be the locative मासे.
A month is not a drink; the accusative here measures time.
'From a month' would be the ablative मासात्.
Right: An accusative of a time word gives the length of time: 'for a month'.
questions.explain: सप्ताहम्, मासम्: accusative = how long.
questions.rule: Time word in the accusative = duration.
questions.teaches: An accusative of a time word says how long: सप्ताहम् 'for seven days', मासम् 'for a month'.

questions.q: By verse 65, with what is the kumbha group taken in the first line?
optionExplain: Right: कुंभादीन् गुडांबुना = kumbha and the others, with jaggery water.
Honey is not named; ghee is in the second line.
Buttermilk (takra) belongs to line 05.02.137.
Whey and urine are vehicles of verse 63.
questions.explain: गुड = jaggery; अम्बु = water; -ना = with (inst. sg.).

questions.q: Match each clear word of verse 65 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Only the clear words are matched; the doubtful drug names of the first token stay open.
questions.rule: तद्वत् = likewise; गुड = jaggery; अम्बु = water; अद्यात् = should eat; फाणित = treacle.

questions.q: Put the items named after अद्यात् in verse 65 in the text's order.
questions.explain: śyāmā and trivṛt first, then snuk milk, ghee and phāṇita, all in the instrumental -ऐः.
questions.teaches: One long compound in -ऐः (with) lists what accompanies the eating.

questions.q: Which split of अद्याच्छ्यामा (start of the second line) is right?
optionExplain: There is no word च्छ्यामा; the verb is अद्यात्.
Right: त् before श becomes च्, and श after it becomes छ: अद्याच्छ्यामा.
There is no drug छ्यामा, and ः would not give च्छ.
म् before श would give an anusvara: अद्यं श्यामा.
questions.explain: अद्यात् = one should eat; श्यामा = a drug name (disputed).

questions.q: By verse 65, which action does the second line prescribe?
optionExplain: पिबेत् is the verb of verse 64, not of this line.
Smelling comes in line 05.02.123.
Right: अद्यात् is the optative of √अद्: 'one should eat'.
No cooking verb is printed in this verse.
questions.explain: अद्यात् (√अद्, eat) differs from पिबेत् (√पा, drink).

questions.q: Like अद्यात् + श्यामा → अद्याच्छ्यामा, which is the joined form of तत् + शृणु (invented)?
optionExplain: Within a phrase त् and श do not stand apart; they join as च्छ.
त् becomes द् only before a voiced sound; श is voiceless.
No rule turns त् into श् before श.
Right: त् + श → च्छ: तत् + शृणु → तच्छृणु.
questions.explain: अद्याच्छ्यामा, तच्छृणु: त् + श → च्छ.
questions.teaches: A final त् before श becomes च् and the श becomes छ: अद्यात् + श्यामा → अद्याच्छ्यामा, तत् + शृणु → तच्छृणु.

questions.q: By verse 66, what is drunk combined with kāsāri juice and broth?
optionExplain: Right: युक्तं वा स्नुक्पयः पिबेत् = or one should drink snuk milk, combined.
dantī juice comes in line 05.02.144.
Jaggery water belongs to verse 65.
The harītakī decoction belongs to line 05.02.130.
questions.explain: स्नुक्पयः = the milk (latex) of snuk; युक्त = combined.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 66 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The first line gives the snuk-milk drink; the second the drugs of a powder.
questions.rule: युक्तम् = combined; यूष = broth; पयः = milk; अर्क = madar; रजः = powder.

questions.q: Put the clear drug names of the powder in verse 66 in the text's order.
questions.explain: nikumbha, kumbha, (śyāmā, printed śyābhā), arka, śaṅkhinī, samalā; rajas closes the compound.
questions.rule: निकुम्भ · कुम्भ · (श्यामा) · अर्क · शङ्खिनी · समला · रजः.
questions.teaches: The powder compound lists its drugs first and names the powder (रजः) last.

questions.q: In verse 66, what is अर्क in the powder compound?
options: The sun, as heat for drying
optionExplain: arka can mean 'sun', but here it is a member of a drug list.
Right: arka stands in a list of drugs: Calotropis procera or gigantea (standard).
No distillation is named; रजः says it is a powder.
No salt is named in this verse.
questions.explain: अर्क = madar (Calotropis, standard); the word also means 'sun'.

questions.q: Which of these does verse 66 state?
options: The powder is kept in urine for a week
kāsāri is identified as a known plant
Broth (yūṣa) is among the things combined
arka is one drug of the powder
snuk milk may be drunk combined with kāsāri juice
optionExplain: No: that is said in line 05.02.121, the next verse.
No: kāsāri is unidentified.
Right: यूष ... आद्यैः.
Right: ...अर्क... रजः.
Right: कासारिरस ... युक्तं स्नुक्पयः.
questions.explain: Snuk milk with kāsāri juice, broth and the like; then a powder that includes arka.

questions.q: Like आद्यैः + युक्तम् → आद्यैर्युक्तम्, which is the joined form of देवैः + युक्तः (invented)?
optionExplain: The visarga is not dropped after ऐ; it becomes र्.
ः becomes स् only before त / थ (or स).
Right: After ऐ, visarga before a voiced sound (य) becomes र्: देवैर्युक्तः.
ओ comes from अः, not from ऐः.
questions.explain: आद्यैर्युक्तम्, देवैर्युक्तः: ऐः + voiced → ऐर्.
questions.rule: ऐः before a voiced sound → ऐर्.
questions.teaches: A visarga after ऐ becomes र् before a voiced sound: आद्यैः + युक्तम् → आद्यैर्युक्तम्, देवैः + युक्तः → देवैर्युक्तः.

questions.q: By verse 67, where is the powder kept at night?
optionExplain: No honey is named in this verse.
No ghee is named in this verse.
Jaggery water belongs to verse 65.
Right: रात्रौ मूत्रे = at night, in urine.
questions.explain: रात्रौ = at night (loc.); मूत्रे = in urine (loc.).

questions.q: Match each word of verse 67 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Night and day, then keeping, then the garland or cloth that is sprinkled.
questions.rule: रात्रौ = at night; दिवा = by day; स्थापयेत् = should keep; माल्यम् = garland; वासः = cloth.

questions.q: Put the clear phrases of verse 67 in the text's order.
questions.explain: Night in urine, keeping for seven days, also in snuk milk, then the sprinkled garland or cloth.
questions.rule: रात्रौ मूत्रे · सप्ताहं स्थापयेत् · स्नुक्क्षीरेऽपि · माल्यं वासोऽवचूर्णितम्.
questions.teaches: The steeping comes first; only then (ततः) is the garland or cloth sprinkled.

questions.q: By verse 67, what is sprinkled with the powder?
optionExplain: Right: माल्यं वासोऽवचूर्णितम्: both neuter, both go with अवचूर्णितम्.
The body is not named; the powder goes on the garland or cloth.
No food is named in this verse.
No bed or pillow is named in this verse.
questions.explain: माल्य = garland; वासस् = cloth; अवचूर्णित = sprinkled with powder.

questions.q: Which split of वासोऽवचूर्णितं is right?
optionExplain: अ + अ would give आ: वासावचूर्णितम्.
Right: अः before अ becomes ओ, and the अ is marked ऽ: वासोऽवचूर्णितम्.
There is no word वचूर्णित; the prefix is अव-.
ः before व would give ओ with no ऽ: वासो वचूर्णितम्.
questions.explain: वासस् (n.) = cloth; nom./acc. sg. वासः.

questions.q: Like वासः + अवचूर्णितम् → वासोऽवचूर्णितम्, which is the joined form of रामः + अपि (invented)?
optionExplain: That would be राम + अपि (अ + अ → आ), with no visarga.
The visarga does not stay before a vowel; it turns into ओ.
Right: अः + अ → ओऽ: रामः + अपि → रामोऽपि.
ए comes from a final ए (e.g. a locative), not from अः.
questions.explain: वासोऽवचूर्णितम्, रामोऽपि: अः + अ → ओऽ.
questions.teaches: A final अः before अ becomes ओ and the अ is marked ऽ: वासोऽवचूर्णितम्, रामोऽपि.

questions.q: By verse 68, who is purged by smelling and wearing the sprinkled garland or cloth?
optionExplain: A hard bowel is not named; the verse says मृदु, soft.
Children and the old are named in verse 59, not here.
Belly disease (jaṭhara) is named in line 05.02.138.
Right: मृदुकोष्ठो विरिच्यते = one of soft bowel (koṣṭha) is purged.
questions.explain: मृदुकोष्ठ = one whose bowel is soft, easily purged; विरिच्यते = is purged.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 68 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Smelling and purging in the first line; the fruit to be taken in the second.
questions.rule: आजिघ्रेत् = should smell; मृदुकोष्ठ = soft bowel; विरिच्यते = is purged; फल = fruit; ग्राह्य = to be taken.

questions.q: Put the clear phrases of verse 68 in the text's order.
questions.explain: Smell it; the soft-bowelled one is purged; then the fruit, not too dry, is taken.
questions.rule: आजिघ्रेत् · मृदुकोष्ठो विरिच्यते · नातिशुष्कं फलं ग्राह्यम्.
questions.teaches: The garland recipe ends with its result (purging); the śaṅkhinī recipe begins with choosing the fruit.

questions.q: By verse 68, which śaṅkhinī fruit is to be taken?
options: One that is not too dry
optionExplain: Right: नातिशुष्कं फलं ग्राह्यम् = a fruit not too dry is to be taken.
अतिशुष्क (too dry) is exactly what is ruled out by न.
No roasting is named; embers belong to verse 63.
No soaking of the fruit is named in this verse.
questions.explain: न + अतिशुष्क = not too dry.

questions.q: Which split of मृदुकोष्ठो विरिच्यते is right?
optionExplain: म् would stay as an anusvara: मृदुकोष्ठं विरिच्यते.
Right: अः before a voiced sound (व) becomes ओ: मृदुकोष्ठो विरिच्यते.
ए would stay ए: मृदुकोष्ठे विरिच्यते.
आ would stay आ: मृदुकोष्ठा विरिच्यते.
questions.explain: मृदुकोष्ठः = m. nom. sg., the subject of the passive विरिच्यते.

questions.q: Like न + अतिशुष्कम् → नातिशुष्कम् (not too dry), which is the joined form of न + अतिमात्रम् (invented)?
optionExplain: ए would come from अ + इ, not from अ + अ.
औ comes from अ + ओ or औ, not from अ + अ.
Right: अ + अ → आ: न + अतिमात्रम् → नातिमात्रम्, 'not too much'.
Within a word-group अ and अ do not stand apart; they merge as आ.
questions.explain: नातिशुष्कम्, नातिमात्रम्: न + अति → नाति, 'not too'.
questions.teaches: न + अति- joins as नाति-, 'not too': नातिशुष्कम् 'not too dry', नातिमात्रम् 'not too much'.

questions.q: By verse 69, which part of samalā is taken?
optionExplain: The fruit is that of śaṅkhinī, in line 05.02.124.
No bark is named in this verse.
No leaves are named in this verse.
Right: समलायास्तथा मूलम् = and also the root of samalā.
questions.explain: मूल = root; समलायाः = of samalā (gen.).

questions.q: Match each word of verse 69 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The root is added; the pair is sharp; it is prescribed in a list of disorders.
questions.rule: मूल = root; तीक्ष्ण = sharp; गर = compound poison; श्वयथु = swelling; कल्पयेत् = should prescribe.

questions.q: Put the disorders named after the Kapha-afflictions in verse 69 in the text's order.
questions.explain: Kapha-afflictions, then udara, gara and swelling; आदिषु adds 'and the like'.
questions.teaches: The locative plural -आदिषु closes the list: 'in udara, gara, swelling and the like'.

questions.q: In verse 69, what does ते (those two) refer to?
options: The śaṅkhinī fruit and the samalā root
The garland and the cloth of verse 67
The urine and the snuk milk of verse 67
The arka and the śyāmā of verse 66
optionExplain: Right: Line 05.02.124 names the fruit, this line the root: the pair.
Those are sprinkled with a powder; they are not called sharp.
Those are steeping liquids, not the drugs described here.
Those are members of an earlier powder, not this pair.
questions.explain: ते = n. nom. du.: फलम् (n.) and मूलम् (n.).

questions.q: In which does verse 69 say to prescribe the two drugs?
optionExplain: Right: ...श्वयथु...
Right: ...गर...
No: bhagandara is named in line 05.02.139.
Right: ...उदर...
No: heart disease is named in line 05.02.128.
questions.explain: Kapha-afflictions, udara, gara, swelling and the like.

questions.q: Like समलायाः + तथा → समलायास्तथा, which is the joined form of कन्यायाः + तत्र (invented)?
optionExplain: The visarga drops after आ only before a voiced sound; त is voiceless.
Right: ः before त becomes स्: कन्यायाः + तत्र → कन्यायास्तत्र.
ओ is not produced here; the आ stays.
ः becomes र् only after other vowels before voiced sounds.
questions.explain: समलायास्तथा, कन्यायास्तत्र: ः + त → स्त.
questions.teaches: A visarga before त becomes स्: समलायाः + तथा → समलायास्तथा, कन्यायाः + तत्र → कन्यायास्तत्र.

questions.q: By verse 70, how large is the lump of the two drugs?
optionExplain: A palmful (pāṇitala) is the measure of line 05.02.96.
No añjali is named in this verse.
Right: अक्षमात्रं तयोः पिण्डम् = a lump of the two, an akṣa in measure.
No pala is named in this verse.
questions.explain: अक्ष = a measure, synonym of कर्ष; मात्र = 'in measure'.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 70 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The lump with madirā and salt, applied in heart disease.
questions.rule: पिण्ड = lump; मदिरा = spirit; लवण = salt; हृद्रोग = heart disease; योजयेत् = should apply.

questions.q: Put the phrases of verse 70 in the text's order.
questions.explain: Measure and lump, its vehicle, the heart disease, then the gulma and the verb.
questions.rule: अक्षमात्रं पिण्डम् · मदिरालवणान्वितम् · हृद्रोगे वातकफजे · तद्गुल्मेऽपि योजयेत्.
questions.teaches: The verse gives dose and vehicle first, then the disorders, then the verb योजयेत्.

questions.q: Which heart disease does verse 70 name?
options: One born of all three doṣas
One born of Vāta and Kapha
optionExplain: Pitta is not named in this verse.
Only two doṣas are named: वात and कफ.
Poison (gara) is named in verse 69, not as a cause here.
Right: हृद्रोगे वातकफजे = in heart disease born of Vāta and Kapha.
questions.explain: वातकफज = born (-ज) of Vāta and Kapha.

questions.q: Which split of तद्गुल्मेऽपि is right?
optionExplain: Right: ए before अ stays ए and the अ is marked ऽ: तद्गुल्मेऽपि.
अ + अ would give आ: तद्गुल्मापि.
अः + अ would give ओऽ: तद्गुल्मोऽपि.
There is no word पि; the word is अपि, 'also'.
questions.explain: तद्गुल्मे = loc. sg., 'in its gulma'; अपि = also.

questions.q: Like वातकफज (born of Vāta and Kapha), which invented compound means born of Pitta?
optionExplain: -घ्न means 'destroying': 'destroying Pitta'.
Right: -ज (from √जन्) at the end of a compound means 'born of'.
-हर means 'removing': 'removing Pitta'.
-वत् means 'like' or 'having': not 'born of'.
questions.explain: वातकफज, पित्तज: -ज = born of.
questions.teaches: -ज at the end of a compound means 'born of': वातकफज 'born of Vāta and Kapha', पित्तज 'born of Pitta'.

questions.q: By verse 71, with what is the pressed oil drunk?
optionExplain: Madirā with salt is the vehicle of verse 70.
Jaggery water belongs to verse 65.
Right: हरीतकीकषायेण ... पिबेत् = drink with a decoction of harītakī.
kāsāri juice belongs to verse 66.
questions.explain: हरीतकी = हरड़, Terminalia chebula (standard); कषाय = decoction.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 71 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Powder and paste in portions; the oil pressed out of them.
questions.rule: चूर्ण = powder; भाग = portion; तिल = sesame; कल्क = paste; पीडित = pressed out.

questions.q: Put the phrases of verse 71 in the text's order.
questions.explain: Two portions of śaṅkhinī powder, one of sesame paste, the decoction, then the pressed oil drunk.
questions.rule: शङ्खिनीचूर्णभागौ द्वौ · तिलकल्कस्य चापरः · हरीतकीकषायेण · तत्तैलं पीडितं पिबेत्.
questions.teaches: The ingredients and their proportion come first, the drinking of the oil last.

questions.q: By verse 71, what is the one other portion (अपरः) made of?
optionExplain: śaṅkhinī powder makes the two portions (भागौ द्वौ).
The harītakī decoction is the drink it is taken with.
samalā root belongs to verses 69-70.
Right: तिलकल्कस्य चापरः = and one more (portion) of sesame paste.
questions.explain: द्वौ भागौ = two portions (śaṅkhinī); अपरः = one other (tila).

questions.q: By verse 71, how is the oil obtained?
options: It is pressed out of the mixture
It is cooked with the ten roots
It is bought as plain sesame oil
It is drawn off a fermented drink
optionExplain: Right: तत्तैलं पीडितम् = the oil of that, pressed out.
No cooking and no daśamūla are named here.
The oil is that of the mixture (तत्), not oil from elsewhere.
No fermentation is named in this verse.
questions.explain: पीडित = pressed, squeezed (√पीड्).

questions.q: Like च + अपरः → चापरः, which is the joined form of च + अत्र (invented)?
optionExplain: ए would come from अ + इ.
Right: अ + अ → आ: च + अत्र → चात्र.
ओ would come from अ + उ.
Within a phrase अ and अ do not stand apart; they merge as आ.
questions.explain: चापरः, चात्र: अ + अ → आ.
questions.teaches: Two short अ sounds merge into आ: च + अपरः → चापरः, च + अत्र → चात्र.

questions.q: Verse 72 says this procedure holds also for which of these?
optionExplain: harītakī was the decoction of verse 71, not in this list.
dantī is named in the second line, for its root.
Right: ...करञ्जेषु ... विधिः = this procedure also in karañja.
arka belongs to the powder of verse 66.
questions.explain: करञ्ज = Pongamia pinnata, pongam tree (standard).
questions.rule: अतसी · सर्षप · एरण्ड · करञ्ज → अयं विधिः.
questions.section: दन्ती-द्रवन्ती: गुण, घृत, तैल और लेह

questions.q: Match each clear word of verse 72 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Two of the plants of the first line, then the words that describe the root.
questions.rule: अतसी = flax; करञ्ज = pongam; विधि = procedure; स्थिर = firm; स्थूल = thick.
questions.section: दन्ती-द्रवन्ती: गुण, घृत, तैल और लेह

questions.q: Put the words of the second line of verse 72 in their order.
questions.explain: Firm and thick, the root, born of dantī and dravantī.
questions.teaches: The second line describes the root first (firm, thick) and names its source last.
questions.section: दन्ती-द्रवन्ती: गुण, घृत, तैल और लेह

questions.q: By verse 72, what should the dantī-dravantī root be like?
optionExplain: The verse says स्थिर (firm) and स्थूल (thick), the opposite.
Neither dryness nor hollowness is named here.
Length is not named; स्थूल means thick.
Right: स्थिरस्थूलम् = firm and thick.
questions.explain: स्थिर = firm; स्थूल = thick.
questions.section: दन्ती-द्रवन्ती: गुण, घृत, तैल और लेह

questions.q: By verse 72, the new root is born of which plants?
optionExplain: Right: दन्तीद्रवन्तिजम् = born of dantī and dravantī.
Those are the drugs of verses 68-70.
Those are named in verse 65.
Those are the plants the procedure extends to.
questions.explain: दन्ती = Baliospermum montanum (probable); द्रवन्ती = disputed.
questions.section: दन्ती-द्रवन्ती: गुण, घृत, तैल और लेह

questions.q: Like करञ्जेषु (in the karañjas, loc. pl.), which is the locative plural of वृक्ष (tree)?
optionExplain: वृक्षैः is the instrumental plural: 'with trees'.
Right: An अ-stem makes its locative plural in -एषु: करञ्जेषु, वृक्षेषु.
वृक्षाणाम् is the genitive plural: 'of trees'.
वृक्षे is the locative singular: 'in a tree'.
questions.explain: करञ्जेषु, वृक्षेषु: -एषु = in (plural).
questions.teaches: Masculine अ-stems form the locative plural in -एषु: करञ्जेषु 'in the karañjas', वृक्षेषु 'in the trees'.
questions.section: दन्ती-द्रवन्ती: गुण, घृत, तैल और लेह

questions.q: By verse 73, which doṣa does the root provoke?
optionExplain: Pitta is dissolved (विलायनम्), not provoked.
Kapha is dissolved together with Pitta.
Right: प्रकोपि वातस्य = provoking Vāta.
The verse names Vāta as provoked.
questions.explain: प्रकोपिन् = provoking; विलायन = dissolving.
questions.section: दन्ती-द्रवन्ती: गुण, घृत, तैल और लेह

questions.q: Match each word of verse 73 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Colour, speed of action, weight, and the effect on Pitta and Kapha.
questions.rule: आताम्र = slightly coppery; श्याव = dusky; आशुकारि = quick-acting; गुरु = heavy; विलायन = dissolving.
questions.section: दन्ती-द्रवन्ती: गुण, घृत, तैल और लेह

questions.q: Put these qualities of the root in the order of verse 73.
questions.explain: Colour first, then sharp-hot, quick-acting, (vikāṣi), heavy, provoking Vāta.
questions.rule: आताम्रश्यावम् · तीक्ष्णोष्णम् · आशुकारि · (विकाषि) · गुरु · प्रकोपि वातस्य.
questions.teaches: The verse moves from colour to qualities to the action on the doṣas.
questions.section: दन्ती-द्रवन्ती: गुण, घृत, तैल और लेह

questions.q: By verse 73, what does the root do to Pitta and Kapha?
optionExplain: Provoking is said of Vāta only.
No binding is named; विलायन is the opposite.
The root is called उष्ण, hot; no cooling is named.
Right: पित्तश्लेष्मविलायनम् = dissolving (melting) Pitta and Kapha.
questions.explain: विलायन = melting, dissolving.
questions.section: दन्ती-द्रवन्ती: गुण, घृत, तैल और लेह

questions.q: Which qualities does verse 73 give the root?
optionExplain: No: the root is उष्ण, hot.
Right: ...उष्णम्.
Right: तीक्ष्ण...
Right: गुरु.
No: it is आशुकारि, quick-acting.
questions.explain: Sharp, hot, quick-acting, heavy; not cold, not slow.
questions.section: दन्ती-द्रवन्ती: गुण, घृत, तैल और लेह

questions.q: Like तीक्ष्ण + उष्णम् → तीक्ष्णोष्णम्, which is the joined form of शीत + उदकम् (invented)?
optionExplain: Right: अ + उ → ओ: शीत + उदकम् → शीतोदकम्.
औ would come from अ + ओ or औ.
The अ is not lost; अ + उ merge as ओ.
ए would come from अ + इ.
questions.explain: तीक्ष्णोष्णम्, शीतोदकम्: अ + उ → ओ.
questions.teaches: अ before उ merges into ओ: तीक्ष्ण + उष्णम् → तीक्ष्णोष्णम्, शीत + उदकम् → शीतोदकम्.
questions.section: दन्ती-द्रवन्ती: गुण, घृत, तैल और लेह

questions.q: By verse 74, what is the root smeared with?
optionExplain: Neither ghee nor jaggery is named in this verse.
Right: क्षौद्रपिप्पलीलिप्तम् = smeared with honey and pippalī.
Madirā with salt belongs to verse 70.
Snuk milk belongs to verses 64-67.
questions.explain: क्षौद्र = honey; पिप्पली = long pepper, Piper longum (standard); लिप्त = smeared.
questions.section: दन्ती-द्रवन्ती: गुण, घृत, तैल और लेह

questions.q: Match each word of verse 74 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Smearing, the clay and kuśa of the sweating, the sunshine of the drying.
questions.rule: क्षौद्र = honey; पिप्पली = long pepper; लिप्त = smeared; मृत् = clay; आतप = sunshine.
questions.section: दन्ती-द्रवन्ती: गुण, घृत, तैल और लेह

questions.q: Put the steps of verse 74 in the text's order.
items: स्वेदयेन्मृत्कुशांतरे (make sweat between clay and kuśa)
questions.explain: Smearing, then sweating between clay and kuśa, then drying in the sun.
questions.teaches: The root is coated, sweated and dried, in that order.
questions.section: दन्ती-द्रवन्ती: गुण, घृत, तैल और लेह

questions.q: By verse 74, where is the smeared root made to sweat?
optionExplain: Embers belong to verse 63.
Urine as a steeping liquid belongs to verse 67.
Right: स्वेदयेन्मृत्कुशान्तरे = make it sweat within clay and kuśa.
No rice is named in this verse.
questions.explain: मृत् = clay; कुश = kuśa grass (standard); अन्तर = within, between.
questions.section: दन्ती-द्रवन्ती: गुण, घृत, तैल और लेह

questions.q: Which split of स्वेदयेन्मृत् is right?
optionExplain: There is no word अमृत् here; the word is मृत्, clay.
There is no word न्मृत्; the verb is स्वेदयेत्.
स्वेदयेम् is not the verb; the optative is स्वेदयेत्.
Right: त् before a nasal (म) becomes न्: स्वेदयेन्मृत्.
questions.explain: स्वेदयेत् = one should make sweat (caus. opt.); मृत् = clay.
questions.section: दन्ती-द्रवन्ती: गुण, घृत, तैल और लेह

questions.q: Like स्वेदयेत् + मृत् → स्वेदयेन्मृत्, which is the joined form of तत् + मूलम् (invented)?
optionExplain: Right: त् before a nasal becomes न्: तत् + मूलम् → तन्मूलम्.
Within a phrase त् does not stay before म; it becomes न्.
No rule turns त् into स् before म.
त् becomes the dental nasal न्, not म्.
questions.explain: स्वेदयेन्मृत्, तन्मूलम्: त् + nasal → न्.
questions.teaches: A final त् before a nasal usually becomes न्: स्वेदयेत् + मृत् → स्वेदयेन्मृत्, तत् + मूलम् → तन्मूलम्.
questions.section: दन्ती-द्रवन्ती: गुण, घृत, तैल और लेह

questions.q: By verse 75, which of these is one of the drinks taken with the root?
optionExplain: Jaggery water belongs to verse 65.
Right: ...तक्र... = buttermilk, in the list of drinks.
No honey water is named in this verse.
kāsāri juice belongs to verse 66.
questions.explain: तक्र = buttermilk; मस्तु = curd whey; आसव = fermented drink.
questions.section: दन्ती-द्रवन्ती: गुण, घृत, तैल और लेह

questions.q: Match each patient of verse 75 to the disorder named.
questions.explain: Each word in -ई names a person who has the disorder.
questions.rule: गुल्मी · प्रमेही · जठरी · गरी = the one having gulma, prameha, jaṭhara, gara.
questions.section: दन्ती-द्रवन्ती: गुण, घृत, तैल और लेह

questions.q: Put the drinks of verse 75 in the text's order.
questions.explain: mastu, madirā, takra, pīlu juice, āsava; -ऐः closes the compound: 'with'.
questions.teaches: The drinks stand in one compound with the instrumental plural ending -ऐः.
questions.section: दन्ती-द्रवन्ती: गुण, घृत, तैल और लेह

questions.q: In verse 75, what does the ending -ई of गुल्मी and प्रमेही say?
options: The person who has the disorder
optionExplain: The disorder is गुल्म or प्रमेह, without -ई.
No drug is named by -ई; the drugs are the drinks of line 1.
Right: गुल्मिन् = one having gulma; nom. sg. गुल्मी.
-इन् means 'having', not 'freed from'.
questions.explain: -इन् (nom. sg. -ई) = having: गुल्मी, प्रमेही, जठरी, गरी.
questions.section: दन्ती-द्रवन्ती: गुण, घृत, तैल और लेह

questions.q: Which patients does verse 75 name?
optionExplain: Right: गुल्मी.
No: bhagandara is named in line 05.02.139.
Right: गरी.
Right: प्रमेही.
No: the soft bowel belongs to verse 68.
questions.explain: gulmī, pramehī, jaṭharī and garī are named here, after the abhiṣyanna body.
questions.section: दन्ती-द्रवन्ती: गुण, घृत, तैल और लेह

questions.q: Like गुल्म → गुल्मी (one having gulma), which word means one having fever (ज्वर)?
optionExplain: ज्वरा is not the -इन् form; it does not mean 'one having'.
ज्वरम् is the accusative of ज्वर, 'the fever'.
ज्वरेण is the instrumental: 'by fever'.
Right: ज्वर + -इन् → ज्वरिन्, nom. sg. ज्वरी: 'one having fever'.
questions.explain: गुल्मी, ज्वरी: -इन् = having.
questions.teaches: The suffix -इन् (nom. sg. -ई) makes 'one having': गुल्मी, प्रमेही, ज्वरी.
questions.section: दन्ती-द्रवन्ती: गुण, घृत, तैल और लेह

questions.q: By verse 76, the juices of which animals are named?
optionExplain: Right: गोमृगाजरसैः = with the juices of cow (गो), deer (मृग) and goat (अज).
None of these animals is named in this verse.
Only the cow is right; horse and elephant are not named.
Only the goat is right; sheep and hare are not named.
questions.explain: गो = cow; मृग = deer; अज = goat; रस = juice (perhaps meat juice).
questions.section: दन्ती-द्रवन्ती: गुण, घृत, तैल और लेह

questions.q: Match each word of verse 76 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Animals of the juices, a patient, and the cooking with daśamūla.
questions.rule: मृग = deer; अज = goat; भगन्दरी = one with fistula; सिद्ध = cooked; दशमूल = ten roots.
questions.section: दन्ती-द्रवन्ती: गुण, घृत, तैल और लेह

questions.q: Put these phrases of verse 76 in the text's order.
questions.explain: Juices, patients, 'cooked', then the daśamūla juice at the end.
questions.rule: गोमृगाजरसैः · पाण्डुक्रिमिकोष्ठी भगन्दरी · सिद्धम् · ... दशमूलरसेन च.
questions.teaches: The list of patients ends and the cooking (सिद्धम्) begins in the second line.
questions.section: दन्ती-द्रवन्ती: गुण, घृत, तैल और लेह

questions.q: In verse 76, what does क्रिमिकोष्ठी mean?
options: One with worms in the bowel
optionExplain: A soft bowel (मृदुकोष्ठ) belongs to verse 68.
Right: क्रिमि = worm; कोष्ठ = bowel; -ई = having.
Belly disease (जठरी) is named in verse 75.
That is भगन्दरी, the next word.
questions.explain: क्रिमि-कोष्ठ-इन् = having worms in the bowel.
questions.section: दन्ती-द्रवन्ती: गुण, घृत, तैल और लेह

questions.q: By verse 76, with which juice is the preparation also cooked?
optionExplain: dhātrī juice comes in line 05.02.147.
pīlu juice is a drink of verse 75.
Right: दशमूलरसेन च = and with the juice of the daśamūla.
kāsāri juice belongs to verse 66.
questions.explain: दशमूल = the ten roots (a named group, not listed here).
questions.section: दन्ती-द्रवन्ती: गुण, घृत, तैल और लेह

questions.q: Like मृग + अज → मृगाज, which is the joined form of अश्व + अज (invented)?
optionExplain: ए would come from अ + इ.
ओ would come from अ + उ.
The two अ do not reduce to one short अ; they give आ.
Right: अ + अ → आ: अश्व + अज → अश्वाज.
questions.explain: मृगाज, अश्वाज: अ + अ → आ.
questions.teaches: In a compound, अ + अ merge into आ: मृग + अज → मृगाज, अश्व + अज → अश्वाज.
questions.section: दन्ती-द्रवन्ती: गुण, घृत, तैल और लेह

questions.q: By verse 77, which preparation overcomes visarpa and vidradhi?
optionExplain: Right: विसर्पविद्रधि... जयेद् घृतम् = the ghee may overcome visarpa, vidradhi...
The oil (तैलं तु) gets the second list.
mahāsneha belongs to line 05.02.143.
The lick is named in line 05.02.145.
questions.explain: घृत = ghee; विसर्प = spreading skin inflammation (probable); विद्रधि = deep abscess.
questions.rule: घृत → विसर्प, विद्रधि ... · तैल → मेह, अर्श ...
questions.section: दन्ती-द्रवन्ती: गुण, घृत, तैल और लेह

questions.q: Match each disorder of verse 77 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Three from the ghee list, two from the oil list.
questions.rule: विसर्प = spreading skin disease; विद्रधि = abscess; दाह = burning; अर्शस् = piles; विबन्ध = constipation.
questions.section: दन्ती-द्रवन्ती: गुण, घृत, तैल और लेह

questions.q: Put the items the oil overcomes (after gulma) in the order of verse 77.
questions.explain: meha, arśas, vibandha, Kapha, wind; the accusative -आन् closes the compound.
questions.teaches: The oil list moves from disorders to the two doṣas Kapha and wind.
questions.section: दन्ती-द्रवन्ती: गुण, घृत, तैल और लेह

questions.q: In verse 77, which of these does the oil, not the ghee, overcome?
optionExplain: visarpa is in the ghee list.
Right: तैलं तु ... अर्शो... = the oil overcomes piles.
vidradhi is in the ghee list.
Burning closes the ghee list.
questions.explain: तु = but, on the other hand: it separates the oil list from the ghee list.
questions.section: दन्ती-द्रवन्ती: गुण, घृत, तैल और लेह

questions.q: Which does verse 77 put in the ghee list?
optionExplain: No: meha is in the oil list.
No: vibandha is in the oil list.
Right: विसर्प...
Right: ...विद्रधि...
Right: ...दाहान्.
questions.explain: Ghee: visarpa, vidradhi, alajī, kaṣā, burning. Oil: gulma, meha, arśas, vibandha, Kapha, wind.
questions.rule: घृत: विसर्प · विद्रधि · दाह; तैल: मेह · अर्श · विबन्ध.
questions.section: दन्ती-द्रवन्ती: गुण, घृत, तैल और लेह

questions.q: Like दाहान् (the object of जयेत्, acc. pl.), which is the accusative plural of रोग?
optionExplain: रोगाः is the nominative plural, a subject.
रोगैः is the instrumental plural: 'with diseases'.
Right: A masculine अ-stem makes its accusative plural in -आन्: दाहान्, रोगान्.
रोगेषु is the locative plural: 'in diseases'.
questions.explain: जयेत् takes its object in the accusative: दाहान्, रोगान्.
questions.teaches: The object of जयेत् stands in the accusative; a masculine अ-stem's accusative plural ends in -आन्: दाहान्, रोगान्.
questions.section: दन्ती-द्रवन्ती: गुण, घृत, तैल और लेह

questions.q: By verse 78, which preparation overcomes the obstruction of stool, semen and wind?
optionExplain: The ghee overcomes visarpa, vidradhi and the like.
The oil overcomes gulma, meha, piles and the like.
That oil belongs to verse 71 and no use is stated for it.
Right: महास्नेहः शकृच्छुक्रवात... = the great sneha (overcomes)...
questions.explain: महास्नेह = the great sneha (unctuous substance).
questions.section: दन्ती-द्रवन्ती: गुण, घृत, तैल और लेह

questions.q: Match each word of verse 78 to its meaning.
questions.explain: What the mahāsneha overcomes, then what the lick is combined with.
questions.rule: शकृत् = stool; शुक्र = semen; व्यथा = pain; गुड = jaggery; क्षौद्र = honey.
questions.section: दन्ती-द्रवन्ती: गुण, घृत, तैल और लेह

questions.q: Put the members of गुडक्षौद्रघृतान्वितः (verse 78) in their order.
questions.explain: Jaggery, honey, ghee, then -अन्वित, 'combined with'.
questions.teaches: -अन्वित at the end of a compound means 'combined with' the members before it.
questions.section: दन्ती-द्रवन्ती: गुण, घृत, तैल और लेह

questions.q: By verse 78, in whose juice is the next preparation made?
optionExplain: Right: दन्त्या रसे वा भृङ्ग्याश्च = in the juice of dantī, or of bhṛṅgī.
dhātrī comes in line 05.02.147; harītakī in verse 71.
kāsāri belongs to verse 66, pīlu to verse 75.
Those belong to the powder of verse 66 and to verse 69.
questions.explain: दन्ती = Baliospermum montanum (probable); भृङ्गी = disputed.
questions.section: दन्ती-द्रवन्ती: गुण, घृत, तैल और लेह

questions.q: Which split of दन्त्या रसे is right?
optionExplain: म् would stay as an anusvara: दन्त्यां रसे.
Right: आः before a voiced sound (र) drops its visarga: दन्त्या रसे.
अः before र would give ओ: दन्त्यो रसे.
आ + अ would merge into आ in one word: दन्त्यारसे.
questions.explain: दन्त्याः = gen. sg. of दन्ती, 'of dantī'; रसे = in the juice.
questions.section: दन्ती-द्रवन्ती: गुण, घृत, तैल और लेह

questions.q: Like दन्त्याः + रसे → दन्त्या रसे, which is the joined form of कन्याः + गच्छन्ति (invented)?
optionExplain: ओ comes from अः, not from आः.
र् comes after vowels other than अ / आ.
Right: आः before a voiced sound loses its visarga: कन्या गच्छन्ति.
ः becomes स् only before त / थ (or स).
questions.explain: दन्त्या रसे, कन्या गच्छन्ति: आः + voiced → आ.
questions.teaches: After आ a visarga drops before a voiced sound: दन्त्याः + रसे → दन्त्या रसे, कन्याः + गच्छन्ति → कन्या गच्छन्ति.
questions.section: दन्ती-द्रवन्ती: गुण, घृत, तैल और लेह

questions.q: By verse 79, for what purpose is the lick cooked?
optionExplain: Vomiting (vamana) is not named in this verse.
No nourishing is named in this verse.
No massage is named; a लेह is licked.
Right: सिद्धो विरेकार्थे = cooked for the purpose of purging (vireka).
questions.explain: विरेक = purging (virecana); अर्थे = for the purpose of.
questions.section: दन्ती-द्रवन्ती: गुण, घृत, तैल और लेह

questions.q: Match each word of verse 79 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The lick and what it dispels, then the fever of the second line.
questions.rule: लेह = lick; दाह = burning; सन्ताप = heat; मेह = urinary disorders; ज्वर = fever.
questions.section: दन्ती-द्रवन्ती: गुण, घृत, तैल और लेह

questions.q: Put what the lick dispels in the order of verse 79.
questions.explain: Burning, heat, meha; -नुत् closes the compound: 'dispelling'.
questions.teaches: -नुत् at the end of a compound names what is driven away.
questions.section: दन्ती-द्रवन्ती: गुण, घृत, तैल और लेह

questions.q: By verse 79, with which drug is the same lick made for thirst and fever?
optionExplain: Right: स एवाजगन्धया = that very (lick) with ajagandhā.
dhātrī juice comes in line 05.02.147, for another preparation.
pippalī was smeared on the root in verse 74.
samalā root belongs to verse 69.
questions.explain: अजगन्धा = a drug name, lit. 'goat-smell' (disputed).
questions.section: दन्ती-द्रवन्ती: गुण, घृत, तैल और लेह

questions.q: What does -नुत् in दाहसंतापमेहनुत् mean?
optionExplain: 'Causing' would be -कर or -कृत्.
Right: नुद् = to push away: -नुत् = dispelling burning, heat and meha.
'Born of' is -ज, as in वातकफज.
'Having' is -इन्, as in गुल्मी.
questions.explain: -नुत् (from √नुद्) = pushing away, dispelling.
questions.rule: X-नुत् = X को दूर करने वाला.
questions.section: दन्ती-द्रवन्ती: गुण, घृत, तैल और लेह

questions.q: Like दाहसन्तापमेहनुत्, which invented compound means dispelling fever?
optionExplain: -ज means 'born of': 'born of fever'.
-ई (-इन्) means 'having': 'one having fever'.
Right: -नुत् = dispelling: ज्वरनुत् 'dispelling fever'.
-कर means 'causing': 'causing fever'.
questions.explain: दाहसन्तापमेहनुत्, ज्वरनुत्: -नुत् = dispelling.
questions.teaches: -नुत् at the end of a compound means 'dispelling': दाहसन्तापमेहनुत्, ज्वरनुत्.
questions.section: दन्ती-द्रवन्ती: गुण, घृत, तैल और लेह

questions.q: In verse 80, in which juice are the roots of dantī and dravantī cooked?
optionExplain: bhṛṅgī juice belongs to the leha of line 05.02.144, not to this verse.
pathyā is named in line 05.02.150 for its own leha, not as the cooking juice here.
No lemon is named in this verse.
Right: पचेद्धात्रीरसे = one should cook in the juice of dhātrī (āmalakī, standard).
questions.explain: धात्री = āmalakī, Phyllanthus emblica, Indian gooseberry (standard).
questions.section: दन्ती के लेह, चूर्ण और मोदक

questions.q: Match each word of verse 80 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Roots are cooked in dhātrī juice; the preparation is then employed in oil or in ghee.
questions.rule: मूल = root; पचेत् = should cook; धात्री = āmalakī; तैल = oil; घृत = ghee.
questions.section: दन्ती के लेह, चूर्ण और मोदक

questions.q: Put the words of the first line of verse 80 in their order.
questions.explain: Of dantī and dravantī, the roots, one should cook, in dhātrī juice, then.
questions.teaches: The owners (dantī and dravantī, genitive dual) come first, then the thing taken (roots), then the cooking.
questions.section: दन्ती के लेह, चूर्ण और मोदक

questions.q: Which split of दंतीद्रवंत्योर्मूलानि is right?
optionExplain: Right: -ओः before a voiced sound keeps r: दन्तीद्रवन्त्योः + मूलानि → -त्योर्मूलानि.
-अः before म would become -ओ (…न्त्यो मूलानि); no र् would appear.
-औ before a consonant stays औ; it gives no र्.
There is no word ओर्मूलानि; the ending -योः belongs to the compound.
questions.explain: दन्तीद्रवन्त्योः = of dantī and dravantī (gen. du.); मूलानि = roots.
questions.section: दन्ती के लेह, चूर्ण और मोदक

questions.q: Which of these does verse 80 state?
options: The roots are first dried in the sun
The roots of dantī and dravantī are taken
Oil and ghee are both named, joined by athavā (or)
They are cooked in dhātrī juice
optionExplain: No: no drying is named in this verse.
Right: दन्तीद्रवन्त्योर्मूलानि.
Right: तैले घृतेऽथवा, in oil or in ghee.
Right: पचेद्धात्रीरसे.
No: dravantī is disputed on the card.
questions.explain: Roots of dantī and dravantī, cooked in dhātrī juice; oil or ghee is named.
questions.section: दन्ती के लेह, चूर्ण और मोदक

questions.q: Like दन्तीद्रवन्त्योः (of dantī and dravantī, gen. du. of -ई stems), which form of नदी means of the two rivers?
optionExplain: नदीनाम् is the genitive plural: 'of the rivers'.
Right: -ई stem genitive dual: नदी → नद्योः, like दन्तीद्रवन्त्योः.
नद्याः is genitive/ablative singular: 'of a river'.
नदीभ्याम् is dual, but instrumental, dative or ablative.
questions.explain: दन्तीद्रवन्त्योः, नद्योः: -ई stems take -योः in the genitive dual.
questions.teaches: A feminine -ई stem forms its genitive dual in -योः: दन्ती + द्रवन्ती → दन्तीद्रवन्त्योः, नदी → नद्योः.
questions.section: दन्ती के लेह, चूर्ण और मोदक

questions.q: In verse 81, what is the leha joined with the kalka of śyāmā and the others?
optionExplain: No emetic (vamana) is named in this verse.
A leha is licked, not rubbed on; no skin use is named.
Right: लेहः सिद्धं विरेचनम् = the leha is an accomplished purgative.
Soups (yūṣa) come in line 05.02.153, not here.
questions.explain: लेह = a preparation to be licked; विरेचन = purgative; सिद्ध = accomplished.
questions.section: दन्ती के लेह, चूर्ण और मोदक

questions.q: Match each word of verse 81 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The first line names the śyāmā leha as a purgative; the second the lehas of pathyā, akṣa and daśamūla.
questions.rule: लेह = lick; कल्क = paste; विरेचन = purgative; पथ्या = harītakī; अक्ष = vibhītaka.
questions.section: दन्ती के लेह, चूर्ण और मोदक

questions.q: Put the drugs whose lehas are made 'likewise' in verse 81 in the text's order.
questions.explain: पथ्याक्षदशमूलानाम्: pathyā, then akṣa, then the ten roots.
questions.teaches: One dvandva compound in the genitive plural, पथ्याक्षदशमूलानाम्, names the three sources of the further lehas.
questions.section: दन्ती के लेह, चूर्ण और मोदक

questions.q: Which split of श्यामादिकल्कयुक्तोऽयं is right?
optionExplain: -ए + अ gives -एऽ (युक्तेऽयम्), not -ओऽ.
-आः before a vowel drops the visarga (युक्ता अयम्); no ओ.
-म् + अ joins as -मयम् (युक्तमयम्), not -ओऽयम्.
Right: -अः + अ → -ओऽ: युक्तः + अयम् → युक्तोऽयम्.
questions.explain: युक्तः (m. nom. sg.) agrees with लेहः; अयम् = this.
questions.section: दन्ती के लेह, चूर्ण और मोदक

questions.q: In verse 81, with what are the lehas of pathyā, akṣa and daśamūla made?
optionExplain: Right: पृथग्रसैः = with separate juices (pṛthak = separately).
पृथक् says separately, not one juice for all.
No urine is named in this verse.
Neither honey nor jaggery is named in this verse.
questions.explain: तद्वत् = likewise; लेहाः = lehas; पृथग्रसैः = with separate juices.
questions.section: दन्ती के लेह, चूर्ण और मोदक

questions.q: Like पथ्या + अक्ष → पथ्याक्ष, which is the joined form of रुद्र + अक्ष?
optionExplain: ए comes from अ + इ, not from अ + अ.
Right: अ + अ → आ (like vowels lengthen): रुद्र + अक्ष → रुद्राक्ष.
औ comes from अ + ओ/औ, not from अ + अ.
The two अ do not vanish; they merge into a long आ.
questions.explain: पथ्याक्ष (आ + अ → आ), रुद्राक्ष (अ + अ → आ).
questions.teaches: Two like a-vowels merge into one long आ: पथ्या + अक्ष → पथ्याक्ष, रुद्र + अक्ष → रुद्राक्ष.
questions.section: दन्ती के लेह, चूर्ण और मोदक

questions.q: In verse 82, with what is the powder steeped (भावितम्)?
optionExplain: No urine is named in this verse.
Neither honey nor ghee is named in this verse.
Right: तद्रसेनैव भावितम् = steeped with its (own) juice alone.
daśamūla is named in line 05.02.150, not as a steeping liquid here.
questions.explain: तद्रसेन = with its juice; एव = alone; भावित = steeped.
questions.section: दन्ती के लेह, चूर्ण और मोदक

questions.q: Match each word of verse 82 to its meaning.
questions.explain: A steeped powder, beneficial in obstruction and in Vāta gulma.
questions.rule: चूर्ण = powder; भावित = steeped; विबन्ध = constipation; गुल्म = abdominal lump; हित = beneficial.
questions.section: दन्ती के लेह, चूर्ण और मोदक

questions.q: Put these clear words of the second line of verse 82 in their order.
questions.explain: In obstruction, (…), risen from Vāta, in gulma, and joined with sour, beneficial.
questions.teaches: The places of use come first in the locative; 'joined with sour' and 'beneficial' close the line.
questions.section: दन्ती के लेह, चूर्ण और मोदक

questions.q: In verse 82, which gulma is the powder beneficial in?
optionExplain: Pitta is not named in this verse.
Kapha is not named in this verse.
Blood (rakta) is not named in this verse.
Right: वातोत्थे गुल्मे = in gulma risen from Vāta.
questions.explain: वात + उत्थ = risen from Vāta.
questions.section: दन्ती के लेह, चूर्ण और मोदक

questions.q: In verse 82, what is the powder joined with when it is beneficial?
optionExplain: Right: चाम्लयुतं हितम् = and, joined with sour, beneficial.
No sweet is named; the verse says अम्ल.
No bitter is named; the verse says अम्ल.
No pungent is named; the verse says अम्ल.
questions.explain: अम्ल = sour; युत = joined with.
questions.section: दन्ती के लेह, चूर्ण और मोदक

questions.q: Like वात + उत्थ → वातोत्थ (risen from Vāta), which is the joined form of कफ + उत्थ?
optionExplain: अ + उ gives ओ, not a long ऊ.
Right: अ + उ → ओ: कफ + उत्थ → कफोत्थ.
औ comes from अ + ओ/औ, not from अ + उ.
व् arises from उ before a vowel, not from अ + उ.
questions.explain: वातोत्थ, कफोत्थ: अ + उ → ओ.
questions.teaches: अ before उ merges into ओ: वात + उत्थ → वातोत्थ, कफ + उत्थ → कफोत्थ.
questions.section: दन्ती के लेह, चूर्ण और मोदक

questions.q: In verse 83, what should be prepared with the roots cooked with mudga?
optionExplain: Modakas come in line 05.02.162, not here.
No oil is prepared in this verse.
Right: यूषादींश्च प्रकल्पयेत् = and one should prepare soups and the like.
No ariṣṭa is named in this verse.
questions.explain: यूष = soup; मुद्ग = green gram (Vigna radiata, standard); प्रकल्पयेत् = should prepare.
questions.section: दन्ती के लेह, चूर्ण और मोदक

questions.q: Put the five drugs of the second line of verse 83 in the text's order.
questions.explain: दन्तीद्रवन्तीमरिचस्वर्णक्षीरीयवानकम्: dantī, dravantī, marica, svarṇakṣīrī, yavānaka.
questions.section: दन्ती के लेह, चूर्ण और मोदक

questions.q: Match each name in verse 83 to its meaning on the card.
questions.explain: mudga and yūṣa from the first line; marica, svarṇakṣīrī and yavānaka from the drug list.
questions.rule: मुद्ग = green gram; मरिच = black pepper; स्वर्णक्षीरी = Argemone mexicana (probable); यवानक = ajwain (probable); यूष = soup.
questions.teaches: Names in this list carry the data's confidence: marica standard, svarṇakṣīrī and yavānaka probable.
questions.section: दन्ती के लेह, चूर्ण और मोदक

questions.q: Which drug named in verse 83 has a disputed identity?
optionExplain: marica = black pepper, Piper nigrum (standard).
mudga = green gram, Vigna radiata (standard).
yavānaka = ajwain, Trachyspermum ammi (probable, not disputed).
Right: dravantī is disputed: several purgative plants are proposed, none fixed.
questions.explain: standard: dantī, marica, mudga · probable: svarṇakṣīrī, yavānaka · disputed: dravantī.
questions.section: दन्ती के लेह, चूर्ण और मोदक

questions.q: Which split of मुद्गादिसिद्धैस्तन्मूलैः is right?
optionExplain: Right: -ऐः before त becomes -ऐस्: सिद्धैः + तन्मूलैः → सिद्धैस्तन्मूलैः.
-आः before त would give -आस्त (सिद्धास्तन्), not -ऐस्त.
There is no word स्तन्मूलैः; the स् is the visarga of सिद्धैः.
The स् is not doubled into the next word; it replaces the visarga.
questions.explain: सिद्धैः (inst. pl.) = cooked; तन्मूलैः = with their roots.
questions.section: दन्ती के लेह, चूर्ण और मोदक

questions.q: Like तत् + मूलैः → तन्मूलैः, which is the joined form of तत् + मात्रा (invented)?
optionExplain: त् is a dental; it becomes the dental nasal न्, not म्.
Right: त् before a nasal (म) becomes the nasal न्: तत् + मात्रा → तन्मात्रा.
त् does not become स् before म.
No vowel is inserted; त् joins directly as न्.
questions.explain: तन्मूलैः, तन्मात्रा: त् + nasal → न् + nasal.
questions.teaches: A final त् before a nasal consonant is normally nasalised to न्: तत् + मूलैः → तन्मूलैः, तत् + मात्रा → तन्मात्रा.
questions.section: दन्ती के लेह, चूर्ण और मोदक

questions.q: In verse 84, with what is the urine-steeped powder drunk?
optionExplain: No honey is named in this verse.
No milk is named in this verse.
Right: मूत्रभावितमाज्येन पिबेत् = steeped in urine, one should drink it with ghee.
Whey belongs to line 05.02.97, not to this verse.
questions.explain: आज्य = ghee; पिबेत् = one should drink.
questions.section: दन्ती के लेह, चूर्ण और मोदक

questions.q: Match each word of verse 84 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Drugs powdered, steeped in urine, drunk with ghee; satiation after digestion.
questions.rule: शुण्ठी = dried ginger; चूर्णित = powdered; मूत्रभावित = steeped in urine; आज्य = ghee; तर्पण = satiation.
questions.section: दन्ती के लेह, चूर्ण और मोदक

questions.q: Put the steps of verse 84 in the text's order.
questions.explain: Powdered, steeped in urine, drunk with ghee, and satiation once it is digested.
questions.rule: चूर्णितम् · मूत्रभावितम् · आज्येन पिबेत् · जीर्णे तर्पणम्.
questions.teaches: The verse runs from making the powder to the satiation that follows its digestion.
questions.section: दन्ती के लेह, चूर्ण और मोदक

questions.q: In verse 84, what does the verse name after जीर्णे (when digested)?
optionExplain: No vomiting is named in this verse.
No second dose is named in this verse.
No fasting is named; the verse says तर्पण, satiation.
Right: जीर्णे च तर्पणम् = and when digested, satiation.
questions.explain: जीर्णे = when digested (loc. abs.); तर्पण = satiation.
questions.section: दन्ती के लेह, चूर्ण और मोदक

questions.q: Which of these does verse 84 state?
options: The powder is steeped in urine
śuṇṭhī is one of the drugs
optionExplain: No: agnika is only probably citraka.
No: the animal is not stated.
Right: चूर्णितम्.
Right: मूत्रभावितम्.
Right: सशुण्ठ्यग्निकपृथ्वीकम्, with śuṇṭhī.
questions.explain: With śuṇṭhī, agnika and pṛthvīka, powdered, steeped in urine, drunk with ghee.
questions.rule: शुण्ठी · अग्निक · पृथ्वीक → चूर्णित → मूत्रभावित → आज्येन.
questions.section: दन्ती के लेह, चूर्ण और मोदक

questions.q: Like पिबेत् (one should drink, optative of √पा), which optative of √पठ् (read) means one should read?
optionExplain: Right: The optative in -एत् says 'one should': पिबेत्, पठेत्.
पठति is the present: 'reads'.
पठितम् is the past participle: 'read'.
पठित्वा is the absolutive: 'having read'.
questions.explain: पिबेत्, पठेत्: optative third singular in -एत्.
questions.teaches: The optative third singular ends in -एत् and gives the recipe's 'one should': पिबेत्, पठेत्.
questions.section: दन्ती के लेह, चूर्ण और मोदक

questions.q: In verse 85, for whom is the preparation said to be beneficial?
options: A child and an old person
optionExplain: The verse says बाल and वृद्ध, and सर्वरोगेषु, not 'only'.
Right: बाले वृद्धे च तद्धितम् = in a child and an old person that is beneficial.
No pregnant woman is named in this verse.
No hard koṣṭha is named in this verse.
questions.explain: बाल = child; वृद्ध = old person; सर्वदा = always.
questions.rule: सर्वदा · सर्वरोगेषु · बाले वृद्धे च → हितम्.
questions.section: दन्ती के लेह, चूर्ण और मोदक

questions.q: Put the first four disorders of the second line of verse 85 in their order.
questions.explain: दुर्भुक्त-अजीर्ण-पार्श्वार्ति-गुल्म-प्लीह-उदरेषु: ill-eating, indigestion, side pain, gulma, then spleen and belly.
questions.section: दन्ती के लेह, चूर्ण और मोदक

questions.q: Match each word of verse 85 to its meaning.
questions.explain: सर्वदा opens the verse; the rest come from the disorder compound.
questions.rule: सर्वदा = always; दुर्भुक्त = ill-eating; अजीर्ण = indigestion; पार्श्व + आर्ति = side + pain; गुल्म = abdominal lump.
questions.teaches: पार्श्वार्ति = पार्श्व (side) + आर्ति (pain): अ + आ → आ inside the compound.
questions.section: दन्ती के लेह, चूर्ण और मोदक

questions.q: In verse 85, what does अजीर्ण mean?
options: Old age (worn out by the years)
Freshly cooked and still warm food
optionExplain: jīrṇa can mean 'old', but beside दुर्भुक्त it is 'digested'; a- negates it.
Nothing about fresh food is said; ajīrṇa is a disorder in the list.
Right: अ + जीर्ण: jīrṇa here is 'digested', so ajīrṇa = undigested, indigestion.
Old ghee is not named; ajīrṇa stands among disorders.
questions.explain: जीर्ण = digested (or old); अजीर्ण = undigested, indigestion (in this list).
questions.section: दन्ती के लेह, चूर्ण और मोदक

questions.q: Which of these does verse 85 name?
optionExplain: Right: बाले.
Right: वृद्धे.
No: kuṣṭha is not named in this verse.
No: fever is named in line 05.02.146, not here.
Right: in the disorder compound.
questions.explain: Always, in all ailments, for child and old; ill-eating, indigestion, side pain, gulma, spleen, belly.
questions.rule: बाल · वृद्ध · दुर्भुक्त · अजीर्ण · पार्श्वार्ति · गुल्म · प्लीहा · उदर.
questions.section: दन्ती के लेह, चूर्ण और मोदक

questions.q: Like सर्वदा (सर्व + the time suffix -दा), which word built on तत् means then, at that time?
optionExplain: -त्र makes a word of place: तत्र = there.
-था makes a word of manner: तथा = so, thus.
तस्मात् is ablative: 'from that, therefore'.
Right: -दा makes a word of time: सर्व → सर्वदा, तत् → तदा.
questions.explain: सर्वदा, तदा: the suffix -दा says 'at the time'.
questions.teaches: The suffix -दा forms adverbs of time: सर्वदा 'always', तदा 'then', यदा 'when'.
questions.section: दन्ती के लेह, चूर्ण और मोदक

questions.q: In verse 86, how many pathyā go with the jaggery?
optionExplain: Right: पथ्या विंशतिः स्यात् = there should be twenty pathyā.
Eight is the number of palas of jaggery.
Ten belongs to pippalī and trivṛt in line 05.02.161.
Two karṣas belong to dantī and citraka in line 05.02.161.
questions.explain: विंशतिः = twenty; पथ्या = harītakī.
questions.section: दन्ती के लेह, चूर्ण और मोदक

questions.q: Match each word of verse 86 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Two disorders and the verb of the first line; jaggery and pathyā from the recipe.
questions.rule: गण्डमाला = scrofula (probable); पाण्डुरोग = anaemia (probable); शस्यते = is commended; गुड = jaggery; पथ्या = harītakī.
questions.section: दन्ती के लेह, चूर्ण और मोदक

questions.q: Put these words of the second line of verse 86 in their order.
questions.explain: Of jaggery, in eight palas, pathyā, twenty.
questions.rule: गुडस्य · अष्टपले · पथ्या · विंशतिः · (स्यात् पलं पलम्).
questions.teaches: The measure of jaggery (eight palas) is named before the number of pathyā (twenty).
questions.section: दन्ती के लेह, चूर्ण और मोदक

questions.q: In verse 86, what is the measure of jaggery?
optionExplain: Twenty is the number of pathyā, not palas of jaggery.
Right: गुडस्याष्टपले = in eight palas of jaggery.
The measure printed is pala, not karṣa.
No prastha is named in this verse.
questions.explain: अष्ट = eight; पल = a measure of weight (not converted).
questions.section: दन्ती के लेह, चूर्ण और मोदक

questions.q: In verse 86, which word says the preparation 'is commended'?
optionExplain: हितम् (beneficial) is the word of line 05.02.157, not of this verse.
पिबेत् (should drink) is not in this verse.
Right: शस्यते = is commended (passive of √शंस्).
स्यात् (should be) goes with the twenty pathyā.
questions.explain: शस्यते = is commended; स्यात् = should be.
questions.section: दन्ती के लेह, चूर्ण और मोदक

questions.q: Like शस्यते (is commended, passive of √शंस्), which passive of √नी (lead) means is led?
optionExplain: नयति is active present: 'leads'.
नीतम् is the past participle: 'led'.
नेष्यति is the future: 'will lead'.
Right: The passive takes -यते: √नी → नीयते 'is led', like शस्यते.
questions.explain: शस्यते, नीयते: present passive in -यते.
questions.rule: Passive present = root + -यते (some roots change, e.g. √वच् → उच्यते).
questions.teaches: The present passive is built with -यते: √शंस् → शस्यते 'is commended', √नी → नीयते 'is led'.
questions.section: दन्ती के लेह, चूर्ण और मोदक

questions.q: In verse 87, which pair of drugs is given 'two karṣas' (कर्षौ)?
optionExplain: Right: दन्तीचित्रकयोः कर्षौ = of dantī and citraka, two karṣas.
pippalī and trivṛt get ten (दश).
pathyā and jaggery belong to line 05.02.160.
śuṇṭhī and agnika belong to line 05.02.155.
questions.explain: कर्षौ = two karṣas (dual of कर्ष, a measure).
