questions.rule: दन्ती + चित्रक → कर्षौ · पिप्पली + त्रिवृत् → दश.
questions.section: दन्ती के लेह, चूर्ण और मोदक

questions.q: Match each phrase of verse 87 to its meaning.
pairs: two karṣas of dantī and citraka
questions.explain: Two measured pairs, then the balls, then the interval of taking one.
questions.rule: कर्षौ = two karṣas; दश = ten; मोदक = ball; दशमे दशमेऽहनि = every tenth day.
questions.section: दन्ती के लेह, चूर्ण और मोदक

questions.q: Put the four drugs of verse 87 in the text's order.
questions.explain: दन्तीचित्रकयोः, then पिप्पलीत्रिवृतोः.
questions.teaches: Each measure follows a dual dvandva in the genitive: दन्तीचित्रकयोः कर्षौ, पिप्पलीत्रिवृतोर्दश.
questions.section: दन्ती के लेह, चूर्ण और मोदक

questions.q: In verse 87, how often is one modaka to be taken?
optionExplain: No daily dose is named; the verse says दशमे दशमे.
Right: दशमे दशमेऽहनि = on every tenth day; एकम् = one.
No third day is named in this verse.
No pakṣa (fortnight) is named in this verse.
questions.explain: दशम = tenth; repeated दशमे दशमे = every tenth; अहनि = on the day.
questions.section: दन्ती के लेह, चूर्ण और मोदक

questions.q: In verse 87, what is citraka (चित्रक)?
optionExplain: Long pepper is pippalī, the third drug.
Turpeth is trivṛt, the fourth drug.
Right: citraka = leadwort, Plumbago zeylanica (standard).
Dried ginger is śuṇṭhī of line 05.02.155.
questions.explain: चित्रक = चीता (leadwort); पिप्पली = पीपर; त्रिवृत् = निशोथ.
questions.section: दन्ती के लेह, चूर्ण और मोदक

questions.q: Like दशमे दशमेऽहनि (on every tenth day), which phrase means on every fifth day?
optionExplain: Unrepeated, पञ्चमेऽहनि is 'on the fifth day' only, once.
पञ्चभिः अहोभिः = with five days, a span, not a repeat.
A repeated cardinal counts 'five days each', not 'every fifth'.
Right: The ordinal repeated in the locative says 'on every fifth day'.
questions.explain: दशमे दशमे, पञ्चमे पञ्चमे: the repeated ordinal = 'every N-th'.
questions.rule: Ordinal × 2 in loc. + अहनि = every N-th day.
questions.teaches: Repeating an ordinal in the locative gives 'every N-th': दशमे दशमेऽहनि, पञ्चमे पञ्चमेऽहनि.
questions.section: दन्ती के लेह, चूर्ण और मोदक

questions.q: In verse 88, what is drunk after the modakas?
optionExplain: Right: उष्णाम्भोऽनुपिबन् = drinking warm water after.
The verse says उष्ण, warm.
No milk is named in this verse.
No buttermilk (takra) is named in this verse.
questions.explain: उष्ण = warm; अम्भः = water; अनु-पिबन् = drinking after.
questions.section: दन्ती के लेह, चूर्ण और मोदक

questions.q: Match each word of verse 88 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The first line gives the way of eating; the second line the claim.
questions.rule: उष्ण = warm; अम्भः = water; अनुपिबन् = drinking after; विधि = method; निबर्हण = destroying.
questions.section: दन्ती के लेह, चूर्ण और मोदक

questions.q: Put the words of the second line of verse 88 in their order.
questions.explain: These, without avoidances, would be, destroyers of all ailments.
questions.teaches: Two plural predicates (निष्परिहाराः, सर्वव्याधिनिबर्हणाः) describe एते, the modakas.
questions.section: दन्ती के लेह, चूर्ण और मोदक

questions.q: In verse 88, what does निष्परिहाराः say about the modakas?
options: They must never be taken by anyone at all
Nothing need be avoided with them
They need a very strict diet alongside them
They suit only a single disorder
optionExplain: परिहार is avoidance by the patient; the modakas are to be eaten.
Right: निः + परिहार = without avoidance: no restrictions.
That is the opposite: निष्- removes the avoidances.
The same line calls them destroyers of all ailments.
questions.explain: निष्परिहार = without avoidance (restrictions); सर्वव्याधि = all ailments.
questions.section: दन्ती के लेह, चूर्ण और मोदक

questions.q: Verse 88: drinking warm water after, one should ____ (eat) them all by this method. Type it in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: खादेत् = one should eat (optative of √खाद्).
questions.teaches: खादेत् is the verb of the modaka recipe of lines 05.02.161-162.
questions.section: दन्ती के लेह, चूर्ण और मोदक

questions.q: Like उष्णाम्भः + अनुपिबन् → उष्णाम्भोऽनुपिबन्, which is the joined form of रामः + अत्र (invented)?
optionExplain: The visarga before अ does not just vanish here; -अः + अ gives -ओऽ.
-एऽ comes from -ए + अ, not from -अः + अ.
Right: -अः + अ → -ओऽ: रामः + अत्र → रामोऽत्र.
र् replaces visarga after other vowels, not after अ before अ.
questions.explain: उष्णाम्भोऽनुपिबन्, रामोऽत्र: -अः + अ → -ओऽ (the ऽ marks the lost अ).
questions.teaches: Visarga after अ, before अ, gives -ओ and the next अ drops (ऽ): अम्भः + अनु → अम्भोऽनु, रामः + अत्र → रामोऽत्र.
questions.section: दन्ती के लेह, चूर्ण और मोदक

questions.q: In verse 89, which of these is among the disorders the preparation especially helps?
optionExplain: Fever is not named in this verse.
Cough is not named in this verse.
Madness is not named in this verse.
Right: The compound ends with अर्शसाम्: piles (standard).
questions.explain: अर्शस् = haemorrhoids, piles (standard).
questions.section: दन्ती के लेह, चूर्ण और मोदक

questions.q: Put the five disorders of verse 89 in the text's order.
questions.explain: ग्रहणी-पाण्डु-कण्डु-कोठ-अर्शसाम्: one dvandva in the genitive plural.
questions.section: दन्ती के लेह, चूर्ण और मोदक

questions.q: Match each disorder of verse 89 to its meaning on the card.
questions.explain: Five disorders in one compound, each with the data's identification.
questions.rule: ग्रहणी = bowel disorder; पाण्डु = anaemia; कण्डु = itching; कोठ = wheals; अर्शस् = piles.
questions.teaches: arśas = piles is standard; pāṇḍu = anaemia and koṭha = wheals are probable equivalents.
questions.section: दन्ती के लेह, चूर्ण और मोदक

questions.q: Which split of विशेषाद्ग्रहणी is right?
optionExplain: Right: -त् before a voiced sound (ग) becomes -द्: विशेषात् + ग्रहणी → विशेषाद्ग्रहणी.
-अः before ग would give -ओ (विशेषो ग्रहणी), not -आद्.
-आः before a voiced sound drops the visarga (विशेषा ग्रहणी); no द्.
There is no word द्ग्रहणी; the द् belongs to विशेषात्.
questions.explain: विशेषात् = especially (ind.); ग्रहणी opens the disorder compound.
questions.section: दन्ती के लेह, चूर्ण और मोदक

questions.q: Which of these disorders does verse 89 name?
optionExplain: Right: the third member.
No: the spleen is named in line 05.02.158, not here.
Right: the fourth member.
No: wasting is named in line 05.02.168, not here.
Right: the first member.
questions.explain: ग्रहणी, पाण्डु, कण्डु, कोठ, अर्शस्: these five only.
questions.rule: विशेषात् · ग्रहणी · पाण्डु · कण्डु · कोठ · अर्शस् → हिताः.
questions.section: दन्ती के लेह, चूर्ण और मोदक

questions.q: Like विशेषात् + ग्रहणी → विशेषाद्ग्रहणी, which is the joined form of तस्मात् + गच्छति (invented)?
optionExplain: Unvoiced त् does not stay before a voiced ग.
Right: -त् before the voiced ग becomes -द्: तस्माद्गच्छति.
त् becomes न् only before a nasal, not before ग.
त् does not copy the next consonant before ग.
questions.explain: विशेषाद्ग्रहणी, तस्माद्गच्छति: -त् + voiced → -द्.
questions.teaches: A final त् becomes द् before a voiced consonant: विशेषात् + ग्रहणी → विशेषाद्ग्रहणी, तस्मात् + गच्छति → तस्माद्गच्छति.
questions.section: दन्ती के लेह, चूर्ण और मोदक

questions.q: By verse 90, by whose method is harītakī to be prepared?
optionExplain: dantī is not named in this verse; the verse says त्रिवृत्.
snuhī is not named in this verse; the verse says त्रिवृत्.
Right: त्रिवृद्विधानेन = by the method of trivṛt.
tilvaka is not named in this verse; the verse says त्रिवृत्.
questions.explain: त्रिवृत्-विधान = the method (procedure) of trivṛt; अपि = also.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 90 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The first line says how harītakī is prepared; the second says what it removes.
questions.rule: हरीतकी = chebulic myrobalan; विधान = method; उपकल्पयेत् = should prepare; विशेषात् = especially; अपहा = removing.

questions.q: Put the disorders that verse 90's harītakī removes in the text's order.
questions.explain: grahaṇī, pāṇḍu, śoṣa, moha, udara; the compound ends in -अपहाम्, 'removing'.
questions.teaches: One compound lists five disorders and closes with -अपहा, 'removing' them.

questions.q: Which split of विधानेनोपकल्पयेत् is right?
optionExplain: अ + अ would give आ: विधानेनापकल्पयेत्.
There is no word पकल्पयेत्; the ओ comes from अ + उ.
विधानेनः is not a form; the instrumental is विधानेन.
Right: अ + उ → ओ: विधानेन + उपकल्पयेत् → विधानेनोपकल्पयेत्.
questions.explain: विधानेन = by the method (inst.); उपकल्पयेत् = should prepare.

questions.q: Which of these does verse 90 say harītakī removes?
optionExplain: No: piles are named in line 05.02.165, not in this verse.
Right: शोष is the third member.
No: itching is named in line 05.02.165, not in this verse.
Right: ग्रहणी is the first member.
Right: मोह is the fourth member.
questions.explain: ग्रहणी, पाण्डु, शोष, मोह, उदर: these five are in verse 90.
questions.rule: ग्रहणी · पाण्डु · शोष · मोह · उदर → अपहाम्.

questions.q: Like ...अपहाम् qualifying हरीतकीम् (f. acc.), which form qualifies पथ्याम् (f. acc.) as कफ-अपहा, removing Kapha (invented)?
optionExplain: Right: Feminine accusative singular, like पथ्याम् and हरीतकीम्.
That is the masculine or neuter form; पथ्या is feminine.
That is masculine nominative; पथ्याम् is accusative.
That ending is locative or dual; पथ्याम् is singular accusative.
questions.explain: An adjective takes the gender, case and number of its noun: हरीतकीम् ... अपहाम्, पथ्याम् ... कफापहाम्.
questions.teaches: -अपहा 'removing' agrees with its noun: हरीतकीम् ... अपहाम्, पथ्याम् कफापहाम्.

questions.q: In verse 91, what is sindhūttha?
optionExplain: Dried ginger is नागर, the last drug of the compound.
Right: सिन्धूत्थ = rock salt, saindhava (standard).
viḍaṅga, Embelia ribes, is the next member, not sindhūttha.
Long pepper is not named in this verse.
questions.explain: सिन्धूत्थ = 'risen from the Sindhu': rock salt (standard).

questions.q: Match each drug word of verse 91 to its meaning on the card.
questions.explain: Three companions of pathyā from the first line; the vatsaka decoction from the second.
questions.rule: सिन्धूत्थ = rock salt; विडङ्ग = Embelia ribes; नागर = dried ginger; वत्सक = kuṭaja; निर्यूह = decoction.

questions.q: Put the drugs drunk with pathyā in verse 91 in the text's order.
questions.explain: sindhūttha, viḍaṅga, utpala, nāgara: the compound begins with स- 'together with'.
questions.teaches: A compound beginning with स- means 'together with' the drugs it lists.

questions.q: Which drugs does the first line of verse 91 add to pathyā?
optionExplain: No: jaggery is not named in this verse.
Right: the last member.
Right: the first member of the स- compound.
No: vatsaka is in the second line, as a decoction to drink it with.
Right: the second member.
questions.explain: ससिन्धूत्थविडङ्गोत्पलनागराम् = with rock salt, viḍaṅga, utpala and dried ginger.
questions.rule: पहली पंक्ति: सिन्धूत्थ · विडङ्ग · उत्पल · नागर; दूसरी: मूत्र · वत्सकादि-निर्यूह.

questions.q: Which rendering of मूत्रेण वत्सकादेर्वा निर्यूहेण is right?
options: with urine, and a decoction of vatsaka etc.
with milk, or a decoction of vatsaka etc.
with urine, or a decoction of vatsaka etc.
with urine, or a paste of vatsaka etc.
optionExplain: वा means 'or', not 'and'.
मूत्र means urine, not milk.
Right: मूत्रेण = with urine; वा = or; निर्यूहेण = with a decoction.
निर्यूह is a decoction, not a paste.
questions.explain: मूत्रेण · वत्सकादेः · वा · निर्यूहेण: two ways, joined by 'or'.

questions.q: Like ससिन्धूत्थ...नागराम् (together with rock salt and the rest), what does सघृतां पथ्याम् (invented) mean?
optionExplain: 'Without ghee' would be निर्घृताम्; स- means 'with'.
स- adds a companion; it does not replace the noun.
'Cooked in ghee' would need a word like सिद्ध; स- says only 'with'.
Right: स- + घृत = 'with ghee', agreeing with पथ्याम्.
questions.explain: स- at the start of a compound adjective = 'together with'.
questions.teaches: A स- compound means 'together with': ससिन्धूत्थाम् पथ्याम्, सघृताम् पथ्याम् 'pathyā with ghee'.

questions.q: By verse 92, with what is the powder eaten?
optionExplain: Right: गुडेन भक्षयेत् = one should eat it with jaggery.
No honey is named in this verse.
No ghee is named in this verse.
Rock salt belongs to line 05.02.169, not this verse.
questions.explain: गुड = jaggery; भक्षयेत् = should eat.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 92 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The powder of two drugs, eaten with jaggery, then lukewarm water.
questions.rule: पथ्या = chebulic myrobalan; नागर = dried ginger; चूर्ण = powder; गुड = jaggery; कोष्ण = lukewarm.

questions.q: Put the steps of verse 92 in the text's order.
items: तोयं कोष्णं च पिबेदनु (then drink lukewarm water)
questions.explain: The powder is named, eaten with jaggery, and lukewarm water is drunk after.
questions.rule: चूर्णम् · गुडेन भक्षयेत् · तोयं कोष्णं च पिबेदनु.
questions.teaches: अनु 'afterwards' puts the drink of lukewarm water after the eating.

questions.q: Which split of पिबेदनु is right?
optionExplain: त् before न becomes न्: that would be पिबेन्नु.
Right: त् before a vowel becomes द्: पिबेत् + अनु → पिबेदनु.
There is no word दनु here, and पिबे is not the verb form.
पिबेः + अनु would give पिबेरनु, with र्.
questions.explain: पिबेत् = should drink; अनु = afterwards.

questions.q: Which of these does verse 92 state?
options: The powder is of pathyā and nāgara
The powder is mixed with honey
optionExplain: No: the water is drunk after (अनु).
Right: पथ्यानागरचूर्णम्.
Right: गुडेन भक्षयेत्.
Right: तोयं कोष्णम्.
No: no honey is named in this verse.
questions.explain: Powder of pathyā and nāgara; eaten with jaggery; lukewarm water after.

questions.q: Like पिबेत् + अनु → पिबेदनु, which is the joined form of भक्षयेत् + अपि (invented)?
optionExplain: The त् is voiced to द् before a vowel; it does not stay त.
No य् is inserted; त् simply becomes द्.
Right: त् before a vowel becomes द्: भक्षयेत् + अपि → भक्षयेदपि.
The vowel of अपि stays short.
questions.explain: पिबेदनु, भक्षयेदपि: final त् becomes द् before a vowel.
questions.teaches: A final त् becomes द् before a vowel: पिबेत् + अनु → पिबेदनु, भक्षयेत् + अपि → भक्षयेदपि.

questions.q: By verse 93, what size are the pills?
options: The size of a kola seed
optionExplain: The kola-seed size belongs to line 05.02.177.
No karṣa is named in this verse.
No palmful is named in this verse.
Right: माषप्रमाणाः = of the measure of a māṣa.
questions.explain: माष = a small measure; प्रमाण = measure, size.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 93 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Pills to be made, with honey; dry; for one with yakṣman.
questions.rule: गुलिका = pill; कार्य = to be made; क्षौद्र = honey; शुष्क = dry; यक्ष्मी = one with yakṣman.

questions.q: Put these words of verse 93 in the text's order.
questions.explain: Pills, to be made, with honey and juice; of māṣa measure, dry; one with yakṣman.
questions.rule: गुलिकाः · कार्याः · क्षौद्ररसान्विताः · माषप्रमाणाः · शुष्काः · यक्ष्मी.
questions.teaches: The pills are described first (made, with honey), then their size and dryness, then who takes them.

questions.q: Which of these does verse 93 state about the pills?
options: They are made from pathyā and trivṛt
They are of the measure of a māṣa
They are of the size of a kola seed
optionExplain: Right: पथ्या and त्रिवृत् are the two drugs named.
No: no milk is named in this verse.
Right: माषप्रमाणाः.
Right: शुष्काः.
No: that size is in line 05.02.177.
questions.explain: Pathyā and trivṛt pills, with honey and juice, māṣa-sized and dry.

questions.q: Which split of माषप्रमाणास्ताः is right?
optionExplain: Right: आः before त becomes आस्: माषप्रमाणाः + ताः → माषप्रमाणास्ताः.
That would give माषप्रमाणस्ताः, with a short अ.
Final म् before त gives ं: माषप्रमाणांताः.
There is no word स्ताः; the स् comes from the visarga.
questions.explain: माषप्रमाणाः (of māṣa measure, f. pl.) + ताः (those, f. pl.).

questions.q: Like माषप्रमाणाः + ताः → माषप्रमाणास्ताः, which is the joined form of शुष्काः + तत्र (invented)?
optionExplain: श् comes before च, छ; before त the visarga becomes स्.
Right: ः before त becomes स्: शुष्काः + तत्र → शुष्कास्तत्र.
The visarga is not dropped before त; it becomes स्.
आः keeps its आ; ओ comes only from अः before voiced sounds.
questions.explain: माषप्रमाणास्ताः, शुष्कास्तत्र: visarga before त → स्.
questions.teaches: Visarga before त becomes स्: माषप्रमाणाः + ताः → माषप्रमाणास्ताः, शुष्काः + तत्र → शुष्कास्तत्र.

questions.q: By verse 94, how is the purgative of pathyā, trivṛt and hot water described?
optionExplain: Strength is not mentioned in this verse.
No season is named in this verse.
Right: सर्वत्र इष्टं विरेचनम् = a purgative desired everywhere.
The verse calls it desired (इष्ट), not harsh.
questions.explain: सर्वत्र = everywhere; इष्ट = desired; विरेचन = purgative.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 94 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The first line praises the purgative; the second line makes balls of steeped pathyā powder.
questions.rule: सर्वत्र = everywhere; इष्ट = desired; स्नुक् = a spurge; भावित = steeped; मोदक = ball.

questions.q: Put the words of the second line of verse 94 in the text's order.
questions.explain: When the pathyā powder has been steeped in snuk-milk, one should make balls: the steeping is named first.
questions.teaches: A locative phrase (स्नुक्क्षीरभाविते पथ्याचूर्णे) says 'when the powder has been steeped'; the making of balls follows it.

questions.q: Which split of सर्वत्रेष्टं is right?
optionExplain: अ + अ would give आ: सर्वत्राष्टम्.
There is no form सर्वत्रे; the adverb is सर्वत्र.
There is no word एष्टम्; ए comes from अ + इ.
Right: अ + इ → ए: सर्वत्र + इष्टम् → सर्वत्रेष्टम्.
questions.explain: सर्वत्र = everywhere; इष्टम् = desired.

questions.q: In verse 94, what is snuk-kṣīra, in which the powder is steeped?
options: The milky sap of the snuk spurge
The juice of the pathyā fruit
optionExplain: Right: स्नुक्क्षीर = the milk (milky sap) of snuk, a spurge.
No cow's milk is named; the 'milk' is the plant's own sap.
pathyā is the powder being steeped, not the liquid.
trivṛt belongs to the first line's purgative.
questions.explain: स्नुक् = snuhī, a spurge (probable: Euphorbia neriifolia); क्षीर = its milky sap.

questions.q: Like सर्वत्र + इष्टम् → सर्वत्रेष्टम्, which is the joined form of अत्र + इष्टम् (invented)?
optionExplain: The अ is not lost; it merges with इ into ए.
Right: अ + इ → ए: अत्र + इष्टम् → अत्रेष्टम्.
ऐ comes from अ + ए, not from अ + इ.
No य् is inserted between अ and इ.
questions.explain: सर्वत्रेष्टम्, अत्रेष्टम्: अ + इ → ए.
questions.teaches: अ before इ merges into ए: सर्वत्र + इष्टम् → सर्वत्रेष्टम्, अत्र + इष्टम् → अत्रेष्टम्.

questions.q: By verse 95, with what are the balls given to lick?
optionExplain: Castor oil belongs to line 05.02.179, not this verse.
Jaggery belongs to line 05.02.172, not this verse.
Right: नवनीतेन लेहयेत् = should make (him) lick with fresh butter.
Neither honey nor ghee is named in this verse.
questions.explain: नवनीत = fresh butter; लेहयेत् = should make lick.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 95 to its meaning on the card.
questions.explain: The size (kola seed), the vehicle (butter), and two organs from the list of disorders.
questions.rule: कोल = jujube; अस्थि = seed; नवनीत = fresh butter; यकृत् = liver; प्लीहा = spleen.

questions.q: Put the first six members of the second line's compound (verse 95) in order.
questions.explain: gulma, udara, yakṛt, plīha, śūla, ānāha; vibandha closes the list.
questions.rule: गुल्म · उदर · यकृत् · प्लीह · शूल · आनाह · (विबन्ध).
questions.teaches: The disorders are listed in one compound ending in -विबन्धिनः, 'one with ... constipation'.

questions.q: In verse 95, what is ānāha, as the card gives it?
options: A hard lump in the belly
Pain or colic in the belly
optionExplain: A lump in the abdomen is gulma, the first member.
Pain is śūla, the member before ānāha.
plīha names the spleen, not ānāha.
Right: आनाह = distension of the abdomen with retention of stool and wind.
questions.explain: आनाह = distension with retention of stool and wind (standard).
questions.rule: गुल्म = lump; शूल = pain; आनाह = distension; विबन्ध = constipation.

questions.q: Which split of शुष्कांश्च is right?
optionExplain: Right: न् before च becomes ंश्: शुष्कान् + च → शुष्कांश्च.
Visarga before च gives श्: that would be शुष्काश्च.
म् before च gives ं: that would be शुष्कां च.
There is no word अश्च, and ं + अ would not give ांश्च.
questions.explain: शुष्कान् (dry, m. acc. pl., agreeing with the balls) + च (and).

questions.q: Like शुष्कान् + च → शुष्कांश्च, which is the joined form of मोदकान् + च (invented)?
optionExplain: That is the form from मोदकाः (nominative), not मोदकान्.
Right: न् before च becomes ंश्: मोदकान् + च → मोदकांश्च.
Final न् does not stay unchanged before च.
The श् sibilant is inserted before च: ंश्च.
questions.explain: शुष्कांश्च, मोदकांश्च: न् + च → ंश्च.
questions.teaches: Final न् before च becomes anusvara + श्: शुष्कान् + च → शुष्कांश्च, मोदकान् + च → मोदकांश्च.

questions.q: By verse 96, with which oil is the preparation licked?
optionExplain: Sesame oil is not named in this verse.
Mustard oil is not named in this verse.
Right: एरण्डतैलेन = with eraṇḍa (castor) oil.
Fresh butter belongs to line 05.02.177.
questions.explain: एरण्ड = castor, Ricinus communis (standard); तैल = oil.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 96 to its meaning on the card.
questions.explain: The oil, the two additions, the after-drink, and what the whole is called.
questions.rule: एरण्ड = castor; कुष्ठ = costus; त्रिकटुक = three pungents; सुखोदक = pleasant water; विरेचन = purgative.

questions.q: Put the phrases of verse 96 in the text's order.
questions.explain: Lick, with castor oil, joined with kuṣṭha and trikaṭuka; drink pleasant water after; this purgative is easy.
questions.rule: लिह्यात् · एरण्डतैलेन · कुष्ठत्रिकटुकान्वितम् · सुखोदकं चानुपिबेत् · सुखमेतद्विरेचनम्.
questions.teaches: The verse gives the action (lick) first, then the vehicle and the additions, then the after-drink and a judgement.

questions.q: By verse 96, how is this purgative described?
optionExplain: No comparison of strength is made in this verse.
No patient group is named in this verse.
'Desired everywhere' is said of the purgative in line 05.02.175.
Right: सुखम् एतद् विरेचनम् = this purgative is easy.
questions.explain: सुख = easy, comfortable; एतत् = this.

questions.q: Which three drugs make up trikaṭuka, as the card gives them?
optionExplain: No: kuṣṭha is named beside trikaṭuka, not inside it.
No: castor gives the oil it is licked with.
Right: one of the three pungents.
Right: one of the three pungents.
Right: one of the three pungents.
questions.explain: त्रिकटुक = śuṇṭhī, pippalī, marica (standard).

questions.q: Like च + अनुपिबेत् → चानुपिबेत्, which is the joined form of च + अपि (invented)?
optionExplain: Right: अ + अ → आ: च + अपि → चापि.
ओ comes from अ + उ, not from अ + अ.
ऐ comes from अ + ए, not from अ + अ.
The two अ merge into a long आ; neither is simply lost.
questions.explain: चानुपिबेत्, चापि: अ + अ → आ.
questions.teaches: Two अ sounds merge into आ: च + अनुपिबेत् → चानुपिबेत्, च + अपि → चापि.

questions.q: By verse 97, what can even a small amount be given?
optionExplain: Smallness of action is what a large amount (प्रभूत) can be given.
Right: अल्पस्यापि महार्थत्वम् = great purposefulness even of a small amount.
Keeping time is not mentioned in this verse.
Taste is not mentioned in this verse.
questions.explain: अल्प = small amount; महार्थत्व = great purposefulness.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 97 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Two amounts in the first line; three of the five means in the second.
questions.rule: अल्प = small; प्रभूत = large; संश्लेष = combination; विश्लेष = separation; संस्कार = processing.

questions.q: Put the five means of verse 97 in the text's order.
questions.explain: Combination, separation, time, processing, method; the instrumental -भिः says 'by means of'.
questions.teaches: The five means are named in a row ending in the instrumental plural -भिः: '...युक्तिभिः', 'by ... method'.

questions.q: By verse 97, what can a large amount be given?
optionExplain: Great purposefulness is what a small amount (अल्प) can be given.
Digestion is not mentioned in this verse.
Right: प्रभूतस्याल्पकर्मताम् = smallness of action of a large amount.
Smell is not mentioned in this verse.
questions.explain: प्रभूत = large amount; अल्पकर्मता = smallness of action.

questions.q: Which of these are means named in verse 97?
optionExplain: No: मात्रा is not named in this verse.
Right: the fourth means.
Right: the third means.
No: देश is not named in this verse.
Right: the fifth means.
questions.explain: संश्लेष, विश्लेष, काल, संस्कार, युक्ति: the five means.

questions.q: Like अल्पकर्मता (smallness of action, abstract noun in -ता), which word means lightness, from लघु (invented)?
optionExplain: -तर makes a comparative: 'lighter'.
-तम makes a superlative: 'lightest'.
लघूकृत is a participle: 'made light'.
Right: -ता makes an abstract noun: लघु 'light' → लघुता 'lightness'.
questions.explain: अल्पकर्मता, लघुता: -ता forms a feminine abstract noun ('-ness').
questions.teaches: -ता (and -त्व) form abstract nouns: अल्पकर्मता 'smallness of action', महार्थत्व 'great purposefulness', लघुता 'lightness'.

questions.q: By verse 98, purgatives are given with things agreeable to what?
optionExplain: Right: मनोऽनुकूलैः = with (things) agreeable to the mind.
No doṣa is named in this verse.
No season is named in this verse.
The belly (koṣṭha) is not named in this verse.
questions.explain: मनः = mind; अनुकूल = agreeable.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 98 to its meaning on the card.
questions.explain: Four drugs from the first line and the madya of the second.
questions.rule: दाडिम = pomegranate; एला = cardamom; सितोपला = rock sugar; मातुलुङ्ग = citron; मद्य = intoxicating drink.

questions.q: Put these members of the first line of verse 98 in the text's order.
questions.explain: Pomegranate, cardamom, rock sugar, mākṣika, citron: the list ends in the instrumental -ऐः.
questions.teaches: The pleasant additions stand in one instrumental compound: '... with pomegranate, cardamom ...'.

questions.q: Which split of मनोऽनुकूलैः is right?
optionExplain: अ + अ would give आ: मनानुकूलैः.
Right: अः + अ → ओऽ: मनः + अनुकूलैः → मनोऽनुकूलैः.
There is no word नुकूलैः; the ऽ marks a lost अ.
स् before न would not give ओऽ, and नुकूलैः is no word.
questions.explain: मनः (mind) + अनुकूलैः (agreeable, inst. pl.).

questions.q: In verse 98, what does देयानि say about the purgatives?
optionExplain: 'Have been given' would be the past participle दत्तानि.
The present would be a form like दीयन्ते.
Right: देयानि = to be given (gerundive of √दा).
No negation (न) is in this verse.
questions.explain: देय = to be given; it agrees with विरेचनानि (n. nom. pl.).

questions.q: Like देयानि विरेचनानि (to be given, from √दा), which form means to be drunk (√पा), with विरेचनानि (invented)?
optionExplain: पीतानि is the past participle: 'drunk'.
पिबन्ति is a present verb: 'they drink'.
पीत्वा is the absolutive: 'having drunk'.
Right: The gerundive in -य: √पा → पेय, neuter plural पेयानि.
questions.explain: देयानि, पेयानि: the gerundive 'is to be ...' agrees with its noun.
questions.teaches: The gerundive in -य says 'is to be done': √दा → देयानि 'to be given', √पा → पेयानि 'to be drunk'.

questions.q: By unit 99, what is the name of the chapter that ends here?
optionExplain: Right: विरेचनकल्पो नाम = named Virecanakalpa (the purgative preparations).
Vamanakalpa (emesis) is the first chapter, closed at line 05.01.71.
Enema is not the name given in this unit.
Ṛtucaryā is a Sūtrasthāna chapter.
questions.explain: विरेचन = purgation; कल्प = preparations.

questions.q: Put the words of unit 99 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Thus, Virecanakalpa, named, the second, chapter.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 99 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The words of the colophon around the chapter's name and number.
questions.rule: इति = thus; विरेचन = purgation; कल्प = preparations; द्वितीय = second; अध्याय = chapter.
questions.teaches: Unit 99: इति = thus, विरेचनकल्प = the purgative preparations, द्वितीय = second, अध्याय = chapter.

questions.q: Which split of विरेचनकल्पो नाम is right?
optionExplain: म् before न would give ं: विरेचनकल्पं नाम.
Right: अः → ओ before a voiced consonant (न): विरेचनकल्पः नाम → विरेचनकल्पो नाम.
A final ए stays ए before न.
A final औ stays औ before न.
questions.explain: विरेचनकल्पः (m. nom. sg.) + नाम (named).

questions.q: Unit 99 calls this chapter the ____ (second) chapter. Type it in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: द्वितीयोऽध्यायः = द्वितीयः (second) + अध्यायः (chapter).
questions.teaches: Unit 99 names the chapter Virecanakalpa and calls it the second (द्वितीय) chapter.

questions.q: Like विरेचनकल्पः + नाम → विरेचनकल्पो नाम, which is the joined form of योगः + भवति (invented)?
optionExplain: Dropping to आ happens only after a long आः.
Visarga becomes र् only after vowels other than अ or आ.
Right: अः before a voiced consonant (भ) becomes ओ.
स् appears only before त or थ.
questions.explain: विरेचनकल्पो नाम, योगो भवति: अः → ओ before a voiced consonant.
questions.teaches: -अः before a voiced consonant becomes -ओ: विरेचनकल्पो नाम, योगो भवति.

questions.q: What topic does unit 1 say will be explained?
options: The best emetic drugs and how one should collect them
The doses of oil to give before any emesis
The signs that a patient will soon recover
Mishaps of emesis and purgation, and their remedy
optionExplain: The title compound speaks of mishaps (व्यापत्), not of choosing drugs.
No dose or oil is named in this unit.
Signs of recovery are not the topic named here.
Right: वमन-विरेचन-व्यापत्-सिद्धि: the accomplishment in the mishaps of vamana and virecana.
questions.explain: The unit is the opening formula; its topic is the vamana-virecana-vyāpat-siddhi.
questions.rule: Chapter topic: mishaps (व्यापत्) of vamana and virecana, and their siddhi.
questions.section: वमन का अयोग और उसका उपाय

questions.q: Match each member of the title compound to its meaning.
questions.explain: The compound joins four members: vamana, virecana, vyāpat, siddhi.
questions.rule: वमन = emesis; विरेचन = purgation; व्यापत् = mishap; सिद्धि = accomplishment.
questions.section: वमन का अयोग और उसका उपाय

questions.q: Put the members of the title compound in the order of the text.
questions.explain: The compound runs vamana, virecana, vyāpat, siddhim.
questions.teaches: The title names first the two cleansings, then their mishap, then its siddhi.
questions.section: वमन का अयोग और उसका उपाय

questions.q: Which is the right split of अथातो?
optionExplain: Right: अ + अ → आ (अथातः); then अः before the voiced व becomes ओ: अथातो.
ओ + अ would give अथोऽतः, not अथातो.
अ + इ gives ए: अथेतः, not अथातो.
अथा and तः are not the words; they are अथ (now) and अतः (therefore).
questions.explain: अथ (now) + अतः (therefore); अतः becomes अतो before the voiced व of वमन.
questions.rule: अ + अ → आ; अः → ओ before a voiced sound.
questions.section: वमन का अयोग और उसका उपाय

questions.q: What is the form of व्याख्यास्यामः, as the word split gives it?
options: 1st person plural future: we shall explain
1st person plural optative: we should explain
optionExplain: -स्यामः is first person plural and future, not 3rd singular present.
Right: The gram label is 1 pl. fut. of vi-ā-√khyā.
An optative would end in -एम; this is the future.
A past participle would end in -त; this is a finite future verb.
questions.explain: व्याख्यास्यामः = we shall explain: the explanation is still to come.
questions.section: वमन का अयोग और उसका उपाय

questions.q: Like व्याख्यास्यामः (we shall explain), which invented form means we shall speak (√वद्)?
optionExplain: This is the present: we speak.
This is the optative: we should speak.
Right: -(इ)ष्यामः is the 1st person plural future, like -स्यामः in व्याख्यास्यामः.
This is a past participle: spoken.
questions.explain: The future 1st plural ends in -स्यामः / -इष्यामः: व्याख्यास्यामः, वदिष्यामः.
questions.teaches: The 1st person plural future ends in -स्यामः or -इष्यामः (व्याख्यास्यामः, वदिष्यामः): we shall ...
questions.section: वमन का अयोग और उसका उपाय

questions.q: According to unit 2, where does the emetic go under these conditions?
optionExplain: The unit says अधः, downward, not upward.
Blood and skin are not named in the unit.
The verb गच्छति says it goes, and the direction is अधः.
Right: वमनम् अधो गच्छति: the emetic goes downward.
questions.explain: The mishap is that the emetic goes the wrong way: downward.
questions.rule: Emetic + these conditions → अधो गच्छति (goes downward).
questions.section: वमन का अयोग और उसका उपाय

questions.q: Match each description of the patient to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four of the five instrumentals that describe the one who drinks the emetic.
questions.rule: अतिक्षुधित = very hungry; मृदुकोष्ठ = soft bowel; अल्पश्लेष्मा = little phlegm; दुर्बल = weak.
questions.section: वमन का अयोग और उसका उपाय

questions.q: Put these descriptions of the patient in the order of the text (दुर्बमेन left out).
questions.explain: The text runs very hungry, soft bowel, little phlegm, (hard to make vomit), weak.
questions.teaches: The patient's conditions come first in the unit, from very hungry to weak.
questions.section: वमन का अयोग और उसका उपाय

questions.q: Which of these does unit 2 name as conditions of the medicine itself?
optionExplain: Right: हीनमात्रम्, the first condition of the medicine.
The unit says deficient dose, not great dose.
Not in this unit; the emetic named here is very cold.
Right: अतितीक्ष्णम् is named.
Right: अतिशीतम् is named.
questions.explain: The medicine's conditions are deficient dose, very sharp, very cold (and drunk in indigestion).
questions.section: वमन का अयोग और उसका उपाय

questions.q: A weak patient drinks an emetic that is very cold. What does unit 2 lead you to expect?
options: The emetic may go downward instead of up
The emetic may act faster than usual
The patient may vomit blood at once
The emetic may turn into a purgative drug
optionExplain: Right: दुर्बल and अतिशीत are both in the unit's list; the result is अधो गच्छति.
Speed is not mentioned in the unit.
Blood is not mentioned in the unit.
The unit says it goes downward; it does not say it changes kind.
questions.explain: Each listed condition, joined by वा (or), is a case in which the emetic goes downward.
questions.rule: Weak patient or very cold emetic → the emetic goes downward.
questions.section: वमन का अयोग और उसका उपाय

questions.q: Join the invented pair शीतेन + अल्पेन as मृदुकोष्ठेन + अल्पश्लेष्मणा is joined. Which is right?
optionExplain: The two short अ do not leave a single short अ.
Right: अ + अ → आ: शीतेन + अल्पेन = शीतेनाल्पेन.
ओ is made from अ + उ, not अ + अ.
ए is made from अ + इ, not अ + अ.
questions.explain: Same rule as मृदुकोष्ठेन + अल्पश्लेष्मणा = मृदुकोष्ठेनाल्पश्लेष्मणा.
questions.teaches: A final अ and an initial अ join into आ (मृदुकोष्ठेन + अल्पश्लेष्मणा → मृदुकोष्ठेनाल्पश्लेष्मणा).
questions.section: वमन का अयोग और उसका उपाय

questions.q: What does unit 3 say happens to the waste matter (मल)?
options: It hardens and stays fixed inside
optionExplain: Nothing is said to be expelled; the desired result is not attained.
The unit says stirred up, not digested.
Right: मल-उत्क्लेशः: stirring up of the waste matter.
The word is उत्क्लेश, stirring up, not hardening.
questions.explain: The two results: non-attainment of the desired, and stirring up of mala.
questions.rule: मल + उत्क्लेश = the waste matter is stirred up.
questions.section: वमन का अयोग और उसका उपाय

questions.q: Match each word of unit 3 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words carry the whole line.
questions.rule: तत्र = in that case; ईप्सित = desired; अनवाप्तिः = non-attainment; उत्क्लेशः = stirring up.
questions.section: वमन का अयोग और उसका उपाय

questions.q: Put the parts of unit 3 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: The line runs: in that case, the desired, non-attainment; waste matter, stirring up, and.
questions.rule: तत्र · ईप्सित · अनवाप्तिः · मल · उत्क्लेशः · च.
questions.teaches: Unit 3 names first the failure (desired not attained), then the stirring up of mala.
questions.section: वमन का अयोग और उसका उपाय

questions.q: Which is the right split of मलोत्क्लेशश्च?
optionExplain: मलो and त्क्लेशः are not the words.
श्च is not a word: श् is the visarga of उत्क्लेशः before च.
अ + इ would give ए (मलेत्क्लेश), not ओ.
Right: अ + उ → ओ (मलोत्क्लेश); the visarga of उत्क्लेशः becomes श् before च.
questions.explain: मल (waste matter) + उत्क्लेशः (stirring up) + च (and).
questions.section: वमन का अयोग और उसका उपाय

questions.q: Which situation does तत्र (in that case) at the start of unit 3 point back to?
optionExplain: Right: Unit 3 follows the list of unit 2, which ends with वमनमधो गच्छति.
The formula names the topic; it describes no case.
That case comes later, in unit 6.
That case comes later, in unit 9.
questions.explain: तत्र = there, in that case: the case just described, the emetic going downward.
questions.rule: तत्र points back to the case just stated.
questions.section: वमन का अयोग और उसका उपाय

questions.q: Join the invented pair रोगः + च as उत्क्लेशः + च is joined. Which is right?
optionExplain: The visarga becomes ओ only before a voiced sound; च is not voiced.
Right: A visarga before च becomes श्: रोगः + च = रोगश्च.
The visarga does not become च्.
Before च the visarga becomes the palatal श्, not स्.
questions.explain: Same rule as उत्क्लेशः + च = उत्क्लेशश्च.
questions.teaches: A visarga before च becomes श् (उत्क्लेशः + च → उत्क्लेशश्च; रोगः + च → रोगश्च).
questions.section: वमन का अयोग और उसका उपाय

questions.q: What does unit 4 say must be done before making him vomit again?
options: Make him fast for a whole day first
Sweat him in a heated room
optionExplain: No fasting is named in the unit.
No purgative is named; the unit speaks of oiling, then emesis.
Right: पुनराशु स्नेहयित्वा: having quickly made him unctuous again.
Sweating is not named in the unit.
questions.explain: The order is: oil him again quickly, then make him vomit.
questions.section: वमन का अयोग और उसका उपाय

questions.q: Put the words of unit 4 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Him, again quickly, having oiled, by suitable ones, regarding dose and time, should make vomit.
questions.rule: तं · पुनराशु · स्नेहयित्वा · यौगिकैः · मात्राकालाद्यपेक्षं · वामयेत्.
questions.section: वमन का अयोग और उसका उपाय

questions.q: Match each word of unit 4 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words give the steps and their timing.
questions.rule: पुनः = again; आशु = quickly; स्नेहयित्वा = having made unctuous; वामयेत् = should make vomit.
questions.teaches: The remedy is a repeat: oil again, quickly, then make him vomit.
questions.section: वमन का अयोग और उसका उपाय

questions.q: Which is the right split of मात्राकालाद्यपेक्षम्?
optionExplain: काला and दि are not the words; they are काल and आदि.
कालात् + अपेक्षम् would give कालादपेक्षम्, with no य.
अदि is not a word; the word is आदि, and so on.
Right: अ + आ → आ (कालादि); इ before a different vowel becomes य् (आद्यपेक्षम्).
questions.explain: With regard to dose (मात्रा), time (काल) and so on (आदि).
questions.rule: अ + आ → आ; इ + अ → य.
questions.section: वमन का अयोग और उसका उपाय

questions.q: In unit 4, which form shows that the oiling comes before the vomiting?
options: वामयेत्, an optative: should make vomit
optionExplain: Right: An absolutive in -त्वा marks an action done before the main verb.
This is the main verb, the later step.
This says by what means, not which step comes first.
This says how fast, not in what order.
questions.explain: स्नेहयित्वा (having oiled) comes first; वामयेत् (should make vomit) is the main action.
questions.section: वमन का अयोग और उसका उपाय

questions.q: Like स्नेहयित्वा (having made unctuous), which invented form means having made him sweat (causative of √स्विद्)?
optionExplain: This is the optative: should make sweat.
Right: A causative stem in -अय takes -इत्वा: स्वेदय + इत्वा, like स्नेहय + इत्वा.
This is the present: makes sweat.
This is a past participle: made to sweat.
questions.explain: Causative absolutive: -अयित्वा (स्नेहयित्वा, स्वेदयित्वा).
questions.teaches: A causative absolutive ends in -अयित्वा (स्नेहयित्वा, स्वेदयित्वा): having made (him) ...
questions.section: वमन का अयोग और उसका उपाय

questions.q: What does unit 5 say one should avoid (परिहरेत्)?
options: The oiling that comes before the emesis
optionExplain: Food is not named in the unit.
Unit 4 repeats the emesis; unit 5 does not forbid it.
Right: व्यापत्करणानि ... परिहरेत्: one should avoid the causes of mishap.
Unit 4 prescribes the oiling; unit 5 does not reject it.
questions.explain: The object of परिहरेत् is व्यापत्करणानि, the causes of mishap.
questions.rule: परिहरेत् व्यापत्करणानि = should avoid the causes of mishap.
questions.section: वमन का अयोग और उसका उपाय

questions.q: Match each word of unit 5 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words give what is avoided and what is kept in mind.
questions.rule: व्यापत्करणानि = causes of mishap; पूर्वम् = earlier; स्मरन् = remembering; परिहरेत् = should avoid.
questions.section: वमन का अयोग और उसका उपाय

questions.q: Put the words of unit 5 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Causes of mishap, and, the earlier atikrama, remembering, should avoid.
questions.teaches: The unit puts the object first (causes of mishap) and the verb last (परिहरेत्).
questions.section: वमन का अयोग और उसका उपाय

questions.q: What is the form of स्मरन्, as the word split gives it?
optionExplain: An absolutive would end in -त्वा (स्मृत्वा).
An optative would end in -एत् (स्मरेत्).
A future would be built with -स्य- (स्मरिष्यति).
Right: The gram label is pres. part. √smṛ.
questions.explain: स्मरन् = remembering, at the same time as avoiding.
questions.section: वमन का अयोग और उसका उपाय

questions.q: A physician repeats the emesis as unit 4 says. What does unit 5 add to that step?
options: Avoid the causes of mishap, minding the earlier atikrama
Halve the dose of the second emetic and give it at night
Wait one month before trying again
Give a purgative instead of an emetic
optionExplain: Right: This is exactly what unit 5 says.
No dose change is stated in the unit.
No waiting time is stated.
The unit names no purgative.
questions.explain: Unit 5 adds a caution to the repeat of unit 4: avoid the causes of mishap.
questions.rule: Repeat the emesis (v.4) + avoid the causes of mishap (v.5).
questions.section: वमन का अयोग और उसका उपाय

questions.q: Like परि + हरेत् = परिहरेत् (should avoid), which invented form means one should bring (आ + √हृ)?
optionExplain: This is the present: he brings.
Right: आ + हरेत्: the prefix stands before the optative in -एत्, as in परिहरेत्.
This is an absolutive: having brought.
This is the future: he will bring.
questions.explain: Prefix + optative: परि + हरेत् = परिहरेत्; आ + हरेत् = आहरेत्.
questions.rule: Optative 3rd sg = stem + -एत्; a prefix stands before it.
questions.teaches: A verb prefix stands before the optative form (परि + हरेत् = परिहरेत्, should avoid; आ + हरेत् = आहरेत्, should bring).
questions.section: वमन का अयोग और उसका उपाय

questions.q: According to unit 6, in which direction does the purgative go under these conditions?
optionExplain: The unit says ऊर्ध्व, upward.
That is a different mishap, in unit 9.
Right: भेषजमूर्ध्व प्रवर्त्तते (printed ऊर्ध्व, read ऊर्ध्वम्): the medicine goes upward.
The limbs are not named in this unit.
questions.explain: The purgative's mishap here is going the wrong way: upward.
questions.rule: Purgative + these conditions → ऊर्ध्व प्रवर्त्तते (goes upward; ऊर्ध्व read ऊर्ध्वम्).

questions.q: Match each word of unit 6 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Two patients and two words for what is drunk.
questions.rule: अजीर्णिनः = one with indigestion; श्लेष्मवतः = one with phlegm; विरेचनम् = purgative; भेषजम् = medicine.

questions.q: Put these clear words of unit 6 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Two patients first, then the qualities very hot, sharp, salty, then the purgative.
questions.rule: अजीर्णिनः · श्लेष्मवतः · अत्युष्ण · तीक्ष्ण · लवण · विरेचनम्.
questions.teaches: Unit 6 names the patients first, then the medicine's qualities, then the purgative.

questions.q: Unit 2 has a very cold emetic going down. Which quality does unit 6 give for a purgative going up?
optionExplain: Very cold belongs to the emetic of unit 2.
Deficient dose belongs to the emetic of unit 2.
Dry is not named in unit 6.
Right: अति-उष्ण is the first quality of the purgative in unit 6.
questions.explain: The two lists differ: a very cold emetic goes down (unit 2), a very hot purgative goes up (unit 6).
questions.rule: Unit 2: अतिशीत वमन → नीचे; unit 6: अत्युष्ण विरेचन → ऊपर.

questions.q: A patient with indigestion takes a very salty purgative. What does unit 6 lead you to expect?
options: It may go downward too fast
It may be digested without effect
optionExplain: Right: अजीर्णिन् and लवण are both in the unit; the result is ऊर्ध्वं प्रवर्तते.
The unit's result is going upward.
Stiffened doṣas are not mentioned in this unit.
Being digested is the mishap of unit 9, with a hard bowel.
questions.explain: Indigestion in the patient and a salty purgative are both causes of going upward.
questions.rule: अजीर्ण / श्लेष्मा + उष्ण, तीक्ष्ण, लवण विरेचन → ऊपर जाता है.

questions.q: Join the invented pair बलवतः + अपि as श्लेष्मवतः + अति is joined. Which is right?
optionExplain: आ is not made from अः + अ.
Right: अः + अ → ओऽ: the visarga with अ becomes ओ and the next अ drops (avagraha).
ए is not made from अः + अ.
-अः does not become -र् before अ; that happens after other vowels (इः, उः).
questions.explain: Same rule as श्लेष्मवतः + अति = श्लेष्मवतोऽति.
questions.teaches: A final -अः before अ becomes ओ and the अ is dropped, marked ऽ (श्लेष्मवतोऽत्युष्ण; बलवतोऽपि).

questions.q: What does पूर्वोक्ता in unit 7 mean?
optionExplain: उक्ता is a past participle: already stated.
No other teachers are named.
Right: पूर्व (before) + उक्ता (stated).
उक्ता means stated, not unstated.
questions.explain: पूर्वोक्ता = stated before: the unit points back, it gives nothing new.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 7 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are the clear parts of the short line.
questions.rule: तत्र = there; पूर्व = before; उक्ता = stated; साधनम् = remedy.

questions.q: Put the words of unit 7 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: There, stated before, mishap (and) remedy, and.
questions.teaches: Unit 7 is a pointer: there (in that case), the mishap as stated before, and the remedy.

questions.q: Which is the right split of पूर्वोक्ता?
optionExplain: पूर्वो and क्ता are not the words.
अ + ओ would give औ: पूर्वौक्ता.
अ + इ would give ए: पूर्वेक्ता.
Right: अ + उ → ओ: पूर्व + उक्ता = पूर्वोक्ता.
questions.explain: पूर्व (before) + उक्ता (stated).

questions.q: A student says unit 7 names a new drug for this mishap. What does the card say?
options: No drug; it points back to what was said before
It names a cold drink as the drug for this case
It forbids giving any remedy at all in this case
It names oil as the one drug of choice here
optionExplain: Right: पूर्वोक्ता (stated before) refers back; no drug is named in the line.
No drink or drug is named in the line.
The line has no verb and no negation.
No oil or drug is named in the line.
questions.explain: Unit 7 has no verb and names no drug; पूर्वोक्ता points back to what was stated before.
questions.rule: पूर्वोक्ता = stated before: a cross-reference, not a new remedy.

questions.q: Join the invented pair हित + उक्तम् as पूर्व + उक्ता is joined. Which is right?
optionExplain: औ is made from अ + ओ or औ, not अ + उ.
Right: अ + उ → ओ, as in पूर्वोक्ता.
The अ does not drop before उ.
आ is made from अ + अ, not अ + उ.
questions.explain: Same rule as पूर्व + उक्ता = पूर्वोक्ता.
questions.teaches: A final अ and an initial उ join into ओ (पूर्व + उक्ता → पूर्वोक्ता; हित + उक्तम् → हितोक्तम्).

questions.q: What does unit 8 say one should not apply if it still rises upward?
optionExplain: Oil is not named in this unit.
The unit says third, तृतीयम्.
Right: न तृतीयम् अवचारयेत्: one should not apply a third (medicine).
Water is not named in this unit.
questions.explain: The limit is a number: no third medicine.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 8 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are the clear words of the damaged line.
questions.rule: अतः = after this; ऊर्ध्वम् = upward; उत्तिष्ठति = rises; तृतीयम् = third.

questions.q: Put these clear words of unit 8 in the order of the text (the damaged compound left out).
questions.explain: Even after this, upward, it rises; not a third (medicine) should one apply.
questions.rule: अतोऽपि · ऊर्ध्वम् · उत्तिष्ठति · न · तृतीयम् · अवचारयेत्.
questions.teaches: Unit 8 states the case first (it still rises upward), then the limit (no third medicine).

questions.q: Which is the right split of अतोऽप्यूर्ध्वम्?
optionExplain: प्यूर्ध्वम् is not a word.
अ + अ would give आ: अतापि, with no ऽ.
पि is not a word; the word is अपि, even.
Right: अः + अ → ओऽ (अतोऽपि); इ before ऊ becomes य् (अप्यूर्ध्वम्).
questions.explain: अतः (after this) + अपि (even) + ऊर्ध्वम् (upward).
questions.rule: अः + अ → ओऽ; इ + ऊ → यू.

questions.q: What is the form of अवचारयेत्, as the word split gives it?
options: Causative optative, 3rd sg: one should apply
Causative absolutive: having first applied it
Causative present, 3rd sg: he applies it
Causative future, 3rd sg: he will apply
optionExplain: Right: The gram label is opt. 3 sg. caus. ava-√car.
An absolutive would end in -य (अवचार्य).
The present would be अवचारयति.
The future would be अवचारयिष्यति.
questions.explain: अवचारयेत् = one should apply: with न it states the limit.

questions.q: Like न ... अवचारयेत् (one should not apply), which invented sentence means one should not give milk?
optionExplain: ददाति is the present: he does not give.
Right: न with the optative दद्यात् (should give) forbids; क्षीरम् is the accusative object, like तृतीयम्.
दत्त्वा is an absolutive: not having given.
क्षीरेण is instrumental (by milk); the object needs the accusative क्षीरम्.
questions.explain: न + optative = one should not ...: न तृतीयम् अवचारयेत्; क्षीरं न दद्यात्.
questions.rule: न + optative 3rd sg = a prohibition (one should not ...).
questions.teaches: न with an optative states a prohibition, the thing forbidden in the accusative (न तृतीयम् अवचारयेत्; क्षीरं न दद्यात्).

questions.q: What does unit 9 say happens to the medicine under these conditions?
options: It turns into a poison inside
optionExplain: Going upward is the mishap of unit 6.
Going downward is the mishap of unit 2.
Right: भक्तवत् उपैति पाकम्: it undergoes digestion like food.
Poison is not named in the unit.
questions.explain: This mishap is neither upward nor downward: the medicine is digested like food.
questions.section: औषध का बिना शोधन पच जाना

questions.q: Match each word of unit 9 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These clear words give the first cause and the result.
questions.rule: क्रूरकोष्ठ = hard bowel; भेषजम् = medicine; भक्तवत् = like food; पाकम् = digestion.
questions.section: औषध का बिना शोधन पच जाना

questions.q: Put these clear words of unit 9 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Hard bowel, medicine, downward-acting, like food, undergoes, digestion.
questions.rule: क्रूरकोष्ठस्य · भेषजम् · अधोभागिकम् · भक्तवत् · उपैति · पाकम्.
questions.teaches: Unit 9 gives the cause first, then the medicine, then the result: it undergoes digestion like food.
questions.section: औषध का बिना शोधन पच जाना

questions.q: Unit 2 names a soft bowel (मृदुकोष्ठ). Which bowel does unit 9 name?
optionExplain: That is unit 2, where the emetic goes downward.
Dry is not the word in unit 9.
Empty is not the word in unit 9.
Right: क्रूर-कोष्ठस्य: of one with a hard bowel.
questions.explain: Soft bowel → emetic goes down (unit 2); hard bowel → medicine digested like food (unit 9).
questions.section: औषध का बिना शोधन पच जाना

questions.q: A patient has a hard bowel (क्रूरकोष्ठ). By unit 9, what may happen to the medicine he drinks?
options: It may be digested like food
It may go downward at once, far too strongly
It may rise upward and cause vomiting
It may stiffen the doṣas into knots
optionExplain: Right: क्रूरकोष्ठ is a cause named in unit 9; the result is भक्तवत् पाकम्.
Unit 9 says it is digested like food, not that it goes down.
Going upward is the purgative's mishap of unit 6.
Stiffened doṣas are not named in unit 9.
questions.explain: A hard bowel is named in unit 9 as a cause of the medicine being digested like food.
questions.section: औषध का बिना शोधन पच जाना

questions.q: Built like भक्तवत् (like food), which invented word means like milk?
optionExplain: This is the instrumental: by milk.
Right: -वत् after a noun means like that thing: क्षीर + वत्.
This is the ablative: from milk.
This is the plain noun: milk.
questions.explain: भक्त + वत् = like food; क्षीर + वत् = like milk.
questions.teaches: The indeclinable suffix -वत् means like (भक्तवत् = like food; क्षीरवत् = like milk).
questions.section: औषध का बिना शोधन पच जाना

questions.q: What do the aroused doṣas produce, according to unit 10, if not expelled in time?
options: A clean, light and empty bowel
optionExplain: Nothing good is said to follow; they produce vibhrama.
Hunger is not named in the unit.
Right: विभ्रमं कुर्वन्ति: they produce a disturbance.
Sleep is not named in the unit.
questions.explain: Aroused doṣas left inside past their time → vibhrama.
questions.rule: समुदीर्ण दोष + not expelled in time → विभ्रम.
questions.section: औषध का बिना शोधन पच जाना

questions.q: Match each word of unit 10 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words carry the condition and the result.
questions.rule: समुदीर्णाः = aroused; यथाकालम् = at the proper time; अनिर्ह्रियमाणाः = not being expelled; कुर्वन्ति = they produce.
questions.section: औषध का बिना शोधन पच जाना

questions.q: Put the parts of unit 10 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: There, the aroused doṣas, at the proper time, not being expelled, produce disturbance.
questions.rule: तत्र · समुदीर्णा दोषा · यथाकालम् · अनिर्ह्रियमाणा · विभ्रमं कुर्वंति.
questions.teaches: Unit 10 is a chain: aroused doṣas, not expelled in time, produce vibhrama.
questions.section: औषध का बिना शोधन पच जाना

questions.q: What is the form of अनिर्ह्रियमाणाः in unit 10?
options: An active optative verb: should expel
A past participle: something already expelled before
A negated passive present participle: not being expelled
optionExplain: An optative would end in -एत्; this is a participle.
A past participle would be निर्हृत; -यमाण is present passive.
An absolutive would end in -त्वा or -य.
Right: The gram label is pass. part. of nir-√hṛ, with the negative अ-.
questions.explain: अ (not) + निर्ह्रियमाण (being expelled), nominative plural agreeing with दोषाः.
questions.section: औषध का बिना शोधन पच जाना

questions.q: A physician leaves the aroused doṣas inside past the proper time. What does unit 10 predict?
optionExplain: Right: Not expelled at the proper time, they produce vibhrama.
The unit says they produce vibhrama.
The unit says nothing of leaving by themselves.
Strength is not named in the unit.
questions.explain: The condition is not being expelled yathākālam; the result is vibhrama.
questions.section: औषध का बिना शोधन पच जाना

questions.q: Built like यथाकालम् (at the proper time), what does the invented यथाबलम् mean?
optionExplain: यथा- means in keeping with, not against.
Right: यथा- + noun = in keeping with that noun: यथा + बलम्.
That would need a negative such as अ- or निर्-.
यथा- does not mean after.
questions.explain: यथाकालम् = according to (the proper) time; यथाबलम् = according to strength.
questions.teaches: यथा- before a noun makes an indeclinable meaning according to that noun (यथाकालम्, यथाबलम्).
questions.section: औषध का बिना शोधन पच जाना

questions.q: According to unit 11, what kind of bowel should he have?
options: Dry and rough in the bowel (रूक्ष)
optionExplain: The unit says well unctuous, the opposite of dry.
Fasting is not named in the unit.
Right: सु-स्निग्ध-कोष्ठम्: having a well-unctuous bowel.
Cooling is not named in the unit.
questions.explain: सुस्निग्धकोष्ठ = whose bowel is well unctuous.
questions.section: औषध का बिना शोधन पच जाना

questions.q: Match each word of unit 11 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words describe the patient and what he is given.
questions.rule: सुस्निग्ध = well unctuous; अनल्पम् = plentiful; अन्नम् = food; औषधम् = medicine.
questions.section: औषध का बिना शोधन पच जाना

questions.q: The word of unit 11 meaning plentiful, not little, is ____. Type it in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: अनल्पम् = अन् (not) + अल्पम् (little): plentiful.
questions.teaches: The negative अन्- before अल्प gives अनल्प, not little: plentiful.
questions.section: औषध का बिना शोधन पच जाना

questions.q: Which is the right split of चौषधम्?
optionExplain: चौ and षधम् are not the words.
अ + उ would give ओ: चोषधम्.
अ + इ would give ए: चेषधम्.
Right: अ + औ → औ: च + औषधम् = चौषधम्.
questions.explain: च (and) + औषधम् (medicine).
questions.section: औषध का बिना शोधन पच जाना

questions.q: Put the words of unit 11 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Him, well-unctuous in bowel, plentiful food and the medicine, should make drink.
questions.rule: तं · सुस्निग्धकोष्ठम् · अनल्पम् · अन्नं · चौषधं · पाययेत्.
questions.section: औषध का बिना शोधन पच जाना

questions.q: अनल्प is अन् + अल्प. Which invented word, built the same way, means not hot?
optionExplain: Right: Before a vowel the negative is अन्-: अन् + उष्ण = अनुष्ण.
Before a vowel the negative is अन्-, not अ-.
The vowel stays उ; nothing turns it into ओ.
The negative अ of अन्- is not dropped.
questions.explain: Same build as अन् + अल्प = अनल्प.
questions.teaches: Before a vowel the negative prefix is अन्- (अन् + अल्प = अनल्प; अन् + उष्ण = अनुष्ण).
questions.section: औषध का बिना शोधन पच जाना

questions.q: In unit 12, what happens to the doṣas of the medicine drunk in these conditions?
options: They are expelled upward at once
They are digested along with food
They move into the blood and skin
optionExplain: Nothing is said to go upward or out in unit 12.
Right: स्तब्धदोषं विग्रथितम्: with the doṣas stiffened, knotted, clumped.
Digestion like food was the case of unit 9 (05.03.9), not this one.
Blood and skin are not named in unit 12.
questions.explain: The result named is स्तब्धदोष (stiffened doṣas) and विग्रथित (knotted, clumped).
questions.rule: Unit 12: the doṣas are stabdha and vigrathita.
questions.section: स्तम्भित दोष और अधोभाग की गुरुता

questions.q: Match each word of unit 12 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Two of the causes, the cold treatment, and the clumped result.
questions.rule: कषायम् = decoction; रूक्षम् = dry; शीतोपचारेण = by cold treatment; विग्रथितम् = clumped.
questions.section: स्तम्भित दोष और अधोभाग की गुरुता

questions.q: Put these words of unit 12 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Decoction, dry, drunk, by cold treatment, with stiffened doṣas, becomes.
questions.rule: कषायम् · रूक्षं · पीतं · शीतोपचारेण · स्तब्धदोषं · भवति.
questions.teaches: Unit 12 lists the causes first (decoction, dry medicine, drunk, cold treatment) and the result last.
questions.section: स्तम्भित दोष और अधोभाग की गुरुता

questions.q: Which is the right split of शीतोपचारेण?
optionExplain: शीतो and पचारेण are not the words; they are शीत and उपचारेण.
There is no word ओपचारेण; अ + ओ would give औ (शीतौपचारेण).
Right: अ + उ → ओ: शीत + उपचारेण = शीतोपचारेण, by cold treatment.
पचारेण is not a word, and शीतः before प would stay शीतः, not शीतो.
questions.explain: शीत (cold) + उपचारेण (by treatment): अ + उ → ओ.
questions.rule: अ + उ → ओ across a compound join.
questions.section: स्तम्भित दोष और अधोभाग की गुरुता

questions.q: A dry medicine is drunk together with cold treatment. Which outcome does unit 12 lead you to expect?
options: The medicine goes upward out of the mouth
The medicine works faster and more strongly
The patient gets a burning pain in the anus
optionExplain: Going upward was the purgative case of unit 6 (05.03.6).
Unit 12 names failure, not a stronger action.
No burning or anal pain is named in unit 12.
Right: रूक्ष भेषज and शीतोपचार are both in the list; the result is stabdha-doṣa, vigrathita.
questions.explain: Each listed condition, joined by वा (or), leads to the stiffened, clumped, failed state.
questions.rule: Dry medicine or cold treatment → stiffened, clumped doṣas.
questions.section: स्तम्भित दोष और अधोभाग की गुरुता

questions.q: स्तब्धदोषम् means having stiffened doṣas. Which invented compound, in the same case and built the same way, means having little strength?
optionExplain: Right: Adjective + noun as a bahuvrīhi: अल्प (little) + बलम् (strength) = having little strength, like स्तब्ध + दोषम्.
The adjective stands first in this kind of compound: स्तब्ध-दोष, not दोष-स्तब्ध.
These are two separate words in different cases, not one compound.
This is an instrumental (by one ...), not the nominative form matching स्तब्धदोषम्.
questions.explain: Pattern: describing word + noun = 'having (such a) noun': स्तब्ध-दोष, अल्प-बल.
questions.rule: Bahuvrīhi: adjective first, then the noun; the whole describes someone or something.
questions.teaches: A bahuvrīhi puts the describing word first and the noun last, meaning 'having ...' (स्तब्धदोष = having stiffened doṣas; अल्पबल = having little strength).
questions.section: स्तम्भित दोष और अधोभाग की गुरुता

questions.q: In the vomiting case, how does unit 13 say he should be made to vomit again?
options: With a cold drink of water
optionExplain: The first clause uses वमनेन, vomiting, not a purgative.
Right: वमनेन भूयो वामयेत्: with vomiting one should make him vomit again.
Fasting is not named in unit 13.
Cold water is not named in unit 13.
questions.explain: The emesis case is answered by emesis again.
questions.rule: वमनेन भूयो वामयेत् = make him vomit again with vomiting.
questions.section: स्तम्भित दोष और अधोभाग की गुरुता

questions.q: Match each word of unit 13 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four words that set the case, the repeat and the timing.
questions.rule: तत्र = in that case; भूयः = again; वामयेत् = should make vomit; तृतीये = third.
questions.section: स्तम्भित दोष और अधोभाग की गुरुता

questions.q: Put these parts of unit 13 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: In that case, with vomiting, make vomit again; purge again; on the third day.
questions.rule: तत्र · वमनेन · भूयो वामयेत् · पुनर्विरेचयेत् · तृतीयेऽहनि.
questions.teaches: Unit 13 gives the emesis remedy first, then the purgation remedy, then the third-day case.
questions.section: स्तम्भित दोष और अधोभाग की गुरुता

questions.q: Which is the right split of तृतीयेऽहनि?
optionExplain: अः + अ would give ओऽ: तृतीयोऽहनि, not तृतीयेऽहनि.
There is no word इहनि; the word is अहनि, on the day.
Right: ए + अ: the ए stays and the अ is dropped, shown by the avagraha ऽ: तृतीयेऽहनि.
हनि is not the word; the ऽ marks the dropped अ of अहनि.
questions.explain: तृतीये (third, loc.) + अहनि (on the day): on the third day.
questions.rule: ए + अ → एऽ (the अ drops, marked by ऽ).
questions.section: स्तम्भित दोष और अधोभाग की गुरुता

questions.q: A patient oiled and sweated took a purgative that failed with doṣas stiffened. What does unit 13 prescribe?
optionExplain: The purgation case is answered by purging again, not by a change of route.
Cold treatment was one cause of failure in unit 12 (05.03.12).
Unit 13 repeats the cleansing; it does not stop it.
Right: स्निग्धस्विन्नस्य पुनर्विरेचयेत्: the oiled and sweated one should be purged again.
questions.explain: The cleansing that failed is repeated: emesis again, or purgation again.
questions.rule: Failed purgation in one oiled and sweated → purge again.
questions.section: स्तम्भित दोष और अधोभाग की गुरुता

questions.q: भूयः + वामयेत् gives भूयो वामयेत्. Join the invented pair रामः + वदति the same way. Which is right?
optionExplain: Right: अः before a voiced consonant (here व) becomes ओ: रामः + वदति = रामो वदति.
The visarga becomes र् only after a vowel other than अ/आ (पुनर्, as in पुनर्विरेचयेत्).
The visarga becomes स् only before त/थ, not before व.
अः does not turn into आ; before a voiced sound it becomes ओ.
questions.explain: Same rule as भूयः + वामयेत् = भूयो वामयेत्.
questions.rule: अः → ओ before a voiced consonant.
questions.teaches: A final अः becomes ओ before a voiced consonant (भूयः + वामयेत् → भूयो वामयेत्; रामः + वदति → रामो वदति).
questions.section: स्तम्भित दोष और अधोभाग की गुरुता

questions.q: In unit 14, by which two means should the patient be made to sweat?
options: A steam room and a pot of hot water
optionExplain: Neither is named in unit 14.
Right: पिण्डप्रस्तराभ्यां स्वेदयेत्: by lump and by layer fomentation.
Neither is named in unit 14.
Neither is named in unit 14.
questions.explain: The dual instrumental names two means: piṇḍa and prastara.
questions.rule: पिण्ड + प्रस्तर = the two means of sweating in unit 14.
questions.section: स्तम्भित दोष और अधोभाग की गुरुता

questions.q: Match each word of unit 14 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words set the occasion, the preparation and the action.
questions.rule: उभयोः = both; संशोधनयोः = the two purifications; अभ्यक्तम् = anointed; स्वेदयेत् = should make sweat.
questions.section: स्तम्भित दोष और अधोभाग की गुरुता

questions.q: Unit 14 ends: पिण्डप्रस्तराभ्यां ____ (one should make him sweat). Type it in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: स्वेदयेत् = causative optative of √स्विद्: one should make (him) sweat.
questions.teaches: The last word of unit 14 is स्वेदयेत्, should make sweat.
questions.section: स्तम्भित दोष और अधोभाग की गुरुता

questions.q: What is the form of पिण्डप्रस्तराभ्याम्, as the word split gives it?
options: Genitive plural: of the many lumps and layers
Instrumental dual: by the two, lump and layer
Nominative dual: the two, lump and layer
optionExplain: A genitive plural would end in -आणाम्/-आनाम्, not -आभ्याम्.
A locative singular would end in -ए, not -आभ्याम्.
Right: -आभ्याम् here is the instrumental dual of a dvandva: by lump and layer.
A nominative dual would end in -औ, not -आभ्याम्.
questions.explain: पिण्डप्रस्तराभ्याम् = by (the two) lump and layer: instrumental dual.
questions.rule: -आभ्याम् after a dvandva of two = by the two.
questions.section: स्तम्भित दोष और अधोभाग की गुरुता

questions.q: Which is the right split of उभयोश्च?
optionExplain: श्च is not a word; श् is the visarga of उभयोः before च.
ओश्च is not a word; the word is उभयोः, of/in both.
उभयो is not a form; the word is उभयोः, whose visarga becomes श् before च.
Right: A visarga before च becomes श्: उभयोः + च = उभयोश्च.
questions.explain: उभयोः (of/in both) + च (and).
questions.section: स्तम्भित दोष और अधोभाग की गुरुता

questions.q: पिण्ड + प्रस्तर gives पिण्डप्रस्तराभ्याम्. Which invented form means by the sun and the moon (सूर्य + चन्द्र)?
optionExplain: Right: A dvandva of two takes the dual: सूर्य-चन्द्र + -आभ्याम् = by the sun and the moon, like पिण्डप्रस्तराभ्याम्.
This is an instrumental singular; two members joined as a pair take the dual.
This is the genitive/locative dual: of or in the sun and the moon.
This is a nominative plural, not 'by'.
questions.explain: Same build as पिण्ड-प्रस्तर-आभ्याम्: two members, instrumental dual.
questions.rule: Dvandva of two + -आभ्याम् = by the two.
questions.teaches: A dvandva of two members takes the dual; by them = -आभ्याम् (पिण्डप्रस्तराभ्याम्, सूर्यचन्द्राभ्याम्).
questions.section: स्तम्भित दोष और अधोभाग की गुरुता

questions.q: In which part of the body does unit 15 place the heaviness and stiffness?
optionExplain: The head is not named in unit 15.
Right: अधोभागे: in the lower part; there the belly is very heavy and stiff.
Neither chest nor throat is named in unit 15.
The limbs are not named in unit 15.
questions.explain: The signs of unit 15 are placed अधोभागे, in the lower part.
questions.rule: Unit 15: signs in the अधोभाग, the lower part.
questions.section: स्तम्भित दोष और अधोभाग की गुरुता

questions.q: Match each word of unit 15 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Two words of the causes, one of the patient, one of the signs.
questions.rule: अकृत्वा = without having done; पीतवतः = of one who drank; सामस्य = with āma; शूलः = piercing pain.
questions.section: स्तम्भित दोष और अधोभाग की गुरुता

questions.q: Put these parts of unit 15 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Oiled and sweated, without vomiting, having drunk a purgative, with āma; colic, obstruction of wind and stool.
questions.rule: स्निग्धस्विन्नस्य · वमनमकृत्वा · विरेचनं पीतवतः · सामस्य · शूलो · वातपुरीषसंगश्च.
questions.teaches: Unit 15 gives the patients first (genitives) and the signs after, ending with भवति.
questions.section: स्तम्भित दोष और अधोभाग की गुरुता

questions.q: Which of these does unit 15 name as signs in the lower part?
options: Excessive heaviness and stiffness of the belly
optionExplain: Right: अत्यर्थ-गुरु-स्तब्ध-उदरता.
Burning (दहति) comes in 05.03.21, not here.
Right: वात-पुरीष-सङ्गः is named.
Vomiting is not named in unit 15.
Right: शूलः is named.
questions.explain: Three signs: heavy stiff belly, śūla, and obstruction of wind and stool.
questions.section: स्तम्भित दोष और अधोभाग की गुरुता

questions.q: A patient oiled and sweated drinks a purgative. Which omitted step does unit 15 name as one cause of trouble?
options: The oiling was not done first
The sweating was not done first
The emesis (वमन) was not done first
The meat broth was not given first
optionExplain: The patient is स्निग्ध, oiled: the oiling was done.
The patient is स्विन्न, sweated: the sweating was done.
Right: वमनमकृत्वा विरेचनं पीतवतः: having drunk the purgative without having done emesis.
No meat broth is named in unit 15.
questions.explain: Oiled and sweated, but no emesis before the purgative: one of the three cases.
questions.rule: Purgative without prior emesis → lower-part heaviness, colic, obstruction.
questions.section: स्तम्भित दोष और अधोभाग की गुरुता

questions.q: Like अकृत्वा (without having done), which invented form means without having drunk (√पा)?
optionExplain: This is an imperfect: he drank; it is not an absolutive at all.
This is a past participle: not drunk; it is not an absolutive.
This is a past active participle: one who has drunk.
Right: Negative अ- + the absolutive पीत्वा (having drunk) = without having drunk, like अ + कृत्वा.
questions.explain: Same build as अ + कृत्वा: अ + पीत्वा.
questions.teaches: Negative अ- before an absolutive in -त्वा means 'without having ...' (अकृत्वा, अपीत्वा).
questions.section: स्तम्भित दोष और अधोभाग की गुरुता

questions.q: What is the last step that unit 16 prescribes for the ayogin patient?
options: Make him vomit with salted water
Let him rest and fast for a week
Give him only a meat broth to drink
optionExplain: Right: पुनस्तीक्ष्णैर्विरेचयेत्: the main verb, the final step.
Vomiting is not named in unit 16.
Rest and fasting are not named in unit 16.
The meat broth is an earlier step, not the last one.
questions.explain: All earlier steps are absolutives; the finite verb विरेचयेत् is the last step.
questions.rule: Unit 16 ends with पुनस्तीक्ष्णैर्विरेचयेत्: purge again.
questions.section: स्तम्भित दोष और अधोभाग की गुरुता

questions.q: Put the steps of unit 16 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Decoction enema, feeding with broths, oil enema, further oiling, then purging.
questions.section: स्तम्भित दोष और अधोभाग की गुरुता

questions.q: Match each step of unit 16 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four absolutives: the steps done before the final purging.
questions.rule: आस्थाप्य = decoction enema; भोजयित्वा = fed; अनुवास्य = oil enema; उपस्नेह्य = oiled further.
questions.teaches: The four absolutives of unit 16 are the preparatory steps; विरेचयेत् is the goal.
questions.section: स्तम्भित दोष और अधोभाग की गुरुता

questions.q: Which is the right split of तैलेनानुवास्य?
optionExplain: नानुवास्य is not the word; the words are तैलेन (with oil) and अनुवास्य.
Right: अ + अ → आ: तैलेन + अनुवास्य = तैलेनानुवास्य, having given an oil enema with oil.
There is no word आनुवास्य; the absolutive is अनुवास्य.
तैलम् + अनुवास्य would give तैलमनुवास्य, with म्.
questions.explain: तैलेन (with oil) + अनुवास्य (having given anuvāsana).
questions.section: स्तम्भित दोष और अधोभाग की गुरुता

questions.q: Between the decoction enema and the oil enema, with what does unit 16 say the patient is fed?
optionExplain: Milk is not named; pippalī goes into the oil of the enema.
Rice gruel is not named in unit 16.
Right: जाङ्गलरसैश्च भोजयित्वा: having fed him with broths of dry-land animals.
Honey and water are not named in unit 16.
questions.explain: The feeding step uses जाङ्गलरस, broths of dry-land animals (standard: meat broths).
questions.rule: Step 2 of unit 16: feed with jāṅgala rasa.
questions.section: स्तम्भित दोष और अधोभाग की गुरुता

questions.q: आस्थाप्य has a prefix and ends in -य; भोजयित्वा has none and ends in -त्वा. Which invented form means having brought (आ + √नी)?
optionExplain: A prefixed verb does not take -त्वा; that ending is for verbs with no prefix.
This has no prefix: it means having led, not having brought (आ + √नी).
This is an optative: he should bring; it is not an absolutive.
Right: With a prefix (आ-) the absolutive takes -य: आनीय, like आ-स्थाप्य, अनु-वास्य.
questions.explain: Prefix + root → -य (आस्थाप्य, अनुवास्य, उपस्नेह्य); no prefix → -त्वा (भोजयित्वा).
questions.teaches: An absolutive takes -य when the verb has a prefix (आस्थाप्य, अनुवास्य, आनीय) and -त्वा when it has none (भोजयित्वा).
questions.section: स्तम्भित दोष और अधोभाग की गुरुता

questions.q: What does the medicine of unit 17 first do to the doṣas?
options: Fully expels them from the body
Calms them so they settle down
Carries them upward to the head
optionExplain: Right: भृशम् उत्क्लिश्य दोषान्: having greatly agitated the doṣas.
The unit names agitation and its ill effects, not expulsion.
उत्क्लिश्य means agitating, the opposite of calming.
The head is not named in unit 17.
questions.explain: The medicine stirs the doṣas up (उत्क्लेश) and then the effects follow.

questions.q: Match each effect named in unit 17 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The four members of the dvandva जाड्य-तन्द्रा-दौर्बल्य-अङ्गसाद.
questions.rule: जाड्य = dullness; तन्द्रा = drowsiness; दौर्बल्य = weakness; अङ्गसाद = sinking of the limbs.

questions.q: Put the four effects of unit 17 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Dullness, drowsiness, weakness, sinking of the limbs.
questions.teaches: The effects of the agitated doṣas run from dullness to sinking of the limbs.

questions.q: Which of these patients does unit 17 name?
optionExplain: Not here: the lean one comes in 05.03.23.
Right: कफ-उल्वणस्य is named.
Right: अति-स्निग्धस्य is named.
Right: मन्द-अग्नेः is named.
Not here: unit 17 names the very unctuous one, the opposite.
questions.explain: The patients of unit 17 are heavy, oily and slow: Kapha-abundant, very unctuous, heavy-bowelled, slow fire.

questions.q: Which is the right split of कफोल्वणस्यातिस्निग्धस्य?
optionExplain: कफो and ल्वणस्य are not the words; they are कफ and उल्वणस्य.
Right: अ + उ → ओ (कफोल्वण); अ + अ → आ (उल्वणस्यातिस्निग्धस्य).
There is no word ओल्वण; अ + ओ would give औ, not ओ.
उल्वणस्या and तिस्निग्धस्य are not the words; the join is -स्य + अति.
questions.explain: कफ-उल्वणस्य (of one with Kapha abundant) + अति-स्निग्धस्य (of one very unctuous).
questions.rule: अ + उ → ओ; अ + अ → आ.

questions.q: कफ + उल्वण gives कफोल्वण. Join the invented pair पित्त + उल्वण the same way. Which is right?
optionExplain: औ comes from अ + ओ or अ + औ, not from अ + उ.
The अ is not simply dropped; अ + उ merges into ओ.
Right: अ + उ → ओ: पित्त + उल्वण = पित्तोल्वण, with Pitta abundant.
व् is inserted only after उ/ऊ before a vowel, not after अ.
questions.explain: Same rule as कफ + उल्वण = कफोल्वण.
questions.teaches: A final अ and an initial उ merge into ओ (कफ + उल्वण → कफोल्वण; पित्त + उल्वण → पित्तोल्वण).

questions.q: According to unit 18, how should the action be done?
options: Only at night, in a cool room
optionExplain: The unit says शीघ्रम्, quickly, not slowly.
No meal is named in unit 18.
Neither time nor place is named in unit 18.
Right: तच्छीघ्रमुल्लिखेत्: one should scrape that up quickly.
questions.explain: शीघ्रम् = quickly: the one adverb of the unit.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 18 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The whole unit is these three words.
questions.rule: तत् = that; शीघ्रम् = quickly; उल्लिखेत् = should scrape up.

questions.q: Put the three words of unit 18 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: That, quickly, should scrape up.
questions.teaches: Unit 18 is three words: तत् (that), शीघ्रम् (quickly), उल्लिखेत् (should scrape up).

questions.q: Which is the right split of तच्छीघ्रम्?
optionExplain: Right: त् + श् → च्छ: तत् + शीघ्रम् = तच्छीघ्रम्.
तच् is not a word; the pronoun is तत्, changed by the following श्.
छीघ्रम् is not a word; the word is शीघ्रम्, quickly.
तच्छी and घ्रम् are not words.
questions.explain: तत् (that) + शीघ्रम् (quickly): the त् and श् join as च्छ.

questions.q: What is the form of उल्लिखेत्, as the word split gives it?
options: Optative 3rd singular: one should scrape up
optionExplain: A present would end in -ति (उल्लिखति), not -एत्.
Right: The gram label is opt. 3 sg. of ud-√likh: a rule-giving 'should'.
A past participle would end in -त (उल्लिखित).
An absolutive with a prefix would end in -य (उल्लिख्य).
questions.explain: -एत् marks the optative: the text prescribes (should ...).

questions.q: तत् + शीघ्रम् gives तच्छीघ्रम्. Join the invented pair तत् + शृणु (hear that) the same way. Which is right?
optionExplain: त् does not stay unchanged before श्; it becomes palatal.
त् becomes द् before voiced sounds; श् is not voiced.
Right: त् + श् → च्छ: तत् + शृणु = तच्छृणु, like तच्छीघ्रम्.
त् does not turn into श् here; the join gives च्छ.
questions.explain: Same rule as तत् + शीघ्रम् = तच्छीघ्रम्.
questions.teaches: A final त् before श् gives च्छ (तत् + शीघ्रम् → तच्छीघ्रम्; तत् + शृणु → तच्छृणु).

questions.q: In unit 19, what has been done to the patient first?
options: He has been given a cold bath
He has been fed a heavy meal
He has been bled from a vein
He has been made to fast (लङ्घित)
optionExplain: No bath is named in unit 19.
Feeding is not named; he is made to fast.
Bloodletting is not named in unit 19.
Right: लङ्घितम्: one made to fast; the first of the three descriptions.
questions.explain: The order of the unit: made to fast, fire kindled, made unctuous again, then purified.
questions.rule: Unit 19 starts with लङ्घित: made to fast.

questions.q: Put the words of unit 19 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Made to fast, fire kindled, again, unctuous, with sharp and hot (ones), should purify.
questions.rule: लंघितं · संधुक्षिताग्निं · पुनः · स्निग्धं · तीक्ष्णोष्णैः · विशोधयेत्.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 19 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Three preparations and the final action.
questions.rule: लङ्घितम् = made to fast; संधुक्षिताग्निम् = fire kindled; स्निग्धम् = unctuous; विशोधयेत् = should purify.
questions.teaches: Fasting, kindled fire and fresh oiling prepare the patient for the repeated purification.

questions.q: Which is the right split of तीक्ष्णोष्णैः?
optionExplain: Right: अ + उ → ओ: तीक्ष्ण + उष्णैः = तीक्ष्णोष्णैः, with sharp and hot (ones).
ष्णैः is not a word; the second member is उष्णैः, hot.
अः + उ would give तीक्ष्ण उष्णैः (the visarga drops), not one ओ.
There is no word ओष्ण; अ + ओ would give औ.
questions.explain: तीक्ष्ण (sharp) + उष्णैः (hot): a dvandva in the instrumental plural.

questions.q: Which pair of qualities does unit 19 want in what purifies him?
optionExplain: These are the qualities that cause bloating in 05.03.20.
