Right: तीक्ष्णोष्णैर्विशोधयेत्: one should purify with sharp and hot (ones).
Mildness was part of the trouble in 05.03.17; unit 19 asks for sharp.
Unit 19 names sharp and hot, not heavy and oily.
questions.explain: The purifying agents are qualified only as तीक्ष्ण and उष्ण.
questions.rule: Repeat cleansing: with तीक्ष्ण-उष्ण (sharp and hot).

questions.q: संधुक्षित + अग्निम् gives संधुक्षिताग्निम्. Which invented word joins दीप्त + अग्निम् (whose fire is bright)?
optionExplain: The two short अ do not leave a single short अ; they merge into आ.
ए comes from अ + इ, not from अ + अ.
Right: अ + अ → आ: दीप्त + अग्निम् = दीप्ताग्निम्, like संधुक्षिताग्निम्.
ओ comes from अ + उ, not from अ + अ.
questions.explain: Same rule as संधुक्षित + अग्निम्.
questions.teaches: A final अ and an initial अ merge into आ (संधुक्षित + अग्निम् → संधुक्षिताग्निम्; दीप्त + अग्निम् → दीप्ताग्निम्).

questions.q: What does the medicine produce in unit 20?
options: A burning fever in the whole body
optionExplain: Fever is not named in unit 20.
Bleeding is not named in unit 20.
Fainting is not named in unit 20.
Right: भृशमाध्मानं करोति: it produces great bloating.
questions.explain: The single effect named is ādhmāna, bloating, made great (भृशम्).
questions.rule: Unit 20: cold or dry medicine → bhṛśam ādhmānam.

questions.q: Match each patient word of unit 20 to its meaning.
pairs: for one having Vāta and phlegm
questions.explain: Four of the datives that name who is given the medicine.
questions.rule: वातश्लेष्मवते = Vāta and phlegm; रूक्षाय = dry; सोदावर्त्ताय = with udāvarta; मंदाग्नये = slow fire.

questions.q: Put these patient words of unit 20 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Vāta and phlegm, dry, with udāvarta, slow fire.
questions.teaches: Unit 20 names the patients (datives) before the medicine and its effect.

questions.q: Which qualities of the medicine does unit 20 name as producing the bloating?
optionExplain: Right: शीतं रूक्षं वा दत्तमौषधम्: a cold or dry medicine given.
These are the qualities prescribed for purifying in 05.03.19.
Unit 20 does not name heavy or oily.
No taste is named as the cause in unit 20.
questions.explain: Cold and dry are the two qualities joined by वा in unit 20.

questions.q: Unit 20: शीतं रूक्षं वा दत्तमौषधं भृशम् ____ करोति (produces great bloating). Type it in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: आध्मानम् = bloating (ādhmāna), the object of करोति.
questions.teaches: The effect of unit 20 is आध्मान, bloating.

questions.q: रूक्षाय means for one dry (dative). Which invented form means for one weak (दुर्बल)?
optionExplain: This is the instrumental: by one weak.
Right: -आय is the dative singular of an अ-stem: दुर्बलाय = for one weak, like रूक्षाय.
This is the genitive: of one weak.
This is the ablative: from one weak.
questions.explain: Same ending as रूक्षाय, सोदावर्त्ताय: -आय, for one ...
questions.teaches: The dative singular of an अ-stem ends in -आय and means 'for (one) ...' (रूक्षाय, दुर्बलाय).

questions.q: From what does unit 21 say the trouble arises?
options: From excess of blood in the veins
From too much sleep in the day
From a fall or blow to the belly
optionExplain: Blood is not named in unit 21.
Sleep is not named in unit 21.
Right: मलसङ्गात्: from obstruction of waste (mala); the ablative gives the cause.
No injury is named in unit 21.
questions.explain: The ablative मलसङ्गात् names the cause: the waste is obstructed.

questions.q: Match each phrase of unit 21 to its meaning.
pairs: pricking in the anus and bladder
questions.explain: Four of the symptoms and the simile that goes with the flanks.
questions.rule: दृतिवत् = like a leather bag; पार्श्वयोः = flanks; शिरःपृष्ठरुजा = head and back pain; पायुबस्तिनिस्तोदः = pricking.

questions.q: Put the symptoms of unit 21 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Burns the belly, inner pain, fullness of flanks, head and back pain, śvāsa, pricking in anus and bladder.
questions.rule: दहत्युदरम् · अंतःशूलं · पार्श्वयोरापूर्णता · शिरःपृष्ठरुजा · श्वासः · पायुवस्तिनिस्तोदश्च.
questions.teaches: Unit 21 lists the signs in this order: belly burning, inner pain, full flanks, head and back pain, śvāsa, pricking in anus and bladder.

questions.q: Which of these does unit 21 name?
options: Fullness of the flanks like a leather bag
optionExplain: Thirst is not named in unit 21.
Right: श्वासः is named.
Right: दृतिवत् पार्श्वयोः आपूर्णता.
Right: दहति उदरम्, it burns the belly.
Vomiting is not named in unit 21.
questions.explain: The symptoms: burning belly, inner śūla, full flanks, head and back pain, śvāsa, pricking in anus and bladder.
questions.rule: Unit 21 symptoms: belly burns · śūla · flanks full · head-back pain · śvāsa · anus-bladder pricking.

questions.q: To what does unit 21 compare the fullness of the two flanks?
optionExplain: No fruit is named in unit 21.
A drum is not named in unit 21.
A pot is not named in unit 21.
Right: दृतिवत्: like a leather bag, a full, blown-up skin bag.
questions.explain: -वत् makes a simile: दृति-वत्, like a leather bag.

questions.q: दहति + उदरम् gives दहत्युदरम्. Join the invented pair इति + उक्तम् the same way. Which is right?
optionExplain: Right: इ before a different vowel becomes य्: इति + उक्तम् = इत्युक्तम्, like दहत्युदरम्.
Two vowels are not left side by side; इ turns into य्.
ओ comes from अ + उ, not from इ + उ.
No र् is inserted between इ and उ; the इ itself turns into य्.
questions.explain: Same rule as दहति + उदरम् = दहत्युदरम्.
questions.rule: इ + a different vowel → य् + vowel.
questions.teaches: A final इ before a different vowel becomes य् (दहति + उदरम् → दहत्युदरम्; इति + उक्तम् → इत्युक्तम्).

questions.q: Which two conditions do the procedures of unit 22 take away?
optionExplain: Neither fever nor thirst is named in unit 22.
Right: उदावर्त-आनाह-हर: taking away udāvarta and ānāha.
Neither cough nor hiccup is named in unit 22.
Neither swelling nor itching is named in unit 22.
questions.explain: The procedures are qualified as उदावर्त-आनाह-हर.
questions.rule: Unit 22: procedures that remove udāvarta and ānāha.

questions.q: Put the procedures of unit 22 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Anointing, sweating, wick, kindling, powder, enema.
questions.rule: अभ्यङ्ग · स्वेद · वर्ति · दीपन · चूर्ण · बस्ति.

questions.q: Match each procedure of unit 22 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four of the six members of the compound.
questions.rule: अभ्यङ्ग = anointing; वर्ति = wick; चूर्ण = powder; बस्ति = medicated enema.
questions.teaches: The compound lists six procedures (abhyaṅga, sveda, varti, dīpana, cūrṇa, basti), all qualified as taking away udāvarta and ānāha.

questions.q: Which of these are in the list of unit 22?
optionExplain: Emesis is not in the list of unit 22.
Right: दीपन is the fourth procedure.
Bloodletting is not in the list of unit 22.
Right: वर्ति is the third procedure.
Right: स्वेद is the second procedure.
questions.explain: The list: abhyaṅga, sveda, varti, dīpana, cūrṇa, basti.
questions.rule: Unit 22 list: अभ्यङ्ग · स्वेद · वर्ति · दीपन · चूर्ण · बस्ति.

questions.q: A patient bloated after a cold, dry medicine. Following unit 22, which treatment fits?
options: A further cold and dry medicine
optionExplain: Cold and dry medicine caused the bloating (05.03.20).
Unit 22 prescribes six active procedures.
Right: उपचरेत् with abhyaṅga, sveda, varti, dīpana, cūrṇa and basti.
Neither fasting nor cold water is named in unit 22.
questions.explain: The bloated patient of 05.03.20-21 is treated with the six procedures of unit 22.
questions.rule: Bloating (with udāvarta, ānāha) → abhyaṅga, sveda, varti, dīpana, cūrṇa, basti.

questions.q: क्रियाभिः is the instrumental plural of क्रिया (by procedures). Which invented form means by garlands (माला)?
optionExplain: This is the dual (by two garlands), not the plural.
This is the instrumental singular: by a garland.
This is the locative plural: in garlands.
Right: An आ-stem feminine takes -आभिः in the instrumental plural: मालाभिः, like क्रियाभिः.
questions.explain: Same ending as क्रियाभिः: -आभिः.
questions.teaches: A feminine आ-stem makes its instrumental plural in -आभिः (क्रिया → क्रियाभिः; माला → मालाभिः).

questions.q: What does the strong medicine of unit 23 bring about?
options: Ādhmāna, a great bloating of the belly
optionExplain: Right: परिकर्त्तिकामापादयति: it brings about parikartikā, cutting-around pain.
Great bloating came from a cold or dry medicine in 05.03.20.
Stiffened, clumped doṣas were the failure of 05.03.12.
Going upward was the purgative case of 05.03.6.
questions.explain: The result of unit 23 is परिकर्तिका: cutting-around pain in the lower belly and anus.
questions.rule: Strong medicine in a weak or unready patient → parikartikā.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 23 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four of the patients named in the instrumental: by whom the strong medicine is taken.
questions.rule: क्षामेण = lean; अल्पबलेन = little strength; स्विन्नेन = sweated; सामेन = with āma.

questions.q: Put these parts of unit 23 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Lean and weak, soft bowel and fire, dry or oiled, sweated or with āma; strong medicine taken; brings parikartikā.
questions.rule: क्षामेणाल्पबलेन · मृदुकोष्ठाग्निना · रूक्षेण स्निग्धेन वा · स्विन्नेन सामेन वा · बलवदौषधमुपयुक्तं · परिकर्त्तिकामापादयति.
questions.teaches: Unit 23 names the patients first (instrumentals), then the strong medicine, and the result last.

questions.q: Which of these patients does unit 23 name as taking the strong medicine?
options: One with soft bowel and soft fire
optionExplain: Right: मृदु-कोष्ठ-अग्निना is named.
Right: सामेन is named.
Not here: unit 23 names soft fire, the opposite.
Right: क्षामेण is named first.
Not here: the hard bowel comes in 05.03.33.
questions.explain: Unit 23's patients are weak or unready: lean, weak, soft bowel and fire, dry or oiled, sweated or with āma.
questions.rule: Unit 23: क्षाम · अल्पबल · मृदुकोष्ठाग्नि · रूक्ष/स्निग्ध · स्विन्न/साम.

questions.q: A lean, weak man takes a strong medicine. Which doṣas does unit 23 say it corrupts?
optionExplain: Kapha is not named in unit 23.
Right: सपित्तमनिलं परिदूष्य: having corrupted wind together with Pitta.
The pair is Pitta with anila (wind), not with Kapha.
Neither blood nor Kapha is named in unit 23.
questions.explain: स-पित्तम् अनिलम्: wind with Pitta is what the strong medicine corrupts.
questions.rule: Unit 23: the strong medicine corrupts अनिल with पित्त.

questions.q: बलवत् + औषधम् gives बलवदौषधम्. Join the invented pair महत् + औषधम् (a great medicine) the same way. Which is right?
optionExplain: The त् does not stay voiceless before a vowel; it becomes द्.
त् becomes न् only before a nasal, and nothing doubles here.
Right: त् before a vowel becomes द्: महत् + औषधम् = महदौषधम्, like बलवदौषधम्.
The त् cannot simply drop; it turns into द्.
questions.explain: Same rule as बलवत् + औषधम् = बलवदौषधम्.
questions.rule: Final त् → द् before a vowel.
questions.teaches: A final त् becomes द् before a vowel (बलवत् + औषधम् → बलवदौषधम्; महत् + औषधम् → महदौषधम्).

questions.q: Which places does unit 24 name for the cutting pain?
options: Head, eyes, ears and the throat
Knees, ankles, hands and the feet
Navel, bladder, anus and male organ
optionExplain: None of these is named in unit 24.
None of these is named in unit 24.
None of these is named in unit 24.
Right: नाभिबस्तिगुदमेढ्रे: in the navel, bladder, anus and male organ.
questions.explain: The four places are one dvandva in the locative: नाभि-बस्ति-गुद-मेढ्र.

questions.q: Match each place named in unit 24 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The four members of the locative dvandva नाभिबस्तिगुदमेढ्रे.
questions.rule: नाभि = navel; बस्ति = bladder; गुद = anus; मेढ्र = male organ.

questions.q: Put these parts of unit 24 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: There; in navel, bladder, anus, male organ; with burning; cutting pain; obstruction of wind; and binding.
questions.rule: तत्र · नाभिबस्तिगुदमेढ्रे · सदाहं · परिकर्त्तनम् · अनिलसंगो · विष्टंभश्च.
questions.teaches: Unit 24 gives the place first, then three signs: burning cutting pain, obstruction of wind, binding.

questions.q: What does अनिलसंगः mean in unit 24?
options: Excess of wind in the belly
optionExplain: Right: अनिल (wind) + सङ्ग (sticking, obstruction): wind held back.
सङ्ग means sticking, obstruction, not excess.
सङ्ग is the opposite: the wind is held back.
Pain is परिकर्तन; सङ्ग is obstruction.
questions.explain: अनिलसङ्गः is a tatpuruṣa: obstruction of wind (anila).
questions.rule: सङ्ग = obstruction; अनिलसङ्ग = obstruction of wind.

questions.q: A patient with parikartikā describes the pain at his navel. Which kind of pain does unit 24 name there?
optionExplain: Coldness is not named; the pain is with burning.
Right: सदाहं परिकर्त्तनम्: cutting-around pain together with burning.
Itching is not named in unit 24.
Numbness is not named; the pain is a cutting one.
questions.explain: स-दाहम् (with burning) + परिकर्तनम् (cutting around).

questions.q: विष्टम्भः + च gives विष्टंभश्च. Join the invented pair रामः + च the same way. Which is right?
optionExplain: Before च the visarga becomes the palatal श्, not the dental स्.
अः becomes ओ only before a voiced sound; च is not voiced.
Right: A visarga before च becomes श्: रामः + च = रामश्च, like विष्टम्भः + च.
The visarga does not simply drop before च.
questions.explain: Same rule as विष्टम्भः + च = विष्टम्भश्च.
questions.teaches: A visarga before च becomes श् (विष्टम्भः + च → विष्टम्भश्च; रामः + च → रामश्च).

questions.q: What kind of enema does unit 25 prescribe for parikartikā?
options: Sharp enemas mixed with cow urine
Milk enemas boiled with long pepper
optionExplain: The oil enema comes in 05.03.27, with liquorice oil.
Sharp ones and urine belonged to 05.03.16.
Long pepper is not named in unit 25.
Right: पिच्छाबस्तिभिरास्थापयेत्: give āsthāpana with slimy enemas.
questions.explain: The first remedy is āsthāpana with picchā-bastis.

questions.q: Match each member of कृष्णतिलमधुकमधुयुक्तैः to its meaning.
questions.explain: The ingredients joined with the slimy enemas.
questions.rule: कृष्ण = black; तिल = sesame; मधुक = probably liquorice; मधु = honey.

questions.q: Put these words of unit 25 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Him; joined with black sesame, liquorice and honey; with slimy enemas; one should give āsthāpana.
questions.teaches: Unit 25 names the patient, then the ingredients, then the enema, and the verb last.

questions.q: Unit 25 names both मधुक and मधु. What does the unit data take मधुक to be?
optionExplain: Right: madhuka: probably liquorice (probable), kept apart from madhūka (mahua).
मधु is honey; मधुक is a separate item in the list.
The data keeps मधुक apart from मधूक, mahua.
Sesame is तिल, a separate member of the list.
questions.explain: मधुक ≠ मधु ≠ मधूक: probably liquorice.

questions.q: Which is the right split of पिच्छाबस्तिभिरास्थापयेत्?
optionExplain: रास्थापयेत् is not a word; the र् is the visarga of -भिः.
Right: A visarga after इ before a vowel becomes र्: -भिः + आ- = -भिरा-.
-भ्यः + आ would give -भ्य आस्थापयेत्, not -भिरा-.
भिरास्थापयेत् is not a word; -भिः is the case ending.
questions.explain: पिच्छाबस्तिभिः (with slimy enemas) + आस्थापयेत् (should give āsthāpana).

questions.q: पिच्छाबस्तिभिः is the instrumental plural of बस्ति: with enemas. Which invented form means with fires (अग्नि)?
optionExplain: This is the instrumental singular: with fire, one.
This is the locative plural: in fires.
Right: An इ-stem takes -भिः in the instrumental plural: बस्ति-भिः, अग्नि-भिः.
This is the accusative plural: fires (as object).
questions.explain: Same ending as बस्तिभिः: -भिः.
questions.teaches: An इ-stem noun takes -भिः in the instrumental plural (बस्तिभिः with enemas; अग्निभिः with fires).

questions.q: In unit 26, what is the milk boiled with?
options: The rind of the pomegranate fruit
A paste of sesame and deodar
optionExplain: These were joined with the slimy enemas of 05.03.25.
Pomegranate rind is added to curd in 05.03.30.
That paste comes in 05.03.32, with hot water.
Right: क्षीरिवृक्षशृतक्षीरेण: with milk boiled with the milk-bearing trees.
questions.explain: The compound reads: kṣīri-vṛkṣa (milky trees) – śṛta (boiled) – kṣīra (milk).

questions.q: Match each member of क्षीरिवृक्षशृतक्षीरेण to its meaning.
questions.explain: The whole unit is this one compound and वा.
questions.rule: क्षीरि = milk-bearing; वृक्ष = tree; शृत = boiled; क्षीरेण = with milk.

questions.q: Unit 26 reads क्षीरिवृक्षशृत____ वा; the blank is the word for with milk. Type it in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: क्षीरेण = with milk, instrumental singular of क्षीर.
questions.teaches: The last member of the compound is क्षीरेण, with milk.

questions.q: What does शृत mean in क्षीरिवृक्षशृतक्षीरेण?
optionExplain: Right: शृत = boiled (the glossary's fixed rendering): milk boiled with the trees.
Cooling is not named; शृत means boiled.
Curd (दधि) comes in 05.03.30; शृत means boiled.
No sweetening is named; शृत means boiled.
questions.explain: शृत-क्षीर = boiled milk.

questions.q: A physician offers this patient the option introduced by वा in unit 26. What does he prepare?
optionExplain: That drink comes in 05.03.31.
Right: क्षीरिवृक्षशृतक्षीरेण वा: or with milk boiled with the milk-bearing trees.
That food comes in 05.03.30.
That paste comes in 05.03.32.
questions.explain: Unit 26 offers, with वा, milk boiled with the kṣīrivṛkṣa; the line names no single tree.
questions.rule: Unit 26: or milk boiled with kṣīrivṛkṣa.

questions.q: क्षीरिवृक्ष-शृत-क्षीर means milk boiled with milky trees. Which invented compound, built the same way, means water boiled with deodar?
optionExplain: This would be deodar boiled with water: the liquid must come last.
शृत must follow what the liquid is boiled with, not stand first.
Right: Same order: what it is boiled with (देवदारु) + शृत + the liquid (जल).
This has no word for water; it is only 'boiled with deodar'.
questions.explain: Pattern: X-शृत-liquid = liquid boiled with X.
questions.rule: In X-शृत-Y, Y is the liquid boiled with X.
questions.teaches: In a compound X-शृत-Y the last member is the liquid and X is what it is boiled with (क्षीरिवृक्षशृतक्षीर; देवदारुशृतजल).

questions.q: What kind of enema does unit 27 prescribe?
options: An enema of cold water alone
optionExplain: Āsthāpana came in 05.03.25; here the verb is अनुवासयेत्.
The slimy enemas were in 05.03.25.
Cold water is sprinkled on him; it is not the enema.
Right: अनुवासयेत्: one should give anuvāsana, the oil enema.
questions.explain: The verb अनु-√वस् (causative) names the oil enema.
questions.rule: Unit 27: anuvāsana with ghee-maṇḍa and liquorice oil.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 27 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words describe the patient before the oil enema.
questions.rule: शीताम्बु = cold water; परिषिक्तम् = sprinkled; पयसा = with milk; भुक्तवन्तम् = one who has eaten.

questions.q: Put these parts of unit 27 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Sprinkled with cold water, and him, having eaten with milk; with ghee-maṇḍa, with liquorice oil; give anuvāsana.
questions.rule: शीतांबुपरिषिक्तं · चैनं · पयसा भुक्तवंतं · घृतमंडेन · यष्टीमधुकतैलेन · अनुवासयेत्.
questions.teaches: Unit 27 first describes the patient (sprinkled, fed with milk), then the means, and ends with the verb.

questions.q: What is the patient's state before the oil enema in unit 27?
options: Sprinkled with cold water, fed with milk
Fasted, and sweated with a hot bolus
Purged, and given a decoction to drink
Oiled, and fed honey with hot water
optionExplain: Right: शीताम्बुपरिषिक्तं ... पयसा भुक्तवन्तम्: both describe him.
Neither fasting nor sweating is named in unit 27.
Neither is named in unit 27.
Honey and hot water are not named in unit 27.
questions.explain: Two accusatives describe the patient: sprinkled with cold water; having eaten with milk.
questions.rule: Before anuvāsana: cold-water sprinkling and a meal with milk.

questions.q: Which is the right split of चैनं?
optionExplain: अ + इ gives ए (चेनम्), not ऐ; and इनम् is not the pronoun.
Right: अ + ए → ऐ: च + एनम् = चैनम्, and him.
चे and नम् are not the words here.
There is no word चः; the particle is च.
questions.explain: च (and) + एनम् (him).

questions.q: च + एनम् gives चैनम्. Join the invented pair न + एव (not at all) the same way. Which is right?
optionExplain: ए would come from अ + इ, not from अ + ए.
No य् is inserted between अ and ए.
Right: अ + ए → ऐ: न + एव = नैव, like च + एनम् = चैनम्.
The two vowels do not stand side by side; they merge into ऐ.
questions.explain: Same rule as च + एनम्.
questions.teaches: A final अ and an initial ए merge into ऐ (च + एनम् → चैनम्; न + एव → नैव).

questions.q: What kind of procedure does verse 28 approve for the lean patient?
optionExplain: These are for the one with āma, in the second line.
Sharp and hot are not named in verse 28.
Cold is not named; dry food is for the one with āma.
Right: क्षामस्य मधुरो बृंहणश्च सर्वो विधिरिष्टः: for the lean, every sweet and bulking procedure.
questions.explain: The first line is for the lean (क्षाम): sweet and bulking.

questions.q: Match each term of verse 28 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The key terms of the two regimens.
questions.rule: बृंहण = bulking; लङ्घन = fasting; दीपन = kindling; अन्नपान = food and drink.

questions.q: Put these parts of verse 28 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: For the lean: sweet and bulking, every procedure desired; with āma: fasting and kindling, light dry hot food and drink.
questions.rule: क्षामस्य · मधुरो बृंहणश्च · सर्वो विधिरिष्टः · सामे · लंघनो दीपनश्च · लघुरूक्षोष्णं चान्नपानं.
questions.teaches: Verse 28 gives the lean patient's regimen in line one and the āma patient's regimen in line two.

questions.q: In verse 28, for whom is light, dry and hot food and drink approved?
options: The one with a hard bowel
optionExplain: Right: सामे ... लघुरूक्षोष्णं चान्नपानं: in one with āma, light, dry, hot food and drink.
The lean one gets sweet and bulking procedures.
That patient is not taken up in verse 28.
The hard bowel comes in 05.03.33, not here.
questions.explain: Line two belongs to the सामे (locative): the one with āma.

questions.q: Which pair from verse 28 is a true pair of opposites, one for each patient?
optionExplain: Both belong to the lean one; they are not opposed.
Right: Bulking is for the lean, fasting for the one with āma: they pull in opposite directions.
Both describe the āma patient's food; they are not opposed.
Both belong to the āma patient; they work together.
questions.explain: One regimen builds the body up, the other lightens it.

questions.q: लघुरूक्षोष्णम् joins रूक्ष + उष्णम्. Join the invented pair मधुर + उष्णम् the same way. Which is right?
optionExplain: औ comes from अ + ओ or अ + औ, not from अ + उ.
The अ is not dropped; अ + उ merge into ओ.
Right: अ + उ → ओ: मधुर + उष्णम् = मधुरोष्णम्, like रूक्ष + उष्णम् = रूक्षोष्णम्.
No व् is inserted after अ.
questions.explain: Same rule as रूक्ष + उष्णम् = रूक्षोष्णम्.
questions.teaches: A final अ and an initial उ merge into ओ (रूक्ष + उष्णम् → रूक्षोष्णम्; मधुर + उष्णम् → मधुरोष्णम्).

questions.q: What state does निरामीभूते, the opening word of unit 29, describe?
optionExplain: निर्- means without; the āma has gone.
That was क्षाम, अल्पबल of 05.03.23.
That is क्रूरकोष्ठ of 05.03.33.
Right: निर्-आमी-भूते: when he has become free of raw (āma) matter.
questions.explain: निर्-आमी-भूत = become free of āma: the clear opening of a low-confidence unit.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 29 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Clear words of unit 29: the occasion, the food, the addition and the verb.
questions.rule: निरामीभूते = free of āma; दधि = curd; दाडिमत्वचा = with pomegranate rind; युञ्जीत = should employ.

questions.q: Put these clear parts of unit 29 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Free of āma; light, kṣāra, sour; when Vāta is in excess; curd with sour; joined with pomegranate rind; employ in food and drink.
questions.rule: निरामीभूते · लघुक्षाराम्लं · वातेऽधिके · दधि साम्लं · दाडिमत्वचा युक्तं · भोजने पाने च युंजीत.
questions.teaches: Unit 29 gives the general diet after āma first, then the curd for excess Vāta, and the verb last.

questions.q: Which part of the pomegranate does unit 29 add to the curd?
optionExplain: Right: दाडिमत्वचा युक्तम्: joined with the rind of dāḍima (pomegranate).
The juice goes with ghee in 05.03.31, not with the curd here.
Seeds are not named in unit 29.
The root is not named in unit 29.
questions.explain: दाडिम-त्वचा: instrumental of त्वच्, skin, rind.

questions.q: A patient free of āma now has Vāta in excess. What does unit 29 give him?
options: Curd with sour, with pomegranate rind
optionExplain: That was the enema milk of 05.03.26.
Right: वातेऽधिके दधि साम्लं दाडिमत्वचा युक्तम्: curd with sour, joined with pomegranate rind.
That was the oil enema of 05.03.27.
These went into the slimy enemas of 05.03.25.
questions.explain: Excess Vāta: the curd preparation.
questions.rule: Vāta in excess → sour curd with dāḍima rind.

questions.q: वाते + अधिके gives वातेऽधिके. Join the invented pair वने + अस्मिन् (in this forest) the same way. Which is right?
optionExplain: The ए does not turn into आ.
ए + अ here gives एऽ, not अय्.
Right: ए + अ: the ए stays and the अ drops, shown by ऽ: वनेऽस्मिन्.
ओऽ comes from अः + अ, not from ए + अ.
questions.explain: Same rule as वाते + अधिके = वातेऽधिके.
questions.teaches: A final ए before अ stays, and the अ drops, marked by ऽ (वाते + अधिके → वातेऽधिके; वने + अस्मिन् → वनेऽस्मिन्).

questions.q: What should the patient drink, according to unit 30?
optionExplain: Curd with the rind was the food of 05.03.30.
That milk was for the enema of 05.03.26.
Honey and hot water are not named in unit 30.
Right: सदाडिमरसं च सर्पिः पिबेत्: drink ghee with pomegranate juice.
questions.explain: The drink is सर्पिः (ghee) with dāḍima juice.

questions.q: Match each part of unit 30 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The whole unit: with pomegranate juice, ghee, should drink.
questions.rule: स- = together with; दाडिमरस = pomegranate juice; सर्पिः = ghee; पिबेत् = should drink.

questions.q: Put the words of unit 30 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: With pomegranate juice, and, ghee, should drink.
questions.teaches: Unit 30 names what goes with the ghee first, then the ghee, and the verb last.

questions.q: In सदाडिमरसम्, what does the prefix स- add?
optionExplain: Right: स- in a bahuvrīhi = having, together with: with pomegranate juice.
Without would be अ- or निर्-, the opposite of स-.
Very much would be अति- or भृशम्, not स-.
Good would be सु-, not स-.
questions.explain: स-दाडिम-रसम् = (ghee) together with pomegranate juice.

questions.q: A student reads सर्पिः in unit 30 as snake. What does the unit data give for it?
options: A snake, as the word sounds
optionExplain: Snake is सर्प; सर्पिः (sarpis) is ghee.
Right: सर्पिः is the neuter s-stem sarpis, ghee; snake is सर्प.
Sesame oil would be तिलतैल; सर्पिः is ghee.
Honey is मधु; सर्पिः is ghee.
questions.explain: सर्पिस् (n.) = ghee; do not confuse with सर्प.

questions.q: सदाडिमरसम् means together with pomegranate juice. Which invented word, built the same way, means together with honey (मधु)?
optionExplain: अ- means without: without honey.
निर्- means without: free of honey.
Right: स- + मधु = together with honey, like स- + दाडिमरस.
सु- means good: good honey.
questions.explain: Same build as स-दाडिमरस.
questions.rule: स- + noun = together with that noun.
questions.teaches: स- before a noun makes a bahuvrīhi 'together with ...' (सदाडिमरस with pomegranate juice; समधु with honey).

questions.q: With which liquid does unit 31 pair the paste?
optionExplain: Cold water was sprinkled on the patient in 05.03.27.
Boiled milk was the enema of 05.03.26.
The juice went with ghee in 05.03.31.
Right: उष्णांबुना: with hot water.
questions.explain: उष्ण-अम्बुना = with hot water.
questions.rule: Unit 31: the paste with hot water.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 31 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The whole unit apart from वा.
questions.rule: उष्णाम्बुना = with hot water; तिल = sesame; देवदारु = deodar cedar; कल्कम् = paste.

questions.q: What kind of preparation is the कल्क of unit 31?
optionExplain: Right: कल्क = paste (Hindi लुगदी): the drugs ground wet.
A decoction is कषाय / क्वाथ / निर्यूह, not कल्क.
Fermented drinks are not named; कल्क is a paste.
A dry powder is चूर्ण, not कल्क.
questions.explain: कल्क = paste.
questions.teaches: कल्क is a paste (लुगदी), distinct from a decoction (क्वाथ) or a powder (चूर्ण).

questions.q: Which is the right split of उष्णांबुना?
optionExplain: अः + अ would give उष्णोऽम्बुना, not उष्णाम्बुना.
Right: अ + अ → आ: उष्ण + अम्बुना = उष्णाम्बुना (printed with anusvara, उष्णांबुना).
बुना is not a word; the second member is अम्बुना.
बुना is not a word; the second member is अम्बुना, and उष्ण is a compound member with no ending.
questions.explain: उष्ण (hot) + अम्बुना (with water).

questions.q: Which of these drugs are in the paste of unit 31?
optionExplain: Right: तिल is the first member.
Not here: palāśa comes in 05.03.35.
Right: देवदारु is the second member.
Not here: madhuka was in the enema of 05.03.25.
Not here: dāḍima comes in 05.03.30-31.
questions.explain: The paste is तिल-देवदारु-कल्क: sesame and deodar.

questions.q: उष्ण + अम्बुना gives उष्णाम्बुना. Join the invented pair उष्ण + अन्नम् (hot food) the same way. Which is right?
optionExplain: The two अ do not leave one short अ; they merge into आ.
ए comes from अ + इ, not from अ + अ.
Right: अ + अ → आ: उष्ण + अन्नम् = उष्णान्नम्.
ओ comes from अ + उ, not from अ + अ.
questions.explain: Same rule as उष्ण + अम्बुना.
questions.teaches: A final अ and an initial अ merge into आ (उष्ण + अम्बुना → उष्णाम्बुना; उष्ण + अन्नम् → उष्णान्नम्).

questions.q: In unit 32, what does the mild purifying medicine fail to do?
optionExplain: It does agitate them: उत्क्लेश्य, having agitated.
The outflow is mixed with Pitta and Kapha; that happens.
Reaching the bowel is not what the unit denies.
Right: दोषान्न निर्हरति: it does not expel the doṣas.
questions.explain: Agitated but not expelled: that is the failure of unit 32.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 32 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The patient, the medicine and the result.
questions.rule: क्रूरकोष्ठ = hard bowel; बहुदोष = many doṣas; शोधनम् = purifying; परिस्रवति = flows out all round.

questions.q: Put these parts of unit 32 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Hard bowel; mild or unctuous; purifying medicine applied; having agitated; does not expel the doṣas; flows out.
questions.rule: क्रूरकोष्ठस्य · मृदु स्निग्धं वा · शोधनमवचारितम् · उत्क्लेश्य · दोषान्न निर्हरति · परिस्रवति.
questions.teaches: Unit 32 runs patient → weak medicine → agitation → no expulsion → outflow.

questions.q: Which qualities of the purifying medicine does unit 32 name?
optionExplain: Not here: sharp ones are the later cure of 05.03.36.
Not named in unit 32.
Right: स्निग्धं वा is named.
Right: मृदु is named.
Right: अल्प-मात्रा is named.
questions.explain: The medicine was too weak for this patient: small dose, mild or unctuous.

questions.q: A hard-bowelled patient with many doṣas got a mild purifying medicine. With what does unit 32 say the outflow is mixed?
optionExplain: Right: पित्तकफसंसृष्टम्: mixed with Pitta and Kapha.
Neither blood nor Vāta is named in unit 32.
Vāta is not named; the outflow is with Pitta and Kapha.
Food and water are not named in unit 32.
questions.explain: पित्त-कफ-संसृष्टम् = mixed with Pitta and Kapha.
questions.rule: Parisrava: outflow mixed with Pitta and Kapha.

questions.q: क्रूरकोष्ठस्य means of one with a hard bowel. Which invented form, built the same way, means of one with a soft bowel?
optionExplain: The describing word comes first in this compound: मृदु-कोष्ठ.
Right: Bahuvrīhi: मृदु (soft) + कोष्ठ, genitive -स्य, like क्रूर-कोष्ठस्य.
This is the instrumental (by one ...), not the genitive.
These are two separate words: soft, of the bowel.
questions.explain: Same build as क्रूरकोष्ठस्य.
questions.rule: Adjective + कोष्ठ as a bahuvrīhi = having such a bowel.
questions.teaches: A bahuvrīhi of adjective + कोष्ठ names the patient by his bowel (क्रूरकोष्ठ hard-bowelled; मृदुकोष्ठ soft-bowelled).

questions.q: Which of these is named in unit 33?
optionExplain: Fever is not named in unit 33.
Vomiting is not named in unit 33.
Right: कण्डू is one member of the long list.
Thirst is not named in unit 33.
questions.explain: Eight troubles in one dvandva; itching is one of them.

questions.q: Match each trouble of unit 33 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four members of the dvandva.
questions.rule: गौरव = heaviness; शोष = drying; कण्डू = itching; पाण्डुता = paleness.

questions.q: Put these first six troubles of unit 33 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Binding, heaviness, drying, koṭha, itching, paleness (then sinking of the limbs and piercing pain).
questions.rule: विष्टम्भ · गौरव · शोष · कोठ · कण्डू · पाण्डुता.
questions.teaches: The list of unit 33 runs viṣṭambha, gaurava, śoṣa, koṭha, kaṇḍū, pāṇḍutā, aṅgasāda, śūla.

questions.q: What does the unit data take कोठ to be?
options: Certainly a large boil that is filled with pus
The bowel, the same as कोष्ठ
Probably wheals, a rash like urticaria
optionExplain: The data gives wheals (probable), not a boil, and not as certain.
कोष्ठ is the bowel; कोठ is a skin eruption.
Fever is not what कोठ names.
Right: koṭha: wheals, an urticaria-like eruption (probable).
questions.explain: कोठ ≠ कोष्ठ: a skin eruption, probably wheals.

questions.q: After a failed mild purification a patient shows these. Which belong to unit 33's list?
optionExplain: Right: गौरव.
Not named in unit 33.
Right: पाण्डुता.
Not here: burning cutting pain was the parikartikā of 05.03.24.
Right: शूल, the last member.
questions.explain: The list: viṣṭambha, gaurava, śoṣa, koṭha, kaṇḍū, pāṇḍutā, aṅgasāda, śūla.
questions.rule: Unit 33: eight troubles; burning and thirst are not among them.

questions.q: च + आपादयति gives चापादयति. Join the invented pair च + आगच्छति the same way. Which is right?
optionExplain: Right: अ + आ → आ: च + आगच्छति = चागच्छति.
ए comes from अ + इ, not from अ + आ.
औ comes from अ + ओ/औ, not from अ + आ.
The long आ is not lost; अ + आ gives आ.
questions.explain: Same rule as च + आपादयति = चापादयति.
questions.teaches: A final अ and an initial आ merge into आ (च + आपादयति → चापादयति; च + आगच्छति → चागच्छति).

questions.q: What is added to the decoctions in unit 34?
optionExplain: Urine is not named in unit 34.
Right: मधुयुक्तैः: joined with honey.
Salt is not named in unit 34.
Oil is not named in unit 34.
questions.explain: The decoctions are मधु-युक्त, joined with honey.

questions.q: Match each plant of unit 34 to its identification in the data.
questions.explain: Four of the five plants with the data's identifications.
questions.rule: धव = axlewood; अश्वकर्ण = probably sal; पलाश = flame of the forest; वला = country mallow.

questions.q: Put the five plants of unit 34 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Tiniśa, dhava, aśvakarṇa, palāśa, valā.
questions.teaches: Unit 34's decoction lists five trees and shrubs: tiniśa, dhava, aśvakarṇa, palāśa, valā.

questions.q: Which plant of unit 34 has only a probable identification in the data?
optionExplain: palāśa is a standard identification.
dhava is a standard identification.
Right: aśvakarṇa: probably sal; the other four are standard.
tiniśa is a standard identification.
questions.explain: Four standard, one probable: aśvakarṇa.

questions.q: Which is the right split of धवाश्वकर्ण?
optionExplain: अः + अ would give धवोऽश्वकर्ण, not धवाश्व-.
धवाश् and वकर्ण are not words.
श्वकर्ण is not the plant; the plant is अश्वकर्ण.
Right: अ + अ → आ: धव + अश्वकर्ण = धवाश्वकर्ण.
questions.explain: धव (axlewood) + अश्वकर्ण (probably sal), members of one dvandva.

questions.q: मधुयुक्तैः + आस्थापयेत् gives मधुयुक्तैरास्थापयेत्. Join the invented pair तैः + उक्तम् (said by them) the same way. Which is right?
optionExplain: Right: A visarga after ऐ before a vowel becomes र्: तैः + उक्तम् = तैरुक्तम्.
The visarga does not simply drop here; it becomes र्.
No य् comes in; the visarga becomes र्.
The visarga becomes स् only before त/थ, not before a vowel.
questions.explain: Same rule as मधुयुक्तैः + आस्थापयेत्.
questions.teaches: A visarga after ऐ before a vowel becomes र् (मधुयुक्तैः + आस्थापयेत् → मधुयुक्तैरास्थापयेत्; तैः + उक्तम् → तैरुक्तम्).

questions.q: When does unit 35 have the patient purified again?
options: While the outflow is still running
Before any oiling has been done
Only after three days of fasting
optionExplain: The unit waits until the outflow has subsided.
Right: उपशान्तपरिस्रवम्: one whose flowing out has subsided.
He is made unctuous again before purification.
Fasting and days are not named in unit 35.
questions.explain: उपशान्त-परिस्रव: the outflow has stopped first.

questions.q: Put the words of unit 35 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Whose outflow has subsided, and, again made unctuous, with sharp (ones), should purify.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 35 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The condition, the preparation and the action.
questions.rule: उपशान्त = subsided; परिस्रव = flowing out; उपस्निग्धम् = made further unctuous; शोधयेत् = should purify.
questions.teaches: Unit 35: once the outflow subsides, oil again, then purify with sharp ones.

questions.q: Which is the right split of पुनरुपस्निग्धं?
optionExplain: रुपस्निग्धम् is not a word; the र् is the visarga of पुनः.
पुनरु and पस्निग्धम् are not words.
Right: A visarga after उ before a vowel becomes र्: पुनः + उप- = पुनरुप-.
There is no word रुपस्निग्धम्; the word is उपस्निग्धम्.
questions.explain: पुनः (again) + उपस्निग्धम् (made further unctuous).

questions.q: Which quality does unit 35 want in what purifies him, unlike the failed medicine of 05.03.33?
optionExplain: Mild was the failed medicine of 05.03.33.
Cold is not named in unit 35.
Heavy is not named in unit 35.
Right: तीक्ष्णैः शोधयेत्: purify with sharp (ones).
questions.explain: Mild failed; sharp is prescribed for the repeat purification.

questions.q: उपशान्तपरिस्रवम् means him whose outflow has subsided. Which invented word means him whose pain (शूल) has subsided?
optionExplain: Right: Bahuvrīhi: उपशान्त + शूल, accusative -म्, like उपशान्त-परिस्रवम्.
This is the instrumental (by one ...), not the accusative 'him'.
These are two separate words, not one compound.
अन्- negates: whose pain has not subsided.
questions.explain: Same build as उपशान्त-परिस्रवम्.
questions.rule: Participle + noun as a bahuvrīhi = one whose (noun) is so.
questions.teaches: A bahuvrīhi of participle + noun describes a person (उपशान्तपरिस्रव = whose outflow has subsided; उपशान्तशूल = whose pain has subsided).

questions.q: In verse 36, what does one who has drunk medicine do with the urge?
options: Waits until it comes by itself
Sends it forth or holds it back
Lets it pass and then sleeps
optionExplain: Waiting is not in the verse; it names sending forth or holding back.
Right: वेगमुदीरयति निगृह्णाति वा: he sends forth the urge, or holds it back.
Sleep is not named; the two acts are udīrayati and nigṛhṇāti.
No physician is named in the 'when' clause.
questions.explain: The 'when' clause of verse 36 names two acts: उदीरयति (sends forth) and निगृह्णाति (holds back).
questions.rule: Verse 36: वेग sent forth or held back after drinking medicine.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 36 to its meaning.
questions.explain: शुद्धे is a locative 'when purified'; योजयेत् an optative; the last three come from the second line.
questions.rule: शुद्धे = when purified; योजयेत् = should employ; वेग = urge; उदीरयति = sends forth; निगृह्णाति = holds back.

questions.q: Put these parts of the second line of verse 36 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: One who has drunk medicine; when; sends forth the urge; holds back; or.
questions.teaches: The second line of verse 36 is a 'when' clause: subject, यदा, then two verbs joined by वा.

questions.q: Which split of पीतौषधो is right?
optionExplain: षधः is no word; the औ comes from अ + औ.
अ + उ gives ओ, not औ.
Right: अ + औ → औ, and अः → ओ before the voiced य of यदा: पीत + औषधः.
ए before औ would give अयौ, not औ.
questions.explain: पीत-औषधः is a bahuvrīhi: one by whom medicine has been drunk.

questions.q: According to verse 36, at what point are the powders (चूर्ण) to be employed?
options: While the urge is held back
Only after the next trouble arises
Once the patient has been purified
optionExplain: The verse places them after purification, not before.
Holding back the urge is the new trouble, not the time for powders.
The verse ties the powders to purification, not to a trouble.
Right: शुद्धे च ... योजयेत्: when he is purified, one should employ them.
questions.explain: The locative शुद्धे sets the time: once purified.
questions.rule: Verse 36: शुद्धे → powders and the like.

questions.q: पीतौषधः + यदा gives पीतौषधो यदा. Join the invented pair रामः + यदा the same way. Which is right?
optionExplain: Right: अः becomes ओ before a voiced consonant such as य: रामः + यदा = रामो यदा.
अः does not become अर्; that change belongs to other vowels (इः → इर्).
ः becomes श् before च, छ or श, never before य.
Dropping to आ is the rule for आः, not for अः.
questions.explain: Same rule as पीतौषधः + यदा = पीतौषधो यदा.
questions.rule: अः → ओ before a voiced consonant.
questions.teaches: A final अः becomes ओ before a voiced consonant (पीतौषधः + यदा → पीतौषधो यदा; रामः + यदा → रामो यदा).

questions.q: What arises in the patient according to unit 37?
optionExplain: Parikartikā was the trouble of 05.03.23-24.
Right: तदा प्रवाहिकाऽस्य जायते: then pravāhikā arises in him.
Bloating was the trouble of 05.03.20-21.
Parisrava was the trouble of 05.03.33-34.
questions.explain: Unit 37 names pravāhikā, the new trouble after the urge is forced or held.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 37 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four words: तदा answers the यदा of 05.03.38.
questions.rule: तदा = then; प्रवाहिका = dysentery; अस्य = in him; जायते = arises.

questions.q: Put the words of unit 37 in the order of the text, after the split.
questions.explain: Then; pravāhikā; in him; arises.
questions.teaches: Unit 37 opens with तदा, which closes the यदा ... तदा sentence begun in 05.03.38.

questions.q: What does the name प्रवाहिका literally say, according to the card?
optionExplain: That is parikartikā, a different trouble.
That is the trouble of 05.03.42.
Right: प्र-√वह्: to flow forth; the data glosses pravāhikā 'a flowing forth'.
That is closer to ādhmāna, bloating.
questions.explain: प्रवाहिका comes from प्र + √वह् (carry, flow): flowing forth.

questions.q: Which modern name does the unit data give for pravāhikā, and with which confidence word?
optionExplain: The tag in the data is standard, not disputed.
The data names dysentery, not diarrhoea.
Colic is not the data's equivalent.
Right: The data: usual modern equivalent dysentery, tagged standard.
questions.explain: Pravāhikā = dysentery (standard): painful straining with mucus and blood.

questions.q: Complete the invented sentence ततो ज्वरो ____ (then fever arises). Type it in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: जायते (3 sg. present of √जन्) means 'arises', as in प्रवाहिकाऽस्य जायते.
questions.teaches: जायते = arises (√जन्, present, 3rd person singular), used of any trouble that comes up: ज्वरो जायते.

questions.q: What does the patient pass in unit 38?
optionExplain: Right: कफमुपविशति: he passes Kapha.
Pitta is not named in unit 38.
Undigested food is not named here.
Pus is not named in unit 38.
questions.explain: The object of उपविशति is कफम्.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 38 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The five descriptions of the Kapha, in the text's order.
questions.rule: स-दाह-शूल = with burning and pain; स-पिच्छ = with slime; श्वेत = white; कृष्ण = black; स-रक्त = with blood.

questions.q: Put these parts of unit 38 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: In that; with burning and pain; with slime; white, black or with blood; flowing forth violently; passes Kapha.
questions.rule: तस्यां · सदाहशूलं · सपिच्छं · श्वेतं कृष्णं सरक्तं वा · भृशं प्रवहमानः · कफमुपविशति.
questions.teaches: Unit 38 lists the qualities of the Kapha first and names the Kapha and the verb last.

questions.q: Which of these does unit 38 name as qualities of the Kapha passed?
optionExplain: Right: सपिच्छम् is named.
Right: श्वेतम् is named.
Not named: the unit has burning, the opposite.
Not named: yellow is not in unit 38.
Right: कृष्णम् is named.
questions.explain: Unit 38: with burning and pain, with slime, white, black, or with blood.

questions.q: A patient with pravāhikā strains hard at stool. Which words of unit 38 describe how he flows forth?
optionExplain: This describes the Kapha: with burning and pain.
Right: भृशम् = violently; प्रवहमानः = flowing forth.
This only says 'in that' (the pravāhikā).
This is what he passes, not how he flows.
questions.explain: भृशम् प्रवहमानः: flowing forth violently.

questions.q: स- + रक्त gives सरक्त, with blood. Which word means with foam, from फेन (foam)?
optionExplain: अ- means 'without', the opposite.
सु- means 'good, well', not 'with'.
Right: स- = with: स + फेन = सफेन, like स + रक्त = सरक्त.
The prefix comes first, not at the end.
questions.explain: The prefix स- forms a bahuvrīhi 'with X', as सपिच्छ, सरक्त, सदाहशूल.
questions.teaches: The prefix स- makes 'with X' (सरक्त with blood, सपिच्छ with slime; invented सफेन with foam).

questions.q: By which procedure does unit 39 say pravāhikā should be treated?
options: A separate procedure of its own
optionExplain: Ādhmāna is not named in unit 39.
Ayoga is not named in unit 39.
The unit borrows parisrava's procedure.
Right: परिस्रवविधिना: by the procedure of parisrava.
questions.explain: Unit 39 points to the procedure of parisrava.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 39 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The four words of unit 39 after the split.
questions.rule: तम् = him; परिस्रव = oozing; विधिना = by the procedure; उपचरेत् = should treat.

questions.q: Put the words of unit 39 in the order of the text, after the split.
questions.explain: Him; of parisrava; by the procedure; should treat.
questions.teaches: Unit 39 is one clause: object, the means (an instrumental compound), then the optative verb.

questions.q: Which split of विधिनोपचरेत् is right?
optionExplain: Right: आ + उ → ओ: विधिना + उपचरेत् = विधिनोपचरेत्.
पचरेत् is no word; the ओ is the join of आ + उ.
इ before उ would give यु, not ओ.
औ before उ would give आवु, not ओ.
questions.explain: विधिना is the instrumental of विधि: by the procedure.

questions.q: A student reads unit 39 to learn the steps of treatment. What does he find there?
options: Only the name of parisrava's procedure
Cold water, then food with milk
optionExplain: No steps are listed in unit 39.
Right: The data: the procedure it refers to is not stated in this line.
No steps are listed in unit 39.
No steps are listed in unit 39.
questions.explain: Unit 39 refers to a procedure; it does not spell it out.
questions.rule: Unit 39 names a procedure, no steps.

questions.q: विधिना + उपचरेत् gives विधिनोपचरेत्. Join the invented pair यथा + उक्तम् the same way. Which is right?
optionExplain: औ comes from अ/आ + ओ/औ, not from आ + उ.
The two vowels do not stay apart here; they join.
Right: आ + उ → ओ: यथा + उक्तम् = यथोक्तम्.
The आ does not vanish; आ + उ gives ओ.
questions.explain: Same rule as विधिना + उपचरेत्.
questions.teaches: अ or आ followed by उ joins to ओ (विधिना + उपचरेत् → विधिनोपचरेत्; यथा + उक्तम् → यथोक्तम्).

questions.q: In unit 40, holding back which things agitates the doṣas?
options: Urine, faeces, wind and the like
Sleep, thirst, hunger and the like
Tears, sneezes, yawns and the like
Medicine, belching, vomiting and the like
optionExplain: Those urges are not named in unit 40.
These are not named in unit 40.
These are not named in unit 40.
Right: भेषजोद्गारच्छर्द्यादीनां निग्रहात्: from holding back medicine, belching, vomiting and the like.
questions.explain: The compound lists भेषज, उद्गार, छर्दि, then आदि.
questions.rule: Unit 40: holding back भेषज · उद्गार · छर्दि.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 40 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Words of the cause (निग्रहात्, उद्गार, छर्दि), the path (उपाश्रित्य) and the result (घोरम्).
questions.rule: निग्रह = holding back; उद्गार = belching; छर्दि = vomiting; उपाश्रित्य = having resorted to; घोर = dreadful.

questions.q: Put the steps of unit 40 in the order the text gives them.
items: Medicine, belching, vomiting are held back
Vāta and the others are agitated
They bring on a dreadful affliction
questions.explain: Drunk medicine; holding back; doṣas agitated; they go to the heart; a dreadful affliction.
questions.rule: पीतौषध → निग्रह → वातादयः कुपिताः → हृदयमुपाश्रित्य → घोरम् आवहन्ति.
questions.teaches: Unit 40 is a causal chain: holding back after medicine → agitated doṣas → they settle in the heart → a dreadful affliction.

questions.q: Whom does वातादयः (Vāta and the others) cover, according to the unit data?
optionExplain: Right: The data: Vāta and the others = the doṣas Vāta, Pitta, Kapha.
आदयः (and the others) adds more than Vāta.
Blood is not among the 'others' in the data.
Vāta is named first in वातादयः.
questions.explain: वात + आदयः: Vāta and the others, i.e. the three doṣas.

questions.q: After an emetic, a man forcibly stops his belching. Where does unit 40 say the agitated doṣas settle?
optionExplain: The head is not named in unit 40.
Right: हृदयमुपाश्रित्य: having resorted to the heart.
The belly is not named in unit 40.
The joints are not named in unit 40.
questions.explain: The path of unit 40 ends at the heart (हृदय).

questions.q: वात + आदयः gives वातादयः, Vāta and the others. Join the invented pair पित्त + आदयः the same way. Which is right?
optionExplain: The long आ of आदयः cannot shorten.
ए comes from अ + इ, not from अ + आ.
Right: अ + आ → आ: पित्त + आदयः = पित्तादयः.
Inside a compound the vowels join; they do not stay apart.
questions.explain: Same rule as वात + आदयः.
questions.teaches: अ + आ joins to आ (वात + आदयः → वातादयः; पित्त + आदयः → पित्तादयः, 'Pitta and the others').

questions.q: From what does the patient's torment come in unit 41?
options: Affliction of the chief vital spot
optionExplain: Blood loss is not the cause in unit 41.
Bloating was ādhmāna, another trouble.
Cold water is not named in unit 41.
Right: प्रधानमर्मोपतापात्: from affliction of the chief vital spot (marma).
questions.explain: The ablative उपतापात् gives the cause: affliction of the chief marma.

questions.q: Match each sign of unit 41 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five of the signs, all clear in the print.
questions.rule: मोह = bewilderment; हिक्का = hiccup; कास = cough; कटकटायति = gnashes; उद्वृताक्ष = eyes turned up.

questions.q: Put these parts of unit 41 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Cause; tormented by pains; gnashes teeth; eyes turned up; bites tongue.
questions.rule: प्रधानमर्मोपतापात् · वेदनाभिरत्यर्थमातुरः पीड्यते · दंतान्कटकटायति · उद्वृताक्षो · जिव्हां खादयति.
questions.teaches: Unit 41 gives the cause first, then the pains, and ends with the acts of the mouth and eyes.

questions.q: Which of these signs does unit 41 name?
optionExplain: Right: उद्वृताक्षः is named.
Not named in unit 41.
Right: कास is named.
Right: हिक्का is named.
Not named in unit 41.
questions.explain: Unit 41 names bewilderment, hiccup, cough, saliva, side-pain, trembling, lost consciousness, gnashing, turned-up eyes, tongue-biting.
questions.rule: हिक्का · कास · उद्वृताक्ष are in unit 41; fever and thirst are not.

questions.q: A watcher sees the patient bite his tongue. Which word of unit 41 says 'bites'?
optionExplain: Right: जिव्हां खादयति: he bites (literally 'makes eat') the tongue.
This is the gnashing of the teeth.
This means 'is tormented'.
This is the patient, not an act.
questions.explain: खादयति is literally 'makes eat'; the data renders it 'bites'.

questions.q: उपतापात् is the ablative: from affliction. Which form says from anger, from क्रोध, in the same case?
optionExplain: -स्य is the genitive, 'of anger'.
Right: a-stem ablative singular -आत्: क्रोध → क्रोधात्, like उपताप → उपतापात्.
-ए is the locative, 'in anger'.
-अम् is the accusative.
questions.explain: The ablative of an a-stem ends in -आत् and can give the cause: 'from'.
questions.teaches: An a-stem noun takes -आत् in the ablative singular, which can name a cause (उपतापात् from affliction; क्रोधात् from anger).

questions.q: What name does unit 42 say they give this condition?
optionExplain: That is the trouble of 05.03.23-24.
That is the trouble of 05.03.39.
Right: तं हृदयापसरणमाहुः: they call it hṛdayāpasaraṇa.
That is the trouble of 05.03.20.
questions.explain: आहुः (they call) gives the name: हृदयापसरण.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 42 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The physician (भिषक्), how he acts (शीघ्रम्, अमुह्यन्), the sweating and the verb.
questions.rule: भिषक् = physician; शीघ्रम् = quickly; अमुह्यन् = not bewildered; धान्यस्वेद = grain-sweating; दद्यात् = should give.

questions.q: Put these parts of unit 42 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: The name; to him the physician; having sweated with grains; a sharp avapīḍa; should give.
questions.rule: तं हृदयापसरणमाहुः · तस्मै भिषक् · धान्यस्वेदेन परिस्वेद्य · तीक्ष्णमवपीडं · दद्यात्.
questions.teaches: Unit 42 names the condition first, then the physician, the sweating, and the sharp avapīḍa last.

questions.q: What does अमुह्यन् say about the physician in unit 42?
options: He acts slowly, after long thought
He calls a second physician to help
He waits for the urge to return
optionExplain: The unit says शीघ्रम्, quickly.
No second physician is named.
Waiting is not in unit 42.
Right: अ- (not) + मुह्यन् (being bewildered): not being bewildered.
questions.explain: अमुह्यन् is a present participle with the negative अ-.

questions.q: The patient has been sweated with grains. What kind of avapīḍa does unit 42 tell the physician to give?
optionExplain: Right: तीक्ष्णमवपीडं दद्यात्: he should give a sharp avapīḍa.
The unit says तीक्ष्ण, the opposite of mild.
Cold is not named in unit 42.
Oily is not named for the avapīḍa.
questions.explain: तीक्ष्णम् qualifies अवपीडम्.

questions.q: अ- before मुह्यन् gives अमुह्यन्, not being bewildered. Which form means not knowing, from जानन्?
optionExplain: अन्- is used only before a vowel.
Right: Before a consonant the negative prefix is अ-: अ + जानन् = अजानन्.
नि- is not the negative prefix.
Changing the ending does not negate the word.
questions.explain: Same pattern as अमुह्यन्.
questions.rule: Negative अ- before a consonant, अन्- before a vowel.
questions.teaches: The negative prefix is अ- before a consonant and अन्- before a vowel (अमुह्यन् not bewildered; अजानन् not knowing).

questions.q: Which treatment does unit 43 name?
optionExplain: Purging is not named in unit 43.
The oil enema comes later, in 05.03.50.
Right: वमनम्: vomiting-treatment.
No enema is named in unit 43.
questions.explain: The last word of unit 43 is वमनं.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 43 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The members of the three words of unit 43.
questions.rule: यष्टीमधुक = liquorice; मिश्र = mixed; तण्डुल = rice grain; अम्बु = water; वमन = vomiting-treatment.

questions.q: Put the words of unit 43 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Mixed with liquorice; with rice-water; vomiting-treatment.
questions.teaches: Unit 43 names the added drug, then the liquid it is mixed in, and the treatment last.

questions.q: What is mixed into the rice-water in unit 43?
optionExplain: Honey was mixed in the enema of 05.03.35, not here.
Salt is not named in unit 43.
Oil is not named in unit 43.
Right: यष्टीमधुकमिश्रेण: mixed with yaṣṭīmadhuka (liquorice, standard).
questions.explain: The drug named with -मिश्र is यष्टीमधुक.

questions.q: A physician prepares the vamana of unit 43. Which liquid carries the liquorice?
optionExplain: Right: तंदुलांबुना: with taṇḍula-water (rice-water).
Milk is not named in unit 43.
Plain warm water is not named here.
Gruel is not named in unit 43.
questions.explain: तण्डुल + अम्बु: water of rice grain.

questions.q: तण्डुल + अम्बुना gives तण्डुलाम्बुना. Join the invented pair शीत + अम्बुना (with cold water) the same way. Which is right?
optionExplain: The two अ join to a long आ; it is not dropped.
Right: अ + अ → आ: शीत + अम्बुना = शीताम्बुना.
ओ comes from अ + उ, not from अ + अ.
ए comes from अ + इ, not from अ + अ.
questions.explain: Same rule as तण्डुल + अम्बुना.
questions.teaches: Two short अ join to a long आ (तण्डुल + अम्बुना → तण्डुलाम्बुना; शीत + अम्बुना → शीताम्बुना).

questions.q: What does unit 44 offer as the other means of vamana?
optionExplain: Sweets are not named in unit 44.
Sour things are not named in unit 44.
Right: कटुभिर्वा: or with pungents.
Salty things are not named in unit 44.
questions.explain: Unit 44 offers कटु (pungent) things as the alternative.

questions.q: Match each part of unit 44 to its meaning.
questions.explain: कटुभिः = कटु + -भिः; वा joins it as an alternative to the liquorice rice-water of 05.03.45.

questions.q: Unit 44 offers vamana with pungents. Type the stem for 'pungent': ____. Type it in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: कटु = pungent (taste); कटुभिः = with pungents.
questions.teaches: कटु is the stem of कटुभिः: pungent.

questions.q: Which split of कटुभिर्वा is right?
optionExplain: भिर्वा is no word; -भिः is the ending of कटु.
There is no अर्वा here, and the ई is not printed.
र्वा is no word; the र् comes from the visarga.
Right: इः → इर् before a voiced sound: कटुभिः + वा = कटुभिर्वा.
questions.explain: The र् of कटुभिर्वा is the visarga of कटुभिः before व.

questions.q: In unit 44, what does वा (or) set the pungents against?
optionExplain: Right: The data: one statement, 'vamana with ... or with pungents'.
The avapīḍa is a separate step, not the vamana.
Sweating is not a means of vamana.
The oil enema belongs to another trouble.
questions.explain: Unit 44 continues 05.03.45: vamana with liquorice rice-water, or with pungents.

questions.q: कटु takes -भिः: कटुभिः, with pungents. Which form says with the teachers, from गुरु?
optionExplain: -णा is the instrumental singular, 'with a teacher'.
Right: u-stem instrumental plural -भिः: गुरु → गुरुभिः, like कटु → कटुभिः.
-भ्यः is the dative or ablative plural.
-णाम् is the genitive plural, 'of the teachers'.
questions.explain: Same ending as कटुभिः.
questions.teaches: u-stems take -भिः in the instrumental plural (कटुभिः with pungents; गुरुभिः with the teachers).

questions.q: What does unit 45 say to do first with the remainder of the doṣa?
options: Draw it out with a strong purge
Leave it to pass away by itself
Burn it out with kṣāra at once
optionExplain: No purge is named in unit 45.
The unit treats the remainder; it is not left.
Right: दोषशेषं पाचनीयैः पाचयेत्: cook the remainder with pācanīyas.
Kṣāra is not named in unit 45.
questions.explain: पाचयेत् (should cause to cook) acts on दोषशेषम्.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 45 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The two steps: cooking the remainder, giving bastis by prominence.
questions.rule: दोषशेष = remainder; पाचनीय = to be cooked; उच्छ्रय = prominence; बस्ति = enema; वितरेत् = should give.

questions.q: Put these parts of unit 45 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Then; the remainder of the doṣa; should cook with pācanīyas; and according to prominence; should give bastis.
questions.rule: ततो · दोषशेषं · पाचनीयैः पाचयेत् · यथादोषोच्छ्रयं च · बस्तीन् वितरेत्.
questions.teaches: Unit 45 has two optative clauses joined by च: first the cooking, then the bastis.

questions.q: By what does unit 45 set the choice of bastis?
optionExplain: The season is not named in unit 45.
Age is not named in unit 45.
The fire (agni) is not named here.
Right: यथादोषोच्छ्रयम्: according to the prominence of the doṣa.
questions.explain: यथा + दोष + उच्छ्रय: according to the doṣa's height, prominence.

questions.q: After the vamana, some doṣa remains in the patient. Which steps does unit 45 give?
options: Give bastis by the doṣa's prominence
optionExplain: Not here: the avapīḍa was in 05.03.44.
Right: पाचनीयैः पाचयेत्.
Right: यथादोषोच्छ्रयं बस्तीन् वितरेत्.
Not here: grain-sweating was in 05.03.44.
questions.explain: Unit 45: cooking with pācanīyas and bastis by prominence.

questions.q: दोष + उच्छ्रय gives दोषोच्छ्रय. Join the invented pair महा + उत्सवः (a great festival) the same way. Which is right?
optionExplain: Right: आ + उ → ओ: महा + उत्सवः = महोत्सवः.
औ comes from अ/आ + ओ/औ, not + उ.
Inside a compound the vowels join.
The आ does not vanish; it joins with उ to ओ.
questions.explain: Same rule as दोष + उच्छ्रय.
questions.teaches: अ or आ before उ joins to ओ (दोष + उच्छ्रय → दोषोच्छ्रय; महा + उत्सवः → महोत्सवः).

questions.q: What does the dry medicine of unit 46 agitate?
optionExplain: Pitta is not named in unit 46.
Right: वायुं कोपयति: it agitates Vāyu.
Kapha is not named in unit 46.
Blood is not named in unit 46.
questions.explain: The object of कोपयति is वायुम्.

questions.q: Match each patient word of unit 46 to its meaning.
pairs: by one with a soft koṣṭha
questions.explain: Four of the patients named in the instrumental.
questions.rule: अब्रह्मचारी = not continent; वेगविधारी = holds back urges; मृदुकोष्ठ = soft koṣṭha; सुकुमार = delicate.

questions.q: Put these parts of unit 46 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Patients first; then the dry medicine used in excess; then excess purging agitates Vāyu.
questions.rule: अस्निग्धस्विन्नेन · अब्रह्मचारिणा · वेगविधारिणा · मृदुकोष्ठेन सुकुमारेण वा · रूक्षमौषधमतिमात्रं प्रयुक्तम् · अतिविरेकाद्वायुं कोपयति.
questions.teaches: Unit 46 names the patients first, the medicine next, and the path and result last.

questions.q: How is the medicine of unit 46 described?
options: Oily, and in a small dose
optionExplain: The unit says dry (रूक्ष) and excess (अतिमात्र).
Sharp is not named; excess is.
Right: रूक्षमौषधमतिमात्रं प्रयुक्तम्: a dry medicine used in excess.
Neither cold nor milk is named.
questions.explain: रूक्ष = dry; अतिमात्रम् = in excess.

questions.q: A delicate man who holds back his urges takes too much of a dry purgative. Through what does unit 46 say Vāyu is agitated?
optionExplain: Vomiting is not named in unit 46.
Sleep is not named in unit 46.
Food is not named in unit 46.
Right: अतिविरेकात्: from excessive purging.
questions.explain: The ablative अतिविरेकात् gives the path: excess purging.

questions.q: ब्रह्मचारिन् gives ब्रह्मचारिणा (ण after र). Which is the instrumental singular of the invented बलिन् (a strong one)?
optionExplain: Right: in-stems take -इना; with no र or ष before it, the न stays न: बलिना.
न becomes ण only after र, ष or ऋ, as in ब्रह्मचारिणा; बलिन् has none.
-एन is the a-stem ending, not the in-stem one.
-इनः is genitive/ablative singular or nominative plural.
questions.explain: in-stem instrumental singular = -इना; न → ण after र (ब्रह्मचारिणा, वेगविधारिणा).
questions.rule: in-stem instr. sg. -इना; ण only after र/ष/ऋ.
questions.teaches: in-stems take -इना in the instrumental singular, and न turns to ण after र (ब्रह्मचारिणा) but not in बलिना.

questions.q: What kinds of signs does unit 47 list?
optionExplain: None of these is named in unit 47.
Right: शूलं मूर्च्छा भ्रमः कंपः: pain, fainting, giddiness, trembling, and more.
None of these is named in unit 47.
None of these is named in unit 47.
questions.explain: The list of unit 47 begins शूलं मूर्च्छा भ्रमः कंपः.

questions.q: Match each sign of unit 47 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five of the nine signs of unit 47.
questions.rule: मूर्च्छा = fainting; भ्रम = giddiness; कम्प = trembling; स्तम्भ = stiffness; संज्ञानाश = loss of consciousness.

questions.q: Put these signs of unit 47 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Pain; fainting; giddiness; trembling; stiffness; pricking.
questions.rule: शूलं · मूर्च्छा · भ्रमः · कंपः · स्तंभो · निस्तोदो.
questions.teaches: Unit 47 lists its signs one after another; after निस्तोद come भेद, उद्वेष्टन and संज्ञानाश.

questions.q: What do निस्तोद and भेद name in unit 47?
optionExplain: Burning and itching are not these words.
Neither word means swelling or redness.
Right: निस्तोद = pricking pain; भेद = splitting pain.
Neither word means thirst or dryness.
questions.explain: Both are kinds of pain: तुद् prick, भिद् split.

questions.q: Which places does unit 47 name especially for these signs?
optionExplain: Not named in unit 47.
Not named in unit 47.
Right: पृष्ठ is named.
Right: श्रोणी is named.
Right: पार्श्व is named.
questions.explain: The clear places are पार्श्व, पृष्ठ, श्रोणी; the rest of the compound is uncertain.

questions.q: भेदः + उद्वेष्टनम् is printed भेद उद्वेष्टनम्. Join the invented pair कम्पः + इति the same way. Which is right?
optionExplain: अः → ओ is the rule before a voiced consonant or अ, not before इ.
The vowels do not join after the visarga drops.
अः does not become अर्.
Right: अः before a vowel other than अ loses the visarga, and the gap stays: कम्प इति.
questions.explain: Same rule as भेदः + उद्वेष्टनम् → भेद उद्वेष्टनम्.
questions.rule: अः + vowel (not अ) → अ, with a gap.
questions.teaches: Before a vowel other than अ, final अः drops its visarga and the gap stays (भेद उद्वेष्टनम्; कम्प इति).

questions.q: With what does unit 48 give the anuvāsana?
optionExplain: Right: यष्टीमधुविपक्केन तैलेन: with oil cooked with yaṣṭīmadhu.
Neither ghee nor honey is named in unit 48.
Milk is not named in unit 48.
Rice-water was for the vamana of 05.03.45.
questions.explain: तैलेन (with oil) is qualified by यष्टीमधु-विपक्व (cooked with liquorice).

questions.q: Match each word of unit 48 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The two absolutives, the means, and the verb of unit 48.
questions.rule: अभ्यज्य = having anointed; धान्यैः = with grains; स्वेदयित्वा = having made sweat; तैल = oil; अनुवासयेत् = give anuvāsana.

questions.q: Put the steps of unit 48 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Having anointed him; having sweated with grains; with oil cooked with liquorice; give anuvāsana.
questions.rule: तमभ्यज्य · धान्यैः स्वेदयित्वा · यष्टीमधुविपक्केन तैलेन · अनुवासयेत्.
questions.teaches: Unit 48 gives two prior acts (absolutives) and then the main act, the anuvāsana.

questions.q: What kind of enema is anuvāsana, according to the unit data?
optionExplain: Āsthāpana is the decoction enema; anuvāsana is unctuous.
Right: The data: anuvāsana = an unctuous (oil or ghee) enema, standard.
The picchā enema was in 05.03.25, another kind.
Milk and honey are not its definition.
questions.explain: अनुवासन = स्नेह-बस्ति: an oil or ghee enema.

questions.q: A physician has anointed the patient of unit 48. What does he do next, before the enema?
optionExplain: Vomiting is not in unit 48.
Avapīḍa was in 05.03.44, for another trouble.
Right: धान्यैः स्वेदयित्वा: having made him sweat with grains.
Fasting is not in unit 48.
questions.explain: Anointing, then grain-sweating, then the anuvāsana.

questions.q: अभि + √अञ्ज् gives अभ्यज्य (prefix: -य); plain √स्विद् causative gives स्वेदयित्वा (-त्वा). Which is the absolutive of प्र + √विश् (enter)?
optionExplain: -त्वा is for a verb without a prefix.
This is the past participle, not the absolutive.
This is the present tense, 'enters'.
Right: With a prefix the absolutive ends in -य: प्र + √विश् = प्रविश्य.
questions.explain: Same pattern as अभ्यज्य.
questions.teaches: An absolutive takes -य when the verb has a prefix (अभ्यज्य, प्रविश्य) and -त्वा when it has none (स्वेदयित्वा).

questions.q: What does हर in वातहर mean?
optionExplain: Right: हर is literally 'carrying off': वातहर = taking away Vāta.
That is the opposite of हर.
हर does not mean covering.
हर does not mean cooling.
questions.explain: -हर at the end of a compound = that which takes away X.

questions.q: Match each part of unit 49 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Two compounds: वात-हर and अन्न-पान.
questions.rule: वात = Vāta; हर = taking away; अन्न = food; पान = drink.

questions.q: Put the words of unit 49 in the order of the text, after the split.
questions.explain: Taking away Vāta; and; food and drink.
questions.teaches: Unit 49 adds, with च, food and drink that takes away Vāta to the anuvāsana of 05.03.50.

questions.q: Which split of चान्नपानं is right?
optionExplain: नपानम् is no word; the न्न belongs to अन्न.
Right: अ + अ → आ: च + अन्नपानम् = चान्नपानम्.
न्नपानम् is no word, and चा is not च.
ए + अ would give एऽ, not आ.
questions.explain: च (and) + अन्नपानम् (food and drink).

questions.q: A patient whose Vāyu was agitated by excessive purging has had the oil enema. Which diet does unit 49 point to?
options: Food and drink that increase Vāta
A full fast with no food
Food and drink that remove Vāta
Only cold water for a day
optionExplain: हर takes away; it does not raise.
The unit gives food and drink, not a fast.
Right: वातहरं चान्नपानं: and food and drink that take away Vāta.
Cold water is not named in unit 49.
questions.explain: Unit 49's diet is वातहर: Vāta-removing.

questions.q: वात + हर gives वातहरम्, taking away Vāta. Which word means taking away Kapha, for अन्नपानम्?
optionExplain: The thing taken away comes first, हर last.
No vowel stands between the members: कफ + हर.
The अ of कफ does not lengthen before ह.
Right: Same pattern: कफ + हर = कफहरम्, neuter like अन्नपानम्.
questions.explain: X + हर = taking away X (वातहर, कफहर).
questions.teaches: A compound ending in -हर means 'taking away' the first member (वातहर; invented कफहरं अन्नपानम्).

questions.q: According to unit 50, what does the excessive medicine do to the dhātus (body tissues)?
options: Liquefies them and makes them flow
Dries them and makes them hard
Builds them up and strengthens them
Leaves them and takes only mala
optionExplain: Right: धातूनपि द्रवीकृत्य स्रावयेत्: having liquefied even the dhātus, it makes them flow.
Drying is the opposite: the unit says द्रवीकृत्य, having liquefied.
Nothing in unit 50 strengthens the dhātus; it makes them flow out.
अपि, 'even', adds the dhātus to the mala drawn out.
questions.explain: Unit 50: all the mala is drawn out, and even the dhātus are liquefied and made to flow.
questions.section: अतियोग से मल और धातु का स्राव

questions.q: Match each word of unit 50 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The two conditions of the patient and the three acts of the medicine, as the card glosses them.
questions.rule: स्निग्धस्विन्न = oiled and sweated; क्षुधित = hungry; निर्हृत्य = having drawn out; द्रवीकृत्य = having liquefied; स्रावयेत् = would cause to flow.
questions.section: अतियोग से मल और धातु का स्राव

questions.q: Put these parts of unit 50 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Patient (oiled-sweated, very soft koṣṭha, or hungry); the medicine used; all mala drawn out; dhātus liquefied; flow, atiyogi.
questions.teaches: Unit 50 names the patient first (genitives in -स्य), then the medicine, its two absolutives, and last the verdict अतियोगि भवति.
questions.section: अतियोग से मल और धातु का स्राव

questions.q: Which split of the printed स्रावयेदतियोगि is right?
optionExplain: दतियोगि is no word; the द् is the voiced form of the verb's final त्.
Right: A final त् becomes द् before a vowel: स्रावयेत् + अतियोगि → स्रावयेदतियोगि.
That would print स्रावयेद्दतियोगि, with two द.
स्रावयः is no optative, and अः before अ gives ओऽ, not एद.
questions.explain: स्रावयेत् (3 sg. optative causative of √स्रु) + अतियोगि: त् → द् before a vowel.
questions.rule: त् → द् before a vowel: स्रावयेदतियोगि.
questions.section: अतियोग से मल और धातु का स्राव

questions.q: A patient is oiled, sweated and has a very soft koṣṭha. By unit 50, what may a medicine of sharp force do?
optionExplain: Unit 50 describes too much action, not none.
Lodging is not this unit's trouble; here everything flows out.
Right: Unit 50: in such a patient a sharp medicine draws out mala and dhātus: अतियोगि भवति.
Unit 50 says the medicine makes things flow, the opposite.
questions.explain: The three conditions (oiled-sweated, very soft koṣṭha, hungry) plus a sharp medicine lead to atiyoga.
questions.rule: Soft, prepared patient + sharp medicine → atiyoga.
questions.section: अतियोग से मल और धातु का स्राव

questions.q: धातून् + अपि gives धातूनपि. Join the invented pair वृक्षान् + अपि (even the trees) the same way. Which is right?
optionExplain: न् is doubled only after a short vowel; here आ precedes it.
The vowel अ of अपि cannot vanish into an anusvāra.
No ओ arises: न् + अ is just न.
Right: A final न् simply joins the following vowel: वृक्षान् + अपि = वृक्षानपि, like धातून् + अपि.
questions.explain: Same join as धातूनपि: consonant + vowel, written together.
questions.rule: Final न् after a long vowel + vowel → न + vowel.
questions.teaches: A final न् after a long vowel joins a following vowel unchanged (धातून् + अपि → धातूनपि; वृक्षान् + अपि → वृक्षानपि).
questions.section: अतियोग से मल और धातु का स्राव

questions.q: In unit 51, with what is the patient anointed first?
optionExplain: Right: शतधौतघृतेनाभ्यज्य: having anointed him with ghṛta washed a hundred times.
Oil and salt are not named in unit 51.
Milk is not the anointing substance here.
Sugar and honey go into the lehas, not the anointing.
questions.explain: The anointing (अभ्यज्य) uses शतधौत घृत, ghee washed a hundred times.
questions.section: अतियोग से मल और धातु का स्राव

questions.q: Match each word of unit 51 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Three outer forms, one oral form and the verb, as the card glosses them.
questions.rule: प्रदेह = smearing; परिषेक = pouring; अवगाह = immersion; लेह = licked preparation; स्तम्भयेत् = should make firm.
questions.section: अतियोग से मल और धातु का स्राव

questions.q: Put the five forms of use in unit 51 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: प्रदेह-परिषेक-अवगाह-अन्न-पानैः: smearing, pouring, immersion, food, drink.
questions.teaches: The long compound of unit 51 moves from the outside of the body (smearing, pouring, immersion) to food and drink.
questions.section: अतियोग से मल और धातु का स्राव

questions.q: Which of these does unit 51 name as contents of the lehas (licked preparations)?
optionExplain: Right: शर्करामधुमद्भिः, containing sugar and honey.
Not named for the lehas: the ghee is for the anointing.
Right: honey is the second content named.
Not named in unit 51; cold water comes in 05.03.54.
Not named in unit 51.
questions.explain: शर्करा-मधुमद्भिः लेहैः: lehas that contain sugar and honey.
questions.rule: Leha contents in unit 51: शर्करा, मधु.
questions.section: अतियोग से मल और धातु का स्राव

questions.q: After the anointing, what is the aim of all the measures of unit 51?
optionExplain: No vomiting is ordered; the trouble is too much flow.
Right: The single verb is स्तम्भयेत्, he should make him firm (check the flow).
Loosening would worsen an atiyoga; the verb is स्तम्भयेत्.
Kindling is not the stated aim of unit 51.
questions.explain: All the forms and lehas serve one verb: स्तम्भयेत्.
questions.rule: Unit 51: everything is for स्तम्भन, making firm.
questions.section: अतियोग से मल और धातु का स्राव

questions.q: शर्करामधुमद्भिः + च gives शर्करामधुमद्भिश्च. Join the invented pair लेहैः + च the same way. Which is right?
optionExplain: ः → र् is the change before other voiced sounds, not before च.
स् comes before त/थ; before च the visarga becomes श्.
Right: A visarga before च becomes श्: लेहैः + च = लेहैश्च.
The visarga does not turn into च्.
questions.explain: Same rule as मद्भिः + च → मद्भिश्च.
questions.teaches: A visarga before च becomes श् (मधुमद्भिः + च → मधुमद्भिश्च; लेहैः + च → लेहैश्च).
questions.section: अतियोग से मल और धातु का स्राव

questions.q: Whose blood is named in the drink list of unit 52?
optionExplain: मृग is not in unit 52.
मेष is not in unit 52.
शश is not in unit 52.
Right: छागासृक् = छाग + असृक्: goat's blood.
questions.explain: The one animal item in the list is छाग-असृक्, goat's blood.
questions.section: अतियोग से मल और धातु का स्राव

questions.q: Match each item of unit 52 to the meaning the card gives it.
questions.explain: Sandalwood and vetiver are standard identifications, cardamom probable, parched rice standard.
questions.rule: चन्दन = sandalwood; उशीर = vetiver; एला = cardamom; लाज = parched rice; शीतोदक = cold water.
questions.section: अतियोग से मल और धातु का स्राव

questions.q: Put these items of unit 52 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: चन्दन (अञ्जन) उशीर · छाग-असृक् · शीत-उदक · एला · लाज-सक्तु.
questions.rule: Sandalwood · vetiver · goat's blood · cold water · cardamom · parched-rice saktu.
questions.teaches: The list of unit 52 runs: candana, añjana, uśīra, goat's blood, cold water, elā, saktu of lāja; the verb पाययेत् comes last.
questions.section: अतियोग से मल और धातु का स्राव

questions.q: Which split of the printed अंजनोशीर is right?
optionExplain: Right: अ + उ → ओ: अंजन + उशीर → अंजनोशीर.
शीर is no item; the ओ comes from अ + उ.
There is no word ओशीर, and अ + ओ would give औ.
ए + उ would give अयु, not ओ.
questions.explain: Inside the dvandva, अञ्जन and उशीर join by अ + उ → ओ.
questions.section: अतियोग से मल और धातु का स्राव

questions.q: Which item of unit 52 does the data call disputed and leave unidentified?
optionExplain: Uśīra is vetiver root, tagged standard.
Right: Añjana: a collyrium mineral such as stibnite, or a plant; disputed, left unidentified.
Candana is sandalwood, tagged standard.
Elā is cardamom, tagged probable, not disputed.
questions.explain: Only añjana has the label disputed in unit 52.
questions.rule: अञ्जन = disputed; उशीर, चन्दन = standard; एला = probable.
questions.section: अतियोग से मल और धातु का स्राव

questions.q: शीत + उदक gives शीतोदक, cold water. Which is the right join of the invented pair उष्ण + उदक (hot water)?
optionExplain: अ + उ does not give आ.
औ comes from अ + ओ or अ + औ, not अ + उ.
Right: अ + उ → ओ: उष्ण + उदक = उष्णोदक, like शीत + उदक = शीतोदक.
The अ cannot simply drop before उ.
questions.explain: Same guṇa join as शीतोदक.
questions.teaches: अ + उ becomes ओ inside compounds (शीत + उदक → शीतोदक; उष्ण + उदक → उष्णोदक).
questions.section: अतियोग से मल और धातु का स्राव

questions.q: What kind of basti does unit 53 prescribe?
optionExplain: Salt is not named in unit 53.
Blood is drunk in 05.03.54, not given as basti here.
No such basti is named.
Right: पिच्छाबस्ति: picchā = slime; a mucilaginous enema.
questions.explain: Unit 53 names one basti: पिच्छाबस्ति.
questions.section: अतियोग से मल और धातु का स्राव

questions.q: Match each word of unit 53 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four words: the compound, the dative pronoun and the optative verb.
questions.rule: पिच्छा = slime; बस्ति = enema; अस्मै = to him; दद्यात् = should give.
questions.section: अतियोग से मल और धातु का स्राव

questions.q: Put the words of unit 53 in the order of the text, after the split.
questions.explain: A picchā-basti; and; to him; should give.
questions.teaches: The printed चास्मै hides two words, च and अस्मै; the verb दद्यात् closes the line.
questions.section: अतियोग से मल और धातु का स्राव

questions.q: Which split of the printed चास्मै is right?
optionExplain: Right: अ + अ → आ: च + अस्मै → चास्मै.
चा and स्मै are not words; the आ comes from अ + अ.
There is no word चास्.
There is no form आस्मै; the dative is अस्मै.
questions.explain: च + अस्मै: two short अ join as आ.
questions.section: अतियोग से मल और धातु का स्राव

questions.q: What does unit 53 say about the contents of the picchā-basti?
optionExplain: Goat's blood is in the drink list of 05.03.54, not in this basti.
Right: The unit names the basti only; its contents are not stated.
These go into the lehas of unit 51 (05.03.53), not into this basti.
That oil was the anuvāsana of 05.03.50.
questions.explain: Unit 53 gives the name of the basti and nothing more.
questions.rule: Contents of the picchā-basti: not stated in unit 53.
