questions.section: अतियोग से मल और धातु का स्राव

questions.q: Using the pronoun of चास्मै, complete वैद्यः ____ औषधं ददाति (he gives him medicine). Type it in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: अस्मै is the dative 'to him', as in पिच्छाबस्तिं चास्मै दद्यात्.
questions.teaches: अस्मै (dative singular of इदम्) marks the receiver of a gift: अस्मै ददाति, he gives to him.
questions.section: अतियोग से मल और धातु का स्राव

questions.q: In unit 54, what is the second option, the one marked by वा, for the anuvāsana?
optionExplain: Oil is not named in unit 54.
Goat's blood was a drink in the list of unit 52 (05.03.54).
Right: सर्पिर्मंडो वा: or the maṇḍa of ghee.
Cold water was a drink, not an anuvāsana.
questions.explain: Two options: milk-ghee cooked with the sweet group, or ghee-maṇḍa.
questions.section: अतियोग से मल और धातु का स्राव

questions.q: Match each term of unit 54 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The card's glosses: madhura-varga, siddha, maṇḍa, anuvāsana.
questions.rule: मधुरवर्ग = sweet group; सिद्ध = cooked; मण्ड = clear upper part; अनुवासन = unctuous enema.
questions.section: अतियोग से मल और धातु का स्राव

questions.q: Put these parts of unit 54 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Cooked with the sweet group; milk-ghee; ghee-maṇḍa; or, as anuvāsana.
questions.rule: मधुरवर्गसिद्धं च · क्षीरसर्पिः · सर्पिर्मंडो · वा ऽनुवासनं.
questions.teaches: Unit 54 names the first option with its qualifier first, the second option with वा, and the use (अनुवासनम्) last.
questions.section: अतियोग से मल और धातु का स्राव

questions.q: Which split of the printed सर्पिर्मंडो is right?
optionExplain: रमण्ड is no word, and the stem is सर्पिस्, not सर्पी.
That join would give सर्पिरमण्डः, with a vowel after र्.
सर्पिर is no stem; the र् comes from the visarga.
Right: इः → इर् before a voiced sound (म), and अः → ओ before voiced व: सर्पिर्मण्डो (वा).
questions.explain: सर्पिः + मण्डः: the visarga after इ turns into र् before म.
questions.section: अतियोग से मल और धातु का स्राव

questions.q: What does unit 54 tell us about the sweet group (मधुरवर्ग)?
options: It is listed item by item
It is taken by mouth alone
optionExplain: Right: The card: madhura-varga = the group of sweet things; not itemised.
No member of the group is named here.
It is used to cook the anuvāsana ghee.
It qualifies the milk-ghee (सिद्धम्); it does not replace it.
questions.explain: Unit 54 names the sweet group only as what the milk-ghee is cooked with.
questions.rule: मधुरवर्गसिद्धम् = cooked with the sweet group (members not given).
questions.section: अतियोग से मल और धातु का स्राव

questions.q: सर्पिः + मण्डः gives सर्पिर्मण्डः. Join the invented pair सर्पिः + मधु (ghee and honey) the same way. Which is right?
optionExplain: The visarga does not simply drop after इ.
Right: इः → इर् before a voiced sound: सर्पिः + मधु = सर्पिर्मधु.
स् appears before त/थ, not before म.
Lengthening with loss of र् happens only before र्.
questions.explain: Same rule as सर्पिः + मण्डः.
questions.rule: इः before a voiced sound → इर्.
questions.teaches: A visarga after इ or उ becomes र् before a voiced sound (सर्पिः + मण्डः → सर्पिर्मण्डः; सर्पिः + मधु → सर्पिर्मधु).
questions.section: अतियोग से मल और धातु का स्राव

questions.q: Which disease's procedure does unit 55 tell the physician to carry out?
optionExplain: Pravāhikā had its own treatment in 05.03.41, not here.
Fever is not named in unit 55.
Right: रक्तपित्तविधानं कुर्यात्: carry out the procedure for raktapitta.
Vomiting comes in 05.03.60, not here.
questions.explain: Unit 55 refers to the raktapitta procedure.
questions.section: अतियोग से मल और धातु का स्राव

questions.q: Match each part of unit 55 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The compound रक्त-पित्त-विधानम् and the verb.
questions.rule: रक्त = blood; पित्त = Pitta; विधान = procedure; कुर्यात् = should do.
questions.section: अतियोग से मल और धातु का स्राव

questions.q: Complete unit 55: रक्तपित्त____ं च कुर्यात् (the procedure for raktapitta). Type it in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: विधानम् = procedure, the last member of the compound रक्तपित्तविधानम्.
questions.teaches: विधान means a laid-down procedure; रक्तपित्तविधानम् = the procedure for raktapitta.
questions.section: अतियोग से मल और धातु का स्राव

questions.q: What does the data say the verb form कुर्यात् is?
optionExplain: A future would be करिष्यति.
A past would be अकरोत् or चकार.
The absolutive is कृत्वा.
Right: The data: 3 sg. optative of √कृ, 'should do'.
questions.explain: कुर्यात्, like दद्यात् and पिबेत्, is an optative of instruction.
questions.section: अतियोग से मल और धातु का स्राव

questions.q: A student wants the steps of the raktapitta procedure from unit 55. What does unit 55 give?
options: The full list of its steps
optionExplain: Right: रक्तपित्तविधानं च कुर्यात् names the procedure; its steps are not described here.
No step is listed in unit 55.
No drug or dose is named in unit 55.
No sign of the disease is given in unit 55.
questions.explain: Unit 55 only points to the raktapitta procedure; the card's limits say it does not describe it.
questions.rule: Unit 55: reference only, procedure not described.
questions.section: अतियोग से मल और धातु का स्राव

questions.q: What does the invented sentence ज्वरविधानं कुर्यात् mean, on the pattern of unit 55?
options: He has done the fever procedure
He should do the fever procedure
He should avoid the fever rules
optionExplain: कुर्यात् is optative, not past.
Right: X-विधानं कुर्यात् = he should carry out the procedure for X; here X = ज्वर, fever.
ज्वर is the first member of the compound, not the subject.
कुर्यात् means 'should do', not 'avoid'.
questions.explain: Same frame as रक्तपित्तविधानं कुर्यात्.
questions.rule: X-विधानं कुर्यात् = carry out the procedure for X.
questions.teaches: A disease name + विधानम् + कुर्यात् tells the physician to follow that disease's procedure (रक्तपित्तविधानं कुर्यात्; invented ज्वरविधानं कुर्यात्).
questions.section: अतियोग से मल और धातु का स्राव

questions.q: Unit 56 turns to the excess of which therapy?
optionExplain: Virecana's excess is taken up later, in 05.03.67.
Basti is not the therapy whose excess is named here.
Right: विशेषेण तु वमनातियोगे: but especially in the excess of vamana.
Nasya is not named in unit 56.
questions.explain: From unit 56 the measures are special to vamana-atiyoga.
questions.section: वमन का अतियोग: जिह्वा और नेत्र-विकार

questions.q: Match each word of unit 56 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The ingredients and the drink of unit 56, as the card glosses them.
questions.rule: सिता = white sugar; क्षौद्र = honey; फलरस = fruit juice; मन्थ = churned drink; पिबेत् = should drink.
questions.section: वमन का अतियोग: जिह्वा और नेत्र-विकार

questions.q: Put these parts of unit 56 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Especially; in excess of vamana; with ghee, sitā, honey; with fruit juices a mantha; should drink.
questions.rule: विशेषेण तु · वमनातियोगे · सघृतसिताक्षौद्रं · फलरसैर्मंथं · पिबेत्.
questions.teaches: Unit 56 names the occasion (वमनातियोगे) before the drink, and its verb पिबेत् stands last.
questions.section: वमन का अतियोग: जिह्वा और नेत्र-विकार

questions.q: Which of these go with the mantha of unit 56?
optionExplain: Right: स-घृत, with ghee.
Right: फलरसैः, with fruit juices.
Not here: goat's blood was in the drink list of 05.03.54.
Right: सिता is named.
Not named in unit 56.
Right: क्षौद्र is named.
questions.explain: स-घृत-सिता-क्षौद्रम् ... फलरसैः मन्थम्: four companions of the mantha.
questions.rule: Mantha of unit 56: ghee, sitā, kṣaudra, fruit juices.
questions.section: वमन का अतियोग: जिह्वा और नेत्र-विकार

questions.q: After vamana a patient has vomited far too much. By unit 56, what should he drink?
options: A peyā with milk and binding drugs
Cold water with añjana and blood
A mantha with ghee, sugar, honey
optionExplain: That is the gruel and milk of 05.03.59.
That is the general drink list of 05.03.54.
Rice-water for vomiting belongs to virecana's excess, 05.03.67.
Right: Unit 56: सघृतसिताक्षौद्रं फलरसैर्मन्थं पिबेत्.
questions.explain: The first special remedy for vamana-atiyoga is the mantha.
questions.rule: वमनातियोग → मन्थ with ghee, sitā, kṣaudra, fruit juices.
questions.section: वमन का अतियोग: जिह्वा और नेत्र-विकार

questions.q: फलरसैः + मन्थम् gives फलरसैर्मन्थम्. Join the invented pair जलैः + मिश्रम् (mixed with waters) the same way. Which is right?
optionExplain: Right: A visarga after ऐ becomes र् before a voiced sound: जलैः + मिश्रम् = जलैर्मिश्रम्.
The visarga does not drop after ऐ before म.
स् appears before त/थ, not before म.
The vowel ऐ does not change to औ.
questions.explain: Same rule as फलरसैः + मन्थम्.
questions.rule: Vowel other than अ/आ + ः before a voiced sound → र्.
questions.teaches: A visarga after a vowel other than अ or आ becomes र् before a voiced sound (फलरसैः + मन्थम् → फलरसैर्मन्थम्; जलैः + मिश्रम् → जलैर्मिश्रम्).
questions.section: वमन का अतियोग: जिह्वा और नेत्र-विकार

questions.q: In unit 57, the peyā (thin gruel) is cooked with shoots of which trees?
optionExplain: Fruit trees are not named in unit 57.
Right: क्षीरिवृक्षशुंगसिद्धाम्: cooked with shoots of the milky trees.
Thorny trees are not named in unit 57.
Flowering trees are not named in unit 57.
questions.explain: The gruel's shoots come from the kṣīrivṛkṣa, the milky-sap trees.
questions.section: वमन का अतियोग: जिह्वा और नेत्र-विकार

questions.q: Match each word of unit 57 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The card's glosses for the gruel and the milk of unit 57.
questions.rule: क्षीरिवृक्ष = milky trees; शुंग = shoots; पेया = thin gruel; संग्राहि = binding; भोजने = at the meal.
questions.section: वमन का अतियोग: जिह्वा और नेत्र-विकार

questions.q: Put these parts of unit 57 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Gruel cooked with milky-tree shoots, with mākṣika; or milk; and milk cooked with binding substances; at the meal.
questions.rule: Gruel · milk · binding milk · meal and verb.
questions.teaches: Unit 57 lists the gruel first, then plain milk, then the binding milk, and closes with भोजने and the verb.
questions.section: वमन का अतियोग: जिह्वा और नेत्र-विकार

questions.q: In unit 57, with what is the second, cooked milk (after क्षीरं वा) prepared?
optionExplain: Those shoots cook the gruel, not this milk.
Fruit juices went with the mantha of 05.03.58.
Right: संग्राहिद्रव्यसिद्धं क्षीरम्: milk cooked with binding substances.
The sweet group cooked the anuvāsana ghee of 05.03.56.
questions.explain: Keep the two cooked items apart: gruel with shoots; milk with binding substances.
questions.section: वमन का अतियोग: जिह्वा और नेत्र-विकार

questions.q: How does the data identify the mākṣika beside the gruel?
optionExplain: The data does not call it certain or standard.
The mineral sense is only noted as used elsewhere.
White sugar was sitā, in 05.03.58.
Right: The data: mākṣika beside gruel is probably honey (probable); also a mineral name elsewhere.
questions.explain: Mākṣika: probably honey; the translation keeps the term.
questions.section: वमन का अतियोग: जिह्वा और नेत्र-विकार

questions.q: Unit 57 has -सिद्धां पेयाम् (f.) and -सिद्धं क्षीरम् (n.). Which invented phrase agrees correctly?
optionExplain: Right: पेया is feminine accusative, so -सिद्धाम् agrees with it, like क्षीरिवृक्षशुंगसिद्धां पेयाम्.
क्षीरम् is neuter; it needs -सिद्धम्.
पेयाम् is feminine; -सिद्धम् does not agree.
-सिद्धः is masculine nominative; it fits neither noun here.
questions.explain: The participle सिद्ध takes the gender, case and number of its noun.
questions.teaches: सिद्ध agrees with its noun: f. -सिद्धां पेयाम्, n. -सिद्धं क्षीरम् (invented मधुसिद्धां पेयाम्).
questions.section: वमन का अतियोग: जिह्वा और नेत्र-विकार

questions.q: With what are the drugs of unit 58 licked?
optionExplain: Ghee is not named in unit 58.
Right: मधुना लिह्यात्: he should lick them with honey.
Milk was in 05.03.59, not here.
Water is not named in unit 58.
questions.explain: One vehicle: मधुना, with honey.
questions.section: वमन का अतियोग: जिह्वा और नेत्र-विकार

questions.q: Match each drug of unit 58 to the data's identification.
questions.explain: Only mustā is standard; madhuka is probable; añjana disputed; dhanikā unidentified.
questions.rule: मधुक = liquorice (probable); मुस्ता = nut-grass (standard); धनिका = unidentified; अञ्जन = disputed.
questions.section: वमन का अतियोग: जिह्वा और नेत्र-विकार

questions.q: Put the five drugs of unit 58 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: धनिका-मधुक-मधुरस-मुस्ता-अंजनानि.
questions.teaches: The drug compound of unit 58 has five members; the last, अञ्जन, carries the plural ending -आनि for the whole list.
questions.section: वमन का अतियोग: जिह्वा और नेत्र-विकार

questions.q: Which split of the printed सोद्गारायां is right?
optionExplain: द्गारा is no word; the ओ comes from अ + उ.
ए + उ would give अयु, not ओ.
Right: अ + उ → ओ: स + उद्गारायाम् → सोद्गारायाम्, with belching.
अ + औ would give औ, printing सौद्गा-.
questions.explain: स- (with) + उद्गार (belching): a bahuvrīhi qualifying छर्दि.
questions.section: वमन का अतियोग: जिह्वा और नेत्र-विकार

questions.q: After an excess of vamana a patient vomits with belching. In what form does unit 58 give the drugs?
optionExplain: पिबेत् was the verb of the mantha in unit 56 (05.03.58).
No basti is named in unit 58.
Smearing was in 05.03.53, not here.
Right: मधुना लिह्यात्: he should lick them with honey.
questions.explain: The verb of unit 58 is लिह्यात्, should lick.
questions.rule: सोद्गारा छर्दि → drugs licked with honey.
questions.section: वमन का अतियोग: जिह्वा और नेत्र-विकार

questions.q: What does the invented sentence मधुना चूर्णं लिह्यात् mean?
options: He should lick the powder with honey
He licked the powder with honey
He should drink the powder in honey
The honey should lick the powder
optionExplain: Right: मधुना = with honey (instrumental); लिह्यात् = should lick (optative), as in unit 58.
लिह्यात् is optative, not past.
Drinking would be पिबेत्.
मधुना is instrumental, 'with honey', not the subject.
questions.explain: Same frame as unit 58: X मधुना लिह्यात्.
questions.rule: मधुना लिह्यात् = should lick with honey.
questions.teaches: Instrumental मधुना names the vehicle and लिह्यात् the act of licking (unit 58; invented मधुना चूर्णं लिह्यात्).
questions.section: वमन का अतियोग: जिह्वा और नेत्र-विकार

questions.q: Which three troubles does unit 59 treat?
optionExplain: None of these is named in unit 59.
Right: वाक्संगे हनुसंहनने ऽनिलार्त्तौ: speech obstructed, jaws closed, affliction by wind.
These were signs in 05.03.43, not here.
Belching with vomiting was 05.03.60.
questions.explain: Three locatives open unit 59: वाक्संगे, हनुसंहनने, अनिलार्त्तौ.
questions.section: वमन का अतियोग: जिह्वा और नेत्र-विकार

questions.q: Match each term of unit 59 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The three troubles and two parts of the treatment.
questions.rule: वाक्संग = speech blocked; हनुसंहनन = jaws closed; अनिलार्त्ति = wind affliction; अल्पतण्डुला = with few grains; स्नेहस्वेदौ = oiling and sweating.
questions.section: वमन का अतियोग: जिह्वा और नेत्र-विकार

questions.q: Put these parts of unit 59 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Speech; jaws; wind; the gruel to drink; oiling and sweating.
questions.rule: वाक्संगे · हनुसंहनने · ऽनिलार्त्तौ च · ... पेयां पिबेत् · स्नेहस्वेदौ चावचारयेत्.
questions.teaches: Unit 59 names three troubles first, then the gruel with पिबेत्, and last the outer measures with अवचारयेत्.
questions.section: वमन का अतियोग: जिह्वा और नेत्र-विकार

questions.q: What is the peyā (thin gruel) of unit 59 cooked with?
optionExplain: Those shoots cooked the gruel of unit 57 (05.03.59).
Fruit juices went with the mantha of 05.03.58.
Right: घृतमांसरससिद्धाम्: cooked with ghṛta and meat-broth.
Binding substances cooked the milk of unit 57 (05.03.59).
questions.explain: Two gruels so far: with milky-tree shoots (unit 57), and with ghee and meat-broth (unit 59).
questions.section: वमन का अतियोग: जिह्वा और नेत्र-विकार

questions.q: What modern name does the data give for हनुसंहनन, and with what label?
optionExplain: The label is probable, not standard.
Paralysis is not the data's name.
Tetanus is not named in the data.
Right: The data: closing of the jaws (lockjaw-like, trismus; probable).
questions.explain: हनुसंहनन: literally close joining of the jaws; trismus, probable.
questions.section: वमन का अतियोग: जिह्वा और नेत्र-विकार

questions.q: स्नेहस्वेदौ is a dual dvandva: oiling and sweating. Which invented word names the pair pain and burning (शूल, दाह, both m.)?
optionExplain: Right: A dvandva of two masculine nouns takes the dual -औ: शूलदाहौ, like स्नेहस्वेदौ.
-आः is plural; a pair takes the dual.
This is a genitive phrase: two burnings of pain.
-अम् is singular, not the dual of a pair.
questions.explain: Same pattern as स्नेह + स्वेद → स्नेहस्वेदौ.
questions.rule: Two masculine members in a dvandva → dual -औ.
questions.teaches: A dvandva naming two things takes the dual of the last member (स्नेहस्वेदौ; invented शूलदाहौ).
questions.section: वमन का अतियोग: जिह्वा और नेत्र-विकार

questions.q: Which trouble of the tongue does unit 60 deal with?
optionExplain: That case is 05.03.64 (निर्गतां जिव्हाम्).
Right: जिव्हाप्रवेशे: when the tongue goes in.
Biting the tongue was a sign in 05.03.43.
Dryness is not named in unit 60.
questions.explain: प्रवेश = entering: the tongue drawn back inside.
questions.section: वमन का अतियोग: जिह्वा और नेत्र-विकार

questions.q: Match each word of unit 60 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Three qualities of the mouth-holds; the quality and animal of the broth.
questions.rule: स्निग्ध = oily; अम्ल = sour; लवण = salty; हृद्य = pleasing; अज = goat.
questions.section: वमन का अतियोग: जिह्वा और नेत्र-विकार

questions.q: Put these words of unit 60 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: The occasion; oily-sour-salty; kavala and gaṇḍūṣa; pleasing; goat meat-broths.
questions.teaches: Unit 60 names the occasion (locative) first; each remedy follows its qualities: adjectives before the noun.
questions.section: वमन का अतियोग: जिह्वा और नेत्र-विकार

questions.q: By the card, which mouth-hold is a mouthful of liquid held without moving?
optionExplain: Kavala is a smaller quantity, held and swished.
A leha is licked, not held in the mouth.
Right: The data: gaṇḍūṣa is a mouth filled with liquid and held without moving (standard).
A mantha is a churned drink.
questions.explain: Gaṇḍūṣa: filled and held still; kavala: smaller and swished.
questions.rule: गण्डूष = full and still; कवल = small and moved.
questions.section: वमन का अतियोग: जिह्वा और नेत्र-विकार

questions.q: Which broth does unit 60 give when the tongue goes in?
optionExplain: Fowl is not named in unit 60.
Deer is not named in unit 60.
Pulse soup is not named in unit 60.
Right: अजमांसरसान्: broths of goat meat.
questions.explain: अज = goat; the broths are also called हृद्य, pleasing.
questions.section: वमन का अतियोग: जिह्वा और नेत्र-विकार

questions.q: हृद्यान् + च gives हृद्यांश्च. Join the invented pair वृक्षान् + च the same way. Which is right?
optionExplain: Right: A final न् before च becomes ं + श्: वृक्षान् + च = वृक्षांश्च.
That is वृक्षाः + च, a nominative plural, not the accusative वृक्षान्.
The श् before च is missing.
न् + च does not give नच.
questions.explain: Same rule as हृद्यान् + च.
questions.teaches: A final न् before च becomes anusvāra + श् (हृद्यान् + च → हृद्यांश्च; वृक्षान् + च → वृक्षांश्च).
questions.section: वमन का अतियोग: जिह्वा और नेत्र-विकार

questions.q: What kind of fruits does unit 61 name?
optionExplain: मधुर is not the word; the text has अम्ल.
Right: फलान्यम्लानि = फलानि अम्लानि: sour fruits.
कषाय is not the word here.
तिक्त is not the word here.
questions.explain: One quality is named: अम्ल, sour.
questions.section: वमन का अतियोग: जिह्वा और नेत्र-विकार

questions.q: Match each word of unit 61 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five words after the split, as the card glosses them.
questions.rule: पुरतः = in front; अस्य = his; फलानि = fruits; अम्लानि = sour; खादयेत् = should cause to eat.
questions.section: वमन का अतियोग: जिह्वा और नेत्र-विकार

questions.q: Put the words of unit 61 in the order of the text, after the split.
questions.explain: In front; and; his; fruits; sour; should cause to eat.
questions.rule: पुरतः · च · अस्य · फलानि · अम्लानि · खादयेत्.
questions.teaches: Two printed tokens (पुरतश्चास्य, फलान्यम्लानि) hold five words; the verb खादयेत् is the third token.
questions.section: वमन का अतियोग: जिह्वा और नेत्र-विकार

questions.q: Which split of the printed फलान्यम्लानि is right?
optionExplain: ए + अ would give एऽ, not न्य.
उ + अ would give व, not य.
Right: इ + अ → य: फलानि + अम्लानि → फलान्यम्लानि.
म्लानि here would lose the अ of अम्ल, sour.
questions.explain: Final इ before a different vowel becomes य्.
questions.section: वमन का अतियोग: जिह्वा और नेत्र-विकार

questions.q: What does the causative खादयेत् of unit 61 tell us about the sour fruits?
options: They are only shown, not eaten
They are cooked into a drink
Someone is made to eat them
optionExplain: A plain 'he should eat' would be खादेत्.
खादयेत् is about eating, not showing.
No cooking or drink is in unit 61.
Right: खादयेत् is causative: he should cause (someone) to eat them, in front of the patient; who eats is not stated.
questions.explain: The -अय- of खादयेत् marks the causative: the physician has the fruits eaten in front of the patient.
questions.rule: खादयेत् = should cause to eat (eater not named).
questions.section: वमन का अतियोग: जिह्वा और नेत्र-विकार

questions.q: What does the invented sentence बालं क्षीरं पाययेत् mean, with the causative पाययेत्?
options: He should make the child drink milk
The child should make him drink milk
He should drink milk with the child
He drank milk as a child
optionExplain: Right: पाययेत् = should cause to drink; बालम् (accusative) is the one made to drink. Like खादयेत्, it is a causative.
बालम् is accusative, the one caused, not the subject.
पाययेत् is causative, not plain पिबेत्.
पाययेत् is optative, not past.
questions.explain: Causative -अय- verbs: the subject makes someone else act.
questions.rule: पाययेत् = should make drink; खादयेत् = should make eat.
questions.teaches: A causative (-अय-) optative tells the physician to make someone else act (खादयेत् in unit 61; invented बालं क्षीरं पाययेत्).
questions.section: वमन का अतियोग: जिह्वा और नेत्र-विकार

questions.q: What is finally done with the tongue that has come out, by unit 62?
options: It is made to go back in
It is left to rest out
optionExplain: No cutting or binding is in unit 62.
Right: प्रवेशयेत्: he should make it enter.
The verb is प्रवेशयेत्, make it enter.
Milk is not named in unit 62.
questions.explain: The last word of unit 62 is प्रवेशयेत्.
questions.section: वमन का अतियोग: जिह्वा और नेत्र-विकार

questions.q: Match each word of unit 62 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The ingredients and the two treatments of the tongue.
questions.rule: तिल = sesame; द्राक्षा = grape or raisin; कल्क = paste; व्योष = three pungents; प्रघृष्ट = rubbed.
questions.section: वमन का अतियोग: जिह्वा और नेत्र-विकार

questions.q: Put these parts of unit 62 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: The tongue gone out; smeared with sesame-grape paste; or rubbed with vyoṣa-salt powder; make it enter.
questions.rule: निर्गतां जिव्हां · तिलद्राक्षाकल्कलिप्तां · व्योषलवणचूर्णप्रघृष्टां वा · प्रवेशयेत्.
questions.teaches: Unit 62 states the trouble (निर्गतां जिव्हाम्), two options joined by वा, and the act (प्रवेशयेत्).
questions.section: वमन का अतियोग: जिह्वा और नेत्र-विकार

questions.q: Which of these make up vyoṣa, as the data gives it?
optionExplain: Right: one of the three pungents.
Right: one of the three pungents.
Not in vyoṣa: sesame is in the other option's paste.
Not in vyoṣa; cardamom was in 05.03.54.
Right: one of the three pungents.
questions.explain: Vyoṣa = śuṇṭhī, pippalī, marica (standard).
questions.section: वमन का अतियोग: जिह्वा और नेत्र-विकार

questions.q: Which two treatments does unit 62 offer before the tongue is put back?
options: Honey licking, or a milk gruel
Goat broth, or a sour mouth-hold
optionExplain: These are not the options of unit 62.
Licking and gruel belong to 05.03.59-60.
Right: तिलद्राक्षाकल्कलिप्ताम् ... व्योषलवणचूर्णप्रघृष्टां वा.
Those were for the tongue that went in, unit 60 (05.03.62).
questions.explain: Two options: smear with a paste, or rub with a powder.
questions.section: वमन का अतियोग: जिह्वा और नेत्र-विकार

questions.q: Unit 62 has तिलद्राक्षाकल्कलिप्ताम्, smeared with a paste of sesame and grape. What would the invented निम्बकल्कलिप्ताम् mean?
options: Rubbed with a powder of neem
Free of any paste of neem
Mixed into a drink of neem
Smeared with a paste of neem
optionExplain: Rubbed with powder would be -चूर्णप्रघृष्ट.
Nothing in the compound means 'free of'.
-लिप्त means smeared, not mixed into a drink.
Right: X-कल्क-लिप्त = smeared with a paste of X; here X = निम्ब (neem).
questions.explain: Same compound frame as तिलद्राक्षाकल्कलिप्ताम्.
questions.teaches: The tat-puruṣa X-कल्क-लिप्त means smeared with a paste of X (तिलद्राक्षाकल्कलिप्ताम्; invented निम्बकल्कलिप्ताम्).
questions.section: वमन का अतियोग: जिह्वा और नेत्र-विकार

questions.q: In verse 63, what is done for the one who has lost consciousness?
options: He is made to hear sounds
optionExplain: Right: विसंज्ञं ... शब्दान् श्रावयेत्: he should make him hear sounds.
Water is not in verse 63.
Pressing is for the turned eyes, the first line.
No basti is named in verse 63.
questions.explain: Line two: विसंज्ञम् + श्रावयेत्, make the unconscious one hear.
questions.section: वमन का अतियोग: जिह्वा और नेत्र-विकार

questions.q: Match each word of verse 63 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Line one has four words; विसंज्ञ opens line two.
questions.rule: अक्षिणी = two eyes; व्यावृत्ते = turned aside; घृताभ्यक्ते = anointed with ghee; पीडयेत् = should press; विसंज्ञ = unconscious.
questions.section: वमन का अतियोग: जिह्वा और नेत्र-विकार

questions.q: Put these parts of verse 63 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: The two eyes; turned aside; anointed with ghee; should press; the unconscious one; make hear the sounds.
questions.rule: अक्षिणी · व्यावृत्ते · घृताभ्यक्ते · पीडयेत् · विसंज्ञं · ... श्रावयेत्.
questions.teaches: Each line of verse 63 names its patient or organ first and ends with its own causative verb.
questions.section: वमन का अतियोग: जिह्वा और नेत्र-विकार

questions.q: Which of these sounds does verse 63 name in its second line?
optionExplain: Right: वेणु is read as flute.
Not named in verse 63.
Not named in verse 63.
Not named in verse 63.
Right: गीत is named.
questions.explain: साम-वेणु-गीत-शब्दान्: besides the first member, flute and song.
questions.rule: Sounds of verse 63: साम, वेणु, गीत.
questions.section: वमन का अतियोग: जिह्वा और नेत्र-विकार

questions.q: After an excess of vamana a patient's eyes are turned aside. By verse 63, what is done?
options: Anoint with ghee and press them
optionExplain: Washing is not in verse 63.
Right: अक्षिणी व्यावृत्ते घृताभ्यक्ते पीडयेत्.
Binding is not in verse 63.
Añjana is not named in verse 63.
questions.explain: The eyes are anointed with ghee (घृताभ्यक्ते) and pressed (पीडयेत्).
questions.section: वमन का अतियोग: जिह्वा और नेत्र-विकार

questions.q: घृत + अभ्यक्ते gives घृताभ्यक्ते. Join the invented pair तैल + अभ्यक्ते (anointed with oil) the same way. Which is right?
optionExplain: ए would need अ + इ, not अ + अ.
ओ would need अ + उ, not अ + अ.
Right: अ + अ → आ: तैल + अभ्यक्ते = तैलाभ्यक्ते, like घृताभ्यक्ते.
The two अ do not shrink to one short अ.
questions.explain: Same join as घृत + अभ्यक्ते.
questions.teaches: Two short अ join as आ (घृत + अभ्यक्ते → घृताभ्यक्ते; तैल + अभ्यक्ते → तैलाभ्यक्ते).
questions.section: वमन का अतियोग: जिह्वा और नेत्र-विकार

questions.q: In unit 64, with what liquid is the vomiting done?
optionExplain: Salt is not named in unit 64.
Sugar is not named in unit 64.
Honey is not named in unit 64.
Right: तंदुलांभसा = तण्डुल + अम्भसा: with rice-water.
questions.explain: The single liquid of unit 64 is तण्डुल-अम्भस्, the water of rice.
questions.rule: Unit 64: तंदुलांभसा वमेत्, he should vomit with rice-water.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 64 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five words carry the whole unit: when, with what, and the verb.
questions.rule: अतियोग = excess application; तण्डुल = rice; अम्भस् = water; मिश्र = mixed; वमेत् = should vomit.

questions.q: Put the words of unit 64 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: When (in excess of virecana), with what (rice-water), how (mixed), the act (should vomit).
questions.teaches: Unit 64 opens with the occasion in the locative (विरेचनातियोगे) and closes with the optative वमेत्.

questions.q: Which split of the printed विरेचनातियोगे is right?
optionExplain: Right: अ + अ → आ: विरेचन + अतियोगे → विरेचनातियोगे.
तियोगे is no word; the आ comes from अ + अ.
ए + अ would give एऽ (विरेचनेऽतियोगे), not आ.
अः + अ would give ओऽ (विरेचनोऽतियोगे), not आ.
questions.explain: A tat-puruṣa: विरेचन + अतियोग, in excess of purgation; two short अ join as आ.

questions.q: A patient has been purged far too strongly. What does unit 64 prescribe for him?
options: A fast with no water at all
optionExplain: Unit 64 orders no purgation; the trouble is too much purgation.
Right: विरेचनातियोगे ... वमेत्: in excess of purgation he should vomit.
No fast is named; rice-water is used.
Oiling and sweating are not named in unit 64.
questions.explain: In excess of purgation, unit 64 orders vomiting with rice-water.

questions.q: तंदुल + अंभसा gives तंदुलांभसा. Join the invented pair शीत + अम्भसा (with cold water) the same way. Which is right?
optionExplain: ओ comes from अ + उ, not from अ + अ.
ए comes from अ + इ, not from अ + अ.
Right: अ + अ → आ: शीत + अम्भसा = शीताम्भसा, like तंदुल + अंभसा.
The two अ do not vanish into one short अ; they lengthen to आ.
questions.explain: Same join as तंदुलांभसा: two short अ become आ.
questions.teaches: Two short अ meeting in a compound become one long आ (तंदुल + अंभसा → तंदुलांभसा; शीत + अम्भसा → शीताम्भसा).

questions.q: In unit 65, with what is the priyaṅgu group drunk?
optionExplain: Milk is not named in unit 65.
Meat-broth is not named in unit 65.
Cold water is not named in unit 65; the liquid is तण्डुल-उदक.
Right: प्रियंग्वादिकं च तंडुलोदकेन पिबेत्: with taṇḍula-water.
questions.explain: तंडुलोदकेन = तण्डुल + उदकेन, with the water of rice.
questions.rule: Unit 65: the priyaṅgu group with तण्डुलोदक.

questions.q: Match each drug of unit 65 to the identification the card gives it.
questions.explain: Lodhra, dāḍima and kamala are standard identifications; utpala is probable.
questions.rule: लोध्र = lodh; दाडिम = pomegranate; कमल = lotus; उत्पल = blue water lily; पद्मकेसर = lotus filaments.

questions.q: Put these items of unit 65 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: First alternative: the priyaṅgu group; second: lodhra, añjana, dāḍima skins; third: kamala, utpala, samaṅgā, padma-kesara.
questions.rule: प्रियङ्गु-वर्ग · लोध्र · दाडिम-त्वचः · कमल · उत्पल · पद्मकेसर.
questions.teaches: Unit 65 gives three alternatives in a row: the priyaṅgu group (joined by च), then the lodhra set and the lotus set, each closed by वा.

questions.q: Which split of the printed पिबेल्लोध्र is right?
optionExplain: Right: A final त् before ल becomes ल्: पिबेत् + लोध्र → पिबेल्लोध्र.
ल्लोध्र is no word; the first ल is the verb's final त् changed.
That would print three ल; the drug is लोध्र.
A visarga after ए before ल becomes र् (पिबेर्लोध्र), not ल्ल.
questions.explain: पिबेत् (should drink) + लोध्र: त् assimilates to the following ल.

questions.q: Which item of unit 65 does the data call disputed in identity?
optionExplain: Lodhra is Symplocos racemosa, tagged standard.
Right: Samaṅgā: Mimosa pudica or Rubia cordifolia in different commentaries; disputed.
Dāḍima is pomegranate, tagged standard.
Kamala is the lotus, tagged standard.
questions.explain: Of these four, only samaṅgā carries the label disputed (priyaṅgu and añjana are disputed too).
questions.rule: समङ्गा = disputed; लोध्र, दाडिम, कमल = standard.

questions.q: प्रियंगु + आदिकम् gives प्रियंग्वादिकम्. Join the invented pair मधु + आदिकम् (honey and the rest) the same way. Which is right?
optionExplain: The उ is not kept before व्; it turns into the व् itself.
That would need the guṇa ओ (अव्) first; उ simply becomes व्.
Right: उ before an unlike vowel becomes व्: मधु + आदिकम् = मध्वादिकम्, like प्रियंग्वादिकम्.
The आ of आदिकम् stays long after the व्.
questions.explain: Same join as प्रियंगु + आदिकम्: उ → व् before आ.
questions.teaches: A final उ before an unlike vowel becomes व् (प्रियंगु + आदिकम् → प्रियंग्वादिकम्; मधु + आदिकम् → मध्वादिकम्).

questions.q: Whose skins (त्वचः) close the list of unit 66?
optionExplain: Dāḍima skins were in 05.03.68, not in unit 66.
Lodhra was in 05.03.68, not in unit 66.
Nimba is not named in unit 66.
Right: उदुंबरत्वचः = उदुम्बर + त्वचः: the skins of the cluster fig.
questions.explain: The one tree named with 'skins' in unit 66 is uduṃbara.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 66 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Honey, sugar and cluster fig are standard identifications; त्वचः is plural.
questions.rule: क्षौद्र = honey; शर्करा = sugar; उदुम्बर = cluster fig; त्वचः = skins; वा = or.

questions.q: Put the members of the compound of unit 66 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: क्षौद्र-शर्करा-मधुक-उदुंबरत्वचः: honey, sugar, madhuka, skins of uduṃbara.
questions.teaches: Unit 66 is one compound: two sweet items, madhuka, and the uduṃbara skins, closed by वा.

questions.q: Which split of the printed मधुकोदुंबर is right?
optionExplain: Right: अ + उ → ओ: मधुक + उदुंबर → मधुकोदुंबर.
दुंबर is no word; the ओ comes from अ + उ.
There is no word ओदुंबर, and अ + ओ would give औ.
ए + उ would give अयु, not ओ.
questions.explain: Inside the dvandva, मधुक and उदुंबर join by अ + उ → ओ.

questions.q: Unit 66 has no verb. Which verb does the card carry over from 05.03.68?
optionExplain: वमेत् belongs to 05.03.67, the rice-water vomiting.
Right: The list of alternatives began with पिबेत् in 05.03.68; unit 66 continues it.
Licking is not the verb of this list.
That verb belongs to the protruded guda of 05.03.71.
questions.explain: Unit 66 appears to continue the drink list: पिबेत् is understood.

questions.q: Formed like उदुंबरत्वचः (skins of uduṃbara, acc. pl.), which invented compound means skins of nimba, in the same case?
optionExplain: The member order is reversed: the owner (निम्ब) comes first.
That is instrumental singular, not accusative plural.
Right: Stem निम्ब + त्वचः: only the last member takes the ending, as in उदुंबर-त्वचः.
That is two words (निम्बः + त्वचः), not one compound.
questions.explain: A tat-puruṣa keeps the first member as a bare stem.
questions.rule: Tat-puruṣa: stem + last member with the case ending.
questions.teaches: In a tat-puruṣa the first member stands as a bare stem and only the last member is declined (उदुंबर-त्वचः, निम्ब-त्वचः).

questions.q: Whose procedure (kriyā) does unit 67 order to be carried out?
optionExplain: Raktapitta's procedure was named in 05.03.57, not here.
Fever (jvara) is not named in unit 67.
Indigestion is not named in unit 67.
Right: रक्तातिसारक्रियाम्: the procedure for bloody diarrhoea.
questions.explain: The compound names रक्त-अतिसार, diarrhoea with blood.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 67 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Three members of the compound and the verb.
questions.rule: रक्त = blood; अतिसार = diarrhoea; क्रिया = procedure; कुर्यात् = should do.

questions.q: Put the parts of unit 67 in the order of the text, after the split.
questions.explain: Blood · diarrhoea · procedure · and · should do.
questions.teaches: The compound रक्तातिसारक्रियाम् is रक्त + अतिसार + क्रियाम्; the verb कुर्यात् closes the unit.

questions.q: Which of these does the card say about atisāra?
options: It is a kind of vomiting
It is a disorder of the skin
It literally means excessive going or flowing
optionExplain: Right: atisāra = diarrhoea, tagged standard.
No: vomiting is chardi or vamana, not atisāra.
No: nothing on the card ties atisāra to the skin.
Right: the card gives this literal sense.
questions.explain: atisāra: literally 'excessive flowing'; diarrhoea (standard); with रक्त, bloody diarrhoea.
questions.rule: अतिसार = diarrhoea; रक्तातिसार = diarrhoea with blood.

questions.q: What kind of instruction is unit 67?
options: A pointer to a procedure given elsewhere
A full recipe with its drugs and measures
A list of the signs of a disease
A warning to stop all treatment
optionExplain: Right: It names the procedure for raktātisāra but does not describe it.
No drug or measure is named in unit 67.
No sign is listed; only a procedure is named.
Unit 67 orders a treatment: कुर्यात्.
questions.explain: Unit 67 refers the physician to the known procedure for bloody diarrhoea.
questions.rule: Unit 67 = cross-reference: do the raktātisāra procedure.

questions.q: Complete the invented sentence वैद्यः ज्वरक्रियां ____ (the physician should do the fever procedure). Type it in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: कुर्यात् is the optative 'should do', as in रक्तातिसारक्रियां च कुर्यात्.
questions.teaches: कुर्यात् (3 sg. optative of √कृ) governs an accusative of the thing done: क्रियां कुर्यात्.

questions.q: In unit 68, what is the condition of the guda (rectum)?
optionExplain: No cut is named in unit 68.
Right: गुदं निःसृतम्: the guda that has protruded, come out.
Dryness is not the trouble named; the guda has come out.
No blockage is named in unit 68.
questions.explain: निःसृत (nis-√सृ) = gone out, protruded.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 68 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The state of the guda, three absolutives and the closing verb.
questions.rule: निःसृत = protruded; अभ्यज्य = having anointed; स्वेदयित्वा = having made sweat; स्तंभयित्वा = having made firm; प्रवेशयेत् = should make enter.

questions.q: Put the steps of unit 68 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Anoint · sweat · make firm with astringent things · make it enter.
questions.teaches: Three absolutives give the preparation in order; the optative प्रवेशयेत् is the final act.

questions.q: Which split of the printed निःसृतमभ्यज्य is right?
optionExplain: मभ्यज्य is no word; the म is the ending of निःसृतम्.
अः + अ would give ओऽ (निःसृतोऽभ्यज्य); and गुदम् needs neuter -म्.
Right: A final म् joins a following vowel: निःसृतम् + अभ्यज्य → निःसृतमभ्यज्य.
That would print two म (निःसृतम्मभ्यज्य); मभ्यज्य is no word.
questions.explain: निःसृतम् agrees with गुदम् (n. acc. sg.); अभ्यज्य = having anointed.

questions.q: Which modern equivalent does the data give for guda niḥsṛta?
optionExplain: Arśas is not named; the guda itself has come out.
Raktātisāra is the subject of 05.03.70, not of unit 68.
Bhagandara is not named in unit 68.
Right: The data: guda niḥsṛta corresponds to rectal prolapse (gudabhraṃśa); standard.
questions.explain: niḥsṛta guda = rectum that has come out = rectal prolapse.

questions.q: With a prefix the absolutive ends in -य (अभि + √अञ्ज् → अभ्यज्य). Which invented absolutive of उप + √कृ is right?
optionExplain: Right: Prefix + root → -य; a short root vowel adds त्: उप + √कृ → उपकृत्य, like अभ्यज्य.
-त्वा is used without a prefix (स्वेदयित्वा); with उप the form takes -य.
That is the infinitive 'to help', not an absolutive.
That is the past participle 'helped', not an absolutive.
questions.explain: अभ्यज्य (with prefix, -य) against स्वेदयित्वा (no prefix, -त्वा).
questions.rule: Absolutive: no prefix → -त्वा; with prefix → -य (-त्य after a short vowel).
questions.teaches: An absolutive with a prefix ends in -य (अभ्यज्य, उपकृत्य); without a prefix it ends in -त्वा (स्वेदयित्वा).

questions.q: What does unit 69 say should be dealt with as before?
options: Swelling of the belly and the rest
Obstruction of speech and the rest
Burning of the eyes and the rest
Loss of hunger and the rest
optionExplain: Swelling is not named in unit 69.
Right: वाक्संगादीन्: vāk-saṅga-ādīn, obstruction of speech and the rest.
Burning eyes are not named in unit 69.
Loss of hunger is not named in unit 69.
questions.explain: The object of साधयेत् is वाक्संगादीन्.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 69 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The adverb, the three members of the object compound and the verb.
questions.rule: पूर्ववत् = as before; वाक् = speech; संग = obstruction; आदि = and the rest; साधयेत् = should deal with.

questions.q: Put the words of unit 69 in the order of the text, after the split.
questions.explain: As before · and · obstruction of speech and the rest · should deal with.
questions.teaches: Unit 69 opens with the manner (पूर्ववत्), names the troubles, and closes with साधयेत्.

questions.q: Which split of the printed पूर्ववच्च is right?
optionExplain: पूर्वव and च्च are not words.
A visarga before च becomes श् (पूर्ववश्च), not च्.
Right: A final त् before च becomes च्: पूर्ववत् + च → पूर्ववच्च.
अच्च is no word; च alone is 'and'.
questions.explain: पूर्ववत् (as before) + च (and): त् assimilates to च.

questions.q: What does पूर्ववत् in unit 69 tell the physician?
optionExplain: पूर्व here is the earlier statement, not an earlier time than purgation.
No meal is named; पूर्ववत् means 'as before'.
No time of day is named in unit 69.
Right: पूर्व-वत् = like the former: the treatment already given in the text.
questions.explain: -वत् = like; पूर्ववत् = like what was said before.

questions.q: पूर्ववत् = पूर्व + -वत्, like the former. Which invented form means like a father?
optionExplain: Right: -वत् is added to the stem पितृ: पितृवत्, like पूर्व + वत्.
पिता is the nominative; -वत् takes the stem पितृ.
पितृवान् is 'having a father', a different suffix (-वत् declined).
पितर is not the stem; the stem is पितृ.
questions.explain: The indeclinable -वत् means 'like' and is joined to the bare stem.
questions.teaches: -वत् added to a bare stem makes an indeclinable 'like X' (पूर्ववत् = as before; पितृवत् = like a father).

questions.q: In unit 70, what white thing is put into the blood?
optionExplain: No leaf is named in unit 70.
Right: रक्ते शुक्लं पिचुं ... क्षिपेत्: he should put a white picu into the blood.
Rice is not named in unit 70.
Salt is not named in unit 70.
questions.explain: शुक्लं पिचुम् = a white wad.
questions.section: जीवादान: रक्त की परीक्षा और चिकित्सा

questions.q: Match each word of unit 70 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The clear words of unit 70, as the card glosses them.
questions.rule: उभयत्र = in both; ज्ञानार्थम् = for knowing; रक्ते = in the blood; शुक्लम् = white; क्षिपेत् = should put.
questions.section: जीवादान: रक्त की परीक्षा और चिकित्सा

questions.q: Put these parts of unit 70 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: In both · for knowing · into the blood · a white wad · should put.
questions.rule: उभयत्र · ज्ञानार्थं · रक्ते · शुक्लं पिचुं · क्षिपेत्.
questions.teaches: Unit 70 states where (both cases), why (ज्ञानार्थम्), into what (रक्ते), what (a white picu), and the act (क्षिपेत्).
questions.section: जीवादान: रक्त की परीक्षा और चिकित्सा

questions.q: What does ज्ञानार्थम् in unit 70 express?
optionExplain: A cause would be ablative (ज्ञानात्), not -अर्थम्.
Time after would need an absolutive or ततः, not -अर्थम्.
Right: -अर्थम् at the end of a compound means 'for the sake of': ज्ञान-अर्थम्, for knowing.
Means would be instrumental (ज्ञानेन), not -अर्थम्.
questions.explain: ज्ञान + अर्थम् (ind.) = for the sake of knowing.
questions.rule: X-अर्थम् = for the sake of X.
questions.section: जीवादान: रक्त की परीक्षा और चिकित्सा

questions.q: Why is the white wad put into the blood in unit 70?

To make a lepa from it

No wound is named in unit 70.

questions.rule: Unit 70: the wad is put in ज्ञानार्थम्, for knowing.
questions.section: जीवादान: रक्त की परीक्षा और चिकित्सा

questions.q: उभयत्र (in both) is उभय + -त्र. Which invented form means in another place?
optionExplain: Right: -त्र makes a place adverb: अन्य + त्र = in another place, like उभय + त्र.
-था gives manner: otherwise.
-दा gives time: at another time.
-तर gives 'one of two', a pronoun, not a place.
questions.explain: The suffix -त्र gives 'in (that place)'.
questions.teaches: The suffix -त्र makes a locative adverb of place (उभयत्र = in both; अन्यत्र = elsewhere).
questions.section: जीवादान: रक्त की परीक्षा और चिकित्सा

questions.q: In unit 71, with what is the tested thing washed?
optionExplain: Cold water is not named; the water is कोष्ण, slightly warm.
Right: कोष्णांबुक्षालित: washed with slightly warm (koṣṇa) water.
Milk is not named in unit 71.
Rice-water belongs to 05.03.67, not to this test.
questions.explain: कोष्ण + अम्बु + क्षालित: washed with slightly warm water.
questions.section: जीवादान: रक्त की परीक्षा और चिकित्सा

questions.q: Match each word of unit 71 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The washing and its two possible outcomes.
questions.rule: कोष्ण = slightly warm; अम्बु = water; क्षालित = washed; शुद्ध = clean; वैवर्ण्य = discolouration.
questions.section: जीवादान: रक्त की परीक्षा और चिकित्सा

questions.q: Put these parts of unit 71 in the order of the text.

questions.teaches: Unit 71 pairs each outcome with its verdict: clean → रक्त, discoloured → रक्तपित्त; विद्यात् serves both.
questions.section: जीवादान: रक्त की परीक्षा और चिकित्सा

questions.q: By unit 71, what does discolouration (वैवर्ण्य) after washing show?
optionExplain: Blood is the verdict when the wad comes clean, the other outcome.

Right: वैवर्ण्ये तु रक्तपित्तं विद्यात्: in discolouration, raktapitta.
Kapha is not named in unit 71.
questions.explain: Two outcomes, two verdicts; तु marks the contrast.
questions.section: जीवादान: रक्त की परीक्षा और चिकित्सा

questions.q: After washing in slightly warm water the tested thing comes out clean. What should the physician know, by unit 71?
optionExplain: Raktapitta is the verdict for discolouration, not for a clean wad.
No spoiled test is named; a clean wad has a verdict.

Right: क्षालितशुद्धे रक्तम्: when it is clean after washing, blood.
questions.explain: Clean → रक्त; discoloured → रक्तपित्त.
questions.section: जीवादान: रक्त की परीक्षा और चिकित्सा

questions.q: वैवर्ण्य (discolouration) comes from विवर्ण with vṛddhi of the first vowel and -य. Which invented noun from विरूप is formed the same way?
optionExplain: Right: वि → वै (vṛddhi) and -अ + य → -य: विरूप → वैरूप्य, like विवर्ण → वैवर्ण्य.
वे is guṇa, not vṛddhi; the pattern needs वै.
That uses the suffix -ता, not vṛddhi + -य.
The final अ of the stem drops before -य: वैरूप्य.
questions.explain: Same pattern as वैवर्ण्य: vṛddhi of the first vowel + -य.
questions.rule: vṛddhi + -य makes an abstract noun: विवर्ण → वैवर्ण्य.
questions.teaches: An abstract noun can be made with vṛddhi of the first vowel and -य (विवर्ण → वैवर्ण्य; विरूप → वैरूप्य).
questions.section: जीवादान: रक्त की परीक्षा और चिकित्सा

questions.q: In unit 72, to whom is the mixed food given?
optionExplain: Neither is named in unit 72.
Right: शुने काकाय वा दद्यात्: to a dog or to a crow.
Neither is named in unit 72.
Neither is named in unit 72.
questions.explain: शुने = to a dog; काकाय = to a crow.
questions.section: जीवादान: रक्त की परीक्षा और चिकित्सा

questions.q: Match each word of unit 72 to its meaning.

questions.section: जीवादान: रक्त की परीक्षा और चिकित्सा

questions.q: Put these parts of unit 72 in the order of the text.

questions.teaches: Unit 72 names the thing (food mixed with that), the two receivers in the dative, and the verb दद्यात्.
questions.section: जीवादान: रक्त की परीक्षा और चिकित्सा

questions.q: In which case are शुने and काकाय?
options: Genitive: of a dog, of a crow
Locative: in a dog, in a crow
Dative: to a dog, to a crow
Ablative: from a dog, a crow
optionExplain: Genitives would be शुनः and काकस्य.
Locatives would be शुनि and काके.
Right: Both are dative singular (श्वन्, काक): the receivers of दद्यात्.
Ablatives would be शुनः and काकात्.
questions.explain: दद्यात् (should give) takes the receiver in the dative.
questions.section: जीवादान: रक्त की परीक्षा और चिकित्सा

questions.q: In unit 72, what is mixed with 'that' and given to the dog or crow?
optionExplain: Rice-water belongs to 05.03.67, not to this test.
The wad is the other test (05.03.73); here food is given.
Honey is not named in unit 72.
Right: अन्नं ... तद्विमिश्रम्: food mixed with that.
questions.explain: The thing given is अन्न, food, mixed with that.
questions.section: जीवादान: रक्त की परीक्षा और चिकित्सा

questions.q: तत् + विमिश्रम् gives तद्विमिश्रम्. Join the invented pair तत् + गृहम् (that house) the same way. Which is right?
optionExplain: Right: A final त् before a voiced consonant becomes द्: तत् + गृहम् = तद्गृहम्.
त् does not stay voiceless before the voiced ग.
त् does not take the place of ग; it only becomes voiced.
त् becomes न् only before a nasal, and ग is not one.
questions.explain: Same rule as तद्विमिश्रम्: त् → द् before a voiced sound.
questions.rule: त् → द् before a voiced consonant.
questions.teaches: A final त् becomes द् before a voiced consonant (तत् + विमिश्रम् → तद्विमिश्रम्; तत् + गृहम् → तद्गृहम्).
questions.section: जीवादान: रक्त की परीक्षा और चिकित्सा

questions.q: By unit 73, what is shown when the mixed food is eaten?
optionExplain: Pitta is the verdict when the food is not eaten.

Āma is not named in unit 73.
questions.explain: Eaten → जीव; not eaten → पित्त.
questions.section: जीवादान: रक्त की परीक्षा और चिकित्सा

questions.q: Match each word of unit 73 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The two locative states and the first verdict.
questions.rule: तस्मिन् = in that; भुक्ते = eaten; अभुक्ते = not eaten; जीव = life-blood.
questions.section: जीवादान: रक्त की परीक्षा और चिकित्सा

questions.q: Put the words of unit 73 in the order of the text, after the split.
questions.explain: That · eaten · jīva · not eaten · pitta.
questions.teaches: Unit 73 is two condition-verdict pairs: भुक्ते → जीवम्, अभुक्ते → पित्तम्.
questions.section: जीवादान: रक्त की परीक्षा और चिकित्सा

questions.q: Which split of the printed जीवमभुक्ते is right?
optionExplain: मभुक्ते is no word; the म is the ending of जीवम्.
That would print जीवम्भुक्ते (or जीवं भुक्ते), with no अ, and would lose the 'not'.
Right: A final म् joins a following vowel: जीवम् + अभुक्ते → जीवमभुक्ते.
जीवाम् is no form here, and its आ would show in print (जीवामभुक्ते).
questions.explain: The अ of अभुक्ते is the negation: not eaten.
questions.section: जीवादान: रक्त की परीक्षा और चिकित्सा

questions.q: A dog leaves the blood-mixed food untouched. By unit 73, what is indicated?
optionExplain: Jīva is the verdict when the food is eaten.
Unit 73 gives a verdict for both outcomes.
The two verdicts belong to opposite outcomes.
Right: अभुक्ते पित्तम्: when it is not eaten, pitta.
questions.explain: Not eaten → पित्त.
questions.section: जीवादान: रक्त की परीक्षा और चिकित्सा

questions.q: अभुक्ते = अ + भुक्ते (not eaten). Which invented form means not seen, in the same locative?
optionExplain: Right: The negative अ- stands before a consonant: अ + दृष्टे, like अ + भुक्ते.
अन्- is used only before a vowel; दृष्टे begins with a consonant.
The prefix is अ-, not न-, in such compounds.
That is the nominative, not the locative like अभुक्ते.
questions.explain: Negative prefix: अ- before a consonant, अन्- before a vowel.
questions.teaches: The negative prefix is अ- before a consonant (अभुक्ते, अदृष्टे) and अन्- before a vowel.
questions.section: जीवादान: रक्त की परीक्षा और चिकित्सा

questions.q: By unit 74, by what three troubles is the patient afflicted?

Right: तृण्मूर्च्छामदार्त्तस्य: afflicted by thirst (तृट्), fainting (मूर्च्छा) and mada.
None of these is named in unit 74.
Fainting is named, but hiccup and itch are not.
questions.explain: तृट् + मूर्च्छा + मद + आर्त: afflicted by thirst, fainting and intoxication.
questions.section: जीवादान: रक्त की परीक्षा और चिकित्सा

questions.q: Match each word of unit 74 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Three troubles, the kind of treatment and the time-limit.
questions.rule: तृट् = thirst; मूर्च्छा = fainting; मद = intoxication; पित्तघ्नी = Pitta-destroying; आमरणात् = up to death.
questions.section: जीवादान: रक्त की परीक्षा और चिकित्सा

questions.q: Put these parts of unit 74 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Up to death · for him · afflicted by thirst, fainting, mada · the Pitta-destroying treatment · what is stated for atiyoga · should do.
questions.rule: आमरणात् · तस्य · तृट्-मूर्च्छा-मद-आर्तस्य · क्रियां पित्तघ्नीम् · अतियोगोक्तम् · कुर्यात्.
questions.teaches: Unit 74 names the patient (genitive), then two objects joined by च, then the verb कुर्यात्.
questions.section: जीवादान: रक्त की परीक्षा और चिकित्सा

questions.q: Which split of the printed तृण्मूर्च्छा is right?
optionExplain: तृण 'grass' would keep its अ: तृणमूर्च्छा, without the virāma.
There is no word तृन्; the ण् is the changed ट्.
Right: A ट् before a nasal becomes ण्: तृट् + मूर्च्छा → तृण्मूर्च्छा.
There is no word तृः, and a visarga does not become ण्.
questions.explain: The data: तृण्- is तृट् (thirst) before म.
questions.rule: ट् → ण् before a nasal: तृट् + मूर्च्छा → तृण्मूर्च्छा.
questions.section: जीवादान: रक्त की परीक्षा और चिकित्सा

questions.q: Besides the Pitta-destroying treatment, what else does unit 74 order?

optionExplain: No purgation is ordered; the patient already suffers excess.
No fast is named in unit 74.
Bloodletting is not named in unit 74.
Right: अतियोगोक्तं च: and what is stated for excess (atiyoga).
questions.explain: Two objects of कुर्यात्: पित्तघ्नी क्रिया and अतियोगोक्तम्.
questions.section: जीवादान: रक्त की परीक्षा और चिकित्सा

questions.q: पित्तघ्नीम् (f.) agrees with क्रियाम्. Which invented phrase means a Kapha-destroying medicine (औषधम्, n.) in the accusative?
optionExplain: Right: -घ्न agrees with its noun: neuter औषधम् takes कफघ्नम्, as feminine क्रियाम् takes पित्तघ्नीम्.
-घ्नी is feminine; औषधम् is neuter.
कफघ्नः is masculine nominative, not neuter accusative.
कफघ्नेन is instrumental, not accusative.
questions.explain: An adjective in -घ्न takes the gender, case and number of its noun.
questions.teaches: Adjectives in -घ्न ('destroying') agree with their noun: क्रियां पित्तघ्नीम् (f.), औषधं कफघ्नम् (n.).
questions.section: जीवादान: रक्त की परीक्षा और चिकित्सा

questions.q: In unit 75, whose blood heads the list, the rest unnamed?
optionExplain: Goat's blood was in 05.03.54, not in unit 75.
Right: खड्गादिरुधिरम्: the blood of khaḍga and the rest.
Mṛga is not named in unit 75.
Śaśa is not named in unit 75.

questions.section: जीवादान: रक्त की परीक्षा और चिकित्सा

questions.q: Match each word of unit 75 to its meaning.

questions.q: Put these parts of unit 75 in the order of the text.

questions.section: जीवादान: रक्त की परीक्षा और चिकित्सा

questions.q: Khaḍga has two meanings. Which does the card take in unit 75?

optionExplain: The card notes this sense, but a sword has no blood to take.

questions.q: By unit 75, with what is the blood taken?

questions.q: शीघ्रम् + उपयुंजीत gives शीघ्रमुपयुंजीत. Join the invented pair शीघ्रम् + आगच्छति (comes quickly) the same way. Which is right?
optionExplain: Right: A final म् joins a following vowel: शीघ्रम् + आगच्छति = शीघ्रमागच्छति.
The म् does not drop before a vowel.
The long आ of आगच्छति stays long.
The म् is not doubled.

questions.teaches: A final म् before a vowel simply joins it (शीघ्रम् + उपयुंजीत → शीघ्रमुपयुंजीत; शीघ्रम् + आगच्छति → शीघ्रमागच्छति).
questions.section: जीवादान: रक्त की परीक्षा और चिकित्सा

questions.q: In unit 76, what is boiled with the four plants?
optionExplain: Water is not the liquid named in unit 76.
Right: शृतं पयः: boiled milk.
Oil is not named in unit 76.
Meat-broth is not named in unit 76.

questions.section: जीवादान: रक्त की परीक्षा और चिकित्सा

questions.q: Match each word of unit 76 to its meaning.

Dūrvā is Bermuda grass, tagged standard.

questions.q: By unit 76, where is the boiled milk put?
optionExplain: The eyes are not named in unit 76.

The head is not named in unit 76.

questions.section: जीवादान: रक्त की परीक्षा और चिकित्सा

questions.q: दूर्वा + उशीरैः gives दूर्वोशीरैः. Join the invented pair द्राक्षा + उदकम् (grape-water) the same way. Which is right?
optionExplain: Right: आ + उ → ओ: द्राक्षा + उदकम् = द्राक्षोदकम्, like दूर्वा + उशीर.
