आ + उ does not give आ.
questions.explain: Same guṇa join as दूर्वोशीर: आ + उ → ओ.
questions.teaches: आ + उ becomes ओ (दूर्वा + उशीरैः → दूर्वोशीरैः; द्राक्षा + उदकम् → द्राक्षोदकम्).
questions.section: जीवादान: रक्त की परीक्षा और चिकित्सा

questions.q: In unit 77, according to what should the remaining complications be countered?
optionExplain: No season (ऋतु) is named in unit 77.
Right: यथामयम् = यथा + आमयम्: according to the disease.
Age is not named in unit 77.
The unit says यथामयम्, by the disease, not by the drug.
questions.explain: Unit 77: यथामयं दोषानपेक्ष्य प्रतिकुर्यात्, counter by the disease, having regard to the doṣas.
questions.section: शेष उपद्रव और दोनों शोधनों की तुलना

questions.q: Match each word of unit 77 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The unit's own glosses: the remaining complications, the measure (the disease), the regard (the doṣas), the act.
questions.rule: शेषेषु = in the remaining; उपद्रव = complication; यथामयम् = by the disease; अपेक्ष्य = having regard to; प्रतिकुर्यात् = should counter.
questions.section: शेष उपद्रव और दोनों शोधनों की तुलना

questions.q: Put these parts of unit 77 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Where (the remaining complications), how (by the disease, regarding the doṣas), the act, and the further reading.
questions.teaches: Unit 77 names the complications first (locative), then the two guides (disease, doṣas), the verb, and last the text to consult.
questions.section: शेष उपद्रव और दोनों शोधनों की तुलना

questions.q: Which split of the printed चेक्षेत is right?
optionExplain: क्षेत is no word; the ए comes from अ + ई.
चेत् before a vowel would print चेदीक्षेत.
Right: अ + ई → ए: च + ईक्षेत (should look to) → चेक्षेत.
अ + ए gives ऐ: that would print चैक्षेत.
questions.explain: च (and) + ईक्षेत (3 sg. optative middle of √ईक्ष्, should look to).
questions.rule: अ + ई → ए: चेक्षेत = च + ईक्षेत.
questions.section: शेष उपद्रव और दोनों शोधनों की तुलना

questions.q: A complication appears that the chapter has not described. Besides countering it, what does unit 77 tell the physician to look to?
optionExplain: No chapter on poisons is named in unit 77.
Diet rules are not named in unit 77.
The unit names no list of emetic fruits.
Right: वस्तिव्यापत्तिसिद्धिं चेक्षेत: and he should look to the basti-vyāpat-siddhi.
questions.explain: Unit 77 ends by pointing to the basti-vyāpat-siddhi, literally the cure of basti complications.
questions.section: शेष उपद्रव और दोनों शोधनों की तुलना

questions.q: दोषान् + अपेक्ष्य gives दोषानपेक्ष्य. Join the invented pair गुणान् + अवेक्ष्य (having observed the qualities) the same way. Which is right?
optionExplain: Right: A final न् after a long vowel joins the next vowel unchanged: गुणान् + अवेक्ष्य = गुणानवेक्ष्य.
न् is doubled only after a short vowel; here आ stands before it.
The vowel अ of अवेक्ष्य cannot vanish into an anusvāra.
No ओ arises from न् + अ.
questions.explain: Same join as दोषान् + अपेक्ष्य → दोषानपेक्ष्य.
questions.rule: Final न् (after a long vowel) + vowel → न + vowel.
questions.teaches: A final न् after a long vowel joins a following vowel unchanged (दोषान् + अपेक्ष्य → दोषानपेक्ष्य; गुणान् + अवेक्ष्य → गुणानवेक्ष्य).
questions.section: शेष उपद्रव और दोनों शोधनों की तुलना

questions.q: In unit 78, what does यथावस्थम् mean?
optionExplain: No text or authority is named in unit 78.
Right: यथा + अवस्थम्: according to the condition (अवस्था).
No meal is named in unit 78.
Speed is not the sense of यथावस्थम्.
questions.explain: यथावस्थम् = according to the condition.
questions.section: शेष उपद्रव और दोनों शोधनों की तुलना

questions.q: Match each word of unit 78 to its meaning.
questions.explain: All five glosses are the unit's own; उत्तिष्ठेत् is kept literal.
questions.rule: एवम् = thus; उभयतोभाग = both portions; शोधन = cleansing; यथावस्थम् = by the condition; उत्तिष्ठेत् = should rise up.
questions.section: शेष उपद्रव और दोनों शोधनों की तुलना

questions.q: Put the words of unit 78 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Thus · in both portions · also · in cleansing · according to the condition · should rise up.
questions.rule: एवम् · उभयतोभागे · अपि · शोधने · यथावस्थम् · उत्तिष्ठेत्.
questions.teaches: Unit 78 names the kind of cleansing (two locatives) before the measure यथावस्थम् and the verb उत्तिष्ठेत्.
questions.section: शेष उपद्रव और दोनों शोधनों की तुलना

questions.q: Which split of the printed उभयतोभागे is right?
optionExplain: ए does not turn into ओ; the word is उभयतः.
ओभाग is no word.
Right: अः before a voiced consonant becomes ओ: उभयतः + भागे → उभयतोभागे.
ओ + अ would print उभयतोऽभागे, with an avagraha.
questions.explain: उभयतः (on both sides) + भागे (in the portion): the visarga after अ turns to ओ before भ.
questions.section: शेष उपद्रव और दोनों शोधनों की तुलना

questions.q: Unit 78 opens with एवम् (thus). What does this word tell the reader?
options: A new, opposite rule begins here
The whole chapter ends at this point
Only basti is meant by this rule
The rule before applies here too
optionExplain: एवम् carries a rule over; it does not start an opposite one.
The chapter goes on; its colophon is at 05.03.111.
The unit speaks of शोधन through both portions, not of basti.
Right: एवम् … अपि: thus also; the preceding rule is carried over to cleansing through both portions.
questions.explain: एवम् (thus) with अपि (also) extends what was said before.
questions.section: शेष उपद्रव और दोनों शोधनों की तुलना

questions.q: उभयतः + भागे gives उभयतोभागे. Which is the right join of the invented pair ततः + गच्छति (then he goes)?
optionExplain: Right: अः before a voiced consonant becomes ओ: ततः + गच्छति = ततो गच्छति.
ः → र् happens after vowels other than अ/आ, not after अ.
ः → स् happens before त/थ, not before ग.
अः does not become आ.
questions.explain: Same rule as उभयतोभागे.
questions.teaches: A visarga after अ becomes ओ before a voiced consonant (उभयतः + भागे → उभयतोभागे; ततः + गच्छति → ततो गच्छति).
questions.section: शेष उपद्रव और दोनों शोधनों की तुलना

questions.q: In unit 79, what in emesis corresponds to parikartikā (cutting pain) of purgation?
optionExplain: Dry belching corresponds to pravāhaṇa, the third pair.
Right: या तु विरेचने परिकर्त्तिका तद्वमने कंठक्षणनं: in emesis it is injury of the throat.
The flow of Kapha corresponds to parisrava, the second pair.
No burning is named in unit 79.
questions.explain: First pair: parikartikā (purgation) = kaṇṭha-kṣaṇana (emesis).
questions.section: शेष उपद्रव और दोनों शोधनों की तुलना

questions.q: Match each word of unit 79 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The three purgation troubles, the throat injury of emesis, and शुष्क, the word that makes the belching dry.
questions.rule: परिकर्तिका = cutting pain; कण्ठक्षणन = throat injury; परिस्रव = discharge; शुष्क = dry; प्रवाहण = straining.
questions.section: शेष उपद्रव और दोनों शोधनों की तुलना

questions.q: Put these parts of unit 79 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Cutting pain, then throat injury; discharge, then flow of Kapha; then straining (paired with dry belching).
questions.teaches: Each pair of unit 79 names the purgation trouble with a relative word (या, यः, यत्) and its emesis form with a correlative (तत्, सः).
questions.section: शेष उपद्रव और दोनों शोधनों की तुलना

questions.q: Match each trouble of purgation to its counterpart in emesis, as unit 79 pairs them.
questions.explain: Cutting pain ↔ throat injury; discharge ↔ flow of Kapha; straining ↔ dry belching.
questions.rule: Unit 79: three purgation troubles, three emesis counterparts.
questions.section: शेष उपद्रव और दोनों शोधनों की तुलना

questions.q: After an emetic, a patient has dry belching (śuṣka-udgāra). Which purgation trouble does unit 79 pair with it?
optionExplain: Cutting pain is paired with injury of the throat.
Discharge is paired with the flow of Kapha.
Right: यत्प्रवाहणं स शुष्कोद्गार: what is straining, that is dry belching.
Distension is not among the pairs of unit 79.
questions.explain: Third pair: pravāhaṇa (purgation) = śuṣka-udgāra (emesis).
questions.section: शेष उपद्रव और दोनों शोधनों की तुलना

questions.q: तत् + वमने gives तद्वमने. Join the invented pair तत् + भोजनम् (that food) the same way. Which is right?
optionExplain: Before a voiced consonant the त् does not stay voiceless.
त् → न् happens only before a nasal (न, म).
त् does not take the place of the next consonant here; it only becomes voiced.
Right: त् becomes द् before a voiced consonant: तत् + भोजनम् = तद्भोजनम्.
questions.explain: Same rule as तद्वमने.
questions.teaches: A final त् becomes द् before a voiced consonant (तत् + वमने → तद्वमने; तत् + भोजनम् → तद्भोजनम्).
questions.section: शेष उपद्रव और दोनों शोधनों की तुलना

questions.q: In unit 80, what does भवन्ति mean?
optionExplain: Right: भवन्ति: 3rd person plural present of √भू, there are.
The data labels भवन्ति present, not past.
That would be an imperative (भवन्तु).
That would be a future (भविष्यन्ति).
questions.explain: भवन्ति = there are (the following).
questions.section: शेष उपद्रव और दोनों शोधनों की तुलना

questions.q: Match each word of unit 80 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The verb, the joining word and the word for 'on this point'.
questions.rule: भवन्ति = there are; च = and; अत्र = here, on this point.
questions.section: शेष उपद्रव और दोनों शोधनों की तुलना

questions.q: Put the three words of unit 80 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: The verb first, then च and अत्र, joined as चात्र.
questions.teaches: चात्र hides two words: च and अत्र, written together.
questions.section: शेष उपद्रव और दोनों शोधनों की तुलना

questions.q: Which feature of the verb भवन्ति shows that more than one thing follows?
optionExplain: The data labels it present tense, and tense says nothing of number.
Right: भवन्ति is 3rd person plural: 'there are', so several things (the verses) follow.
भवन्ति is an active present form, not a passive.
It is a present indicative, not an imperative.
questions.explain: Number, not tense, tells how many: भवन्ति is plural.
questions.section: शेष उपद्रव और दोनों शोधनों की तुलना

questions.q: Reading on after unit 80, what kind of text does the reader meet next?
optionExplain: The colophon comes only at 05.03.111.
The third chapter has not yet ended.
Right: The units after the formula are verses: the first, 05.03.84-85, lists why a medicine fails.
The formula turns from prose to verse.
questions.explain: भवन्ति चात्र introduces the verses that follow the prose.
questions.section: शेष उपद्रव और दोनों शोधनों की तुलना

questions.q: च + अत्र gives चात्र. Which is the joined form of the invented pair न + अत्र (not here)?
optionExplain: Two अ do not shrink to one short अ; they give आ.
ओऽ arises from अः + अ, and न has no visarga.
ऐ comes from अ + ए, not from अ + अ.
Right: Short अ + short अ → आ: न + अत्र = नात्र, like च + अत्र = चात्र.
questions.explain: Same rule as चात्र.
questions.teaches: Short अ + short अ join as आ (च + अत्र → चात्र; न + अत्र → नात्र).
questions.section: शेष उपद्रव और दोनों शोधनों की तुलना

questions.q: Which of these is a fault of the medicine named in verse 81?
optionExplain: Right: अल्पम्, scanty, is the third fault of the list.
No taste is named among the faults of verse 81.
Heat is not named among the faults of verse 81.
Thinness is not named in verse 81.
questions.explain: The six faults: excessive, wrong time, scanty, not soaked, improperly prepared, old.
questions.section: औषध के बिगड़ने के कारण और उपाय

questions.q: Match each word of verse 81 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four of the faults and the word that makes the failure certain.
questions.rule: अतिमात्रम् = excessive; अकाले = wrong time; अभावितम् = not soaked; असम्यक्संस्कृतम् = improperly prepared; ध्रुवम् = surely.
questions.section: औषध के बिगड़ने के कारण और उपाय

questions.q: Put the six faults of verse 81 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Excessive · wrong time · scanty · not soaked with equal-potency ones · improperly prepared · old.
questions.teaches: Verse 81 lists four faults in line 1 and two in line 2, then gives the verdict व्यापद्येतौषधं ध्रुवम्.
questions.section: औषध के बिगड़ने के कारण और उपाय

questions.q: Which split of the printed तुल्यवीर्यैरभावितं is right?
optionExplain: That would print तुल्यवीर्यैर्भावितम्, with no अ after र्.
Right: ऐः before a vowel becomes ऐर्: तुल्यवीर्यैः + अभावितम् → तुल्यवीर्यैरभावितम्; the fault is 'not soaked'.
रभावित is no word; the र् is the changed visarga.
तुल्यवीर्यैर is no form; the instrumental plural ends in ऐः.
questions.explain: The अ after र् is the negative अ-: अ-भावितम्, not soaked.
questions.section: औषध के बिगड़ने के कारण और उपाय

questions.q: A medicine is given in the right dose and time but not soaked with drugs of equal potency. By verse 81, what follows?
optionExplain: Verse 81 says any of the six faults makes it fail.
Poison is not named in verse 81.
Right: Not soaked (अभावितम्) is one of the six faults: व्यापद्येतौषधं ध्रुवम्.
No second dose is named in verse 81.
questions.explain: Any one of the six faults is enough: the medicine would surely go wrong.
questions.section: औषध के बिगड़ने के कारण और उपाय

questions.q: अकाले + अल्पम् gives अकालेऽल्पम्. Join the invented pair वने + अस्मिन् (in this forest) the same way. Which is right?
optionExplain: ए does not turn into आ.
ऐ arises from अ + ए, not from ए + अ.
ओऽ arises from अः + अ; here the ending is ए.
Right: ए + अ: the ए stays and the अ is dropped, marked by ऽ: वने + अस्मिन् = वनेऽस्मिन्.
questions.explain: Same rule as अकालेऽल्पम्.
questions.teaches: After a final ए a following अ is dropped and marked with an avagraha (अकाले + अल्पम् → अकालेऽल्पम्; वने + अस्मिन् → वनेऽस्मिन्).
questions.section: औषध के बिगड़ने के कारण और उपाय

questions.q: In verse 82, what does भूयः mean in पाययेदौषधं भूयः?
optionExplain: Right: भूयः = again, more.
Never would be न कदापि; भूयः is 'again'.
Slowly would be शनैः.
At night would be रात्रौ.
questions.explain: पाययेत् औषधं भूयः: he should make (him) drink the medicine again.
questions.section: औषध के बिगड़ने के कारण और उपाय

questions.q: Match each word of verse 82 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Clear words only; the damaged word of line 1 is left out.
questions.rule: छर्दन = vomiting; रेचन = purging; पाययेत् = should make drink; औषध = medicine; निहन्ति = destroys.
questions.section: औषध के बिगड़ने के कारण और उपाय

questions.q: Put these parts of verse 82 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Line 1: chardana, then durvireca and recana; line 2: make drink the medicine, again, it destroys, for they are so.
questions.rule: छर्दनं न तु · दुर्विरेचं न रेचनं · पाययेदौषधं · भूयः · तं निहंति · तथा हि ते.
questions.teaches: Line 1 of verse 82 names the vomiting word first and the purging words second; line 2 opens with the verb पाययेत्.
questions.section: औषध के बिगड़ने के कारण और उपाय

questions.q: Which split of the printed भूयस्तं is right?
optionExplain: स्तम् is no word here; the स् is the changed visarga.
Right: A visarga before त becomes स्: भूयः + तम् → भूयस्तम्.
स्तम् is no word; the स् of भूयस्तं is the changed visarga.
An ओ cannot become स्.
questions.explain: भूयः (again) + तम् (him, that): ः → स् before त.
questions.section: औषध के बिगड़ने के कारण और उपाय

questions.q: Which two therapies does line 1 of verse 82 set side by side?
optionExplain: Neither basti nor sweating is named in verse 82.
Neither oiling nor fasting is named in verse 82.
Right: छर्दन (vomiting) and रेचन / दुर्विरेच (purging): the two cleansings of the chapter.
Neither is named in verse 82.
questions.explain: chardana belongs to emesis, recana to purgation.
questions.section: औषध के बिगड़ने के कारण और उपाय

questions.q: पाययेत् + औषधम् gives पाययेदौषधम्. Join the invented pair दद्यात् + अन्नम् (he should give food) the same way. Which is right?
optionExplain: Before a vowel the त् does not stay voiceless.
त् → न् happens only before a nasal.
The two words are joined; the त् does not simply vanish.
Right: A final त् becomes द् before a vowel: दद्यात् + अन्नम् = दद्यादन्नम्.
questions.explain: Same rule as पाययेदौषधम्.
questions.teaches: A final त् becomes द् before a vowel (पाययेत् + औषधम् → पाययेदौषधम्; दद्यात् + अन्नम् → दद्यादन्नम्).
questions.section: औषध के बिगड़ने के कारण और उपाय

questions.q: In verse 83, with what is the drink (पीतम्) mixed when it goes upward?
optionExplain: Right: कफसंसृष्टम्: mixed with Kapha.
Pitta is not named in verse 83.
Blood is not named in verse 83.
Vāta is not named in verse 83.
questions.explain: Line 1: ऊर्ध्वं कफसंसृष्टं पीतं याति, what is drunk goes upward mixed with Kapha.
questions.section: औषध के बिगड़ने के कारण और उपाय

questions.q: Match each word of verse 83 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Three words of line 1 and two of the patient's states in line 2.
questions.rule: ऊर्ध्वम् = upward; संसृष्ट = mixed; पीत = drunk; वमित = made to vomit; लङ्घित = made to fast.
questions.section: औषध के बिगड़ने के कारण और उपाय

questions.q: Put these words of line 2 of verse 83 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Made to vomit · cleansed · made to fast · he should make drink.
questions.teaches: Three past participles (वमित, शुद्ध, लङ्घित) describe the patient before the verb पाययेत्.
questions.section: औषध के बिगड़ने के कारण और उपाय

questions.q: Which split of the printed यस्योर्ध्वं is right?
optionExplain: यस्यः is no form; the genitive is यस्य.
Right: अ + ऊ → ओ: यस्य + ऊर्ध्वम् → यस्योर्ध्वम्.
उ + ऊ would give ऊ, not ओ.
ए + ऊ would not give ओ.
questions.explain: यस्य (in whom, gen.) + ऊर्ध्वम् (upward): अ + ऊ → ओ.
questions.section: औषध के बिगड़ने के कारण और उपाय

questions.q: By verse 83, in what state is the patient before he is made to drink?
optionExplain: No oiling, sweating or feeding is named in verse 83.
No purging, bathing or rest is named in verse 83.
Right: वमितं … शुद्धं लंघितं पाययेत्: made to vomit, cleansed and made to fast, then made to drink.
None of these is named in verse 83.
questions.explain: Line 2 gives three states of the patient, then the verb.
questions.section: औषध के बिगड़ने के कारण और उपाय

questions.q: याति + आनुलोमिकम् gives यात्यानुलोमिकम्. Join the invented pair अस्ति + अत्र (there is here) the same way. Which is right?
optionExplain: ए would come from अ + इ, the other way round.
ई would come from इ + इ.
The अ of अत्र cannot vanish.
Right: इ before an unlike vowel becomes य्: अस्ति + अत्र = अस्त्यत्र.
questions.explain: Same rule as यात्यानुलोमिकम्.
questions.teaches: A final इ before an unlike vowel becomes य् (याति + आनुलोमिकम् → यात्यानुलोमिकम्; अस्ति + अत्र → अस्त्यत्र).
questions.section: औषध के बिगड़ने के कारण और उपाय

questions.q: In verse 84, what is the state of the doṣa when hot water is ordered?
optionExplain: Right: विबद्धेऽल्पे … दोषे: when the doṣa is held back and scanty (and flows after a long time).
Too free a flow is the opposite of विबद्ध, held back.
Blood is not named in verse 84.
No movement to the head is named in verse 84.
questions.explain: Three locatives describe the doṣa: held back, scanty, flowing after a long time.
questions.rule: विबद्ध + अल्प + चिरात् स्रवत् → उष्ण जल.
questions.section: औषध के बिगड़ने के कारण और उपाय

questions.q: Match each word of verse 84 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Two states of the doṣa, two of the troubles and the verb that ends the verse.
questions.rule: विबद्ध = held back; अल्प = scanty; आध्मान = distension; तृष्णा = thirst; अनुशाम्यति = subsides.
questions.section: औषध के बिगड़ने के कारण और उपाय

questions.q: Put the four troubles that subside in verse 84 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Distension · vomiting · thirst · obstruction.
questions.teaches: Line 2 of verse 84 lists four troubles under one singular verb, अनुशाम्यति.
questions.section: औषध के बिगड़ने के कारण और उपाय

questions.q: Which of these does verse 84 say subside by the hot water?
optionExplain: Not named in verse 84.
Not named in verse 84.
Right: तृष्णा is the third trouble named.
Right: आध्मानम् is the first trouble named.
Not named in verse 84.
questions.explain: The four that subside: ādhmāna, vomiting, thirst, vibandha.
questions.section: औषध के बिगड़ने के कारण और उपाय

questions.q: After a purgative a patient has bloating and thirst; the doṣa comes scanty and late. Which measure of verse 84 fits?
optionExplain: Verse 84 orders hot (उष्ण) water, not cold.
Right: उष्णं पिबेज्जलं: he should drink hot water; by that distension and thirst subside.
No basti is named in verse 84.
Fasting is not named in verse 84.
questions.explain: Scanty, held-back doṣa → hot water → the troubles subside.
questions.section: औषध के बिगड़ने के कारण और उपाय

questions.q: पिबेत् + जलम् gives पिबेज्जलम्. Join the invented pair तत् + जलम् (that water) the same way. Which is right?
optionExplain: Before ज the त् does not stop at द्; it becomes ज्.
च् arises before च/छ, not before ज.
Right: A final त् before ज becomes ज्: तत् + जलम् = तज्जलम्.
त् → न् happens only before a nasal.
questions.explain: Same rule as पिबेज्जलम्.
questions.teaches: A final त् becomes ज् before ज (पिबेत् + जलम् → पिबेज्जलम्; तत् + जलम् → तज्जलम्).
questions.section: औषध के बिगड़ने के कारण और उपाय

questions.q: In verse 85, what treatment is ordered for the medicine that moves neither up nor down?
optionExplain: Fasting is not named in verse 85.
Oiling is not named in verse 85.
No emetic is ordered in verse 85.
Right: स्वेदं तत्रावचारयेत्: in that case he should apply sweating.
questions.explain: The single remedy of verse 85 is स्वेद.
questions.section: औषध के बिगड़ने के कारण और उपाय

questions.q: Match each word of verse 85 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The state of the medicine, its two blocked ways and the two signs.
questions.rule: दोषरुद्ध = obstructed by doṣa; ऊर्ध्वम् = upward; अधः = downward; उद्गार = belching; अङ्गशूल = limb pain.
questions.section: औषध के बिगड़ने के कारण और उपाय

questions.q: Put the four quarter-lines of verse 85 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The condition (two quarters), the signs, the remedy.
questions.rule: भेषजं … चेत् · नोर्ध्वं नाधः … · सोद्गारं … वा · स्वेदं …
questions.teaches: Verse 85 runs: if-clause (चेत्), the blocked ways, the signs, and the remedy (तत्र … अवचारयेत्).
questions.section: औषध के बिगड़ने के कारण और उपाय

questions.q: Which split of the printed चेन्नोर्ध्वं is right?
optionExplain: Right: त् → न् before the nasal न; अ + ऊ → ओ: चेत् + न + ऊर्ध्वम् → चेन्नोर्ध्वम्.
चे and नोर्ध्वम् are no words.
नु + ऊर्ध्वम् would print नूर्ध्वम्, not नोर्ध्वम्.
नौ + ऊर्ध्वम् would print नावूर्ध्वम्.
questions.explain: चेत् (if) + न (not) + ऊर्ध्वम् (upward).
questions.rule: त् + न → न्न; अ + ऊ → ओ.
questions.section: औषध के बिगड़ने के कारण और उपाय

questions.q: The medicine stays put, neither vomited nor purged, and the patient belches. By verse 85, which measure fits?
optionExplain: Cold water is not named in verse 85.
Right: With belching (सोद्गारम्) when the medicine moves neither way: स्वेदम् अवचारयेत्.
Fasting is not named in verse 85.
No sharper drug is named in verse 85.
questions.explain: Blocked medicine with belching or limb pain → sweating.
questions.section: औषध के बिगड़ने के कारण और उपाय

questions.q: स + अङ्गशूलम् gives साङ्गशूलम्. Join the invented pair स + आमम् (with āma) the same way. Which is right?
optionExplain: The long आ of आमम् cannot shrink to अ.
ऐ arises from अ + ए, not from अ + आ.
Right: अ + आ → आ: स + आमम् = सामम्, like स + अङ्ग → साङ्ग.
ओ arises from अ + उ, not from अ + आ.
questions.explain: Like vowels join long: अ + अ or अ + आ → आ.
questions.teaches: अ before अ or आ joins as आ (स + अङ्गशूलम् → साङ्गशूलम्; स + आमम् → सामम्).
questions.section: औषध के बिगड़ने के कारण और उपाय

questions.q: In verse 86, how soon should he scrape up (उल्लिखेत्)?
optionExplain: शनैः is not in verse 86; the word is क्षिप्रम्.
No time of day is named in verse 86.
No later day is named in verse 86.
Right: क्षिप्रमुल्लिखेत्: he should quickly scrape (it) up.
questions.explain: क्षिप्रम् = quickly.
questions.section: औषध के बिगड़ने के कारण और उपाय

questions.q: Match each word of verse 86 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Clear words of both lines; the long compound is left out.
questions.rule: क्षिप्रम् = quickly; उल्लिखेत् = should scrape up; सुशीत = very cold; स्तम्भयेत् = should check; भिषक् = physician.
questions.section: औषध के बिगड़ने के कारण और उपाय

questions.q: Put these parts of verse 86 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Line 1: the compound, then 'quickly scrape up'; line 2: the condition, 'with very cold (ones)', the verb and the physician.
questions.teaches: Each line of verse 86 has its own optative: उल्लिखेत् ends line 1; स्तम्भयेत् stands just before भिषक् at the end of line 2.
questions.section: औषध के बिगड़ने के कारण और उपाय

questions.q: Which split of the printed स्तंभयेद्भिषक् is right?
optionExplain: Right: त् becomes द् before a voiced consonant: स्तंभयेत् + भिषक् → स्तंभयेद्भिषक्.
द्भिषक् is no word; the द् is the verb's changed त्.
अः before भ would become ओ: स्तंभयो भिषक्.
That would print स्तंभयेदभिषक्, with अ after द्.
questions.explain: स्तम्भयेत् (should check) + भिषक् (the physician).
questions.section: औषध के बिगड़ने के कारण और उपाय

questions.q: In verse 86, when (it is) undigested and does not set in motion, with what does the physician check?
optionExplain: Verse 86 says सुशीतैः, very cold, not hot.
Right: सुशीतैः स्तंभयेद्भिषक्: the physician should check with very cold (ones).
Sharpness is not named in verse 86.
Oiliness is not named in verse 86.
questions.explain: Line 2: सुशीतैः, with very cold (ones), what they are is unstated.
questions.section: औषध के बिगड़ने के कारण और उपाय

questions.q: क्षिप्रम् + उल्लिखेत् gives क्षिप्रमुल्लिखेत्. Join the invented pair जलम् + उष्णम् (the water, hot) the same way. Which is right?
optionExplain: The anusvāra is written before a consonant, not before a vowel.
The म् cannot drop to let अ + उ join as ओ.
Right: A final म् before a vowel is simply joined to it: जलम् + उष्णम् = जलमुष्णम्.
No ओ arises; म् + उ is just मु.
questions.explain: Same join as क्षिप्रमुल्लिखेत्.
questions.teaches: A final म् before a vowel joins it as a syllable (क्षिप्रम् + उल्लिखेत् → क्षिप्रमुल्लिखेत्; जलम् + उष्णम् → जलमुष्णम्).
questions.section: औषध के बिगड़ने के कारण और उपाय

questions.q: In verse 87, where does the medicine stay when Kapha obstructs it?
optionExplain: The head is not named in verse 87.
The belly is not named in verse 87.
The throat is not named in verse 87.
Right: तिष्ठत्युरसि भेषजं: the medicine stays in the chest.
questions.explain: उरसि = in the chest (locative of उरस्).
questions.section: औषध के बिगड़ने के कारण और उपाय

questions.q: Match each word of verse 87 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five clear words of the two lines.
questions.rule: कदाचित् = sometimes; श्लेष्मन् = Kapha; रुद्ध = obstructed; उरस् = chest; क्षीण = diminished.
questions.section: औषध के बिगड़ने के कारण और उपाय

questions.q: Put these parts of verse 87 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Obstructed by Kapha · stays in the chest · when Kapha is diminished · or at night · it moves on.
questions.rule: कदाचिच्छ्लेष्मणा रुद्धं · तिष्ठत्युरसि भेषजं · क्षीणे श्लेष्मणि · रात्रौ वा · तत्प्रवर्त्तते.
questions.teaches: Line 1 of verse 87 gives the blockage, line 2 the release: Kapha diminished, then the medicine moves.
questions.section: औषध के बिगड़ने के कारण और उपाय

questions.q: Which split of the printed कदाचिच्छ्लेष्मणा is right?
optionExplain: Right: त् + श → च्छ: कदाचित् + श्लेष्मणा → कदाचिच्छ्लेष्मणा.
कदाचि and च्छ्लेष्मणा are no words.
छ्लेष्मन् is no word; the word is श्लेष्मन्.
कदाचिः is no form; the word is कदाचित्.
questions.explain: कदाचित् (sometimes) + श्लेष्मणा (by Kapha): त् before श gives च्छ.
questions.section: औषध के बिगड़ने के कारण और उपाय

questions.q: By verse 87, on what does the medicine's moving on depend?
optionExplain: Vāta is not named in verse 87.
Right: क्षीणे श्लेष्मणि … तत्प्रवर्त्तते: when Kapha has diminished, it moves on.
No new dose is named in verse 87.
Hot water is not named in verse 87.
questions.explain: Kapha blocks it; Kapha's diminishing releases it.
questions.section: औषध के बिगड़ने के कारण और उपाय

questions.q: तत् + प्रवर्त्तते gives तत्प्रवर्त्तते, unchanged. Join the invented pair तत् + पिबेत् (he should drink that) the same way. Which is right?
optionExplain: त् → द् happens before voiced sounds, not before प.
त् does not take the form of प.
Right: Before a voiceless consonant such as प the final त् stays as it is: तत् + पिबेत् = तत्पिबेत्.
त् → न् happens only before a nasal.
questions.explain: Same as तत्प्रवर्त्तते: no change before a voiceless consonant.
questions.teaches: A final त् stays unchanged before a voiceless consonant (तत् + प्रवर्तते → तत्प्रवर्तते; तत् + पिबेत् → तत्पिबेत्).
questions.section: औषध के बिगड़ने के कारण और उपाय

questions.q: In verse 88, by what is the medicine (held) in the second line?
optionExplain: Kapha is the obstructer of 05.03.96, not of this line.
Pitta is not named in verse 88.
Blood is not named in verse 88.
Right: वायुना भेषजे: when the medicine (is held) by Vāyu, wind.
questions.explain: Line 2: वायुना (instrumental), by Vāyu.
questions.section: औषध के बिगड़ने के कारण और उपाय

questions.q: Match each word of verse 88 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Clear words only; the flagged words are left out.
questions.rule: तिष्ठति = staying; ऊर्ध्वगत = gone upward; वायुना = by Vāyu; भेषज = medicine; पिबेत् = should drink.
questions.section: औषध के बिगड़ने के कारण और उपाय

questions.q: Put these words of verse 88 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Staying · gone upward · or even · by Vāyu · in the medicine · should drink.
questions.rule: तिष्ठति · ऊर्ध्वगते · अपि वा · वायुना · भेषजे · पिबेत्.
questions.teaches: Line 1 of verse 88 names जीर्णे, तिष्ठति and ऊर्ध्वगते (syntax uncertain); line 2 turns, with तु, to the case of Vāyu and ends in पिबेत्.
questions.section: औषध के बिगड़ने के कारण और उपाय

questions.q: Which split of the printed तिष्ठत्यूर्ध्वगते is right?
optionExplain: Right: इ before an unlike vowel becomes य्: तिष्ठति + ऊर्ध्वगते → तिष्ठत्यूर्ध्वगते.
तिष्ठत्य is no form.
ए + ऊ would not give यू.
यूर्ध्वगत is no word.
questions.explain: तिष्ठति (staying) + ऊर्ध्वगते (gone upward): इ + ऊ → यू.
questions.section: औषध के बिगड़ने के कारण और उपाय

questions.q: In verse 88, which word marks the turn to the second, different case?
optionExplain: वा joins the states of line 1; it does not turn to a new case.
Right: वायुना भेषजे त्वन्यत्…: तु, but, sets the Vāyu case against line 1.
अपि only adds 'gone upward' to the list of line 1.
अन्यत् names the other drink, not the turn.
questions.explain: तु opens the contrast: but when (held) by Vāyu …
questions.section: औषध के बिगड़ने के कारण और उपाय

questions.q: तु + अन्यत् gives त्वन्यत्. Join the invented pair मधु + अस्ति (there is honey) the same way. Which is right?
optionExplain: ओ would come from अ + उ, the other way round.
ऊ would come from उ + उ.
Right: उ before an unlike vowel becomes व्: मधु + अस्ति = मध्वस्ति.
अव् comes from ओ before a vowel, not from उ.
questions.explain: Same rule as त्वन्यत्.
questions.teaches: A final उ before an unlike vowel becomes व् (तु + अन्यत् → त्वन्यत्; मधु + अस्ति → मध्वस्ति).
questions.section: औषध के बिगड़ने के कारण और उपाय

questions.q: In verse 89, what kind of medicine is recommended when delusion, giddiness and fainting arise?
options: Fatty and salty, given with dry food
Astringent and making the body firm
optionExplain: That is the remedy of the next verse (05.03.103), for signs of Kapha.
Fat and salt belong to 05.03.99, not to verse 89.
Making firm is the remedy for atiyoga (05.03.53), not this verse.
Right: पित्तघ्नं स्वादुशीतं च भेषजं तत्र शस्यते: Pitta-destroying, sweet and cool.
questions.explain: Verse 89 names three qualities of the medicine: पित्तघ्न, स्वादु, शीत.
questions.rule: Signs while the medicine digests → Pitta-destroying, sweet, cool medicine.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 89 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Three signs of the first line and two words of the remedy in the second, as the card glosses them.
questions.rule: मोह = delusion; भ्रम = giddiness; मूर्च्छा = fainting; पित्तघ्न = Pitta-destroying; शस्यते = is recommended.

questions.q: Put the words of the second line of verse 89 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: पित्तघ्नं स्वादुशीतं च भेषजं तत्र शस्यते: the qualities first, then the medicine, then 'is recommended'.
questions.rule: पित्तघ्नं · स्वादुशीतं · च · भेषजं · तत्र · शस्यते.
questions.teaches: The remedy line of verse 89 puts the qualities (Pitta-destroying, sweet-cool) before the noun भेषजम् and ends with the passive verb शस्यते.

questions.q: Which split of the printed स्युर्जीर्यति is right?
optionExplain: Right: A visarga after उ becomes र् before a voiced sound: स्युः + जीर्यति → स्युर्जीर्यति.
र्जीर्यति is no word; the र् is the changed visarga of स्युः.
त् before ज would give ज्ज: स्युज्जीर्यति.
म् before a consonant would become anusvāra: स्युंजीर्यति.
questions.explain: स्युः (3 pl. optative of √अस्, 'may be') + जीर्यति (while being digested).
questions.rule: उः before a voiced sound → उर्.

questions.q: A patient on a cleansing medicine grows giddy and faints. By verse 89, which medicine fits?
options: A drink of hot water, taken at once
A dry food, given after digestion
optionExplain: That suits the Kapha signs of 05.03.102-103, not giddiness and fainting.
Right: Giddiness and fainting are named in verse 89; its remedy is Pitta-destroying, sweet and cool.
Hot water is for a held-back doṣa (05.03.90), not for these signs.
Dry food belongs to 05.03.98, not to verse 89.
questions.explain: भ्रम and मूर्च्छा → the medicine of verse 89: पित्तघ्न, स्वादु, शीत.
questions.rule: Verse 89: giddiness, fainting → sweet, cool, Pitta-destroying.

questions.q: पित्तघ्नम् means 'Pitta-destroying'. By the same pattern, what does an invented कफघ्नम् mean?
optionExplain: That would be कफज or कफकृत, not -घ्न.
Increasing is -वर्धन; -घ्न destroys.
Right: -घ्न at the end of a compound means 'destroying' the first member: कफ + घ्न = Kapha-destroying.
-घ्न is active: it destroys, it is not destroyed.
questions.explain: Same pattern as पित्तघ्नम्: X-घ्न = X-destroying.
questions.teaches: -घ्न (from √हन्) at the end of a compound means 'destroying' the first member: पित्तघ्न, कफघ्न.

questions.q: In verse 90, by what is (the medicine) enveloped when salivation and horripilation appear?
optionExplain: Pitta belongs to verse 89's remedy (पित्तघ्न), not to this covering.
Vāta is not named in verse 90.
Blood is not named in verse 90.
Right: कफावृते: when enveloped by Kapha.
questions.explain: कफ + आवृते: enveloped by Kapha.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 90 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Three signs and two qualities of the medicine, as the card glosses them.
questions.rule: लाला = salivation; विष्टम्भ = obstruction; रोमहर्ष = horripilation; तीक्ष्णोष्ण = sharp and hot; कफनुत् = Kapha-dispelling.

questions.q: Put these words of verse 90 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: The signs (लाला … विष्टंभ, रोमहर्ष), the cause (कफावृते), then the medicine: तीक्ष्णोष्णं … कफनुत्.
questions.teaches: Verse 90 runs signs → Kapha covering → qualities of the medicine, with the Kapha-dispelling quality near the end.

questions.q: Which split of the printed तीक्ष्णोष्णं is right?
optionExplain: Right: अ + उ → ओ: तीक्ष्ण + उष्णम् → तीक्ष्णोष्णम्.
ष्णम् is no word; the ओ comes from अ + उ.
अः before a vowel other than अ loses its visarga: तीक्ष्ण उष्णम्, two words.
अ + ओ would give औ: तीक्ष्णौष्णम्.
questions.explain: तीक्ष्ण (sharp) + उष्णम् (hot): the guṇa join अ + उ → ओ.

questions.q: After the medicine, a patient drools and his hair stands on end. Which medicine does verse 90 support?
options: Fatty, salty and drunk once more
optionExplain: That is verse 89's remedy, for delusion, giddiness and fainting.
Right: Salivation and horripilation show Kapha covering: the medicine is तीक्ष्णोष्ण, कफनुत्.
Making firm is for atiyoga (05.03.53), not for Kapha covering.
Fat and salt are for medicine held by Vāta (05.03.99).
questions.explain: लाला and रोमहर्ष → कफावृत → तीक्ष्ण, उष्ण, कफनुत् medicine.
questions.rule: Kapha signs → sharp, hot, Kapha-dispelling medicine.

questions.q: कफनुत् + हितम् gives कफनुद्धितम्. Join the invented pair वातनुत् + हितम् (Vāta-dispelling, beneficial) the same way. Which is right?
optionExplain: त् cannot stand unchanged before ह; it becomes द् (and here ह becomes ध).
The त् cannot stay voiceless before a voiced sound; it must become द्, giving द्ध.
Right: त् + ह → द्ध: वातनुत् + हितम् = वातनुद्धितम्, like कफनुद्धितम्.
The द् of the join cannot vanish; the form needs द्ध.
questions.explain: Same join as कफनुत् + हितम् → कफनुद्धितम्.
questions.teaches: A final त् before ह becomes द्, and the ह may become ध (as printed here): कफनुत् + हितम् → कफनुद्धितम्; वातनुत् + हितम् → वातनुद्धितम्.

questions.q: In verse 91, which complication is called 'severe' (भृश)?
optionExplain: परिस्रवः stands without भृश.
परिकर्तः stands without भृश.
Heaviness comes as स-गौरवम्, 'with heaviness', not भृश.
Right: भृशाध्मानम्: severe distension.
questions.explain: भृश + आध्मानम् = severe distension.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 91 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five items of the list, as the card glosses them.
questions.rule: गौरव = heaviness; उत्क्लेश = stirring up; आध्मान = distension; परिकर्त = cutting pain; परिस्रव = discharge.

questions.q: Put these complications of verse 91 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Line 1: contrary movement, knottedness (with heaviness). Line 2: stirring up of the doṣa, severe distension, cutting pain, discharge.
questions.rule: गति · ग्रथितत्व · उत्क्लेश · आध्मान · परिकर्त · परिस्रव.
questions.teaches: Verse 91 lists, in order: contrary movement, knottedness with heaviness, stirring up of the doṣa, severe distension, cutting pain, discharge.

questions.q: Which split of the printed पायोर्ग्रथितत्वं is right?
optionExplain: Right: A visarga after ओ becomes र् before a voiced sound: पायोः + ग्रथितत्वम् → पायोर्ग्रथितत्वम्.
र्ग्रथितत्वम् is no word; the र् is the changed visarga of पायोः.
That would print पायुर्ग्रथितत्वम्; the text has ओ, the genitive पायोः.
त् before ग would give द्: पायोद्ग्रथितत्वम्.
questions.explain: पायोः (genitive of पायु, anus) + ग्रथितत्वम् (knottedness).
questions.rule: ओः before a voiced sound → ओर्.

questions.q: After purgation, a patient feels a cutting pain. Which item of verse 91 names this?
optionExplain: परिस्रव is discharge, a flowing out.
Right: परिकर्त is glossed cutting pain.
उत्क्लेश is stirring up of the doṣa.
ग्रथितत्व is knottedness.
questions.explain: Cutting pain = परिकर्तः, an item of verse 91.

questions.q: सगौरवम् means 'with heaviness'. By the same pattern, what does an invented सशूलम् mean?
optionExplain: 'Without' would be निः- or अ-: निःशूल, अशूल.
स- adds 'with'; it does not mean 'only'.
Right: स- at the head of a bahuvrīhi means 'with': स + शूल = with pain.
स- is not a word of time.
questions.explain: Same pattern as सगौरवम्: स + X = with X.
questions.teaches: स- at the head of a bahuvrīhi means 'together with': सगौरव = with heaviness, सशूल = with pain.

questions.q: In verse 92, together with what are the twelve said to be stated?
options: With the doṣas that cause them
optionExplain: No doṣa is named in the summing-up; स-साधन = with remedy.
Causes are not the word here; साधन means remedy.
Signs are not the word here; साधन means remedy.
Right: ससाधनाः: with their remedies.
questions.explain: द्वादशोक्ताः ससाधनाः: twelve are stated, with their remedies.

questions.q: Match each item of verse 92 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The four complications of the verse and its closing word.
questions.rule: प्रवाहिका = dysentery (probable); हृद्ग्रहण = seizing of the heart; सर्वाङ्गपरिग्रह = whole-body gripping; सर्वधातुस्रव = flow of all dhātus; ससाधन = with remedies.

questions.q: Put these parts of verse 92 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Three complications, the flow of all dhātus, then the summing-up: twelve stated with remedies.
questions.rule: प्रवाहिका · हृद्ग्रहण · सर्वाङ्गपरिग्रह · सर्वधातुस्रव · द्वादश उक्ताः ससाधनाः.
questions.teaches: Verse 92 ends the list with pravāhikā, seizing of the heart, gripping of the whole body and the flow of all dhātus, then sums up: twelve, with remedies.

questions.q: Which split of the printed सर्वधातुस्रवेणैता is right?
optionExplain: Right: अ + ए → ऐ: स्रवेण + एताः → स्रवेणैता; the visarga of एताः drops before the voiced द of द्वादश.
आ + इ would give ए (स्रवेणेता), not ऐ.
अ + इ gives ए, not ऐ.
There is no form स्रवेणै; the ऐ is the join of अ and ए.
questions.explain: सर्वधातुस्रवेण (with the flow of all dhātus) + एताः (these): vṛddhi join अ + ए → ऐ.

questions.q: After purgation, a patient strains often and passes loose stools. Which item of verse 92 fits?
optionExplain: That is seizing of the heart, not straining at stool.
Right: Pravāhikā: straining with frequent loose stools, probably dysentery.
That is gripping of the whole body.
That is the flow of all the dhātus, not straining with loose stools.
questions.explain: Straining with frequent loose stools = प्रवाहिका (probably dysentery).

questions.q: द्वादश + उक्ताः gives द्वादशोक्ताः. Which is the right join of the invented pair दश + उक्ताः (ten are stated)?
optionExplain: अ + उ does not give आ.
औ comes from अ + ओ or अ + औ, not अ + उ.
Right: अ + उ → ओ: दश + उक्ताः = दशोक्ताः, like द्वादशोक्ताः.
The अ cannot simply drop before उ.
questions.explain: Same guṇa join as द्वादशोक्ताः.
questions.teaches: Final अ + initial उ → ओ: द्वादश + उक्ताः → द्वादशोक्ताः; दश + उक्ताः → दशोक्ताः.

questions.q: From what, according to unit 93, do the complications (vyāpad) arise?
options: From giving it in a cold season
From a lapse in the application
optionExplain: Digestion is not named in unit 93.
No season is named in unit 93.
Oiling is not named in unit 93.
Right: योगविभ्रंशात्: from a slip, a lapse, in the application (yoga).
questions.explain: योग (application) + विभ्रंशात् (from a lapse), in the ablative of cause.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 93 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The four key words of the line, as the card glosses them.
questions.rule: व्यापद् = complication; योग = application; विभ्रंश = lapse; विरेचन = purgation.

questions.q: Put the words of unit 93 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: व्यापदो योगविभ्रंशाद्विविधेऽपि विरेचने: complications, from a lapse in application, even in various, purgation.
questions.teaches: Unit 93 names the result first (व्यापदः), then its cause in the ablative (योगविभ्रंशात्), then where it happens (विरेचने).

questions.q: The printed व्यापदो योग… stands for which form before योग?
optionExplain: Right: अः before a voiced sound becomes ओ: व्यापदः + योग… → व्यापदो योग….
आ would stay आ before य: व्यापदा योग….
म् before य would become anusvāra: व्यापदं योग….
औ stays औ before a consonant: व्यापदौ योग….
questions.explain: व्यापदः, nominative plural: the visarga with अ becomes ओ before the voiced य.
questions.rule: अः before a voiced consonant → ओ.

questions.q: Unit 93: ____ (complications) arise from a lapse in the application. Type it in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: व्यापदः (nom. pl. of व्यापद्), printed व्यापदो before योग.
questions.teaches: Unit 93 names the complications of cleansing व्यापद् and traces them to a lapse in the application.

questions.q: योगविभ्रंशात् is ablative: from a lapse. Which invented form of अतियोग (excess) means from excess?
optionExplain: -ए is the locative: 'in excess'.
Right: -आत् is the ablative of an अ-stem: 'from'. अतियोग → अतियोगात्, like विभ्रंश → विभ्रंशात्.
-एन is the instrumental: 'by excess'.
-स्य is the genitive: 'of excess'.
questions.explain: Ablative singular of अ-stems in -आत् marks the cause, 'from'.
questions.teaches: The ablative singular of an अ-stem ends in -आत् and can mark the cause: योगविभ्रंशात् 'from a lapse', अतियोगात् 'from excess'.

questions.q: What does verse 94 call the śāstra?
options: The root of every remedy for the twelve
A wall that keeps back every complication
The light of sound and unsound conduct
The memory of the earlier physicians
optionExplain: No 'root' is named; the image is ज्योतिः, light.
No wall is named; the image is light.
Right: ज्योतिर्हि शास्त्रं नयदुर्नयानाम्: the śāstra is the light of naya and durnaya.
Earlier physicians are not named; the image is light.
questions.explain: ज्योतिः = light; नय-दुर्नय = sound and unsound conduct.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 94 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five key words of the verse, as the card glosses them.
questions.rule: उत्पद्यमान = arising; दिशा = by the direction; आशु = quickly; सिद्धि = cure; ज्योतिः = light.

questions.q: Put these parts of verse 94 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Arising complications, through a deviation in cleansing; by this direction, quickly; strive for cure; for the śāstra is the light.
questions.rule: उत्पद्यमानासु · तासु तासु व्यापत्सु · संशोधनविभ्रमेण · दिशाऽनयैवाशु · यतेत सिद्धौ · ज्योतिर्हि शास्त्रम्.
questions.teaches: Verse 94 sets the situation (complications arising from a deviation in cleansing), gives the command (strive quickly by this direction) and ends with the reason (हि: the śāstra is light).

questions.q: Which split of the printed ज्योतिर्हि is right?
optionExplain: र्हि is no word; the र् is the changed visarga of ज्योतिः.
A long ई would print ज्योतीर्हि; the text has short इ.
म् before ह would become anusvāra: ज्योतिंहि.
Right: A visarga after इ becomes र् before a voiced sound: ज्योतिः + हि → ज्योतिर्हि.
questions.explain: ज्योतिः (light, n. nom. sg.) + हि (for): इः before a voiced sound → इर्.
questions.rule: इः before a voiced sound → इर्.

questions.q: A complication arises from a deviation in cleansing. What does verse 94 tell the physician to do?
options: Strive quickly for cure by this direction
Stop all cleansing and wait for a season
Give the same medicine again in double dose
Send the patient to another physician
optionExplain: Right: दिशाऽनयैवाशु यतेत सिद्धौ: by this very direction he should quickly strive for the cure.
Verse 94 asks for quick effort, not waiting.
No dose is named; the guidance is 'this direction'.
Verse 94 tells the physician himself to strive.
questions.explain: Situation: complications from a deviation in cleansing. Command: यतेत सिद्धौ, quickly, by this direction.

questions.q: दुर्- turns नय 'sound conduct' into दुर्नय 'unsound conduct'. By the same pattern, what does दुर्जन mean?
optionExplain: 'Good' would be सत्- or सु-: सज्जन.
Right: दुर्- means 'bad, ill': दुर् + जन = a bad person, as दुर् + नय = unsound conduct.
दुर्- marks badness, not number.
'No' would be अ- or निः-, not दुर्-.
questions.explain: Same prefix as दुर्नय: दुर्- = bad.
questions.teaches: The prefix दुर्- means 'bad, ill': नय → दुर्नय (unsound conduct), जन → दुर्जन (a bad person).

questions.q: What is the name of the chapter closed by unit 95?
optionExplain: Basti (enema) is not in this chapter's name.
That is the name of the first chapter of Kalpasthāna.
Right: वमनविरेचनव्यापत्सिद्धिर्नाम: named the cure of the complications of emesis and purgation.
No नेत्र or बस्ति is in this chapter's name.
questions.explain: The colophon names the chapter after its subject: the cure of vyāpad in vamana and virecana.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 95 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The four members of the chapter's name and its number.
questions.rule: वमन = emesis; विरेचन = purgation; व्यापत् = complication; सिद्धि = cure; तृतीय = third.

questions.q: Put the members of the chapter's name in the order of the text.
questions.explain: वमन-विरेचन-व्यापत्-सिद्धि: emesis, purgation, complication, cure.
questions.teaches: The chapter's name is read from the end: the cure (सिद्धि) of the complications (व्यापत्) of emesis and purgation.

questions.q: Which split of the printed सिद्धिर्नाम is right?
optionExplain: र्नाम is no word; the र् is the changed visarga of सिद्धिः.
म् before न would become anusvāra: सिद्धिंनाम.
That would print सिद्धिरनाम, with an अ after र्.
Right: A visarga after इ becomes र् before the voiced न: सिद्धिः + नाम → सिद्धिर्नाम.
questions.explain: सिद्धिः (nom. sg.) + नाम (named).
questions.rule: इः before a voiced sound → इर्.

questions.q: The chapter's first line (05.03.1) promised to explain this same title. What does unit 95 mark?
options: That the promised explanation is complete
A fresh list of the twelve complications
A new remedy for vyāpad in enemas (basti)
The name of the fourth chapter to follow
optionExplain: Right: इति … अध्यायः: thus (ends) the chapter that 05.03.1 announced.
The list was in 05.03.104-107; the colophon adds nothing.
No remedy is given in a colophon.
It names this, the third, chapter.
questions.explain: Opening line: व्याख्यास्यामः (we shall explain). Colophon: इति (thus), the chapter is done.
questions.rule: A colophon closes the chapter its opening line announced.

questions.q: तृतीयोऽध्यायः means the third chapter. Which invented form means the fourth chapter?
optionExplain: That is plural: four chapters.
Right: चतुर्थः (fourth) + अध्यायः: अः + अ → ओऽ, as in तृतीयोऽध्यायः.
That is locative: in the fourth chapter.
चतुर्धा means fourfold, not fourth.
questions.explain: Ordinal + अध्यायः, joined by अः + अ → ओऽ.
questions.teaches: Ordinals in -अः join अध्यायः as -ओऽध्यायः: तृतीयोऽध्यायः (third chapter), चतुर्थोऽध्यायः (fourth chapter).

questions.q: Which topic does unit 1 announce for the chapter?
options: The rules of the daily routine
The signs of a healthy body
optionExplain: No daily routine is named; the word is बस्तिकल्प.
Nasal drops are not named; basti is the medicated enema.
Right: बस्तिकल्पम्: kalpa (set of preparations) of basti, the medicated enema.
The formula names only the Basti-kalpa.
questions.explain: The formula names one topic: बस्तिकल्प, the preparations for basti (medicated enema).
questions.rule: बस्ति = medicated enema; कल्प = set of preparations.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 1 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These five words make up the whole formula.
questions.rule: अथ = now; अतः = therefore; बस्ति = enema; कल्प = preparations; व्याख्यास्यामः = we shall explain.

questions.q: Put the words of the formula in the order of unit 1.
questions.explain: Now, therefore, the Basti-kalpa, we shall explain: the topic stands before the verb.
questions.teaches: The opening formula runs: अथ (now), अतः (therefore), the topic in the accusative, and the verb last.

questions.q: Which is the right split of अथातो in unit 1?
optionExplain: Neither अथा nor तो is the word; the words are अथ and अतः.
आतः is not a word here; the word is अतः, therefore.
अथ is an indeclinable with no visarga, and the base form is अतः.
Right: अ + अ → आ (अथा-), and -अः before a voiced sound (here ब) → -ओ.
questions.explain: अथ (now) + अतः (therefore) = अथातो before बस्तिकल्पं.
questions.rule: अ + अ → आ; -अः before a voiced consonant → -ओ.

questions.q: Who speaks in व्याख्यास्यामः, and when is the action set?
optionExplain: Right: The data labels it 1st person plural future: we shall explain.
That would be a 3rd person singular present, like व्याख्याति.
No past tense is used; -स्यामः marks the future.
It is not an imperative; -स्यामः is the 'we' future ending.
questions.explain: व्याख्यास्यामः = 1 pl. future of वि-आ-√ख्या: we shall explain.

questions.q: Using the same formula, which line would announce an invented Vamana-kalpa?
optionExplain: वमनकल्पः is nominative; the object of 'we shall explain' takes the accusative.
Right: The topic is the object, so it stays accusative (-ं / -म्), as with बस्तिकल्पम्.
व्याख्यास्यति is 'he will explain'; the formula uses 'we'.
वमनकल्पेन is instrumental, 'by means of', not the object.
questions.explain: Only the topic word changes; it stays an accusative object of व्याख्यास्यामः.
questions.teaches: In the opening formula the topic is the accusative object (-म्) of व्याख्यास्यामः, 'we shall explain'.

questions.q: How far is the mixture cooked down in verse 2?
optionExplain: Half (अर्द्ध) belongs to the tulā of meat, not to the cooking.
An eighth is the end point of the recipe in verse 9, not here.
Right: चतुर्थशेषम्: with a fourth part remaining.
The verse keeps a quarter; it does not boil the water away.
questions.explain: पचेदप्सु चतुर्थशेषम्: cook in water, with a quarter remaining.
questions.rule: Verse 2 ends the cooking at चतुर्थशेष, a quarter.

questions.q: Match each drug of verse 2 to its identity as the card gives it.
questions.explain: Balā, guḍūcī and triphalā are standard identifications; dvipañcamūla is the group called daśamūla.
questions.rule: बला = country mallow; गुडूची = giloy; त्रिफला = three myrobalans; द्विपंचमूल = ten roots.

questions.q: Put these drugs of verse 2, line 1, in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Line 1 runs balā, guḍūcī, triphalā, with rāsnā, then the ten-root group.
questions.teaches: Line 1 names five items in this order, all measured by the pala (पलोन्मितानि).

questions.q: Which is the right split of फलान्यर्द्धतुलां in verse 2?
optionExplain: यर्द्धतुला is not a word; the measure is अर्द्धतुला, half a tulā.
-आः before a vowel drops its visarga; it would not give न्य.
There is no word अन्यर्द्धतुला, and अष्टौ needs the plural फलानि.
Right: इ before a different vowel becomes य्: फलानि + अर्द्ध… = फलान्यर्द्ध….
questions.explain: आठ फल (अष्टौ फलानि) and half a tulā (अर्द्धतुलाम्) are two separate items.

questions.q: In verse 2, what quantity of goat meat is cooked?
optionExplain: Right: अर्द्धतुलां च मांसाच्छागात्: half a tulā of goat meat.
Eight (अष्टौ) counts the fruits, not the meat.
A quarter is what remains after cooking, not the meat.
No prastha is named in this verse.
questions.explain: The meat is in the ablative (मांसात् छागात्, from goat meat); its amount is अर्द्धतुला.
questions.rule: अर्द्धतुला = half a tulā (a large unit of weight).

questions.q: Join invented पचेत् + अन्नम् as one sandhi string, like पचेदप्सु. Which is right?
optionExplain: त् does not stay voiceless before a vowel.
Right: Final त् becomes द् before a vowel, as in पचेत् + अप्सु = पचेदप्सु.
त् becomes न् only before a nasal, not before अ.
त् → च्छ only before श्, not before a vowel.
questions.explain: Same rule as पचेत् + अप्सु → पचेदप्सु.
questions.teaches: A final त् becomes द् before a vowel (पचेत् + अप्सु = पचेदप्सु; पचेत् + अन्नम् = पचेदन्नम्).

questions.q: In verse 3, at what point are the pastes added?
optionExplain: The cooking was in verse 2; पूते comes after it.
The pastes are part of the basti, not added afterwards.
Right: पूते: when (it) has been strained; then the pastes follow.
The verse speaks of straining, not of boiling.
questions.explain: पूते is a locative absolute: when strained.
questions.rule: पूते = when strained (√पू, to purify, strain).

questions.q: Put these paste drugs of verse 3 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: After यवानीफल the compound runs bilva, kuṣṭha, vacā, (śatāhvā, printed with a letter slip), ghana, pippalī.

questions.q: Match each drug of verse 3 to its identity as the card gives it.
questions.explain: These five identifications are labelled standard in the data.
questions.rule: बिल्व = bael; कुष्ठ = costus; वचा = sweet flag; पिप्पली = long pepper; मृद्वीका = grape/raisin.
questions.teaches: The paste drugs and additions of verse 3 have standard identifications: bael, costus, sweet flag, long pepper, grape.

questions.q: Which is the right split of सुखोष्णो in verse 3?
optionExplain: म् before a vowel stays: it would be सुखमुष्णः.
-अः before a vowel drops the visarga and does not join: सुख उष्णः.
औ before a vowel becomes आव्: it would be सुखावुष्णः.
Right: अ + उ → ओ (सुखोष्ण); -अः before the voiced ल → -ओ.
questions.explain: सुखोष्ण = pleasantly warm: सुख + उष्ण.

questions.q: Besides the pastes, which of these does verse 3 add to the basti?
optionExplain: Right: घृत is in the same compound.
Urine is added in the recipe of verse 10, not here.
Right: लवणान्वितः, endowed with salt.
Milk is not named in this verse.
Right: मृद्वीका-क्षौद्र-घृतैः names honey.
questions.explain: Verse 3 adds grape, honey, ghee, oil and salt, and the basti is pleasantly warm.
questions.rule: Additions: मृद्वीका, क्षौद्र, घृत, तैल, लवण.

questions.q: Join invented घृत + अन्वितः, like लवणान्वितः. Which is right?
optionExplain: Right: अ + अ → आ, as in लवण + अन्वितः = लवणान्वितः.
ओ comes from अ + उ, not from अ + अ.
ए comes from अ + इ, not from अ + अ.
The two vowels do not simply lose one; they merge into आ.
questions.explain: Same rule as लवण + अन्वितः → लवणान्वितः.
questions.teaches: Two short अ vowels merge into आ (लवण + अन्वितः = लवणान्वितः; घृत + अन्वितः = घृतान्वितः).

questions.q: According to verse 4, for whom is this basti also beneficial?
optionExplain: Fever is not named in this verse.
Right: स्वस्थे हितः: beneficial in (for) a healthy person.
Age is not mentioned.
Children are not mentioned.
questions.explain: Besides destroying all diseases, the basti is स्वस्थे हितः, good for the healthy too.
questions.rule: स्वस्थे हितः = beneficial for a healthy person.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 4 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words carry the praise in line 1 and the rule in line 2.
questions.rule: सर्वगदप्रमाथी = destroyer of all diseases; स्वस्थे = in the healthy; कल्कः = paste; दद्यात् = should give.

questions.q: Put these phrases of verse 4 in the verse's order.
items: बस्तौ च यस्मिन् प्रणितो न कल्कः
questions.explain: First the praise (destroyer, good for the healthy, life-giving and nourishing), then the rule for bastis without a paste.
questions.rule: Praise in line 1; rule in line 2.
questions.teaches: Verse 4 moves from what the basti does (line 1) to where it is used (line 2).

questions.q: Which is the right split of दद्यादमुमेव in verse 4?
optionExplain: दमुम् is not a word; the pronoun is अमुम्.
मेव is not a word; एव (very) follows अमुम्.
Right: त् → द् before a vowel; म् + ए joins as मे.
म् + इ would give मि, not मे; the word is एव.
questions.explain: दद्यात् (one should give) + अमुम् (this) + एव (very).

questions.q: A basti recipe states no paste. What does verse 4 say to do there?
optionExplain: The verse does not forbid the basti; it supplies what is missing.
Milk is not mentioned in the verse.
Temperature is not the subject of line 2.
Right: बस्तौ यस्मिन् न कल्कः … दद्यादमुमेव तत्र: in that basti give this very one.
questions.explain: The rule fills a gap: where no paste is stated, this one (taken as the paste of verse 3) is given.

questions.q: Join invented हितः + भवति, like स्वस्थे हितो जीवन…. Which is right?
optionExplain: Right: -अः before a voiced consonant (भ) becomes -ओ.
-र् comes from -इः or -उः, not from -अः.
-अः never becomes -आ; before the voiced भ it becomes -ओ.
स् appears before त्, not before a voiced भ.
questions.explain: Same rule as हितः + जीवन… → हितो जीवन….
questions.teaches: A final -अः becomes -ओ before a voiced consonant (हितः + जीवन = हितो जीवन; हितः + भवति = हितो भवति).

questions.q: What does verse 5 say this nirūha removes?
optionExplain: Kapha is not named in this verse.
Right: सर्वानिलव्याधिहरः: remover of all anila (wind, Vāta) diseases.
Pitta is not named in this verse.
No fever or thirst is mentioned.
questions.explain: अनिल = wind = Vāta; the nirūha removes all its diseases.
questions.rule: सर्व-अनिल-व्याधि-हर = remover of all Vāta diseases.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 5 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are the key words of the recipe and its claim.
questions.rule: रस = liquid; अम्ल = sour; त्रिस्नेह = three fats; निरूह = decoction enema; अनिल = Vāta.

questions.q: Put these words of verse 5 in the verse's order (the damaged word is left out).
questions.explain: Ten roots, the sour-joined rasa, goat meat; then the three fats, the foremost nirūha, and its claim.
questions.rule: द्विपंचमूलस्य · रसोऽम्लयुक्तः · सच्छागमांसस्य · त्रिस्नेहयुक्तः · प्रवरो निरूहः · सर्वानिलव्याधिहरः.
questions.teaches: Line 1 gives the ingredients of the rasa; line 2 adds the three fats and names the result.

questions.q: Which is the right split of रसोऽम्लयुक्तः in verse 5?
optionExplain: म्लयुक्त is not a word; the word is अम्लयुक्त.
म् before a vowel stays: it would be रसमम्ल….
Right: -अः + अ- → -ओ, and the अ- is dropped (shown by ऽ).
आ + अ → आ, giving रसाम्ल…, not रसोऽम्ल….
questions.explain: रसः (liquid) + अम्लयुक्तः (joined with sour).

questions.q: A student says verse 5 names the three fats as ghee, oil and marrow. What does the card say?
options: The verse names them in line 2
The verse names oil and honey
The verse does not name them
optionExplain: Line 2 has only त्रिस्नेहयुक्तः, with no names.
Ghee is not named in this verse.
Neither oil nor honey is named here.
Right: त्रिस्नेह is named as a group only; its members are not given here.
questions.explain: The three fats are conventionally ghee, oil and vasā or majjā, but this verse does not list them.
questions.rule: Only what the verse names belongs to its list.

questions.q: A basti (masc.) joined with honey: which invented phrase agrees (words shown unjoined), like त्रिस्नेहयुक्तः निरूहः?
optionExplain: Right: बस्ति is masculine here, so the -युक्त compound takes -अः, like निरूहः.
-आ is the feminine ending.
-अम् is neuter (or accusative), not masculine nominative.
-आः is plural; बस्तिः is singular.
questions.explain: An adjective compound ending in -युक्त agrees with its noun: त्रिस्नेहयुक्तः निरूहः (m. nom. sg.).
questions.rule: Adjective agrees with the noun in gender, number, case.
questions.teaches: An adjective compound like त्रिस्नेहयुक्त agrees with its noun: masculine singular nominative -अः (निरूहः, बस्तिः).

questions.q: Which measure does verse 6 use for the liquid?
optionExplain: The akṣa is named in verse 10, not here.
Right: प्रस्थो रसात्: a prastha from the liquid; and again until प्रस्थसमः.
Half a tulā is the meat in verse 2.
Two āḍhakas of water come in verse 9.
questions.explain: The measure in this verse is the prastha, used twice.
questions.rule: प्रस्थ = a unit of measure; the verse uses it twice.

questions.q: Put these drugs of verse 6 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: One long compound runs balā, paṭolī, the small five roots, trāyantikā, eraṇḍa, yava.
questions.rule: बला · पटोली · लघुपंचमूल · त्रायन्तिका · एरण्ड · यव.

questions.q: Match each drug of verse 6 to its identity as the card gives it.
questions.explain: These four are standard identifications in the data; trāyantikā is disputed and left out.
questions.rule: बला = country mallow; पटोली = pointed gourd; एरण्ड = castor; यव = barley.
questions.teaches: Of the six drugs of verse 6, balā, paṭolī, eraṇḍa and yava have standard identifications.

questions.q: What does सुसिद्धात् at the end of the compound mean?
optionExplain: सु means well, not half.
सिद्ध means cooked, the opposite of raw.
Right: सु (well) + सिद्ध (cooked), ablative -आत्: from what is well cooked.
Grinding is not named; सिद्ध is cooked.
questions.explain: The whole drug compound ends in this ablative: from (the) well-cooked (mass).
questions.rule: सुसिद्धात् = from the well-cooked (सिद्ध = पकाया हुआ).

questions.q: How long is the prastha of liquid with goat broth cooked again in verse 6?
options: Until it is thick as paste
optionExplain: An eighth is the end point in verse 9.
A quarter is the end point in verse 2.
Thickness is not mentioned.
Right: साध्यः पुनः प्रस्थसमः स यावत्: prepared again until it equals a prastha.
questions.explain: The end point is प्रस्थसम, equal to a prastha.
questions.rule: यावत् प्रस्थसमः = until it equals a prastha.

questions.q: Like यवात् (from barley), which invented form means from milk?
optionExplain: Right: -आत् is the ablative singular, 'from', as in यवात्, रसात्, सुसिद्धात्.
-एन is instrumental, 'with milk'.
-अस्य is genitive, 'of milk'.
-ए is locative, 'in milk'.
questions.explain: The ablative of an अ-stem ends in -आत्.
questions.teaches: The ablative singular of an अ-stem ends in -आत्, 'from' (यवात्, रसात्; क्षीरात् from milk).

questions.q: Which word of verse 7 means at once?
optionExplain: पुनः means again (verse 6).
Right: सद्यः = at once; it closes the verse.
तत्र means there (verse 4).
सर्वत्र means everywhere (verse 4).
questions.explain: चक्षुर्बलं चोपदधाति सद्यः: it at once bestows strength of the eyes.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 7 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Kṛṣṇā is another name of pippalī; saindhava is rock salt.
questions.rule: कृष्णा = long pepper; सर्पिः = ghee; मधु = honey; सैंधव = rock salt; दीपन = kindler.

questions.q: Put these additions of verse 7 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: First the paste, then oil, ghee, honey and rock salt under one स-.
questions.teaches: Verse 7 adds the paste first, then four additions in the order oil, ghee, honey, rock salt.

questions.q: Which is the right split of स्याद्दीपनो in verse 7?
optionExplain: द्दीपन is not a word; the word is दीपन.
द्दीपन is not a word; the first द् is स्यात्'s त् voiced, and the noun is दीपनः.
Right: त् → द् before the voiced द; -अः → -ओ before the voiced म.
स्याः is not the verb; the verb is स्यात्, it would be.
questions.explain: स्यात् (it would be) + दीपनः (a kindler).

questions.q: Which effects does verse 7 name for this basti?
optionExplain: Fever is not named in this verse.
Right: मांसबलप्रदः, giver of flesh and strength.
Right: the same compound names strength.
Kapha is not named in this verse.
Right: स्याद्दीपनः.
questions.explain: The verse names kindling, flesh and strength, and strength of the eyes at once.

questions.q: Join invented च + उष्णम्, like चोपदधाति. Which is right?
optionExplain: औ comes from अ + ओ or औ, not from अ + उ.
The अ does not simply drop; it merges with उ into ओ.
व् comes from उ before a vowel, not from अ.
Right: अ + उ → ओ, as in च + उपदधाति = चोपदधाति.
questions.explain: Same rule as च + उपदधाति → चोपदधाति.
questions.teaches: अ + उ gives ओ (च + उपदधाति = चोपदधाति; च + उष्णम् = चोष्णम्).

questions.q: How much eraṇḍa root does verse 8 give?
optionExplain: Right: एरंडमूलात् त्रिपलम्: three palas from the eraṇḍa root.
Half a tulā is the meat of verse 2.
The prastha is the measure of verse 6.
The akṣa is the measure in verse 10.
questions.explain: त्रिपलम् = three palas.

questions.q: Match each drug of verse 8 to its identity as the card gives it.
questions.explain: All five are labelled standard in the data; chinnaruhā is a name of guḍūcī.
questions.rule: एरण्ड = castor; छिन्नरुहा = giloy; अश्वगन्धा = winter cherry; पुनर्नवा = hogweed; देवदारु = deodar.

questions.q: Put these drugs of verse 8, line 2, in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The list runs rāsnā, balā, chinnaruhā, aśvagandhā, punarnavā, then āragvadha and devadāru.
questions.rule: रास्ना · बला · छिन्नरुहा · अश्वगन्धा · पुनर्नवा (· आरग्वध · देवदारु).
questions.teaches: Line 2 is one compound of seven drug names, from rāsnā to devadāru, with no quantities.

questions.q: Which is the right split of बलाच्छिन्नरुहा in verse 8?
optionExplain: शिन्नरुहा is not a word; the drug is छिन्नरुहा, giloy.
Right: छ after a vowel becomes च्छ (always after a short vowel, optionally after a long one like आ): बला + छिन्न… = बलाच्छिन्न….
बलाच् is not a word; the drug is बला.
-आः before छ would become -आश्छ, not -आच्छ.
questions.explain: Two drug names of the list: बला (country mallow) and छिन्नरुहा (giloy).
questions.rule: Vowel + छ → vowel + च्छ (optional after a long vowel).

questions.q: Verse 8 has no verb. Where are its drugs cooked?
optionExplain: पचेत् is the verb of verse 2; verse 8 has no verb.
Verse 2 is a different recipe.
Right: The notes: the drugs are cooked in the next line, विपाचयेत्, one should cook thoroughly.
The paste of verse 10 is ground; these drugs are cooked.
questions.explain: Verse 8 lists; verse 9 cooks (विपाचयेत्) with eight fruits in two āḍhakas of water.
questions.rule: List in verse 8 → cooking in verse 9.

questions.q: Like त्रिपलम् (three palas), which invented form means two palas?
optionExplain: The number goes in as its stem द्वि, not as द्वौ.
-आः is masculine plural; the dvigu is neuter singular.
In a dvigu the number comes first.
Right: Number + measure make a dvigu compound, neuter singular -म्, like त्रिपलम्.
questions.explain: त्रि + पल → त्रिपलम्; द्वि + पल → द्विपलम्.
questions.teaches: A number stem plus a measure makes a dvigu compound in neuter -म् (त्रिपलम्, द्विपलम्; also द्विपंचमूलम्).

questions.q: How much water does verse 9 give for the cooking?
optionExplain: Right: सलिलाढकाभ्याम्: with two āḍhakas of water (dual).
The prastha is the measure of verse 6.
Palas are not given for the water here.
Half a tulā is the meat of verse 2.
questions.explain: सलिल = water; आढकाभ्याम् = with two āḍhakas.
questions.rule: सलिल-आढकाभ्याम् = with two āḍhakas of water.

questions.q: Match each paste drug of verse 9 to its identity as the card gives it.
questions.explain: These five are labelled standard in the data; vatsaka is a name of kuṭaja.
questions.rule: वचा = sweet flag; यष्टी = liquorice; कणा = long pepper; वत्सकबीज = kuṭaja seeds; मुस्त = nut-grass.

questions.q: Put these paste drugs of verse 9 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: After the unclear word the list runs priyaṅgu, yaṣṭī, kaṇā, vatsaka seeds, musta.
questions.teaches: The paste list of verse 9 ends priyaṅgu, yaṣṭī, kaṇā, vatsaka seeds, musta; its use is in verse 10.

questions.q: Which is the right split of अष्टमशेषितेऽस्मिन् in verse 9?
optionExplain: -अः + अ- would give -ओऽ (शेषितोऽस्मिन्), not -एऽ.
Right: -ए + अ- → -ए, and the अ- is dropped (shown by ऽ).
स्मिन् is not a word; the pronoun is अस्मिन्.
ऐ before a vowel becomes आय्, not एऽ.
questions.explain: अष्टमशेषिते (being left at an eighth) + अस्मिन् (this): a locative absolute.

questions.q: Someone following verse 9 stops cooking when a quarter is left. What does the verse say?
options: Right, a quarter is the end point
Cook on until an eighth remains
Cook until no water is left
optionExplain: A quarter is the end point of verse 2, not of verse 9.
Half is not named as an end point.
Right: अष्टमशेषिते: the end point is an eighth, not a quarter.
The verse keeps an eighth.
questions.explain: Verse 2 ends at a quarter (चतुर्थशेष); verse 9 at an eighth (अष्टमशेष).
questions.rule: Verse 9: cook down to an eighth.

questions.q: Like सलिलाढकाभ्याम् (with two āḍhakas), which invented form means with two hands?
optionExplain: -एन is instrumental singular: with one hand.
-ऐः is instrumental plural: with many hands.
-अयोः is genitive or locative dual, not 'with'.
Right: -आभ्याम् is the instrumental dual of an अ-stem: with two.
questions.explain: आढक → आढकाभ्याम्, हस्त → हस्ताभ्याम्.
questions.teaches: The instrumental dual of an अ-stem ends in -आभ्याम्, 'with two' (आढकाभ्याम्, हस्ताभ्याम्).

questions.q: Which two actions does verse 10 give this basti?
optionExplain: Right: लेखनदीपनः: lekhana (scraping) and dīpana (kindling).
Neither is named; the word is लेखन-दीपन.
Nourishing (बृंहण) is said of the basti of verse 4, not here.
Neither is named in this verse.
questions.explain: बस्तिर्जयेल्लेखनदीपनोऽसौ: that scraping and kindling basti would overcome ….

questions.q: Match each word of verse 10 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words give the preparation, an addition and what the basti does.
questions.rule: सुपिष्टम् = well ground; लवण = salt; मूत्र = urine; लेखन = scraping; जयेत् = would overcome.

questions.q: Put these words of verse 10, line 2, in the verse's order.
questions.explain: With mākṣika, with oil, with urine; then the basti and its verb.
questions.teaches: Line 2 lists three additions (mākṣika, oil, urine) before naming the basti and its verb जयेत्.

questions.q: Which is the right split of बस्तिर्जयेल्लेखन… in verse 10?
optionExplain: जयेल् is not a word; the verb is जयेत्.
Right: -इः before a voiced sound → -इर्; त् + ल → ल्ल.
म् before ज would be ं, not र्.
ल्लेखन is not a word; the word is लेखन.
questions.explain: बस्तिः (the basti) + जयेत् (would overcome) + लेखनदीपनः (scraping and kindling).

questions.q: Mākṣika stands beside oil and urine in verse 10. What does the card say it is?
optionExplain: A mineral is only the other sense; the data says probably honey.
Salt is a separate item (लवणांश).
Right: The data: mākṣika is probably honey; the word can also name a mineral.
Ghee is not named in this verse.
questions.explain: Mākṣika is hedged: probably honey; the text does not say.

questions.q: Join invented तत् + लभते, like जयेत् + लेखन. Which is right?
optionExplain: Before ल the त् assimilates fully to ल्; it does not stop at द्.
In sandhi the त् does not stay before ल.
Anusvara comes from म्, not from त्.
Right: त् before ल becomes ल्: जयेत् + लेखन = जयेल्लेखन.
questions.explain: Same rule as जयेत् + लेखन → जयेल्लेखन.

questions.teaches: A final न् before त् becomes ं + स् (तान् + तान् = तांस्तान्; देवान् + तत्र = देवांस्तत्र).

questions.q: Like चतुष्पले 'in four palas', which invented form means in a measure of two palas?

questions.q: In verse 13, which word does युक्तं (joined) agree with?

questions.q: Like …हितो निरूहः, which invented phrase says milk (पयः, neuter) is beneficial in visarpa?
