questions.explain: Kuṣṭha is costus root; akṣa and prasṛta are measures; sārṣapa qualifies the oil.
questions.rule: कुष्ठ = costus; अक्ष = weight unit; प्रसृत = handful; क्षौद्र = honey; सार्षप = of mustard.
questions.teaches: Verse 19 mixes drugs (कुष्ठ, क्षौद्र) with measures (अक्ष, प्रसृत); सार्षप is an adjective 'of mustard'.

questions.q: In line 2 of verse 19, what does सार्षपस्य qualify?
optionExplain: क्षौद्रस्य stands first, far from सार्षपस्य.
Kṣāra is a separate item, not mustard.
फलाह्वय is a separate, unidentified item.
Right: तैलस्य च सार्षपस्य: of mustard oil.
questions.explain: सार्षपस्य (adj., gen.) agrees with the second तैलस्य: of mustard oil.
questions.rule: An adjective qualifies the noun it agrees with, here तैलस्य.

questions.q: Which is the right split of सकुष्ठैरक्षप्रमाणैः in verse 19?
optionExplain: Right: -ऐः before a vowel → -ऐर्: सकुष्ठैर् + अक्ष….
रक्षप्रमाण is no word; the र् comes from the visarga of -ऐः.
ऐरक्षप्रमाण is no word; the measure is अक्षप्रमाण.
म् before a vowel stays: it would read सकुष्ठमक्ष….
questions.explain: सकुष्ठैः (with kuṣṭha) + अक्षप्रमाणैः (with akṣa-measures).

questions.q: Like क्षौद्रस्य 'of honey', which form means of milk, from क्षीर (neuter)?
optionExplain: Instrumental: 'with milk'.
Right: Genitive singular -अस्य of an -अ stem, like क्षौद्रस्य.
Ablative: 'from milk'.
Locative: 'in milk'.
questions.explain: क्षौद्र → क्षौद्रस्य; क्षीर → क्षीरस्य.
questions.teaches: An -अ stem takes -अस्य in the genitive singular, 'of' (क्षौद्रस्य, तैलस्य, क्षीरस्य).

questions.q: In verse 20, who is named first to receive the nirūha?
optionExplain: Pitta is not named in verse 20.
Burning is not named in verse 20.
Right: कफरोगिताय: for one afflicted with Kapha disease.
Gulma is not named in verse 20.
questions.explain: The list of recipients opens with कफरोगिताय.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 20, line 1, to its meaning.
pairs: to one with slow digestive fire
to one with aversion to food
questions.explain: Line 1 is one sentence: give the nirūha to these three.
questions.rule: कफरोगिताय · मंदाग्नये · अशनविद्विषे = the three recipients; दद्यात् निरूहम् = should give the nirūha.

questions.q: Put these words of verse 20, line 1, in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The verb and object first, then the three recipients.
questions.teaches: Line 1 of verse 20 puts 'should give the nirūha' first and then names three recipients in the dative.

questions.q: Which is the right split of मंदाग्नये in verse 20?
optionExplain: ग्नये is no word; the word is अग्नये.
म् before a vowel stays: it would read मंदमग्नये.
-अः before अ becomes -ओऽ: it would read मंदोऽग्नये.
Right: अ + अ → आ: मंद + अग्नये = मंदाग्नये.
questions.explain: मंद (slow) + अग्नि (fire), dative मंदाग्नये: to one with slow fire.

questions.q: Which case do the three recipients in verse 20 take?
optionExplain: Right: -आय and -ए (कफरोगिताय, मंदाग्नये, अशनविद्विषे) are dative endings.
The genitive would be -अस्य or -एः.
The locative is used for conditions (verse 17), not recipients.
The subject is the giver; the recipients are not nominative.
questions.explain: With दद्यात् (should give), the receiver stands in the dative.

questions.q: Like मंदाग्नये, which invented form names the weak man (दुर्बल) as the one to whom a basti is given?
optionExplain: Genitive: 'of the weak man'.
Right: Dative singular -आय of an -अ stem (दुर्बल → दुर्बलाय).
Instrumental: 'by the weak man'.
Nominative: 'the weak man' as subject.
questions.explain: The receiver of दद्यात् stands in the dative: -आय for -अ stems, -अये for masculine -इ stems (मंदाग्नये).
questions.teaches: The one to whom something is given stands in the dative: -आय for -अ stems (दुर्बलाय), -अये for masculine -इ stems (मंदाग्नये).

questions.q: Which two treatments are named in verse 21, line 1?
optionExplain: Neither grinding nor straining is named in verse 21.
Neither boiling nor cooling is named in verse 21.
Right: क्षुण्णानि धौतानि: crushed, washed.
Neither frying nor soaking is named in verse 21.
questions.explain: क्षुण्ण = crushed (√क्षुद्); धौत = washed (√धाव्).
questions.section: पुनर्नवादि निरूह: सब दोषों के मेल में

questions.q: Match each word of verse 21 to its meaning as the card gives it.
questions.explain: Dvipañcamūla is 'two fives of roots', the daśamūla group.
questions.rule: द्विपंचमूल = ten roots; क्षुण्ण = crushed; धौत = washed; बिल्व = bael; कुलत्थ = horse gram.
questions.section: पुनर्नवादि निरूह: सब दोषों के मेल में

questions.q: Put these items of verse 21, line 2, in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Bilva, then the compound yava, aṅkola, kulattha, dhānya.
questions.teaches: Line 2 of verse 21 lists bilva, yava, aṅkola, kulattha and dhānya, then gives the prasṛta measure for the fruits.
questions.section: पुनर्नवादि निरूह: सब दोषों के मेल में

questions.q: In verse 21, which measure is given for the fruits?
optionExplain: The pala is the share in line 1 (पलांशकानि), not the fruits' measure.
No akṣa is named in verse 21.
No tulā is named in verse 21.
Right: फलानि च स्युः प्रसृतोन्मितानि: the fruits measured by prasṛtas.
questions.explain: Line 1 has पलांशकानि (a pala as share); line 2 measures the fruits by prasṛta.
questions.section: पुनर्नवादि निरूह: सब दोषों के मेल में

questions.q: Which is the right split of प्रसृतोन्मितानि in verse 21?
optionExplain: Right: अ + उ → ओ: प्रसृत + उन्मितानि = प्रसृतोन्मितानि.
न्मित is no word; the word is उन्मित, measured.
-अः before a vowel drops the visarga and does not join.
म् before a vowel stays: it would read प्रसृतमुन्मितानि.
questions.explain: प्रसृत (handful-measure) + उन्मितानि (measured).
questions.section: पुनर्नवादि निरूह: सब दोषों के मेल में

questions.q: Like क्षुण्णानि धौतानि फलानि, which invented phrase means washed leaves, with पत्राणि (neuter plural)?
optionExplain: -आः is masculine plural.
Right: Neuter plural noun, neuter plural participle -आनि, like धौतानि फलानि.
-एभ्यः is dative or ablative plural.
-अम् is singular.
questions.explain: A participle agrees with its noun: धौतानि फलानि, धौतानि पत्राणि.
questions.teaches: A participle used as an adjective agrees with a neuter plural noun in -आनि (क्षुण्णानि धौतानि फलानि; धौतानि पत्राणि).
questions.section: पुनर्नवादि निरूह: सब दोषों के मेल में

questions.q: How much water is the milk prepared with in verse 22?
optionExplain: No prasṛta is named in verse 22.
No pala is named in verse 22.
Right: जलद्व्याढकसाधितं: prepared with two āḍhakas of water.
No tulā is named in verse 22.
questions.explain: जल-द्वि-आढक-साधितम्: prepared with two āḍhakas of water.
questions.section: पुनर्नवादि निरूह: सब दोषों के मेल में

questions.q: Match each word of verse 22, line 1, to its meaning.
questions.explain: Line 1 describes preparing and straining the milk.
questions.rule: पयः = milk; जल = water; शुचि = clean; वस्त्र = cloth; पूत = strained.
questions.section: पुनर्नवादि निरूह: सब दोषों के मेल में

questions.q: Put these words of verse 22, line 1, in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Milk, prepared with two āḍhakas of water, that milk remaining, strained through clean cloth.
questions.teaches: Line 1 of verse 22 gives the steps in order: prepare with water, keep the milk, strain through a clean cloth.
questions.section: पुनर्नवादि निरूह: सब दोषों के मेल में

questions.q: Why is पयः in verse 22 read as milk, not water?
options: Because पयः can only mean milk
Because the next verse names cow milk
Because basti never uses plain water
Water (जल) is named apart, and क्षीर remains
optionExplain: पयस् can mean milk or water; the card says so.
No cow is named; the reason is in this line.
The card makes no such claim.
Right: जल is a separate word, and तत्क्षीरावशिष्टं says that milk remains.
questions.explain: Context decides: water is named as जल, and the remainder is क्षीर, milk.
questions.rule: पयस् = milk or water; context decides.
questions.section: पुनर्नवादि निरूह: सब दोषों के मेल में

questions.q: Which is the right split of जलद्व्याढक in verse 22?
optionExplain: Right: इ + आ → या: द्वि + आढक = द्व्याढक.
जलद् and व्याढक are not the words here.
द्वय + आढक would give द्वयाढक.
ढक is no word; the measure is आढक.
questions.explain: जल (water) + द्वि (two) + आढक (a measure).
questions.section: पुनर्नवादि निरूह: सब दोषों के मेल में

questions.q: Join invented त्रि + आढक, like द्वि + आढक → द्व्याढक. Which is right?
optionExplain: The इ does not stay; it becomes य्.
Right: इ before a different vowel becomes य्: त्रि + आढक = त्र्याढक.
The इ is not dropped; it becomes य्.
ए comes from अ + इ, not from इ + आ.
questions.explain: Same rule as द्वि + आढक → द्व्याढक.
questions.teaches: Final इ before a different vowel becomes य् (द्वि + आढक = द्व्याढक; त्रि + आढक = त्र्याढक).
questions.section: पुनर्नवादि निरूह: सब दोषों के मेल में

questions.q: In verse 23, how warm should the preparation be?
options: Hot, as it comes off the fire
Neither too hot nor too cold
optionExplain: The verse says 'not too hot'.
The verse says 'not too cold'.
Right: नात्युष्णशीतं: not too hot, not too cold.
No sun is named in verse 23.
questions.explain: न-अति-उष्ण-शीतम्: neither too hot nor too cold.
questions.section: पुनर्नवादि निरूह: सब दोषों के मेल में

questions.q: Match each word of verse 23 to its meaning as the card gives it.
questions.explain: Yavānī and madana are standard identifications in the data.
questions.rule: यवानी = ajwain; मदन = emetic nut; गुड = jaggery; सैंधव = rock salt; नव = fresh.
questions.section: पुनर्नवादि निरूह: सब दोषों के मेल में

questions.q: Put these phrases of verse 23 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Pastes and yavānī, madana, the temperature, jaggery and salt, the three liquids, the triad of prasṛtis.
questions.rule: कल्कैर्यवान्या · मदनैश्च युक्तं · नात्युष्णशीतं · गुडसैंधवाक्तं · क्षौद्रस्य… · युक्तं प्रसृतित्रयेण.
questions.teaches: Verse 23 adds pastes, sets the warmth, adds jaggery and rock salt, then honey, oil and fresh ghee by a triad of prasṛtis.
questions.section: पुनर्नवादि निरूह: सब दोषों के मेल में

questions.q: Of which three substances is the set of three prasṛtis in verse 23?
optionExplain: Jaggery and salt are 'smeared in' (आक्त), not measured by prasṛti.
Ajwain and madana go with the pastes.
Water is not named in verse 23.
Right: क्षौद्रस्य तैलस्य च सर्पिषश्च नवस्य: of honey, oil and fresh ghee.
questions.explain: The three genitives belong to प्रसृतित्रयेण.
questions.section: पुनर्नवादि निरूह: सब दोषों के मेल में

questions.q: Which is the right split of गुडसैंधवाक्तं in verse 23?
optionExplain: Right: अ + आ → आ: सैंधव + आक्तम् = सैंधवाक्तम्.
क्त is no word; the participle is आक्त, smeared.
-अः before a vowel drops the visarga and does not join.
म् before a vowel stays: it would read सैंधवमाक्तम्.
questions.explain: गुड (jaggery) + सैंधव (rock salt) + आक्त (smeared).
questions.section: पुनर्नवादि निरूह: सब दोषों के मेल में

questions.q: Like सर्पिषः … नवस्य 'of fresh ghee', which invented phrase means of fresh honey?
optionExplain: नवेन is instrumental; it does not agree with the genitive.
Right: The adjective takes the same genitive singular as its noun: नवस्य क्षौद्रस्य.
नवानाम् is genitive plural; क्षौद्रस्य is singular.
नवः is nominative; it does not agree.
questions.explain: An adjective agrees with its noun in case and number: नवस्य सर्पिषः, नवस्य क्षौद्रस्य.
questions.rule: Adjective agrees in case and number.
questions.teaches: An adjective agrees with its noun in case and number: नवस्य सर्पिषः 'of fresh ghee', नवस्य क्षौद्रस्य 'of fresh honey'.
questions.section: पुनर्नवादि निरूह: सब दोषों के मेल में

questions.q: In unit 24, who should give the nirūha?
optionExplain: The text names the विधिज्ञ, not any attendant.
No self-giving is stated.
Right: विधिज्ञः: knower of the rule.
-ज्ञ is joined to विधि, the rule, not to drugs.
questions.explain: दद्यान्निरूहं विधिना विधिज्ञः: the knower of the rule gives it by the rule.
questions.rule: विधिज्ञ = one who knows the rule.
questions.section: पुनर्नवादि निरूह: सब दोषों के मेल में

questions.q: Match each word of unit 24 to its meaning.
questions.explain: All five words stand in the unit's one line.
questions.rule: दद्यात् = should give; विधिना = by the rule; विधिज्ञः = knower of the rule; आमय = ailment; घ्न = destroying.
questions.section: पुनर्नवादि निरूह: सब दोषों के मेल में

questions.q: Put these words of unit 24 in the text's order.
questions.explain: Give the nirūha, by the rule, the knower of the rule, that (nirūha), destroyer of ailments.
questions.teaches: Unit 24 gives the verb and object (दद्यान्निरूहं), how (विधिना), who (विधिज्ञः) and what the nirūha does (…आमयघ्नं).
questions.section: पुनर्नवादि निरूह: सब दोषों के मेल में

questions.q: Which is the right split of दद्यान्निरूहं in unit 24?
optionExplain: दद्या and न्निरूह are not the words.
-आः before a voiced consonant would give दद्या निरूहम्.
दद्यम् is no form of √दा here; the optative is दद्यात्.
Right: त् before न becomes न्: दद्यात् + निरूहम् = दद्यान्निरूहम्.
questions.explain: दद्यात् (should give) + निरूहम् (the nirūha).
questions.section: पुनर्नवादि निरूह: सब दोषों के मेल में

questions.q: In unit 24, what does तं (that) refer to?
optionExplain: Right: तं is the nirūha prepared in lines 05.04.39-45.
The giver is विधिज्ञः, nominative; तं is accusative.
No patient is named in unit 24.
विधि is in the instrumental विधिना; तं is masculine accusative like निरूहम्.
questions.explain: तं (m. acc. sg.) agrees with निरूहम्, the object of दद्यात्.
questions.rule: A pronoun agrees with the noun it points to.
questions.section: पुनर्नवादि निरूह: सब दोषों के मेल में

questions.q: Like विधिज्ञः 'one who knows the rule' (nominative), which invented nominative means one who knows basti?
optionExplain: -घ्न means destroying, as in आमयघ्न, not knowing.
Right: -ज्ञ = knower; nominative -अः, like विधिज्ञः.
Instrumental: 'by the basti'.
-अम् is accusative; the giver is nominative.
questions.explain: X + ज्ञ = one who knows X: विधिज्ञः, बस्तिज्ञः.
questions.teaches: A compound ending in -ज्ञ means 'one who knows' (विधिज्ञः, बस्तिज्ञः); one ending in -घ्न means 'destroying' (आमयघ्न).
questions.section: पुनर्नवादि निरूह: सब दोषों के मेल में

questions.q: What does verse 25, line 1, say the bastis are declared to be?
optionExplain: Slimy is said later, in line 05.04.61, not in verse 25.
Scraping is said of triphalā juice in line 05.04.58.
Right: चित्रान्: varied, the name they declare (प्रचक्षते).
Nourishing is said in line 05.04.59, not here.
questions.explain: बस्तीन् … चित्रान् प्रचक्षते: they declare the bastis to be citra, varied.
questions.section: शोधन, ग्राही और लेखन बस्ति के द्रव्य

questions.q: Match each clear word of verse 25, line 1, to its meaning.
questions.explain: Line 1 is a full sentence: hence they declare the bastis (arranged half and half) to be varied.
questions.rule: बस्तीन् = bastis; अतः = hence; चित्रान् = varied; प्रचक्षते = they declare.
questions.section: शोधन, ग्राही और लेखन बस्ति के द्रव्य

questions.q: Put these clear words of verse 25, line 1, in the printed order.
questions.explain: Object, the particle hence, the predicate varied, and the verb last.
questions.teaches: Line 1 of verse 25 names the bastis (accusative), then अतः, the name चित्रान्, and ends with the verb प्रचक्षते.
questions.section: शोधन, ग्राही और लेखन बस्ति के द्रव्य

questions.q: Which split of बस्तीनतश्चित्रान् in verse 25 is right?
optionExplain: म् before च becomes anusvara or ञ्, never श्.
With आतः the print would read बस्तीनातश्…, with a long आ.
-आः before च gives -आश्, a long vowel: …ताश्चित्रान्.
Right: न् before a vowel joins it (बस्तीनतः); -अः before च becomes -अश् (अतश्चित्रान्).
questions.explain: बस्तीन् (bastis) + अतः (hence) + चित्रान् (varied).
questions.section: शोधन, ग्राही और लेखन बस्ति के द्रव्य

questions.q: A student says verse 25 tells which drug list goes with the citra bastis. What does the card say?
options: The text leaves the link unstated
Each one takes the kośātakī list
Each half is one of the drug lists
Only the nirūha takes this list
optionExplain: Right: The notes say plainly that no list is tied to a basti.
Not stated: the card ties no list to a basti.
The verse does not say what is halved.
Nirūha is not named in verse 25.
questions.explain: Verse 25 names the citra bastis and starts a list, but never links the two.
questions.rule: No list is assigned to a basti in the text.
questions.section: शोधन, ग्राही और लेखन बस्ति के द्रव्य

questions.q: Like अतः + चित्रान् → अतश्चित्रान्, how does invented ततः + चरेत् join?
optionExplain: -ओ arises only before voiced sounds; च is unvoiced.
Right: -अः before च becomes -अश्, as in अतश्चित्रान्.
र् comes from -इः/-उः before voiced sounds, not from -अः before च.
Before च the visarga becomes the palatal श्, not the dental स्.
questions.explain: The visarga takes the place of the following consonant: palatal च → श्.
questions.teaches: A visarga before च/छ becomes श् (अतः + चित्रान् → अतश्चित्रान्; ततः + चरेत् → ततश्चरेत्).
questions.section: शोधन, ग्राही और लेखन बस्ति के द्रव्य

questions.q: Which part of śyāmā and trivṛt does verse 26 name?
optionExplain: No flower is named in verse 26.
No bark is named in verse 26.
Right: श्यामात्रिवृतोर्मूलं: the root of śyāmā and trivṛt.
No leaf is named in verse 26.
questions.explain: श्यामा-त्रिवृतोः (of the two) + मूलम् (root).

Plural: three or more.

questions.explain: Adjective and noun agree in the dual: a-stems take -औ (शीतौ), i/u-stems lengthen (बस्ती, मृदू).
questions.teaches: In the masculine nominative dual a-stems end in -औ (शीतौ), i-stems in -ई (बस्ती), u-stems in -ऊ (मृदू).

questions.q: What does शोणित mean in verse 40?
optionExplain: Milk is क्षीर, in line 1.
Flesh (मांस) is not named in verse 40.
Right: शोणित = blood; the line lists the animals whose blood is meant.
Fat (वसा) is not named in verse 40.
questions.explain: …शोणितैः: with the bloods (of hare and the rest).

questions.q: Match each clear word of verse 40 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words are clear in the print; the doubtful ones are left out.
questions.rule: अजा = goat; महिषी = she-buffalo; शश = hare; मार्जार = cat; जीवनीय = life-promoting.

questions.q: Put these clear animals of verse 40, line 2, in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Hare and antelope open the compound; cat and she-buffalo follow (the doubtful दक्ष stands between).
questions.teaches: The blood list of verse 40 runs hare, antelope, (a doubtful name), cat, she-buffalo, and an unclear last member.

questions.q: Which split of शशैण in verse 40 is right?
optionExplain: अ + इ gives ए: it would read शशेण.
-अः before a vowel loses the visarga and does not merge: शश एण.
ए + अ gives ए with an avagraha: शशेऽण.
Right: अ + ए → ऐ: शश + एण = शशैण.
questions.explain: शश (hare) + एण (antelope).

questions.q: What are the milks of verse 40 also joined with?
optionExplain: Right: जीवनीययुतैः: joined with the jīvanīya (life-promoting) ones.
Honey and sugar go with the bastis of verse 39.
Ghee and añjana are in verse 39.
Mustard paste is in line 05.04.87.
questions.explain: Line 1 ends: जीवनीययुतैरपि, also joined with life-promoting drugs.

questions.q: Like the instrumental …शोणितैः (with bloods), which invented word means with the blood of a hare?
optionExplain: Nominative or accusative, not with.
Right: A tat-puruṣa शश-शोणित with the instrumental singular -एन.
Genitive: of the hare's blood.
Locative: in the hare's blood.
questions.explain: With = instrumental; a neuter a-stem takes -एन in the singular, -ऐः in the plural.
questions.teaches: Neuter a-stems in the instrumental take -एन (singular) and -ऐः (plural): शोणितैः, शशशोणितेन.

questions.q: In verse 41, where is the basti said to be recommended (प्रशस्यते)?
optionExplain: Ānāha is named in line 05.04.95.
Atiyoga was named in line 05.04.71.
Right: बस्तिर्जीवादाने प्रशस्यते: in jīvādāna the basti is recommended.
Mūtrakṛcchra is named in line 05.04.95.
questions.explain: Line 1 closes the jīvādāna recipe of lines 05.04.77-78.

questions.q: Match each clear word of verse 41 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The first three close the jīvādāna recipe; the last two open the new topic.
questions.rule: सद्यस्क = fresh; मृदित = crushed; प्रशस्यते = is recommended; सुकुमार = delicate; मृदु = mild.

questions.q: Put these words of verse 41, line 1, in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Two adjectives, the subject, the condition, and the verb last.
questions.teaches: Line 1 of verse 41 reads: with fresh, crushed (ones), the basti in jīvādāna is recommended.

questions.q: Which split of अथेमान् in verse 41 is right?
optionExplain: अ + ए gives ऐ: it would read अथैमान्.
-अः before a vowel loses the visarga and does not merge: अथ इमान्.
ओ before इ becomes अव्: it would read अथविमान्.
Right: अ + इ → ए: अथ + इमान् = अथेमान्.
questions.explain: अथ (now) + इमान् (these, accusative plural).

questions.q: For whom are the mild nirūhas announced in verse 41?
optionExplain: Right: सुकुमाराणाम्: of the delicate, the mild nirūhas.
They are named in line 05.04.96 and get a sharp basti.
Mūtrakṛcchra is named in line 05.04.95.
They are named in line 05.04.97.
questions.explain: अथ इमान् सुकुमाराणां निरूहान् … मृदून्: these mild nirūhas of the delicate.

questions.q: Like सद्यस्कैः + मृदितैः → सद्यस्कैर्मृदितैः, how does invented शीतैः + मधुरैः join?
optionExplain: The visarga after ऐ is not dropped; it becomes र् before voiced म.
Right: -ऐः before a voiced sound becomes -ऐर्, as in सद्यस्कैर्मृदितैः.
स् appears before त/थ, not before म.
-ओ comes from -अः, not from -ऐः.
questions.explain: A visarga after a vowel other than अ/आ becomes र् before a voiced sound.
questions.teaches: A visarga after ऐ (not अ/आ) becomes र् before a voiced sound: सद्यस्कैः + मृदितैः → सद्यस्कैर्मृदितैः; शीतैः + मधुरैः → शीतैर्मधुरैः.

questions.q: By what measure will the author state the bastis in verse 42?
optionExplain: Pala is not the measure named in verse 42.
Añjali is not named in verse 42.
Right: प्रसृतैः पृथक्: by prasṛtas, separately.
Kuḍava is not named in verse 42.
questions.explain: वक्ष्यामि प्रसृतैः पृथक्: I shall state by prasṛtas, separately.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 42, line 1, to its meaning.
questions.explain: Line 1 is clear; line 2 has two conjectural readings.
questions.rule: कर्मणा = by the action; विप्लुत = harmed; वक्ष्यामि = I shall state; पृथक् = separately; प्रसृत = palmful.

questions.q: Put these words of verse 42, line 1, in the verse's order.
questions.explain: For whom, the verb, then the measure and the manner.
questions.rule: कर्मणा · विप्लुतानां च · वक्ष्यामि · प्रसृतैः · पृथक्.
questions.teaches: Line 1 of verse 42: and of those harmed by the action, I shall state by prasṛtas, separately.

questions.q: What does the form वक्ष्यामि in verse 42 show?
options: Optative, third person: one should state
Future, first person: I shall state
optionExplain: The present of √वच् is वच्मि; -ष्यामि marks the future.
-ष्यामि marks the future, not the optative.
The past would be उवाच; -ष्यामि is the future.
Right: The data's label: future, 1st singular of √वच्.
questions.explain: वक्ष्यामि: the author promises what follows.

questions.q: Whom does verse 42 add to the delicate of line 05.04.80?
optionExplain: Right: कर्मणा विप्लुतानां च: and of those harmed by the action.
They are named in line 05.04.97.
Jīvādāna closed in line 05.04.79.
Ānāha is named in line 05.04.95.
questions.explain: च adds a second group to the delicate: those harmed by karman.

questions.q: Like वक्ष्यामि (I shall state), which invented form means I shall give, from √दा?
optionExplain: Present: I give.
Right: Future 1st singular: दा + स्यामि.
Optative: I would give.
Absolutive: having given.
questions.explain: The future adds -स्य- (-ष्य- after some sounds) and the person ending -आमि.
questions.teaches: The future 1st singular ends in -स्यामि or -ष्यामि: वक्ष्यामि (I shall state), दास्यामि (I shall give).

questions.q: With what is the basti churned in verse 43?
options: A pestle and a stone mortar
optionExplain: No pestle or mortar is named in verse 43.
No hand is named; खजेन is the instrument.
Right: खजेन मथितः: churned with the khaja.
No ladle is named in verse 43.
questions.explain: खज = churning stick; the instrumental खजेन names the tool.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 43 to its meaning as the card gives it.
questions.explain: Line 1 gives the tool and the effects; line 2 the new items.
questions.rule: खज = churning stick; वातघ्न = Vāta-destroying; बलवर्णकृत् = strength- and colour-making; प्रसन्ना = clear liquor (probable); क्षौद्र = honey.

questions.q: Put the four one-prasṛta items of verse 43, line 2, in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The genitive compound runs oil, prasannā, honey, ghee.
questions.teaches: Line 2 of verse 43: one prasṛta each of taila, prasannā, kṣaudra and sarpis (oil, clear liquor, honey, ghee).

questions.q: Which rule turns मथितः into मथितो before बस्तिः in verse 43?
options: The visarga drops and अ grows long
optionExplain: Before unvoiced sounds it becomes श्/ष्/स् or stays: अश्च, अस्त.
-इः before a voiced sound becomes -इर्, as in बस्तिर्वातघ्नो.
That is not a sandhi rule; -आः loses the visarga, -अः gives -ओ.
Right: ब is voiced, so मथितः + बस्तिः → मथितो बस्तिः.
questions.explain: The same rule gives वातघ्नो before बल.

questions.q: Which does verse 43 say the khaja-churned basti does?
optionExplain: Right: बल- in बलवर्णकृत्.
Right: वातघ्नः.
Right: वर्ण- in बलवर्णकृत्.
Worms are named in lines 05.04.88 and 05.04.91, not here.
Kapha is not named in verse 43.
questions.explain: वातघ्नो बलवर्णकृत्: Vāta-destroying, strength- and colour-making.
questions.rule: Effects of verse 43: वात-नाश, बल, वर्ण.

questions.q: Like एक + एकः → एकैकः (one each), how does invented तत्र + एव join?
optionExplain: Right: अ + ए → ऐ, as in एकैकः.
ए would come from अ + इ, not अ + ए.
ओ comes from अ + उ.
अय् comes from ए before a vowel, not from अ.
questions.explain: अ/आ + ए/ऐ → ऐ.
questions.teaches: अ or आ before ए or ऐ gives ऐ: एक + एकः → एकैकः; तत्र + एव → तत्रैव.

questions.q: What does verse 44 say the basti with bilva roots and kaulattha conquers?
optionExplain: Kapha is not named in verse 44.
Right: स वातजित्: that (basti) conquers Vāta.
Pitta is not named in verse 44.
Worms are named in line 05.04.88, not here.
questions.explain: वातजित् = Vāta-conquering.

questions.q: Match each clear word of verse 44 to its meaning as the card gives it.
questions.explain: Bilva, kaulattha, paṭola and nimba are standard identifications.
questions.rule: बिल्व = bael; कौलत्थ = horse gram; पटोल = pointed gourd; निम्ब = neem; अम्भस् = water.

questions.q: Put these drugs of verse 44, line 2, in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The compound runs paṭola, nimba, bhūtīka, rāsnā; the fifth name follows in the next token.
questions.teaches: Line 2 of verse 44 names paṭola (pointed gourd), nimba (neem), bhūtīka and rāsnā, then a fifth drug, and their water.

questions.q: In स वातजित् of verse 44, why does सः lose its visarga?
options: It is a print slip for सो
सः drops it before a consonant
स is a stem, not a pronoun
optionExplain: Other -अः words become -ओ before voiced sounds: मथितो बस्तिः (line 05.04.83).
No flag is raised; स before a consonant is regular.
Right: The pronoun सः (and एषः) drops the visarga before any consonant: स वातजित्.
स here is the pronoun that (basti), masculine nominative.
questions.explain: सः + वातजित् → स वातजित्.

questions.q: Of what preparation of paṭola and the rest does verse 44 speak?
optionExplain: No decoction is named for paṭola and the rest; the text says ambhas, water.
No paste is named for them in verse 44.
No juice is named in verse 44.
Right: …अम्भसः: of the water; the notes say the text says water, not decoction.
questions.explain: The text says ambhas, water; nothing is added.

questions.q: Like बिल्व + आदि → बिल्वादि, how does invented पटोल + आदि join?
optionExplain: Right: अ + आ → आ, as in बिल्वादि.
ए would come from अ + इ.
औ would come from अ + ओ/औ.
य् comes from इ/ई before a vowel.
questions.explain: Like vowels merge into the long vowel: अ + आ → आ.
questions.teaches: अ or आ before अ or आ merges into आ: बिल्व + आदि → बिल्वादि; पटोल + आदि → पटोलादि.

questions.q: A paste of which drug does the basti of verse 45 have?
optionExplain: Pippalī paste is in line 05.04.91.
Right: सर्षपकल्कवान्: having a paste of mustard.
Liquorice is not named in verse 45.
Uśīra is in line 05.04.74.
questions.explain: सर्षप-कल्क-वान्: having (-वान्) a paste (कल्क) of mustard (सर्षप).

questions.q: Match each word of verse 45 to its meaning as the card gives it.
questions.explain: Four disorders destroyed and the drug of the paste.
questions.rule: अभिष्यन्द = oozing; कृमि = worms; कुष्ठ = skin disease; प्रमेह = urinary disorders; सर्षप = mustard.

questions.q: Put the disorders that the basti of verse 45 destroys in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The compound runs abhiṣyanda, kṛmi, kuṣṭha, prameha, then -हा (destroyer).
questions.teaches: Verse 45 ends: (the basti) destroying abhiṣyanda, kṛmi (worms), kuṣṭha (skin disease) and prameha (urinary disorders).

questions.q: Which split of पृथगाज्याच्च in verse 45 is right?
optionExplain: म् before च gives anusvara: आज्यं च.
-अः before च gives -अश्: आज्यश्च.
Right: क् before a vowel becomes ग्; त् before च becomes च्.
ए does not change before च: आज्ये च.
questions.explain: पृथक् (separately) + आज्यात् (from ghee) + च (and).
questions.rule: क् + vowel → ग्; त् + च → च्च.

questions.q: Besides the waters, from what does verse 45 take one prasṛta?
optionExplain: Oil is in line 05.04.84, not in verse 45.
Milk is not named in verse 45.
Honey is not named in verse 45.
Right: पृथगाज्याच्च: and (one) from ghee.
questions.explain: प्रसृतः पृथगाज्याच्च: a prasṛta separately, and (one) from ghee.

questions.q: Like सर्षपकल्कवान् (having mustard paste), which invented word says a basti has a paste of pippalī?
optionExplain: Right: -वान् (masc. nom. sg.) = having; basti is masculine.
Feminine; in this verse basti is masculine (सर्षपकल्कवान्, सपञ्चतिक्तः).
Plural; one basti is meant.
Only the paste itself, not having a paste.
questions.explain: The suffix -वत् (nom. sg. m. -वान्) means having.
questions.teaches: -वत् (masculine nominative singular -वान्) makes a having-word: सर्षपकल्कवान्, पिप्पलीकल्कवान् बस्तिः.

questions.q: What does कषायाः mean in verse 46?
optionExplain: Kaṣāya as taste is not meant: the notes say preparation.
Right: Here kaṣāya is the preparation, decoction, measured in prasṛtas.
Paste is कल्क, not कषाय.
Powder (चूर्ण) is not named in verse 46.
questions.explain: कषायाः प्रसृताः पञ्च: five prasṛtas of decoctions.

questions.q: Match each clear drug of verse 46 to its identification as the card gives it.
questions.explain: All four are standard identifications.
questions.rule: विडङ्ग = false black pepper; त्रिफला = the three fruits; शिग्रुफल = drumstick fruit; मुस्ता = nutgrass.

questions.q: Put these drugs of verse 46 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The compound runs viḍaṅga, triphalā, śigru fruit, mustā; a fifth (conjectural) name ends it.
questions.teaches: Line 1 of verse 46 lists viḍaṅga, triphalā, the fruit of śigru, mustā and a fifth drug, whose decoctions are used.

questions.q: What does the form विमथ्य in verse 46 show?
optionExplain: The participle is मथित (line 05.04.83), not विमथ्य.
An optative would end in -एत्/-ईयात्.
Right: With the prefix वि- the absolutive takes -य, not -त्वा.
A future would have -स्य-/-ष्य-.
questions.explain: विमथ्य तान्: having churned them.

questions.q: What is done to the decoctions and oil in verse 46?
options: They are boiled down by half
optionExplain: No boiling down is said in verse 46.
No cooling or straining is said.
No fermenting is said in verse 46.
Right: विमथ्य तान्: having churned them.
questions.explain: Five prasṛtas of decoction and one of oil are churned.

questions.q: Like वि + √मथ् → विमथ्य, which invented absolutive means having joined, from सम् + √युज्?
optionExplain: Right: Prefix + root: the absolutive ends in -य.
-त्वा is used without a prefix; with सम्- it is -य.
Past participle: joined, not having joined.
Infinitive: to join.
questions.explain: With a prefix the absolutive takes -य; without, -त्वा.
questions.teaches: With a prefix the absolutive ends in -य (विमथ्य, संयुज्य); without one it ends in -त्वा (कृत्वा).

questions.q: What does the nirūha of verse 47 destroy?
optionExplain: Burning is not named in verse 47.
Right: निरूहः कृमिहा: the nirūha destroying worms.
Vāta-conquering was the basti of line 05.04.85.
Ānāha is named in line 05.04.95.
questions.explain: कृमि-हा: worm-destroying.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 47 to its meaning as the card gives it.
questions.explain: Pippalī, ikṣu and vidārī are standard identifications.
questions.rule: पिप्पली = long pepper; इक्षु = sugarcane; विदारी = Indian kudzu; कल्क = paste; क्षौद्र = honey.

questions.q: Put these items of verse 47, line 2, in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The compound runs payasyā, ikṣu, sthirā, rāsnā, vidārī, honey (and ghee last).
questions.rule: पयस्या · इक्षु · स्थिरा · रास्ना · विदारी · क्षौद्र.
questions.teaches: Line 2 of verse 47 lists payasyā, ikṣu, sthirā, rāsnā, vidārī, kṣaudra (honey) and sarpis (ghee).

questions.q: Which split of पयस्येक्षु in verse 47 is right?
optionExplain: ए before इ becomes अय् or stays apart: पयस्य इक्षु.
अ + ऐ gives ऐ: it would read पयस्यैक्षु.
Right: आ + इ → ए: पयस्या + इक्षु = पयस्येक्षु.
इ + इ gives ई: it would read पयसीक्षु.
questions.explain: पयस्या (a disputed drug) + इक्षु (sugarcane).

questions.q: Which two drugs make the paste of the nirūha in verse 47?
optionExplain: Mustard paste and the five bitters go with the basti of lines 05.04.87-88.
Honey and ghee are in the new list of line 2.
These gave decoctions in line 05.04.89.
Right: वेल्लपिप्पलीकल्कयोजितः: joined with a paste of vella and pippalī.
questions.explain: The paste of verse 47: vella (disputed) and pippalī (long pepper).

questions.q: Like कृमि + हन् → कृमिहा (worm-destroying), which invented word means Kapha-destroying in the same form?
optionExplain: Right: Compounds in -हन् take the nominative singular -हा.
-हः is not the nominative of -हन्.
That is the bare stem, not the nominative.
-हम् is not a form of -हन्.
questions.explain: X-हन् (destroying X) gives the masculine nominative singular X-हा.
questions.teaches: Words in -हन् (destroying) have the masculine nominative singular -हा: कृमिहा, कफहा, प्रमेहहा.

questions.q: What does the basti of verse 48 make, by the card?
optionExplain: Strength and colour were said in line 05.04.83.
Right: वृषत्वकृत्: making virility.
Sharpness is the topic of line 05.04.98.
Mildness is the topic of line 05.04.99.
questions.explain: वृषत्व-कृत्: virility-making.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 48 to its meaning as the card gives it.
questions.explain: These words are clear; the paste word is left out.
questions.rule: एकैकः = one each; वृषत्वकृत् = virility-making; गोमूत्र = cow's urine; दधिमण्ड = curd water; काञ्जिक = fermented gruel.

questions.q: Put the items of verse 48, line 2, in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The compound runs oil, cow's urine, dadhimaṇḍa, sour kāñjika.
questions.teaches: Line 2 of verse 48: four, from oil, cow's urine, dadhimaṇḍa (curd water) and sour kāñjika (fermented gruel).

questions.q: Which split of चत्वारस्तैल in verse 48 is right?
optionExplain: A long आ would show in the print: चत्वारास्तैल.
The neuter would read चत्वारि तैल-; no स् appears.
Right: -अः before त becomes -अस्: चत्वारस्तैल.
स्तैल is no word; the स् comes from the visarga.
questions.explain: चत्वारः (four, masc. nom.) + तैल- (oil).

questions.q: Which of these is NOT in the list of verse 48, line 2?
optionExplain: Oil opens the list.
Gomūtra is the second item.
Dadhimaṇḍa is the third item.
Right: Honey is in line 05.04.92, not in the list of four.
questions.explain: The four: oil, cow's urine, curd water, sour kāñjika.
questions.rule: Line 2 of verse 48: तैल, गोमूत्र, दधिमण्ड, अम्लकाञ्जिक.

questions.q: Like वृषत्वकृत् (virility-making), which invented word means strength-making?
optionExplain: Right: -कृत् at the end of a compound means making.
Past participle: made by strength.
Absolutive: having made strength, not making.
Infinitive: to make strength.
questions.explain: X-कृत् = X-making (an agent noun at the end of a compound).
questions.teaches: -कृत् at the end of a compound makes an agent word: वृषत्वकृत् (virility-making), बलकृत् (strength-making).

questions.q: Which basti does verse 49 desire for one dulled by mild bastis?
optionExplain: Oily, sweet, cool is for one depleted by sharp ones (line 05.04.97).
Right: तीक्ष्णोऽन्यो बस्तिरिष्यते: another, sharp basti is desired.
Mild bastis are what dulled him.
Verse 49 desires another basti.
questions.explain: मृदुबस्तिजडीभूते तीक्ष्णः: dulled by mild ones, give a sharp one.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 49 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Two conditions for the slightly warm basti; one for the sharp one.
questions.rule: कवोष्ण = slightly warm; आनाह = distension; मूत्रकृच्छ्र = painful urination; जडीभूत = dulled; तीक्ष्ण = sharp.

questions.q: Put these phrases of verse 49 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The warm basti and its two conditions; then the dulled patient and the sharp basti.
questions.rule: बस्तिः कवोष्णः · सानाहे · मूत्रकृच्छ्रे परो मतः · मृदुबस्तिजडीभूते · तीक्ष्णो ऽन्यो बस्तिरिष्यते.
questions.teaches: Verse 49: slightly warm basti, in ānāha and mūtrakṛcchra, held best; in one dulled by mild bastis, another, sharp basti.

questions.q: Which split of बस्तिरिष्यते in verse 49 is right?
optionExplain: र् + ए would read बस्तिरेष्यते.
ई + इ merges into ई: बस्तीष्यते.
Right: -इः before a vowel becomes -इर्: बस्तिरिष्यते.
म् before a vowel stays: बस्तिमिष्यते.
questions.explain: बस्तिः (basti) + इष्यते (is desired).

questions.q: A patient has ānāha. Which basti does verse 49 hold best?
optionExplain: The sharp basti is for one dulled by mild bastis.
Cool with honey and sugar is the jīvādāna basti of line 05.04.76.
Oily and mild is for one depleted by sharp bastis (line 05.04.97).
Right: बस्तिः कवोष्णः सानाहे … परो मतः.
questions.explain: Ānāha and mūtrakṛcchra: kavoṣṇa, slightly warm.

questions.q: Like परः + मतः → परो मतः, how does invented हितः + मतः join?
optionExplain: Right: -अः before a voiced sound becomes -ओ, as in परो मतः.
र् comes from -इः/-उः, not from -अः.
स् appears before त/थ, not before म.
Dropping to -आ happens with -आः, not -अः.
questions.explain: म is voiced, so -अः → -ओ.
questions.teaches: -अः before a voiced consonant becomes -ओ: परः + मतः → परो मतः; हितः + मतः → हितो मतः.

questions.q: What does तीक्ष्णत्वम् mean in verse 50?
optionExplain: Mildness is मार्दव, line 05.04.99.
Right: तीक्ष्ण (sharp) + -त्व (the quality): sharpness.
Oiliness would be स्निग्धता or स्नेह.
Coolness would be शैत्य; शिशिर is the adjective cool.
questions.explain: तीक्ष्णत्वं मूत्र…सर्षपैः: sharpness by urine and the rest.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 50, line 1, to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four qualities of the basti for one depleted by sharp ones.
questions.rule: स्निग्ध = oily; मधुर = sweet; शिशिर = cool; मृदु = mild; विकर्षित = drawn out.

questions.q: Put the sharpness drugs of verse 50 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The compound runs urine, bilva, agni, salt, kṣāra, mustard.
questions.rule: मूत्र · बिल्व · अग्नि · लवण · क्षार · सर्षप.
questions.teaches: Line 2 of verse 50: sharpness by mūtra (urine), bilva (bael), agni, lavaṇa (salt), kṣāra and sarṣapa (mustard).

questions.q: Which of these is NOT among the sharpness drugs of verse 50?
optionExplain: Lavaṇa is the fourth sharpness item.
Kṣāra is the fifth sharpness item.
Right: Milk gives mildness, in line 05.04.99.
Sarṣapa closes the list.
questions.explain: The six: urine, bilva, agni, salt, kṣāra, mustard.
questions.rule: Sharpness: मूत्र, बिल्व, अग्नि, लवण, क्षार, सर्षप.

questions.q: A patient was drawn out by sharp bastis. Which basti suits him, by verse 50?
optionExplain: Sharp is what depleted him.
Salt and kṣāra give sharpness.
Mustard gives sharpness; bitter is not named.
Right: तीक्ष्णैर्विकर्षिते स्निग्धो मधुरः शिशिरो मृदुः.
questions.explain: Depleted by sharp → oily, sweet, cool, mild.
questions.rule: Depleted by sharp → the opposite qualities.

questions.q: Like तीक्ष्ण → तीक्ष्णत्वम् (sharpness), which invented -त्व word means mildness?
optionExplain: Right: -त्व nouns are neuter: nominative singular -त्वम्.
-त्व nouns are neuter, not masculine.
-त्वा is the absolutive ending, not the quality suffix.
Locative: in mildness, not the nominative.
questions.explain: Adjective + -त्व = the quality, neuter: तीक्ष्णत्वम्, मृदुत्वम्.
questions.teaches: Adding -त्व to an adjective makes a neuter noun of the quality: तीक्ष्ण → तीक्ष्णत्वम् (sharpness), मृदु → मृदुत्वम् (mildness).

questions.q: By what does unit 51 say mildness is produced?
optionExplain: These give sharpness, line 05.04.98.
Right: क्षीराज्याद्यैः: by milk, ghee and the rest.
These give sharpness, line 05.04.98.
These give sharpness, line 05.04.98.
questions.explain: मार्दवं … क्षीराज्याद्यैः: mildness by milk, ghee and so on.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 51 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The unit is one short sentence.
questions.rule: मार्दव = mildness; विधातव्य = to be produced; प्राप्तकालम् = in due time; तु = but; आज्य = ghee.

questions.q: Put the words of unit 51 in the printed order.
questions.explain: Time, the gerundive, the means with तु, and the subject last.
questions.teaches: Unit 51 reads: in due time is to be produced, by milk, ghee and the rest, but, mildness.

questions.q: Which split of क्षीराज्याद्यैस्तु in unit 51 is right?
optionExplain: -अः before त gives -अस्: आद्यस्तु, with no ऐ.
ए does not change before त: आद्ये तु.
Right: -ऐः before त becomes -ऐस्: आद्यैस्तु.
म् before त gives anusvara: आद्यं तु.
questions.explain: क्षीर (milk) + आज्य (ghee) + आद्यैः (and the rest, instr. pl.) + तु (but).

questions.q: In unit 51, what does तु set mildness against?
options: The basti of the delicate one
optionExplain: Jīvādāna closed at line 05.04.79.
The nirūha of line 05.04.91 is not contrasted here.
The delicate are named in line 05.04.80, not contrasted here.
Right: The notes: tu contrasts mildness with sharpness by urine and the rest.
questions.explain: Sharpness by urine and so on; but mildness by milk, ghee and so on.

questions.q: Like वि + √धा → विधातव्यम् (to be produced), which invented gerundive means to be done, from √कृ?
optionExplain: Right: -तव्य is the gerundive: to be done.
Absolutive: having done.
Past participle: done.
Present: he does.
questions.explain: -तव्य added to the root (with guṇa) gives to be X-ed.
questions.teaches: The suffix -तव्य makes a gerundive, to be X-ed: विधातव्यम् (to be produced), कर्तव्यम् (to be done).

questions.q: What does सात्म्य mean in unit 52?
optionExplain: Strength is बल, the first member of the list.
Right: सात्म्य = what is agreeable or suitable by habit.
Region is देश, the third member.
No heat of drugs is named in unit 52.
questions.explain: The fourth member, सात्म्य, is what suits a person by habit.

questions.q: Match each factor of unit 52 to its meaning as the card gives it.
questions.explain: One dvandva compound names the five factors to be distinguished.
questions.rule: बल = strength; काल = time/season; देश = region; सात्म्य = what suits by habit; प्रकृति = constitution.

questions.q: Put the five factors of unit 52 in the text's order.
questions.explain: बल-काल-देश-सात्म्य-प्रकृतीः: strength, time, region, habit-suitability, constitutions.
questions.teaches: Unit 52: a basti is applied after distinguishing strength, time, region, sātmya and constitutions, in that order.

questions.q: Which noun of unit 52 is the subject of the sentence that continues into line 05.04.101?
optionExplain: प्रकृतीः is the end of the accusative dvandva: what is distinguished.
बल is only the first member of the accusative compound.
Right: बस्तिः is masculine nominative singular: the basti that, once applied, removes the diseases.
देश is a member inside the same accusative compound.
questions.explain: The five factors are the object of प्रविभज्य; the basti is the subject.
questions.rule: Subject = बस्तिः (nom.); object of distinguishing = the five factors (acc.).

questions.q: A physician gives every patient the same basti without asking about habit or season. What does unit 52 require instead?
options: First find which disease the patient's family has had
First give the patient a day's fast before any basti
First check the season alone and ignore the rest
First distinguish strength, time, region, habit-suitability, constitution
optionExplain: Family history is not in unit 52.
No fast is named in unit 52.
Season is one of five; all five are to be distinguished.
Right: This is the unit's own list of what must be distinguished.
questions.explain: प्रविभज्य: the basti is applied after the five factors are told apart.
questions.rule: Apply a basti after weighing bala, kāla, deśa, sātmya, prakṛti.

questions.q: प्र-वि + √भज् gives प्रविभज्य, having distinguished. Which is the absolutive of invented सम् + √युज्, having joined?
optionExplain: Right: With a prefix the absolutive takes -य: सम् + युज् + य = संयुज्य.
-त्वा is used without a prefix; with सम् the ending is -य.
That is a past participle (joined), like योजितः, not an absolutive.
That is a present verb (he joins), not an absolutive.
questions.explain: Prefixed root + -य = absolutive (प्रविभज्य, संयुज्य).
questions.teaches: An absolutive of a prefixed root ends in -य (प्रविभज्य; invented संयुज्य), not -त्वा.

questions.q: For those afflicted by heat, which bastis does verse 53 name?
optionExplain: Pleasantly warm ones are for those afflicted by cold.
Right: उष्णार्तानां शीतान्: for the heat-afflicted, cool ones.
Sharp bastis are not named in verse 53.
Oily bastis are not named in verse 53.
questions.explain: Line 2 pairs heat with cool and cold with pleasantly warm.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 53 to its meaning as the card gives it.
questions.explain: Line 1 gives how diseases are removed; line 2 the heat and cold pair.
questions.rule: औषधवर्ग = drug-group; निवर्तयति = causes to turn back; उष्णार्त = heat-afflicted; शीतार्त = cold-afflicted; सुखोष्ण = pleasantly warm.

questions.q: Put these phrases of verse 53 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: By their own drug groups, their own diseases, it turns back; for heat, cool; for cold, pleasantly warm.
questions.rule: स्वैः स्वैः औषधवर्गैः · स्वान् स्वान् रोगान् · निवर्तयति · उष्णार्तानां शीतान् · शीतार्तानां सुखोष्णान्.
questions.teaches: Verse 53: each disease is turned back by its own drug group; cool bastis for the heat-afflicted, pleasantly warm for the cold-afflicted.

questions.q: Which split of शीतांश्छीतार्त्तानां in verse 53 is right?
optionExplain: म् before श gives only anusvara: शीतं शीतार्तानाम्, with no छ.
A visarga before श gives शीताः शीत- or शीताश्शीत-, with no anusvara.
Right: Final न् before श is printed here as ंश् and the श after it as छ (standard spelling शीताञ्छीत-): शीतान् + शीतार्तानाम्.
छीतार्त is no word; the छ comes from श by sandhi.
questions.explain: शीतान् (cool ones) + शीतार्तानाम् (for those afflicted by cold).

questions.q: A physician uses one fixed drug mixture in the basti for every disease. Which teaching of verse 53 does he ignore?
options: Every basti must be given cool to all
A basti must never contain any drugs
Only diseases of heat may get bastis
Each disease is turned back by its own drug group
optionExplain: Cool is only for the heat-afflicted; the cold-afflicted get warm.
Verse 53 names drug groups in the basti.
Verse 53 gives bastis for heat and for cold alike.
Right: स्वैः स्वैरौषधवर्गैः स्वान् स्वान् रोगान्: each by its own group.
questions.explain: The repetition स्वैः स्वैः … स्वान् स्वान् matches each disease to its own drugs.
questions.rule: Own drug group for own disease.

questions.q: Verse 53 repeats स्वैः स्वैः for each one's own. What does invented गृहे गृहे mean?
options: In a house within a house
optionExplain: Right: A repeated word gives the sense each or every: गृहे गृहे = in house after house.
Two houses would be the dual गृहयोः.
Large would need a word like महति; repetition does not mean size.
Repetition gives distribution, not one inside another.
questions.explain: Repeating a word distributes it: each, every, respective (स्वैः स्वैः, स्वान् स्वान्).
questions.teaches: A word said twice gives the sense each or respective (स्वैः स्वैः; invented गृहे गृहे = in every house).

questions.q: What does युञ्जीत (printed युंजीत) mean in verse 54?
optionExplain: A past form would be different; the gram label says optative.
Right: Optative 3rd singular middle of √युज्: one should apply.
That would be a future passive, not an optative.
That would be a present participle, not a finite verb.
questions.explain: युञ्जीत governs the bastis of line 1.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 54 line 1, and one of line 2, to its meaning.
questions.explain: Line 1: bastis joined with drugs suitable to that; line 2: in diseases.
questions.rule: तद् = that; योग्य = suitable; औषध = drugs; युक्त = joined with; व्याधिषु = in diseases.

questions.q: Put the members of the compound तद्योग्यौषधयुक्तान् in their order.
questions.explain: तद्-योग्य-औषध-युक्तान्: joined with drugs suitable to that.
questions.teaches: Verse 54 line 1: bastis joined with drugs suitable to that (heat or cold) are to be applied.

questions.q: Which split of बस्तीञ्च in verse 54 is right?
optionExplain: A visarga before च becomes श्: it would give बस्तीश्च.
ञ्च is no word; the ञ् comes from न् by sandhi.
Right: बस्तीन् + च: the print writes the न् as ञ् before च (the standard sandhi gives बस्तींश्च, as in सुखोष्णांश्च of line 05.04.102).
बस्तिम् has a short इ; it would give बस्तिं च, not बस्तीञ्च.
questions.explain: बस्तीन् (bastis, acc. pl.) + च (and).

questions.q: In verse 54 line 1, what does तद् (that) refer to?
options: The strength and region of line 05.04.100
The kuṣṭha and meha of line 05.04.105
The oil inside the basti itself
The heat or cold of line 05.04.102
optionExplain: Those factors were to be distinguished; तद् points to heat or cold.
That line comes later and is not what तद् points back to.
No oil is named in verse 54.
Right: The notes: तद् refers to the heat or cold in the line before.
questions.explain: Bastis are joined with drugs suited to the heat or cold to be treated.
questions.rule: तद् = the heat or cold of 05.04.102.

questions.q: दद्यात् in verse 54 means one should give. Which invented phrase means one should give a basti?
optionExplain: Right: दद्यात् is the optative: should give.
ददौ is the perfect: he gave.
दास्यति is the future: he will give.
दत्तवान् is a past active participle: he has given.
questions.explain: The optative (दद्यात्, युञ्जीत) gives the rule: one should do it.
questions.teaches: An optative such as दद्यात् or युञ्जीत states what one should do (invented बस्तिं दद्यात्, one should give a basti).

questions.q: What does मेदस्विन् mean in unit 55?
optionExplain: That is मेधाविन्, from मेधा; here it is मेदस्, fat.
Right: मेदस्विन् = having much medas (fat tissue): fat, obese.
Thin and wasted people come in line 05.04.106.
No fever is named in unit 55.
questions.explain: मेदस् + -विन् = one who has much fat.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 55 to its meaning as the card gives it.
questions.explain: The unit names the fat, those to be cleansed, and men with kuṣṭha and meha.
questions.rule: मेदस्विन् = fat; विशोध्य = to be cleansed; नर = man; कुष्ठ = skin disease; मेह = urinary disorder.

questions.q: Put these parts of unit 55 in the text's order.
questions.explain: The fat, those to be cleansed, and the men who are afflicted by kuṣṭha and meha.
questions.rule: मेदस्विनः · विशोध्याः · ये च नराः · कुष्ठमेहार्ताः.
questions.teaches: Unit 55 names the fat, those to be cleansed, and men afflicted by kuṣṭha (skin disease) and meha (urinary disorder).

questions.q: Which split of कुष्ठमेहार्त्ताः in unit 55 is right?
optionExplain: ए + आ would give अया: मेहयार्ताः.
-अः before आ drops the visarga with no merging: मेह आर्ताः.
Right: अ + आ → आ: मेह + आर्ताः = मेहार्ताः.
र्ताः is no word; the र् belongs to आर्त.
questions.explain: कुष्ठ (skin disease) + मेह (urinary disorder) + आर्ताः (afflicted).

questions.q: Five people come to the clinic. Which of them does unit 55 itself name?
options: A man who is thin and dried-up
optionExplain: Right: मेह-आर्ताः.
Right: कुष्ठ-आर्ताः.
Right: मेदस्विनः.
Fainted (मूर्च्छित) is in line 05.04.106, not here.
Thin and dried-up (कृश, शुष्क) are in line 05.04.106.
questions.explain: Unit 55 names the fat, those to be cleansed, and men with kuṣṭha and meha.
questions.rule: Unit 55: मेदस्विन्, विशोध्य, कुष्ठ- and मेह-आर्त.

questions.q: Like विशोध्याः + ये → विशोध्या ये, how does invented नराः + गच्छन्ति (the men go) join?
optionExplain: -ओ comes from -अः, not from -आः.
र् comes from -इः/-उः before voiced sounds, not from -आः.
श् stands only before च/छ/श, not before ग.
Right: -आः before a voiced sound (ग) drops its visarga, as in विशोध्या ये.
questions.explain: -आः + voiced consonant or vowel → -आ (visarga lost).
questions.teaches: A visarga after -आ is dropped before a voiced sound (विशोध्याः + ये → विशोध्या ये; invented नरा गच्छन्ति).

questions.q: What does कृश mean in unit 56?
optionExplain: Right: कृश = thin, lean.
Fat is मेदस्विन्, in line 05.04.105.
No swelling is named in unit 56.
Strong would be the opposite of दुर्बल, which is in the list.
questions.explain: कृश stands in the second compound: thin, dried-up, purified bodies.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 56 to its meaning as the card gives it.
questions.explain: All are states of the body named after न.
questions.rule: क्षीण = wasted; क्षत = injured; दुर्बल = weak; मूर्च्छित = fainted; शुष्क = dried-up.

questions.q: Put these states of unit 56 in the text's order.
questions.explain: क्षीण-क्षत-दुर्बल-मूर्च्छित, then कृश-शुष्क-शुद्ध-देहानाम्.
questions.rule: क्षीण · क्षत · दुर्बल · मूर्च्छित · कृश · शुष्क.
questions.teaches: Unit 56 lists, after न: wasted, injured, weak, fainted, thin, dried-up and purified bodies.

questions.q: In unit 56, what does the ending of देहानाम् show?
options: Genitive plural: of those with such bodies
Accusative plural: such bodies as object
optionExplain: The nominative plural would be देहाः.
Right: -आनाम् is the genitive plural; the compound is a bahuvrīhi: of those whose bodies are thin and the rest.
The accusative plural would be देहान्.
The locative plural would be देहेषु.
questions.explain: न … देहानाम्: not of those with … bodies.

questions.q: A patient is weak and has fainted. Does unit 56 by itself state the treatment he gets?
options: Yes: it gives him a nourishing basti
Yes: it gives him a cool basti
No: it opens with न and has no verb
Yes: it orders a day's fasting
optionExplain: No basti kind is named in unit 56.
Cool is said for the heat-afflicted in line 05.04.102.
Right: The unit only lists the people under न; the verb comes in line 05.04.107.
No fasting is named in unit 56.
questions.explain: Keep to what the unit contains: a list after न, no verb.
questions.rule: Unit 56: no verb, only a list after न.

questions.q: Like कृशदेह (one whose body is thin), what does invented दृढदेहः mean?
options: A firm part of a body
optionExplain: That would be an abstract noun like देहदार्ढ्यम्.
A bahuvrīhi describes the owner, not a part.
No verb or action is in the compound.
Right: A bahuvrīhi: firm (दृढ) + body (देह) describes the person who has it.
questions.explain: In a bahuvrīhi the compound describes someone else: the person with such a body.
questions.rule: Adjective + देह (bahuvrīhi) = one whose body is …
questions.teaches: Adjective + देह makes a bahuvrīhi: one whose body is so (कृशदेह; invented दृढदेहः, one whose body is firm).

questions.q: What does दद्यात् mean in unit 57?
optionExplain: Right: Optative 3rd singular of √दा: one should give.
A past form would be ददौ or अददात्.
The future would be दास्यति.
Having given would be दत्त्वा.
questions.explain: दद्यात् opens the unit and governs विशोधनीयान्.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 57 to its meaning as the card gives it.
questions.explain: The unit gives a verb, its object and a bahuvrīhi about life bound up in the doṣas.
questions.rule: दद्यात् = should give; विशोधनीय = cleansing; दोष = doṣa; निबद्ध = bound; आयुस् = life.

questions.q: Put the words of unit 57 in the text's order, after the split.
questions.explain: Should give, cleansing ones, life-bound-in-doṣas, who, and.
questions.teaches: Unit 57 reads: dadyāt viśodhanīyān doṣanibaddhāyuṣaḥ ye ca, one should give cleansing ones, and those whose life is bound up in the doṣas.

questions.q: Which split of दद्याद्विशोधनीयान् in unit 57 is right?
optionExplain: द्विशोधनीय is no word; the द् is the changed त्.
Right: Final त् before a voiced sound (व) becomes द्.
म् before व would give दद्यां विशोधनीयान्.
A final अ would stay: दद्यातविशोधनीयान्.
questions.explain: दद्यात् (should give) + विशोधनीयान् (cleansing ones).

questions.q: Whom does the bahuvrīhi दोषनिबद्धायुः describe?
options: A doṣa that is held fast by life
A life that is free of all doṣas
A person whose life is bound up in the doṣas
A basti that binds the doṣas fast
optionExplain: The head is life (आयुस्), and it describes a person.
निबद्ध is bound, not freed.
Right: Doṣa + bound + life: the one whose life is bound up with the doṣas.
No basti is named inside the compound.
questions.explain: Bahuvrīhi: the compound describes its owner, here people (ये).
questions.rule: दोषनिबद्धायुः = one whose life is bound up in the doṣas.

questions.q: Like दद्यात् + विशोधनीयान् → दद्याद्विशोधनीयान्, how does invented पिबेत् + दुग्धम् (he should drink milk) join?
optionExplain: त् becomes न् only before a nasal.
त् becomes च् only before च/छ.
त् becomes ल् only before ल.
Right: Final त् before a voiced द becomes द्.
questions.explain: -त् + voiced consonant → -द्.
questions.teaches: Final त् becomes द् before a voiced sound (दद्याद्विशोधनीयान्; invented पिबेद्दुग्धम्).

questions.q: Which number is the chapter that unit 58 closes?
optionExplain: Right: चतुर्थः = fourth.
Third would be तृतीयः.
Fifth would be पञ्चमः.
Fortieth would be चत्वारिंशः; चतुर्थ is fourth.
questions.explain: चतुर्थोऽध्यायः = the fourth chapter.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 58 to its meaning.
questions.explain: इति बस्तिकल्पो नाम चतुर्थोऽध्यायः.
questions.rule: इति = thus; बस्ति = basti; कल्प = preparation; नाम = named; अध्याय = chapter.

questions.q: Put the words of unit 58 in the text's order, after the split.
questions.explain: Thus, Bastikalpa, named, fourth, chapter.
questions.teaches: The colophon: iti bastikalpo nāma caturtho 'dhyāyaḥ, thus the fourth chapter, named Bastikalpa.

questions.q: Which split is right for चतुर्थोऽध्यायः?
optionExplain: अ + अ would merge to आ: चतुर्थाध्यायः.
Right: -अः before अ gives -ओ and the अ is shown by ऽ.
ध्यायः is not the word; the chapter is अध्यायः.
म् before a vowel would give चतुर्थमध्यायः.
questions.explain: चतुर्थः (fourth) + अध्यायः (chapter).

questions.q: A student asks what the chapter title Bastikalpa names. What does the card say?
optionExplain: Complications (व्यापद्) are not in this title.
The title names bastis, not body parts.
Right: बस्ति-कल्प: the preparations of bastis.
The title names no season or collecting.
questions.explain: बस्तिकल्पः is a tat-puruṣa: kalpa (preparation) of basti.

questions.q: Like बस्तिकल्पः + नाम → बस्तिकल्पो नाम, how does invented वमनकल्पः + नाम join?
optionExplain: -आ comes from -आः, not from -अः.
र् comes from -इः/-उः before voiced sounds, not from -अः.
स् stands only before त/थ, not before न.
Right: -अः before a voiced sound (न) becomes -ओ.
questions.explain: -अः + voiced consonant → -ओ.
questions.teaches: -अः before a voiced consonant becomes -ओ (बस्तिकल्पो नाम; invented वमनकल्पो नाम).

questions.q: Which topic does unit 1 announce for the chapter?
options: The kalpa of the siddhabasti enemas
The weights and measures of drugs
optionExplain: Right: सिद्धबस्तिकल्पम् = the kalpa (preparation) of the siddhabasti.
No emetic (vamana) is named in this line; it names the siddhabasti.
No mishap or purgation is named in this line.
The line names no measure; it names the siddhabasti.
questions.explain: The opening formula names the chapter's topic: the siddhabasti-kalpa.
questions.rule: अथातः X व्याख्यास्यामः = now, therefore, we shall explain X.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 1 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The four words make the whole opening formula.
questions.rule: अथ = now; अतः = therefore; व्याख्यास्यामः = we shall explain.

questions.q: Put these words of unit 1 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: The formula runs: now, therefore, the topic, we shall explain.
questions.teaches: An opening formula puts the topic between अथातः and the verb व्याख्यास्यामः.

questions.q: Which split of अथातः is right?
optionExplain: तः is not a word here, and अथा is not the particle अथ.
Right: अ + अ gives आ: अथ + अतः = अथातः.
A visarga after अ before अ would give अथोऽतः, not अथातः.
आतः is not a word; the second word is अतः (therefore).
questions.explain: Two particles join: अथ (now) + अतः (therefore).
questions.rule: अ + अ → आ: अथ + अतः = अथातः.

questions.q: What does the card say the form व्याख्यास्यामः is?
options: Third person singular optative: one should explain
First person plural past: we explained
First person plural future: we shall explain
optionExplain: An optative would end in -एत् or -ईत; this ends in -स्यामः.
The -स्य- marks the future, not a past tense.
Right: The data labels it 1 pl. fut. of vi-ā-√khyā.
An imperative to one person would not end in -आमः.
questions.explain: -स्यामः = 'we shall ...': the author promises what follows.
questions.rule: व्याख्यास्यामः = we shall explain (1 pl. future).

questions.q: An invented heading joins अथ + अतः before बस्तिकल्पम्. Which joined form is right?
optionExplain: The visarga stays only before an unvoiced sound such as स in सिद्ध-.
र् replaces a visarga after vowels other than अ/आ, not after अ.
Dropping the visarga to -आ happens after -आः, not after -अः.
Right: -अः before a voiced consonant (ब) becomes -ओ.
questions.explain: In unit 1 the visarga stays because सिद्ध- begins with स; before ब it becomes ओ.
questions.rule: -अः + voiced consonant → -ओ: अथातः + बस्ति → अथातो बस्ति.
questions.teaches: -अः before a voiced consonant becomes -ओ (अथातो बस्तिकल्पम्); before स it stays (अथातः सिद्ध-).

questions.q: For whom does verse 2 say the siddhabastis should be employed?
options: Only for the strong and the young
Only for those with Vāta disorders
Only for children and the old
optionExplain: Right: सर्व-देहिनाम् = of / for all embodied beings.
The verse limits them to no group; it says all embodied beings.
No doṣa or disorder is named in this verse.
No age group is named here; the verse says all.
questions.explain: The verse sets no limit: all embodied beings, at all times (सर्वदा).
questions.rule: सर्वदा सर्वदेहिनाम् = at all times, for all embodied beings.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 2 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words give the instruction and two of the qualities.
questions.rule: प्रयुञ्जीत = one should employ; सर्वदा = at all times; बहुफलान् = of many benefits; सुखान् = pleasant.

questions.q: Put these words of line 1 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Line 1 runs: the siddhabastis, one should employ, at all times, for all embodied beings.
questions.teaches: Line 1 gives object, verb, then when (सर्वदा) and for whom (सर्वदेहिनाम्).

questions.q: Which split of सिद्धबस्तीन्प्रयुंजीत is right?
optionExplain: न 'not' would forbid what the verse commends for all beings at all times.
Right: The accusative plural -ईन् is the object of प्रयुञ्जीत (one should employ).
न्प्रयुञ्जीत is not a word.
सिद्धबस्तीन is not a form; the ending is -ईन्.
questions.explain: सिद्धबस्तीन् (the siddhabastis, acc. pl.) + प्रयुञ्जीत (one should employ).
questions.rule: -ईन् = masculine accusative plural of an -इ stem (बस्तीन्).

questions.q: Which statements fit verse 2 about the siddhabastis?
options: Quick to act within an hour
They are to be employed at all times
To be given only by a royal physician
optionExplain: सुखान् = pleasant.
Nothing about cost or collecting is said.
No time of action is named.
सर्वदा = at all times.
बहुफलान् = of many benefits.
No physician is named.
questions.explain: The verse says: at all times, for all beings; of many benefits, pleasant (and two qualities on flagged words).

questions.q: Like प्रयुञ्जीत (one should employ, √युज्), which form means one should eat (√भुज्)?
optionExplain: This is the present tense: 'he eats'.
This is the future: 'he will eat'.
Right: Same 3 sg optative ātmanepada pattern: -उञ्जीत, as in प्रयुञ्जीत.
This is the past participle: 'eaten'.
questions.explain: √युज् and √भुज् form the optative the same way: युञ्जीत, भुञ्जीत.
questions.rule: 3 sg optative ātmanepada ends in -ईत: प्रयुञ्जीत, भुञ्जीत.
questions.teaches: The ending -ईत marks a 3rd-person singular optative (ātmanepada): 'one should ...' (प्रयुञ्जीत, भुञ्जीत).

questions.q: Which two things does verse 3 call equal (समे)?
optionExplain: These follow; the equal pair is मधुतैले.
Castor root gives the decoction in line 2.
The decoction is in line 2; समे goes with मधुतैले.
Right: मधुतैले समे = honey and oil, equal (dual).
questions.explain: मधुतैले (dual) and समे (dual) agree: honey and oil, equal.
questions.rule: मधुतैले समे = honey and oil in equal parts.
questions.section: एरण्डमूल का निरूह और यापन बस्ति

questions.q: Match each word of verse 3 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are the readable items, the word for equal and the kind of enema.
questions.rule: मधु = honey; तैल = oil; सैन्धव = rock salt; सम = equal; निरूह = decoction enema.
questions.section: एरण्डमूल का निरूह और यापन बस्ति

questions.q: Put these words of verse 3 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Line 1 lists the items and measures; line 2 ends by naming the nirūha.
questions.rule: मधुतैले समे · कर्षः · सैंधवात् द्विपिचुः · मिशिः ‖ … निरूहो माधुतैलिकः.
questions.teaches: Verse 3 lists honey and oil (equal), a karṣa, two picu from rock salt and miśi, then names the nirūha.
questions.section: एरण्डमूल का निरूह और यापन बस्ति

questions.q: What does the word माधुतैलिकः tell about this nirūha?
options: It is made with honey (madhu) and oil (taila)
It is made with milk (kṣīra) and oil (taila)
It is given only in the spring month
It is made with ghee and rock salt alone
optionExplain: Right: माधुतैलिक is formed from मधु + तैल: made with honey and oil.
Milk is not named in this verse.
The card reads मधु as honey here, not as a season.
Ghee is not named, and honey and oil are.
questions.explain: The derived adjective names the two key items: honey and oil.
questions.rule: माधुतैलिक = made with मधु (honey) and तैल (oil).
questions.section: एरण्डमूल का निरूह और यापन बस्ति

questions.q: What kind of enema does verse 3 name with माधुतैलिकः?
optionExplain: The yāpana is in verses 5-6.
Right: निरूहो माधुतैलिकः: the line calls it a nirūha.
Yuktaratha is named in verse 7.
The line names a nirūha, a decoction enema.
questions.explain: Line 2 closes with the enema's kind: निरूहः.
questions.section: एरण्डमूल का निरूह और यापन बस्ति

questions.q: In सैंधवाद्द्विपिचुः, सैन्धवात् became सैंधवाद्. Join an invented सैन्धवात् + गुडः the same way. Which is right?
optionExplain: त् does not stay unvoiced before a voiced consonant.
त् does not take the place of the next consonant before ग.
Right: Final त् becomes द् before a voiced consonant (ग), as before द.
त् becomes न् only before a nasal (न, म).
questions.explain: Same rule as सैन्धवात् + द्विपिचुः = सैन्धवाद्द्विपिचुः.
questions.rule: Final त् → द् before a voiced consonant.
questions.teaches: Final त् becomes द् before a voiced consonant: सैन्धवात् + द्वि → सैन्धवाद्द्वि; + गुडः → सैन्धवाद्गुडः.
questions.section: एरण्डमूल का निरूह और यापन बस्ति

questions.q: With licorice (यष्टीमधु) added, what does verse 4 say the nirūha does?
options: It is fattening and brings on deep sleep
It clears the voice and the skin
It removes the faults of the enema
optionExplain: Neither is named in this verse.
Voice and skin are not named here.
That phrase belongs to verse 8.
Right: सयष्टीमधुकः ... चक्षुष्यो रक्तपित्तजित्.
questions.explain: Line 2: with licorice, cakṣuṣya (good for the eyes) and raktapitta-jit.
questions.section: एरण्डमूल का निरूह और यापन बस्ति

questions.q: Match each disorder of verse 4 to its meaning on the card.
questions.explain: These are four of the disorders the nirūha dispels.
questions.rule: अर्शस् = haemorrhoids; कृमि = worms; गुल्म = abdominal lump; अन्त्रवृद्धि = hernia.
questions.section: एरण्डमूल का निरूह और यापन बस्ति

questions.q: Put the disorders that the nirūha dispels in the order of verse 4.
questions.explain: Line 1 runs prameha, arśas, then the compound kṛmi-gulma-antravṛddhi-nut.
questions.teaches: The nirūha dispels prameha, arśas, worms, gulma and antravṛddhi, in that order.
questions.section: एरण्डमूल का निरूह और यापन बस्ति

questions.q: Why is चक्षुष्यः printed as चक्षुष्यो before रक्तपित्तजित्?
options: -ओ marks the vocative of the word
-ओ marks a dual form of the word
optionExplain: Right: Regular visarga sandhi: चक्षुष्यः + रक्त → चक्षुष्यो रक्त.
The vocative of चक्षुष्य would be चक्षुष्य; the card gives nom. sg.
The card labels it m. nom. sg.
The card labels it masculine.
questions.explain: The form is nominative singular; only sandhi changes -अः to -ओ.
questions.section: एरण्डमूल का निरूह और यापन बस्ति

questions.q: Which ending in verse 4 means dispelling the listed disorders?
optionExplain: -जित् = conquering; verse 4 uses it with रक्तपित्त.
Right: कृमिगुल्मान्त्रवृद्धिनुत् = dispelling worms, gulma and hernia.
-कर = making, as in verse 2 (करान्); it is not in verse 4.
-हर = removing; it is in verse 8, not verse 4.
questions.explain: Line 1 ends in -नुत्: the nirūha dispels prameha, arśas, worms, gulma, antravṛddhi.
questions.section: एरण्डमूल का निरूह और यापन बस्ति

questions.q: Like रक्तपित्तजित् (conquering raktapitta), what does an invented ज्वरजित् mean (ज्वर = fever)?
optionExplain: That would be ज्वरज, with -ज (born).
That would need -कर (making), as in बलबुद्धिकर.
Right: -जित् at the end of a compound means 'conquering X'.
-जित् is active: it conquers, it is not conquered.
questions.explain: Same build as रक्तपित्तजित् and शूलजित्: X + जित् = conquering X.
questions.teaches: A compound ending in -जित् means 'conquering X' (रक्तपित्तजित्, ज्वरजित्).
questions.section: एरण्डमूल का निरूह और यापन बस्ति

questions.q: Which four substances does verse 5 say the yāpana has?
options: Honey, milk, oil and rock salt
Ghee, curd, oil and cow's urine
optionExplain: Milk and rock salt are not in this verse.
Curd and cow's urine are not in this verse.
Sugar and sesame are not in this verse.
Right: मधु-तैल-वसा-आज्य-वान् = having honey, oil, fat and ghee.
questions.explain: The -वान् compound lists four: honey, oil, fat, ghee (आज्य).
questions.rule: मधुतैलवसाज्यवान् = having honey, oil, fat, ghee.
questions.section: एरण्डमूल का निरूह और यापन बस्ति

questions.q: Match each word of verse 5 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are readable members of the pain compound.
questions.rule: पायु = anus; जानु = knee; ऊरु = thigh; घनकल्क = thick paste.
questions.section: एरण्डमूल का निरूह और यापन बस्ति

questions.q: Put the four substances of line 1 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The compound runs honey, oil, fat, ghee, then -वान् (having).
questions.teaches: The yāpana has honey, oil, fat (vasā) and ghee (ājya), in that order.
questions.section: एरण्डमूल का निरूह और यापन बस्ति

questions.q: Which split of the end of मधुतैलवसाज्यवान् is right?
optionExplain: Right: आ + आ gives आ; आज्य = ghee, -वान् = having.
The card reads आज्य (ghee) + -वान्; यवान् (barley) is not on the card.
The word is वसा (fat), with long आ.
अज्य is not a word; the word is आज्य (ghee).
questions.explain: Fat (वसा) and ghee (आज्य) join with आ + आ → आ.
questions.rule: आ + आ → आ: वसा + आज्य = वसाज्य.
questions.section: एरण्डमूल का निरूह और यापन बस्ति

questions.q: Which body parts does the readable part of verse 5 name for pain?
optionExplain: Eyes are in verse 4, not here.
जानु = knee.
No chest is named.
No head (शिरस्) is named.
पायु = anus.
ऊरु = thigh.
questions.explain: Readable members: anus, knee, thigh, bladder region, penis; the middle word is damaged.
questions.rule: पायु · जानु · ऊरु · (अस्पष्ट) · बस्ति · मेहन + शूलजित्.
questions.section: एरण्डमूल का निरूह और यापन बस्ति

questions.q: Like आज्यवान् (having ghee), which invented form means having milk (क्षीर)?
optionExplain: -जित् means 'conquering', not 'having'.
Right: -वत् (nom. m. -वान्) after a stem in -अ means 'having X'.
This is the ablative, 'from milk'.
This is the noun 'milk' itself.
questions.explain: Same suffix as मधुतैलवसाज्यवान्: X + -वान् = having X.
questions.teaches: The suffix -वत् (masc. nom. -वान्) means 'having X': आज्यवान्, क्षीरवान्.
questions.section: एरण्डमूल का निरूह और यापन बस्ति

questions.q: Which measure does verse 6 give for the ghee, honey, fat and oil?
optionExplain: Half an akṣa goes with the rock salt.
Half a pala goes with hapuṣā.
Right: प्रसृत-अंशैः = with prasṛta portions.
A karṣa is named in verse 3, not here.
questions.explain: The four substances are measured in prasṛta portions.
questions.rule: प्रसृतांशैः घृतक्षौद्रवसातैलैः = with ghee, honey, fat, oil in prasṛta portions.
questions.section: एरण्डमूल का निरूह और यापन बस्ति

questions.q: Put these four substances in the order of verse 6.
questions.explain: The compound runs ghee, honey, fat, oil.
questions.section: एरण्डमूल का निरूह और यापन बस्ति

questions.q: Match each word of verse 6 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words carry the substances and the half measures.
questions.rule: क्षौद्र = honey; वसा = fat; अर्ध = half; अन्वित = accompanied by.
questions.teaches: In verse 6, क्षौद्र is honey and अर्ध + measure gives the half measures of salt and hapuṣā.
questions.section: एरण्डमूल का निरूह और यापन बस्ति

questions.q: Which split of प्रसृतांशैर्घृत is right?
optionExplain: The measure is प्रसृत, not प्रसृता.
र्घृत is not a word; the र् comes from the visarga of अंशैः.
The र् replaces the visarga; it is not part of घृत.
Right: अ + अ → आ; -ऐः before a voiced sound (घ) becomes -ऐर्.
questions.explain: The visarga of अंशैः turns into र् before घृत.
questions.section: एरण्डमूल का निरूह और यापन बस्ति

questions.q: Which word gives the action of verse 6, and what does it mean?
optionExplain: Right: प्र-√क्ळृप्, 3 sg optative: one should prepare.
पाचयेत् is the verb of verse 10.
प्रयुञ्जीत is the verb of verse 2.
That is the verb of unit 1.
questions.explain: Verse 6's own verb is प्रकल्पयेत्.
questions.section: एरण्डमूल का निरूह और यापन बस्ति

questions.q: Join an invented अंशैः + दत्तम् (given in portions) by the rule of प्रसृतांशैर्घृत. Which is right?
optionExplain: The visarga does not stay before a voiced consonant.
Right: -ऐः before a voiced consonant (द) becomes -ऐर्.
The visarga is not dropped after ऐ.
स् replaces a visarga only before त-type unvoiced sounds.
questions.explain: Same rule as अंशैः + घृत = अंशैर्घृत.
questions.rule: Visarga after a vowel other than अ/आ → र् before a voiced sound.
questions.teaches: A visarga after a vowel other than अ/आ becomes र् before a voiced sound: अंशैः + घृत → अंशैर्घृत.
questions.section: एरण्डमूल का निरूह और यापन बस्ति

questions.q: What does verse 7 call this enema?
optionExplain: That name is given in verse 9.
That is the nirūha of verse 3.
Right: एष युक्तरथो बस्तिः = this is the yuktaratha enema.
The yāpana is in verses 5-6.
questions.explain: The verse names itself: एष युक्तरथो बस्तिः.

questions.q: Match each drug of verse 7 to its meaning on the card.
questions.explain: Three drugs and the literal sense of the enema's name.
questions.rule: वचा = sweet flag; पिप्पली = long pepper; युक्तरथ = harnessed chariot; सैन्धव = rock salt.

questions.q: Put these items in the order of verse 7.
questions.explain: Line 1 (after the decoction): honey, oil, with rock salt; line 2: this, yuktaratha, enema.
questions.rule: मधु · तैलं · ससैंधवं ‖ एष · युक्तरथो · बस्तिः.
questions.teaches: Verse 7 lists honey, oil and rock salt, then names it: एष युक्तरथो बस्तिः.

questions.q: What does स- at the start of ससैन्धवम् and सवचा- mean?
optionExplain: 'Without' would be निर्- or अ-, as in निर्व्यापद्.
'Equal' is सम, as in verse 3 (समे).
'Good' would be सु-.
Right: स- opening a bahuvrīhi = 'with X'.
questions.explain: ससैन्धवम् = with rock salt; सवचापिप्पलीफलः = with vacā, pippalī and fruit.

questions.q: Which of these is not an ingredient of the yuktaratha in verse 7?
optionExplain: Right: Cow's urine is not named in verse 7.
सवचा- = with vacā, in line 2.
-पिप्पली- is named in line 2.
-फलः closes the line-2 compound: with fruit.
questions.explain: The verse names castor-root decoction, honey, oil, rock salt, vacā, pippalī and fruit.
questions.rule: युक्तरथ: एरण्डमूल-क्वाथ, मधु, तैल, सैन्धव, वचा, पिप्पली, फल.

questions.q: Built like ससैन्धवम् (with rock salt), what does an invented सघृतम् mean?
optionExplain: That would be निर्घृतम्.
Right: स- + घृत = with ghee.
That would need सम (equal).
स- adds an accompaniment; it does not mean 'alone'.
questions.explain: Same prefix as ससैन्धवम् and सवचा-.
questions.teaches: स- before a noun makes a bahuvrīhi 'with X': ससैन्धवम्, सघृतम्.

questions.q: What does verse 8 say the preparation removes?
options: Pain of the knee and thigh
optionExplain: Worms and gulma are in verse 4.
Those pains are in verse 5.
Right: बस्ति-दोष-हरः = removing the faults of the enema.
Those are in verse 11.
questions.explain: बस्तिदोषहरः: -हर = removing; the data reads the faults as those of the enema.
questions.rule: बस्तिदोषहरः = removing the faults of the enema.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 8 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Three readable drugs and the closing adjective.
questions.rule: हिङ्गु = asafoetida; सैन्धव = rock salt; सुरदारु = deodar; शिवः = auspicious.

questions.q: Put these readable items in the order of verse 8.
questions.explain: Line 1: honey, (two flagged words), asafoetida, rock salt; line 2: suradāru, rāsnā.
questions.teaches: The clear items of verse 8 run honey, asafoetida, rock salt, suradāru, rāsnā.

questions.q: What does शिवः describe in verse 8?
options: The god Śiva, who taught the formula
A further drug of the list
optionExplain: No teacher or deity is named in the verse.
The card glosses शिवः as 'auspicious', an adjective.
No patient is named; शिवः goes with the preparation.
Right: शिवः (m. nom. sg.) agrees with the preparation, like बस्तिदोषहरः.
questions.explain: The two closing adjectives describe the preparation: removing enema faults, auspicious.

questions.q: Which of these does verse 8 name?
optionExplain: Cow's urine is in verse 10.
Vacā is in verse 7.
Named in line 2.
Named in line 1.
Named in line 1.
Licorice is in verse 4, not here.
questions.explain: Readable items: decoction, honey, śatāhvā, asafoetida, rock salt, suradāru, rāsnā.
questions.rule: Verse 8: मधु · शताह्वा · हिङ्गु · सैन्धव · सुरदारु · रास्ना.

questions.q: Like बस्तिदोषहरः (removing the faults of the enema), what does an invented शूलहरः mean (शूल = pain)?
optionExplain: Right: -हर at the end of a compound = removing X.
That would be शूलज (with -ज, born).
That would need a word like -पूर्ण.
-हर is active: it removes; it is not overcome.
questions.explain: Same build as बस्तिदोषहरः: X + हर = removing X.
questions.teaches: A compound ending in -हर means 'removing X': बस्तिदोषहरः, शूलहरः.

questions.q: What does verse 9 say this enema is called?
optionExplain: That is the enema of verse 7.
Right: सिद्धबस्तिरिति स्मृतः = it is called the siddhabasti.
That is the nirūha of verse 3.
The yāpana is in verses 5-6.
