questions.explain: The verse closes by naming the enema: siddhabasti.
questions.rule: ... सिद्धबस्तिरिति स्मृतः = ... is called the siddhabasti.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 9 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Three ingredients and the naming word.
questions.rule: पञ्चमूल = five roots; मागधिका = long pepper; स्मृतः = is called; सैन्धव = rock salt.

questions.q: Put these ingredients in the order of verse 9.
questions.explain: Line 1: of the pañcamūla, (decoction, oil), māgadhikā, honey; line 2: with rock salt, ..., siddhabasti.
questions.teaches: Verse 9 runs from the pañcamūla through māgadhikā, honey and rock salt to the name siddhabasti.

questions.q: In सिद्धबस्तिरिति स्मृतः, what does इति स्मृतः do?
optionExplain: स्मृतः is a past participle, not an optative like प्रयुञ्जीत.
No negative न stands in the line.
Right: इति marks the name; स्मृतः = is called, is remembered.
At all times is सर्वदा, in verse 2.
questions.explain: The line ends by naming the enema: it is called the siddhabasti.
questions.rule: X इति स्मृतः = it is called X.

questions.q: Which root group does verse 9 name (पंचमूलस्य)?
optionExplain: The ten roots are cooked in verse 10.
Castor root gives the decoction in verses 3 and 7.
Triphalā is in verse 10, and it is a fruit group.
Right: पञ्चमूलस्य निःक्वाथः = decoction of the pañcamūla.
questions.explain: Verse 9 uses the five-root group; which one of the two pañcamūlas is not stated.

questions.q: Like सिद्धबस्तिः + इति = सिद्धबस्तिरिति, how does an invented कृमिः + इति join?
optionExplain: Right: A visarga after इ becomes र् before a vowel.
The visarga does not stay before a vowel.
That would be कृमि + इति with no visarga.
स् replaces a visarga before त-type sounds, not before a vowel.
questions.explain: Same rule as बस्तिः + इति → बस्तिरिति.
questions.teaches: A visarga after a vowel other than अ/आ becomes र् before a vowel: बस्तिः + इति → बस्तिरिति.

questions.q: In which liquid does verse 10 say the drugs are cooked?
optionExplain: No milk is named in this verse.
Right: पाचयेत् गोमूत्रे = one should cook in cow's urine.
That base is in verses 3 and 7.
Honey is not named in this verse.
questions.explain: गोमूत्रे is a locative: in cow's urine.
questions.rule: पाचयेत् ... गोमूत्रे = cook in cow's urine.

questions.q: Put the drugs to be cooked in the order of verse 10.
questions.explain: The compound runs dvipañcamūla, triphalā, phala, bilva, then पाचयेत्.

questions.q: Match each drug of verse 10 to its meaning on the card.
questions.explain: Two paste drugs and two cooked drugs, with the card's identifications.
questions.rule: वत्सक = probably kuṭaja; तोयद = probably musta; बिल्व = bael; त्रिफला = the three fruits.
questions.teaches: In verse 10, vatsaka (probably kuṭaja) and toyada (probably musta) are ground drugs; bilva and triphalā are cooked.

questions.q: What does द्विपञ्चमूल mean on the card?
optionExplain: द्वि multiplies the group; it does not pick two roots.
द्वि goes with the group, not with the cooking.
Right: द्वि + पञ्चमूल = both pañcamūlas, ten roots.
No fruits are counted in this word.
questions.explain: A number before a group name doubles the group: two pañcamūlas.

questions.q: Which drugs does line 2 of verse 10 give in ground form (पिष्टैः)?
optionExplain: These are named in line 1, with पाचयेत् (cook).
The ten roots are named in line 1, not as ground drugs.
These come in verse 11.
Right: पिष्टैः पाठावत्सकतोयदैः = with the ground ones of these three.
questions.explain: Line 1 names what is cooked in cow's urine; line 2 names ground drugs, whose exact link (तेनै) is unclear.
questions.rule: पिष्टैः पाठावत्सकतोयदैः = with ground pāṭhā, vatsaka, toyada.

questions.q: Like त्रिफला (the three fruits), what does an invented त्रिकटु name (कटु = pungent)?
options: A group of three pungent drugs
One drug that is three times as pungent
A drug pungent in three seasons
Three doses of one pungent drug
optionExplain: Right: A number + noun names a group of that many, as त्रिफला.
त्रि counts the members; it does not intensify.
No season is in the word.
The word names a group, not a dose.
questions.explain: Same build as त्रिफला and पञ्चमूल: number + item = a group of that many.
questions.rule: Number + noun = a named group (त्रिफला, पञ्चमूल).
questions.teaches: A compound of a number and a noun names a group of that many items: त्रिफला, पञ्चमूल, त्रिकटु.

questions.q: In which disorders does verse 11 say the enema is suitable?
options: Vāta disorders, raktapitta and eye disease
Pain of the anus, knee and thigh
optionExplain: None of these is named in verse 11.
Right: कफव्याधि-पाण्डुरोग-विसूचिषु = in these three.
These are in verse 4.
These are in verse 5.
questions.explain: The locative compound names three: Kapha disorders, pāṇḍu disease, visūcī.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 11 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Two added substances and two of the disorders.
questions.rule: क्षौद्र = honey; लवण = salt; पाण्डुरोग = anaemia with pallor; विसूची = acute vomiting and purging.

questions.q: Put the added items of line 1 in the order of verse 11.
questions.explain: Line 1: with fruits, with honey and oil, with kṣāra, with salt.
questions.teaches: Verse 11 adds, in order: fruits, honey and oil, kṣāra, salt.

questions.q: Which case is विसूचिषु, and what does it mean here?
optionExplain: The instrumental plural would end in -भिः.
The genitive plural would end in -नाम्.
Right: -षु is the locative plural ending: 'in'.
The dative plural would end in -भ्यः.
questions.explain: The disorders stand in the locative: the enema is suitable in them.

questions.q: Does verse 11 name the fruits that are added (सफलैः)?
optionExplain: No madana is named in verse 11.
Triphalā is cooked in verse 10; सफलैः names none.
Bilva is in verse 10; सफलैः names none.
Right: स-फलैः = with fruits; no fruit is named.
questions.explain: The card says the fruits are not named.

questions.q: Like क्षौद्रतैलाभ्याम् (with honey and oil), which invented form means with ghee and honey (घृत, मधु)?
optionExplain: Right: -भ्याम् is the instrumental dual: two things, 'with'.
-भिः is plural, for three or more.
-ना is singular.
-नोः is genitive or locative dual, not 'with'.
questions.explain: A dvandva of two items takes the dual: क्षौद्रतैलाभ्याम्, घृतमधुभ्याम्.
questions.teaches: A dvandva of two items in the instrumental takes the dual ending -भ्याम्: क्षौद्रतैलाभ्याम्, घृतमधुभ्याम्.

questions.q: In which conditions does line 1 of verse 12 say the enema is esteemed?
options: Fever, cough and swelling of the feet
Blocked semen and wind; bladder āṭopa
Pain of the head, ear and the nape
optionExplain: None of these is named in verse 12.
Right: शुक्रानिलविबन्धेषु बस्त्याटोपेषु = in obstructions of semen and wind, in āṭopa of the bladder region.
These are in verse 4, not here.
Head and ear pains come in verse 17.
questions.explain: Two locatives name the conditions: obstructions (of semen and wind) and āṭopa of the bladder region.

questions.q: Match each drug of verse 12 to its identification on the card.
questions.explain: Four drugs of line 2 with the identifications the data marks standard.
questions.rule: मुस्त = nut-grass; अमृता = guḍūcī; एरण्ड = castor; पुनर्नवा = Boerhavia diffusa.

questions.q: Put these drugs of line 2 in the order of verse 12.
questions.explain: After musta the compound runs pāṭhā, amṛtā, eraṇḍa, balā, rāsnā and ends with punarnavā.
questions.rule: मुस्त · पाठा · अमृता · एरण्ड · बला · रास्ना · पुनर्नवा.
questions.teaches: Line 2 of verse 12 lists musta, pāṭhā, amṛtā, eraṇḍa, balā, rāsnā, punarnavā, in that order.

questions.q: Which split of शुक्रानिल is right?
optionExplain: A visarga after अ before अ would give शुक्रोऽनिल.
इल is not a word here; the second member is अनिल (wind).
Right: अ + अ → आ: शुक्र (semen) + अनिल (wind).
निल is not a word; the stem is शुक्र, not शुक्रा.
questions.explain: Inside the compound, शुक्र + अनिल join with अ + अ → आ.
questions.rule: अ + अ → आ: शुक्र + अनिल = शुक्रानिल.

questions.q: What does the card say बस्ति means inside बस्त्याटोपेषु?
optionExplain: Elsewhere basti is the enema, but here it names the place of the āṭopa.
The card reads basti here as a body region, not a device.
That enema (of verse 11) is the subject of पूजितः; बस्ति in the compound is the place of the āṭopa.
Right: The data reads basti here as the bladder region: āṭopa of the bladder region.
questions.explain: बस्ति-आटोप = rumbling distension of the bladder region; the enema is the subject (पूजितः).

questions.q: Like विबन्धेषु (in obstructions), which invented form means in fevers (ज्वर)?
optionExplain: Right: -एषु is the locative plural of an -अ stem: 'in'.
-ऐः is the instrumental plural: 'with fevers'.
-आणाम् is the genitive plural: 'of fevers'.
-आन् is the accusative plural: fevers as object.
questions.explain: Same ending as विबन्धेषु and बस्त्याटोपेषु: -एषु = in.
questions.teaches: The ending -एषु marks the locative plural of an -अ stem, 'in X': विबन्धेषु, आटोपेषु, ज्वरेषु.

questions.q: Which pañcamūla (group of five roots) does verse 13 name?
optionExplain: The verse says कनीयः, smaller, not the greater group.
Right: कनीयः पञ्चमूलम् = the lesser pañcamūla.
Two pañcamūlas are in verse 10, not here.
The pañcamūla without gokṣura comes in verse 19.
questions.explain: कनीयः (smaller, lesser) qualifies पञ्चमूलम्.
questions.rule: कनीयः पञ्चमूलम् = the lesser group of five roots.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 13 to its meaning on the card.
questions.explain: Three drugs of line 1 (standard identifications) and the word that names the root group.
questions.rule: मञ्जिष्ठा = Indian madder; आरग्वध = Indian laburnum; उशीर = vetiver; कनीयः = lesser.

questions.q: Put these four drugs in the order of line 1 of verse 13.
questions.explain: The compound opens mañjiṣṭhā, āragvadha, uśīra, trāyamāṇā; the end of the line is conjectural.
questions.rule: मञ्जिष्ठा · आरग्वध · उशीर · त्रायमाणा · (अनुमानित: अक्ष, रोहिणी).
questions.teaches: Line 1 of verse 13 runs mañjiṣṭhā, āragvadha, uśīra, trāyamāṇā before its doubtful end.

questions.q: What does मदनाष्टकम् mean on the card?
options: An eighth part of one madana
Madana boiled down to an eighth
optionExplain: The compound counts madana itself: a group of eight of them.
An eighth part would be अष्टमांश, not अष्टक.
Right: मदन + अष्टक: अष्टक = a set of eight.
No boiling is in the word; अष्टक counts eight items.
questions.explain: -अष्टक names a group of eight, here of madana (probably emetic nut).
questions.rule: X-अष्टक = a set of eight X.

questions.q: Does verse 13 list the five roots of the lesser pañcamūla?
options: Yes; it lists them after madana
Yes; they are the drugs of line 1
Yes; it names bṛhatī and four more
No; it names the group only
optionExplain: Nothing follows madana in this verse.
Line 1 holds mañjiṣṭhā and others, not the five roots.
Bṛhatī heads a pañcamūla in verse 22, not here.
Right: The card says the text does not list the members.
questions.explain: Only the group name stands in the text: कनीयः पञ्चमूलम्.
questions.rule: A group name (पञ्चमूल) can stand without its members.

questions.q: Like मदनाष्टकम् (a set of eight madana), what does an invented ओषधिपञ्चकम् mean (ओषधि = herb)?
options: The fifth herb of a list
A herb five times as strong
optionExplain: Right: -पञ्चक names a group of five, as -अष्टक a group of eight.
The fifth would be पञ्चम, not पञ्चक.
The suffix counts members; it does not intensify.
The word names a group of herbs, not portions.
questions.explain: Number + -क names a set: अष्टक (eight), पञ्चक (five).
questions.rule: X-पञ्चक = a set of five X.
questions.teaches: A number word with -क names a set of that many: मदनाष्टकम् (eight madana), ओषधिपञ्चकम् (five herbs).

questions.q: In what is the drug list first cooked in verse 14?
options: In an āḍhaka of meat juice
optionExplain: The two prasthas of milk are added in line 2.
Right: जलाढके = in an āḍhaka of water.
No urine is named in this verse.
No meat juice is named in this verse.
questions.explain: Line 1 opens with जलाढके: water first, milk later.
questions.rule: जल-आढके पचेत् = cook in an āḍhaka of water.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 14 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four words carry the whole procedure.
questions.rule: पाद = a quarter; शेष = remaining; परिस्रुत = strained.

questions.q: Put the steps of verse 14 in the order of the text.
items: Cook in an āḍhaka of water
questions.explain: Water cooking, reduction to a quarter, straining, then milk and a second cooking.
questions.teaches: Verse 14: cook in water to a quarter, strain, add two prasthas of milk, cook again till milk remains.

questions.q: Which split of पचेत्तच्च is right?
optionExplain: पचेत would join as पचेततच्च; the card reads पचेत् with final त्.
तः is not a word here, and -अः + च would give -अश्च.
Right: पचेत् (one should cook) + तत् (that) + च (and); त् before च becomes च्.
त्तत् is not a word.
questions.explain: Three words: पचेत् · तत् · च; तत् + च → तच्च.
questions.rule: Final त् + च → च्च: तत् + च = तच्च.

questions.q: Until when is the milk mixture cooked the second time?
options: Until a quarter of it is left
Until it thickens into a paste
Until half of the milk is left
Until only the milk is left
optionExplain: The quarter belongs to the first cooking in water.
No paste is named in verse 14.
No half is named; the text says the milk remains.
Right: क्षीरशेषम् = until the milk remains, the water having boiled away.
questions.explain: First cooking: पादशेष (a quarter); second cooking: क्षीरशेष (milk remains).
questions.rule: क्षीरशेषं पुनः पचेत् = cook again until the milk remains.

questions.q: Join an invented तत् + चूर्णम् (that powder) by the rule of तच्च. Which is right?
optionExplain: Right: Final त् becomes च् before च: तत् + चूर्णम् → तच्चूर्णम्.
त् does not stay before च; it takes the place of च.
त् → द् happens before voiced sounds; च is unvoiced.
त् → ज् happens before ज, not before च.
questions.explain: Same rule as तत् + च = तच्च in verse 14.
questions.teaches: Final त् becomes च् before च: तत् + च → तच्च; तत् + चूर्णम् → तच्चूर्णम्.

questions.q: Which three substances come with the prefix स- (with) in line 1 of verse 15?
optionExplain: Oil and kṣāra are not in this line.
Right: स-सर्पिः-मधु-सैन्धवः = with ghee, honey and rock salt.
Milk and sugar are not in this compound.
Oil and fat are not named here.
questions.explain: The bahuvrīhi ससर्पिर्मधुसैन्धवः lists ghee, honey, rock salt.
questions.rule: स- + सर्पिस् + मधु + सैन्धव = with ghee, honey, rock salt.

questions.q: Match each word of line 1 of verse 15 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words make up the first half of line 1.
questions.rule: स-पाद = with a quarter more; जाङ्गल = of dry land; सर्पिस् = ghee.

questions.q: Put these parts of line 1 in the order of verse 15.
questions.explain: First the juice, then the स- compound: ghee, honey, rock salt.
questions.teaches: Line 1 of verse 15 gives the jāṅgala juice, then ghee, honey and rock salt.

questions.q: Which split of ससर्पिर्मधु is right?
optionExplain: सर्प is 'snake' and इर्मधु is not a word.
सस and अर्पिः are not the words; the stem is सर्पिस् (ghee).
Right: -इः before a voiced sound (म) becomes -इर्: सर्पिः + मधु → सर्पिर्मधु.
धु is not a word; मधु (honey) is whole.
questions.explain: स- (with) + सर्पिः (ghee) + मधु (honey); the visarga turns to र्.

questions.q: Does verse 15 say what unit the sapāda (one and a quarter) counts?
options: Yes: one and a quarter prastha
Yes: one and a quarter pala
Yes: one and a quarter āḍhaka
No; the unit is not stated
optionExplain: No prastha is named in this verse.
No pala is named in this verse.
No āḍhaka is named in this verse.
Right: The card says what sapāda counts is not stated.
questions.explain: सपाद means 'with a quarter more', but no measure follows it.
questions.rule: सपाद = one and a quarter (of an unstated unit).

questions.q: Join the invented pair सर्पिः + दधि (ghee, curd) by the rule of ससर्पिर्मधु. Which is right?
optionExplain: Right: -इः before a voiced consonant (द) becomes -इर्.
स् stands before त/थ, which are unvoiced; द is voiced.
The visarga is not dropped after इ; it turns to र्.
ष् stands before ट/ठ, not before द.
questions.explain: Same rule as सर्पिः + मधु = सर्पिर्मधु.
questions.teaches: A visarga after इ becomes र् before a voiced consonant: सर्पिः + मधु → सर्पिर्मधु; सर्पिः + दधि → सर्पिर्दधि.

questions.q: Which four things does the warm enema of verse 16 increase?
options: Fat, blood, marrow and the semen too
Strength, voice, sleep and the skin
Flesh, fat, bone and also marrow
optionExplain: Fat, blood and marrow are not in this compound.
Right: मांस-अग्नि-बल-शुक्र-विवर्धनः.
Voice, sleep and skin are not named.
Only flesh of these is increased; fat (medas) is in line 2 among the disorders.
questions.explain: The compound ending in -विवर्धनः lists four: flesh, agni, strength, semen.
questions.rule: मांस · अग्नि · बल · शुक्र + विवर्धनः = increasing.

questions.q: Match each word of line 1 of verse 16 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words describe the enema in line 1.

questions.q: Put the four things increased in the order of verse 16.
questions.explain: The compound runs flesh, digestive fire, strength, semen, then -विवर्धनः.
questions.teaches: The warm enema increases flesh, agni, strength and semen, in that order.

questions.q: Which split of सुखोष्णो is right?
optionExplain: A visarga after अ before उ would be dropped: सुख उष्णः.
खोष्ण is not a word.
Right: अ + उ → ओ; -अः before the voiced म becomes -ओ.
म् before a vowel stays: सुखमुष्णः.
questions.explain: सुख (comfortably) + उष्ण (warm), joined with अ + उ → ओ.
questions.rule: अ + उ → ओ: सुख + उष्ण = सुखोष्ण.

questions.q: Which verb governs the disorders that start in line 2 of verse 16?
optionExplain: पचेत् governs the cooking, not the disorders.
पूजितः closes the earlier sentence of verse 11-12.
विवर्धनः governs flesh, agni, strength and semen.
Right: The card: line 2 begins the list of what it destroys (हन्यात्, 05.05.34).
questions.explain: Line 2 starts a list in the accusative that runs to हन्यात् in verse 18.
questions.rule: Disorders of 05.05.31-34 = objects of हन्यात् (it may destroy).

questions.q: Join an invented मधुर + उदकम् (sweet water) by the rule of सुखोष्ण. Which is right?
optionExplain: Right: अ + उ → ओ, as in सुख + उष्ण = सुखोष्ण.
अ + उ does not give ऊ.
The vowels join; they do not stand side by side.
औ comes from अ + ओ/औ, not from अ + उ.
questions.explain: अ + उ joins as ओ (guṇa).
questions.teaches: अ/आ + उ/ऊ → ओ: सुख + उष्ण → सुखोष्ण; मधुर + उदकम् → मधुरोदकम्.

questions.q: What does रुजः at the end of line 2 of verse 17 mean?
optionExplain: Swelling (शोफ) is in verse 18, not रुजः.
Right: रुजः = pains; it governs every body part before it.
No wound is named; रुजः means pains.
Fever is in line 1; रुजः means pains.
questions.explain: The compound ends in रुजः: pains of groin, thigh, waist and the rest.
questions.rule: X-Y-Z-रुजः = the pains of X, Y, Z.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 17 to its meaning on the card.
questions.explain: Clear words of the two lines.
questions.rule: आध्मान = bloating; प्रवाहिका = dysentery with straining; विषमज्वर = irregular fever; श्रोत्र = ear.

questions.q: Put these body parts in the order of line 2 of verse 17.
questions.explain: The pain compound opens groin, thigh, waist, flank.
questions.rule: वङ्क्षण · ऊरु · कटी · कुक्षि · … · श्रोत्र · शिरः + रुजः.
questions.teaches: The pain list of verse 17 opens with groin, thigh, waist and flank.

questions.q: Which split of वङ्क्षणोरु is right?
optionExplain: A visarga after अ before ऊ would be dropped: वङ्क्षण ऊरु.
रु is not a word; the thigh is ऊरु.
Right: अ + ऊ → ओ: वङ्क्षण (groin) + ऊरु (thigh).
Neither part is a word.
questions.explain: Inside the compound, अ + ऊ joins as ओ.
questions.rule: अ + ऊ → ओ: वङ्क्षण + ऊरु = वङ्क्षणोरु.

questions.q: Which body parts does line 2 of verse 17 name for pain?
optionExplain: No chest is named.
वङ्क्षण = groin.
कटी = waist, hip.
No eyes are named in verse 17.
The knee (जानु) is in verse 5, not here.
शिरः = head, in शिरोरुजः.
questions.explain: Groin, thigh, waist, flank, (nape), ear and head carry the pains.
questions.rule: वङ्क्षण · ऊरु · कटी · कुक्षि · (मन्या) · श्रोत्र · शिरः.

questions.q: शिरोरुजः joins शिरः + रुजः. Join an invented शिरः + वेदना (head pain) the same way. Which is right?
optionExplain: The visarga does not drop to bare -अ here.
र् replaces a visarga after vowels other than अ/आ.
स् stands before त/थ, not before व.
Right: -अः before a voiced consonant (व) becomes -ओ.
questions.explain: Same rule as शिरः + रुजः = शिरोरुजः.
questions.teaches: -अः becomes -ओ before a voiced consonant: शिरः + रुजः → शिरोरुजः; शिरः + वेदना → शिरोवेदना.

questions.q: What title does verse 18 give this enema among the yāpanas?
optionExplain: Right: राजा यापनानाम् = the king of the yāpanas.
Nirūhas are not named in this verse.
Oil enemas are not named here.
No purgative is named here.
questions.explain: यापनानाम् (genitive plural) depends on राजा: king of the yāpanas.
questions.rule: राजा यापनानाम् = king of the yāpanas.

questions.q: Match each word of line 2 of verse 18 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The four titles of the enema.
questions.rule: चक्षुष्य = good for the eyes; पुत्र-द = son-giving; रसायन = rejuvenative.

questions.q: Put the words of line 2 of verse 18 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Line 2: good for the eyes, giver of sons, king of the yāpanas, rasāyana.
questions.teaches: Verse 18 calls the enema चक्षुष्य, पुत्रद, king of the yāpanas and रसायन, in that order.

questions.q: What form is हन्यात्, as the card gives it?
optionExplain: The present would be हन्ति.
Right: √हन्, 3 sg optative: it would / may destroy.
The past participle would be हत.
The absolutive would be हत्वा.
questions.explain: -यात् marks the optative of √हन्.

questions.q: Which disorders does line 1 of verse 18 name, apart from its unclear last word?
optionExplain: No hiccup is named.
The eyes are praised in line 2; no eye disease is named.
कास = cough.
उन्माद = insanity.
असृग्दर (probable identification).
Worms (कृमि) are in verse 4.
questions.explain: Line 1: asṛgdara, unmāda, śopha, kāsa, then an unclear word.

questions.q: Like पुत्रदः (giver of sons), what does an invented बलदः mean (बल = strength)?
optionExplain: That would be बलज, with -ज (born).
That would be बलजित्, with -जित्.
Right: -द at the end of a compound means 'giving X'.
That would be बलवान्, with -वत्.
questions.explain: Same build as पुत्रद: X + -द = giving X.
questions.teaches: A compound ending in -द means 'giving X': पुत्रद (giving sons), बलद (giving strength).

questions.q: In what liquid is the pañcamūla of verse 19 cooked?
optionExplain: Water is the liquid of verse 14.
Cow's urine is the liquid of verse 10.
No meat juice is named in verse 19.
Right: क्षीराढके = in an āḍhaka of milk.
questions.explain: क्षीर-आढके: the roots are cooked in milk.
questions.rule: क्षीराढके विपचेत् = cook in an āḍhaka of milk.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 19 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words give the measure, the action and the added group.
questions.rule: पृथक् = separately; पल-अंश = portion of a pala; विपचेत् = one should cook.

questions.q: Put these words of line 2 in the order of verse 19.
questions.explain: Line 2: in an āḍhaka of milk, four prasthas, with the ground ones beginning with licorice, joined.
questions.teaches: Line 2 of verse 19 gives the milk, four prasthas, and the ground licorice group, in that order.

questions.q: Which split of यष्ट्यादिभिः is right?
optionExplain: Right: इ + आ → या: यष्टि (licorice) + आदिभिः (beginning with).
यष्ट्य is not a word; the stem is यष्टि.
A visarga after इ before a vowel would give यष्टिरादिभिः.
दिभिः is not a word; the second member is आदि.
questions.explain: Before a different vowel, इ becomes य्: यष्टि + आदि → यष्ट्यादि.

questions.q: How does verse 19 measure the roots of its pañcamūla?
optionExplain: No total of two palas is given; the text says separately.
Right: पृथक्पलांशम् = separately, in portions of a pala.
No prasṛta is named; the roots are taken separately.
The measure is the pala, a weight.
questions.explain: पृथक् (separately) + पल-अंश (pala portion).

questions.q: Like चतुःप्रस्थम् (four prasthas), what does an invented त्रिप्रस्थम् mean?
optionExplain: The third would be तृतीय प्रस्थ.
A third would be प्रस्थ-त्रिभाग.
Right: Number + measure (dvigu) = that many of the measure.
No cooking is in the word.
questions.explain: Same build as चतुःप्रस्थ and द्विप्रस्थ (verse 14): number + measure.
questions.teaches: A number joined to a measure counts that measure: चतुःप्रस्थम् (four prasthas), त्रिप्रस्थम् (three prasthas).

questions.q: For whom especially does verse 20 esteem this enema?
options: People with a strong digestive fire
Children, the old, women, the delicate
optionExplain: None of these is named in the verse.
No digestive fire is named in verse 20.
No king or minister is named here.
Right: बाल-वृद्ध-स्त्री-सुकुमार-सुखात्मनाम्.
questions.explain: The genitive compound lists children, the old, women, the delicate, the comfort-natured.

questions.q: Match each word of line 2 of verse 20 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four of the five groups of line 2.
questions.rule: बाल = child; वृद्ध = old; स्त्री = woman; सुकुमार = delicate.

questions.q: Put these groups in the order of line 2 of verse 20.
questions.explain: Children, the old, women, the delicate, the comfort-natured.
questions.teaches: Verse 20 names, in order, children, the old, women, the delicate and those of comfortable nature.

questions.q: Which case is सुखात्मनाम्, and how does the card render it?
optionExplain: Right: -नाम् is the genitive plural; the data renders it 'for'.
The locative plural would end in -सु.
The instrumental plural would end in -भिः.
The accusative plural would be -आत्मनः.
questions.explain: The whole compound stands in the genitive plural: for (of) these people.

questions.q: What does विशेषात् add to the praise in verse 20?
optionExplain: The card: 'especially', not 'only'.
Right: विशेषात् = especially; it stresses, it does not exclude.
No exception is stated.
No feeding or time is named.
questions.explain: The enema is esteemed for all; these groups are stressed.

questions.q: सुखात्मन् joins सुख + आत्मन्. Join an invented हित + आहार (wholesome food) the same way. Which is right?
optionExplain: The long आ of आहार does not vanish.
ए comes from अ + इ, not from अ + आ.
Right: अ + आ → आ, as in सुख + आत्मन् = सुखात्मन्.
औ comes from अ + ओ/औ, not from अ + आ.
questions.explain: Like vowels join long: अ + आ → आ.
questions.teaches: अ + आ joins as आ: सुख + आत्मन् → सुखात्मन्; हित + आहार → हिताहार.

questions.q: What kind of enema does line 2 of verse 21 name?
optionExplain: Cow's urine is in verse 10, not here.
No meat juice is named in verse 21.
No oil enema is named here.
Right: क्षीरबस्तिः = milk enema.
questions.explain: क्षीर (milk) + बस्ति (enema): the kṣīrabasti.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 21 to its meaning on the card.
questions.explain: Two structure words and two plants (standard identifications).
questions.rule: तद्वत् = likewise; साधित = prepared; गुडूची = giloy; सारिवा = Indian sarsaparilla.

questions.q: Put the plants of the milk enema in the order of line 2 of verse 21.
questions.explain: Line 2: abhīru, guḍūcī, the pair of bṛhatī.
questions.teaches: The milk enema of verse 21 takes abhīru, guḍūcī and the bṛhatī pair, in that order.

questions.q: Which split of क्षीरबस्तिस्तथा is right?
optionExplain: Right: A visarga before त becomes स्: बस्तिः + तथा → बस्तिस्तथा.
स्तथा is not a word; the स् comes from the visarga.
म् before त would give क्षीरबस्तिं तथा.
अथा is not a word; the word is तथा (likewise).
questions.explain: क्षीरबस्तिः (nom.) + तथा (likewise).

questions.q: What does बृहतीद्वय mean on the card?
options: Two palas of the bṛhatī root, weighed
A pair of bṛhatī; the second is unnamed
Bṛhatī root cooked down twice in milk
Bṛhatī joined with guḍūcī as one drug
optionExplain: द्वय counts plants, not palas.
Right: द्वय = pair; the usual partner kaṇṭakārī is probable, not named.
No cooking is in the word.
Guḍūcī is a separate member of the list.
questions.explain: -द्वय = a pair; the text does not name the second plant.

questions.q: Like बृहतीद्वय (the pair of bṛhatī), what does an invented पञ्चमूलद्वयम् mean?
optionExplain: The second would be द्वितीय पञ्चमूल.
Half would be अर्ध-पञ्चमूल.
Right: -द्वय after a noun names a pair of that thing.
The pair is of whole groups, not of roots.
questions.explain: Same build as बृहतीद्वय: X + द्वय = the pair of X.
questions.teaches: -द्वय after a noun means 'the pair of X': बृहतीद्वय, पञ्चमूलद्वयम्.

questions.q: With the paste of which two drugs is the milk of verse 22 cooked?
optionExplain: These are in verse 21.
Neither is named in verse 22.
Neither is named in verse 22.
Right: मागधिका-यष्टीमधुक-कल्कवत्.
questions.explain: The paste is of māgadhikā (long pepper) and yaṣṭīmadhuka (licorice).
questions.rule: मागधिका = long pepper; यष्टीमधुक = licorice; कल्क = paste.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 22 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The two drugs, the paste and the measure.
questions.rule: मागधिका = long pepper; यष्टीमधुक = licorice; कल्क = paste; पल-उन्मित = measured by a pala.

questions.q: Put these words of line 1 in the order of verse 22.
questions.explain: Line 1: cooked, milk, long pepper, licorice, having the paste.
questions.teaches: Verse 22 opens 'cooked milk' and then names the paste of long pepper and licorice.

questions.q: Which split of पलोन्मितम् is right?
optionExplain: Right: अ + उ → ओ: पल + उन्मित (measured).
न्मितम् is not a word.
A visarga after अ before उ would be dropped: पल उन्मितम्.
म् before a vowel stays: पलमुन्मितम्.
questions.explain: Inside the compound, पल + उन्मित joins as पलोन्मित.

questions.q: Which pañcamūla does line 2 of verse 22 name?
options: The one with castor at its head
optionExplain: Bilva is not named in verse 22.
Right: बृहत्यादि पञ्चमूलम् = the pañcamūla headed by bṛhatī.
Musta heads the list of verse 12.
Castor is not named in verse 22.
questions.explain: बृहती-आदि = beginning with bṛhatī; the members are not listed.

questions.q: Like प्रतिद्रव्यम् (for each drug), what does an invented प्रतिदिनम् mean?
optionExplain: प्रति here distributes; it does not oppose.
Before would be प्राक्.
Right: प्रति- before a noun (avyayībhāva) = for each, every.
प्रति- means each one, not one only.
questions.explain: Same build as प्रतिद्रव्यम्: प्रति + noun = each / every.
questions.teaches: प्रति- before a noun as an indeclinable compound means 'for each': प्रतिद्रव्यम् (each drug), प्रतिदिनम् (every day).

questions.q: Which milk is cooked with the grains in verse 23?
optionExplain: The verse says छागल, of a goat.
No buffalo is named in the verse.
No sheep is named in the verse.
Right: छागलं क्षीरम् = goat's milk.
questions.explain: छागल = of a goat; क्षीर = milk.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 23 to its meaning on the card.
questions.explain: Three grains of line 1 and the sugar of line 2.
questions.rule: शालि = winter rice; गोधूम = wheat; माष = black gram; सिता = crystallised sugar.

questions.q: Put the grains in the order of line 1 of verse 23.
questions.explain: Line 1: śāli rice, wheat, barley, black gram, then सयष्टिकम्.
questions.rule: द्विपलं · शालि · गोधूम · यव · माषं · सयष्टिकम्.
questions.teaches: The grains of verse 23 are śāli rice, wheat, barley and black gram, in that order.

questions.q: What does तैः in तैः सिद्धम् point to, on the card?
options: The grains and drugs named before it
The two salts that follow later on
The egg fluid named after the milk
The children and women of verse 20
optionExplain: Right: तैः = by those: the ingredients just listed.
The salts come in verse 24, after this.
The egg fluid follows; तैः looks back.
Those people are not ingredients.
questions.explain: तैः is instrumental plural: the milk is cooked with those ingredients.
questions.rule: तैः = with / by those (instrumental plural of तद्).

questions.q: Does verse 23 say whether the two palas are for each grain?
options: Yes; two palas of rice only
optionExplain: The text gives no 'each'.
Right: The card: each grain or all together is not decided.
The text does not say 'in total' either.
द्विपलम् stands before the whole list.
questions.explain: द्विपलम् is given once; its scope is not stated.

questions.q: Which invented phrase means cooked with those drugs, built like तैः सिद्धम्?
optionExplain: This is the locative: cooked in those drugs.
This is the genitive: cooked of those drugs.
Right: तैः and द्रव्यैः are both instrumental plural: with those drugs.
This is the accusative, not 'with'.
questions.explain: The instrumental gives 'with / by': तैः, द्रव्यैः.
questions.rule: तैः = instrumental plural of तद्: with those.
questions.teaches: तैः (with those) is the instrumental plural of तद्, and its noun takes the same case: तैर्द्रव्यैः सिद्धम्.

questions.q: What does verse 24 say the enema makes, supremely?
optionExplain: Neither is named in verse 24.
Sleep is not named in verse 24.
The eyes are praised in verse 18, not here.
Right: शुक्रकृत् = maker of semen; परम् = supremely.
questions.explain: शुक्र + -कृत् (making) = maker of semen.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 24 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Two additives, the effect and the word for the formula.
questions.rule: आज्य = ghee; क्षौद्र = honey; शुक्रकृत् = maker of semen; कल्प = formula.

questions.q: Put these words of line 1 in the order of verse 24.
questions.explain: Line 1: with ghee, honey, two salts; by those; the enema; maker of semen; supremely.
questions.teaches: Line 1 of verse 24 runs: additives, तैः, बस्तिः, शुक्रकृत्, परम्.

questions.q: Which split of the end of मत्स्याद्यण्डरसेष्वपि is right?
optionExplain: Right: उ + अ → व: रसेषु (in the fluids) + अपि (also).
रसेष्व is not a form; the locative plural is रसेषु.
वपि is not a word; the word is अपि.
रसेषः is not a form of रस.
questions.explain: Before a different vowel, उ becomes व्: रसेषु + अपि → रसेष्वपि.

questions.q: Where else does verse 24 say this formula (kalpa) holds?
options: In the juice of dry-land animals
In the egg fluids of other creatures
In the milk of goats, sheep and cows
In decoctions of cow's urine and roots
optionExplain: Jāṅgala juice is in verse 15, not here.
Right: मत्स्याद्यण्डरसेषु अपि = also in egg fluids of fish and the like.
Goat's milk is in verse 23; no extension to milks is made.
No cow's urine is named in verse 24.
questions.explain: Line 2 extends the formula to egg fluids (peacock, gonarda, fish and the like).
questions.rule: कल्पो ऽयं … अण्डरसेषु अपि = this formula also in egg fluids.

questions.q: कल्पो ऽयम् joins कल्पः + अयम्. Join an invented योगः + अयम् (this formula) the same way. Which is right?
optionExplain: अ + अ → आ applies to bare vowels, not to -अः.
र् replaces a visarga after vowels other than अ/आ.
Right: -अः + अ → -ओ ऽ: the अ of अयम् is elided (avagraha).
The visarga does not vanish without a trace here.
questions.explain: Same rule as कल्पः + अयम् = कल्पोऽयम्.
questions.teaches: -अः before अ becomes -ओ and the अ is elided (ऽ): कल्पः + अयम् → कल्पोऽयम्; योगः + अयम् → योगोऽयम्.

questions.q: Whose flesh gives the juice in verse 25?
optionExplain: Goat testes come in verse 26.
The peacock's eggs are in verse 24.
Fish eggs are in verse 24.
Right: रसः कुलीरमांसस्य = the juice of crab flesh.
questions.explain: कुलीर = crab; मांस = flesh; रस = juice.
questions.rule: कुलीरमांसस्य रसः = juice of crab flesh.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 25 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Two creatures, an additive and the closing word.
questions.rule: कुलीर = crab; चटक = sparrow; शर्करा = sugar; मत = considered.

questions.q: Put these words in the order of verse 25.
questions.explain: The juice, of crab flesh, joined with sparrow-egg fluid; then the enema, most aphrodisiac, considered.
questions.rule: रसः · कुलीरमांसस्य · चटकाण्डरसान्वितः ‖ … बस्तिर् · वृषतमो · मतः.
questions.teaches: Verse 25 names the crab juice and the sparrow-egg fluid, then calls the enema वृषतम.

questions.q: What does the suffix -तम add in वृषतमः?
optionExplain: Right: -तम marks the superlative: most bull-like, most aphrodisiac.
The comparative suffix is -तर.
Likeness is -वत् or इव.
Negation is अ- / न-, before the word.
questions.explain: वृष (bull) + -तम (most) = most bull-like.

questions.q: In verse 25, what is the crab juice joined with?
options: The fluid of a fowl's egg
optionExplain: The fowl's egg is in verse 23.
Right: चटक-अण्ड-रस-अन्वितः = joined with sparrow-egg fluid.
Goat's milk is in verse 23.
Peacock eggs are in verse 24.
questions.explain: Line 1 joins crab juice with sparrow-egg fluid; line 2 adds sugar, ghee, honey.

questions.q: Beside वृषतमः (most aphrodisiac), which form means more aphrodisiac (the comparative)?
optionExplain: -वत् means 'like' (like a bull).
-त्व makes an abstract noun: bull-ness.
Right: -तर marks the comparative: more.
This is the superlative of the verse: most.
questions.explain: -तर (more) and -तम (most) build the comparison of adjectives.
questions.teaches: -तर marks the comparative and -तम the superlative: वृषतरः (more), वृषतमः (most aphrodisiac).

questions.q: What is cooked (सिद्धम्) in line 2 of verse 26?
optionExplain: The meat is in line 1; line 2 cooks milk.
Ghee is not named in verse 26.
Cow's urine is not named here.
Right: सिद्धं पयः = cooked milk.
questions.explain: सिद्धम् agrees with पयः: milk, cooked.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 26 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Words of the animal items and the last additive.
questions.rule: मुष्क = testis; बस्त = he-goat; आमिष = flesh; मधु = honey.

questions.q: Put the items with the milk in the order of line 2 of verse 26.
questions.explain: Line 2: he-goat's testis, uccaṭā, ikṣuraka, honey.
questions.rule: सिद्धं पयो · बस्तमुष्क · उच्चटा · इक्षुरकं · मधु.
questions.teaches: The milk of verse 26 goes with he-goat's testis, uccaṭā, ikṣuraka and honey, in that order.

questions.q: Which split of उच्चटेक्षुरकम् is right?
optionExplain: Right: आ + इ → ए: उच्चटा + इक्षुरक.
एक्षुरक is not a word, and अ + ए would give ऐ.
-आः before a vowel drops the visarga with no join.
म् before a vowel stays: उच्चटमिक्षुरकम्.
questions.explain: आ/अ + इ joins as ए.

questions.q: Whose flesh (आमिष) does line 1 of verse 26 name?
optionExplain: The goat gives testes here; no fowl is named.
Right: कुलीर-चटक-आमिषैः = with the flesh of crab and sparrow.
These are in verse 24.
Neither is named in verse 26.
questions.explain: The second word of line 1 names crab and sparrow flesh.
questions.rule: कुलीरचटकामिषैः = with crab and sparrow flesh.

questions.q: Join an invented शर्करा + इक्षु (sugar, sugarcane) by the rule of उच्चटेक्षुरक. Which is right?
optionExplain: ऐ comes from अ/आ + ए/ऐ, not + इ.
The इ does not vanish.
Right: आ + इ → ए, as in उच्चटा + इक्षुरक.
आ + इ does not give ई.
questions.explain: आ + इ joins as ए (guṇa).
questions.teaches: अ/आ + इ/ई → ए: उच्चटा + इक्षुरक → उच्चटेक्षुरक; शर्करा + इक्षु → शर्करेक्षु.

questions.q: With which plants is the milk of line 2 of verse 27 cooked?
optionExplain: These open the list of verse 12.
These are in verse 21.
These make the paste of verse 22.
Right: आत्मगुप्ता-उच्चटा-इक्षुरैः.
questions.explain: The milk is cooked with cowhage, uccaṭā and ikṣura.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 27 to its meaning.
questions.explain: A plant, the food, the milk and the praise word.
questions.rule: आत्मगुप्ता = cowhage; भोज्य = food; पयस् = milk; पर = supreme.

questions.q: Put these words of line 2 in the order of verse 27.
questions.explain: Line 2: with cooked milk, food, then the three plants.
questions.rule: सिद्धेन · पयसा · भोज्यम् · आत्मगुप्ता · उच्चटा · इक्षुरैः.
questions.teaches: Line 2 of verse 27 runs: with cooked milk, food, cowhage, uccaṭā, ikṣura.

questions.q: What form is भोज्यम्, as the card gives it?
options: A gerundive: to be eaten, food
optionExplain: Right: √भुज् + -य: what is to be eaten, food.
The past participle would be भुक्त.
The absolutive would be भुक्त्वा.
The present would be भुङ्क्ते.
questions.explain: -य after the root makes a gerundive: to be eaten.

questions.q: With what is the food of verse 27 taken?
options: With the juice of crab flesh and sugar
With milk cooked with the plants
With ghee and the two unnamed salts
With a decoction made in cow's urine
optionExplain: Crab juice is in verse 25.
Right: सिद्धेन पयसा = with the cooked milk.
These are in verse 24.
No cow's urine is named.
questions.explain: The instrumental सिद्धेन पयसा gives 'with cooked milk'.
questions.rule: सिद्धेन पयसा भोज्यम् = food with cooked milk.

questions.q: Like सिद्धेन पयसा (with cooked milk), which invented phrase means with cooked ghee (घृत)?
optionExplain: सिद्धम् is nominative / accusative; it must agree with घृतेन.
घृतम् is not instrumental; 'with' needs घृतेन.
Right: Adjective and noun both in the instrumental singular.
सिद्धस्य is genitive; it does not agree.
questions.explain: An adjective takes the case of its noun: सिद्धेन पयसा, सिद्धेन घृतेन.
questions.rule: Adjective agrees with its noun in case, number, gender.
questions.teaches: An adjective agrees with its noun: सिद्धेन पयसा (with cooked milk), सिद्धेन घृतेन (with cooked ghee).

questions.q: Which word of verse 28 gives the timing of the enemas?
optionExplain: This is 'a hundred women', the result.
This is the verb 'uses'.
This is 'nourished'.
Right: दश-दश-अहेन = by ten-ten days.
questions.explain: Line 1 gives the timing: दशदशाहेन.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 28 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The comparison and the result.
questions.rule: वाजी = stallion; इव = like; पुष्ट = nourished; प्रमदा = woman.

questions.q: Put these words of line 1 in the order of verse 28.
questions.explain: Line 1: thereafter, at ten-ten days, he who, the enemas, uses.
questions.teaches: Line 1 of verse 28 runs अतः, दशदशाहेन, यः तु, बस्तीन्, निषेवते.

questions.q: Which split of बस्तीन्निषेवते is right?
optionExplain: Right: बस्तीन् (the enemas, acc. pl.) + निषेवते (uses).
न्निषेवते is not a word.
That would be singular and stay two words: बस्तिं निषेवते.
न 'not' would deny the use the verse promises.
questions.explain: The accusative plural बस्तीन् is the object of निषेवते.
questions.rule: -ईन् = masculine accusative plural of an -इ stem.

questions.q: In verse 28, who goes to a hundred women?
options: The man who uses these enemas
optionExplain: No physician is named.
Right: यस्तु बस्तीन्निषेवते … गच्छति: he who uses them.
The stallion is only the comparison (इव).
That is a title of the enema in verse 18.
questions.explain: यः (who) in line 1 is the subject of गच्छति in line 2.
questions.rule: यः … निषेवते … गच्छति = he who uses … goes.

questions.q: वाजीव joins वाजी + इव. Join an invented नदी + इव (like a river) the same way. Which is right?
optionExplain: ई → य् happens before an unlike vowel, not before इ.
ए comes from अ + इ, not from ई + इ.
Right: ई + इ → ई: like vowels join long.
No य् is inserted between like vowels.
questions.explain: Same rule as वाजी + इव = वाजीव.
questions.teaches: Like vowels join long: वाजी + इव → वाजीव; नदी + इव → नदीव.

questions.q: With what are these preparations joined in verse 29?
optionExplain: No salt is named in verse 29.
No urine is named in verse 29.
No ghee is named in verse 29.
Right: माक्षिकसंयुक्ताः = joined with honey.
questions.explain: माक्षिक = bee-honey in this context.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 29 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The additive, the effect and the pair of opposites.
questions.rule: माक्षिक = honey; अतिवृष = exceedingly potent; अतियोग = excess; अयोग = lack.

questions.q: Put the words of line 1 in the order of verse 29.
questions.explain: Line 1: these, joined with honey, make, exceedingly potent, a man.
questions.teaches: Line 1 of verse 29 runs एते, माक्षिकसंयुक्ताः, कुर्वन्ति, अतिवृषम्, नरम्.

questions.q: Which split of नातियोगम् is right?
optionExplain: Right: अ + अ → आ: न (not) + अतियोगम् (excess).
A visarga after अ before अ would give नोऽतियोगम्.
आतियोग is not a word; the word is अतियोग.
Neither part is a word.
questions.explain: न + अतियोगम् join with अ + अ → आ.
questions.rule: अ + अ → आ: न + अतियोगम् = नातियोगम्.

questions.q: What does line 2 of verse 29 say is brought about?
optionExplain: Each is denied with न.
Right: नातियोगं न चायोगम् = neither atiyoga nor ayoga.
Atiyoga is denied too.
Ayoga is denied too.
questions.explain: Two negatives: न अतियोगम्, न च अयोगम्.

questions.q: कुर्वन्त्यतिवृषम् joins कुर्वन्ति + अतिवृषम्. Join an invented भवन्ति + अत्र (they are here) the same way. Which is right?
optionExplain: ई would need इ + इ; the next vowel is अ.
ए comes from अ + इ, not from इ + अ.
Right: इ before an unlike vowel becomes य्.
The इ itself becomes य्; no य् is added after it.
questions.explain: Same rule as कुर्वन्ति + अतिवृषम् = कुर्वन्त्यतिवृषम्.
questions.teaches: इ/ई before an unlike vowel becomes य्: कुर्वन्ति + अति → कुर्वन्त्यति; भवन्ति + अत्र → भवन्त्यत्र.

questions.q: What does verse 30 say nirūha enemas are?
optionExplain: Nourishing (bṛṃhaṇa) is said of the sneha enemas.
Kindling comes in verse 33, as a treatment, not here.
Checking is not said of nirūha in verse 30.
Right: निरूहा लेखनाः = nirūha enemas are scraping (lekhana).
questions.explain: Line 1 pairs nirūha with lekhana and sneha-basti with bṛṃhaṇa.
questions.section: यापन का अतियोग और परिहार-रहित प्रयोग

questions.q: Match each word of verse 30 to its meaning on the card.
questions.explain: Two effects, the word that softens them, and the verdict on anuvāsana.
questions.rule: लेखन = scraping; बृंहण = nourishing; प्रायः = mostly; न इष्टम् = not desired.
questions.section: यापन का अतियोग और परिहार-रहित प्रयोग

questions.q: Put the phrases of verse 30 in their order.
questions.explain: Two kinds, then yāpana having both, then the conclusion with तस्मात्.
questions.rule: निरूह लेखन · स्नेहबस्ति बृंहण · यापन में दोनों · इसलिए अनुवासन नहीं.
questions.teaches: Verse 30 argues in steps: nirūha scrapes, sneha nourishes, yāpana has both, therefore no anuvāsana in yāpana.
questions.section: यापन का अतियोग और परिहार-रहित प्रयोग

questions.q: Which split of यापनेषूभयं is right?
optionExplain: Right: उ + उ → ऊ: यापनेषु (in the yāpana) + उभयम् (both).
उ + अ would give व: यापनेष्वभयम्, not ऊ.
यापनेषू is no form; the locative plural ends in -एषु.
षूभयम् is not a word; the ending -षु belongs to यापनेषु.
questions.explain: The long ऊ comes from two short उ: -एषु + उभयम्.
questions.rule: उ + उ → ऊ: यापनेषु + उभयम् = यापनेषूभयम्.
questions.section: यापन का अतियोग और परिहार-रहित प्रयोग

questions.q: Why, by verse 30, is anuvāsana not desired in the yāpana enemas?
optionExplain: Sharpness is not the reason the verse gives.
Right: यापनेषूभयं तस्मात्: there is both in yāpana; therefore not.
The verse says nothing about the patient here.
No season is named in verse 30.
questions.explain: तस्मात् (therefore) ties the verdict to the line before it: in yāpana there is both.
questions.rule: उभयम् … तस्मात् न इष्टम् = both are there, hence not desired.
questions.section: यापन का अतियोग और परिहार-रहित प्रयोग

questions.q: Like नेष्टम् (न + इष्टम्), how do न + इच्छति (wishes) join?
optionExplain: ऐ comes from अ + ए, not from अ + इ.
अ + इ does not give ई; the guṇa vowel is ए.
Right: अ + इ → ए: न + इच्छति = नेच्छति, as न + इष्टम् = नेष्टम्.
No य is inserted; the two vowels merge to ए.
questions.explain: अ + इ → ए is the same join as in नेष्टम्.
questions.teaches: अ + इ joins to ए: न + इष्टम् = नेष्टम्, न + इच्छति = नेच्छति.
questions.section: यापन का अतियोग और परिहार-रहित प्रयोग

questions.q: Why might the enemas of verse 31 not return?
optionExplain: Sharp enemas are the remedy in line 2, not the cause.
Urine goes into the remedy enemas, not the cause.
Warmth is not named in verse 31.
Right: मृदुत्वात् = because of mildness (ablative of cause).
questions.explain: The ablative मृदुत्वात् gives the reason: mildness.
questions.rule: मृदुत्वात् न निवर्तेरन् = they may not return because of mildness.
questions.section: यापन का अतियोग और परिहार-रहित प्रयोग

questions.q: Match each word of verse 31 to its meaning on the card.
questions.explain: The cause in line 1 and the features of the remedy in line 2.
questions.rule: मृदुत्वात् = from mildness; समूत्र = with urine; तीक्ष्ण = sharp; क्षिप्रम् = quickly.
questions.section: यापन का अतियोग और परिहार-रहित प्रयोग

questions.q: Put the phrases of verse 31 in their order.
questions.explain: First the trouble (not returning), the person, then the sharp urine enemas and the āsthāpana.
questions.rule: न निवर्तेरन् · यस्य प्रयोजिताः · समूत्रैः तीक्ष्णैः · आस्थाप्य क्षिप्रम्.
questions.teaches: Verse 31 states the trouble first (mild enemas not returning) and then the remedy: a sharp āsthāpana with urine.
questions.section: यापन का अतियोग और परिहार-रहित प्रयोग

questions.q: With which enemas is the āsthāpana given in line 2 of verse 31?
optionExplain: Right: समूत्रैः बस्तिभिः तीक्ष्णैः = with sharp enemas with urine.
Mildness is the trouble; milk is not named here.
No oil or ghee is named in verse 31.
Honey is not named; the remedy is sharp, not mild.
questions.explain: The remedy is the opposite of the cause: sharp against mild.
questions.section: यापन का अतियोग और परिहार-रहित प्रयोग

questions.q: Does verse 31 itself say what then happens to him (सः)?
options: No; the line has no main verb
Yes; he gets an anuvāsana next
Yes; he must fast for a day
optionExplain: No recovery is stated in verse 31.
Right: The card: the verb is missing, the sentence continues or is lost.
No anuvāsana is prescribed in this verse.
No fasting is named in verse 31.
questions.explain: सः stands without a verb; build nothing on the missing clause.
questions.rule: An absolutive (आस्थाप्य) needs a main verb, which this unit lacks.
questions.section: यापन का अतियोग और परिहार-रहित प्रयोग

questions.q: Like आस्थाप्य (prefix आ- with -य), which invented form means having come, from आ + √गम्?
optionExplain: -त्वा is used without a prefix; with आ- the form takes -य.
This is a future verb, 'will come', not 'having come'.
Right: With a prefix the absolutive takes -य: आ + गम् + य = आगम्य.
This is a present verb, 'comes', not an absolutive.
questions.explain: Prefix + root takes -य (आस्थाप्य, आगम्य); a bare root takes -त्वा.
questions.teaches: With a prefix the absolutive ends in -य (आस्थाप्य, आगम्य); without one it ends in -त्वा.
questions.section: यापन का अतियोग और परिहार-रहित प्रयोग

questions.q: From what does verse 32 say these troubles arise?
optionExplain: अत्यर्थ means excessive, not too little.
Those are the remedy of verse 31, not this cause.
Verse 30 calls that undesired but names no troubles.
Right: यापनात्यर्थसेवनात् = from excessive use of yāpana.
questions.explain: The ablative at the end of the verse gives the cause.
questions.rule: यापना-अत्यर्थ-सेवनात् = from excessive use of yāpana.
questions.section: यापन का अतियोग और परिहार-रहित प्रयोग

questions.q: Match each trouble of verse 32 to its meaning on the card.
questions.explain: Four of the troubles, with the senses the data gives.
questions.rule: शोफ = swelling; अग्निनाश = loss of agni; परिकर्तिका = cutting pain; अतिसार = diarrhoea.
questions.section: यापन का अतियोग और परिहार-रहित प्रयोग

questions.q: Put these troubles in the order of verse 32.
questions.explain: Line 1 runs śopha, agni-nāśa, (pallor), śūla, (arśas), parikartikā; line 2 adds fever and diarrhoea.
questions.rule: शोफ · अग्निनाश · पाण्डुत्व · शूल · अर्शः · परिकर्तिका ‖ ज्वर · अतिसार.
questions.teaches: Excess of yāpana: śopha, agni-nāśa, pallor, śūla, arśas, parikartikā, then fever and diarrhoea.
questions.section: यापन का अतियोग और परिहार-रहित प्रयोग

questions.q: Which of these does verse 32 name as results of excessive yāpana?
optionExplain: Cough is not in verse 32.
Named first in line 1.
Named in line 2: अतिसारश्च.
Named in line 2: ज्वरश्च.
Vomiting is not in verse 32.
questions.explain: Only items printed in the verse count: śopha, fever and diarrhoea are; cough and vomiting are not.
questions.rule: Count as listed only what the verse names.
questions.section: यापन का अतियोग और परिहार-रहित प्रयोग

questions.q: Which split of ज्वरश्चातिसारश्च is right?
optionExplain: Right: ः → श् before च; च + अ → चा: fever and diarrhoea.
चाति is not a word; च joins with अतिसार.
आतिसार is not a word; the noun is अतिसार.
The noun is the one word अतिसार, not अति + सार here.
questions.explain: Visarga before च becomes श्; च + अतिसारः gives चातिसारः.
questions.rule: ज्वरः च → ज्वरश्च; च + अतिसारः → चातिसारः.
questions.section: यापन का अतियोग और परिहार-रहित प्रयोग

questions.q: With the same ending as सेवनात् (from use), which invented form says from excessive eating?
optionExplain: -ए is the locative, 'in eating'.
Right: -आत् is the ablative, 'from', as in सेवनात्.
-अस्य is the genitive, 'of eating'.
-अम् is nominative or accusative, not 'from'.
questions.explain: The ablative -आत् names the cause: from excessive use, from excessive eating.
questions.teaches: The ablative -आत् names a cause: यापनात्यर्थसेवनात् (from excessive use of yāpana), अत्यर्थभोजनात् (from excessive eating).
questions.section: यापन का अतियोग और परिहार-रहित प्रयोग

questions.q: What kind of treatment does verse 33 say is desired in that case?
optionExplain: Lekhana is said of nirūha in verse 30.
Bṛṃhaṇa is said of sneha enemas in verse 30.
Right: दीपनी क्रिया = a treatment kindling the digestive fire.
That is the remedy of verse 31, a different trouble.
questions.explain: After loss of the digestive fire, the treatment kindles it.
questions.section: यापन का अतियोग और परिहार-रहित प्रयोग

questions.q: Match each word of verse 33 to its meaning on the card.
questions.explain: Two drinks, the kind of treatment, and the manner of using yāpana.
questions.rule: अरिष्ट, सीधु = fermented drinks; दीपनी = kindling; युक्त्या = with judgement.
questions.section: यापन का अतियोग और परिहार-रहित प्रयोग

questions.q: Put the phrases of verse 33 in their order.
questions.explain: The means, the treatment, then the advice on using yāpana.
questions.rule: अरिष्ट-क्षार-सीधु आदि · दीपनी क्रिया इष्ट · युक्ति से सेवन · यापन भी.
questions.teaches: Verse 33 first names the kindling treatment (ariṣṭa, kṣāra, sīdhu) and then says to use yāpana with judgement.
questions.section: यापन का अतियोग और परिहार-रहित प्रयोग

questions.q: To what does तत्र (in that case) refer in verse 33, by the card?
options: The enemas that do not return
optionExplain: That case had its own remedy in verse 31.
Verse 30 only calls that undesired.
No decoction is being cooked in these lines.
Right: The card: tatra refers to the troubles of 05.05.62-63.
questions.explain: The kindling treatment answers loss of agni and the other troubles just listed.
questions.rule: तत्र = in that case (the troubles of verse 32).
questions.section: यापन का अतियोग और परिहार-रहित प्रयोग

questions.q: Which split of सीध्वाद्यैः is right?
optionExplain: Right: उ + आ → वा: सीधु + आद्यैः = सीध्वाद्यैः.
A visarga after उ before a vowel gives र्: सीधुराद्यैः.
उ + अ gives व, so the result would be सीध्वद्यैः.
सीध्वा is no form; the drink's stem is सीधु.
questions.explain: The long आ after व् shows the second word begins with आ: आद्यैः.
questions.section: यापन का अतियोग और परिहार-रहित प्रयोग

questions.q: Like अरिष्टक्षारसीध्वाद्यैः, what does an invented घृततैलाद्यैः mean?
options: Without any ghee and without oil
With ghee, oil and so forth
The first of ghee and oil
optionExplain: Nothing in -आद्यैः negates; it adds 'and so forth'.
Right: -आद्यैः = with X and the rest, as in verse 33.
-आद्य is 'and the rest', not 'before'.
आदि here means 'and so forth', not 'first part'.
questions.explain: -आद्यैः (instrumental plural) closes a list: with these and the like.
questions.rule: X-आद्यैः = with X and so forth.
questions.teaches: -आद्यैः closes an open list in the instrumental: with ariṣṭa, kṣāra, sīdhu and so forth; with ghee, oil and so forth.
questions.section: यापन का अतियोग और परिहार-रहित प्रयोग

questions.q: What does verse 34 say there is in the yāpana enemas?
options: A risk of fever and swelling
optionExplain: The word is निः-परिहार: without avoidance.
No anuvāsana is named in verse 34.
Right: निष्परिहारता = absence of avoidance, no restrictions.
Those come from excess, in verse 32.
questions.explain: निः (without) + परिहार (avoidance) + ता (-ness).
questions.section: यापन का अतियोग और परिहार-रहित प्रयोग

questions.q: Put the three reasons of verse 34 in their order.
questions.explain: Drug, quantity, then time: each reason in the ablative.
questions.section: यापन का अतियोग और परिहार-रहित प्रयोग

questions.q: Match each word of verse 34 to its meaning on the card.
questions.explain: The parts of the three reasons and the key noun.
questions.rule: पाद = quarter; हीन = reduced; अल्पकाल = short time; परिहार = avoidance.
questions.teaches: पादहीन = reduced by a quarter; अल्पकाल = short time; परिहार = avoidance (of food, regimen).
questions.section: यापन का अतियोग और परिहार-रहित प्रयोग

questions.q: What does पादहीनप्रमाणतः mean on the card?
options: A quantity more by a quarter
A quantity less by a quarter
optionExplain: That would leave a quarter; हीन says a quarter is taken off.
हीन means reduced, not increased.
पाद here is one quarter, not the foot.
Right: पाद (quarter) + हीन (reduced): three quarters remain.
questions.explain: X-हीन = lacking X: the quantity lacks a quarter.
questions.section: यापन का अतियोग और परिहार-रहित प्रयोग

questions.q: Does verse 34 list which restrictions (परिहार) are dropped?
options: No; it does not list them
optionExplain: Right: The card: the text does not list the restrictions.
No such list is in verse 34.
No food is named in verse 34.
No conduct is named in verse 34.
questions.explain: Only the general word परिहार stands; its members are not given here.
questions.rule: Read no list into a general term.
questions.section: यापन का अतियोग और परिहार-रहित प्रयोग

questions.q: Like निष्परिहारता (absence of avoidance), what does an invented मृदुता mean (मृदु = mild)?
optionExplain: A person would be the adjective itself, not -ता.
Right: -ता makes an abstract noun: मृदु → मृदुता, mildness.
A past participle would be needed for 'made'.
The superlative is -तम: मृदुतम.
questions.explain: -ता turns an adjective into a '-ness' noun, like -त्व in मृदुत्व (verse 31).
questions.teaches: The suffix -ता makes an abstract noun: निष्परिहारता (freedom from avoidance), मृदुता (mildness).
questions.section: यापन का अतियोग और परिहार-रहित प्रयोग

questions.q: What kind of enemas does verse 35 say one should apply?
optionExplain: विवर्जित means free from, not bound by.
Those are the remedy of verse 31.
Right: परिहारविवर्जितान् = free from restrictions.
No honey is named in verse 35.
questions.explain: The verse ends with the enemas' quality: without restrictions.
questions.section: यापन का अतियोग और परिहार-रहित प्रयोग

questions.q: Match each word of verse 35 to its meaning on the card.
questions.explain: The setting, the verb and the quality of the enemas.
questions.rule: द्रव्येषु = in the drugs; यापनार्थ = meant for yāpana; युञ्ज्यात् = should apply; विवर्जित = free from.
questions.section: यापन का अतियोग और परिहार-रहित प्रयोग

questions.q: Put these parts of verse 35 in their order.
questions.explain: The drugs come first, the enemas and the verb in line 2.
questions.rule: द्रव्येषु यापनार्थेषु · … · बस्तीन् सर्वेषु वा · युञ्ज्यात् परिहारविवर्जितान्.
questions.teaches: Verse 35 names the yāpana drugs in line 1 and in line 2 the enemas free from restrictions with the verb युञ्ज्यात्.
questions.section: यापन का अतियोग और परिहार-रहित प्रयोग

questions.q: What case is बस्तीन् in verse 35, and why?
optionExplain: The nominative plural would be बस्तयः.
The locative plural would be बस्तिषु.
The instrumental plural would be बस्तिभिः.
Right: बस्तीन् is what one should apply (युञ्ज्यात्).
questions.explain: -ईन् is the accusative plural of a masculine -इ stem.
questions.rule: बस्ति → बस्तीन् (acc. pl.), object of युञ्ज्यात्.
questions.section: यापन का अतियोग और परिहार-रहित प्रयोग

questions.q: Which word of verse 35 carries on the point of verse 34 (no restrictions)?
optionExplain: Right: Free from parihāra: the same point as निष्परिहारता.
This names the drugs' purpose, not freedom from restriction.
This only says 'in the drugs'.
This says 'in all', not 'without restrictions'.
questions.explain: निष्परिहारता (verse 34) and परिहारविवर्जित (verse 35) say the same thing.
questions.section: यापन का अतियोग और परिहार-रहित प्रयोग

questions.q: Like यापनार्थेषु (meant for yāpana), what does an invented वमनार्थेषु द्रव्येषु mean?
options: In the drugs free of emesis
In the drugs meant for emesis
In the drugs caused by emesis
optionExplain: Freedom would need विवर्जित or निः-, not -अर्थ.
Right: -अर्थ = meant for: वमन-अर्थ = meant for emesis.
-अर्थ gives purpose, not cause.
-अर्थ says nothing about time.
questions.explain: X-अर्थ at the end of a compound = for the purpose of X.
questions.teaches: -अर्थ at the end of a compound gives purpose: यापनार्थ (meant for yāpana), वमनार्थ (meant for emesis).
questions.section: यापन का अतियोग और परिहार-रहित प्रयोग

questions.q: How much of each drug does verse 36 take?
optionExplain: A prastha comes in 05.05.77, not here.
No pala is named in verse 36.
Right: तुलाम्, with पृथक् (separately): a tulā of each.
Droṇas measure the water, not the drugs.
questions.explain: पृथक् … तुलाम् = separately, a tulā (of each).
questions.rule: तुला = the measure of each drug here.

questions.q: Match each drug of verse 36 to its identification on the card.
questions.explain: Four drugs with the confidence words of the data.
questions.rule: सहाचर, अभीरु = probable; गोक्षुरक = standard; रास्ना = disputed.

questions.q: Put the drugs of verse 36 in their order.
questions.explain: The compound opens with sahācara and closes with gokṣuraka in the ablative.
questions.teaches: The list of verse 36: sahācara, abhīru, balā, rāsnā, gokṣuraka.

questions.q: How much water does verse 36 use, and to what is it reduced?
options: Five droṇas, to a hundred palas
A hundred droṇas, to a quarter
A hundred droṇas, to five droṇas
optionExplain: The hundred droṇas are the water; five droṇas remain.
The remainder is five droṇas, not a quarter.
The unit is droṇa, not prastha.
Right: जलद्रोणशते … पञ्चद्रोणावशेषिते.
questions.explain: Start: a hundred droṇas; end: five droṇas remain.

questions.q: Which split of पञ्चद्रोणावशेषिते is right?
optionExplain: Right: अ + अ → आ: द्रोण + अवशेषिते (remaining).
वशेषित is no word; the word is अवशेषित.
A visarga would give द्रोणोऽवशेषिते; this is inside a compound.
षिते is no word; the participle is अवशेषिते.
questions.explain: Inside the compound the stem द्रोण meets अवशेषित: अ + अ → आ.

questions.q: Like पञ्चद्रोणावशेषिते (when five droṇas remain), what does an invented पादावशेषिते mean?
options: A quarter of the rest is drunk
optionExplain: अवशेषित means remaining, not added.
Right: पाद (quarter) + अवशेषिते (remaining), locative: 'when'.
Nothing about drinking is in the form.
The locative of अवशेषित marks what remains.
questions.explain: X-अवशेषिते (locative) = when X remains.
questions.teaches: X-अवशेषिते (locative) marks the boiling-down point: पञ्चद्रोणावशेषिते (five droṇas left), पादावशेषिते (a quarter left).

questions.q: What has happened to the decoction when the drugs of verse 37 come in?
options: It is boiled a second time
optionExplain: No second boiling is named in verse 37.
No honey is named in verse 37.
Right: पूतशीते = when strained and cooled.
No time of keeping is named in verse 37.
questions.explain: पूत (strained) + शीत (cooled), in the locative: 'when'.

questions.q: Match each word of line 1 of verse 37 to its meaning on the card.
questions.explain: The clear words of line 1 only.
questions.rule: पूत = strained; बिस = lotus stalk; द्राक्षा = grape; निदिग्धिका = yellow-berried nightshade.

questions.q: Put these clear drugs in the order of line 1 of verse 37.
questions.explain: Bisa opens the compound, drākṣā follows, nidigdhikā closes it (with the unclear words between).
questions.teaches: The paste list opens with bisa and drākṣā and line 1 closes with nidigdhikā.

questions.q: What does the card say about line 2 of verse 37?
options: It holds the verb of the recipe
It is garbled; nothing is built on it
optionExplain: The division is not safe, so no drug is certain.
The measures are in verse 36, not line 2 here.
The verb comes in 05.05.77 (क्षिपेत्).
Right: The card: the compound cannot be divided safely.
questions.explain: A garbled line stays unsplit and unused.
questions.rule: Damaged print: no identification is built on it.

questions.q: Which of these drugs does line 1 of verse 37 name?
optionExplain: Named first in the compound.
Closes the compound of line 1.
Named second in the compound.
Candana comes in verse 38.
Sahācara heads verse 36, not verse 37.
questions.explain: Bisa, drākṣā and nidigdhikā are in line 1; sahācara and candana belong to the neighbouring verses.
questions.rule: Keep each list to its own verse.

questions.q: Like पूतशीते (when strained and cooled), what does an invented पक्वशीते mean (पक्व = cooked)?
optionExplain: Right: Two participles in a locative compound: 'when X-ed and Y-ed'.
शीत here is 'cooled', a state, not cold water.
The compound says both have happened, not 'before'.
The order of the compound is cooked, then cooled.
questions.explain: X-Y-ए (locative) = when X-ed and Y-ed.
questions.teaches: A compound of two past participles in the locative marks the moment: पूतशीते (when strained and cooled), पक्वशीते (when cooked and cooled).

questions.q: Which of these drugs does verse 38 name?
optionExplain: Gokṣuraka is in verse 36.
Right: चन्दनम् closes line 1 of verse 38.
Drākṣā is in verse 37.
Paṭola opens verse 39.
questions.explain: Line 1 ends with candana.

questions.q: Match each drug of verse 38 to its meaning on the card.
questions.explain: Four drugs whose sense the data gives as plain or standard.
questions.rule: मृणाल = lotus fibre; उत्पल = blue lotus; चन्दन = sandalwood; खर्जूर = date.

questions.q: Put the drugs of line 1 of verse 38 in their order.
questions.explain: Two aṣṭavarga drugs, udīcya, the two lotus items, then sandalwood.
questions.rule: जीवक · ऋषभक · उदीच्य · मृणाल · उत्पल · चन्दन.
questions.teaches: Line 1 of verse 38: jīvaka, ṛṣabhaka, udīcya, mṛṇāla, utpala, candana.

questions.q: What does तालमज्जा mean on the card?
options: The juice or sap of the palmyra tree
optionExplain: Bark would be त्वक्; मज्जा is the kernel.
Juice would be रस; मज्जा is the kernel.
Right: ताल = palmyra palm; मज्जा = kernel (majjā).
Leaf would be पत्र; मज्जा is the kernel.
questions.explain: मज्जा is rendered 'kernel (majjā)' in this book.

questions.q: Which split of जीवकर्षभक is right?
optionExplain: कर्षभक is no drug name; the second drug is ऋषभक.
अर्षभक is no word; अर् comes from अ + ऋ.
Neither part is a word; the drugs are जीवक, ऋषभक.
Right: अ + ऋ → अर्: जीवक + ऋषभक = जीवकर्षभक.
questions.explain: The र् before ष shows a hidden ऋ: अ + ऋ → अर्.

questions.q: Like जीवकर्षभक (जीवक + ऋषभक), how do देव + ऋषि join?
optionExplain: Right: अ + ऋ → अर्: देव + ऋषि = देवर्षि.
अ + ऋ gives short अर्, not आर्.
The vowel ऋ does not turn into र् + अ here.
रि is a spelling of ऋ alone; the join gives अर्.
questions.explain: Same join as in the drug names: अ + ऋ → अर्.
questions.teaches: अ + ऋ joins to अर्: जीवक + ऋषभक = जीवकर्षभक, देव + ऋषि = देवर्षि.

questions.q: What is done with the drugs of the list in verse 39?
options: Made into a paste, put in
Dried and kept in a jar
optionExplain: No milk or drinking is named in verse 39.
Right: कल्कीकृत्य क्षिपेत् तस्मिन् = made into a paste, put into that.
No burning is named in verse 39.
No drying is named in verse 39.
questions.explain: The absolutive कल्कीकृत्य comes before the verb क्षिपेत्.
questions.rule: कल्कीकृत्य क्षिपेत् = make a paste, then put it in.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 39 to its meaning on the card.
questions.explain: One clear drug and the three words of the procedure.
questions.rule: पटोल = pointed gourd; कल्कीकृत्य = making a paste; क्षिपेत् = should put; तस्मिन् = into that.

questions.q: Put the words of line 2 of verse 39 in their order.
questions.explain: Make the paste, put it in that, and separately a prastha-measured item.
questions.rule: कल्कीकृत्य · क्षिपेत् · तस्मिन् · पृथक् च · प्रस्थसंमितम्.
questions.teaches: Line 2 of verse 39 is the step: make a kalka, put it into the decoction, and separately add a prastha-measured item.

questions.q: Into what is the paste put (तस्मिन्), by the card?
options: The two āḍhakas of cow's milk
The oil and ghee of verse 40
The paste of the previous verse
optionExplain: The milk is named later, in verse 41.
Those are further items, not 'that'.
Right: The card: tasmin is the decoction of 05.05.72.
The paste is what is put in, not where.
questions.explain: तस्मिन् points back to the decoction strained and cooled in verse 37.

questions.q: What does the card say about मेदा in verse 39?
optionExplain: मेदा here is a drug, not flour.
The drug medā is a different word from medas.
Asparagus is the probable abhīru of verse 36.
Right: The data: medā is disputed; Hindi writes 'मेदा नामक द्रव्य'.
questions.explain: A disputed drug keeps its Sanskrit name with the word 'disputed'.

questions.q: Like कल्कीकृत्य (having made into a paste), what does an invented चूर्णीकृत्य mean (चूर्ण = powder)?
optionExplain: Right: X-ी + कृत्य = having turned into X.
The -ी + कृ pattern makes, it does not remove.
Mixing would be a different verb or 'with'.
That would be an optative; -य marks 'having done'.
questions.explain: Noun with -ी + कृत्य = having made (something) into that noun.
questions.teaches: Noun + -ी + कृत्य = having made into that: कल्कीकृत्य (into a paste), चूर्णीकृत्य (into powder).

questions.q: From the testes of which animals is the juice of verse 40?
optionExplain: These three give eggs in line 2, not testes.
Right: वराह-महिष-बस्त-मुष्क-उद्भवम्.
None of these is named in verse 40.
None of these is named in verse 40.
questions.explain: Line 1 names three mammals; line 2 three birds.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 40 to its meaning on the card.
questions.explain: The three animals of line 1 and the organ.
questions.rule: वराह = boar; महिष = buffalo; बस्त = he-goat; मुष्क = testis.

questions.q: Put the animals of verse 40 in their order.
questions.explain: Three mammals in line 1, three birds in line 2.
questions.rule: वराह · महिष · बस्त ‖ शिखी · कुक्कुट · हंस.
questions.teaches: Verse 40: boar, buffalo, he-goat (testes juice), then peacock, cock, swan (eggs).

questions.q: What does बस्त mean in verse 40?
optionExplain: The enema is बस्ति; बस्त is the goat.
The bladder sense belongs to बस्ति, not बस्त.
Right: बस्त = he-goat, one of three animals of line 1.
बस्त is the goat; no device is meant here.
questions.explain: Do not confuse बस्त (goat) with बस्ति (enema, bladder).

questions.q: What does the card say about the oil, ghee and eggs of line 2?
options: The oil is pressed from the eggs
The eggs replace oil and ghee
The eggs must be left out
It is not said how they relate
optionExplain: That is one reading; the Sanskrit does not decide.
Nothing says the eggs replace them.
The eggs are named, not excluded.
Right: The data: whether from the eggs or cooked with them is not stated.
questions.explain: The loose agreement (सम्भवम् singular, तैलसर्पिषी dual) leaves the relation open.
questions.rule: Keep the literal 'arising from'; decide nothing more.

questions.q: Like मुष्कोद्भवम् (arising from the testes), what does an invented जलोद्भवम् mean?
optionExplain: Right: -उद्भव = born of, arising from.
-उद्भव names the source, not the product.
Mixing would need सह or a 'with' word.
Freedom would need निः- or विवर्जित.
questions.explain: X-उद्भव = arising from X; अ + उ → ओ in the join.
questions.teaches: X-उद्भव (with अ + उ → ओ) means arising from X: मुष्कोद्भवम् (from testes), जलोद्भवम् (from water).

questions.q: Of which two drugs is the expressed juice in verse 41?
optionExplain: These are paste drugs of verse 37.
Right: धात्री-विदारी-स्वरसम्.
These are paste drugs of verse 38.
These are paste drugs of verse 39.
questions.explain: The svarasa is of dhātrī (emblic myrobalan) and vidārī.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 41 to its meaning on the card.
questions.explain: A drug, the form of preparation, an instrument and the word for sound.
questions.rule: धात्री = emblic myrobalan; स्वरस = expressed juice; भेरी = kettledrum; निनाद = sound.

questions.q: Put the phrases of verse 41 in their order.
questions.explain: Juice, milk, then the instruments, their sounds and 'which is prepared'.
questions.rule: स्वरस · दो आढक दूध · वाद्य · ध्वनियों से · तैयार.
questions.teaches: Verse 41: svarasa of dhātrī and vidārī, two āḍhakas of cow's milk, prepared with the sounds of drums.

questions.q: How much cow's milk does verse 41 name?
optionExplain: The measure is āḍhaka, not prastha.
द्वयम् makes it a pair, two.
Right: गव्य-क्षीर-आढक-द्वयम् = a pair of āḍhakas of cow's milk.
A hundred droṇas is the water of verse 36.
questions.explain: -द्वयम् = a pair: two āḍhakas.

questions.q: What does निनादैः साधितम् say about the preparation?
optionExplain: The verse names sounds, not silence.
निनाद is sound, not a vessel.
No time of day is named in verse 41.
Right: निनादैः (instrumental) = with the sounds; साधितम् = prepared.
questions.explain: The instrumental निनादैः gives the accompaniment.

questions.q: Like आढकद्वयम् (two āḍhakas), what does an invented पलद्वयम् mean?
optionExplain: Right: -द्वयम् = a pair of: two palas.
Half would be अर्ध-पल.
That would be सार्ध-पल or अध्यर्ध-पल.
The second would be द्वितीय.
questions.explain: -द्वय at the end of a compound counts two.
questions.teaches: X-द्वयम् means a pair of X: आढकद्वयम् (two āḍhakas), पलद्वयम् (two palas).

questions.q: Where is the prepared substance placed in verse 42?
options: On a white cloth on the ground
Under a tree in the shade
optionExplain: The white cloth covers it; it is not on the ground.
Right: आरोपितं गजस्कन्धे = placed on the shoulder of an elephant.
Vṛṣadhvaja is worshipped; no temple is named.
The shade comes from a white umbrella, not a tree.
questions.explain: गज-स्कन्धे (locative) = on the elephant's shoulder.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 42 to its meaning on the card.
questions.explain: The four describing words of the honouring.
questions.rule: सित = white; छत्र = umbrella; अवगुण्ठित = covered; आरोपित = placed.

questions.q: Put the phrases of verse 42 in their order.
questions.explain: Umbrella, cloth, elephant, worship.
questions.teaches: Verse 42 runs: white umbrella shade, white cloth cover, placed on an elephant, Vṛṣadhvaja worshipped.

questions.q: What does वृषध्वज mean on the card?
options: A bull-shaped flag on the elephant
The giver of virility to men
The bull that carries the drug
optionExplain: It is the accusative object of worship, a deity.
वृष here is the bull of the banner, not virility.
Right: Literally 'having a bull as banner'; the usual epithet of Śiva.
The elephant carries it; no bull carries anything.
questions.explain: A bahuvrīhi: one whose banner (ध्वज) is a bull (वृष).

questions.q: Which split of सितवस्त्रावगुंठितं is right?
optionExplain: वगुण्ठित is no word; the participle is अवगुण्ठित.
A visarga would give वस्त्रोऽवगुण्ठितम्; this is inside a compound.
वस्त्राव is no word; the stem is वस्त्र.
Right: अ + अ → आ: वस्त्र + अवगुण्ठितम् (covered).
questions.explain: Same join as द्रोण + अवशेषित in verse 36: अ + अ → आ.

questions.q: Like पूजयित्वा (having worshipped, no prefix), which invented form means having eaten, from √भुज्?
optionExplain: Right: A bare root takes -त्वा: भुज् + त्वा = भुक्त्वा.
-य is used after a prefix; the bare root takes -त्वा.
This is a future verb, 'will eat'.
This is a present verb, 'eats'.
questions.explain: No prefix → -त्वा (पूजयित्वा, भुक्त्वा); prefix → -य (आस्थाप्य).
questions.teaches: Without a prefix the absolutive ends in -त्वा: पूजयित्वा, भुक्त्वा; with a prefix in -य: आस्थाप्य.

questions.q: What is performed before the enema is given in verse 43?
optionExplain: No fast is named in verse 43.
Right: कृत्वा स्वस्त्ययनम् = having performed the svastyayana.
No nirūha is named here; the enema is a sneha-basti.
No massage is named in verse 43.
questions.explain: The absolutive कृत्वा comes before the main verb दद्यात्.
questions.rule: कृत्वा स्वस्त्ययनं दद्यात् = after the rite, give.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 43 to its meaning on the card.
questions.explain: The rite, the verb, its manner and the result.
questions.rule: स्वस्त्ययन = auspicious rite; दद्यात् = should give; अयन्त्रणम् = unrestrained; अतिवृषता = excess virility.

questions.q: Put the words of line 1 of verse 43 in their order.
questions.explain: Having done, the rite, should give, the sneha-basti, without restriction.
questions.teaches: Line 1 of verse 43 is the recipe's main command: after the svastyayana, give the sneha-basti without restriction.

questions.q: Why does the card read अयन्त्रणम् as an adverb?
options: Every word ending in -म् is an adverb
It is a verb in the optative
It is neuter, but basti is masculine
It is dual, and adverbs are dual
optionExplain: -म् is also the accusative of many nouns.
The optative verb is दद्यात्.
Right: Gender disagrees with स्नेहबस्तिम्, so it modifies the giving.
It is singular; adverbs are not dual.
questions.explain: An adjective must agree with its noun; अयन्त्रणम् (n.) cannot agree with बस्तिम् (m.).

questions.q: Which kind of enema does verse 43 say is given?
optionExplain: Urine enemas belong to verse 31.
No milk enema is named in verse 43.
The āsthāpana belongs to verse 31.
Right: स्नेहबस्तिम् = the sneha-basti.
questions.explain: The whole recipe from verse 36 ends in a sneha-basti.

questions.q: Like दद्यात् (he should give), which invented form means he should drink, from √पा?
optionExplain: Right: Optative 3rd singular: 'should drink', like दद्यात्.
This is the present: 'drinks'.
This is the absolutive: 'having drunk'.
This is the future: 'will drink'.
questions.explain: The optative gives the instruction: दद्यात्, पिबेत्.
questions.teaches: Recipes give orders in the optative: दद्यात् (should give), क्षिपेत् (should put), पिबेत् (should drink).

questions.q: What does line 1 of verse 44 say he would become, besides free of wrinkles?
options: Strong, fat and free of disease
optionExplain: Neither strength nor fat is named in verse 44.
Right: कान्तः चिरंजीवी = handsome, long-lived.
Neither wisdom nor calm is named in verse 44.
Neither is named in verse 44.
questions.explain: Two nominatives follow the wrinkle word: कान्तः and चिरंजीवी.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 44 to its meaning on the card.
questions.explain: The promised qualities and the key words of line 2.
questions.rule: कान्त = handsome; चिरंजीवी = long-lived; हित = beneficial; क्षीण = wasted.

questions.q: Put the words of line 2 of verse 44 in their order.
questions.explain: The compound runs: lost semen, injured, wasted, irregular fever.
questions.teaches: Line 2 of verse 44: beneficial for those with lost semen, the injured, the wasted and those with viṣamajvara.

questions.q: What does विषमज्वर mean on the card?
optionExplain: विषम is 'irregular', not विष (poison).
विषम means uneven, not high.
Right: विषम = irregular; the data: intermittent fever, probable.
No cough is in the word.
questions.explain: विषम (irregular) + ज्वर (fever): do not read विष (poison) into it.

questions.q: For whom does verse 44 say it is beneficial?
optionExplain: Obesity is not named in verse 44.
नष्टशुक्र is named first.
Children are named in verse 20, not here.
विषमज्वरिणाम् closes the list.
क्षीण is named in line 2.
questions.explain: Line 2 lists lost semen, injured, wasted, irregular fever; nothing else.
