questions.rule: हितः + genitive plural = beneficial for those.

questions.q: Like ज्वरिणाम् (of those having fever, from ज्वरिन्), what does an invented शूलिनाम् mean?
options: Of the colic itself, as a disease
optionExplain: The colic itself would be शूलस्य.
Freedom would need निः-: निःशूल.
Causing would need a word like -कर.
Right: -इन् = having; -इनाम् = of those having.
questions.explain: -इन् makes a possessor; the genitive plural -इनाम् says 'for/of those having'.
questions.teaches: -इन् makes 'one who has X': ज्वरिन् (feverish), शूलिन् (one with colic); genitive plural -इनाम्.

questions.q: Which two titles does line 1 of verse 45 give the enema?
options: King of yāpanas; good for eyes
optionExplain: Right: पुत्रदाता रसायनम्.
Those titles belong to the mustādi yāpana of verse 18.
These are the effects of verse 30.
These come in verses 33 and 43.
questions.explain: Two nominatives: पुत्रदाता and रसायनम्.
questions.rule: पुत्रदाता = giver of sons; रसायन = rejuvenating tonic.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 45 to its meaning on the card.
questions.explain: Two titles and the two key words of the closing rule.
questions.rule: पुत्रदाता = giver of a son; रसायन = rejuvenating tonic; कल्प्य = to be devised; नैकशः = in many ways.

questions.q: Put the words of line 2 of verse 45 in their order.
questions.explain: Thus, other bastis also, to be devised, and cooked, in many ways.
questions.rule: एवं च · बस्तयोऽन्येऽपि · कल्प्याः · पाक्याश्च · नैकशः.
questions.teaches: Line 2 of verse 45 turns the recipe into a pattern: other bastis are to be devised and cooked in many ways.

questions.q: Which split of नैकशः is right?
optionExplain: अ + इ would give ए: नेकशः, not नैकशः.
Right: अ + ए → ऐ: न + एकशः, 'not singly'.
नै and कशः are not words here.
ऐकशः is no word; the adverb is एकशः.
questions.explain: ऐ comes from अ + ए (or अ + ऐ); here न + एकशः.

questions.q: What does verse 45 say about other bastis?
options: They are forbidden for these men
They are made in one fixed way
Devised and cooked in many ways
They are made of milk only
optionExplain: Nothing is forbidden in verse 45.
नैकशः means not singly: many ways.
Right: कल्प्याः पाक्याश्च नैकशः.
No milk is named in verse 45.
questions.explain: एवम् (in this way) makes the recipe a model for others.
questions.rule: एवं … अन्ये अपि कल्प्याः = others too are to be devised thus.

questions.q: Like कल्प्याः, पाक्याः (to be devised, to be cooked), which invented form means to be drunk, from √पा?
optionExplain: पीत is the past participle, 'drunk'.
पीत्वा is the absolutive, 'having drunk'.
पिबेत् is the optative, 'should drink'.
Right: Gerundive in -य: पा → पेय, 'to be drunk'.
questions.explain: The gerundive -य says 'to be X-ed': कल्प्य, पाक्य, पेय.
questions.teaches: The gerundive in -य means 'to be X-ed': कल्प्य (to be devised), पाक्य (to be cooked), पेय (to be drunk).

questions.q: How many times does verse 46 say one should have it cooked?
options: A hundred or a thousand times
Once only, then strained and kept
optionExplain: Right: शतं वारान् सहस्रं वा.
The verse speaks of many cookings.
No seven and no day are named.
That is the boiling of verse 36.
questions.explain: शतम् … सहस्रं वा = a hundred or a thousand (times).

questions.q: Match each word of verse 46 to its meaning on the card.
questions.explain: The verb, its condition, and the announcement of line 2.
questions.rule: पाचयेत् = should have cooked; सम्भवे सति = when possible; दोषघ्न = doṣa-destroying; वक्ष्यन्ते = will be told.

questions.q: Put the words of line 1 of verse 46 in their order.
questions.explain: A hundred times, or a thousand, should have cooked, when possible.
questions.rule: शतं वारान् · सहस्रं वा · पाचयेत् · संभवे सति.
questions.teaches: Line 1 of verse 46: a hundred or a thousand times, one should have it cooked, when possible.

questions.q: What tense and voice is वक्ष्यन्ते?
optionExplain: A past would be उक्ताः; वक्ष्य- is future.
Right: The data: 3 pl. future passive of √वच्.
The present passive would be उच्यन्ते.
The optative passive would be उच्येरन्.
questions.explain: -ष्य- marks the future; वक्ष्यन्ते looks ahead to the next recipes.

questions.q: What does line 2 of verse 46 say will be described next?
options: Yāpana enemas for old and weak men
optionExplain: Line 2 names sneha-bastis, not nirūha.
Complications are not announced here.
Right: दोषघ्नाः … वक्ष्यन्ते स्नेहबस्तयः.
Yāpana is not named in line 2.
questions.explain: The chapter turns from this recipe to doṣa-destroying sneha-bastis.

questions.q: Like सम्भवे सति (when it is possible), what does an invented काले सति mean?
options: For a long time, whatever happens
optionExplain: Wrong time would need अकाले.
Without would need विना or निः-.
Duration would need चिरम् or an accusative.
Right: Locative + सति = 'when X is (there)'.
questions.explain: The locative absolute: noun in -ए + सति = when there is that.
questions.rule: X-े सति = when there is X.
questions.teaches: A locative with सति is a locative absolute: सम्भवे सति (when possible), काले सति (when there is time).

questions.q: What is दशमूल, the first item of verse 47, by the card?
options: Ten pala of a single root
The root of a ten-leaved herb
optionExplain: Right: दश (ten) + मूल (root): the traditional group of ten roots.
Nothing is boiled ten times; दश counts the roots.
No pala is given in verse 47; दश counts roots.
The card reads it as a group of ten roots, not one plant.
questions.explain: दशमूल names a group: ten roots taken together.

questions.q: Match each drug of verse 47 to its identification on the card.
questions.explain: Four clear names of the list with the identifications the data gives.
questions.rule: वरा = probably triphalā; अश्वगन्धा = Withania; पुनर्नवा = Boerhavia; गुडूची = giloy.

questions.q: Put the drugs of line 1 of verse 47 in their order.
questions.explain: Line 1 runs daśamūla, varā, rāsnā, aśvagandhā, punarnavā.
questions.teaches: Line 1 of verse 47: daśamūla, varā, rāsnā, aśvagandhā, punarnavā, all in the accusative.

questions.q: Which of these does verse 47 name?
optionExplain: Named at the end of line 1.
Named inside the compound of line 2.
Śatāvarī comes in verse 48, not 47.
Opens the compound of line 2.
Jīvantī comes in verse 52, not 47.
questions.explain: Only names printed in verse 47 count; śatāvarī and jīvantī belong to later verses.
questions.rule: Count as listed only what the verse names.

questions.q: Why do the drug names of verse 47 stand in the accusative?
options: They are subjects of the sentence
They are objects of a later verb
optionExplain: A subject would be nominative; these end in -आम्, -म्.
Right: The card: no verb here; the list is most probably the object of vipācya in verse 49.
These are drug names, not diseases.
Address uses the vocative; these are drugs.
questions.explain: An accusative list waits for its verb; here it most probably comes two verses later.

questions.q: Like रास्नाम् + अश्वगन्धाम् → रास्नामश्वगन्धाम्, how do invented वचाम् + अभयाम् join?
optionExplain: Anusvāra replaces म् only before a consonant, not before अ.
The म् cannot simply drop before a vowel.
Right: Final म् before a vowel stays म् and joins it: वचाम् + अभयाम्.
No long आ arises; अ stays short after म्.
questions.explain: म् + vowel → म joined to the vowel, as in रास्नामश्वगन्धाम्.
questions.teaches: A final म् before a vowel joins it: रास्नाम् + अश्वगन्धाम् → रास्नामश्वगन्धाम्; वचाम् + अभयाम् → वचामभयाम्.

questions.q: By verse 48, with which measure are yava, māṣa and the other grains measured?
optionExplain: Palāṃśika stands in line 1; the grains carry their own measure word, prasṛta-unmita.
Droṇa is the remainder of the boiling in verse 49.
Āḍhaka measures the oil in verse 49.
Right: प्रसृतोन्मितान् = measured by prasṛta, the cupped-palm measure.
questions.explain: The measure word is joined to the grains in one compound: prasṛta-unmita.

questions.q: Match each grain of verse 48 to its meaning on the card.
questions.explain: Four items of line 2 with their ordinary names.
questions.rule: यव = barley; माष = black gram; अतसी = flax; कुलत्थ = horse gram.

questions.q: Put the items of line 2 of verse 48 in their order.
questions.explain: The compound runs yava, māṣa, atasī, kola, kulattha.
questions.teaches: Line 2 of verse 48: yava, māṣa, atasī, kola, kulattha, measured by the prasṛta.

questions.q: What does पलांशिक (printed पळांशिकं) mean on the card?
optionExplain: Right: पल (a weight) + अंशिक (having as share).
That is said of the grains in line 2.
No quarter is named; अंश here is share, not quarter.
Cutting is not in the word; it names the share.
questions.explain: अंश = share; पलांशिक = one whose share is a pala.
questions.rule: पल + अंशिक = जिसका भाग एक पल.

questions.q: A student writes a pala of each drug for verse 48. Is each in the Sanskrit?
options: No; each is not in the Sanskrit
No; the verse gives no measures at all
optionExplain: Palāṃśika means having a pala as share, nothing about each.
Right: The card: the noun is not stated and 'each' is not in the text.
Prasṛta is a measure, the cupped palm.
It gives two: pala and prasṛta.
questions.explain: Do not supply 'each': the verse gives the measure, not its distribution.

questions.q: Like माष + अतसी → माषातसी, how do invented तिल + अतसी join in a compound?
optionExplain: ए comes from अ + इ, not from अ + अ.
ओ comes from अ + उ, not from अ + अ.
Right: अ + अ → आ: तिल + अतसी = तिलातसी, as माष + अतसी = माषातसी.
Inside a compound the two अ must merge.
questions.explain: Two short अ merge into one long आ.
questions.teaches: अ + अ → आ: माष + अतसी = माषातसी; तिल + अतसी = तिलातसी.

questions.q: In verse 49, until how much water is left is the boiling continued?
optionExplain: The remainder word joins droṇa (droṇa-śeṣa), not vaha.
The āḍhaka measures the oil, not the remainder.

questions.q: Which split of पेष्यैर्जीवनीयैः is right?

questions.q: Like विपाच्य (prefix वि- + absolutive -य), which invented form means having ground, from प्र + √पिष्?

The visarga after उ is not dropped before न.
No न् is doubled; the visarga becomes र्.
questions.explain: Visarga after a vowel other than अ/आ becomes र् before a voiced sound.
questions.teaches: After उ (or इ) a visarga before a voiced sound becomes र्: हरेणुः + नीलिनी = हरेणुर्नीलिनी; गुरुः + नमति = गुरुर्नमति.

questions.q: Which diseases does the oil of verse 58 remove?
optionExplain: Pitta was the target of verse 55.
Right: कफरोगनुत् = removing diseases of Kapha.
That was said of the oil in verse 50.
Semen ailments were named in verse 54.
questions.explain: The last compound names the target: kapha-roga-nud.
questions.rule: कफ-रोग-नुद् = कफ रोग दूर करने वाला.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 58 to its meaning on the card.
questions.explain: Two drugs, the oil, and the word for the proportion.
questions.rule: दन्ती = जंगली जमालगोटा; अजमोदा = सम्भवतः अजमोद; एरण्डतैल = अरंडी का तेल; समैः = समान.

questions.q: Put the phrases of verse 58 in their order.
questions.explain: The last drugs, the equal share, the castor oil or oil, then its use.
questions.rule: बिल्व-अजमोदा, चपला · दन्ती, रास्ना, समान · एरण्ड-तेल या · तेल, कफ-रोग-नाशक.
questions.teaches: Verse 58 ends the Kapha list and says: with those, equal, castor oil or oil is prepared; it removes Kapha diseases.

questions.q: What does तैः समैः mean, by the card?
optionExplain: No second cooking is named; समैः is 'equal'.
No half is named; समैः is 'equal'.
Right: The card: with those, equal; probably 'in equal parts'.
तैः is instrumental 'with those', not 'without'.
questions.explain: सम = equal; 'parts' is understood, not printed.

questions.q: Which oil does verse 58 allow to be prepared?
options: Ghee with a quarter of oil
optionExplain: Castor oil is named first; sesame is not named.
That is the Pitta anuvāsana of verse 55.
Marsh-animal fat is in verse 50.
Right: साध्यम् एरण्डतैलं वा तैलं वा = castor oil or oil.
questions.explain: वा … वा offers two choices: castor oil or another oil.

questions.q: Like एरण्डतैलं वा तैलं वा, what does an invented घृतं वा तैलं वा पिबेत् mean?
options: He may drink either ghee or oil
He should drink both of them together
He should drink neither of them
He drinks ghee, but never oil
optionExplain: Right: वा … वा = either … or.
Both together would use च, not वा.
'Neither' would need न; वा offers a choice.
वा … वा keeps both open as choices.
questions.explain: Each वा follows one of the alternatives.
questions.rule: X वा Y वा = X या Y.
questions.teaches: वा … वा after two words means either … or: एरण्डतैलं वा तैलं वा (castor oil or oil); घृतं वा तैलं वा.

questions.q: How fast does verse 59 say that anuvāsana destroys these disorders?
optionExplain: No month is named in verse 59.
Right: चाशु = च + आशु, and quickly.
No number of doses is named.
No fasting is named in verse 59.
questions.explain: आशु = quickly; it qualifies हन्यात्.

questions.q: Match each disorder of verse 59 to its meaning on the card.
questions.explain: Four disorders with the senses the data gives.
questions.rule: उदावर्त = वायु उलटा; गुल्म = गाँठ; अर्शस् = बवासीर; अश्मरी = पथरी.

questions.q: Put these disorders in the order of verse 59.
questions.explain: Line 1 runs vardhma, udāvarta, gulma, arśas (spleen, meha); line 2 ānāha, aśmarī.
questions.rule: वर्ध्म · उदावर्त · गुल्म · अर्शः · (प्लीहा · मेह) ‖ आनाह · अश्मरी.
questions.teaches: The anuvāsana of verse 59 destroys vardhma, udāvarta, gulma, arśas, spleen disorder, meha, then ānāha and aśmarī.

questions.q: Which of these does verse 59 name?
optionExplain: Named in the compound of line 1.
Fever is not in verse 59.
Cough is not in verse 59.
Named in line 2.
Named in line 2.
questions.explain: Only disorders printed in the verse count.
questions.rule: Count as listed only what the verse names.

questions.q: Which split of हन्यात्तदनुवासनं is right?
optionExplain: That would give हन्यातद-, with a single त.
तत + अ would give ता: हन्यात्तता- is not printed.
Right: त् + त → त्त; तत् + अ → तद (voiced before a vowel).
तद् + न gives तन्न, and नुवासन is no word.
questions.explain: हन्यात् keeps its त् before त; तत् becomes तद् before the vowel अ.

questions.q: Like हन्यात् (would destroy, optative of √हन्), which invented form means would go, from √गम्?
optionExplain: This is the present, 'goes'.
This is the future, 'will go'.
This is the absolutive, 'having gone'.
Right: The optative 3rd singular of √गम् is गच्छेत्.
questions.explain: हन्यात्, गच्छेत्, पचेत्: optatives say what would or should happen.
questions.teaches: The optative states what would or should happen: हन्यात् (would destroy), गच्छेत् (would go).

questions.q: With what is the oil of verse 60 first prepared?
optionExplain: Right: साधितं पञ्चमूलेन = prepared with the five roots.
Daśamūla opened the Vāta oil of verse 47.
Fruits and sour are in verse 61.
That was the Pitta ghee of verse 55.
questions.explain: pañca = five: a group of five roots, not ten.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 60 to its meaning on the card.
questions.explain: The two groups, the target and the action word.
questions.rule: पञ्चमूल = पाँच जड़ें; बिल्वादि = बेल आदि; श्लेष्मन् = कफ; घातिन् = नाशक.

questions.q: Put the phrases of verse 60 in their order.
questions.explain: Five roots, or bilvādi; the anuvāsana's action; or other Kapha-destroying substances.
questions.rule: पञ्चमूल से साधित · तेल, या बिल्वादि से · श्लेष्म-हर अनुवासन · या कफ-घाती द्रव्यों से.
questions.teaches: Verse 60: oil with pañcamūla or bilvādi is a phlegm-removing anuvāsana; or one with any Kapha-destroying substances.

questions.q: What does बिल्वादिना mean, by the card?
options: With the first part of bilva
optionExplain: आदि adds 'and the rest'.
Right: बिल्व + आदि = bilva and the rest (instrumental).
आदि here is 'and so on', not 'before'.
आदि is not a part of the fruit here.
questions.explain: -आदि closes an open group named by its first member.

questions.q: A physician has neither pañcamūla nor bilvādi. What does verse 60 still allow?
options: Ghee with a quarter of oil
optionExplain: Verse 60 offers an anuvāsana option, not only nirūha.
That is the Pitta anuvāsana of verse 55.
Right: द्रव्यैर्वा कफघातिभिः = or with Kapha-destroying substances.
The third option keeps the anuvāsana possible.
questions.explain: The last वा opens a general choice: any Kapha-destroying drug.

questions.q: Like कफघातिभिः (by Kapha-destroying ones), what does an invented विषघाती mean?
optionExplain: 'Born of' would be -ज, not -घातिन्.
-घातिन् is active: it strikes, it is not struck.
'Increasing' would be -वर्धन.
Right: -घातिन् (nom. -घाती) = destroying X.
questions.explain: -घातिन् from √हन्, 'to strike, kill': the one who destroys.
questions.teaches: -घातिन् at the end of a compound means destroying: कफघातिन् = Kapha-destroying, विषघातिन् (nom. विषघाती) = poison-destroying.

questions.q: In which condition does verse 61 use the anvāsana cooked with fruits?
optionExplain: Right: सिद्धमन्वासनं कफे = the cooked anvāsana, in Kapha.
Pitta is not named in verse 61.
Fever is not named in verse 61.
Those get the nirūha of line 2.
questions.explain: Each remedy has its locative: कफे for the anvāsana, शूलानाहे for the nirūha.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 61 to its meaning on the card.
questions.explain: Two enemas and the two troubles of line 2.
questions.rule: अन्वासन = अनुवासन; निरूह = क्वाथ-बस्ति; शूल = पीड़ा; आनाह = पेट फूलना.

questions.q: Put the phrases of verse 61 in their order.
questions.explain: First the anvāsana and its condition, then the nirūha and its condition.
questions.rule: फल और अठगुना अम्ल · सिद्ध अन्वासन, कफ में · शूल-आनाह में · उससे युक्त निरूह.
questions.teaches: Verse 61: in Kapha an anvāsana cooked with fruits in eightfold sour; in pain and distension a nirūha joined with that.

questions.q: Which enema does verse 61 give for pain and distension?
optionExplain: The anvāsana is for Kapha, in line 1.
Right: शूलानाहे तु तद्युक्तो निरूहः.
Milk is not named in verse 61.
A nirūha, an enema, is named.
questions.explain: तु (but) turns to the second condition and its own remedy.

questions.q: Does verse 61 say what is eightfold?
options: No; the noun is not stated
optionExplain: अष्टगुणे is with अम्ले, not a count of fruits.
No pala is named in verse 61.
Right: The card: what is eightfold is not stated.
Urine rests on a conjectural reading, not this word.
questions.explain: अष्टगुणे अम्ले is literally 'in the eightfold sour'; the measure is left open.

questions.q: Like शूल + आनाहे → शूलानाहे, how do invented ज्वर + आनाहे join?
optionExplain: ए comes from अ + इ, not from अ + आ.
ओ comes from अ + उ, not from अ + आ.
Inside a compound अ and आ must merge.
Right: अ + आ → आ: ज्वर + आनाहे = ज्वरानाहे.
questions.explain: अ + आ merge into one long आ.
questions.teaches: अ + आ → आ: शूल + आनाहे = शूलानाहे; ज्वर + आनाहे = ज्वरानाहे.

questions.q: What does Agniveśa ask the sage about in verse 62?
options: Which fruit is always good in basti
Which oil suits a Kapha anuvāsana
How much decoction a single nirūha needs
When a basti must never be given
optionExplain: Right: किं तु फलानां बस्तिकर्मणि हितं सततं स्यात्: which of the fruits may be always beneficial in basti-action.
Oils for anuvāsana came earlier; verse 62 asks about fruits.
No measure is asked about in verse 62.
The question is about what is beneficial, not about forbidden times.
questions.explain: The question is about fruits (फलानाम्) that are beneficial (हितम्) in basti-action (बस्तिकर्मणि).
questions.rule: Verse 62: Agniveśa asks which fruit is always beneficial in basti; Punarvasu answers.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 62 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words describe the asker, the question and the answer.
questions.rule: धीमान् = wise; हितम् = beneficial; सततम् = always; प्रशशास = instructed.

questions.q: Put these phrases of verse 62 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: First the asking, then the asker, then the question about fruits in basti, then Punarvasu's instruction.
questions.rule: पृच्छतिस्म मुनिम् · धीमान् अग्निवेशः · किं तु फलानाम् · बस्तिकर्मणि हितम् · पुनर्वसुः प्रशशास.
questions.teaches: Verse 62 runs: he asked the sage; the wise Agniveśa; which of the fruits; beneficial in basti; Punarvasu instructed.

questions.q: Which is the right split of मुनिमित्यथ?
optionExplain: Neither piece is a word.
Right: म् joins the next vowel (मुनिमि-), and इ before a different vowel becomes य्: इति + अथ = इत्यथ.
A visarga after इ before a vowel becomes र्: that would give मुनिरित्यथ.
इत + अथ would give इताथ (अ + अ = आ), not इत्यथ.
questions.explain: मुनिम् (the sage, accusative) + इति (thus) + अथ (then).
questions.rule: इ + different vowel → य् + vowel: इति + अथ = इत्यथ.

questions.q: In verse 62, whom does तम् (him) refer to, the one Punarvasu instructed?
optionExplain: The sage asked is Punarvasu himself, the one who instructs.
तम् is masculine and is the person instructed; फल is neuter.
Right: The card: तम् = him, Agniveśa, who asked the question.
Other disciples appear only in 05.05.131, and तम् is singular.
questions.explain: Agniveśa asks, Punarvasu (the sage) instructs him (तम्).

questions.q: Like पृच्छति स्म (asked), what does the invented वदति स्म mean?
optionExplain: स्म does not make a future.
That would be the optative वदेत्.
स्म is not a negative; न would be.
Right: A present form with स्म takes a past sense: वदति स्म = he spoke.
questions.explain: पृच्छति स्म = asked; in the same way वदति स्म = spoke.
questions.teaches: A present-tense verb followed by स्म has a past sense (पृच्छति स्म = asked; वदति स्म = spoke).

questions.q: Which fruit does verse 63 call foremost (प्रवरम्) in heart ailment?
optionExplain: Right: कुटजस्य फलं हृदामये प्रवरम्: the kuṭaja fruit is foremost in heart ailment.
The ikṣvāku fruit is for those with prameha.
The kauṭa-fruit is named for pāṇḍu.
Madana comes in the next verse, not for heart ailment here.
questions.explain: हृदामये = in heart ailment; the fruit named for it is kuṭaja's.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 63 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words carry the framing and the praise of the fruits.
questions.rule: इह = here; हितम् = beneficial; हृदामये = in heart ailment; प्रवरम् = foremost.

questions.q: Put the diseases of verse 63 in the order the verse names them.
questions.explain: The verse runs: kuṣṭha, prameha, heart ailment, pāṇḍu.
questions.teaches: Verse 63 names four diseases in this order: kuṣṭha, prameha, heart ailment (hṛdāmaya), pāṇḍu.

questions.q: Which is the right split of हितमिक्ष्वाकुफलं?
optionExplain: मिक्ष्वाकु is not a word.
Right: Final म् simply joins a following vowel: हितम् + इ- = हितमि-.
अ + इ would give ए: हितमेक्ष्वाकु-.
ए before इ becomes अय् or अ, not -मि-.
questions.explain: हितम् (beneficial) + इक्ष्वाकु-फलम् (the ikṣvāku fruit).
questions.rule: म् + vowel: the म् joins the vowel (हितम् + इ = हितमि).

questions.q: Match each fruit of verse 63 to the disease it is named for.
questions.explain: Each clear fruit is tied to one disease in the verse.
questions.rule: इक्ष्वाकु → प्रमेह; कुटज → हृदामय; कौट → पाण्डु.

questions.q: प्रमेहिणाम् is the genitive plural of प्रमेहिन्. Which form means of the strong ones, from बलिन्?
optionExplain: The vowel stays short in -इनाम्.
This is the nominative plural or the genitive singular.
Right: An -इन् stem makes its genitive plural in -इनाम् (प्रमेहिणाम् has ण only because of the र before it).
This is the instrumental singular, 'by the strong one'.
questions.explain: प्रमेहिन् → प्रमेहिणाम्; बलिन् → बलिनाम्.
questions.teaches: Nouns in -इन् (प्रमेहिन्, बलिन्) form the genitive plural in -इनाम् (ण after र: प्रमेहिणाम्).

questions.q: Which taste does verse 64 name first for madana?
optionExplain: Sour is not named in verse 64.
Salty is not named in verse 64.
Bitter is named, but only with sweet and astringent.
Right: मधुरम् opens line 2: madana is sweet.
questions.explain: मधुरं सकषायतिक्तकम्: sweet, with astringent and bitter.
questions.rule: Madana: मधुर, with कषाय and तिक्त.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 64 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words give madana's qualities on the clear part of line 2.
questions.rule: मधुरम् = sweet; कषाय = astringent (taste); तिक्तक = bitter; अरूक्षम् = not dry.

questions.q: Put these words of verse 64 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Line 1 names kṛtavedhana, beneficial, then madana; line 2 gives madana's qualities: sweet, then not dry.
questions.teaches: Verse 64 first names kṛtavedhana as beneficial, then madana, then madana's qualities: sweet ... not dry.

questions.q: Which is the right split of तदरूक्षं?
optionExplain: Right: त् becomes द् before a vowel: तत् + अ- = तद-; अरूक्षम् = not dry.
त् before र becomes द्: that would print तद्रूक्षम्, and mean the opposite.
That would print तदारूक्षम्, with a long आ.
आ + अ would merge into आ: तदारूक्षम्.
questions.explain: तत् (that) + अरूक्षम् (not dry): madana is not dry.
questions.rule: त् → द् before a vowel; the vowel stays separate: तदरूक्षम्.

questions.q: In सकषायतिक्तकम् of verse 64, what does the first part स- add?
optionExplain: Without would be निर्- or अ-, not स-.
Right: स- = with: madana is sweet with astringent and bitter.
Very would be अति-, as in अतिगहन.
स- can mean 'same' in some words (सवर्ण), but the card reads it here as 'with': sweet, with astringent and bitter.
questions.explain: The card glosses स- as 'with': sweet, with astringent and bitter.
questions.rule: स- at the head of a compound = 'with, accompanied by'.

questions.q: Like अरूक्षम् (not dry) from रूक्षम्, which form means not sour, from अम्लम्?
optionExplain: Before a vowel the negative takes the form अन्-.
स- + अम्ल means 'with sour', not 'not sour'.
Right: The negative अ- becomes अन्- before a vowel: अन् + अम्लम् = अनम्लम्.
-तम means 'most': 'most sour'.
questions.explain: अ- before a consonant (अरूक्ष), अन्- before a vowel (अनम्ल).
questions.rule: Negative prefix: अ- before consonants, अन्- before vowels.
questions.teaches: The negative prefix is अ- before a consonant (अरूक्ष, not dry) and अन्- before a vowel (अनम्ल, not sour).

questions.q: In which use does verse 65 hold madana foremost?
optionExplain: The verse names āsthāpana, not anuvāsana.
Nasal medicine is not mentioned.
No ointment is mentioned.
Right: आस्थापनयोजनासु: in the applications of āsthāpana.
questions.explain: प्रवरं ... आस्थापनयोजनासु: foremost in applications of āsthāpana.

questions.q: Match each quality of madana in verse 65 to its meaning.
pairs: moving the wind in its natural direction
questions.explain: The four qualities that make madana foremost.
questions.rule: हृत् = removing; आशु = quick; निरपाय = without harm; अनुलोमि = moving in the natural direction.

questions.q: Put madana's qualities in the order verse 65 gives them.
questions.explain: Removing Kapha and Pitta, quick-acting, harmless, moving the wind rightly.
questions.teaches: Verse 65 lists madana's qualities: removes Kapha-Pitta, acts quickly, is harmless, moves the wind in its natural direction.

questions.q: Which is the right split of कफपित्तहृदाशुकारि?
optionExplain: Right: त् becomes द् before a vowel: हृत् + आशु- = हृदाशु-.
अ + आ would give आ with त kept: हृताशु-.
द् + अ would print हृदशु-, with a short अ.
शुकारि is not a word.
questions.explain: हृत् (removing) + आशुकारि (acting quickly).
questions.rule: त् → द् before a vowel: हृत् + आ = हृदा.

questions.q: In verse 65, what does अतः (therefore) point back to?
optionExplain: His wisdom is not the reason given.
Right: Because madana removes Kapha-Pitta, acts fast, is harmless and moves the wind rightly, it is foremost.
Kuṭaja is foremost in heart ailment, not the reason here.
No dose is stated in verse 65.
questions.explain: अतः links the qualities (line 1) to the ranking (line 2).

questions.q: By the rule of हृत् + आशु = हृदाशु, how do जगत् + ईशः join?
optionExplain: Before a vowel the त् turns voiced, द्.
त् becomes न् only before a nasal, and ई is not a nasal.
Right: त् becomes द् before a vowel, and the vowel stays: जगदीशः.
The vowel ई would not change to ए.
questions.explain: हृत् + आशु = हृदाशु; जगत् + ईशः = जगदीशः.
questions.rule: Final त् → द् before a vowel.
questions.teaches: A final त् becomes द् before a vowel (हृत् + आशुकारि = हृदाशुकारि; जगत् + ईशः = जगदीशः).

questions.q: What happens in unit 66?
options: The sage names a new fruit for basti use
The disciples leave the sage in silence
The sage puts a question to the disciples
After the sage stops, a request is made again
optionExplain: No fruit is named in unit 66.
Nobody leaves; a request is made.
The request comes from the disciple side, not from the sage.
Right: मुनिवृषभे ... स्थितवति विज्ञापयांबभूव भूयः: when the sage had stopped, he again made a request.
questions.explain: The unit is a bridge: the sage stops, the disciple asks again.
questions.rule: Unit 66: the sage stops speaking; a new request follows.
questions.section: बस्ति दोष कैसे हरती है: वायु ही कारण

questions.q: Match each word of unit 66 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words tell what the sage did and what followed.
questions.rule: निगद्य = having spoken; वाक्यम् = words; स्थितवति = when he had stopped; भूयः = again.
questions.section: बस्ति दोष कैसे हरती है: वायु ही कारण

questions.q: Put these words of unit 66 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: The sage, having spoken his words, stopped; then (he) made a request.
questions.teaches: Unit 66: the sage (मुनिवृषभे), having spoken (निगद्य) his words (वाक्यम्), stopped (स्थितवति); a request was made (विज्ञापयांबभूव).
questions.section: बस्ति दोष कैसे हरती है: वायु ही कारण

questions.q: What does वृषभ (bull) mean inside मुनिवृषभ in unit 66?
options: The best, the chief among sages
A bull that belongs to a sage
A sage who rides on a bull
The youngest sage of a group
optionExplain: Right: The card: 'bull among sages', an epithet for the chief sage.
The card reads it as an epithet, not an animal.
Riding is not in the word.
वृषभ in an epithet means the foremost, not the youngest.
questions.explain: X-वृषभ = the bull among X, the foremost of X.
questions.section: बस्ति दोष कैसे हरती है: वायु ही कारण

questions.q: In मुनिवृषभे ... स्थितवति, what do the two locatives express?
options: To whom the request was made
optionExplain: No place is named; the locatives give the time.
Right: A noun and participle in the locative give the time of the main action: 'when the sage had stopped'.
A person addressed is not put in this pair of locatives.
No reason for stopping is given.
questions.explain: Locative absolute: मुनिवृषभे स्थितवति = when the sage had stopped.
questions.section: बस्ति दोष कैसे हरती है: वायु ही कारण

questions.q: विज्ञापयांबभूव is a perfect built with -आम् + बभूव. Which invented form is built the same way?
optionExplain: This is the future, 'will cause to do'.
This is the absolutive, 'having caused to do'.
Right: -आम् + बभूव after a causative stem, like विज्ञापयांबभूव.
This is the -वत् past active participle.
questions.explain: Causative stems take the perfect with -आम् and an auxiliary (बभूव, चकार, आस).
questions.rule: Periphrastic perfect = stem + -आम् + बभूव / चकार / आस.
questions.teaches: Causative stems form the perfect with -आम् plus an auxiliary: विज्ञापयाम् बभूव, कारयाम् बभूव.
questions.section: बस्ति दोष कैसे हरती है: वायु ही कारण

questions.q: How does unit 67 describe the matter about to be asked (इदम्)?
optionExplain: The word is अतिगहन, very deep, the opposite of simple.
Nothing says it was settled; it is about to be asked.
Secrecy is not mentioned.
Right: अतिगहनम् = very deep, profound.
questions.explain: इदम् अतिगहनम् = this very profound (matter).
questions.section: बस्ति दोष कैसे हरती है: वायु ही कारण

questions.q: Match each word of unit 67 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words describe the matter and the posture of the disciple.
questions.rule: अतिगहनम् = very profound; अन्यशिष्यैः = other disciples; अवनिगतः = bowed to the ground; अग्रतः = in front; निधाय = having placed.
questions.section: बस्ति दोष कैसे हरती है: वायु ही कारण

questions.q: Put these words of unit 67 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: First the matter (this, very profound), then the company (with the other disciples), then the posture (bowed).
questions.teaches: Unit 67 names the matter first (इदम् अतिगहनम्), then the company (सह अन्यशिष्यैः) and the bow (अवनिगतः).
questions.section: बस्ति दोष कैसे हरती है: वायु ही कारण

questions.q: Which is the right split of सहान्यशिष्यैः?
optionExplain: Right: अ + अ merge into आ: सह + अन्य- = सहान्य-.
Neither सहा nor न्यशिष्य is a word.
अः before अ becomes ओ with avagraha: सहोऽन्य-.
Without a vowel to merge there would be no आ: सहन्य-.
questions.explain: सह (together with) + अन्य-शिष्यैः (other disciples).
questions.section: बस्ति दोष कैसे हरती है: वायु ही कारण

questions.q: Which case does सह (together with) take in unit 67?
optionExplain: इदम् is the object of the question, not the word with सह.
Right: अन्यशिष्यैः is instrumental plural, the case सह takes.
अवनिगतः describes the speaker himself.
That locative is in unit 66 and gives the time.
questions.explain: सह + instrumental: सह अन्यशिष्यैः = together with the other disciples.
questions.section: बस्ति दोष कैसे हरती है: वायु ही कारण

questions.q: Using the rule of सह अन्यशिष्यैः, which invented phrase means together with the teacher?
optionExplain: गुरुम् is accusative; सह takes the instrumental.
गुरूणाम् is genitive plural; सह takes the instrumental.
Right: गुरुणा is the instrumental of गुरु, the case सह takes.
गुरौ is locative.
questions.explain: सह + instrumental, whatever the noun: अन्यशिष्यैः सह, गुरुणा सह.
questions.teaches: सह ('together with') takes the instrumental: सह अन्यशिष्यैः, गुरुणा सह.
questions.section: बस्ति दोष कैसे हरती है: वायु ही कारण

questions.q: What do the disciples ask at the end of verse 68?
options: Which fruit is best for the basti
How long a basti must be held in
Who first taught the basti to men
How the basti drives away the doṣas
optionExplain: That was Agniveśa's earlier question (verse 62).
No time of holding is asked.
No first teacher is asked about.
Right: कथम् अपोहति दोषान्: how does it drive away the doṣas?
questions.explain: The question ends with कथम् अपोहति दोषान्.
questions.rule: Verse 68 asks: how does the basti remove the doṣas?
questions.section: बस्ति दोष कैसे हरती है: वायु ही कारण

questions.q: Match each word of verse 68 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are the clear words of the question.
questions.rule: गुरुणा = by the teacher; उक्तः = said; शीघ्रम् = quickly; कथम् = how; अपोहति = drives away.
questions.section: बस्ति दोष कैसे हरती है: वायु ही कारण

questions.q: Put these clear words of line 2 of verse 68 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Line 2 runs: quickly arrives ... from the body ... how ... the doṣas.
questions.teaches: Line 2 of verse 68: quickly arrives (शीघ्रम् आपतति) ... from the body (देहात्) ...; then the question: how (कथम्) does it drive away the doṣas (दोषान्)?
questions.section: बस्ति दोष कैसे हरती है: वायु ही कारण

questions.q: Which is the right split of गुरुणोक्तः?
optionExplain: Right: आ + उ merge into ओ: गुरुणा + उक्तः = गुरुणोक्तः.
क्तः is not a word.
अः before उ loses its visarga and stays apart: गुरुण उक्तः.
ए before उ becomes अय् or अ, not ओ.
questions.explain: गुरुणा (by the teacher) + उक्तः (said).
questions.section: बस्ति दोष कैसे हरती है: वायु ही कारण

questions.q: In गुरुणा उक्तः, what does the instrumental गुरुणा show?
options: To whom it was said: said to the teacher
Who did the saying: said by the teacher
From whom it came: taken from the teacher
About whom it was said: said of the teacher
optionExplain: The one addressed would be dative or accusative.
Right: With a past passive participle (उक्तः) the instrumental names the agent.
Source would be ablative (गुरोः).
The basti, not the teacher, is the subject spoken of.
questions.explain: Past passive participle + instrumental agent: गुरुणा उक्तः = said by the teacher.
questions.section: बस्ति दोष कैसे हरती है: वायु ही कारण

questions.q: On the model of गुरुणा उक्तः, which invented phrase means said by the sage (मुनि)?
optionExplain: मुनिम् is accusative.
मुनेः is genitive or ablative.
Right: मुनिना is the instrumental of मुनि, the agent with उक्तः.
मुनये is dative, 'to the sage'.
questions.explain: Agent in the instrumental with a passive participle: गुरुणा उक्तः, मुनिना उक्तः.
questions.teaches: With a past passive participle the doer stands in the instrumental: गुरुणा उक्तः, मुनिना उक्तः.
questions.section: बस्ति दोष कैसे हरती है: वायु ही कारण

questions.q: Who speaks in unit 69?
optionExplain: The disciple asked in the units before; here the teacher answers.
ऊचे is singular, and its subject is गुरुः.
No patient speaks.
Right: ऊचे गुरुः = the teacher said.
questions.explain: ऊचे (said) + गुरुः (the teacher).
questions.rule: Unit 69 opens the teacher's answer: ऊचे गुरुः.
questions.section: बस्ति दोष कैसे हरती है: वायु ही कारण

questions.q: Match each word of unit 69 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The speaking verb and the places named.
questions.rule: ऊचे = said; देहस्य = of the body; बहिः = outside; अन्तरे = within.
questions.section: बस्ति दोष कैसे हरती है: वायु ही कारण

questions.q: According to unit 69, to what is this (of the body) subject (वश्य)?
optionExplain: Right: मारुत-वश्यम्: subject to the wind.
Pitta is not named in unit 69.
Kapha is not named in unit 69.
The basti is not named in unit 69.
questions.explain: स्तिमित-मारुत-वश्यम्: subject to the (stimita) wind.
questions.rule: Unit 69: what is in the body is subject to the wind.
questions.teaches: The teacher's answer starts from the wind: what rests outside or within the body is subject to the wind (मारुत).
questions.section: बस्ति दोष कैसे हरती है: वायु ही कारण

questions.q: Which pair of places does unit 69 name for what is in the body?
options: In the branches or the storehouse
In the head or in the feet
In the belly or the heart
optionExplain: Those (शाखा, कोष्ठ) come in verse 71.
Right: बहिः ... अन्तरे वा: outside or within.
Head and feet are not named here.
Neither is named in unit 69.
questions.explain: यत् बहिः अपाश्रितम् अन्तरे वा = whatever rests outside or within.
questions.section: बस्ति दोष कैसे हरती है: वायु ही कारण

questions.q: Put these words of unit 69 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: The teacher said; subject to the wind; of the body; outside ...
questions.section: बस्ति दोष कैसे हरती है: वायु ही कारण

questions.q: Like देहस्य (of the body), which invented form means of the wind, from मारुत?
optionExplain: This is the accusative.
This is a dual form (instrumental, dative or ablative).
Right: An -अ noun makes its genitive singular in -अस्य, like देहस्य.
This is the locative, 'in the wind'.
questions.explain: देह → देहस्य; मारुत → मारुतस्य.
questions.teaches: Masculine -अ nouns form the genitive singular in -अस्य: देहस्य (of the body), मारुतस्य (of the wind).
questions.section: बस्ति दोष कैसे हरती है: वायु ही कारण

questions.q: What does the basti produce in the spoiled one, in unit 70?
options: Heat in the region of the belly
optionExplain: Heat is not mentioned.
Dryness is not mentioned.
Anulomatā is movement in the natural direction, not stopping.
Right: जनयन् अनुलोमताम्: producing the natural direction (anulomatā).
questions.explain: अनुलोमता = the natural direction; the basti produces it in the spoiled (wind).
questions.section: बस्ति दोष कैसे हरती है: वायु ही कारण

questions.q: Match each word of unit 70 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words carry the action of the basti.
questions.rule: दुष्टस्य = of the spoiled; जनयन् = producing; अनुलोमताम् = natural direction; हिनस्ति = destroys.
questions.section: बस्ति दोष कैसे हरती है: वायु ही कारण

questions.q: Put these words of unit 70 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Of that spoiled one, producing the natural direction, the basti destroys ...
questions.rule: दुष्टस्य · तस्य · जनयन् · अनुलोमतां · बस्तिः · हिनस्ति.
questions.teaches: Unit 70: of that spoiled (wind), producing the natural direction, the basti destroys (groups of diseases).
questions.section: बस्ति दोष कैसे हरती है: वायु ही कारण

questions.q: Which is the right split of बस्तिर्हिनस्ति?
optionExplain: Right: इः before a voiced sound (ह) becomes इर्: बस्तिर्हिनस्ति.
म् before ह would become an anusvara: बस्तिं हिनस्ति.
र्हिनस्ति is not a word.
That would print बस्तेर्हिनस्ति, with ए.
questions.explain: बस्तिः (the basti, subject) + हिनस्ति (destroys).
questions.rule: Visarga after इ/उ before a voiced sound → र्.
questions.section: बस्ति दोष कैसे हरती है: वायु ही कारण

questions.q: In unit 70, who is doing the producing (जनयन्)?
optionExplain: The wind is in the genitive (दुष्टस्य तस्य); it is what is acted on.
Right: जनयन् is nominative masculine and goes with बस्तिः, the subject of हिनस्ति.
The teacher is the speaker, not the subject of this sentence.
They are the object of हिनस्ति, in the accusative.
questions.explain: जनयन् (nom.) agrees with बस्तिः: the basti, producing the natural direction, destroys ...
questions.rule: A present participle agrees with its subject.
questions.section: बस्ति दोष कैसे हरती है: वायु ही कारण

questions.q: Like जनयन् (producing) beside जनयति, which form means 'going' beside गच्छति?
optionExplain: This is the absolutive, 'having gone'.
This is the infinitive, 'to go'.
Right: The present participle masculine nominative singular ends in -अन्: जनयन्, गच्छन्.
This is the past participle, 'gone'.
questions.explain: जनयति → जनयन्; गच्छति → गच्छन्.
questions.rule: Present participle (m. nom. sg.) = present stem + -न्.
questions.teaches: The present participle 'X-ing' (m. nom. sg.) is the present stem + न्: जनयन् (producing), गच्छन् (going).
questions.section: बस्ति दोष कैसे हरती है: वायु ही कारण

questions.q: According to verse 71, what is the cause in the origin of these diseases?
optionExplain: Pitta is not named in verse 71.
Neither is named as the cause here.
The verse names one cause only: wind.
Right: न तु कश्चिद् अन्यो वायोः परं ... हेतुः: no other cause beyond wind.
questions.explain: वायोः परम् न कश्चिद् अन्यः हेतुः: there is no cause other than wind.
questions.rule: Verse 71: of diseases everywhere, the cause is wind.
questions.section: बस्ति दोष कैसे हरती है: वायु ही कारण

questions.q: Match each word of verse 71 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The places of disease and the words of the conclusion.
questions.rule: शाखा = branch; कोष्ठ = storehouse; मर्म = vital spot; हेतुः = cause; जन्मनि = in origin.
questions.section: बस्ति दोष कैसे हरती है: वायु ही कारण

questions.q: Put the places of diseases in the order verse 71 names them.
questions.explain: Branches, storehouse, then vital spots, the upper (parts), all parts and limbs.
questions.teaches: Verse 71 lists the places of disease: śākhā, koṣṭha, marma, the upper parts, all parts and limbs.
questions.section: बस्ति दोष कैसे हरती है: वायु ही कारण

questions.q: Which is the right split of कोष्ठगताश्च?
optionExplain: Right: आः before च becomes आश्: कोष्ठगताश्च.
न् before च would give an anusvara with श्: कोष्ठगतांश्च.
म् before च would become an anusvara: कोष्ठगतं च.
अश्च is not a word.
questions.explain: कोष्ठगताः (gone to the storehouse, nom. pl., with रोगाः) + च (and).
questions.section: बस्ति दोष कैसे हरती है: वायु ही कारण

questions.q: Which of these does verse 71 name as places of diseases?
optionExplain: Named at the head of the long compound.
Named first.
Named second.
The navel is named in verse 68, not here.
No such place is named.
questions.explain: Verse 71: śākhā, koṣṭha, marma, the upper parts, all parts and limbs.
questions.rule: Places named: शाखा, कोष्ठ, मर्म, ऊर्ध्व, सर्व अवयव-अङ्ग.
questions.section: बस्ति दोष कैसे हरती है: वायु ही कारण

questions.q: वायोः परम् puts वायु in the ablative (beyond wind). Which invented phrase means other than honey?
optionExplain: मधु is nominative or accusative.
Right: मधुनः is the ablative of मधु; अन्य and पर take the ablative.
मधुना is instrumental.
मधुनि is locative.
questions.explain: 'Other than / beyond X' takes X in the ablative: वायोः परम्, मधुनः अन्यत्.
questions.teaches: Words meaning 'other than, beyond' (अन्य, पर) take the ablative: वायोः परम्, मधुनः अन्यत्.
questions.section: बस्ति दोष कैसे हरती है: वायु ही कारण

questions.q: What does verse 72 say wind does to the accumulations of wastes?
optionExplain: Burning and digesting are not named.
Cooling and hardening are not named.
Right: विक्षेप-संहार-करः: the doer of scattering and gathering.
Hiding and storing are not named.
questions.explain: विक्षेप = scattering; संहार = gathering; कर = doer.
questions.section: बस्ति दोष कैसे हरती है: वायु ही कारण

questions.q: Match each word of verse 72 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words carry what wind does and the claim about basti.
questions.rule: विक्षेप = scattering; संहार = gathering; अतिवृद्धस्य = of the greatly increased; भेषजम् = remedy; समम् = equal.
questions.section: बस्ति दोष कैसे हरती है: वायु ही कारण

questions.q: Which remedy does verse 72 say has no equal for the greatly increased wind?
optionExplain: Madana is praised in verse 65, for āsthāpana; it is not named here.
Kuṭaja is for heart ailment (verse 63), not named here.
Nasal medicine is not mentioned.
Right: नान्यद् बस्तेः समं भेषजम्: no other remedy equal to basti.
questions.explain: बस्तेः (than basti) समम् (equal) न अन्यत् भेषजम्.
questions.rule: Verse 72: for increased wind no remedy equals basti.
questions.teaches: Verse 72 says that for pacifying greatly increased wind there is no remedy equal to basti.
questions.section: बस्ति दोष कैसे हरती है: वायु ही कारण

questions.q: Which is the right split of विक्षेपसंहारकरो हि?
optionExplain: Right: अः before a voiced sound (ह) becomes ओ: करो हि.
म् before ह would become an anusvara: करं हि.
ए stays ए before ह: करे हि.
आः before a voiced sound drops the visarga: करा हि.
questions.explain: विक्षेपसंहारकरः (doer of scattering and gathering) + हि (for).
questions.section: बस्ति दोष कैसे हरती है: वायु ही कारण

questions.q: Put these words of line 2 of verse 72 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Of that greatly increased (wind) ... no other ... than basti ... remedy ... because.
questions.rule: तस्य · अतिवृद्धस्य · (न) अन्यत् · बस्तेः · (समं) भेषजम् · (अस्ति) यस्मात्.
questions.section: बस्ति दोष कैसे हरती है: वायु ही कारण

questions.q: नान्यद् is न + अन्यत्. By the same rule, how do न + अस्ति join?
optionExplain: ओ is not made from अ + अ.
Right: अ + अ merge into आ: न + अस्ति = नास्ति.
The two vowels merge into a long आ, not a short अ.
ए comes from अ + इ, not अ + अ.
questions.explain: न + अन्यत् = नान्यत्; न + अस्ति = नास्ति.
questions.teaches: Two short अ vowels merge into आ: न + अन्यत् = नान्यत्, न + अस्ति = नास्ति.
questions.section: बस्ति दोष कैसे हरती है: वायु ही कारण

questions.q: What do some (एके) call basti, according to verse 73?
options: Only a small aid to treatment
optionExplain: The verse ranks it far higher.
A quarter is not mentioned.
Right: सर्वां चिकित्साम् अपि बस्तिम् एके: some (call) basti even the whole treatment.
Kapha is pacified with the wind; the verse does not limit basti to it.
questions.explain: They say 'half of treatment'; some say even 'the whole treatment'.
questions.rule: Basti = चिकित्सार्ध; for some, सर्वा चिकित्सा.
questions.section: बस्ति दोष कैसे हरती है: वायु ही कारण

questions.q: Match each word of verse 73 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words carry the reasoning and the claim.
questions.rule: शाम्यन्ति = are pacified; यत्नेन = with effort; जिते = when conquered; ईरिताः = stirred; अर्धम् = half.
questions.section: बस्ति दोष कैसे हरती है: वायु ही कारण

questions.q: Put the steps of verse 73's reasoning in order.
items: उससे प्रेरित पित्त-कफ आदि भी शान्त
कुछ के मत में: सम्पूर्ण चिकित्सा
questions.explain: Wind conquered → Pitta, Kapha stirred by it also pacified → therefore half of treatment → for some, the whole.
questions.rule: जिते अनिले · शाम्यन्ति पित्तकफादयः · तस्मात् चिकित्सार्धम् · सर्वां चिकित्साम् एके.
questions.teaches: Verse 73 argues: conquer the wind and what it stirs is pacified too; so basti is half of treatment, for some the whole.
questions.section: बस्ति दोष कैसे हरती है: वायु ही कारण

questions.q: Which is the right split of पित्तकफादयोऽपि?
optionExplain: अ + अ would merge into आ: -यापि.
म् would join the vowel: -यमपि.
पि is not a word.
Right: अः before अ becomes ओ and the अ is marked by avagraha: -यो ऽपि.
questions.explain: पित्तकफादयः (Pitta, Kapha and the rest) + अपि (also).
questions.section: बस्ति दोष कैसे हरती है: वायु ही कारण

questions.q: Why are Pitta and Kapha pacified when the wind is conquered, per verse 73?
options: They are stirred by the wind
Basti removes them from the head
They were never increased at all
Madana dries them out at once
optionExplain: Right: तदीरिताः: stirred by it (the wind); with it conquered, they settle.
No head is named in verse 73.
The verse says they are pacified, so they were stirred.
Madana is not named in verse 73.
questions.explain: तत्-ईरिताः = stirred by it: they follow the wind.
questions.rule: Wind conquered → what it stirred is pacified.
questions.section: बस्ति दोष कैसे हरती है: वायु ही कारण

questions.q: जिते अनिले means 'when the wind is conquered'. Which invented phrase means when the sun has risen?
optionExplain: This is a plain statement: 'the sun (has) risen'.
Right: Participle and noun both in the locative: the time of the main action.
This is instrumental: 'by the risen sun'.
This is accusative: 'the risen sun' as an object.
questions.explain: Locative absolute: जिते अनिले, उदिते सूर्ये.
questions.teaches: A noun with a participle, both in the locative, means 'when ...': जिते अनिले (when wind is conquered), उदिते सूर्ये (when the sun has risen).
questions.section: बस्ति दोष कैसे हरती है: वायु ही कारण

questions.q: What does verse 74 compare the basti's drawing of the doṣas to?
options: A river carrying all the mud down to the sea
Fire burning up the dry grass of a whole field
The sun drawing up the juices of the earth
Wind scattering the clouds across the whole sky
optionExplain: No river is named; the simile is the sun (अर्कः).
No fire is named in verse 74.
Right: अर्को भूरसानिव: like the sun (draws) the juices of the earth.
No clouds are named; the verse names the sun and the earth.
questions.explain: The simile: as the sun draws the juices (रसान्) of the earth (भू), the basti draws the doṣas.
questions.rule: Verse 74: basti draws the doṣas like the sun the earth's juices.
questions.section: बस्ति-वीर्य का प्रसार; बस्ति प्रधान कर्म

questions.q: Match each word of verse 74 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words carry the place, the reach, the means and the simile.
questions.rule: पक्वाशयस्थः = staying in the pakvāśaya; आपादमस्तकम् = foot to head; वीर्येण = by potency; आदत्ते = draws; भूरसान् = earth's juices.
questions.section: बस्ति-वीर्य का प्रसार; बस्ति प्रधान कर्म

questions.q: Put these phrases of verse 74 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Staying in the pakvāśaya, the doṣas from foot to head, by potency, the basti draws, like the earth's juices.
questions.teaches: Verse 74 runs: though in the pakvāśaya, the doṣas from foot to head, by its potency, the basti draws, like (the sun) the earth's juices.
questions.section: बस्ति-वीर्य का प्रसार; बस्ति प्रधान कर्म

questions.q: Which is the right split of बस्तिरादत्ते?
optionExplain: रादत्ते is not a word.
म् would join the vowel: बस्तिमादत्ते.
That would print बस्तेरादत्ते, with ए.
Right: इः before a vowel becomes इर्: बस्तिः + आ- = बस्तिरा-.
questions.explain: बस्तिः (the basti, subject) + आदत्ते (draws).
questions.rule: Visarga after इ before a vowel or voiced sound → र्.
questions.section: बस्ति-वीर्य का प्रसार; बस्ति प्रधान कर्म

questions.q: By what means does the basti draw the doṣas, according to verse 74?
options: By being held for a long time
By moving up into the head
By the heat of the sun
optionExplain: Right: वीर्येण = by potency: the instrumental names the means.
No time of holding is stated in verse 74.
The basti stays in the pakvāśaya (-स्थः); it draws from there.
The sun is only the simile, not the means.
questions.explain: पक्वाशयस्थोऽपि ... वीर्येण बस्तिरादत्ते: staying below, it draws by potency.
questions.section: बस्ति-वीर्य का प्रसार; बस्ति प्रधान कर्म

questions.q: पक्वाशयस्थ means staying in the pakvāśaya. On that model, what does the invented जलस्थः mean?
optionExplain: Giving would be -द (जलद).
Right: -स्थ at the end of a compound means 'staying in, situated in' the first member.
Born from would be -ज (जलज).
Without would be निर्- (निर्जल).
questions.explain: X-स्थ = staying in X: पक्वाशयस्थ, जलस्थ.
questions.teaches: -स्थ at the end of a compound means 'staying in': पक्वाशयस्थ (in the pakvāśaya), जलस्थ (in water).
questions.section: बस्ति-वीर्य का प्रसार; बस्ति प्रधान कर्म

questions.q: What is spoken of at the start of verse 75 (यत् तत्र ...)?
options: The taste of the food eaten
The heat of the patient's body
The potency of the drug there
The length of the basti nozzle
optionExplain: No food or taste is named in verse 75.
No heat is named in verse 75.
Right: यत् तत्र औषधवीर्यम्: the potency (vīrya) of the drug that is there.
No nozzle or measure is named in verse 75.
questions.explain: औषध = drug; वीर्य = potency: the subject is the drug's potency.
questions.rule: Verse 75 begins with औषधवीर्य, the potency of the drug.
questions.section: बस्ति-वीर्य का प्रसार; बस्ति प्रधान कर्म

questions.q: Match each word of verse 75 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are the clear words of verse 75.
questions.rule: तत्र = there; औषध = drug; वीर्यम् = potency; अचिरात् = soon; प्रतिपद्यते = obtains.
questions.section: बस्ति-वीर्य का प्रसार; बस्ति प्रधान कर्म

questions.q: Put these words of verse 75 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The drug's potency, by the wind, fully, very soon, samāna obtains.
questions.rule: औषधवीर्यं · वायुना · पर्याप्तम् · अचिरादेव · समानः · प्रतिपद्यते.
questions.teaches: Verse 75 runs: the potency of the drug ... by the wind, fully, very soon, samāna obtains (it).
questions.section: बस्ति-वीर्य का प्रसार; बस्ति प्रधान कर्म

questions.q: What does वीर्य mean in औषधवीर्यम् of verse 75?
options: The seed of the drug plant
optionExplain: A seed is not meant; the card gives potency.
Plain वीर्य can mean semen in Hindi, but here it is potency.
No physician is named in verse 75.
Right: The card: वीर्य = potency, शक्ति, the power of the drug.
questions.explain: Here वीर्य = potency (वीर्य यानी शक्ति), not semen.
questions.rule: औषधवीर्य = the potency of the drug.
questions.section: बस्ति-वीर्य का प्रसार; बस्ति प्रधान कर्म

questions.q: Which wind does verse 75 name as soon obtaining the drug's potency?
optionExplain: Right: अचिरादेव समानः प्रतिपद्यते: very soon samāna obtains (it).
Prāṇa is not named in verse 75; it comes in 05.05.150.
Udāna is not named in verse 75.
Vyāna follows only after samāna, in 05.05.146.
questions.explain: The potency passes to samāna first; vyāna and the rest follow in the next verse.
questions.section: बस्ति-वीर्य का प्रसार; बस्ति प्रधान कर्म

questions.q: By the rule of अचिरात् + एव = अचिरादेव, how do the invented तस्मात् + एव join?
optionExplain: Before a vowel the त् turns voiced, द्.
Right: त् becomes द् before a vowel, and the vowel stays: तस्मादेव.
त् becomes न् only before a nasal; ए is not a nasal.
No य् comes in; the vowel ए joins the द्.
questions.explain: अचिरात् + एव = अचिरादेव; तस्मात् + एव = तस्मादेव.
questions.rule: Final त् → द् before a vowel.
questions.teaches: A final त् becomes द् before a vowel: अचिरात् + एव = अचिरादेव; तस्मात् + एव = तस्मादेव.
questions.section: बस्ति-वीर्य का प्रसार; बस्ति प्रधान कर्म

questions.q: Which wind does verse 76 name first after samāna?
optionExplain: Prāṇa is not named in verse 76.
Udāna is not named in verse 76.
Right: व्यानाद्याः पवनाः: the winds beginning with vyāna.
The verse names vyāna and those that follow it.
questions.explain: समानात् उत्तरम् ... व्यानाद्याः: after samāna, those beginning with vyāna.
questions.rule: After samāna: vyāna and the rest, in order.
questions.section: बस्ति-वीर्य का प्रसार; बस्ति प्रधान कर्म

questions.q: Match each word of verse 76 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are the clear words of verse 76.
questions.rule: उत्तरम् = after; पवनाः = winds; क्रमात् = in order; प्रकृतिम् = natural state; अनुग्रहे = in the support.
questions.section: बस्ति-वीर्य का प्रसार; बस्ति प्रधान कर्म

questions.q: Put these phrases of verse 76 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: After samāna, the winds from vyāna, in order; they go to their natural state, standing in the body's support.
questions.rule: समानादुत्तरं · व्यानाद्याः पवनाः · क्रमात् · (ते ...) प्रकृतिं यान्ति · शरीरानुग्रहे स्थिताः.
questions.teaches: Verse 76: after samāna, the winds beginning with vyāna, in order; they go to their natural state, standing in the support of the body.
questions.section: बस्ति-वीर्य का प्रसार; बस्ति प्रधान कर्म

questions.q: Which is the right split of व्यानाद्याः?
optionExplain: त् would become द् and stay: व्यानादाद्याः.
अः before a vowel loses its visarga and stays apart: व्यान आद्याः.
म् would join the vowel: व्यानमाद्याः.
Right: अ + आ merge into आ: व्यान + आद्याः = व्यानाद्याः.
questions.explain: व्यान + आद्याः (those beginning with) = व्यानाद्याः.
questions.section: बस्ति-वीर्य का प्रसार; बस्ति प्रधान कर्म

questions.q: According to verse 76, to what do the winds go?
options: Out of the body through the mouth
optionExplain: Right: प्रकृतिं यान्ति: they go to their natural state.
No leaving of the body is stated.
Increase is the opposite of returning to prakṛti.
The pakvāśaya is not named in verse 76.
questions.explain: प्रकृति = the natural state; the winds return to it while supporting the body.
questions.rule: Verse 76: the winds go to their natural state (प्रकृति).
questions.section: बस्ति-वीर्य का प्रसार; बस्ति प्रधान कर्म

questions.q: व्यानाद्याः means the winds beginning with vyāna. What does the invented प्राणाद्याः mean?
optionExplain: Ending with would be -अन्त (प्राणान्ताः).
Right: X-आद्य at the end of a compound = 'beginning with X'.
After would be प्राणात् उत्तरम्, as with samāna here.
-आद्य includes the others that follow.
questions.explain: व्यानाद्याः = vyāna and the rest; प्राणाद्याः = prāṇa and the rest.
questions.teaches: -आद्य at the end of a compound means 'beginning with X, and the rest': व्यानाद्याः, प्राणाद्याः.
questions.section: बस्ति-वीर्य का प्रसार; बस्ति प्रधान कर्म

questions.q: What do the winds do with Pitta and phlegm in verse 77?
options: Drive both out through the mouth
Mix the two into a single doṣa
Place each in its own place
optionExplain: Nothing is driven out in verse 77.
No mixing is stated; each goes to its own place.
Right: यथास्थानं निवेश्य: having placed (them) each in its place.
They are settled each in its own place (यथास्थानं निवेश्य), not increased.
questions.explain: पित्तश्लेष्माणौ यथास्थानं निवेश्य: Pitta and phlegm, each set in its own place.
questions.rule: Verse 77: Pitta and phlegm are placed back, each in its own place.
questions.section: बस्ति-वीर्य का प्रसार; बस्ति प्रधान कर्म

questions.q: Match each word of verse 77 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are the clear words of verse 77.
questions.rule: यथास्थानम् = each in its place; निवेश्य = having placed; परितः = all around; स्वान् स्वान् = each its own; तनौ = in the body.
questions.section: बस्ति-वीर्य का प्रसार; बस्ति प्रधान कर्म

questions.q: Put these words of verse 77 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Pitta and phlegm, each in its place, having placed; all around, the qualities of the bhūtas, in the body.
questions.rule: पित्तश्लेष्माणौ · यथास्थानं · निवेश्य च · (संतर्पयन्ति) परितः · (स्वान्स्वान्) भूतगुणान् · तनौ.
questions.teaches: Verse 77: Pitta and phlegm, each in its place, having been placed; then all around, their own bhūta-qualities, in the body.
questions.section: बस्ति-वीर्य का प्रसार; बस्ति प्रधान कर्म

questions.q: पित्तश्लेष्माणौ and तनौ both end in -औ. What is तनौ in verse 77?
options: Dual number: the Pitta and the phlegm
optionExplain: The card glosses तनौ as 'in the body', f. loc. sg.; only पित्तश्लेष्माणौ is dual.
The accusative plural of तनु would be तनूः.
That is पित्तश्लेष्माणौ, the dvandva of two doṣas.
Right: तनु is an उ-stem; its locative singular is तनौ, 'in the body'.
questions.explain: -औ is not always dual: पित्तश्लेष्माणौ is dual (two doṣas), तनौ is locative singular.
questions.rule: -औ: dual of most stems, but locative singular of इ/उ stems (तनौ).
questions.section: बस्ति-वीर्य का प्रसार; बस्ति प्रधान कर्म

questions.q: Who places Pitta and phlegm in their places in verse 77?
options: The winds of the verse before
Pitta itself, by its own heat
optionExplain: Right: The data: the subject is the winds of 05.05.146-147 (vyāna and the rest).
No physician is named in verse 77.
Pitta is the object (accusative), not the doer.
No food is named in verse 77.
questions.explain: पित्तश्लेष्माणौ is accusative; the doers are the winds carried over from verse 76.
questions.rule: Subject of verse 77 = the winds (from verse 76).
questions.section: बस्ति-वीर्य का प्रसार; बस्ति प्रधान कर्म

questions.q: निवेश्य (having placed) has a prefix (नि-), so it ends in -य. Which form means having understood, from वि-√ज्ञा?
optionExplain: -त्वा is used without a prefix (ज्ञात्वा); with वि- it becomes -य.
Right: With a prefix the absolutive takes -य: वि-ज्ञा-य, like नि-वेश्य.
This is the infinitive, 'to understand'.
This is the past participle, 'understood'.
questions.explain: Prefix + root → -य (निवेश्य, विज्ञाय); bare root → -त्वा (ज्ञात्वा).
questions.rule: Absolutive: -त्वा without a prefix, -य with a prefix.
questions.teaches: The absolutive ('having X-ed') ends in -त्वा on a bare root (ज्ञात्वा) and in -य after a prefix (निवेश्य, विज्ञाय).
questions.section: बस्ति-वीर्य का प्रसार; बस्ति प्रधान कर्म

questions.q: Which way does apāna draw, according to verse 78?
optionExplain: Upward (ऊर्ध्वम्) is said of prāṇa.
Crosswise (तिर्यक्) is said of vyāna.
Right: अपानोऽधः: apāna (draws) downward.
No circular movement is named.
questions.explain: व्यानः तिर्यक्, अपानः अधः, प्राणः ऊर्ध्वम्.
questions.section: बस्ति-वीर्य का प्रसार; बस्ति प्रधान कर्म

questions.q: Match each wind of verse 78 to the direction it draws.
questions.explain: Each wind has its own direction in verse 78.
questions.rule: व्यान → तिर्यक् (crosswise); अपान → अधः (down); प्राण → ऊर्ध्वम् (up).
questions.section: बस्ति-वीर्य का प्रसार; बस्ति प्रधान कर्म

questions.q: Put these phrases of verse 78 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Vyāna crosswise, apāna down, prāṇa up, draws; each by its own way; through channels.
questions.rule: व्यानस्तिर्यक् · अपानोऽधः · प्राणश्चोर्ध्वं · प्रकर्षति · यथास्वमेव · नाडीभिः.
questions.teaches: Verse 78 names vyāna (crosswise), apāna (down), prāṇa (up), then the verb, then 'each its own way' and the channels.
questions.section: बस्ति-वीर्य का प्रसार; बस्ति प्रधान कर्म

questions.q: What is the simile of verse 78?
options: The sun drawing up the earth's juices
A fire spreading through dry wood
A wind driving the clouds about
optionExplain: That simile is in verse 74, for the basti in the pakvāśaya.
No fire is named in verse 78.
No clouds are named in verse 78.
Right: नाडीभिर्हारिणीभिरिवोदकम्: like water through carrying channels.
questions.explain: उदकम् ... इव = like water; नाडीभिः हारिणीभिः = through carrying channels.
questions.rule: Verse 78 simile: water in channels (verse 74: sun and earth's juices).
questions.section: बस्ति-वीर्य का प्रसार; बस्ति प्रधान कर्म

questions.q: Three winds are named, yet प्रकर्षति (draws) is singular. How does the card explain it?
options: Each wind draws: the verb goes with each
Only prāṇa draws; the others are still
The three winds form one compound noun
प्रकर्षति is really a plural form
optionExplain: Right: The data: the singular verb is shared, understood with each singular subject.
Each wind is given its own direction of drawing.
They are three separate nominatives, each with its own direction word.
The gram label is 3 sg. pres.; the plural would be प्रकर्षन्ति.
questions.explain: व्यानः ... अपानः ... प्राणः च प्रकर्षति: each one draws, in its own direction.
questions.rule: One singular verb can serve several singular subjects, each taken separately.
questions.section: बस्ति-वीर्य का प्रसार; बस्ति प्रधान कर्म

questions.q: By the rule of व्यानः + तिर्यक् = व्यानस्तिर्यक्, how do the invented रामः + तत्र join?
optionExplain: -अः → -ओ happens before a voiced sound; त is unvoiced.
Right: Visarga becomes स् before त: रामस्तत्र.
र् comes from इः/उः before voiced sounds, not from अः before त.
श् comes before च/छ; before त it is स्.
questions.explain: व्यानः + तिर्यक् = व्यानस्तिर्यक्; रामः + तत्र = रामस्तत्र.
questions.teaches: A visarga becomes स् before त or थ: व्यानः + तिर्यक् = व्यानस्तिर्यक्; रामः + तत्र = रामस्तत्र.
questions.section: बस्ति-वीर्य का प्रसार; बस्ति प्रधान कर्म

questions.q: What does the well-applied basti destroy, according to verse 79?
optionExplain: Fever is not named in verse 79.
Worms are not named in verse 79.
Right: हन्ति सुकृच्छ्रानपि यक्ष्मणः: it destroys even the very difficult yakṣmans (wasting diseases).
Swellings are not named in verse 79.
questions.explain: यक्ष्मन् = wasting disease (tuberculosis-type, probable); सुकृच्छ्र = very difficult.
questions.rule: Verse 79: basti destroys even very difficult yakṣmans.
questions.section: बस्ति-वीर्य का प्रसार; बस्ति प्रधान कर्म

questions.q: Match each word of verse 79 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words carry the action of the basti in verse 79.
questions.rule: सुयोजितः = well applied; व्याप्नुवन् = pervading; प्रसभम् = forcibly; हन्ति = destroys; सुकृच्छ्रान् = very difficult.
questions.section: बस्ति-वीर्य का प्रसार; बस्ति प्रधान कर्म

questions.q: Put these phrases of verse 79 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: By the sirās, the body, the well-applied basti, pervading, forcibly destroys even the very difficult yakṣmans.
questions.rule: सिराभिश्च · वपुः · बस्तिः सुयोजितः · व्याप्नुवन् · प्रसभं हन्ति · सुकृच्छ्रानपि यक्ष्मणः.
questions.teaches: Verse 79 runs: by the sirās, the body, the well-applied basti, pervading, forcibly destroys even the very difficult yakṣmans.
questions.section: बस्ति-वीर्य का प्रसार; बस्ति प्रधान कर्म

questions.q: Which is the right split of वपुर्बस्तिः?
optionExplain: र्बस्तिः is not a word.
म् before ब would give an anusvara: वपुं बस्तिः.
That would print वपोर्बस्तिः, with ओ.
Right: उः before a voiced sound (ब) becomes उर्: वपुर्बस्तिः.
questions.explain: वपुः (the body, object of व्याप्नुवन्) + बस्तिः (the basti, subject).
questions.rule: Visarga after उ before a voiced sound → र्.
questions.section: बस्ति-वीर्य का प्रसार; बस्ति प्रधान कर्म

questions.q: In verse 79, what does the basti pervade (व्याप्नुवन्)?
optionExplain: Right: The data: the body is the object of व्याप्नुवन्.
सिराभिः is instrumental: the sirās are the way, not what is pervaded.
यक्ष्मणः are the object of हन्ति (destroys).
The basti pervades the body; the pakvāśaya is not named in verse 79.
questions.explain: वपुः व्याप्नुवन्: pervading the body; यक्ष्मणः हन्ति: destroys the yakṣmans.
questions.rule: Two objects: वपुः (of व्याप्नुवन्), यक्ष्मणः (of हन्ति).
questions.section: बस्ति-वीर्य का प्रसार; बस्ति प्रधान कर्म

questions.q: सु- means well or very, as in सुयोजितः (well applied). What does the invented सुपक्वम् mean?
optionExplain: Badly would be दुष्- (दुष्पक्व).
Right: सु- (well) + पक्व (cooked) = well cooked.
Not cooked would be अपक्व.
Again would be पुनः, not सु-.
questions.explain: सु-योजित = well applied; सु-कृच्छ्र = very difficult; सु-पक्व = well cooked.
questions.teaches: The prefix सु- means 'well, very': सुयोजित (well applied), सुकृच्छ्र (very difficult), सुपक्व (well cooked).
questions.section: बस्ति-वीर्य का प्रसार; बस्ति प्रधान कर्म

questions.q: What does unit 80 call the basti?
options: A last resort when all else fails
optionExplain: Unit 80 limits basti to no single doṣa.
Unit 80 calls it chief, not a last resort.
Right: सर्वकर्मप्रधानम्: chief (प्रधान) of all procedures (कर्म).
प्रधान ranks it above them.
questions.explain: बस्तिः ... सर्वकर्मप्रधानम्: basti is the chief of all procedures.
questions.section: बस्ति-वीर्य का प्रसार; बस्ति प्रधान कर्म

questions.q: Match each word of unit 80 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words carry the conclusion of unit 80.
questions.rule: तस्मात् = therefore; कर्म = procedure; प्रधानम् = chief; हन्ति = destroys; निःशेषतः = completely.
questions.section: बस्ति-वीर्य का प्रसार; बस्ति प्रधान कर्म

questions.q: Put these words of unit 80 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Basti, therefore, chief of all procedures; the all-ending ones it destroys, and completely.
questions.rule: बस्तिः · तस्मात् · सर्वकर्मप्रधानं · सर्वान्तकान् · हन्ति · निःशेषतश्च.
questions.teaches: Unit 80 runs: basti, therefore, (is) chief of all procedures; it destroys the all-ending (ones) completely.
questions.section: बस्ति-वीर्य का प्रसार; बस्ति प्रधान कर्म

questions.q: Which word is wrong in this rendering of unit 80: Therefore basti is the chief of all procedures, and it destroys the all-ending ones partly?
optionExplain: तस्मात् = therefore: correct.
प्रधानम् = chief: correct.
कर्म = procedures: correct.
Right: निःशेषतः means completely, 'without remainder', not partly.
questions.explain: निःशेषतः = completely; the rest of the line is rendered rightly.
questions.section: बस्ति-वीर्य का प्रसार; बस्ति प्रधान कर्म

questions.q: Why can प्रधानम् be neuter though बस्तिः is masculine, per the card?
options: बस्ति is really a neuter noun
It is a printing error to correct
optionExplain: Right: The data: a predicate noun keeps its own gender; it need not agree with the subject.
The gram label of बस्तिः is m. nom. sg.
No text_flag is raised; the data explains the gender.
सर्वान्तकान् is masculine accusative plural.
questions.explain: बस्तिः (m.) ... प्रधानम् (n.): 'basti is the chief'; the predicate noun keeps its gender.
questions.rule: A predicate noun need not share the subject's gender.
questions.section: बस्ति-वीर्य का प्रसार; बस्ति प्रधान कर्म

questions.q: निःशेषतः is built on निः- (without) + शेष (remainder). What does the invented निःशब्दम् mean?
optionExplain: Much would be बहु-, not निः-.
Right: निः- = without; शब्द = sound: without sound.
By means of would be the instrumental शब्देन.
निः- takes the thing away; it does not name it.
questions.explain: निः-शेष = without remainder; निः-शब्द = without sound.
questions.teaches: The prefix निः- (निर्-, निस्-) means 'without': निःशेष (without remainder, completely), निःशब्द (without sound).
questions.section: बस्ति-वीर्य का प्रसार; बस्ति प्रधान कर्म

questions.q: What does शोधयित्वा in unit 81 mean?
optionExplain: Heating would be from √तप्, not √शुध्.
Binding would be from √बन्ध्.
Right: शोधयित्वा = having cleansed (absolutive of the causative of √शुध्).
Drinking would be पीत्वा, from √पा.
questions.explain: शुध् = to be clean; causative शोधय- = to cleanse; -इत्वा = having done.
questions.section: बस्ति-वीर्य का प्रसार; बस्ति प्रधान कर्म

questions.q: Match each word of unit 81 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are the clear words of unit 81.
questions.rule: शोधयित्वा = having cleansed; कुर्यात् = would make; शुक्र = semen; देह = body; अग्नि = digestive fire.
questions.section: बस्ति-वीर्य का प्रसार; बस्ति प्रधान कर्म

questions.q: Put these words of unit 81 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Having cleansed, it would make (the brightness of) semen, body and digestive fire.
questions.rule: शोधयित्वा · (च) कुर्यात् · (दोषान् तेजः) शुक्र- · देह- · अग्नि-(दीप्तिम्).
questions.teaches: Unit 81 runs: having cleansed, it would make ... the brightness of semen, body and digestive fire.
questions.section: बस्ति-वीर्य का प्रसार; बस्ति प्रधान कर्म

questions.q: Which is the right split of कुर्याद्दोषान्?
optionExplain: म् before द would give an anusvara: कुर्यां दोषान्.
आः before a voiced sound loses its visarga: कुर्या दोषान्.
द्दोषान् is not a word.
Right: त् becomes द् before the voiced द: कुर्याद्दोषान्.
questions.explain: कुर्यात् (would make) + दोषान् (the doṣas).
questions.rule: Final त् → द् before a voiced consonant.
questions.section: बस्ति-वीर्य का प्रसार; बस्ति प्रधान कर्म

questions.q: Which of these does the brightness compound (-दीप्तिम्) of unit 81 name? Choose all that apply.
optionExplain: Right: देह is a member.
Wrong: the eyes are not named in unit 81.
Right: शुक्र is the first clear member.
Right: अग्नि is a member.
Wrong: blood is not named in unit 81.
questions.explain: शुक्र-देह-अग्नि-दीप्तिम्: the brightness of semen, body and digestive fire.
questions.rule: The compound names शुक्र, देह and अग्नि.
questions.section: बस्ति-वीर्य का प्रसार; बस्ति प्रधान कर्म

questions.q: कुर्यात् (would make) is the optative of √कृ. Which form means he would go, from √गम् (गच्छति)?
optionExplain: Right: The optative 3 sg. of an -अ stem ends in -एत्: गच्छ + एत् = गच्छेत्.
This is the present, 'he goes'.
This is the future, 'he will go'.
This is the absolutive, 'having gone'.
questions.explain: कुर्यात् and गच्छेत् are optatives: 'would / should do', 'would / should go'.
questions.rule: Optative 3 sg.: -एत् on -अ stems (गच्छेत्), -यात् on others (कुर्यात्).
questions.teaches: The optative ('would, should') 3rd singular ends in -एत् on -अ stems (गच्छेत्) and in -यात् on some others (कुर्यात्).
questions.section: बस्ति-वीर्य का प्रसार; बस्ति प्रधान कर्म

questions.q: Which number is the chapter that unit 82 closes?
optionExplain: Fourth would be चतुर्थः.
Right: पञ्चमः = fifth.
Sixth would be षष्ठः.
Fiftieth would be पञ्चाशत्तमः; पञ्चम is fifth.
questions.explain: पञ्चमोऽध्यायः = the fifth chapter.
questions.section: बस्ति-वीर्य का प्रसार; बस्ति प्रधान कर्म

questions.q: Match each word of unit 82 to its meaning.
questions.explain: इति सिद्धबस्तिकल्पो नाम पञ्चमोऽध्यायः.
questions.rule: इति = thus; बस्ति = basti; कल्प = preparations; नाम = named; अध्यायः = chapter.
questions.section: बस्ति-वीर्य का प्रसार; बस्ति प्रधान कर्म

questions.q: Put the words of unit 82 in the order of the text, after the split.
questions.explain: Thus, Siddhabastikalpa, named, fifth, chapter.
questions.teaches: The colophon runs: इति सिद्धबस्तिकल्पो नाम पञ्चमोऽध्यायः, thus the fifth chapter, named Siddhabastikalpa.
questions.section: बस्ति-वीर्य का प्रसार; बस्ति प्रधान कर्म

questions.q: Which split is right for पञ्चमोऽध्यायः?
optionExplain: अ + अ would merge to आ: पञ्चमाध्यायः.
ध्यायः is not the word; the chapter is अध्यायः.
Right: -अः before अ gives -ओ, and the lost अ is marked by ऽ.
म् would join the vowel: पञ्चममध्यायः.
questions.explain: पञ्चमः (fifth) + अध्यायः (chapter).
questions.section: बस्ति-वीर्य का प्रसार; बस्ति प्रधान कर्म

questions.q: Which of these is the subject of the chapter named in unit 82?
optionExplain: Complications (व्यापद्) are not in this title.
The title names bastis, not signs of death.
The title names no daily routine.
Right: सिद्धबस्तिकल्प: the kalpa (preparations) of the siddha bastis.
questions.explain: बस्ति + कल्प: the title is about preparing bastis.
questions.section: बस्ति-वीर्य का प्रसार; बस्ति प्रधान कर्म

questions.q: पञ्चमोऽध्यायः means the fifth chapter. Which phrase means the sixth chapter?
optionExplain: Right: षष्ठ = sixth; षष्ठः + अध्यायः = षष्ठोऽध्यायः.
सप्तम is seventh.
चतुर्थ is fourth.
This compound means 'six chapters', not 'the sixth'.
questions.explain: Ordinals: चतुर्थ 4th, पञ्चम 5th, षष्ठ 6th, सप्तम 7th.
questions.teaches: Ordinals name a chapter's place: पञ्चमोऽध्यायः (fifth chapter), षष्ठोऽध्यायः (sixth chapter).
questions.section: बस्ति-वीर्य का प्रसार; बस्ति प्रधान कर्म

questions.q: What subject does unit 1 announce for the chapter?
options: The collecting and storing of emetic fruit
The mishaps of basti and their siddhi
The tastes of food in the cold season
The qualities of a good teacher of medicine
optionExplain: That belongs to the emetic chapter; it is not named here.
Right: बस्ति-व्यापत्ति-सिद्धि: the accomplishment (treatment) of the mishaps of the enema.
Seasons and tastes are not named in this formula.
No teacher is named; the subject is the basti's mishaps.
questions.explain: The formula names one subject: the siddhi of the vyāpatti (mishaps) of basti.
questions.rule: अथातो बस्तिव्यापत्तिसिद्धिं व्याख्यास्यामः = now we shall explain the treatment of basti mishaps.

questions.q: Put the three parts of unit 1 in the text's order.
questions.explain: Opening words, then the subject (object of the verb), then the verb.

questions.q: Match each part of unit 1 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The title compound is basti + vyāpatti + siddhi: the accomplishment of the enema's mishaps.
questions.rule: व्यापत्ति = mishap; सिद्धि = success; व्याख्यास्यामः = we shall explain.
questions.teaches: The chapter title is a tat-puruṣa: the siddhi (success) of the vyāpatti (mishaps) of basti.

questions.q: Which split of अथातो is right?
optionExplain: तः is not a word here; the long आ is two short अ joined.
आतः is not the word; the card reads अतः, therefore.
Right: अ + अ gives आ; the visarga of अतः after अ turns into ओ before the voiced ब.
The ओ is the changed visarga at the end, not a vowel inside.
questions.explain: अथातो = अथ + अतः; the final ओ stands for -अः before a voiced sound.
questions.rule: अ + अ → आ; -अः before a voiced consonant → -ओ.

questions.q: What does the verb form व्याख्यास्यामः tell about who speaks and when?
options: He explained it in the past
You should explain it to us
I am explaining it right now
optionExplain: That would be third person singular, past.
That would be a command to another person.
That would be first person singular, present.
Right: 1 pl. future of vi-ā-√khyā: we shall explain.
questions.explain: The word split labels व्याख्यास्यामः as 1 pl. future.
questions.rule: व्याख्यास्यामः = हम व्याख्या करेंगे (उत्तम पुरुष, बहुवचन, भविष्यत्).

questions.q: By the pattern of बस्ति-व्यापत्ति-सिद्धि, what would वमन-व्यापत्ति-सिद्धि (वमन, emesis) mean?
options: Treatment of the mishaps of emesis
Emesis as the cure of basti mishaps
The success of emesis without mishaps
A mishap caused by a successful cure
optionExplain: Right: Same tat-puruṣa chain: the siddhi of the vyāpatti of vamana.
Nothing in the compound names basti; the first member is वमन.
व्यापत्ति is the mishap itself, not its absence.
The last member (सिद्धि) is the head; it is not a cause.
questions.explain: In X-व्यापत्ति-सिद्धि the first member names the procedure whose mishaps are treated.
questions.rule: X-व्यापत्ति-सिद्धि = the successful treatment of the mishaps of X.
questions.teaches: In a tat-puruṣa the last member is the head: X-vyāpatti-siddhi is the siddhi of the mishaps of X.

questions.q: Which of these does verse 2 name among the mishaps of the basti?
optionExplain: Fever is not named in verse 2.
Right: आध्मान, distension or bloating, is the third name of line 1.
Thirst is not named in verse 2.
Hiccup is not in this list.
questions.explain: Line 1 names vibandha, gaurava, ādhmāna, śiroruj, vāhana and the upward-going.
questions.rule: आध्मान = distension; it is one of the listed mishaps.

questions.q: Match each clear mishap name of line 1 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four names of line 1 are clear; vāhana is obscure and left out.
questions.rule: विबन्ध = obstruction; गौरव = heaviness; आध्मान = distension; शिरोरुज् = head-pain.

questions.q: Put these mishap names in the order of verse 2.
questions.explain: Line 1 runs vibandha ... ādhmāna ... ūrdhvaga; line 2 runs kukṣiśūla ... kartana, srava.
questions.rule: विबन्ध · आध्मान · ऊर्ध्वग ‖ कुक्षिशूल · कर्तन · स्रव.
questions.teaches: Line 1 ends with the upward-going (ऊर्ध्वग); line 2 starts with belly-pain and ends with flow (स्रव).

questions.q: Which split of शिरोरुग् (in the first compound) is right?
optionExplain: शिरो is not the stem; the ओ is the changed visarga of शिरः.
ओरुज् is not a word; the word for pain is रुज्.
