Right: -अः before a voiced र becomes -ओ; final ज् becomes ग् before the voiced व that follows.
उरुग् is not a word; the visarga does not vanish before र here.
questions.explain: शिरः (head) + रुज् (pain) = head-pain.

questions.q: After a basti, a patient has heaviness and belly-pain. Which two of these does verse 2 name?
optionExplain: Not named in verse 2.
Right: the second name of line 1.
Right: the first name of line 2.
Not named in verse 2.
questions.explain: Heaviness (gaurava) is in line 1; belly-pain (kukṣiśūla) opens line 2.

questions.q: Like कुक्षि-शूल (belly-pain), what does पार्श्व-शूल mean (पार्श्व, side)?
options: Pain that moves from the belly
optionExplain: Nothing in the compound negates the pain.
The belly is not named in पार्श्वशूल.
शूल is pain, not swelling.
Right: The first member names the place, the last the pain: side-pain.
questions.explain: कुक्षि-शूल = pain of the belly; पार्श्व-शूल = pain of the side.
questions.rule: Place + शूल = pain in that place (tat-puruṣa).
questions.teaches: Place + शूल is a tat-puruṣa: the pain of that place (kukṣiśūla = belly-pain).

questions.q: From what does verse 3 say the mishaps of the basti come?
options: From cold weather and from hot weather
From a wrong drug and from a wrong time
From a weak patient and a strong one
optionExplain: Right: अयोगात् अतियोगात् च: from non-application and from over-application.
No season is named in verse 3.
Neither drug nor time is named as the cause.
Strength of the patient is not named here.
questions.explain: The two causes are ayoga (non-application) and atiyoga (over-application).

questions.q: Match each word of verse 3 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Two faults, the mishaps they cause, and the word for the basti being applied.
questions.rule: अयोग = non-application; अतियोग = over-application; आपदः = mishaps; योजितः = applied.

questions.q: Put these words of line 1 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: First the two causes, then 'of the basti', the verb, and the six-and-six mishaps.
questions.teaches: Line 1 says: from ayoga and atiyoga of the basti there are six and six mishaps (āpadaḥ).

questions.q: Which split of षट्षडापदः is right?
optionExplain: डापदः is not a word; the ड is the changed ट्.
Right: Final ट् becomes ड् before a vowel: षट् + आपदः → षडापदः.
पदः (feet) does not fit; the word is आपदः, mishaps.
These pieces are not words.
questions.explain: Six (षट्), six (षट्), mishaps (आपदः).
questions.rule: ट् → ड् before a vowel: षट् + आपदः → षडापदः.

questions.q: What does line 2 say about the koṣṭha (belly) of the patient?
optionExplain: The word is गुरु, heavy, not light.
Oiling is denied of the body, and the koṣṭha is called heavy.
Right: गुरुकोष्ठस्य: of one whose koṣṭha is heavy.
Heat of the koṣṭha is not named in verse 3.
questions.explain: The patient of line 2: body not oiled, not sweated; koṣṭha heavy.

questions.q: By the pattern of अयोगात् and अतियोगात्, which form means from over-eating (भोजन, eating)?
optionExplain: अ- negates: from not eating.
This is over-eating itself, not 'from'.
This is 'of eating', a genitive.
Right: अति- gives excess and -आत् gives from: from over-eating.
questions.explain: अ- = not, अति- = over; -आत् = from (ablative).
questions.teaches: Prefix अ- negates and अति- marks excess; the ablative -आत् gives the cause (from ...).

questions.q: What does the faulty basti of verse 4 do with the doṣa?
options: Agitates it but does not expel it
optionExplain: Right: संक्षोभ्य ... अनिर्हरन्: having agitated it, not expelling it.
अनिर्हरन् means not expelling.
संक्षोभ्य says the doṣa is agitated.
No change of doṣa is named.
questions.explain: The basti stirs up the doṣa and, through weakness, does not carry it out.
questions.rule: संक्षोभ्य = having agitated; अनिर्हरन् = not expelling.
questions.section: अयोग से विबन्ध और उसकी चिकित्सा

questions.q: Match each word of verse 4 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Two faults of the basti and two words for what it does.
questions.rule: शीतः = cold; घनः = thick; संक्षोभ्य = having agitated; अनिर्हरन् = not expelling.
questions.section: अयोग से विबन्ध और उसकी चिकित्सा

questions.q: Put these words of line 2 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The basti, having agitated that doṣa, because of weakness, not expelling (it).
questions.rule: बस्तिः · संक्षोभ्य · तं दोषम् · दुर्बलत्वात् · अनिर्हरन्.
questions.teaches: Line 2 is a chain: the basti agitates the doṣa, and because of weakness does not expel it.
questions.section: अयोग से विबन्ध और उसकी चिकित्सा

questions.q: Which split of घनोऽपि is right?
optionExplain: घनो is not the stem form; the ओ is the changed visarga of घनः.
Right: -अः + अ- gives -ओऽ: the अ of अपि drops, marked by the avagraha.
ओपि is not a word; the word is अपि, even.
पि is not a word; the अ of अपि is hidden in ऽ.
questions.explain: Two words: घनः (thick) and अपि (even).
questions.section: अयोग से विबन्ध और उसकी चिकित्सा

questions.q: A physician gives a thick basti. Does verse 4 count it among the faulty ones?
options: No, only a cold basti is named
No, only lack of oil is named
Only if salt is lacking too
optionExplain: Cold is one fault; thick is also named.
Little oil is one fault; thick is also named.
Right: घनोऽपि वा: or even thick.
The verse names thick as a fault on its own, with वा (or).
questions.explain: Line 1 lists three alternatives: cold, or little oil/salt/drug/quantity, or even thick.
questions.section: अयोग से विबन्ध और उसकी चिकित्सा

questions.q: Like अनिर्हरन् (not expelling), which form means not seeing (पश्यन्, seeing)?
optionExplain: अन्- is used before a vowel, not before प.
अति- means over or excess, not not.
This is not a negative form.
Right: Negative अ- before a consonant: अ + पश्यन् = अपश्यन्.
questions.explain: अ + निर्हरन् = अनिर्हरन्; in the same way अ + पश्यन् = अपश्यन्.
questions.rule: Negative prefix: अ- before a consonant, अन्- before a vowel.
questions.teaches: The negative prefix is अ- before a consonant (अनिर्हरन्, अपश्यन्) and अन्- before a vowel.
questions.section: अयोग से विबन्ध और उसकी चिकित्सा

questions.q: Which three does verse 5 say are obstructed?
optionExplain: Right: वात-विट्-मूत्र-विबन्ध: obstruction of wind, stool and urine.
Sweat and tears are not named.
These are not named in verse 5.
None of these is named.
questions.explain: विण्मूत्र = विट् (stool) + मूत्र (urine), after वात (wind).
questions.rule: वात · विट् · मूत्र: तीनों का विबन्ध.
questions.section: अयोग से विबन्ध और उसकी चिकित्सा

questions.q: Put these effects in the order of verse 5.
questions.explain: First the obstruction, then pain in basti and navel, ānāha, hṛllepa, swelling in the anus.
questions.rule: विबन्ध · बस्ति-नाभि-रुज् · आनाह · हृल्लेप · श्वयथुं गुदे.
questions.section: अयोग से विबन्ध और उसकी चिकित्सा

questions.q: Match each effect named in verse 5 to its meaning.
pairs: a coating felt at the heart
questions.explain: Four of the effects of the faulty basti.
questions.rule: विबन्ध = obstruction; आनाह = distension with retention; हृल्लेप = heart-coating; श्वयथु = swelling.
questions.teaches: Verse 5 names obstruction, pain, ānāha, hṛllepa and swelling of the anus as effects.
questions.section: अयोग से विबन्ध और उसकी चिकित्सा

questions.q: In बस्तिनाभिरुज् of verse 5, what does बस्ति mean?
options: The enema given to the patient
The bladder or lower belly, an organ
The doṣa stirred by the enema
optionExplain: That is the sense in verses 3-4, not in this compound.
Right: Beside नाभि (navel) and रुज् (pain), basti names a part of the body.
बस्ति is not a name of a doṣa.
The compound is about places of pain.
questions.explain: The same word basti can mean the enema or the organ; here it is the organ.
questions.rule: बस्ति-नाभि-रुज् = pain in the bladder (lower belly) and navel.
questions.section: अयोग से विबन्ध और उसकी चिकित्सा

questions.q: Where does verse 5 place the swelling (श्वयथु)?
optionExplain: The navel is named with pain, not swelling.
The heart is named with hṛllepa, not swelling.
Right: श्वयथुं गुदे: swelling in the anus.
The feet are not named in verse 5.
questions.explain: गुदे is locative singular: in the anus.
questions.section: अयोग से विबन्ध और उसकी चिकित्सा

questions.q: Like हृद् + लेपम् → हृल्लेपम्, how is तद् + लोकः (that world) joined?
optionExplain: The द् is not left unchanged before ल.
An anusvara is not made from द्.
द् does not turn into त् before ल; it turns into ल्.
Right: द् before ल becomes ल्: तद् + लोकः → तल्लोकः.
questions.explain: हृद् + लेप → हृल्लेप; in the same way तद् + लोक → तल्लोक.
questions.teaches: A final त्/द् before ल becomes ल् (हृद् + लेप = हृल्लेप; तद् + लोक = तल्लोक).
questions.section: अयोग से विबन्ध और उसकी चिकित्सा

questions.q: Which of these is named in line 1 of verse 6?
optionExplain: Right: कण्डू, itching, is the first word of the line.
Fainting is not named in verse 6.
Cough is not named in verse 6.
Vomiting is not named in verse 6.
questions.explain: Line 1: kaṇḍū, gaṇḍa, vaivarṇya, arati, vahni-mārdava.
questions.section: अयोग से विबन्ध और उसकी चिकित्सा

questions.q: Match each word of line 1 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four of the five effects of line 1.
questions.rule: कण्डू = itching; गण्ड = lump; वैवर्ण्य = discolouration; अरति = restlessness.
questions.section: अयोग से विबन्ध और उसकी चिकित्सा

questions.q: Put the effects of line 1 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Itching, lumps, discolouration, restlessness, softness of the fire.
questions.teaches: Line 1 ends the list of effects with softness of the fire (वह्निमार्दव).
questions.section: अयोग से विबन्ध और उसकी चिकित्सा

questions.q: Which split of वैवर्ण्यमरतिं is right?
optionExplain: मरतिम् is not a word; the म् ends वैवर्ण्यम्.
Right: Final म् before a vowel joins it: वैवर्ण्यम् + अरतिम् → वैवर्ण्यमरतिम्.
रति (delight) would reverse the sense; the word is अरति.
वैवर्ण्य is neuter: वैवर्ण्यम्, not -अः.
questions.explain: Two accusatives: वैवर्ण्यम् (discolouration) and अरतिम् (restlessness).
questions.rule: -म् + vowel → the म् is written joined to the vowel.
questions.section: अयोग से विबन्ध और उसकी चिकित्सा

questions.q: After a faulty basti a patient feels restless and ill at ease. Which word of verse 6 names this?
optionExplain: कण्डू is itching, not restlessness.
वैवर्ण्य is a change of colour.
Right: अरतिम्: restlessness, discontent, in line 1.
गण्ड is a lump or swelling.
questions.explain: Line 1: itching, lumps, discolouration, restlessness (arati), softness of the fire.
questions.section: अयोग से विबन्ध और उसकी चिकित्सा

questions.q: Like प्राक् + विहितम् → प्राग्विहितम्, how is वाक् + दानम् (word-giving) joined?
optionExplain: क् does not stay unvoiced before a voiced consonant.
क् turns into the nasal only before a nasal.
The final consonant does not return to च here.
Right: Final क् becomes ग् before the voiced द.
questions.explain: प्राक् + विहित → प्राग्विहित; वाक् + दान → वाग्दान.
questions.rule: Final unvoiced stop + voiced consonant → voiced stop (क् → ग्).
questions.teaches: A final क् becomes ग् before a voiced consonant (प्राग्विहित, वाग्दान).
questions.section: अयोग से विबन्ध और उसकी चिकित्सा

questions.q: Which one of the pair named in verse 6 does verse 7 recommend drinking?
optionExplain: Right: उष्णस्य ... एकस्य पानं प्रशस्यते: drinking of the one, the hot one.
The verse says उष्ण, hot.
The verse says one (एक), not both.
Drinking (पान) is recommended.
questions.explain: Of the two decoctions, the hot one is chosen.
questions.rule: उष्णस्य एकस्य पानम् = गर्म वाले एक का पान.
questions.section: अयोग से विबन्ध और उसकी चिकित्सा

questions.q: Put the measures of verse 7 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Drinking (of the hot decoction), suppositories, sweatings, then purgation.
questions.section: अयोग से विबन्ध और उसकी चिकित्सा

questions.q: Match each word of verse 7 to its meaning.
questions.explain: One recommended drink and three more measures.
questions.rule: पान = drinking; प्रशस्यते = is recommended; फलवर्ति = suppository; स्वेद = sweating; विरेचन = purgation.
questions.teaches: Besides the hot decoction, verse 7 names phalavarti, sveda and virecana.
questions.section: अयोग से विबन्ध और उसकी चिकित्सा

questions.q: Which split of फलवर्त्यस्तथा is right?
optionExplain: अस्तथा is not a word.
Right: A visarga before त becomes स्: -यः + तथा → -यस्तथा.
स्तथा is not a word; the स् is the changed visarga.
The स् is not an extra letter; it replaces the visarga.
questions.explain: फलवर्त्यः (suppositories, f. nom. pl.) + तथा (likewise).
questions.section: अयोग से विबन्ध और उसकी चिकित्सा

questions.q: When does verse 7 say purgation (विरेचन) is given?
optionExplain: The verse makes it wait on knowing the time.
Night is not named.
Right: कालं ज्ञात्वा विरेचनम्: purgation, having known the time.
No fasting or number of days is named.
questions.explain: The verse asks the physician to know the time; it does not say which time.
questions.section: अयोग से विबन्ध और उसकी चिकित्सा

questions.q: Like ज्ञात्वा (having known, √ज्ञा), which form means having heard (√श्रु)?
optionExplain: This is the past participle, heard.
This is the present, hears.
This is the infinitive, to hear.
Right: An absolutive of a root without prefix ends in -त्वा.
questions.explain: ज्ञात्वा and श्रुत्वा are absolutives: having done the action first.
questions.rule: Root without prefix + -त्वा = having ...ed (with a prefix: -य).
questions.teaches: An unprefixed root takes -त्वा for having ...ed (ज्ञात्वा, श्रुत्वा); a prefixed root takes -य (संक्षोभ्य).
questions.section: अयोग से विबन्ध और उसकी चिकित्सा

questions.q: Which of these drugs is named in verse 8?
optionExplain: Right: कुलत्थ is the last drug of line 1.
Pippalī is named in verse 11, not here.
Vacā is named in verse 12, not here.
Citraka is named in verse 13, not here.
questions.explain: Line 1: bilva root, trivṛt, dāru, yava, kola, kulattha.
questions.section: अयोग से विबन्ध और उसकी चिकित्सा

questions.q: Match each drug of verse 8 to its identification.
questions.explain: These four identifications are marked standard in the data; dāru and kola are only probable.
questions.rule: बिल्व = bael; त्रिवृत् = turpeth (निशोथ); यव = barley; कुलत्थ = horse gram.
questions.section: अयोग से विबन्ध और उसकी चिकित्सा

questions.q: Put these drugs in the order of verse 8.
questions.explain: Bilva root first, then trivṛt, dāru, yava, kola, kulattha.
questions.rule: बिल्वमूल · त्रिवृत् · दारु · यव · कोल · कुलत्थ.
questions.teaches: Line 1 lists six drugs from bilva root to kulattha, all qualifying the basti (-वान्, having).
questions.section: अयोग से विबन्ध और उसकी चिकित्सा

questions.q: What does the ending -वान् in कुलत्थवान् and मूत्रवान् mean?
optionExplain: Without would need a word like विना or a negative.
Right: -वान् (matup) makes having X: the basti having these drugs.
Root is मूल, a separate member of the list.
No sequence in time is expressed by -वान्.
questions.explain: -वान् qualifies the basti: it has the drugs, surā and the rest, and urine.
questions.section: अयोग से विबन्ध और उसकी चिकित्सा

questions.q: Which liquids does line 2 put into the basti?
options: Surā and the others, and urine
optionExplain: Neither milk nor ghee is named.
Neither honey nor water is named.
Right: सुरादिमूत्रवान्: having surā and the others, and urine.
Oil is not named in verse 8.
questions.explain: सुरा-आदि = surā and the others (a fermented liquor and the rest); मूत्र = urine.
questions.section: अयोग से विबन्ध और उसकी चिकित्सा

questions.q: Like त्रिवृत् + दारु → त्रिवृद्दारु, how is मरुत् + गणः (the troop of winds) joined?
optionExplain: त् does not stay unvoiced before a voiced consonant.
त् turns into न् only before a nasal.
त् does not take the place of the next consonant before ग.
Right: Final त् becomes द् before the voiced ग.
questions.explain: त्रिवृत् + दारु → त्रिवृद्दारु; मरुत् + गण → मरुद्गण.
questions.teaches: A final त् becomes द् before a voiced consonant (त्रिवृद्दारु, मरुद्गण).
questions.section: अयोग से विबन्ध और उसकी चिकित्सा

questions.q: What kind of nirūha does verse 9 speak of?
optionExplain: Right: निरूहेण मृदुना: by a mild nirūha.
The verse says मृदु, mild.
Cold and thick were faults in verse 4, not named here.
Oil is not named in verse 9.
questions.explain: The trouble arises from a mild nirūha given while āma remains.
questions.rule: मृदु निरूह = हल्की काढ़े की बस्ति.
questions.section: आम में मृदु निरूह: गुरुता, हृद्-शूल

questions.q: Match what line 2 names to what happens to it.
questions.explain: Three objects, three verbs: मूर्च्छयति, रुणद्धि, हिनस्ति.
questions.rule: वायु → मूर्च्छयति; मार्ग → रुणद्धि; अग्नि → हिनस्ति.
questions.section: आम में मृदु निरूह: गुरुता, हृद्-शूल

questions.q: Put these words of line 2 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Stupefies the wind; the path, obstructs; the fire, harms.
questions.rule: मूर्च्छयति · अनिलम् · मार्गम् · रुणद्धि · अग्निम् · हिनस्ति.
questions.teaches: Line 2 has three verbs: मूर्च्छयति (stupefies), रुणद्धि (obstructs), हिनस्ति (harms).
questions.section: आम में मृदु निरूह: गुरुता, हृद्-शूल

questions.q: Which split of दोषैरीरितः is right?
optionExplain: रीरितः is not a word; the र् is the changed visarga.
Right: A visarga after ऐ becomes र् before a vowel: दोषैः + ईरितः → दोषैरीरितः.
दोषः is singular; दोषैः, by the doṣas, is the plural.
The vowel is long ई: ईरितः, stirred.
questions.explain: दोषैः (by the doṣas, inst. pl.) + ईरितः (stirred).
questions.rule: ः after a vowel other than अ/आ + vowel → र्.
questions.section: आम में मृदु निरूह: गुरुता, हृद्-शूल

questions.q: Which of these does line 2 of verse 9 state as effects?
optionExplain: The verse says the fire is harmed (हिनस्ति), not kindled.
Right: मूर्च्छयत्यनिलम्.
Expelling is not named; the doṣas stir it.
Right: मार्गं रुणद्धि.
questions.explain: Line 2: stupefies the wind, obstructs the path, harms the fire.
questions.section: आम में मृदु निरूह: गुरुता, हृद्-शूल

questions.q: Like रुणद्धि + अग्निम् → रुणद्ध्यग्निम्, how is यदि + अपि (even if) joined?
optionExplain: इ + अ does not give a long ई.
इ + अ does not give ए.
Right: इ before a different vowel becomes य्.
The vowels do not simply drop.
questions.explain: रुणद्धि + अग्निम् → रुणद्ध्यग्निम्; यदि + अपि → यद्यपि.
questions.teaches: A final इ before a different vowel becomes य् (रुणद्ध्यग्निम्, मूर्च्छयत्यनिलम्, यद्यपि).
questions.section: आम में मृदु निरूह: गुरुता, हृद्-शूल

questions.q: With what does verse 10 say the patient should be treated?
optionExplain: These are not named; the verse says drying and sweating.
Neither is named in verse 10.
No food or drink is named in verse 10.
Right: रूक्षस्वेदपाचनैः: with drying, sweating and digestive (ones).
questions.explain: The treatment of line 2: rūkṣa, sveda, pācana.
questions.section: आम में मृदु निरूह: गुरुता, हृद्-शूल

questions.q: Put the effects of line 1 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Heaviness, fatigue, heart-pain, burning, bewilderment, twisting pain.
questions.rule: गौरव · क्लम · हृच्छूल · दाह · संमोह · वेष्टन.
questions.section: आम में मृदु निरूह: गुरुता, हृद्-शूल

questions.q: Match each effect of line 1 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four of the six effects of line 1.
questions.rule: क्लम = fatigue; दाह = burning; संमोह = bewilderment; वेष्टन = twisting pain.
questions.teaches: Line 1 adds fatigue, burning, bewilderment and twisting pain to heaviness and heart-pain.
questions.section: आम में मृदु निरूह: गुरुता, हृद्-शूल

questions.q: Which split of हृच्छूल is right?
optionExplain: Right: द् + श gives च्छ: हृद् + शूल → हृच्छूल.
छूल is not a word; the word is शूल, pain.
हृच् is not the stem; the heart is हृद्.
These pieces are not words.
questions.explain: हृद् (heart) + शूल (pain) = heart-pain.
questions.section: आम में मृदु निरूह: गुरुता, हृद्-शूल

questions.q: Which of these is NOT among the means of treatment named in verse 10?
optionExplain: Named: the first member of रूक्षस्वेदपाचनैः.
Right: Oiling is not named; the verse names drying, the opposite.
Named: the second member.
Named: the third member.
questions.explain: Named: rūkṣa, sveda, pācana. Oiling is not among them.
questions.section: आम में मृदु निरूह: गुरुता, हृद्-शूल

questions.q: Like उपचरेत् (should treat), which form means one should go (√गम्, गच्छति)?
optionExplain: This is the present, goes.
This is the past participle, gone.
Right: A thematic verb takes -एत् in the 3 sg optative: गच्छ + एत्.
This is the infinitive, to go.
questions.explain: उपचरेत् = upa-√car + -एत्, should treat; in the same way गच्छेत्, should go.
questions.rule: 3 sg optative of a thematic verb = stem + -एत् (should ...).
questions.teaches: The 3 sg optative of a thematic verb ends in -एत् and gives should (उपचरेत्, गच्छेत्).
questions.section: आम में मृदु निरूह: गुरुता, हृद्-शूल

questions.q: What is the water of verse 11 mixed with before drinking?
optionExplain: Honey is not named in verse 11.
Curd-maṇḍa is named in verse 12, not here.
Ghee is not named in verse 11.
Right: सौवर्चलोन्मिश्रम्: mixed with sauvarcala.
questions.explain: The water is mixed with sauvarcala, a salt (black salt, standard).
questions.section: आम में मृदु निरूह: गुरुता, हृद्-शूल

questions.q: Match each word of verse 11 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Two drugs of line 1, the salt and one quality of the water.
questions.rule: पिप्पली = long pepper; उशीर = vetiver; सौवर्चल = black salt; दीपन = kindling.
questions.section: आम में मृदु निरूह: गुरुता, हृद्-शूल

questions.q: Put the drugs of line 1 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Pippalī, kattṛṇa, uśīra, dāru, sūrvā, then -भृतं जलम्.
questions.teaches: Line 1 names five drugs in one compound ending in -भृतम्, qualifying the water (जलम्).
questions.section: आम में मृदु निरूह: गुरुता, हृद्-शूल

questions.q: Which drug of verse 11 does the data call unidentified?
optionExplain: Right: Sūrvā is unidentified; possibly a variant of mūrvā, itself disputed.
Pippalī is long pepper, a standard identification.
Uśīra is vetiver, a standard identification.
Sauvarcala is black salt, a standard identification.
questions.explain: Standard: pippalī, uśīra, sauvarcala. Probable: dāru. Disputed: kattṛṇa. Unidentified: sūrvā.
questions.section: आम में मृदु निरूह: गुरुता, हृद्-शूल

questions.q: What does line 2 say the water does?
options: Kindles and cleanses in the heart
optionExplain: Cooling is not named.
Right: दीपनं हृदिशोधनम्: kindling, and cleansing in the heart.
Purging is not named in verse 11.
Urine is not named in verse 11.
questions.explain: Two qualities: dīpana and hṛdi-śodhana.
questions.section: आम में मृदु निरूह: गुरुता, हृद्-शूल

questions.q: Like सौवर्चल + उन्मिश्रम् → सौवर्चलोन्मिश्रम्, how is गङ्गा + उदकम् (Ganges water) joined?
optionExplain: औ comes from अ/आ + ओ/औ, not + उ.
The आ does not simply drop.
Right: अ/आ + उ gives ओ.
No व् is inserted between आ and उ.
questions.explain: सौवर्चल + उन्मिश्र → सौवर्चलोन्मिश्र; कत्तृण + उशीर → कत्तृणोशीर; गङ्गा + उदक → गङ्गोदक.
questions.teaches: अ or आ followed by उ becomes ओ (कत्तृणोशीर, सौवर्चलोन्मिश्र, गङ्गोदक).
questions.section: आम में मृदु निरूह: गुरुता, हृद्-शूल

questions.q: Which three drugs does verse 12 name?
optionExplain: These are in verse 11.
These are in verse 13.
These are in verse 8.
Right: वचा-नागर-शठ्यः: vacā, nāgara, śaṭhī.
questions.explain: Verse 12 opens with vacā (sweet flag), nāgara (dry ginger) and śaṭhī.
questions.section: आम में मृदु निरूह: गुरुता, हृद्-शूल

questions.q: Match each word of verse 12 to its meaning.
pairs: the watery or creamy part of curd
questions.explain: Two drugs with standard identifications, the mixing liquid and one drink.
questions.rule: वचा = sweet flag (बच); नागर = dry ginger (सोंठ); दधिमण्ड = curd-maṇḍa; प्रसन्ना = clear liquor.
questions.section: आम में मृदु निरूह: गुरुता, हृद्-शूल

questions.q: Put these liquids in the order of verse 12.
questions.explain: Mixed with curd-maṇḍa; drunk with prasannā, or ariṣṭa, or āsava.
questions.teaches: The drugs, mixed (a conjecture for मूर्च्छिताः) with curd-maṇḍa, are to be drunk with prasannā, ariṣṭa or āsava.
questions.section: आम में मृदु निरूह: गुरुता, हृद्-शूल

questions.q: Which split of स्युररिष्टेनासवेन is right?
optionExplain: Right: -उः before a vowel becomes -उर्; अ + आ gives आ.
ररिष्टेन is not a word; the र् is the changed visarga.
नासवेन is not a word; the word is आसवेन.
The vowel is long: आसव, not असव.
questions.explain: स्युः (should be) + अरिष्टेन (with ariṣṭa) + आसवेन (with āsava).
questions.section: आम में मृदु निरूह: गुरुता, हृद्-शूल

questions.q: Which drinks does line 2 name for taking these drugs?
optionExplain: Right: आसवेन.
Right: अरिष्टेन.
Milk is not named in verse 12.
Water is not named in verse 12.
Right: प्रसन्नया.
questions.explain: Three alternatives joined by वा: prasannā, ariṣṭa, āsava.
questions.section: आम में मृदु निरूह: गुरुता, हृद्-शूल

questions.q: Like पेयाः (to be drunk, agreeing with the drugs), which phrase means the water is to be drunk (जलम्, n.)?
optionExplain: -आः is plural; जलम् is singular.
Right: A gerundive agrees with its noun: neuter singular -अम्.
-आ is feminine; जलम् is neuter.
पीत is drunk (already), not to be drunk.
questions.explain: पेयाः agrees with the feminine plural drugs; पेयम् agrees with neuter जलम्.
questions.rule: Gerundive (-य) = to be ...ed; it agrees with its noun.
questions.teaches: A gerundive like पेय (to be drunk) agrees with its noun in gender and number (शठ्यः पेयाः, जलं पेयम्).
questions.section: आम में मृदु निरूह: गुरुता, हृद्-शूल

questions.q: Which drug does line 2 of verse 13 add to those of line 1?
optionExplain: Pippalī is named in verse 11, not here.
Vacā is named in verse 12, not here.
Right: पिष्ट्वा कुष्ठं च: and kuṣṭha, also ground.
Bilva is named in verse 8, not here.
questions.explain: Line 2 adds kuṣṭha (costus, standard) to pathyā, palāśa, citraka and śaṭhī.
questions.section: आम में मृदु निरूह: गुरुता, हृद्-शूल

questions.q: Match each drug of verse 13 to its identification.
questions.explain: Four drugs with standard identifications in the data.
questions.rule: पथ्या = हरड़; पलाश = ढाक; चित्रक = चीता; कुष्ठ = कूठ (costus).
questions.section: आम में मृदु निरूह: गुरुता, हृद्-शूल

questions.q: Put these clear drug names of line 1 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: After the damaged first word: pathyā, palāśa, citraka, śaṭhī.
questions.teaches: Line 1 is a list of drug names in the accusative, objects of पिष्ट्वा (having ground).
questions.section: आम में मृदु निरूह: गुरुता, हृद्-शूल

questions.q: What does पिष्ट्वा mean in verse 13?
optionExplain: That would be पिष्ट, a past participle.
That would be an infinitive.
That would be a present verb.
Right: Absolutive of √पिष्: having ground, before drinking.
questions.explain: पिष्ट्वा ... पिबेत्: having ground, one should drink.
questions.section: आम में मृदु निरूह: गुरुता, हृद्-शूल

questions.q: Which further item, joined by च, does line 2 give as an object of पिबेत्?
optionExplain: Right: पिबेत् क्षारांश्च दीपनान्: and the kindling kṣāras.
Neither is named in verse 13.
That decoction is not mentioned again here.
Prasannā is named in verse 12, not here.
questions.explain: क्षारान् दीपनान्: kṣāras that kindle. kṣāra is kept as a term.
questions.section: आम में मृदु निरूह: गुरुता, हृद्-शूल

questions.q: Like क्षारान् + च → क्षारांश्च, how is तान् + च (and them) joined?
optionExplain: न् does not stay unchanged before च here.
Right: -न् before च becomes anusvara + श्: तांश्च.
The rule inserts श्, not only a palatal nasal.
No vowel is added after न्.
questions.explain: क्षारान् च → क्षारांश्च; तान् च → तांश्च.
questions.teaches: A final न् before च becomes anusvara + श् (क्षारांश्च, तांश्च).
questions.section: आम में मृदु निरूह: गुरुता, हृद्-शूल

questions.q: Which basti does line 1 of verse 14 prescribe?
options: A basti of honey and salt
optionExplain: Neither oil nor milk is named.
Neither honey nor salt is named here.
Right: समूत्रं दाशमूलिकम्: of the ten roots, with urine.
Cold was a fault in verse 4; curd is not named.
questions.explain: दाशमूलिक = of the daśamūla (group of ten roots); स-मूत्र = with urine.
questions.section: आम में मृदु निरूह: गुरुता, हृद्-शूल

questions.q: Match each word of verse 14 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Two words for the prescribed basti, two for the faulty case of line 2.
questions.rule: समूत्र = with urine; दाशमूलिक = of daśamūla; अल्पवीर्य = of little potency; दोषाढ्य = rich in doṣa.
questions.section: आम में मृदु निरूह: गुरुता, हृद्-शूल

questions.q: Put these words of line 2 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Applied, of little potency; in one rich in doṣa, in a dry one, in one with a harsh abode.
questions.teaches: Line 2 names a weak basti and three kinds of patient (locatives); its verb comes in verse 15.
questions.section: आम में मृदु निरूह: गुरुता, हृद्-शूल

questions.q: Which split of क्रूराशयेऽथवा is right?
optionExplain: एथवा is not a word; the word is अथवा, or.
-अः + अ would give -ओऽ, not -एऽ.
थवा is not a word; the अ of अथवा is hidden in ऽ.
Right: ए + अ keeps ए and the अ drops, marked by the avagraha (ऽ).
questions.explain: क्रूराशये (in one with a harsh abode, loc.) + अथवा (or).
questions.section: आम में मृदु निरूह: गुरुता, हृद्-शूल

questions.q: Which patient is NOT among those named in line 2 of verse 14?
optionExplain: Right: The verse names a dry (रूक्ष) one, not an oiled one.
Named: दोषाढ्ये.
Named: रूक्षे.
Named: क्रूराशये.
questions.explain: Three patients: rich in doṣa, dry, with a harsh abode (āśaya).
questions.section: आम में मृदु निरूह: गुरुता, हृद्-शूल

questions.q: By the pattern of समूत्रम् (with urine), what does सक्षीरम् mean (क्षीर, milk)?
optionExplain: Without would be निः- or अ-, not स-.
Right: स- + noun forms a bahuvrīhi: having X, with X.
स- adds a companion; it does not mean only.
No purpose is expressed by स-.
questions.explain: स-मूत्र = with urine; स-क्षीर = with milk.
questions.teaches: The prefix स- makes a bahuvrīhi meaning with X (समूत्र, सक्षीर).
questions.section: आम में मृदु निरूह: गुरुता, हृद्-शूल

questions.q: What does the wind gone the wrong way cause, according to verse 15?
options: Head-pain together with stiffness of the neck
Distension and pain of the vital parts
optionExplain: Those come from the wind gone upward (05.06.37-38), not from this verse.
Neither fever nor appetite is named in verse 15.
Right: कुर्यादाध्मानं मर्मपीडनम्: it would cause ādhmāna (distension) and marma-pīḍana.
Vomiting and hiccup are not named in verse 15.
questions.explain: The two effects named in verse 15 are ādhmāna and marma-pīḍana.

questions.q: Put these phrases of verse 15 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The basti obstructs the wind; that wind goes the wrong way and causes distension and pain of the marma.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 15 to its meaning.
questions.explain: समीरण and अनिल both name the wind; the two verbs are optatives ('may', 'would').
questions.rule: समीरण = wind; रुन्ध्यात् = may obstruct; कुर्यात् = would cause; आध्मान = distension; मर्म = vital part.
questions.teaches: Verse 15 uses two names of the wind, samīraṇa and anila, and two optative verbs, rundhyāt and kuryāt.

questions.q: Which split of कुर्यादाध्मानं is right?
optionExplain: त् + short अ would give कुर्यादध्मानं, without the long आ; and अध्मान is not the word.
Neither कुर्या nor दाध्मान is a word; the द् is the changed त् of कुर्यात्.
कुर्याद is not a word, and अ + आ would merge into one आ.
Right: त् becomes द् before a vowel; the long आ of आध्मानम् stays: कुर्याद् आध्मानम्.
questions.explain: कुर्यात् (would cause) + आध्मानम् (distension); final -म् shows as anusvara in the print.
questions.rule: त् → द् before a vowel: कुर्यात् + आध्मानम् → कुर्यादाध्मानम्.

questions.q: A basti given to a patient full of doṣa gets covered by doṣa and blocked. What does verse 15 say happens to the wind?
options: It is held back and goes the wrong way
It is pushed out downward along with the stool
It kindles the digestive fire again
It dries up the doṣa in the belly
optionExplain: Right: रुन्ध्यात् समीरणम् ... स विमार्गः अनिलः: obstructed, it goes the wrong way.
Verse 15 says the wind is obstructed, not expelled.
The digestive fire is not named in verse 15.
Verse 15 says nothing about drying the doṣa.
questions.explain: Blocked basti → obstructed wind → wind on the wrong path → distension and marma pain.
questions.rule: बस्ति रुके तो वायु रुके; रुका वायु विमार्ग में जाए.

questions.q: By the pattern of कुर्यात् (would cause), what does the new sentence बस्तिः शूलं कुर्यात् mean?
optionExplain: That would need a past form; कुर्यात् is optative, not past.
Right: कुर्यात् is 3 sg optative: 'would/may cause'; बस्तिः is its subject, शूलम् its object.
बस्तिः is singular, and कुर्यात् is not a plural command.
शूलम् is the object (accusative); the subject is बस्तिः.
questions.explain: Optative 3 sg -यात्/-एत् = 'would, may': रुन्ध्यात्, कुर्यात्.
questions.rule: कुर्यात् = would cause (3 sg optative of √कृ).
questions.teaches: रुन्ध्यात् and कुर्यात् are 3rd-person singular optatives: 'may obstruct', 'would cause'.

questions.q: What does verse 16 say the wind does to the heart?
optionExplain: Burning (विदाह) is of the anus and koṣṭha, not of the heart.
No swelling of the heart is named in verse 16.
Right: रुणद्धि हृदयं शूलैः: it obstructs (grips) the heart with pains.
The heart is named: it is gripped with pains.
questions.explain: हृदय is the object of रुणद्धि; शूलैः (with pains) is the means.
questions.rule: रुणद्धि हृदयं शूलैः = grips the heart with pains.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 16 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are the words of the two lists and the last verb of verse 16.
questions.rule: विदाह = burning; मुष्क = testicle; वंक्षण = groin; वेदना = pain; धावति = runs.

questions.q: Put these effects in the order of verse 16.
questions.explain: Line 1: burning, then pain of testicles and groins; line 2: the heart gripped, then running here and there.
questions.rule: विदाह · मुष्कवंक्षणवेदना ‖ रुणद्धि हृदयं शूलैः · इतश्चेतश्च धावति.
questions.teaches: Verse 16 moves from the anus and groins (line 1) to the heart and the wind's wandering (line 2).

questions.q: Which split of इतश्चेतश्च is right?
optionExplain: च + ए would give चै, not चे; and एतः is not a word.
इति + च would print इति च, with no श्; the word is इतः (hither).
इत and श्च are not words; the श् is the changed visarga.
Right: ः before च becomes श्; अ of च + इ of इतः gives ए: इतश् चेतश् च.
questions.explain: इतः च इतः च = 'hither and hither', i.e. here and there.
questions.rule: ः + च → श्च; अ + इ → ए: च + इतः → चेतः.

questions.q: A patient's wind has gone the wrong way after a basti. Which two signs does verse 16 name?
options: Pain in the testicles and groins
Burning at the anus and koṣṭha
optionExplain: No neck sign is named in verse 16.
Head-pain comes from the wind gone upward (05.06.37), not from verse 16.
Right: मुष्कवंक्षणवेदनाम्.
Right: विदाहं गुदकोष्ठस्य.
questions.explain: Line 1 of verse 16 names burning (anus, koṣṭha) and pain (testicles, groins).

questions.q: Like मुष्क-वंक्षण-वेदना, what does the new compound जानु-जङ्घा-वेदना mean (जानु, knee; जङ्घा, shank)?
options: Pain in the knees and shanks
The knee of a painful shank
Pain that moves away from the knee
optionExplain: Right: The first two members are a dvandva (knee and shank); the last, वेदना, is the head: their pain.
The head of the compound is वेदना (pain), not जानु.
Nothing in the compound negates the pain.
No movement is named; it is the pain of both parts.
questions.explain: Place + place + वेदना = pain in both places (dvandva + tat-puruṣa).
questions.rule: X-Y-वेदना = pain of X and Y.
questions.teaches: मुष्क-वंक्षण-वेदना is a dvandva of two places followed by वेदना: the pain of both.

questions.q: In what state should the patient's body be when the varti of verse 17 is applied?
optionExplain: Fasting and purging are not named in verse 17.
Right: स्वभ्यक्तस्विन्नगात्रस्य: of one whose body is well anointed and sweated.
Verse 17 names anointing and sweating, not cooling.
No drying powder is named in verse 17.
questions.explain: सु-अभ्यक्त (well anointed) + स्विन्न (sweated) + गात्र (body).
questions.rule: स्वभ्यक्त-स्विन्न-गात्र = whose body is well oiled and sweated.

questions.q: Put these parts of verse 17 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Line 1: the prepared body, then the varti; line 2: the bilva nirūha, then what it contains.
questions.rule: स्वभ्यक्तस्विन्नगात्रस्य · वर्तिं प्रयोजयेत् ‖ बिल्वादिः निरूहः · पीलुसर्षपमूत्रवान्.

questions.q: Match each term of verse 17 to its meaning on the card.
questions.explain: Two kinds of treatment (varti, nirūha) and three things the nirūha should have.
questions.rule: वर्ति = suppository; निरूह = decoction enema; पीलु = Salvadora persica (probable); सर्षप = mustard (probable).
questions.teaches: The nirūha of verse 17 begins with bilva and has pīlu, sarṣapa and urine; the varti is a separate suppository.

questions.q: Which split of स्वभ्यक्त is right?
optionExplain: अ + अ would give a long आ (स्वाभ्यक्त), which is not printed.
भ्यक्त is not a word; the word is अभ्यक्त (anointed).
Right: उ before a different vowel becomes व्: सु + अभ्यक्त → स्वभ्यक्त, 'well anointed'.
Neither piece is a word; the व् is the changed उ of सु.
questions.explain: सु (well) + अभ्यक्त (anointed): उ → व् before अ.
questions.rule: उ + unlike vowel → व्: सु + अभ्यक्त = स्वभ्यक्त.

questions.q: A physician prepares the nirūha of verse 17. Which set matches the verse?
options: Bilva group with milk, honey and sesame
Pīlu and mustard in oil, no urine
Bilva group with pīlu, sarṣapa, urine
optionExplain: Milk, honey and sesame are not named; urine is.
Urine (मूत्र) is named in the verse; this option leaves it out.
The verse names the bilva group, pīlu and sarṣapa with the urine.
Right: विल्वादिः ... पीलुसर्षपमूत्रवान्: beginning with bilva, having pīlu, sarṣapa and urine.
questions.explain: The nirūha: the bilva group + pīlu + sarṣapa + urine.

questions.q: Like पीलु-सर्षप-मूत्र-वान्, what does the new phrase तैल-लवण-वान् बस्तिः mean?
options: A basti having oil and salt
A basti without oil and salt
Oil and salt taken from a basti
A basti that makes oil salty
optionExplain: Right: -वान् (matup) means 'having'; the dvandva before it names what the basti has.
-वान् means 'having', not 'without'.
बस्तिः is the noun that has them; nothing is taken from it.
-वान् only means possession; it names no action.
questions.explain: X-Y-वान् = having X and Y; it agrees with its noun (here masculine बस्तिः).
questions.rule: -वत्/-वान् = having: पीलुसर्षपमूत्रवान् = having pīlu, mustard and urine.
questions.teaches: The suffix -वान् (matup) after a list means 'having those things': पीलुसर्षपमूत्रवान् निरूहः.

questions.q: What kind of enema does line 1 of verse 18 name?
optionExplain: The nirūha is named in 05.06.33; line 1 here names the anuvāsana.
Right: चानुवासनम् = च + अनुवासनम्: and an anuvāsana (oil enema).
The varti is named in 05.06.32, not in this line.
Nasya is not named in verse 18.
questions.explain: अनुवासन = an oil enema, the object of साधितम् (prepared).

questions.q: Match each clear word of verse 18 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are the clear words of the two lines; the damaged drug word is left out.
questions.rule: साधित = prepared; अनुवासन = oil enema; बस्ति = enema; तनु = thin.

questions.q: Line 2 of verse 18 calls the basti तनुः (thin) and ____ (mild). Type it in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: बस्तिस्तनुर्मृदुः = बस्तिः तनुः मृदुः: the basti, thin and mild.
questions.teaches: The basti of line 2 has two qualities: तनु (thin) and मृदु (mild).

questions.q: Which word of verse 18 describes the anuvāsana of line 1, not the basti of line 2?
optionExplain: तनुः (thin) describes the basti of line 2.
मृदुः (mild) describes the basti of line 2.
Right: साधितं चानुवासनम्: the anuvāsana is साधित, prepared (neuter, like अनुवासनम्).
बस्तिः is the noun of line 2 itself, not a word about the anuvāsana.
questions.explain: Line 1: साधितम् अनुवासनम् (prepared oil enema); line 2: बस्तिः तनुः मृदुः (thin, mild basti).

questions.q: Which split of बस्तिस्तनुर्मृदुः is right?
optionExplain: तनुः + अमृदुः would print तनुरमृदुः; and the verse calls it mild, not 'not mild'.
स्तनु is not a word; the स् is the changed visarga of बस्तिः.
स्तनुः and र्मृदुः are not words; each first sound belongs to the word before.
Right: ः before त becomes स्; ः after उ before म becomes र्: बस्तिस् तनुर् मृदुः.
questions.explain: Visarga sandhi: -इः + त → -इस्त; -उः + म → -उर्म.

questions.q: साधितम् agrees with the neuter अनुवासनम्. निरूह is masculine: which phrase means a prepared nirūha?
optionExplain: Right: The participle takes the noun's gender, number and case: masculine nominative singular -अः.
साधितम् does not agree with निरूहः: it is neuter nom./acc. or masculine accusative, while निरूहः is masculine nominative.
-आ is feminine; निरूह is masculine.
-औ is dual; निरूहः is one, singular.
questions.explain: A past participle used as an adjective agrees with its noun.
questions.teaches: साधित (prepared) is a past participle; like an adjective it agrees with its noun: साधितम् अनुवासनम्.

questions.q: What does the wind moving upward cause, according to verse 19?
optionExplain: Distension comes from the wind gone the wrong way (05.06.29).
Right: कुर्याद्वायुः शिरोरुजम्: the wind would cause head-pain.
Burning of the anus is named in 05.06.30, for the misdirected wind.
Straining is named in 05.06.45, after a mild basti in great doṣa.
questions.explain: ऊर्ध्वं ... देहम् अनुसरन् वायुः → शिरोरुज्.

questions.q: Put these phrases of verse 19 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The qualities of the basti, its effect on the wind, the wind's upward course, the head-pain.
questions.rule: शीतोऽल्पश्चावृतो दोषैः · प्रतिहंति समीरणं ‖ ऊर्ध्वं सोऽनुसरन्देहं · कुर्याद्वायुः शिरोरुजं.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 19 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Three qualities of the basti, its action on the wind, and the wind's direction.
questions.rule: शीत = cold; अल्प = small; आवृत = covered; प्रतिहन्ति = obstructs; ऊर्ध्वम् = upward.
questions.teaches: The basti of verse 19 is शीत, अल्प and दोषैः आवृत; it प्रतिहन्ति (obstructs) the wind, which goes ऊर्ध्वम्.

questions.q: Which split of सोऽनुसरन् is right?
optionExplain: अ + अ would fuse into आ (सानुसरन्); no ऽ would appear.
सो is not a word; the ओ is the changed visarga of सः.
Right: -अः before अ becomes -ओ and the अ drops, marked by ऽ: सो ऽनुसरन्.
नुसरन् is not a word; the lost अ of अनुसरन् is shown by ऽ.
questions.explain: सः (that) + अनुसरन् (moving along).

questions.q: How does the course of the wind in verse 19 differ from verse 15?
options: Here it goes downward and causes straining
Here it goes the wrong way (vimārga)
Here it stays in the groins and causes pain
Here it goes upward and causes head-pain
optionExplain: Verse 19 says ऊर्ध्वम्, upward, and names head-pain.
That is the word of verse 15; verse 19 says ऊर्ध्वम्, upward.
Groin pain belongs to the misdirected wind of 05.06.30.
Right: ऊर्ध्वं ... शिरोरुजम्; in verse 15 it went the wrong way (vimārga) and caused distension.
questions.explain: Verse 15: vimārga → ādhmāna; verse 19: ūrdhva → śiroruj.
questions.rule: विमार्ग वायु → आध्मान; ऊर्ध्व वायु → शिरोरुज्.

questions.q: Like ऊर्ध्वं सोऽनुसरन्देहम्, what does the new phrase अधः सोऽनुसरन्देहम् mean (अधः, downward)?
options: That, moving downward along the body
That, having left the body upward
Those winds moved down the body
optionExplain: Right: अनुसरन् is a present participle (moving along); अधः gives the direction, देहम् the path.
अनुसरन् is 'moving along', not 'having left'; अधः is downward.
सः and अनुसरन् are singular, and a participle is not a past tense.
A participle is not a command; it describes सः.
questions.explain: Present participle -अन् (m. nom. sg.) = 'while ...ing'; a direction word goes with it.
questions.rule: अनुसरन् = moving along (present participle of अनु-√सृ).
questions.teaches: अनुसरन् is a present participle (m. nom. sg.): 'moving along'; ऊर्ध्वम् gives its direction.

questions.q: Which of these does verse 20 list among the effects of the upward wind?
optionExplain: Hiccup is not named in verse 20.
Right: बाधिर्यम्, deafness, is the third item of line 1.
Fever is not named in verse 20.
Thirst is not named in verse 20.
questions.explain: Line 1: neck stiffness, nasal catarrh, deafness, disturbed vision.

questions.q: Match each effect named in verse 20 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The four effects of line 1, all in the head and neck.
questions.rule: ग्रीवास्तम्भ = neck stiffness; प्रतिश्याय = catarrh; बाधिर्य = deafness; दृष्टिविभ्रम = disturbed vision.

questions.q: Put these words for the preparation of the patient in the order of line 2.
questions.explain: उष्ण-तैल-लवण-प्रदिग्ध-स्विन्न-मर्दितम्: smeared with hot oil and salt, sweated, kneaded.
questions.teaches: Line 2 describes the patient as smeared with hot oil and salt, sweated and kneaded; the remedies follow in 05.06.40-41.

questions.q: Which word in verse 20 names an effect of the wind, not the preparation of the patient?
optionExplain: स्विन्न (sweated) describes the patient in line 2.
प्रदिग्ध (smeared) describes the patient in line 2.
Right: प्रतिश्याय (nasal catarrh) is in the list of effects of line 1.
मर्दित (kneaded) describes the patient in line 2.
questions.explain: Line 1 = effects; line 2 = the patient made ready for treatment.
questions.rule: पंक्ति १ लक्षण, पंक्ति २ उपचार की तैयारी.

questions.q: A patient's wind has gone upward after a basti. Which two signs does verse 20 name?
optionExplain: Right: ग्रीवास्तम्भम्.
Right: दृष्टिविभ्रमम्.
Burning is named in 05.06.30, for the misdirected wind.
Swelling in the apāna is named in 05.06.44, in another case.
questions.explain: Verse 20 names neck stiffness, catarrh, deafness and disturbed vision.
questions.rule: ग्रीवास्तम्भ, दृष्टिविभ्रम: ऊर्ध्व वायु के लक्षण.

questions.q: Like ग्रीवा-स्तम्भ (stiffness of the neck), what does the new compound पृष्ठ-स्तम्भ mean (पृष्ठ, back)?
options: The back of a stiff neck
Stiffness that moves to the back
optionExplain: Nothing in the compound negates the stiffness.
ग्रीवा is not in this compound; पृष्ठ is the place.
No movement is named; it is the stiffness of the back.
Right: Place + स्तम्भ: the last member is the head, the first names where the stiffness is.
questions.explain: X-स्तम्भ = stiffness of X (tat-puruṣa).
questions.rule: ग्रीवा-स्तम्भ = गर्दन की जकड़न; पृष्ठ-स्तम्भ = पीठ की जकड़न.
questions.teaches: ग्रीवा-स्तम्भ is a tat-puruṣa: the stiffness (स्तम्भ) of the neck (ग्रीवा).

questions.q: What kind of smokes does verse 21 prescribe?
optionExplain: Right: तीक्ष्णैः धूमैः: with sharp (strong) smokes.
The verse says तीक्ष्ण, sharp, the opposite of mild.
No cold smoke is named in verse 21.
No scent is named; the smokes are तीक्ष्ण.
questions.explain: तीक्ष्ण = sharp, strong; धूम = inhaled smoke.

questions.q: Put these means of treatment in the order of verse 21.
questions.explain: Line 1: smokes, pradhamana, nasya, mouth-purging; line 2: purgations and bastis.
questions.rule: तीक्ष्णैर्धूमैः · प्रधमनैः · नस्यैः · आस्यविरेचनैः ‖ विरेकैः · बस्तिभिः.

questions.q: Match each term of verse 21 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four of the means and the word for 'quickly'.
questions.rule: प्रधमन = powder-blowing; नस्य = nasal medicine; आस्यविरेचन = mouth-purging; विरेक = purgation; आशु = quickly.
questions.teaches: Verse 21 lists six means: four in line 1 (smoke, pradhamana, nasya, mouth-purging) and two in line 2 (purgation, basti).

questions.q: What does आनुलोमिक mean on the card?
optionExplain: That is the opposite; अनुलोम is 'with the grain'.
Right: आनुलोमिक, from अनुलोम: following the natural (downward) direction.
The nasal routes are नस्य and प्रधमन; आनुलोमिक names a direction.
No cooling is named; the word names a direction.
questions.explain: आनुलोमिक = following the natural direction; which means it qualifies is left open.

questions.q: Which two means of verse 21 act through the nose, as the card explains them?
optionExplain: The basti is an enema, not a nasal route.
Right: blowing of powder into the nose.
Right: nasal medication.
Purgation acts downward, not through the nose.
questions.explain: प्रधमन and नस्य are the nasal routes of verse 21.

questions.q: Like बस्तिभिः ... योजयेत् (should treat with bastis), what does the new phrase तैलैः योजयेत् mean?
options: One has already treated him with oil
optionExplain: तैलैः is instrumental (with oils), not the subject.
योजयेत् is optative, 'should', not a past form.
Right: -ऐः is instrumental plural (with ...); योजयेत् is 3 sg optative, 'one should apply/treat'.
The object would be accusative; तैलैः is instrumental.
questions.explain: Instrumental plural -ऐः/-भिः = 'with'; optative -एत् = 'should'.
questions.rule: धूमैः, नस्यैः, बस्तिभिः योजयेत् = should treat with smokes, nasya, bastis.
questions.teaches: The means in verse 21 are instrumental plurals (-ऐः, -भिः) with the optative योजयेत्, 'one should treat with ...'.

questions.q: What does verse 22 say a mild basti with little drug produces when the doṣa is great?
options: Head-pain from the wind that goes upward
optionExplain: Head-pain comes from the cold, small basti of 05.06.36-37.
These are effects of the upward wind (05.06.38).
Distension is from the misdirected wind (05.06.29).
Right: जनयेच्च प्रवाहिकाम्: and it would produce pravāhikā.
questions.explain: Great doṣa + mild, low-drug basti → little doṣa removed → pravāhikā.

questions.q: Put these steps of verse 22 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Line 1: the condition and the basti; line 2: little doṣa removed, pravāhikā produced.
questions.rule: स्निग्धस्विन्ने महादोषे · बस्तिर्मृद्वल्पभेषजः ‖ अल्पं हरेद्दोषं · जनयेच्च प्रवाहिकाम्.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 22 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Three words describe the basti; two verbs tell its results.
questions.rule: मृदु = mild; अल्प = little; भेषज = drug; हरेत् = would remove; जनयेत् = would produce.
questions.teaches: A basti that is मृदु and अल्पभेषज in great doṣa removes little (हरेत्) and produces pravāhikā (जनयेत्).

questions.q: What, according to verse 22, is wrong with this basti?
options: It is mild, with little drug, for a great doṣa
It is given to one not oiled and not sweated first
It is too sharp for a weak patient
It is given when the doṣa is small
optionExplain: Right: मृदु-अल्प-भेषजः in महादोषे: too weak for the amount of doṣa.
The patient is स्निग्धस्विन्न, oiled and sweated.
The verse calls it mild, not sharp.
The verse says महादोषे, when the doṣa is great.
questions.explain: The fault is the mismatch: great doṣa, mild basti with little drug.
questions.rule: महादोष में मृदु, अल्पभेषज बस्ति = थोड़ा दोष निकले.

questions.q: Which split of मृद्वल्पभेषजः is right?
optionExplain: वल्प is not a word; the व् is the changed उ of मृदु.
Right: उ before a different vowel becomes व्: मृदु + अल्प → मृद्वल्प.
वल्प is not a word, and मृदु + व would print मृदुवल्प.
मृद्व is not a word, and अ + अ would give a long आ.
questions.explain: मृदु (mild) + अल्प (little) + भेषज (drug): a bahuvrīhi, 'mild and with little drug'.
questions.rule: उ + unlike vowel → व्: मृदु + अल्प = मृद्वल्प.

questions.q: Like बस्तिः अल्प-भेषजः (a basti with little drug), what does the new phrase बहु-भेषजः बस्तिः mean?
options: A drug made of many bastis
A basti with no drug in it
optionExplain: बस्तिः is singular; बहु qualifies भेषज, not the basti.
The compound describes बस्तिः; it is not a drug.
Right: A bahuvrīhi: the basti that has much (बहु) drug (भेषज).
बहु is 'much', the opposite of none.
questions.explain: X-भेषजः बस्तिः = a basti whose drug is X (bahuvrīhi agreeing with बस्तिः).
questions.rule: अल्पभेषज = कम औषध वाली; बहुभेषज = बहुत औषध वाली.
questions.teaches: अल्प-भेषजः is a bahuvrīhi describing the basti: 'having little drug'.

questions.q: Where does verse 23 place the sinking (सदन)?
optionExplain: Neck and head signs belong to the upward wind (05.06.37-38).
Pain there is named in 05.06.30, for the misdirected wind.
Heart and sides are not named in verse 23.
Right: सदनं च ऊरुजङ्घयोः: and sinking in the thighs and shanks.
questions.explain: ऊरु = thigh; जङ्घा = shank; both in the locative dual.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 23 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Two signs, the two places of the second, and the verb of line 2.
questions.rule: शोफ = swelling; सदन = weakness; ऊरु = thigh; जङ्घा = shank; प्रवाहते = strains.

questions.q: Put these signs in the order of verse 23.
questions.explain: Line 1: swelling, then sinking; line 2: the being with obstructed wind, who strains.
questions.rule: शोफो बस्तावपाने च · सदनं चोरुजंघयोः ‖ विबद्धमारुतो जन्तुः · प्रवाहते.
questions.teaches: Verse 23 lists swelling (basti, apāna), sinking (thighs, shanks), then the straining of the one whose wind is blocked.

questions.q: In बस्तावपाने, what is the form बस्तौ?
optionExplain: Right: बस्तौ is the locative singular of बस्ति, like अपाने beside it.
The nominative dual of बस्ति is बस्ती; -औ on an -इ stem is the locative singular.
The accusative singular would be बस्तिम्.
The genitive singular would be बस्तेः.
questions.explain: बस्तौ + अपाने: two locatives, 'in the basti and in the apāna'.
questions.rule: -इ stem locative sg. = -औ (बस्तौ); -औ is not always dual.

questions.q: What does बस्ति mean in verse 23?
options: The enema that had been given earlier
The bag used for the enema
The urine held in the body
optionExplain: The enema is the cause (05.06.42); the swelling is in the organ.
Right: Swelling in the basti here is in the organ, the bladder or lower belly.
No device is meant; swelling is a sign in the body.
बस्ति names the organ, not the urine.
questions.explain: basti has several senses in this book; in verse 23 it is the bladder or lower belly.

questions.q: Like विबद्ध-मारुतः जन्तुः (a being whose wind is obstructed), what does the new phrase रुद्ध-मूत्रः जन्तुः mean?
options: Urine that holds back a being
A being who passes much urine
A being whose urine is held back
optionExplain: जन्तुः is the being described; मूत्र is not the subject.
रुद्ध means obstructed, held back; nothing says much urine is passed.
Right: A bahuvrīhi: the being whose urine (मूत्र) is obstructed (रुद्ध).
जन्तुः is singular and is the noun described.
questions.explain: Participle + noun as a bahuvrīhi = 'one whose noun is so'.
questions.teaches: विबद्ध-मारुतः is a bahuvrīhi: 'one whose wind is obstructed', describing जन्तुः.

questions.q: Which three treatments does line 1 of verse 24 name?
optionExplain: These are the means of 05.06.40-41, for the upward wind.
These belong to 05.06.32-33, for the misdirected wind.
Rest and milk are not named; fasting comes in line 2.
Right: स्वेद-अभ्यङ्गान् निरूहान् च: sweatings, anointings and nirūhas.
questions.explain: Line 1 names sveda, abhyaṅga and nirūha, with two adjectives.

questions.q: Put these words of verse 24 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The three treatments, their two adjectives, then the verb at the start of line 2.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 24 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Two treatments, an adjective, the lightening of line 2, and the verb.
questions.rule: स्वेद = sweating; अभ्यङ्ग = anointing; शोधनीय = cleansing; लङ्घन = fasting; विदध्यात् = should prescribe.
questions.teaches: Verse 24 prescribes (विदध्यात्) sveda, abhyaṅga and cleansing nirūhas, with laṅghana (lightening) in line 2.

questions.q: Which split of निरूहांश्च is right?
optionExplain: Right: Final -न् before च becomes anusvara + श्: निरूहांश्च.
-आः before च would print निरूहाश्च, with no anusvara.
-म् before च would print निरूहं च or निरूहञ्च, with no श्.
That would print निरूहांशश्च; अंश (portion) is not in the verse.
questions.explain: निरूहान् is accusative plural, like स्वेदाभ्यङ्गान्, objects of विदध्यात्.

questions.q: A patient has pravāhikā after a mild basti in great doṣa. Which of these does verse 24 prescribe?
optionExplain: Right: named in line 1, cleansing ones.
The varti is for the misdirected wind (05.06.32).
Sharp smokes are for the upward wind (05.06.40).
Right: named in line 1.
Right: named in line 1.
questions.explain: Line 1: sveda, abhyaṅga and nirūhas.
questions.rule: प्रवाहिका में: स्वेद, अभ्यंग, शोधनीय निरूह.

questions.q: Like लङ्घयित्वा (having subjected to fasting), what does the new sentence स्वेदयित्वा बस्तिं विदध्यात् mean?
options: After the basti, one should sweat him
Having sweated (him), one should give a basti
Without sweating, one should give a basti
The basti sweated him, as had been prescribed before
optionExplain: The absolutive names the earlier act: sweating comes first.
Right: -इत्वा is an absolutive: the sweating is done first, then the basti.
-इत्वा names an act that is done, not one left out.
बस्तिम् is the object, and विदध्यात् is optative, not past.
questions.explain: Absolutive -त्वा/-इत्वा = 'having done X', before the main verb.
questions.teaches: लङ्घयित्वा is an absolutive (-इत्वा): 'having subjected (him) to laṅghana', an act done before the next.

questions.q: Which basti does line 2 of verse 25 name among the faulty ones?
options: A large basti with plenty of drug
A basti given after a heavy meal
A small basti with little drug
A basti too hot and too sharp
optionExplain: The verse says अल्प (small) and अल्पभेषज (little drug), not large or plentiful.
No meal is named in verse 25.
Right: बस्तिरल्पोऽल्पभेषजः: बस्तिः अल्पः अल्पभेषजः, small and with little drug.
Verse 25 names no sharp basti; too hot and sharp is the atiyoga basti of 05.06.69.
questions.explain: Line 2 ends with बस्तिः अल्पः अल्पभेषजः: small, with little drug.
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: Match each word of verse 25 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words name the faults that open the statement of 05.06.48-51.
questions.rule: वेग = urge; संरोध = holding back; अतिमात्रा = excess quantity; अल्प = small; भेषज = drug.
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: Put these words of verse 25 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Line 1: holding back the urge, then excess quantity; line 2 ends: the basti small, with little drug.
questions.teaches: Verse 25 lists faults: the urge held back, excess quantity, and a small basti with little drug.
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: Which split of बस्तिरल्पो is right?
optionExplain: रल्प is not a word; the र् is the changed visarga of बस्तिः.
अल्पम् before the vowel of the next word would print अल्पमल्प, not अल्पो ऽल्प.
ई before अ would become य्: बस्त्यल्प; and बस्ती is not the nominative here.
Right: ः after इ becomes र् before a vowel: बस्तिर् अल्पः; -अः then becomes -ओ before the next अ (ऽल्प).
questions.explain: बस्तिः (the basti) + अल्पः (small); then अल्पः + अल्पभेषजः → अल्पोऽल्पभेषजः.
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: A physician reviews a basti that rose up. Which faults are named in verse 25?
options: It was given on an empty stomach
It was small and had little drug
optionExplain: No empty stomach is named in verse 25.
Right: बस्तिरल्पो ऽल्पभेषजः.
No time of day is named in verse 25.
Right: पीडितो वा ऽतिमात्रया names excess quantity.
Right: वेगसंरोधं.
questions.explain: Verse 25 names the held urge, the excess quantity and the small basti with little drug.
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: By the pattern of अतिमात्रया (by excess quantity), what does the new word अल्पमात्रया mean?
optionExplain: Right: -मात्रया is f. instrumental singular: 'by, with' the quantity; अल्प = small.
The subject form would be अल्पमात्रा, without -या.
'Of' needs the genitive अल्पमात्रायाः.
'In' needs the locative, and -या here is singular.
questions.explain: मात्रा (f.) → instrumental मात्रया, 'by the quantity'.
questions.teaches: अतिमात्रया is the feminine instrumental singular of अतिमात्रा: 'by excess quantity'.
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: By which way does the basti come out, according to verse 26?
options: From the anus with the stool
optionExplain: Verse 26 says the basti is thrown upward and leaves by mouth and nose.
Right: मुखनासिकात् निरेति: it comes out from the mouth and nose.
Sweat is not named in verse 26.
The urinary passage is not named in verse 26.
questions.explain: मुख-नासिकात् is an ablative: 'from the mouth and nose'.
questions.rule: मुखनासिकात् = from mouth and nose; निरेति = comes out.
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: Put these words of verse 26 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Or mild, by the wind upward thrown, from mouth and nose, comes out.
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: Match each word of verse 26 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The first two words say how the basti moves; the last three are signs it produces.
questions.rule: मारुत = wind; ऊर्ध्वम् = upward; मूर्च्छा = fainting; हृल्लास = nausea; दाह = burning.
questions.teaches: Verse 26: thrown upward by the wind (मारुत), the basti produces मूर्च्छा, हृल्लास, thirst and दाह.
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: Which split of मारुतेनोर्ध्वं is right?
optionExplain: मारुतेना is not a form; the instrumental of मारुत is मारुतेन.
ओर्ध्वम् is not a word, and अ + ओ would give औ.
Right: अ + ऊ → ओ: मारुतेन + ऊर्ध्वम् → मारुतेनोर्ध्वम्; final म् shows as anusvara.
मारुतेनः is not a form; and -अः before ऊ would drop the visarga, giving मारुतेन ऊर्ध्वम्.
questions.explain: मारुतेन (by the wind) + ऊर्ध्वम् (upward).
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: A basti has come out through a patient's mouth. What does verse 26 say moved it?
options: Its own heat lifted it up
A fit of vomiting drew it up
optionExplain: Straining is not named in verse 26.
Verse 26 names the wind, not heat, as what threw it.
Vomiting is not named in verse 26.
Right: मारुतेनोर्ध्वं विक्षिप्तः: thrown upward by the wind.
questions.explain: विक्षिप्तः (thrown) with the instrumental मारुतेन (by the wind) and ऊर्ध्वम् (upward).
questions.rule: मारुतेन ऊर्ध्वं विक्षिप्तः = thrown upward by the wind.
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: Like मुखनासिकात् निरेति (comes out from mouth and nose), what does the new sentence वायुः गुदात् निरेति mean?
options: The wind comes out from the anus
The wind goes into the anus
The wind of the anus comes out
The wind will come out of the anus
optionExplain: Right: गुदात् is ablative, 'from the anus'; निरेति = comes out; वायुः is the subject.
'Into' would need an accusative or locative, and निरेति means comes out.
'Of the anus' would need the genitive गुदस्य.
निरेति is present, not future.
questions.explain: -आत् ablative = 'from'; निः + √इ = to come out.
questions.rule: गुदात् = from the anus; निरेति = comes out (present).
questions.teaches: मुखनासिकात् is an ablative ('from mouth and nose'); निरेति (niḥ-√i) means 'comes out'.
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: When the fainting is seen, what is done to the face, by verse 27?
options: It is rubbed with warm oil and salt
It is sprinkled with cold water
It is covered with mustard paste
It is held down toward the floor
optionExplain: Verse 27 names cold water, not warm oil and salt.
Right: सिञ्चेत् शीताम्बुना मुखम्: sprinkle the face with cold water.
Mustard is used on the head in 05.06.68, not on the face here.
Face downward belongs to 05.06.54, the next verse.
questions.explain: शीत-अम्बुना (with cold water), मुखम् (the face), सिञ्चेत् (should sprinkle).
questions.rule: शीताम्बु = cold water; सिञ्चेत् = should sprinkle.
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: Put the steps of verse 27 in the text's order.
questions.explain: Seeing the fainting, sprinkle the face, fan, and make him do prāṇāyāma.
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: Match each word of verse 27 to its meaning.
questions.explain: One absolutive and two potentials carry the steps; शीताम्बु and मुखम् say with what and on what.
questions.rule: दृष्ट्वा = having seen; सिञ्चेत् = should sprinkle; शीताम्बु = cold water; मुख = face; कारयेत् = should make do.
questions.teaches: Verse 27 links its steps with the absolutive दृष्ट्वा and the potentials सिञ्चेत् and कारयेत्.
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: Which split of सिंचेच्छीतांबुना is right?
optionExplain: च्छीताम्बुना is not a word; the च्छ comes from त् + श.
छीत is not a word; the छ is the changed श of शीत.
Right: त् + श → च्छ: सिञ्चेत् + शीताम्बुना → सिञ्चेच्छीताम्बुना.
सिञ्चेः would be 2nd person, and ः + श does not give च्छ.
questions.explain: सिञ्चेत् (should sprinkle) + शीत-अम्बुना (with cold water).
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: A patient faints after the basti comes up. Which measures does verse 27 itself order?
options: Sprinkling the face with cold water
Kneading the belly with hot hands
optionExplain: Right: सिञ्चेच्छीताम्बुना मुखं.
That comes in 05.06.54, the next verse.
That comes in 05.06.57, not in verse 27.
Right: प्राणायामं च कारयेत्.
Right: व्यजेत्, should fan.
questions.explain: Verse 27 has three measures: cold water on the face, fanning, prāṇāyāma.
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: By the pattern of दृष्ट्वा (having seen), what does the new sentence रोगिणं दृष्ट्वा वैद्यः बस्तिं ददाति mean?
options: The patient, having seen the physician, gives a basti
The physician will see the patient after the basti
Seeing the basti, the patient gives it to the physician
Having seen the patient, the physician gives a basti
optionExplain: रोगिणम् is accusative, the one seen; the subject is वैद्यः.
दृष्ट्वा is not future, and the seeing comes before the giving.
बस्तिम् is the object of ददाति, and the patient is the one seen.
Right: दृष्ट्वा is an absolutive: the seeing comes first; वैद्यः is the subject of ददाति.
questions.explain: -त्वा absolutive = 'having done': दृष्ट्वा = having seen.
questions.teaches: दृष्ट्वा is the absolutive of √दृश्: 'having seen', an action finished before the main verb.
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: With what are the back, sides and belly kneaded, by verse 28?
options: With cloths soaked in cold water
optionExplain: Right: करैः उष्णैः मृद्यात्: knead with hot hands.
Oil and salt are not named in verse 28.
Cold water is used on the face in 05.06.52, not for kneading.
Mustard belongs to the head in 05.06.68.
questions.explain: करैः उष्णैः: both instrumental plural, 'with hot hands'.
questions.rule: कर = hand; उष्ण = hot; मृद्यात् = should knead.
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: Match each word of verse 28 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Three parts are kneaded; the hair is pulled; the patient lies face downward.
questions.rule: पृष्ठ = back; पार्श्व = side; उदर = belly; केश = hair; अधोमुख = face down.
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: Put these words of verse 28 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Knead the back, sides, belly with hot hands; pull by the hair, shake; frighten.
questions.rule: पृष्ठपार्श्वोदरं · मृद्यात् · करैरुष्णैः ‖ केशेष्वाक्षिप्य · धुन्वीत · भीषयेत्.
questions.teaches: Verse 28 has three acts in order: kneading (मृद्यात्), shaking by the hair (धुन्वीत), frightening (भीषयेत्).
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: Which split of केशेष्वाक्षिप्य is right?
optionExplain: Short अ would print केशेष्वक्षिप्य; the print has वा, from long आ.
Right: उ before a different vowel becomes व्: केशेषु + आक्षिप्य → केशेष्वाक्षिप्य.
केशेष्व is not a word; the व् is the changed उ of केशेषु.
The locative plural is केशेषु with short उ.
questions.explain: केशेषु (in the hair, loc. pl.) + आक्षिप्य (having pulled).
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: Verse 28 says the patient is to be frightened. With what?
options: Loud drums, conches and sudden shouting
A threat that a stronger basti will follow
Snakes or savage beasts, and fanged (ones)
A dark, locked room with no lamp
optionExplain: No sound is named in verse 28.
No such threat is named in verse 28.
Right: भीषयेद् व्यालदंष्ट्रिभिः: with vyāla and daṃṣṭrin.
Darkness is not named in verse 28.
questions.explain: व्याल = snake or savage beast; दंष्ट्रिन् = fanged (animal).
questions.rule: भीषयेत् व्यालदंष्ट्रिभिः = frighten with vyāla and fanged (ones).
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: Like करैः उष्णैः मृद्यात् (knead with hot hands), what does the new sentence हस्तैः शीतैः मृद्यात् mean?
options: One should knead the cold hands
One should knead the hands in the cold
One should knead with cold hands
optionExplain: 'The hands' as object would need the accusative हस्तान्.
The subject would be nominative हस्ताः शीताः.
शीतैः agrees with हस्तैः; it is not a locative 'in the cold'.
Right: हस्तैः शीतैः: noun and adjective both instrumental plural, 'with cold hands'.
questions.explain: Adjective agrees with its noun in case and number: करैः उष्णैः, हस्तैः शीतैः.
questions.teaches: करैः उष्णैः shows an adjective agreeing with its noun in the instrumental plural: 'with hot hands'.
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: With what is pressure made on the throat, by verse 29?
options: With a rope and a stick
optionExplain: Right: पाणिवस्त्रैः गलापीडं कुर्यात्: with hands and cloths.
Rope and stick are not named in verse 29.
Hot hands knead the back and belly in 05.06.54; no oil here.
Mustard is not named in verse 29.
questions.explain: पाणि-वस्त्रैः: a dvandva in the instrumental plural, 'with hands and cloths'.
questions.rule: पाणि = hand; वस्त्र = cloth; गलापीड = pressure on the throat.
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: Match each word of verse 29 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Three things frighten; hands and cloths press the throat.
questions.rule: शस्त्र = weapon; उल्का = firebrand; राजपुरुष = king's man; पाणि = hand; गल = throat.
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: Put these phrases of verse 29 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: First the frightening things and the reason; then the throat pressure with hands and cloths.
questions.rule: शस्त्रोल्काराजपुरुषैः · बस्तिरेति तथा ह्यधः ‖ पाणिवस्त्रैः · गलापीडं कुर्यात्.
questions.teaches: Verse 29 gives a reason inside the list: तथा हि अधः एति, 'for thus the basti goes downward'.
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: Which split of ह्यधः is right?
optionExplain: ह्य is not a word, and अ + अ would give a long आ (ह्याधः).
Right: इ before a different vowel becomes य्: हि + अधः → ह्यधः.
हि + आ would print ह्याधः, with a long आ.
हि + धः would print हिधः; and धः is not a word.
questions.explain: हि (for) + अधः (downward).
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: A patient is frightened with weapons and firebrands. What does verse 29 say this does to the basti?
options: It comes out through the nose
It is absorbed by the body
It rises up to the head
optionExplain: That is the fault of 05.06.50-51, not the effect of frightening.
Absorption is not named in verse 29.
Right: बस्तिरेति तथा ह्यधः: for thus the basti goes downward.
Verse 29 says downward (अधः), not to the head.
questions.explain: अधः एति = goes downward; हि gives the reason.
questions.rule: बस्तिः अधः एति = the basti goes down.
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: By the pattern of पाणिवस्त्रैः (with hands and cloths), what does the new word तैलघृतैः mean?
optionExplain: A dvandva joins equals; no cooking is stated.
'Of' needs the genitive -आनाम्, not -ऐः.
The subject form would be तैलघृतानि.
Right: A dvandva with the instrumental plural -ऐः: 'with oil and ghee'.
questions.explain: dvandva + -ऐः = 'with X and Y'.
questions.rule: पाणिवस्त्रैः = with hands and cloths; तैलघृतैः = with oil and ghee.
questions.teaches: पाणिवस्त्रैः is a dvandva (hand and cloth) in the instrumental plural: 'with hands and cloths'.
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: Which wind draws the basti away, by verse 30?
optionExplain: Right: अपानः पवनः बस्तिं तम् आशु एव अपकर्षति.
Prāṇa is obstructed in verse 30; it does not draw the basti.
Udāna is obstructed with prāṇa; it does not draw the basti.
Samāna is not named in verse 30.
questions.explain: The subject of अपकर्षति is अपानः पवनः.
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: Match each word of verse 30 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words carry the cause (obstruction) and the result (the wind draws the basti away quickly).
questions.rule: निरोध = obstruction; अयन = course; पवन = wind; आशु = quickly; अपकर्षति = draws away.
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: Put these words of verse 30 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Cause first (the obstruction), then the wind described, then what it does to the basti.
questions.rule: प्राणोदाननिरोधाद्धि · सुप्रसिद्धतरायणः ‖ अपानः पवनो · बस्तिं तम् · आश्वेवापकर्षति.
questions.teaches: Verse 30 runs from cause (ablative निरोधात्) to the wind (अपानः) to its act (अपकर्षति).
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: Which split of प्राणोदान is right?
optionExplain: -अः before उ drops the visarga and does not merge: प्राण उदान.
Right: अ + उ → ओ: प्राण + उदान → प्राणोदान.
ओदान is not a word, and अ + ओ would give औ.
प्राणो is not a stem; दान is not the second wind.
questions.explain: प्राण and उदान, two winds, joined in a dvandva.
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: A physician wants apāna to draw a risen basti away. By verse 30, which winds must be obstructed?
optionExplain: Apāna is the one that draws; vyāna is not named.
Apāna draws the basti; it is not obstructed.
Right: प्राणोदाननिरोधात्: from the obstruction of prāṇa and udāna.
Apāna draws the basti; only udāna of this pair is obstructed.
questions.explain: Obstructed: prāṇa and udāna; drawing: apāna.
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: Like प्राणोदाननिरोधात् (from the obstruction of prāṇa and udāna), what does the new sentence वेगनिरोधात् शूलं भवति mean?
options: Holding back the urge arises from pain
In holding back the urge there is pain
Pain arises from holding back the urge
optionExplain: शूलम् is the subject that arises; the ablative names the cause.
There is no verb 'holds back'; भवति = arises, is.
'In' would need the locative निरोधे.
Right: -आत् is an ablative of cause: 'from (because of) the obstruction of the urge'.
questions.explain: Ablative -आत् of a cause = 'from, because of'.
questions.teaches: निरोधात् is an ablative of cause: 'from (because of) the obstruction'.
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: With what is the paste of verse 31 joined?
optionExplain: Right: अम्लसंयुतम्: joined with sour (amla); the sour item is not named.
Honey is not named in verse 31.
Ghee is not named in verse 31.
Milk is not named in verse 31.
questions.explain: अम्ल-संयुत = joined with sour.
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: Match each word of verse 31 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Two drugs make the paste; it is joined with sour and works by its qualities.
questions.rule: कुष्ठ = costus; क्रमुक = areca nut (probable); कल्क = paste; अम्ल = sour; तैक्ष्ण्य = sharpness.
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: Put these words of verse 31 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The paste and what it is joined with; then the three qualities; then what it does.
questions.rule: कुष्ठक्रमुककल्कं · अम्लसंयुतं ‖ औष्ण्यात् · तैक्ष्ण्यात् · सरत्वात् · अनुलोमयेत्.
questions.teaches: Verse 31 gives three causes in the ablative: heat (औष्ण्यात्), sharpness (तैक्ष्ण्यात्), flowing nature (सरत्वात्).
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: What does कुष्ठ name in verse 31, by the card?
options: The skin disease of that name
optionExplain: The word also names a skin disease, but here it is a drug in a paste.
Right: Here kuṣṭha is a drug in the paste (costus, standard), not the disease.
The sour is अम्ल, a separate word.
Areca nut (probable) is kramuka, the second drug.
questions.explain: Same word, two senses: here the drug, since it forms a kalka with kramuka.
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: Why does the paste of verse 31 bring the basti into the natural direction? Choose all the reasons it gives.
optionExplain: Right: सरत्वात्.
Heaviness is not named in verse 31.
Right: तैक्ष्ण्यात्.
Right: औष्ण्यात्.
Coldness is not named; heat is.
questions.explain: Three ablatives of cause: औष्ण्य, तैक्ष्ण्य, सरत्व.
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: By the pattern of सरत्वात् (from flowing nature), what does the new word गुरुत्वात् mean?
optionExplain: That would be the adjective गुरवः, not an abstract noun.
'Into' would not be an ablative.
Right: -त्व makes an abstract noun (गुरु heavy → गुरुत्व heaviness); -आत् is the ablative 'from'.
'Of' would need the genitive गुरोः.
questions.explain: Adjective + -त्व = quality; + -आत् = 'from, because of'.
questions.rule: सरत्वात् = from flowing nature; गुरुत्वात् = from heaviness.
questions.teaches: सरत्वात् is the ablative of सरत्व (abstract noun from सर, flowing): 'from flowing nature'.
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: With what is the trivṛt and pathyā paste given, by verse 32?
optionExplain: Sour goes with the costus paste of 05.06.60, not this one.
Honey is not named in verse 32.
Milk is not named in verse 32.
Right: गोमूत्रेण त्रिवृत्पथ्याकल्कम्: the paste with cow's urine.
questions.explain: गो-मूत्रेण: instrumental, 'with cow's urine'.
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: Match each word of verse 32 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Two drugs and a liquid in line 1; a seat and a basti in line 2.
questions.rule: त्रिवृत् = turpeth; पथ्या = chebulic myrobalan; गोमूत्र = cow's urine; पक्वाशय = large intestine; दाशमूलिक = of daśamūla.
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: Put these words of verse 32 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Line 1: the paste with cow's urine, a downward anulomana; line 2: seat, sweating, the nirūha.
questions.rule: गोमूत्रेण · त्रिवृत्पथ्याकल्कं · अधोऽनुलोमनं ‖ पक्वाशयस्थिते · स्विन्ने · निरूहो दाशमूलिकः.
questions.teaches: Verse 32 line 2 opens the remedies by seat: for the pakvāśaya, a daśamūla nirūha to one sweated.
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: What does पथ्या name in verse 32, by the card?
optionExplain: Right: पथ्या is taken as the drug (haritakī, हरड़), standard.
That is the plain meaning of the word, not used here.
No gruel is named in verse 32.
The ten roots are not listed; pathyā is in the paste of line 1.
questions.explain: In a kalka with trivṛt, पथ्या is a drug name.
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: When (it) is situated in the pakvāśaya and the patient has been sweated, which basti does verse 32 name?
options: A paste of costus and areca nut
An oil basti with rock salt
optionExplain: That paste is drunk (05.06.60); it is not the pakvāśaya basti.
Right: पक्वाशयस्थिते स्विन्ने निरूहो दाशमूलिकः.
Those are for the head (05.06.68).
Oil and rock salt belong to the chest basti of 05.06.67.
questions.explain: Seat pakvāśaya → daśamūla nirūha, after sweating.
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: Like पक्वाशयस्थिते (when situated in the pakvāśaya), what does the new word कण्ठस्थिते mean?
options: From the place of the throat
When (it) is situated in the throat
optionExplain: 'From' would need an ablative, not -स्थिते.
