स्थित means 'situated', not 'stands', and -स्थिते is a locative, not a subject form (that would be कण्ठस्थितः, 'situated in the throat').
Right: -स्थिते is a locative: 'when (it) is situated in'; कण्ठ = throat.
स्थित is a past participle 'situated', not 'having placed'.
questions.explain: X-स्थिते (locative) = 'when (it) is situated in X'.
questions.teaches: पक्वाशयस्थिते is a locative tat-puruṣa: 'when (it) is situated in the pakvāśaya'.
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: In what are yava, kola and kulattha prepared, by verse 33?
optionExplain: Milk is not named in verse 33.
Oil is not named in verse 33.
No gruel is named in verse 33.
Right: मूत्रसाधितैः: prepared in urine.
questions.explain: मूत्र-साधित = prepared in urine (the animal is not named here).
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: Match each drug of verse 33 to its identification on the card.
questions.explain: Three drugs of the first basti, two of the second.
questions.rule: यव = barley; कोल = jujube (probable); कुलत्थ = horse gram; वंश = bamboo (probable); अमृता = giloy (probable).
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: Put these words of verse 33 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Line 1: the three drugs, to be given, prepared in urine; line 2: a basti, cooked in cow's urine, with amṛtā and bamboo shoots.
questions.rule: यवकोलकुलत्थैश्च · विधेयो · मूत्रसाधितैः ‖ बस्तिर् · गौमूत्रसिद्धैर्वा · सामृतावंशपल्लवैः.
questions.teaches: Verse 33 gives two bastis joined by वा: yava, kola and kulattha prepared in urine, or shoots cooked in cow's urine.
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: Which drug does verse 33 join with amṛtā (sa-amṛtā)?
optionExplain: Right: सामृतावंशपल्लवैः: shoots of vaṃśa with amṛtā.
Kulattha belongs to the first basti, with yava and kola.
Pathyā is in the paste of 05.06.62, not here.
Kramuka is in the paste of 05.06.60.
questions.explain: स (with) + अमृता + वंश-पल्लवैः: amṛtā goes with the bamboo shoots.
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: A physician makes the first basti of verse 33 (prepared in urine). Which drugs go in?
optionExplain: Amṛtā is in the second basti, cooked in cow's urine.
Right: कुलत्थ.
The bamboo shoots are in the second basti.
Right: कोल.
Right: यव.
questions.explain: First basti: yava, kola, kulattha in urine; second: amṛtā and vaṃśa shoots in cow's urine.
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: By the pattern of विधेयः (is to be administered), what does the new sentence स्वेदः विधेयः mean?
optionExplain: A gerundive is not a past form.
Right: विधेय is a gerundive: 'is to be done/administered'; it agrees with स्वेदः.
विधेयः is passive in sense: the sweating is what is administered.
There is no negative and no future in the sentence.
questions.explain: Gerundive -य/-तव्य/-अनीय = 'is to be done'.
questions.teaches: विधेयः is a gerundive of vi-√dhā: 'is to be administered', agreeing with its noun.
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: Unit 34 continues a list from 05.06.65. What is it a list of?
options: Signs of the basti thrown upward
Foods for the patient after the basti
Drugs of the basti cooked in cow's urine
Drugs for nasal medication of the head
optionExplain: The signs (fainting, nausea) are in 05.06.51.
No food is named in unit 34.
Right: It adds ingredients to the basti of 05.06.65 (amṛtā and bamboo shoots).
Nasal medication for the head comes in 05.06.68.
questions.explain: The instrumental plural -ऐः ties the unit to the basti of 05.06.65.
questions.rule: Unit 34 = more drugs for the cow's-urine basti.
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: Match each word of unit 34 to its meaning on the card.
questions.explain: Bark and leaf are of pūtīkarañja; śaṭhī is disputed; rohiṣa is a scented grass (probable).
questions.rule: त्वक् = bark; पत्र = leaf; रोहिष = palmarosa (probable); शठी = disputed.
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: After त्वक् (bark), unit 34 names ____ (leaf). Type it in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: त्वक्पत्र = त्वक् (bark) + पत्र (leaf), here of pūtīkarañja.
questions.teaches: पत्र = leaf; with त्वक् it names the bark and leaf of pūtīkarañja.
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: How does the card label the identity of pūtīkarañja and śaṭhī?
optionExplain: Neither has a standard identification on the card.
Both are disputed, not probable or standard.
Proposals exist for both, so they are disputed, not unidentified.
Right: The data marks both 'identity disputed'.
questions.explain: Disputed: proposals exist but scholars differ.
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: Put these items of unit 34 in the text's order.
questions.explain: The compound runs pūtīkarañja, bark, leaf, śaṭhī, (devāhva,) rohiṣa.
questions.rule: पूतीकरञ्ज · त्वक् · पत्र · शठी · (देवाह्व, अनुमानित) · रोहिष.
questions.teaches: Unit 34's compound lists pūtīkarañja's bark and leaf, then śaṭhī, devāhva (conjectural) and rohiṣa.
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: Like the ending -ऐः of unit 34 (with ...), what does the new word निम्बपत्रैः mean (निम्ब = neem)?
optionExplain: Right: -ऐः is the instrumental plural, 'with'; निम्ब-पत्र = neem leaf.
The subject form would be निम्बपत्राणि.
'Of' would need the genitive निम्बपत्राणाम्.
'In' would need the locative निम्बपत्रेषु.
questions.explain: The whole drug list of unit 34 stands in the instrumental plural -ऐः.
questions.teaches: Unit 34's whole compound ends in -ऐः, the instrumental plural: 'with' these drugs.
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: For which seat is the basti of unit 35 given?
options: When (it) is situated in the head
When (it) is situated in the chest
When (it) is held in the throat
optionExplain: The head comes in 05.06.68 with nasal medication and smoke.
Right: उरःस्थिते: when situated in the chest.
The pakvāśaya has the daśamūla nirūha of 05.06.63.
The throat is not a seat named in unit 35.
questions.explain: उरः-स्थिते: locative, 'when (it) is situated in the chest'.
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: Match each word of unit 35 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Three additions, the purgative paste, and the seat.
questions.rule: तैल = oil; गुड = jaggery; सिन्धूत्थ = rock salt; विरेक = purgation; उरः = chest.
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: Put these words of unit 35 in the text's order.
questions.explain: First half: with oil, jaggery, rock salt; with the purgative paste. Second half: cooked with the bilva five roots, the basti, in the chest.
questions.rule: सतैलगुडसिंधूत्थो · विरेकौषधकल्कवान् ‖ बिल्वादिपंचमूलेन · सिद्धो · बस्तिर् · उरःस्थिते.
questions.teaches: Unit 35 describes the basti first and names the seat (उरःस्थिते) last.
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: With what is the chest basti of unit 35 cooked?
options: The five roots beginning with bilva
A paste of costus and areca
optionExplain: The daśamūla nirūha is for the pakvāśaya (05.06.63).
Those are cooked in cow's urine in 05.06.65.
Right: बिल्वादिपञ्चमूलेन सिद्धः: cooked with the bilva five roots.
That paste is drunk in 05.06.60.
questions.explain: बिल्व-आदि पञ्च-मूल = the five roots of which bilva (bael) is the first; the other four are not named.
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: A physician prepares the chest basti of unit 35. Which does the text put in it?
optionExplain: Mustard is for the head (05.06.68).
Cow's urine is not named in unit 35.
Right: सिन्धूत्थ.
Right: गुड.
Right: स-तैल.
Right: विरेकौषधकल्कवान्.
questions.explain: स-तैल-गुड-सिन्धूत्थ + विरेक-औषध-कल्क, cooked with the bilva five roots.
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: By the pattern of कल्कवान् (having a paste), what does the new phrase घृतवान् बस्तिः mean?
optionExplain: घृतवान् describes बस्तिः; the basti is the one that has.
-वत् means having; 'without' would be a- or nir-.
-वान् means 'having'; nothing in घृतवान् says 'like' or 'cooked'.
Right: -वत् (nom. -वान्) means 'having, possessing'; it agrees with बस्तिः.
questions.explain: X-वान् = having X.
questions.rule: कल्कवान् = having a paste; घृतवान् = having ghee.
questions.teaches: कल्कवान् is the possessive -वत् (nom. -वान्): 'having a paste'.
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: With what is the head to be covered, by verse 36?
options: With a cloth soaked in cold water
With warm oil and rock salt
optionExplain: Right: प्रच्छाद्यं सर्षपैः शिरः: the head to be covered with mustard.
Cold water is used on the face in 05.06.52.
Pūtīkarañja is a basti drug in 05.06.66.
Oil and rock salt go in the chest basti of 05.06.67.
questions.explain: सर्षपैः: instrumental plural, 'with mustard'.
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: Match each word of verse 36 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Line 1 has the head measures; घन is one of the faults of the basti in line 2.
questions.rule: नावन = nasal medication; धूम = smoke; सर्षप = mustard; प्रच्छाद्य = to be covered; घन = thick.
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: Put the qualities of the basti in line 2 of verse 36 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Too hot, sharp, sour, thick; or (given to) one excessively sweated.
questions.teaches: Line 2 of verse 36 begins the over-application (atiyoga) statement; it goes on to 05.06.71.
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: Which basti does line 2 of verse 36 describe?
options: One cold, small and with little drug
One too hot, sharp, sour and thick
One thin and mild, for a harsh koṣṭha
One cooked with the bilva five roots
optionExplain: Cold and small bastis are faults of 05.06.36 and 05.06.49.
Right: बस्तिरत्युष्णतीक्ष्णाम्लघनः.
Thin and mild is the basti of 05.06.35, not this line.
That is the chest basti of 05.06.67, a remedy.
questions.explain: बस्तिरत्युष्णतीक्ष्णाम्लघनः: a basti too hot, sharp, sour, thick.
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: A patient's trouble is situated in the head. Which pair of measures does verse 36 give, besides covering the head?
optionExplain: Those are for fainting (05.06.53).
Those frighten the patient (05.06.56).
Right: शिरःस्थे नावनं धूमः.
That is for the pakvāśaya (05.06.63).
questions.explain: Head: nāvana and dhūma, and the head covered with mustard.
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: Like अत्युष्ण (too hot, अति + उष्ण), what does the new phrase अतिशीतः बस्तिः mean?
options: A basti that is not cold
A basti given after the cold
A basti that is too cold
optionExplain: 'Not' would be अ-: अशीत.
अति- means too much, not slightly.
अतिशीतः is an adjective agreeing with बस्तिः, not a time.
Right: अति- = too, excessively; शीत = cold.
questions.explain: अति + vowel: इ → य् (अत्युष्ण); before a consonant it stays अति (अतिशीत).
questions.teaches: अत्युष्ण = अति + उष्ण: अति- means 'too, excessively' (इ → य् before उ).
questions.section: मुख-नासिका से बस्ति निकलना और उपाय

questions.q: What would the basti cause once it has reached over-application, by verse 37?
optionExplain: Right: कुक्षिशूलकरो भवेत्: it would become a cause of belly-pain.
Hiccup comes from the very sharp basti in a weak person, 05.06.87.
Yawning is produced by the basti gone a wrong path, 05.06.80.
Fainting follows the basti that comes out of mouth and nose, 05.06.51.
questions.explain: कुक्षि = belly, शूल = pain, -कर = causing.

questions.q: Put these phrases of verse 37 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Three conditions first (little doṣa, soft koṣṭha, repeated use), then the state reached, then the result.
questions.rule: अल्पे दोषे · मृदौ कोष्ठे · प्रयुक्तो वा पुनः पुनः ‖ अतियोगत्वमापन्नः · कुक्षिशूलकरो भवेत्.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 37 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The first four words give the conditions; अतियोग names the state the basti reaches.
questions.rule: अल्प = little; मृदु = soft; कोष्ठ = storehouse (belly); पुनः पुनः = again and again; अतियोग = over-application.
questions.teaches: Verse 37: a little doṣa, a soft koṣṭha or repeated use bring the basti to अतियोग.

questions.q: Which split of अतियोगत्वमापन्नः is right?
optionExplain: अतियोगत्वमा and पन्नः are not words; the म belongs to -त्वम्.
Right: Final म् joins the next vowel: अतियोगत्वम् + आपन्नः → अतियोगत्वमापन्नः.
-अः before आ loses its visarga and leaves a gap: अतियोगत्व आपन्नः, not त्वमा.
म् + short अ would print मप (त्वमपन्नः); the print has the long मा.
questions.explain: अतियोगत्वम् (the state of over-application, acc.) + आपन्नः (having reached).

questions.q: A physician asks when the basti of 05.06.69 slips into over-application. Which conditions does verse 37 name?
options: It is applied again and again
optionExplain: Right: मृदौ कोष्ठे.
Strength is not named in verse 37.
Verse 37 says soft (मृदु), not hard.
Right: प्रयुक्तो वा पुनः पुनः.
Right: अल्पे दोषे.
questions.explain: Three conditions: little doṣa, soft koṣṭha, repeated application.
questions.rule: अल्प दोष · मृदु कोष्ठ · पुनः पुनः.

questions.q: By the pattern of कुक्षिशूलकरः (causing belly-pain), what does the new word शिरःशूलकरः mean?
optionExplain: Removing would need -हर or -घ्न, not -कर.
-कर is active, 'causing', not 'caused by'.
Right: -कर at the end of a compound = 'making, causing'; शिरः-शूल = head-pain.
कर can mean hand, but at the end of this compound it is 'causing'.
questions.explain: X-शूल-कर = causing X-pain.
questions.teaches: कुक्षिशूलकरः = कुक्षि-शूल-कर: -कर at the end of a compound means 'causing'.

questions.q: To what is this over-application said to be similar in features and treatment, by verse 38?
options: The basti come out of the mouth
optionExplain: Too little application (ayoga) is not named; the verse says अतियोग.
That mishap is 05.06.50-51, not the comparison here.
Over-sweating is one cause in 05.06.69, not the comparison.
Right: विरेचनातियोगेन … तुल्य: similar to over-application of purgation (virecana).
questions.explain: तुल्य takes the instrumental: विरेचनातियोगेन तुल्य = similar to purgation's over-application.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 38 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Line 1: similar in features and treatment to over-application of purgation.
questions.rule: तुल्य = similar; आकृति = features; साधन = treatment; विरेचन = purgation; अतियोग = over-application.

questions.q: Put these drugs of line 2 of verse 38 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: After pṛśniparṇī: sthirā, padma, kāśmarya, then the pair madhūka-utpala.
questions.teaches: Line 2 of verse 38 opens the remedy list for over-application; the list goes on in 05.06.74.

questions.q: Which identification does the card give for काश्मर्य?
optionExplain: Right: kāśmarya = gambhārī, Gmelina arborea (standard).
Mahua is madhūka, the next item.
Blue lotus is utpala (probable).
Śālaparṇī is the probable identity of sthirā.
questions.explain: काश्मर्य = gambhārī (standard).

questions.q: A physician gathers the drugs of line 2 of verse 38 after pṛśniparṇī. Which belong there?
optionExplain: Right: काश्मर्यं.
Drākṣā is ground in 05.06.74, the next line.
Right: पद्मं.
Right: स्थिरां.
Bilva is in the list of 05.06.82, not here.
Right: मधूकोत्पले.
questions.explain: Line 2: (pṛśniparṇī), sthirā, padma, kāśmarya, madhūka, utpala.

questions.q: Like विरेचनातियोगेन तुल्यः, what does the new sentence अयं वमनातियोगेन तुल्यः mean (vamana = emesis)?
options: This is caused by over-application of emesis
This is similar to over-application of emesis
This is unlike the over-application of emesis
This treats the over-application of emesis
optionExplain: With तुल्य the instrumental gives the thing compared, not the cause.
Right: तुल्य with the instrumental = 'similar to'; अयम् = this.
तुल्य means similar; 'unlike' would be अतुल्य.
No word for treating is in the sentence.
questions.explain: तुल्य + instrumental: X-एन तुल्यः = similar to X.
questions.teaches: In verse 38 तुल्य governs the instrumental विरेचनातियोगेन: 'similar to over-application of purgation'.

questions.q: Which liquids does line 1 of verse 39 name for the grinding?
optionExplain: Cow's urine is in 05.06.65 and whey (mastu) in 05.06.83.
Hot water comes with pippalī in 05.06.90.
Right: क्षीरे तण्डुलधावने: in milk, in rice-washing (water).
Āranāla and prasannā come in 05.06.89.
questions.explain: Two locatives: क्षीरे (in milk), तण्डुल-धावने (in rice-washing).

questions.q: Put these words of line 1 of verse 39 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Having ground, drākṣā and madhūka, in milk, in rice-washing.
questions.rule: पिष्ट्वा · द्राक्षां · मधूकं च · क्षीरे · तंडुलधावने.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 39 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The absolutive gives the action; the rest name a drug and the liquids.
questions.rule: पिष्ट्वा = having ground; द्राक्षा = grape/raisin; क्षीर = milk; तण्डुल = rice; प्रसाद = clear part.
questions.teaches: Verse 39: drākṣā and madhūka are ground (पिष्ट्वा) in milk, rice-washing or a clear liquid (प्रसाद).

questions.q: What does प्रसाद mean in line 2 of verse 39?
optionExplain: That is the opposite of the clear part.
A paste is kalka; prasāda is the clear liquid.
Boiling down is not said; prasāda is the clear part.
Right: प्रसाद = clearness: the clear part that settles out of a liquid.
questions.explain: द्राक्षायाः … प्रसादे: in the clear part of drākṣā.

questions.q: Following line 1 of verse 39, what is done with drākṣā and madhūka?
optionExplain: Right: पिष्ट्वा, 'having ground', governs द्राक्षां मधूकं च.
Ghee comes with the basti in 05.06.76, not with these drugs.
Burning to ash is not named here.
Urine is not named in verse 39.
questions.explain: पिष्ट्वा from √पिष्, to grind.

questions.q: By the pattern of पिष्ट्वा (having ground), what does the new sentence औषधं पिष्ट्वा जले क्षिपेत् mean?
options: He grinds the drug while it is in water
Having ground the drug, he should put it in water
The ground drug should be kept out of water
He should grind the drug and drink the water
optionExplain: पिष्ट्वा is an absolutive, a finished earlier act, not 'while'.
Right: -त्वा absolutive: the grinding comes first; क्षिपेत् = should put.
जले is 'in water'; nothing says out of it.
No drinking is in the sentence; क्षिपेत् means put, throw.
questions.explain: X पिष्ट्वा … क्षिपेत् = having ground X, should put.
questions.teaches: पिष्ट्वा is the absolutive (-त्वा) of √पिष्: 'having ground', an act done before the main verb.

questions.q: For which complaint is the basti with ghee applied, by verse 40?
options: Hiccup in one with a soft belly
Pain of the limbs from a wrong path
optionExplain: Too little application is not the subject here; stiffness comes in 05.06.80.
Hiccup is 05.06.86-87.
Right: दाहे ऽतियोगजे: in burning born of over-application.
Limb pain comes from the misled basti of 05.06.79-80.
questions.explain: दाह (burning), अतियोग-ज (born of over-application): both locative.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 40 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Line 1 is one instruction: having added, apply the basti with ghee in burning born of over-application.
questions.rule: विनीय = having added; सघृत = with ghee; युञ्ज्यात् = should apply; दाह = burning; अतियोगज = born of over-application.

questions.q: Put the steps of the remedy of 05.06.73-76 in the text's order.
questions.explain: The drugs are ground in the liquids, added, and the basti with ghee is applied.
questions.teaches: Verse 40 completes the statement 05.06.73-76: grind, add, then apply the basti with ghee for burning.

questions.q: Which split of युंज्याद्दाहे is right?
optionExplain: द्दाहे is not a word; one द comes from the final त्.
त् + आ would print युञ्ज्यादाहे with one द.
युञ्ज्याः would be 2nd person, and -आः before द drops its visarga (युञ्ज्या दाहे), with no doubled द.
Right: त् before द becomes द्: युञ्ज्याद् + दाहे → युञ्ज्याद्दाहे.
questions.explain: युञ्ज्यात् (should apply) + दाहे (in burning).

questions.q: Line 2 of verse 40 begins describing a faulty basti. Which faults does it name?
options: Not preceded by oleation and sweating
optionExplain: A small basti is 05.06.49, not this line.
Right: स्नेहस्वेदैरसंपाद्य.
Right: तीक्ष्ण.
Cold is not named in this line.
Right: अतिमात्रकः.
Right: गुरु.
questions.explain: Line 2: without sneha and sveda; heavy, sharp, of excess quantity.

questions.q: By the pattern of असंपाद्य (without having prepared), what does the new word अविचार्य mean?
optionExplain: Right: अ- negates the -य absolutive of a prefixed root: 'without having done'.
The अ- makes it negative.
'While considering' would be a present participle such as विचारयन्.
A finite past would be a verb form, not an absolutive in -य.
questions.explain: अ + prefix + root + -य = without having done.
questions.teaches: असंपाद्य is a negative absolutive (अ- + -य): 'without having prepared'.

questions.q: What would the faulty basti of verse 41 provoke?
optionExplain: Pitta is not named in verse 41.
Right: मरुतं कोपयेत्: it would provoke the wind.
Kapha is not named in verse 41.
Blood is not named in verse 41.
questions.explain: मरुतम् (acc.) + कोपयेत् (would provoke).

questions.q: Match each word of verse 41 to its meaning.
questions.explain: For whom, how given, what it provokes, which way it went.
questions.rule: दुःस्थित = badly placed; प्रणिहित = introduced; मरुत् = wind; कोपयेत् = would provoke; विमार्गग = gone a wrong path.

questions.q: Put these words of verse 41 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: For one badly placed, introduced …; the wind would provoke, that one gone by a wrong path.
questions.teaches: Verse 41: a basti introduced (प्रणिहितः) for one badly placed provokes the wind (मरुतं कोपयेत्).

questions.q: Which split of कोपयेत्स is right?
optionExplain: त्सः is not a word; the त् ends कोपयेत्.
कोपयेः would be 2nd person; the basti is spoken of in the 3rd.
Right: सः drops its visarga before a consonant: स विमार्गगः.
सा is feminine and keeps its ā; the print has स, the masculine before a consonant.
questions.explain: कोपयेत् (would provoke) + सः (that one), सः → स before व.

questions.q: A basti is given to a patient placed in a bad posture. Which word of verse 41 describes him?
optionExplain: विमार्गगः describes the basti, gone a wrong path.
प्रणिहितः describes the basti, introduced.
कोपयेत् is the verb, would provoke.
Right: दुः-स्थिताय: for one badly placed (dative).
questions.explain: दुः- = badly; स्थित = placed; -आय = for (dative).

questions.q: By the pattern of दुःस्थिताय (for one badly placed), what does the new sentence आतुराय बस्तिं दद्यात् mean?
options: He should give a basti to the patient
He should give the patient's own basti
He should give a basti with the patient
The patient should give a basti
optionExplain: Right: -आय is the dative singular of an a-stem: 'to, for' the patient.
'The patient's' would need the genitive आतुरस्य.
'With' would need the instrumental आतुरेण.
The patient as subject would be आतुरः, not आतुराय.
questions.explain: a-stem dative singular: -आय.
questions.teaches: दुःस्थिताय is a dative singular (-आय): the basti is introduced 'for one badly placed'.

questions.q: Which of these does the basti of 05.06.77-79 produce, by verse 42?
optionExplain: Hiccup is 05.06.87, from a very sharp basti in a weak person.
Right: जृम्भाम्: yawning, one of the four effects.
Fainting is 05.06.51.
Burning from over-application is 05.06.76.
questions.explain: करोति: अङ्गरुजा, जृम्भा, स्तम्भ, पर्वभेद.

questions.q: Put the effects named in line 1 of verse 42 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Limb pain, yawning, stiffness, and splitting of the joints.
questions.rule: करोत्यंगरुजां · जृंभां · स्तंभं · भेदं च पर्वणां.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 42 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four effects; पर्वणाम् (of the joints) goes with भेदम्.
questions.rule: अङ्ग-रुजा = limb pain; जृम्भा = yawning; स्तम्भ = stiffness; भेद = splitting; पर्वन् = joint.
questions.teaches: Verse 42: the misled basti produces अङ्गरुजा, जृम्भा, स्तम्भ and पर्व-भेद.

questions.q: With what is the patient smeared in line 2 of verse 42?
optionExplain: Ghee and honey are not named in verse 42.
Mustard covers the head in 05.06.68.
Right: तैललवणाभ्यक्तम्: smeared with oil and salt.
Cold water on the face is 05.06.52.
questions.explain: तैल-लवण-अभ्यक्त = smeared with oil and salt.

questions.q: A physician prepares the patient of verse 42 for treatment. Which steps does line 2 name?
options: Sweating him with saṃstara and the others
Smearing him with oil and salt
optionExplain: Fanning is for fainting, 05.06.53.
Throat pressure is 05.06.57.
Right: स्वेदितं संस्तरादिभिः.
Right: तैललवणाभ्यक्तम्.
Frightening is 05.06.55-56.
questions.explain: Line 2: smeared with oil and salt, sweated by saṃstara etc.; the enema follows in 05.06.84.

questions.q: By the pattern of तैललवणाभ्यक्तम् (smeared with oil and salt), what does the new phrase घृताभ्यक्तं शिरः mean?
options: The head to be smeared with ghee
optionExplain: अभ्यक्त is a past participle (smeared), not a gerundive (to be smeared).
No word for keeping; अभ्यक्त means smeared.
Nothing negates घृत.
Right: घृत + अभ्यक्त → घृताभ्यक्त (अ + अ → आ): smeared with ghee; it agrees with शिरः.
questions.explain: X-अभ्यक्त = smeared with X.
questions.teaches: तैललवणाभ्यक्तम् = तैल-लवण-अभ्यक्त: अभ्यक्त (smeared) with the means in front.

questions.q: What is boiled (शृतम्) in line 2 of verse 43?
optionExplain: Right: शृतं मस्तु: boiled whey.
Milk is a grinding liquid in 05.06.74.
Oil is used for the anuvāsana in 05.06.85.
Ghee goes with the basti of 05.06.76.
questions.explain: शृतम् agrees with मस्तु (n.).

questions.q: Match each drug of verse 43 to its identification on the card.
questions.explain: All five are standard identifications in the unit data (bilva as bael, per the glossary).
questions.rule: बिल्व = बेल; एरण्ड = अरंडी; वर्षाभू = पुनर्नवा; कुलत्थ = कुलथी; सौवीरक = खट्टी कांजी.

questions.q: Put these items of verse 43 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The compound of line 1 runs bilva … eraṇḍa, varṣābhū …; line 2 adds kulattha, then the boiled mastu.
questions.teaches: Verse 43: whey (मस्तु) is boiled with bilva, eraṇḍa, varṣābhū and the others, with kulattha.

questions.q: What is सौवीरक, by the card?
optionExplain: That is prasannā, 05.06.89.
Right: sauvīraka = a sour fermented gruel, usually of barley (standard).
That is mastu, the thing boiled here.
That is taṇḍula-dhāvana, 05.06.74.
questions.explain: फल-सौवीरक-अन्वित: joined with fruit and sauvīraka.

questions.q: In line 2 of verse 43, which two things does फलसौवीरकान्वितैः (joined with …) name?
optionExplain: Pippalī and salt are 05.06.90.
Honey is not named in verse 43.
Right: फल-सौवीरक-अन्वितैः: joined with fruit and sauvīraka; what is so joined is loose (instrumental plural).
Those join the oil of 05.06.89.
questions.explain: अन्वित = joined with.

questions.q: By the pattern of सकुलत्थैः (together with kulattha), what does the new phrase सलवणं तैलम् mean?
optionExplain: 'Without' would be अ- or निर्-: अलवण.
सलवणम् describes तैलम्; the oil is the head noun.
No word for taking from; स- means with.
Right: स- at the head of a compound = 'with, together with'.
questions.explain: स-X = with X.
questions.teaches: सकुलत्थैः = स-कुलत्थैः: the prefix स- means 'together with'.

questions.q: Which treatment does line 1 of verse 44 order?
optionExplain: Right: आस्थापयेत्: he should give an āsthāpana.
Nāvana is for the head, 05.06.68.
Smoke is named in 05.06.68 and 05.06.91.
Purgation is only compared in 05.06.72.
questions.explain: आ-√स्था (caus.) → आस्थापयेत्.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 44 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Line 1: āsthāpana with rock salt to one who has eaten with jāṅgala juices; line 2: anuvāsana.
questions.rule: आस्थापयेत् = give āsthāpana; सिन्धूत्थ = rock salt; जाङ्गल = dry-country; अशित = one who has eaten; अनुवासयेत् = give anuvāsana.

questions.q: Put these words of line 1 of verse 44 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Should give āsthāpana, with rock salt; to one fed with jāṅgala … juices.
questions.teaches: Line 1 of verse 44: āsthāpana with rock salt for one who has eaten with jāṅgala juices.

questions.q: Which split of जांगलैरशितं is right?
optionExplain: रशित is not a word; the र् is the changed visarga.
Right: -ऐः before a vowel becomes -ऐर्: जाङ्गलैर् + अशितम्.
जाङ्गलैः before श would stay a visarga: जाङ्गलैः शितम्.
म् + अ would print जाङ्गलमशितम्, not -लैर-.
questions.explain: जाङ्गलैः (with dry-country, inst. pl.) + अशितम् (one who has eaten).

questions.q: After the āsthāpana of verse 44, what is the anuvāsana given with?
optionExplain: Whey is boiled in 05.06.83 for the āsthāpana.
Cow's urine is not named in verse 44.
Right: तैलेन … अनुवासयेत्: he should give an anuvāsana with oil.
Rice-washing is 05.06.74.
questions.explain: तैलेन, instrumental: with oil.

questions.q: By the pattern of आस्थापयेत् (he should give an āsthāpana), what does the new form विरेचयेत् mean?
optionExplain: A past form would differ; -एत् is the potential.
The future would be विरेचयिष्यति.
'Having purged' would be the absolutive विरेच्य.
Right: -एत् is the potential 3rd singular: 'he should'; वि-√रिच् caus. = purge.
questions.explain: causative stem + -एत् = he should make (it) happen.
questions.teaches: आस्थापयेत् and अनुवासयेत् are causative potentials (-एत्): 'he should give an āsthāpana / anuvāsana'.

questions.q: What would the very sharp, over-expelling basti cause, by verse 45?
optionExplain: Right: कुर्याद्धिध्माम्: it would cause hiccup.
Yawning is 05.06.80.
Burning from over-application is 05.06.76.
Thirst is among the signs of 05.06.51.
questions.explain: हिध्मा (f.) = hiccup, object of कुर्यात्.

questions.q: Put these words of verse 45 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Where (soft belly, weak), what kind of basti (very sharp, over-expelling), and what it causes.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 45 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Who, what the basti does, what it causes, and what kind of remedy helps.
questions.rule: मृदुकोष्ठ = soft-bellied; अबल = weak; निर्हरन् = expelling; हिध्मा = hiccup; बृंहण = nourishing.
questions.teaches: Verse 45: in the weak, a sharp over-expelling basti causes हिध्मा; the remedy is हिध्माघ्न and बृंहण.

questions.q: Which split of कुर्याद्धिध्मां is right?
optionExplain: धिध्मा is not a word; the ध comes from the ह of हिध्मा.
Right: त् + ह → द्ध: कुर्यात् + हिध्माम् → कुर्याद्धिध्माम्.
कुर्याः would be 2nd person, and ः before ह would not give द्ध.
द्धिध्माम् is not a word; the द् is the final त् of कुर्यात्.
questions.explain: कुर्यात् (would cause) + हिध्माम् (hiccup).

questions.q: A weak patient has hiccup after a sharp basti. What does verse 45 call beneficial?
options: What is sharper and expels more
optionExplain: A very sharp, over-expelling basti caused the hiccup.
Drying and lightening are not named; the verse says nourishing.
Right: हितं तत्र हिध्माघ्नं बृंहणं च यत्.
Frightening belongs to 05.06.55-56.
questions.explain: हिध्माघ्न = hiccup-destroying; बृंहण = nourishing; हित = beneficial.

questions.q: By the pattern of हिध्माघ्नम् (hiccup-destroying), what does the new word कासघ्नम् mean (kāsa = cough)?
optionExplain: -घ्न is active, destroying, not caused by.
Producing would be -कर or -जनन.
-घ्न means the one that strikes down, not the one struck.
Right: -घ्न (from √हन्) at the end of a compound = 'destroying, killing'.
questions.explain: X-घ्न = destroying X.
questions.teaches: हिध्माघ्न = हिध्मा-घ्न: -घ्न at the end of a compound means 'destroying'.

questions.q: Which enema does verse 46 order?
optionExplain: Right: अनुवासयेत्: he should give an anuvāsana.
Āsthāpana is ordered in 05.06.84, not here.
The daśamūla nirūha is 05.06.63.
Nāvana is for the head, 05.06.68.
questions.explain: अनु-√वस् (caus.) → अनुवासयेत्.

questions.q: Put the drugs of line 1 of verse 46 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Balā, sthirā (and the rest), kāśmarya, triphalā: their juices.

questions.q: Match each item of verse 46 to its meaning on the card.
questions.explain: Two juice drugs, the fruit triad, and two liquids of line 2.
questions.rule: त्रिफला = three myrobalans; काश्मर्य = गम्भारी; प्रसन्ना = सुरा का निथार; आरनाल = कांजी; बला = सम्भवतः बरियार.
questions.teaches: Verse 46: oil cooked with balā, sthirā, kāśmarya and triphalā juices, with prasannā and āranāla.

questions.q: Which liquids join the oil in line 2 of verse 46?
options: Milk and the water of washed rice
Hot water, pippalī and some salt
optionExplain: Those make the āsthāpana liquid of 05.06.83.
Right: सप्रसन्नारनालाम्लैः: with prasannā, āranāla and sour (liquids).
Those are the grinding liquids of 05.06.74.
Those come in 05.06.90.
questions.explain: स-प्रसन्ना-आरनाल-अम्ल: together with prasannā, āranāla, sour.

questions.q: A pharmacist is asked for the triphalā of verse 46. Which three does the card name?
optionExplain: These are the other juice drugs of verse 46.
These are in the list of 05.06.82.
Right: triphalā = harītakī, bibhītaka, āmalaka (standard).
These are drugs of 05.06.73-74.
questions.explain: त्रिफला = हरड़, बहेड़ा, आँवला.

questions.q: By the pattern of त्रिफला (the three fruits), what does the new word त्रिकटु mean (kaṭu = pungent)?
options: A drug that is not pungent
optionExplain: Thrice would be the adverb त्रिः, not this compound.
'Third' would be तृतीय.
Negation would need अ-; त्रि- means three.
Right: त्रि- at the head of a compound names a group of three.
questions.explain: त्रि-X = the group of three X.
questions.teaches: त्रिफला = त्रि + फल: a compound naming a group of three (the three myrobalans).

questions.q: With what is the thing given mixed, by line 1 of verse 47?
optionExplain: Right: उष्णाम्बुना … पिप्पल्या: with hot water and with pippalī.
Cold water and honey are not named in verse 47.
Those are the grinding liquids of 05.06.74.
Whey and sauvīraka are 05.06.83.
questions.explain: Two instrumentals with अक्त (mixed, smeared): उष्ण-अम्बुना, पिप्पल्या.
questions.rule: उष्णाम्बु = hot water; पिप्पली = long pepper.

questions.q: Put the measures of line 2 of verse 47 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Smoke, linctus, juice, milk, fomentation; then food that drives away Vāta.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 47 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four of the measures of line 2 and the word that qualifies the food.
questions.rule: धूम = smoke; लेह = linctus; क्षीर = milk; स्वेद = fomentation; वातनुत् = Vāta-dispelling.
questions.teaches: Verse 47 adds smoke, linctus, juice, milk, fomentation and Vāta-dispelling food (वातनुत्).

questions.q: Which split of दद्याल्लवणसंयुतं is right?
optionExplain: ल्लवण is not a word; one ल comes from the final त्.
Right: त् before ल becomes ल्: दद्याल् + लवण… → दद्याल्लवण….
दद्याः is 2nd person, and -आः before ल drops to -आ: दद्या लवण….
त् + अ would print दद्यादलवण…, with द.
questions.explain: दद्यात् (should give) + लवण-संयुतम् (joined with salt).

questions.q: A physician reads line 2 of verse 47. Which measures does it list?
optionExplain: That is for fainting, 05.06.52.
Right: क्षीर.
Right: धूम.
Fasting is not named; food (अन्न) is.
Right: स्वेद.
Right: लेह.
questions.explain: Line 2: smoke, linctus, juice, milk, fomentation, and Vāta-dispelling food.
questions.rule: धूम · लेह · रस · क्षीर · स्वेद · वातनुत् अन्न.

questions.q: By the pattern of वातनुत् (driving away Vāta), what does the new word कफनुत् mean?
optionExplain: Increasing would be -वर्धन, not -नुत्.
Born of would be -ज.
Right: -नुत् (from √नुद्, to push away) = 'driving away'.
Seated would be -स्थ.
questions.explain: X-नुत् = driving away X.
questions.teaches: वातनुत् = वात-नुत्: -नुत् at the end of a compound means 'driving away'.

questions.q: What would the faulty basti strike, by verse 48?
optionExplain: The navel is cut by Vāta and Pitta in 05.06.98, not struck here.
The head is not named in verse 48.
The anus is burnt and scraped in 05.06.106, a different fault.
Right: घट्टयेद्धृदयं बस्तिः: the basti would strike the heart (hṛdaya).
questions.explain: हृदयम् is the object of घट्टयेत् (would strike).

questions.q: Put these phrases of verse 48 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Three faults first (very sharp, with vāta, not properly pressed), then the result and the subject basti.
questions.rule: अतितीक्ष्णः · सवातो वा · न वा सम्यक्प्रपीडितः ‖ घट्टयेद्धृदयं · बस्तिस्तत्र.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 48 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The first three name the faults; घट्टयेत् and हृदय give the harm.
questions.rule: अतितीक्ष्ण = very sharp; सम्यक् = properly; प्रपीडित = pressed; घट्टयेत् = would strike; हृदय = heart.
questions.teaches: Verse 48: a very sharp basti, one with vāta, or one not properly pressed would strike the heart.

questions.q: Which split of घट्टयेद्धृदयं is right?
optionExplain: Right: त् + ह → द्ध: घट्टयेत् + हृदयम् → घट्टयेद्धृदयम्.
A visarga after ए before ह would not give द्ध.
द्धृदयम् is not a word; the द्ध comes from the join itself.
Neither part is a word; the verb is घट्टयेत्.
questions.explain: घट्टयेत् (would strike) + हृदयम् (the heart): final त् + ह gives द्ध.

questions.q: A physician checks a basti before giving it. Which faults does verse 48 say make it strike the heart?
options: It has vāta (wind or air) in it
It is too little in quantity
optionExplain: Right: सवातः.
Right: अतितीक्ष्णः.
Cold is not named in verse 48.
Right: न वा सम्यक्प्रपीडितः.
Quantity is not named in verse 48.
questions.explain: Three faults joined by वा: very sharp, with vāta, not properly pressed.

questions.q: By the pattern of न सम्यक्प्रपीडितः (not properly pressed), what does the new phrase न सम्यक्पक्वः mean?
optionExplain: This drops the न, which negates the phrase.
Right: न + सम्यक् + past participle: not done properly; पक्व = cooked.
Too much would be अति-; सम्यक् means properly.
Not at all would be अपक्वः; न सम्यक् says the cooking was not proper.
questions.explain: न सम्यक् X = not properly X.
questions.teaches: In verse 48 न सम्यक्प्रपीडितः means 'not properly pressed': न negates सम्यक् (properly).

questions.q: Which kind of anuvāsanas does line 2 of verse 49 name?
optionExplain: Pitta is not the doṣa named with -घ्न here.
Slimy bastis come in 05.06.104 and 05.06.110.
Right: वातघ्नैश्चानुवासनैः: with Vāta-destroying anuvāsanas.
Cool and sweet applications are for the anus in 05.06.113.
questions.explain: वात-घ्न = destroying Vāta; अनुवासन = oil enema.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 49 to its meaning.
questions.explain: बदरी and लवण are items of line 1; शृत, हित and अनुवासन come in line 2.
questions.rule: बदरी = jujube; लवण = salt; शृत = boiled; हित = beneficial; अनुवासन = oil enema.

questions.q: Put these words of line 2 of verse 49 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: शृतैर्बस्तिर्हितः · सिद्धो · वातघ्नैश्चानुवासनैः, split into its words.
questions.rule: शृतैः · बस्तिः · हितः · सिद्धो · वातघ्नैः (च) · अनुवासनैः.
questions.teaches: Line 2 of verse 49: a basti with the boiled items is beneficial, with Vāta-destroying anuvāsanas.

questions.q: Which split of वातघ्नैश्चानुवासनैः is right?
optionExplain: चा and नुवासनैः are not words.
ए before च stays ए; it would not print श्च.
म् before च becomes anusvāra, not श्.
Right: ः + च → श्च; च + अ → चा: वातघ्नैश्चानुवासनैः.
questions.explain: Visarga before च becomes श्; अ + अ → आ.

questions.q: What does verse 49 say of the basti made with the boiled items?
optionExplain: Right: शृतैर्बस्तिर्हितः: a basti with the boiled (ones) is beneficial.
That is the faulty basti of 05.06.92-93.
That is the dry, sharp basti of 05.06.96-97.
That is the kṣāra, hot basti of 05.06.105-106.
questions.explain: हितः = beneficial, said of the बस्तिः with the boiled items.

questions.q: By the pattern of वातघ्न (Vāta-destroying), what does the new word कफघ्नः mean?
optionExplain: -घ्न is active, 'destroying', not 'caused by'.
Right: -घ्न at the end of a compound = 'destroying' (from √हन्).
Increasing would be -वर्धन; -घ्न destroys.
Full of would be -मय; -घ्न destroys.
questions.explain: X-घ्न = destroying X.
questions.teaches: वातघ्न in verse 49 = वात + -घ्न: '-घ्न' at the end of a compound means 'destroying'.

questions.q: Which doṣas would the dry, sharp basti aggravate, by verse 50?
optionExplain: Kapha is not named in verse 50.
Kapha is not named; the pair is Vāta and Pitta.
Right: वातपित्ते प्रकोपयेत्: would aggravate Vāta and Pitta (dual).
Kapha is not named in verse 50.
questions.explain: वातपित्ते = Vāta and Pitta, a dvandva in the dual, object of प्रकोपयेत्.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 50 to its meaning.
questions.explain: मृदु and अल्प describe the patient; रूक्ष, तीक्ष्ण, अतिमात्रक the basti.
questions.rule: मृदु = soft; अल्प = little; रूक्ष = dry; तीक्ष्ण = sharp; अतिमात्रक = excessive in quantity.

questions.q: Put these phrases of verse 50 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The patient, the basti's qualities, then: having destroyed, quickly, aggravates Vāta and Pitta.
questions.rule: मृदुकोष्ठाल्पदोषस्य · रूक्षतीक्ष्णातिमात्रकः ‖ हत्वा (…मलान्) शीघ्रं · वातपित्ते प्रकोपयेत्.
questions.teaches: Verse 50: a dry, sharp, excessive basti given to one with a soft belly and little doṣa aggravates Vāta and Pitta.

questions.q: Who is the patient in verse 50?
options: One with a hard belly and much doṣa
One not oiled or sweated first
One with a soft belly and little doṣa
optionExplain: The verse says मृदु (soft) and अल्प (little).
The weak patient is in 05.06.86, with hiccup.
That is the patient of 05.06.77, a different fault.
Right: मृदुकोष्ठाल्पदोषस्य: of one with a soft koṣṭha and little doṣa.
questions.explain: मृदु-कोष्ठ + अल्प-दोष, a genitive: 'of one who has...'.

questions.q: Which qualities of the harmful basti does verse 50 name?
optionExplain: Slimy is the beneficial basti of 05.06.104.
Cool is not named in verse 50.
Right: तीक्ष्ण.
Right: रूक्ष.
Right: अतिमात्रक.
questions.explain: रूक्ष-तीक्ष्ण-अतिमात्रकः: dry, sharp, excessive in quantity.

questions.q: Like वातपित्ते प्रकोपयेत्, what does the new sentence बस्तिः कफं प्रकोपयेत् mean?
options: The basti was aggravated by Kapha
optionExplain: Right: बस्तिः is the subject (nom.), कफम् the object (acc.), प्रकोपयेत् = would aggravate.
कफम् is accusative, the object, not the subject.
प्र-√कुप् (causative) is to aggravate, not to calm.
No passive or instrumental is in the sentence.
questions.explain: Subject in the nominative, object in the accusative, prakopayet = would aggravate.
questions.rule: प्रकोपयेत् = would aggravate (its object in the accusative).
questions.teaches: In verse 50 प्रकोपयेत् (would aggravate) takes वातपित्ते as its object.

questions.q: Which body parts are cut again and again, by verse 51?
optionExplain: The heart is struck in 05.06.93; the flank is not named here.
Right: नाभिबस्तिगुदान् … कृन्तन्तः: cutting the navel, basti and anus.
Head and chest are not named in verse 51.
Mouth and nose are where the basti thrown upward comes out, 05.06.50-51.
questions.explain: नाभि-बस्ति-गुदान्: a dvandva in the accusative plural, object of कृन्तन्तः.

questions.q: Put these words of line 1 of verse 51 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The parts first, then 'they indeed', cutting, his, again and again.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 51 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Line 1 gives the parts and the cutting; line 2 ends with the scraping basti.
questions.rule: नाभि = navel; गुद = anus; कृन्तन्त् = cutting; मुहुर्मुहुः = again and again; निर्लेखन = scraping.
questions.teaches: Verse 51: navel, basti and anus are cut again and again, and the basti becomes scraping (निर्लेखन).

questions.q: What does मुहुर्मुहुः tell about the cutting in verse 51?
optionExplain: Once would be सकृत्; मुहुर्मुहुः is repeated.
Quickly is शीघ्रम्, a word of 05.06.97.
Right: मुहुः मुहुः = again and again, repeatedly.
No time of day is named in verse 51.
questions.explain: The doubled मुहुः stresses repetition.

questions.q: By the end of verse 51, what would the basti become?
optionExplain: Slimy is the remedy of 05.06.104.
Nourishing is the remedy for hiccup, 05.06.87.
Strained is said of the milk in 05.06.110.
Right: बस्तिर्निर्लेखनो भवेत्: the basti would be scraping.
questions.explain: निर्लेखनः (scraping) agrees with बस्तिः; भवेत् = would be.

questions.q: By the join in कृंतंतोऽस्य (कृन्तन्तः + अस्य), how do बालः + अस्ति join?
optionExplain: Right: -अः + अ → -ओ ऽ: बालः + अस्ति → बालोऽस्ति.
That is अ + अ → आ, which needs बाल without the visarga.
-अः does not turn to र्; only other vowels before ः do.
The gap comes before vowels other than अ; before अ it is -ओ ऽ.
questions.explain: -अः + अ → -ओ ऽ (the अ is replaced by the avagraha).
questions.teaches: कृंतंतोऽस्य = कृन्तन्तः + अस्य: -अः before अ becomes -ओ and the अ is marked ऽ.

questions.q: For whom is this basti, by line 2 of verse 52?
optionExplain: That is the patient of the next verse, 05.06.103.
Right: क्षीरभोजिनः: of (for) one who eats milk.
The over-purged one is fed in 05.06.118.
Hiccup is treated in 05.06.86-87.
questions.explain: क्षीर (milk) + भोजिन् (eating), genitive singular.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 52 to its meaning.
questions.explain: स्वादु and शीत describe the drugs; पयस्, इक्षु and तिल are the materials.
questions.rule: स्वादु = sweet; शीत = cool; पयस् = milk; इक्षु = sugarcane; तिल = sesame.

questions.q: Put these phrases of verse 52 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Drugs, milk boiled with sugarcane and the rest, (pastes), then the basti and for whom.
questions.rule: स्वादुशीतौषधैः · पयश्च · इक्ष्वादिभिः शृतं ‖ (…कल्काभ्यां) बस्तिः स्यात् · क्षीरभोजिनः.
questions.teaches: Verse 52: sweet-cool drugs, milk boiled with sugarcane and the rest, pastes; a basti for one who eats milk.

questions.q: Which split of पयश्चेक्ष्वादिभिः is right?
optionExplain: ए before च stays; it would not give श्च.
चेक्षु is not a word; the ए comes from च + इ.
Right: ः + च → श्च; अ + इ → ए: पयश्चेक्ष्वादिभिः.
Neither part is a word.
questions.explain: पयः (milk) + च (and) + इक्षु-आदिभिः (with sugarcane and the rest).

questions.q: By line 1 of verse 52, what is the milk boiled with?
optionExplain: That (conjectural) item is for goat's milk, 05.06.109.
Grape water is drunk with turpeth in 05.06.115.
Black gram is the soup of 05.06.119.
Right: पयश्चेक्ष्वादिभिः शृतं: milk boiled with ikṣu and the rest.
questions.explain: इक्षु-आदिभिः (instrumental) with शृतम् (boiled).

questions.q: By the pattern of क्षीरभोजिनः (of one who eats milk), what does the new word मांसभोजिनः mean?
optionExplain: Right: X-भोजिन् = one who eats X; -इनः = genitive singular.
भोजिन् is the eater, not the thing eaten.
Selling is not in the word; भोजिन् = eating.
Avoiding would need a negative; भोजिन् = eating.
questions.explain: X-भोजिन् = X-eater.
questions.teaches: क्षीरभोजिनः in verse 52 = क्षीर + भोजिन् (one who eats), genitive: 'of one who eats milk'.

questions.q: For whom is the basti of verse 53?
options: One who lives on plain milk
One who eats a distinctly sour taste
One who eats much sweet food
optionExplain: That is the patient of 05.06.101.
Right: व्यक्ताम्लरसभोजिनः: of one who eats a clear sour taste.
Sweet food is not named in verse 53.
That is the over-purged one of 05.06.118.
questions.explain: व्यक्त (clear) + अम्ल (sour) + रस (taste) + भोजिन् (eating).

questions.q: Put these drugs of verse 53 in the verse's order (the flagged licorice word is left out).
questions.explain: सम-सर्जरस-(यष्ट्याह्व) · जिङ्गिणी-कर्दम-अञ्जन.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 53 to its meaning.
questions.explain: सम qualifies the list; विनीय दुग्धे = having put (them) into milk.
questions.rule: सम = equal; कर्दम = mud; विनीय = having put in; दुग्ध = milk; व्यक्त = clear.
questions.teaches: Verse 53: equal parts of the listed drugs are put into milk (विनीय दुग्धे) for one who eats sour taste.

questions.q: What is the case and sense of दुग्धे in verse 53?
optionExplain: The genitive would be दुग्धस्य.
The nominative would be दुग्धम्.
Right: दुग्धे is locative singular: the drugs are put into milk.
The instrumental would be दुग्धेन.
questions.explain: दुग्ध (n.), locative singular -ए: 'in milk'.

questions.q: A patient eats distinctly sour food. Which basti does verse 53 give him?
options: The listed drugs put into milk
optionExplain: That basti is for one who eats milk, 05.06.100-101.
That is the remedy after fainting, 05.06.109-110.
Those go with the remedy of 05.06.95.
Right: विनीय दुग्धे: the listed drugs, put into milk, make his basti.
questions.explain: Verse 53 pairs the sour-eater with the drugs in milk.

questions.q: Like विनीय (vi + √nī, having put in), which absolutive of आ + √नी means having brought?
optionExplain: Right: With a prefix the absolutive ends in -य: आ + नी + य → आनीय.
-त्वा is used without a prefix; with आ it becomes -य.
नीत्वा has no prefix: 'having led', not 'having brought'.
आनयति is a present verb, 'brings', not an absolutive.
questions.explain: Prefix + root → absolutive in -य; bare root → -त्वा.
questions.teaches: विनीय in verse 53 is the absolutive of vi + √nī: with a prefix the absolutive takes -य.

questions.q: Which kind of basti does line 1 of verse 54 call beneficial?
optionExplain: Dry is the harmful basti of 05.06.96.
Right: पिच्छिलश्च हितो बस्तिः: a slimy basti is beneficial.
Salty is in line 2's harmful list.
Sharp is in line 2's harmful list.
questions.explain: पिच्छिलः (slimy) + हितः (beneficial) qualify बस्तिः.

questions.q: Put these qualities of the basti in line 2 of verse 54 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: क्षार-अम्ल-तीक्ष्ण-उष्ण-लवणः: kṣāra, sour, sharp, hot, salty.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 54 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The first three belong to the remedy of line 1; उष्ण and पैत्तिक to line 2.
questions.rule: पिच्छिल = slimy; स्नेह = oil or fat; मधुर = sweet; उष्ण = hot; पैत्तिक = one of Pitta.
questions.teaches: Verse 54: line 1 names the beneficial slimy basti and sweet-boiled sneha; line 2 a kṣāra, hot, salty basti.

questions.q: How do the two lines of verse 54 differ?
options: Line 1 starts a harm; line 2 is a remedy
Line 1 is a remedy; line 2 starts a harm
optionExplain: This reverses them: हितः is in line 1.
Line 2's kṣāra, hot basti causes the harm of 05.06.106.
Right: Line 1: hitaḥ (beneficial); line 2: the basti whose harm comes in 05.06.106.
Line 1 calls the slimy basti हितः, beneficial.
questions.explain: हितः marks line 1 as remedy; line 2 opens the passage 05.06.105-108.

questions.q: A basti is being judged. Which of its qualities put it in line 2's harmful list?
optionExplain: Right: क्षार.
Right: लवण.
Sweet goes with the beneficial sneha of line 1.
Slimy is the beneficial basti of line 1.
Right: उष्ण.
Right: अम्ल.
questions.explain: Line 2: kṣāra, sour, sharp, hot, salty.

questions.q: By the join तीक्ष्ण + उष्ण → तीक्ष्णोष्ण, how do मधुर + उदक join?
optionExplain: अ + उ gives ओ, not ऊ.
औ comes from अ + ओ or अ + औ, not अ + उ.
व् would come from उ + another vowel, not अ + उ.
Right: अ + उ → ओ: मधुर + उदक → मधुरोदक.
questions.explain: अ/आ + उ/ऊ → ओ (guṇa).
questions.teaches: तीक्ष्णोष्ण in verse 54 = तीक्ष्ण + उष्ण: अ + उ joins to ओ.

questions.q: What does the basti make for him, by verse 55?
optionExplain: Right: करोत्यस्य परिस्रवं: it makes a flow for him.
Hiccup comes from the very sharp basti of 05.06.86-87.
Belly-pain follows over-application, 05.06.71.
Distension is not named in verse 55.
questions.explain: परिस्रवम् is the object of करोति.

questions.q: Put these words of line 1 of verse 55 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The anus, then three participles (burning, scraping, damaging), then the main verb.
questions.rule: गुदं · दहन् · लिखन् · क्षिण्वन् · करोत्यस्य परिस्रवं.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 55 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Line 1: what the basti does to the anus; line 2 ends with भूरिशः.
questions.rule: गुद = anus; दहन् = burning; लिखन् = scraping; परिस्रव = flow; भूरिशः = abundantly.
questions.teaches: Verse 55: burning and scraping the anus, the basti makes a flow (परिस्रव) of blood and Pitta.

questions.q: Which split of करोत्यस्य is right?
optionExplain: उ + अ would give व्: करोत्वस्य.
Right: इ → य् before another vowel: करोति + अस्य → करोत्यस्य.
ए + अ would give करोतेऽस्य.
Neither part is a word.
questions.explain: करोति (makes) + अस्य (for him).

questions.q: After the kṣāra, hot basti burns the anus, what else does verse 55 say happens?
options: Faeces and Kapha are held back
optionExplain: Holding back is not in verse 55; it speaks of flow.
Stiffness is from the misled basti, 05.06.80.
Right: स्त्रवत्यस्रं … पित्तं च भूरिशः: blood flows, and Pitta, abundantly.
The head is not named in verse 55.
questions.explain: Line 2 names the flowing blood (अस्र) and Pitta (पित्त).

questions.q: Like दहन् (burning, from √दह्), what does the new participle पठन् (from √पठ्, to read) mean?
optionExplain: Having read would be पठित्वा (absolutive).
A future would be पठिष्यति.
A passive past would be पठितः.
Right: -अन् (m. nom. sg.) is the present participle: 'while reading'.
questions.explain: Root + -अत् / -अन् = present participle, action going on.
questions.teaches: दहन्, लिखन् in verse 55 are present participles (-अन्): 'burning', 'scraping', ongoing action.

questions.q: Into what does he go repeatedly, by verse 56?
optionExplain: Right: मोहं गच्छति चासकृत्: he goes into moha repeatedly.
Hiccup is the harm of 05.06.86-87.
Sleep is not named in verse 56.
Thirst is not named in verse 56.
questions.explain: मोहम् is the object of गच्छति (goes into).

questions.q: Match each word of verse 56 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Line 1 describes the attacks; आज belongs to the milk of line 2.
questions.rule: बहुशः = many times; वेग = urge; मोह = bewilderment; असकृत् = repeatedly; आज = of the goat.

questions.q: Put these words of line 1 of verse 56 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Many times, with excessive urge, into moha, goes, and repeatedly.
questions.teaches: Line 1 of verse 56: many times, with excessive urge, he goes into moha, repeatedly.

questions.q: Which split of क्षुण्णैराजं is right?
optionExplain: -आः before a vowel drops the visarga: क्षुण्णा आजम्.
Right: -ऐः before a vowel → -ऐर्: क्षुण्णैः + आजम् → क्षुण्णैराजम्.
र् + अ would print रज, not the printed रा.
ए would not print ऐ; राजम् is not the word here.
questions.explain: क्षुण्णैः (crushed, inst. pl.) + आजम् (of the goat).

questions.q: A patient keeps fainting after the harsh basti. What does line 2 of verse 56 begin to prepare for him?
optionExplain: That is for burning, 05.06.115.
That is for the purified one, 05.06.117.
Right: आजं पयः शृतं: goat's milk, boiled.
Those are drinks for the over-purged, 05.06.119.
questions.explain: आजम् (of the goat) qualifies पयः (milk); शृतम् = boiled.

questions.q: By असकृत् (a- + sakṛt, once: so repeatedly), what does the new word अनेक (an- + eka, one) mean?
optionExplain: That ignores the negative prefix अन्-.
'First' would be प्रथम.
'Each' would be प्रत्येक.
Right: The negative prefix turns 'one' into 'not one', that is, many.
questions.explain: अ- / अन्- negates: अ-सकृत् = not once; अन्-एक = not one.
questions.teaches: असकृत् in verse 56 = अ- (not) + सकृत् (once): 'repeatedly'.

questions.q: With what is the strained milk joined before it is given, by verse 57?
optionExplain: Right: घृतान्वितं: joined with ghee.
Honey is not named in verse 57.
Sugar goes with the gruel of 05.06.117.
Oil is not named in verse 57.
questions.explain: घृत (ghee) + अन्वित (joined with).

questions.q: Put these words of line 1 of verse 57 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Strained, joined with ghee, a basti, should give, and other slimy (ones).

questions.q: Match each word of verse 57 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Line 1 gives the handling; line 2 says where the same kalpa holds.
questions.rule: पूत = strained; अन्वित = joined with; पल्लव = sprout; कल्प = preparation; यव = barley.
questions.teaches: Verse 57: the milk is strained (पूत) and joined with ghee; the same कल्प holds for vaṭa sprouts, yava, tila.

questions.q: What does अन्यांश्च पिच्छिलान् add to the instruction of verse 57?
options: Slimy ones are to be avoided here
The milk itself must be made slimy
Only a single basti may be given
optionExplain: No negative is in the line; दद्यात् (should give) governs them.
Right: दद्यादन्यांश्च पिच्छिलान्: he should give other slimy (ones) as well.
पिच्छिलान् is masculine accusative plural: other items, not the milk.
अन्यान् (other) adds more; it does not limit.
questions.explain: अन्यान् (other, m. acc. pl.) + च + पिच्छिलान् (slimy ones), objects of दद्यात्.

questions.q: In which items does line 2 of verse 57 say the same preparation holds?
options: Sprouts of vaṭa and the rest
optionExplain: Right: वटादिपल्लवेषु.
Śālmalī is the conjectural item of 05.06.109.
Right: यवतिलेषु.
Sugarcane is boiled with milk in 05.06.100.
Right: यवतिलेषु.
questions.explain: Two locatives: वट-आदि-पल्लवेषु and यव-तिलेषु.

questions.q: Like वटादि (vaṭa and the rest), what does the new phrase निम्बादिपत्राणि mean (patra = leaf)?
options: The leaves that come before nimba
The first leaves of the nimba
The leaves of nimba and the rest
optionExplain: आदि means 'and the rest', not 'before'.
आदि here does not mean the first leaves.
Right: X-आदि = X and the rest; then पत्राणि, the leaves.
Nothing in the word says 'without'.
questions.explain: X-आदि-Y = Y of X and the rest.
questions.teaches: वटादिपल्लवेषु in verse 57 = वट + आदि + पल्लव: 'in the sprouts of vaṭa and the rest'.

questions.q: Where are the cool and sweet applications made, by line 2 of verse 58?
optionExplain: The head is not named in verse 58.
The navel is named in 05.06.98, not here.
The chest is not named in verse 58.
Right: गुदे च: and in (at) the anus.
questions.explain: गुदे is locative: in, at the anus.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 58 to its meaning.
questions.explain: शस्यते closes line 1; line 2 gives the place (गुद) and the cool, sweet coatings.
questions.rule: शस्यते = is recommended; गुद = anus; शीत = cool; मधुर = sweet; प्रलेपन = coating.

questions.q: Put these phrases of verse 58 in the verse's order (the flagged word is left out).
questions.explain: Two plants, karbudāra, is recommended; then at the anus, (cool sweet …), coatings.
questions.rule: सुवर्चलोपोदकयोः · कर्बुदारे च · शस्यते ‖ गुदे च · (…) · प्रलेपनान्.
questions.teaches: Verse 58: the kalpa is recommended in suvarcalā, upodakā and karbudāra; at the anus, cool sweet coatings.

questions.q: Which split of सुवर्चलोपोदकयोः is right?
optionExplain: Right: आ + उ → ओ: सुवर्चला + उपोदकयोः → सुवर्चलोपोदकयोः.
Neither part is a word.
औ + उ would give आवु: सुवर्चलावुपोदकयोः.
-अः before उ leaves a gap: सुवर्चल उपोदकयोः.
questions.explain: The two plants in a dvandva, locative dual: आ + उ joins to ओ.

questions.q: Besides the items of 05.06.111, which plants does verse 58 add for the same kalpa?
optionExplain: These go into the milk basti of 05.06.100-101.
Right: सुवर्चलोपोदकयोः कर्बुदारे च शस्यते.
These are drunk in 05.06.121.
These are in the remedy of 05.06.93-94.
questions.explain: Three locatives with शस्यते (is recommended).

questions.q: Like शस्यते (is recommended), what does the new sentence घृतं शस्यते mean?
optionExplain: An active verb would be शंसति; -यते is passive.
In the passive the subject receives the action.
Right: -यते is the present passive: the subject (घृतम्) is what is recommended.
शस्यते is present, not past.
questions.explain: Root + -य + -ते = present passive.
questions.teaches: शस्यते in verse 58 is the present passive of √शंस्: 'is recommended'.

questions.q: Which procedure is commended here, by line 1 of verse 59?
optionExplain: Hiccup and pain are not named in verse 59.
Kapha and Vāta are not named in verse 59.
Vomiting is not named in verse 59.
Right: रक्तपित्तातिसारघ्नी क्रिया … प्रशस्यते.
questions.explain: रक्तपित्त + अतिसार + -घ्नी (destroying), qualifying क्रिया.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 59 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Two disorders and the procedure in line 1; the drug and its liquid in line 2.
questions.rule: रक्तपित्त = bleeding disorder; अतिसार = diarrhoea; क्रिया = procedure; त्रिवृत् = turpeth; मृद्वीका = grape.

questions.q: Put these words of line 2 of verse 59 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: In burning and the rest, a turpeth paste, with grape water, he should drink.
questions.teaches: Line 2 of verse 59: in dāha and the rest, he should drink a trivṛt paste with grape water.

questions.q: The feminine word रक्तपित्तातिसारघ्नी agrees with which word of verse 59?
optionExplain: Right: क्रिया is feminine nominative singular, like -घ्नी.
रक्तपित्त is inside the compound itself.
अतिसार is inside the compound itself.
त्रिवृत्कल्कम् is accusative, in line 2.
questions.explain: -घ्नी is the feminine of -घ्न, to agree with क्रिया.

questions.q: A patient has burning (dāha) after the harsh basti. What does verse 59 have him drink?
optionExplain: That is a basti, 05.06.109-110, not this drink.
Right: त्रिवृत्कल्कं मृद्वीकावारिणा पिबेत्.
Those are for the over-purged, 05.06.119.
That goes with salt in 05.06.90.
questions.explain: दाहादिषु … पिबेत्: for burning and the rest, he should drink.

questions.q: Like दाहादिषु (in burning and the rest), what does the new word ज्वरादिषु mean?
optionExplain: आदि is 'and the rest', not 'before'.
The locative -एषु / -इषु means 'in', not 'from'.
Right: X-आदिषु = locative plural: in X and the rest.
'By means of' would be instrumental.
questions.explain: X-आदि + locative plural = in X and the rest.
questions.teaches: दाहादिषु in verse 59 = दाह + आदि, locative plural: 'in burning and the rest'.

questions.q: What does 'that' (the turpeth drink) destroy, by line 1 of verse 60?
optionExplain: Kapha and blood are not in this list.
Kapha is not named; the list has Pitta, faeces, Vāta.
Blood is not in line 1 of verse 60.
Right: पित्तशकृद्वातान्हत्वा: having destroyed Pitta, faeces and Vāta.
questions.explain: A dvandva in the accusative plural, object of हत्वा.

questions.q: Put these words of line 1 of verse 60 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: That indeed, Pitta-faeces-Vāta, having destroyed, burning and the rest, would conquer.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 60 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Line 1: what the drink destroys and conquers; line 2: the purified one and his gruel.
questions.rule: शकृत् = faeces; हत्वा = having destroyed; जयेत् = would conquer; विशुद्ध = purified; शर्करा = sugar.
questions.teaches: Verse 60: the turpeth drink destroys Pitta, faeces and Vāta; purified, he drinks cool gruel with sugar.

questions.q: Which split of पिबेच्छीतां is right?
optionExplain: Right: त् + श → च्छ: पिबेत् + शीताम् → पिबेच्छीताम्.
A visarga before श would give पिबेः शीताम् or पिबेश्शीताम्.
च्छीताम् is not a word; the च्छ comes from the join.
पिबेच्छी is not a word.
questions.explain: पिबेत् (should drink) + शीताम् (cool, f. acc.): त् + श → च्छ.

questions.q: The patient is now purified. What gruel does verse 60 give him?
optionExplain: The verse says शीता (cool) and शर्करा (sugar).
Right: पिबेच्छीतां यवागूं शर्करायुतां.
Ghee is not named in verse 60.
Warm and honey are not named in verse 60.
questions.explain: शीताम्, यवागूम्, शर्करायुताम् all feminine accusative.

questions.q: A dvandva takes the gender of its last member (पित्तशकृद्वातान् ends in m. वात). Which nominative fits कफ-वात-पित्त (पित्त is neuter)?
optionExplain: -आः is masculine; the last member पित्त is neuter.
-ए is dual; three members need the plural.
Right: Last member पित्त is neuter; three members, so neuter plural -आनि.
-अः is masculine singular.
questions.explain: Itaretara dvandva: number = count of members, gender = last member.
questions.teaches: पित्तशकृद्वातान् in verse 60 is a dvandva in the masculine, from its last member vāta.

questions.q: For whom is the food of verse 61?
options: One with a soft belly, little doṣa
One who lives on plain milk
optionExplain: That is the patient of 05.06.96.
That is the patient of 05.06.108.
That is the patient of 05.06.101.
Right: अतिविरिक्तस्य क्षीणविट्कस्य: of one over-purged, whose stool is depleted.
questions.explain: Two genitives of the same person: over-purged, stool depleted.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 61 to its meaning.
questions.explain: माष, यूष and कुल्माष make the food; दधि and सुरा are the drinks.
questions.rule: माष = black gram; यूष = soup; कुल्माष = partly cooked grain (probable); दधि = curd; सुरा = intoxicating drink.

questions.q: Put these words of line 2 of verse 61 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: With black-gram soup, kulmāṣa; as drink, curd or else surā.
questions.teaches: Line 2 of verse 61: kulmāṣa with black-gram soup; as drink, curd or else surā.

questions.q: Which split of दध्यथवा is right?
optionExplain: Right: इ → य् before another vowel: दधि + अथवा → दध्यथवा.
Neither part is a word.
ए + अ would give दधेऽथवा.
-इः before a vowel → -इर्: दधिरथवा.
questions.explain: दधि (curd) + अथवा (or else).

questions.q: An over-purged patient's stool is depleted. What food and drink does verse 61 give?
options: Cool gruel with sugar; grape water
Kulmāṣa in black-gram soup; curd or surā
Goat's milk with ghee; hot water
optionExplain: Gruel is for the purified one, 05.06.117; grape water goes with turpeth.
Right: माषयूषेण कुल्माषान्, पानं दध्यथवा सुरां.
Goat's milk is a basti, 05.06.109-110.
Milk with sugarcane is a basti, 05.06.100.
questions.explain: Food: kulmāṣa with black-gram soup; drink: curd or else surā.
questions.rule: भोजन: कुल्माष + माषयूष · पान: दधि / सुरा.

questions.q: Like दध्यथवा सुराम् (curd or else surā), what does the new phrase क्षीरम् अथवा जलम् mean?
optionExplain: Together would be च; अथवा gives a choice.
No negative is in the phrase.
Right: अथवा = 'or else': one of the two.
Mixing is not said; अथवा means or.
questions.explain: X अथवा Y = X or else Y.
questions.teaches: In verse 61 दध्यथवा सुराम् means 'curd or else surā': अथवा offers a choice.

questions.q: How is what the patient passes described in line 1 of verse 62?
optionExplain: Those words describe the flow of 05.06.107.
Dry and hard are not in verse 62.
Slimy and cool describe remedies, not this discharge.
Right: आमं … कुणपं: raw and putrid.
questions.explain: आम = raw, undigested; कुणप = putrid (lit. corpse).

questions.q: Match each word of verse 62 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four words describe the patient; वचा is one of the drugs.
questions.rule: आम = raw; कुणप = putrid; रुग्वान् = having pain; अरुचि = distaste for food; वचा = sweet flag.

questions.q: Put these drugs of line 2 of verse 62 in the verse's order (the unclear word is left out).
questions.explain: स-घन-अतिविषा-कुष्ठ-(नदारु)-वचाः.
questions.teaches: Line 2 of verse 62 lists ghana, ativiṣā, kuṣṭha, (an unclear word) and vacā to drink.

questions.q: What is कुष्ठ in verse 62?
optionExplain: Right: Here kuṣṭha is a drug in a list of drugs: costus (Saussurea costus).
In a list of drugs to drink, kuṣṭha is the drug, not the disease.
Nut-grass is the probable sense of ghana.
Sweet flag is vacā.
questions.explain: Context decides: kuṣṭha among ghana, ativiṣā, vacā is the drug costus.

questions.q: A patient in pain, with aruci, passes raw, putrid stool. What does verse 62 have him do?
options: Take a slimy basti with ghee
optionExplain: That is for the fainting patient, 05.06.110.
Right: पिबेत्: he should drink, with ghana, ativiṣā and the rest.
That is food for the over-purged, 05.06.119.
Coatings at the anus are in 05.06.113.
questions.explain: The verb of verse 62 is पिबेत्, should drink.

questions.q: Like सारुचिः (sa + aruci, with distaste for food), what does the new word सज्वरः mean?
optionExplain: Without would be निर्- or अ-: निर्ज्वर.
Causing would be -कर: ज्वरकर.
Right: स- at the start of a bahuvrīhi = 'with': स + ज्वर = having fever.
No time word is in सज्वर.
questions.explain: स-X = having X, with X.
questions.teaches: सारुचिः in verse 62 = स + अरुचिः: 'with aruci'; स- means 'with'.

questions.q: What is best in that case, by line 2 of verse 63?
options: A basti of its own group
optionExplain: That is the remedy of 05.06.110.
That goes with the remedy of 05.06.95.
Grape water goes with turpeth, 05.06.115.
Right: स्ववर्गीयो बस्तिः श्रेष्ठं: a basti of its own group is best.
questions.explain: स्व (own) + वर्गीय (of the group), with बस्तिः and श्रेष्ठम्.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 63 to its meaning.
questions.explain: स्व-वर्गीय, श्रेष्ठ and भिषग्-जित are in line 2; यः opens the relative clause of line 1.
questions.rule: स्व = own; वर्ग = group; श्रेष्ठ = best; भिषज् = physician; यः = who.

questions.q: Put these words of line 2 of verse 63 in the verse's order (the unclear first word is left out).
questions.explain: In that case, of its own group, a basti, best, conquered by the physician.
questions.teaches: Line 2 of verse 63: in that case a basti of its own group (स्ववर्गीय) is best.

questions.q: Which split of योऽतिसार्यते is right?
optionExplain: Right: -अः + अ → -ओ ऽ: यः + अतिसार्यते → योऽतिसार्यते.
तिसार्यते is not a word; the ऽ marks a lost अ.
अ + अ would give आ: यातिसार्यते.
ये + अ would print येऽतिसार्यते.
questions.explain: यः (who) + अतिसार्यते (is made to flow out).

questions.q: Which clear words of line 1 of verse 63 name what is made to flow out?
optionExplain: Right: वातम्.
Right: पित्तम्.
Right: कफं वा.
Sweat is not named in verse 63.
Urine is not named in verse 63.
questions.explain: Line 1 lists faeces, Vāta, blood, Pitta or Kapha; faeces and blood are conjectural readings.

questions.q: Like स्ववर्गीय (belonging to its own group), what does the new word स्वदेशीय mean?
optionExplain: स्व means own, not foreign.
Right: स्व = own; देश = country; -ईय = belonging to.
No negative is in the word.
-ईय means belonging to, not ruler.
questions.explain: स्व-X-ईय = belonging to one's own X.
questions.teaches: स्ववर्गीयः in verse 63 = स्व + वर्ग + -ईय: 'belonging to its own group'.

questions.q: By line 2 of verse 64, with what should one also know the varieties?
optionExplain: No season is named in verse 64.
Remedies are not named in this verse; it only counts and adds the complications.
Right: विद्यात्सोपद्रवानपि: one should know them also with their complications (upadrava).
Tastes come in the later verses (05.06.128 on), not here.
questions.explain: स-उपद्रवान् = with complications; अपि = also.
questions.section: छत्तीस भेद, उपद्रव, आम में पाचन

questions.q: Match each word of verse 64 to its meaning.
questions.explain: षण्णाम्, द्विसंसर्ग and भेद are in line 1; केवल and उपद्रव in line 2.
questions.rule: षण्णाम् = of six; द्विसंसर्ग = combination of two; भेद = variety; केवल = single; उपद्रव = complication.
questions.section: छत्तीस भेद, उपद्रव, आम में पाचन

questions.q: Put these words of line 1 of verse 64 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Of these six, from the combination of two, (thirty) varieties there are, indeed.
questions.teaches: Line 1 of verse 64: of these six, from the combination of two (द्विसंसर्गात्), varieties (भेदाः) arise.
questions.section: छत्तीस भेद, उपद्रव, आम में पाचन

questions.q: Which split of सोपद्रवानपि is right?
optionExplain: -अः before a vowel other than अ loses the visarga and stays apart: स उपद्रवान्, not सो-.
पद्रवान् is not a word; the ओ comes from अ + उ.
नपि is not a word; the न belongs to उपद्रवान्.
Right: अ + उ → ओ: स + उपद्रवान् → सोपद्रवान्; न् + अ → न: सोपद्रवानपि.
questions.explain: स (with) + उपद्रवान् (complications) + अपि (also).
questions.section: छत्तीस भेद, उपद्रव, आम में पाचन

questions.q: A student counts only the varieties made by combining two of the six. What does line 2 of verse 64 add?
optionExplain: Right: केवलैः सह: together with the single ones the count is thirty-six.
Combining three, four, five and six comes later, in 05.06.150.
Tastes are not named in verse 64.
No time is named in verse 64.
questions.explain: केवलैः सह = together with the single (ones).
questions.section: छत्तीस भेद, उपद्रव, आम में पाचन

questions.q: Like सोपद्रव (with complications), what does the new word सज्वरः mean (ज्वर = fever)?
optionExplain: Free of fever would be निर्ज्वर or विज्वर; स- means with.
Right: स- at the head of a compound = 'with': स + ज्वर = with fever.
स- does not mean cause.
After would be ज्वरात् परम्; स- means with.
questions.explain: स-X = having X, with X.
questions.teaches: सोपद्रवान् in verse 64 = स + उपद्रवान्: 'with (their) complications'.
questions.section: छत्तीस भेद, उपद्रव, आम में पाचन

questions.q: What does verse 65 call śūla, ādhmāna, jvara and the rest?
options: The signs of a good basti
optionExplain: The verse names them as complications, not causes.
Pain and fever are not signs of a well-given basti here.
Right: चैषां विद्यादुपद्रवान्: one should know (them) as the complications (upadrava) of these.
Tastes are not named in verse 65.
questions.explain: उपद्रवान् is the object of विद्यात्; the listed items are the complications.
questions.section: छत्तीस भेद, उपद्रव, आम में पाचन

questions.q: Put these complications of line 1 of verse 65 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The compound of line 1 runs: pain, tenesmus, distension, cutting pain, loss of appetite, fevers.
questions.rule: शूल · प्रवाहिका · आध्मान · परिकर्ति · अरुचि · ज्वर.
questions.section: छत्तीस भेद, उपद्रव, आम में पाचन

questions.q: Match each complication in verse 65 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The first three are from line 1, तृष् and मूर्च्छा from line 2.
questions.rule: शूल = pain; आध्मान = distension; अरुचि = loss of appetite; तृष् = thirst; मूर्च्छा = fainting.
questions.teaches: Verse 65 names the complications: pain, tenesmus, distension, cutting pain, loss of appetite, fever, thirst, bewilderment, burning, fainting.
questions.section: छत्तीस भेद, उपद्रव, आम में पाचन

questions.q: Which split of परिकर्त्यरुचि is right?
optionExplain: -अः + अ would give -ओऽ: परिकर्तोऽरुचि.
ए + अ would give एऽ: परिकर्तेऽरुचि.
उ + अ would give व: परिकर्त्वरुचि.
Right: इ + अ → य: परिकर्ति + अरुचि → परिकर्त्यरुचि.
questions.explain: परिकर्ति (cutting pain) + अरुचि (loss of appetite): इ before a different vowel becomes य्.
questions.section: छत्तीस भेद, उपद्रव, आम में पाचन

questions.q: Which of these signs does verse 65 name as complications of these varieties?
optionExplain: Itching is not named in verse 65.
Right: तृष् (printed तृण्- before मोह).
Cough is not named in verse 65.
Right: दाह.
Right: मूर्च्छा.
questions.explain: Line 2 names thirst, bewilderment, burning and fainting, then 'and so on'.
questions.section: छत्तीस भेद, उपद्रव, आम में पाचन

questions.q: By the pattern of मूर्च्छादीन् … विद्यात्, what does the new phrase ज्वरादीन् विद्यात् mean?
options: One should know fever and so on
One should know the first fever
optionExplain: Right: -आदि at the end of a compound = 'and so on': ज्वर + आदीन् = fever and the rest.
-आदि here does not mean 'first'; it keeps the list open (and so on).
-आदि adds the rest; it does not restrict.
No negative is in the phrase.
questions.explain: X-आदीन् = X and so on (accusative plural).
questions.teaches: मूर्च्छादीन् in verse 65 = मूर्च्छा + आदीन्: 'fainting and so on', which keeps the list open.
questions.section: छत्तीस भेद, उपद्रव, आम में पाचन

questions.q: What does verse 66 say of basti in āma?
optionExplain: Best (श्रेष्ठ) is said of the basti of its own group in 05.06.123, not here.
Right: बस्तिरामे हि प्रतिषिध्यते: in āma basti is indeed forbidden.
No oily basti is named in verse 66.
No repeat is named in verse 66.
questions.explain: प्रतिषिध्यते = is forbidden; the subject is बस्तिः, the place आमे.
questions.section: छत्तीस भेद, उपद्रव, आम में पाचन

questions.q: Match each word of verse 66 to its meaning.
questions.explain: शस्यते and प्रतिषिध्यते are the two verbs: one recommends, one forbids.
questions.rule: आम = undigested matter; पाचन = digestive; शस्यते = is recommended; प्रतिषिध्यते = is forbidden; युत = joined with.
questions.section: छत्तीस भेद, उपद्रव, आम में पाचन

questions.q: Put these words of line 2 of verse 66 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: A digestive is recommended; basti, in āma, indeed, is forbidden.
questions.rule: पाचनं · शस्यते · बस्तिः · आमे · हि · प्रतिषिध्यते.
questions.teaches: Line 2 of verse 66: a digestive (पाचन) is recommended, for in āma basti is forbidden.
questions.section: छत्तीस भेद, उपद्रव, आम में पाचन

questions.q: Which split of कट्वम्ल is right?
optionExplain: इ + अ would give य: कट्यम्ल.
-उः before a vowel would give -उर्: कटुरम्ल.
Right: उ + अ → व: कटु + अम्ल → कट्वम्ल.
ओ + अ would give ओऽ: कटोऽम्ल.
questions.explain: कटु (pungent) + अम्ल (sour): उ before a different vowel becomes व्.
questions.section: छत्तीस भेद, उपद्रव, आम में पाचन

questions.q: A patient still has āma. By verse 66, what should the physician give?
options: A drink with no salt in it
optionExplain: In āma basti is forbidden.
Any basti is forbidden in āma, whatever its drugs.
The drink is joined with pungent, sour and salty (ones).
Right: पाचनं शस्यते … बस्तिरामे हि प्रतिषिध्यते.
questions.explain: Recommended: पाचन; forbidden: बस्ति.
questions.section: छत्तीस भेद, उपद्रव, आम में पाचन

questions.q: Like बस्तिरामे प्रतिषिध्यते, what does the new sentence आमे स्नेहः प्रतिषिध्यते mean (स्नेह = oil)?
optionExplain: Right: आमे = in āma (locative); स्नेहः = subject; प्रतिषिध्यते = is forbidden.
Recommended would be शस्यते.
प्रतिषिध्यते is passive: the subject is what is forbidden.
आमे is the locative (in āma); स्नेहः is the nominative.
questions.explain: Locative = the condition; nominative + passive verb = what is forbidden.
questions.rule: आमे X प्रतिषिध्यते = in āma X is forbidden.
questions.teaches: In verse 66 बस्तिः आमे प्रतिषिध्यते: basti (nominative) is forbidden in āma (locative).
questions.section: छत्तीस भेद, उपद्रव, आम में पाचन

questions.q: Which basti does verse 67 give in wind (samīraṇa)?
options: A basti of the binding group
optionExplain: That one is for stool (शकृति), in line 1.
Right: स्वाद्वम्लो व्यक्तलवणः स्नेहबस्तिः समीरणे.
The digestive is for āma, in 05.06.129.
Basti is forbidden in āma (05.06.129), not in wind.
questions.explain: स्नेह-बस्ति = oil enema; समीरणे = in wind.
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: Match each word of verse 67 to its meaning.
questions.explain: ग्राहिन् and शकृत् are in line 1; स्वादु, व्यक्त and समीरण in line 2.
questions.rule: ग्राहिन् = binding; शकृत् = stool; स्वादु = sweet; व्यक्त = evident; समीरण = wind.
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: Put these words of line 2 of verse 67 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Sweet and sour, with salt evident, an oil enema, in wind.
questions.teaches: Line 2 of verse 67: in wind (समीरणे), an oil enema, sweet and sour, with the salt evident.
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: Which split of स्वाद्वम्लो is right?
optionExplain: इ + अ would give य: स्वाद्यम्लः.
-अः + अ would give -ओऽ: स्वादोऽम्लः.
Right: उ + अ → व: स्वाद्वम्लः; -अः + घोष (व्य-) → -ओ: स्वाद्वम्लो.
अ + अ would give आ: स्वाद्वाम्लः.
questions.explain: स्वादु (sweet) + अम्लः (sour).
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: By line 1 of verse 67, which group should the basti in stool (śakṛti) belong to?
optionExplain: That oil enema is for wind, in line 2.
That is the drink in āma, 05.06.128.
Neither purging nor sharp is named in verse 67.
Right: वातघ्नग्राहिवर्गीयो बस्तिः शकृति शस्यते.
questions.explain: वात-घ्न (Vāta-destroying) + ग्राहि (binding) + वर्गीय (of the group).
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: Like व्यक्तलवणः (with the salt evident), what does the new word व्यक्ताम्लः describe?
optionExplain: Right: व्यक्त + अम्ल as a bahuvrīhi: 'having evident sourness'.
No negative is in the word.
