व्यक्त means evident, the opposite of hidden.
Slightly would be ईषत्-; व्यक्त means clearly present.
questions.explain: व्यक्त-X (bahuvrīhi) = having X evident.
questions.teaches: व्यक्तलवणः in verse 67 is a bahuvrīhi: (a basti) whose salt is evident.
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: By line 2 of verse 68 (सार्यमाणे कफे), what basti is given in the Kapha case?
optionExplain: That is the oil enema in wind, 05.06.131.
Right: सार्यमाणे कफे बस्तिः कषायः कटुतिक्तकः.
That is line 1 of verse 68, not the Kapha line.
That is the drink in āma, 05.06.128.
questions.explain: कषायः (astringent) + कटुतिक्तकः (pungent and bitter).
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: Match each word of verse 68 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The four tastes of the two lists, and बस्ति of line 2.
questions.rule: कषाय = astringent; स्वादु = sweet; तिक्त = bitter; कटु = pungent; बस्ति = enema.
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: Put these words of line 2 of verse 68 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: When Kapha is being made to flow, the basti: astringent, pungent and bitter.
questions.teaches: Line 2 of verse 68: when Kapha is being made to flow, the basti is astringent, pungent and bitter.
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: Which tastes stand in BOTH lists of verse 68?
optionExplain: स्वादु is only in line 1.
कटु is only in line 2.
लवण is in neither list.
Right: कषाय is in line 1 and line 2.
Right: तिक्तक is in line 1 and line 2.
questions.explain: Line 1: कषाय-स्वादु-तिक्तक; line 2: कषाय, कटु-तिक्तक.
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: In कषायस्वादुतिक्तकः of verse 68, what does कषाय mean?
optionExplain: Kaṣāya can mean a decoction, but here it stands among tastes.
Kapha is a separate word (कफे) in line 2.
Right: In a row of tastes, कषाय is the taste: astringent (कसैला).
Blood words are रक्त and अस्र, not कषाय.
questions.explain: Taste row: कषाय (astringent), स्वादु (sweet), तिक्तक (bitter).
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: Like कषायस्वादुतिक्तकः, what does the new phrase मधुराम्ललवणो बस्तिः mean?
options: A sweet basti made of sour salt
A basti with no sweet, sour or salt
A basti only sweet and salty
A basti sweet, sour and salty
optionExplain: In a dvandva the members are equal; none qualifies another.
No negative is in the compound.
अम्ल (sour) is also a member.
Right: A dvandva of three tastes describes the basti: madhura, amla, lavaṇa.
questions.explain: Taste + taste + taste (dvandva) = a basti having all three.
questions.teaches: कषायस्वादुतिक्तकः in verse 68 is a dvandva of tastes: astringent, sweet and bitter.
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: By line 2 of verse 69, what should the drink in the mixed case be joined with?
optionExplain: Right: संसृष्टे … स्यात्कट्वम्ललवणैर्युतं.
That is line 1 of 05.06.132.
That row is not in verse 69.
That is the Kapha basti of 05.06.133.
questions.explain: कटु-अम्ल-लवणैः युतम् = joined with pungent, sour and salty (ones).
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: Match each clear word of verse 69 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The first four are from the list of line 1; संसृष्टे opens line 2.
questions.rule: वायुना = with wind; आमेन = with āma; वर्चसि = in stool; अथवा = or else; संसृष्टे = in the mixed case.
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: Put these clear words of line 2 of verse 69 in the verse's order (the unclear word is left out).
questions.explain: In the mixed case … there should be (it), joined with pungent, sour and salty.
questions.teaches: Line 2 of verse 69: in the mixed case (संसृष्टे) there should be (a drink) joined with pungent, sour and salty.
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: Which phrase of line 2 of verse 69 also occurs in verse 66?
optionExplain: That ends 05.06.133 (verse 68).
Right: 05.06.128 and 05.06.135 both end in कट्वम्ललवणैर्युतं.
That ends 05.06.131 (verse 67).
That is 05.06.153 (verse 78).
questions.explain: The same tastes (pungent, sour, salty) for the drink in āma and in the mixed case.
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: Which things does line 1 of verse 69 name in its combinations?
optionExplain: Right: वर्चसि.
Kapha is not in verse 69.
Right: आमेन.
Pitta is not in verse 69; it comes in 05.06.136.
Right: वायुना, and अनिलैः.
questions.explain: Line 1 has stool, wind and āma, in changing cases.
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: Like आमेन (with āma) in verse 69, what does the new phrase आमेन संसृष्टं पित्तम् mean?
options: Āma that is free of Pitta
optionExplain: Nothing in the phrase says 'free of'.
संसृष्ट means mixed, not destroying.
Right: पित्तम् is the noun; संसृष्टम् agrees with it; आमेन (instrumental) = with āma.
The instrumental here means 'with', not 'in place of'.
questions.explain: Instrumental (-एन) + संसृष्ट = mixed with.
questions.teaches: In verse 69 आमेन, वायुना are instrumentals: 'with āma', 'with wind', the things mixed in.
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: What kind of preparation does verse 70 give for the two that are mixed?
optionExplain: The oil enema is for wind, 05.06.131.
Coatings are not named in verse 70.
The six-taste basti is in 05.06.153.
Right: संसृष्टयोर्भवेत्पानं: there should be a drink.
questions.explain: भवेत् पानम् = there should be a drink.
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: Match each word of verse 70 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four words of the list in line 1, and the verb of line 2.
questions.rule: पित्तेन = with Pitta; असृजा = with blood; तद्वत् = likewise; पुनः = again; भवेत् = there should be.
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: Put these words of line 2 of verse 70 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Of the two mixed, there should be a drink, with pungent, sweet and bitter.
questions.teaches: Line 2 of verse 70: for the two that are mixed, a drink with pungent, sweet and bitter (tastes).
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: Which tastes does the drink of verse 70 have?
optionExplain: Right: सकटुकस्वादुतिक्तकं: with pungent (कटुक), sweet (स्वादु), bitter (तिक्तक).
That is the drink of 05.06.135 (verse 69).
That is the Kapha basti of 05.06.133.
That is the oil enema of 05.06.131.
questions.explain: कटुक = कटु (pungent); स्वादु = sweet; तिक्तक = bitter.
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: Which split of पित्तेनामे is right?
optionExplain: नामे is not a word here; the न belongs to पित्तेन.
Right: अ + आ → आ: पित्तेन + आमे → पित्तेनामे (with Pitta, in āma).
-अः + आ would give -अ आ: पित्त आमे.
ए + आ would give -अ आ or -या: पित्त आमे, पित्तयामे.
questions.explain: पित्तेन (instrumental) + आमे (locative).
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: Like सकटुक (with pungent) in verse 70, what does the new phrase सलवणं पानम् mean?
options: Salt in place of a drink
optionExplain: Without salt would be अलवण; स- means with.
पानम् is the noun; सलवणम् describes it.
Right: स- = with: स + लवण = having salt.
स- adds salt; it does not make it the only thing.
questions.explain: स-X = with X.
questions.teaches: सकटुकस्वादुतिक्तकं in verse 70 = स + कटुक-स्वादु-तिक्तक: 'with pungent, sweet and bitter'.
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: By line 1 of verse 71, which tastes go with āma mixed with Kapha?
optionExplain: That is the drink of 05.06.137 (verse 70).
That is the drink of 05.06.135 (verse 69).
That is the basti of 05.06.142.
Right: तथाऽऽमे कफसंसृष्टे कषायकटुतिक्तकं.
questions.explain: कषाय (astringent) + कटु (pungent) + तिक्तक (bitter).
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: Match each clear word of verse 71 to its meaning.
questions.explain: तथा and कफसंसृष्ट open line 1; युक्त and औषध are in line 2.
questions.rule: तथा = likewise; कफसंसृष्ट = mixed with Kapha; युक्त = joined; औषध = medicine; कषाय = astringent.
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: Put these words of line 1 of verse 71 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Likewise, in āma, mixed with Kapha: astringent, pungent and bitter.
questions.teaches: Line 1 of verse 71: likewise, in āma mixed with Kapha, (the drink is) astringent, pungent and bitter.
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: What is the case in line 2 of verse 71 (आमेन तु कफे युक्ते)?
optionExplain: Right: कफे (locative) is the base; आमेन (instrumental) is what it is joined with.
That is line 1 (आमे कफसंसृष्टे): there āma is the base.
Pitta is not named in verse 71.
questions.explain: Locative = the base; instrumental = the thing joined to it.
questions.rule: आमेन कफे युक्ते = आम से युक्त कफ में.
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: The drink of verse 70 is pungent, sweet and bitter. Which taste of line 1 of verse 71 is not in it?
optionExplain: कटु is in both (कटुक in verse 70).
Right: Verse 71 line 1 has कषाय; verse 70 has no कषाय.
तिक्तक is in both.
स्वादु is in verse 70 but not in verse 71 line 1.
questions.explain: 70: कटु · स्वादु · तिक्त; 71: कषाय · कटु · तिक्त.
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: Like कफे युक्ते (when Kapha is joined), what does the new phrase वाते कुपिते mean (कुपित = aggravated)?
optionExplain: कुपित is a past participle: aggravated, not aggravating.
By Vāta would be the instrumental वातेन.
Right: Two locatives that agree (noun + participle) = 'when X is Y'.
No negative is in the phrase.
questions.explain: Locative noun + locative participle = a condition: when X is Y.
questions.rule: वाते कुपिते = वात कुपित होने पर.
questions.teaches: In verse 71 कफे युक्ते (both locative): 'when Kapha is joined (with āma)'.
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: Which basti does verse 72 call best (uttama) in the mixed case?
optionExplain: That is the Kapha basti of 05.06.133.
That is the drink of 05.06.137.
That is the basti of 05.06.142.
Right: स्यात्कषायाम्लमधुरः संसृष्टे बस्तिरुत्तमः.
questions.explain: कषाय (astringent) + अम्ल (sour) + मधुर (sweet).
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: Match each word of verse 72 to its meaning.
questions.explain: विट्, अस्र and अनिल are in the list of line 1; मधुर and उत्तम in line 2.
questions.rule: उत्तम = best; अनिल = wind; विट् = stool; अस्र = blood; मधुर = sweet.
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: Put these words of line 2 of verse 72 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: There should be, astringent-sour-sweet, in the mixed case, a basti, best.
questions.teaches: Line 2 of verse 72: in the mixed case a basti astringent, sour and sweet would be best.
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: Which split of बस्तिरुत्तमः is right?
optionExplain: Right: -इः before a vowel → -इर्: बस्तिः + उत्तमः → बस्तिरुत्तमः.
रुत्तमः is not a word; the र् is the changed visarga.
म् + उ would give मु: बस्तिमुत्तमः.
ई + उ would give यु: बस्त्युत्तमः.
questions.explain: बस्तिः (basti) + उत्तमः (best).
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: In विट्पित्तास्रे of verse 72, which three are joined?
optionExplain: Wind is अनिले, a separate word; Kapha is not in verse 72.
Right: विट् (stool) + पित्त (Pitta) + अस्र (blood), locative: in these.
The middle member is पित्त, not कफ.
विट् is stool, not विष (poison).
questions.explain: विट्-पित्त-अस्रे: a dvandva of three, locative.
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: कषाय + अम्ल gives कषायाम्ल. By the same sandhi, what does मधुर + अम्ल give?
optionExplain: The two अ must merge into a long आ.
ओ would come from अ + उ, not अ + अ.
Right: अ + अ → आ: मधुर + अम्ल → मधुराम्ल.
ए would come from अ + इ, not अ + अ.
questions.explain: अ + अ → आ (savarṇa-dīrgha).
questions.teaches: कषायाम्लमधुरः in verse 72 = कषाय + अम्ल + मधुर: अ + अ → आ.
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: How should the basti be made with Vāta and in blood, by verse 73?
optionExplain: That is the best basti of 05.06.141.
That is the Kapha basti of 05.06.133.
That is the drink of 05.06.135.
Right: बस्तिर्वातेन रक्ते च कार्यः स्वाद्वम्लतिक्तकः.
questions.explain: स्वादु (sweet) + अम्ल (sour) + तिक्तक (bitter).
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: Match each word of verse 73 to its meaning.
questions.explain: कार्यः, स्वादु and रक्ते are in line 1; the two pairs in line 2.
questions.rule: कार्यः = should be made; स्वादु = sweet; रक्ते = in blood; पित्तशकृत् = Pitta and stool; असृक्पित्त = blood and Pitta.
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: Put these words of line 1 of verse 73 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The basti, with Vāta and in blood, should be made sweet, sour and bitter.
questions.rule: बस्तिः · वातेन · रक्ते · च · कार्यः · स्वाद्वम्लतिक्तकः.
questions.teaches: Line 1 of verse 73: with Vāta and in blood the basti should be made (कार्यः) sweet, sour and bitter.
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: Which split of पित्तशकृतोरसृक्पित्तयोः is right?
optionExplain: Right: -ओः before a vowel → -ओर्: शकृतोः + असृक् → शकृतोरसृक्.
रसृक् is not a word; the र् is the changed visarga.
-अः + अ would give -ओऽ: शकृतोऽसृक्, with an avagraha.
ए + अ would give एऽ: शकृतेऽसृक्.
questions.explain: Two dual dvandvas: पित्त-शकृतोः + असृक्-पित्तयोः.
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: Which of these pairs does line 2 of verse 73 name?
optionExplain: Right: असृक्पित्तयोः.
Āma and Kapha come in 05.06.138-139.
Kapha and wind are not in verse 73.
Kapha is not in verse 73.
Right: पित्तशकृतोः.
questions.explain: Line 2: (stool and blood, flagged), Pitta and stool, blood and Pitta.
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: Like पित्तशकृतोः (of Pitta and stool, dual), what does the new word वातपित्तयोः mean?
optionExplain: Kapha is not in the word; the dual means two.
Right: -योः is the genitive/locative dual: of or in the two.
By would be instrumental; the word joins two.
Subjects would be nominative dual, वातपित्ते.
questions.explain: Dvandva of two + -योः = of/in the two.
questions.teaches: In verse 73 पित्तशकृतोः, असृक्पित्तयोः are dual dvandvas in -योः: 'of (or in) Pitta and stool', 'blood and Pitta'.
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: Which basti does line 1 of verse 74 give in mutual combination?
optionExplain: That is the basti of 05.06.142.
That is the basti of 05.06.147.
Right: बस्तिरन्योन्यसंसर्गे कषायस्वादुतिक्तकः.
That is the best basti of 05.06.141.
questions.explain: कषाय (astringent) + स्वादु (sweet) + तिक्तक (bitter).
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: Match each word of verse 74 to its meaning.
questions.explain: अन्योन्य-संसर्ग is in line 1; कफेन and विट्-पित्त-शोणित in line 2.
questions.rule: अन्योन्य = one another; संसर्ग = combination; कफेन = with Kapha; शोणित = blood; विट् = stool.
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: Put these words of line 2 of verse 74 in the verse's order (the flagged word is left out).
questions.explain: With Kapha, (in stool) or in Pitta; in Kapha, with stool, Pitta and blood.
questions.rule: कफेन · (flagged word) · पित्ते · वा · कफे · विट्पित्तशोणितैः.
questions.teaches: Line 2 of verse 74 begins the Kapha cases: with Kapha, in Pitta; in Kapha with stool, Pitta and blood.
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: Verse 73 makes the basti sweet, sour and bitter. What does line 1 of verse 74 have in place of sour?
optionExplain: कटु is not in line 1 of verse 74.
लवण is not in line 1 of verse 74.
Sweet (स्वादु) is in both; it does not replace sour.
Right: 74: कषाय-स्वादु-तिक्तक; 73: स्वादु-अम्ल-तिक्तक. कषाय stands where अम्ल stood.
questions.explain: Sweet and bitter stay; sour gives way to astringent.
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: What does अन्योन्यसंसर्गे in verse 74 mean?
optionExplain: Right: अन्योन्य = one another; संसर्ग = combination; locative.
No negative is in the word.
Single (ones) are केवल (05.06.125), not अन्योन्य; अन्योन्य means one another.
Six (षण्णाम्) is in 05.06.152, not here.
questions.explain: अन्योन्य-संसर्गे = when (the items) are combined with one another.
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: Like विट्पित्तशोणितैः (with stool, Pitta and blood), what does the new word वातपित्तकफैः mean?
options: Vāta, Pitta and Kapha, as subjects
optionExplain: Of would be the genitive plural -आनाम्.
Right: -ऐः is the instrumental plural: 'with' or 'by' the three.
In would be the locative plural -एषु.
Subjects would be the nominative plural -आः.
questions.explain: Dvandva of three + -ऐः = with the three (instrumental plural).
questions.teaches: विट्पित्तशोणितैः in verse 74 is an instrumental plural dvandva: 'with stool, Pitta and blood'.
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: Which basti does line 2 of verse 75 give in Kapha mixed with wind?
optionExplain: That is the mutual-combination basti of 05.06.144.
That is for wind mixed with Kapha, 05.06.149.
Right: स्याद्बस्तिः कटुतिक्ताम्लः संसृष्टे वायुना कफे.
That is the basti of 05.06.142.
questions.explain: कटु (pungent) + तिक्त (bitter) + अम्ल (sour).
questions.rule: वायु से संसृष्ट कफ: कटु · तिक्त · अम्ल.
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: Match each word of verse 75 to its meaning.
questions.explain: उत्तम is in line 1; the rest are in line 2.
questions.rule: वायुना = with wind; कफे = in Kapha; संसृष्टे = mixed; अम्ल = sour; उत्तम = best.
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: Put these words of line 2 of verse 75 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: There should be a basti, pungent, bitter and sour, in Kapha mixed with wind.
questions.teaches: Line 2 of verse 75: in Kapha mixed with wind, a basti pungent, bitter and sour.
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: Which split of कटुतिक्ताम्लः is right?
optionExplain: म्लः is not a word; the आ comes from अ + अ.
-अः + अ would give -ओऽ: तिक्तोऽम्लः.
ए + अ would give एऽ: तिक्तेऽम्लः.
Right: अ + अ → आ: तिक्त + अम्लः → तिक्ताम्लः.
questions.explain: कटु (pungent) + तिक्त (bitter) + अम्लः (sour).
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: In line 2 of verse 75 (संसृष्टे वायुना कफे), which is the base and which is mixed in?
options: Kapha the base, wind mixed in
Wind the base, Kapha mixed in
Blood the base, Kapha mixed in
Āma the base, Kapha mixed in
optionExplain: Right: कफे (locative) agrees with संसृष्टे; वायुना (instrumental) is what it is mixed with.
That is 05.06.149, मारुते कफसंसृष्टे.
That is 05.06.148, रक्ते कफविमूर्च्छिते.
That is 05.06.138, आमे कफसंसृष्टे.
questions.explain: Locative noun + locative संसृष्टे = the base; instrumental = the partner.
questions.rule: वायुना संसृष्टे कफे = वायु मिला कफ.
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: स्यात् + बस्तिः gives स्याद्बस्तिः. By the same sandhi, what does स्यात् + बलम् give?
optionExplain: त् does not stay voiceless before ब.
Right: त् before a voiced consonant (ब) becomes द्: स्याद्बलम्.
त् becomes द्, not ब्, before ब.
ब stays ब; it does not turn into व.
questions.explain: -त् + voiced consonant → -द्.
questions.teaches: स्याद्बस्तिः in verse 75 = स्यात् + बस्तिः: final त् before voiced ब becomes द्.
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: By line 2 of verse 76, what should it be in wind mixed with Kapha?
optionExplain: That is for Kapha mixed with wind, 05.06.147.
That is the mutual-combination basti, 05.06.144.
Right: मारुते कफसंसृष्टे कट्वम्ललवणो भवेत्.
That is the best basti of 05.06.141.
questions.explain: कटु (pungent) + अम्ल (sour) + लवण (salty).
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: Match each word of verse 76 to its meaning.
questions.explain: रक्त and विमूर्च्छित are in line 1; मारुत, लवण and भवेत् in line 2.
questions.rule: मारुत = wind; विमूर्च्छित = mingled; रक्त = blood; लवण = salty; भवेत् = it should be.
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: Put these words of line 2 of verse 76 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: In wind, mixed with Kapha, pungent-sour-salty it should be.
questions.teaches: Line 2 of verse 76: in wind mixed with Kapha it should be pungent, sour and salty.
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: Verse 75 gives pungent, bitter, sour for Kapha mixed with wind. How does line 2 of verse 76 differ?
options: It is the same three tastes
optionExplain: Sour (अम्ल) is in both lines.
Pungent (कटु) is in both lines.
Bitter in 75 becomes salty in 76.
Right: 76: कटु-अम्ल-लवण; 75: कटु-तिक्त-अम्ल. Pungent and sour stay; salty replaces bitter.
questions.explain: Base Kapha (75) vs base wind (76): तिक्त gives way to लवण.
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: For blood mingled with Kapha, which clear tastes does line 1 of verse 76 name?
optionExplain: Right: तिक्त.
Sour is in line 2, not in line 1.
Salty is in line 2, not in line 1.
Astringent is not in verse 76.
Right: मधुर.
questions.explain: Line 1: मधुर, उषण (read as pungent), तिक्त.
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: Like रक्ते कफविमूर्च्छिते, what does the new phrase पित्ते वातविमूर्च्छिते mean?
optionExplain: Right: पित्ते is the base (locative); वात-विमूर्च्छिते = mingled with Vāta, agreeing with it.
The base is the noun पित्ते; वात is the first member of the compound.
विमूर्च्छित means mingled, not free of.
Fainting is मूर्च्छा (05.06.127); विमूर्च्छित here means mingled.
questions.explain: Locative noun + X-विमूर्च्छिते = in (the noun) mingled with X.
questions.teaches: In verse 76 रक्ते कफविमूर्च्छिते = 'in blood mingled with Kapha': blood the base, Kapha mixed in.
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: By line 2 of verse 77, in which diseases is this method held?
optionExplain: It was stated for atisāra, but अपि (also) extends it to all diseases.
Right: सर्वरोगेष्वपि स्मृता: held also in all diseases.
Kapha is not named in verse 77.
Fever is not named in verse 77.
questions.explain: सर्व-रोगेषु अपि = also in all diseases.
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: Put these numbers of line 1 of verse 77 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The compound counts up: three, four, five, six.
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: Match each word of verse 77 to its meaning.
questions.explain: All five are in line 2.
questions.rule: युक्ति = method; अतिसार = diarrhoea; उक्त = stated; सर्व = all; स्मृत = held.
questions.teaches: Line 2 of verse 77: this method (युक्ति), stated for atisāra, is held (स्मृता) in all diseases.
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: Which split of सर्वरोगेष्वपि is right?
optionExplain: पि is not a word; अपि is.
इ + अ would give य: रोगेष्यपि.
Right: उ + अ → व: रोगेषु + अपि → रोगेष्वपि.
-अः + अ would give -ओऽ: रोगेषोऽपि.
questions.explain: सर्वरोगेषु (in all diseases, locative plural) + अपि (also).
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: A physician meets a combination of four of the items. What does line 1 of verse 77 tell him?
options: To give no basti at all
To stop at pairs of two
optionExplain: Verse 77 forbids nothing.
Verse 77 extends the rule to larger combinations.
Line 1 goes on to three, four, five and six.
Right: त्रिचतुःपंचषड्योगेन … विकल्पयेत्: combinations of three to six are also to be varied (विकल्पयेत्).
questions.explain: विकल्पयेत् = one should vary; the word read as 'thus' (एवम्) is flagged, so only the numbers and विकल्पयेत् are relied on.
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: Like अतिसारोक्ता युक्तिः (the method stated for atisāra), what does the new phrase ज्वरोक्ता युक्तिः mean?
optionExplain: Right: ज्वर + उक्ता → ज्वरोक्ता (अ + उ → ओ): stated for fever.
उक्त means stated, not causing.
युक्तिः is the noun; ज्वरोक्ता describes it.
No negative is in the phrase.
questions.explain: X-उक्त = stated for (or in) X; अ + उ → ओ.
questions.rule: X-उक्ता युक्तिः = X के लिए कही युक्ति.
questions.teaches: अतिसारोक्ता in verse 77 = अतिसार + उक्ता (अ + उ → ओ): 'stated for atisāra'.
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: By line 1 of verse 78, what should there be in the combination of six?
optionExplain: That is for the five, in line 2.
Right: षण्णां संसर्गे पाचनं भवेत्.
The oil enema is for wind, 05.06.131.
No such drink is named in verse 78.
questions.explain: पाचनं भवेत् = there should be a digestive.
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: Match each clear word of verse 78 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The first four are in line 1; हित ends line 2.
questions.rule: युगपत् = at once; षण्णाम् = of six; संसर्ग = combination; पाचन = digestive; हित = beneficial.
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: Put these words of line 2 of verse 78 in the verse's order (the flagged first word is left out).
questions.explain: But, of the five, a basti having six tastes is beneficial.
questions.rule: (flagged word) · तु · पंचानां · बस्तिः · षड्रसिको · हितः.
questions.teaches: Line 2 of verse 78: for the five, a basti having six tastes (षड्रसिकः) is beneficial.
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: What does षड्रसिकः in verse 78 mean?
optionExplain: Sixth would be षष्ठ; षड् is six.
रस is taste, not basti.
Right: षट् (six) + रस (taste) + -इक (having).
-इक means having, not free of.
questions.explain: षड्-रस-इक = having six tastes.
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: By line 2 of verse 78, what is beneficial for the five?
optionExplain: The digestive is for the combination of six, line 1.
That drink is in 05.06.128 and 05.06.135.
Basti is forbidden in āma (05.06.129); here it is beneficial.
Right: पंचानां बस्तिः षड्रसिको हितः.
questions.explain: हितः is said of the बस्तिः षड्रसिकः.
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: षट् + रसिकः gives षड्रसिकः. By the same sandhi, what does षट् + गुणः give?
optionExplain: Right: ट् before a voiced consonant (ग) becomes ड्: षड्गुणः.
ट् does not stay voiceless before ग.
ट् does not turn into ष्.
ग stays ग; the second word does not change.
questions.explain: -ट् + voiced consonant → -ड्.
questions.teaches: षड्रसिकः in verse 78 = षट् + रसिकः: final ट् before voiced र becomes ड्.
questions.section: दोष-संसर्ग के अनुसार बस्ति के रस

questions.q: Which part of the udumbara does line 1 of verse 79 name first?
optionExplain: Sprouts of young udumbara come later, in 05.06.160.
Right: उदुंबरशलाटूनि: the unripe fruits (śalāṭu) of the udumbara.
शलाटु means unripe fruit, not ripe fruit.
No root is named in verse 79.
questions.explain: शलाटु = unripe fruit; the line opens with those of the udumbara (cluster fig).

questions.q: Match each word of verse 79 to its meaning on the card.
questions.explain: Line 1 gives the tree parts; line 2 begins with conch shell and ends its items with lac and kattṛṇa.
questions.rule: उदुम्बर = cluster fig; शलाटु = unripe fruit; त्वच् = bark; शङ्ख = conch shell; लाक्षा = lac.

questions.q: Put these words of line 2 of verse 79 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Conch shell, sal resin, lac, kattṛṇa, and last the measure: with a pala as the portion.
questions.rule: शंखं · सर्जरसं · लाक्षां · कत्तृणं च · पलांशिकं.
questions.teaches: Line 2 of verse 79: conch shell, sarjarasa (sal resin), lac and kattṛṇa, with a pala as the portion.

questions.q: What is सर्जरस, by the card of verse 79?
options: The bark of the sal tree
The resin of the sal tree
optionExplain: The barks of line 1 are of jambū, āmra and udumbara, not sal.
Lac is लाक्षा, a separate item in the same line.
Right: सर्ज (sal tree) + रस (here resin): sarjarasa, resin of the sal (standard).
The unripe figs are the udumbara śalāṭu of line 1.
questions.explain: सर्जरस = resin (rasa) of the sarja (sal) tree; लाक्षा (lac) is listed next to it.

questions.q: A helper gathers the drugs of verse 79. Which of these does the verse name?
optionExplain: Right: उदुंबरशलाटूनि.
Right: शंखं.
Dhātakī flowers come in 05.06.161, not here.
Right: लाक्षां.
Masūra comes in 05.06.159 and 05.06.161, not here.
questions.explain: Verse 79 names unripe udumbara fruits, three barks, conch shell, sarjarasa, lac and kattṛṇa.
questions.rule: शलाटु · त्वचः · शंख · सर्जरस · लाक्षा · कत्तृण.

questions.q: पलांशिकम् = with a pala as the portion. By that pattern, what does the new word कर्षांशिकम् mean?
options: Less than one karṣa in weight
With a karṣa as the portion
optionExplain: अंशिक means 'having a portion', not 'lacking' one.
No number is in the word; only the karṣa as the portion.
Nothing says 'less'; the karṣa itself is the portion.
Right: कर्ष + अंशिक, like पल + अंशिक: the measure named is the portion.
questions.explain: X-अंशिक = having X as the portion; अ + अ → आ joins them.
questions.teaches: Verse 79: पलांशिकम् = पल + अंशिकम्, 'with a pala as the portion' (अ + अ → आ).

questions.q: In which disorders is the ghee to be drunk, by verse 80?
optionExplain: Right: अतिसारेषु सर्वेषु: in all atisāras.
Fever is not named in verse 80.
Heart-pain and cutting are other mishaps of this chapter, not named here.
The verse says सर्वेषु, all, not only a mild one.
questions.explain: अतिसारेषु सर्वेषु = in all diarrhoeas: the locative names where the ghee is used.

questions.q: Put these words of line 1 of verse 80 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Having ground, with these, a prastha of ghee, doubled with milk, one should cook.
questions.rule: पिष्ट्वा · तैः · सर्पिषः प्रस्थं · क्षीरद्विगुणितं · पचेत्.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 80 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Line 1 gives the making, line 2 the use.
questions.rule: पिष्ट्वा = having ground; सर्पिस् = ghee; प्रस्थ = a measure; क्षीर = milk; पेय = to be drunk; यथाबलम् = according to strength.
questions.teaches: Verse 80: having ground the drugs, cook a prastha of ghee doubled with milk; drink it in all atisāras according to strength.

questions.q: Which split of पेयमेतद्यथाबलं is right?
optionExplain: मेतत् is not a word; the म् belongs to पेयम्.
Right: म् + ए → मे; त् → द् before the voiced य: पेयमेतद्यथाबलम्.
Neither एत nor द्यथाबलम् fits; the pronoun is एतत्.
पेयमे is not a form; the word is पेयम्.
questions.explain: पेयम् (to be drunk) + एतत् (this) + यथाबलम् (according to strength).

questions.q: A physician gives this ghee to a patient. How, by verse 80, is it to be drunk?
optionExplain: The prastha is the ghee cooked, not the dose drunk.
Milk goes into the cooking; no daily dose is given.
Right: पेयमेतद्यथाबलम्: this is to be drunk according to strength.
No pala or time of day is named in verse 80.
questions.explain: यथा-बलम् = according to strength; the verse gives no fixed dose.

questions.q: Like पिष्ट्वा (having ground), what does the new form पीत्वा mean?
optionExplain: 'To be drunk' is the gerundive पेय, as in line 2.
'One should drink' would be an optative like पिबेत्.
That is a present tense, पिबति; -त्वा is not a tense.
Right: -त्वा forms the absolutive: पीत्वा = having drunk (√पा), like पिष्ट्वा from √पिष्.
questions.explain: -त्वा = having done (an action finished before the main verb).
questions.teaches: In verse 80 पिष्ट्वा is an absolutive in -त्वा: 'having ground', done before पचेत् (one should cook).

questions.q: What preparation do the drugs of verse 81 make?
optionExplain: Right: यवागूः स्यात्: there should be a yavāgū (gruel).
The ghee cooked with milk is in 05.06.156.
No basti is named in verse 81.
No kalka is named; the items are boiled in water.
questions.explain: The predicate is यवागूः स्यात्: a gruel should be (made).

questions.q: Put these drugs of line 1 of verse 81 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: The compound of line 1 runs kacchurā, dhātakī, bilva, samaṅgā, raktamūlin.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 81 to its meaning on the card.
questions.explain: Four drugs with standard names, and the water they are boiled in.
questions.rule: धातकी = woodfordia; बिल्व = bael; मसूर = lentil; अश्वत्थ = sacred fig; जल = water.
questions.teaches: Verse 81: dhātakī, bilva, masūra and aśvattha tips, among others, boiled in water, make a yavāgū.

questions.q: Which split of स्याज्जले is right?
optionExplain: A visarga after आ drops before ज; it gives no ज्ज.
Right: त् + ज → ज्ज: स्यात् (there should be) + जले (in water).
म् before ज becomes anusvāra or ञ्, not ज्ज.
ज्जले is not a word; the ज्ज comes from the join.
questions.explain: स्यात् + जले: final त् takes the form of the following ज.

questions.q: A cook makes this gruel. In what are the drugs boiled, by verse 81?
optionExplain: Milk goes with the ghee of 05.06.156, not the gruel.
Ghee is not named in verse 81.
Right: जले शृतैः: boiled in water.
No sour liquid is named in verse 81.
questions.explain: जले (locative) = in water; शृतैः = boiled.

questions.q: Like स्यात् + जले → स्याज्जले, how do the invented words भवेत् + जलम् join?
optionExplain: Before ज the त् does not stop at द्; it becomes ज्.
ञ् would come from a nasal, not from त्.
च् stands before च or छ; before ज it is ज्.
Right: Same rule: त् + ज → ज्ज.
questions.explain: Final त् before ज becomes ज्.
questions.teaches: त् + ज → ज्ज: स्यात् + जले = स्याज्जले in verse 81.

questions.q: Which part of the plants does line 1 of verse 82 use?
optionExplain: Right: …प्लक्षपल्लवैः: with the sprouts (pallava).
Barks are in the list of 05.06.154.
Unripe udumbara fruits are in 05.06.154.
No root is named in verse 82.
questions.explain: पल्लव closes the compound of line 1: sprouts.

questions.q: Put these members of the line 1 compound of verse 82 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: बाल-उदुम्बर-कट्वङ्ग-समङ्गा-प्लक्ष-पल्लवैः: the four plants, then the sprouts.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 82 to its meaning.
questions.explain: बाल and पल्लव from line 1; पुष्प, बला and तथा from line 2.
questions.rule: बाल = young; पल्लव = sprout; पुष्प = flower; बला = country mallow; तथा = likewise.
questions.teaches: Verse 82: sprouts of young udumbara and others, with masūra, dhātakī flowers and balā: it should be likewise.

questions.q: Which split of बालोदुंबर is right?
optionExplain: Inside a compound there is no visarga; and -अः before उ would not give ओ.
Right: अ + उ → ओ: बाल + उदुम्बर → बालोदुम्बर.
अ + ओ gives औ, so this would print बालौदुम्बर.
इ + उ gives यु, so this would print बाल्युदुम्बर.
questions.explain: बाल (young) + उदुम्बर (cluster fig): अ and उ merge into ओ.

questions.q: Which items of verse 82 were already named in verse 81?
optionExplain: Right: samaṅgā is in 05.06.158 too.
Right: dhātakī is in 05.06.158 too.
Balā is new in verse 82.
Right: masūra is in 05.06.159 too.
Plakṣa is new in verse 82.
questions.explain: The card: masūra, dhātakī and samaṅgā recur from 05.06.158-159.

questions.q: बलाभिः is the instrumental plural of the feminine बला. What is the instrumental plural of the new feminine word लता?
optionExplain: -ऐः is the instrumental plural of -अ stems (masculine or neuter).
-आभ्यः is the dative or ablative plural.
Right: Feminine -आ stems: -आभिः in the instrumental plural, like बलाभिः.
-आयाः is the genitive or ablative singular.
questions.explain: Feminine -आ + -भिः → -आभिः (with ...).
questions.teaches: बलाभिः in verse 82 = 'with balā': feminine -आ stems take -आभिः in the instrumental plural.

questions.q: From what do mishaps of various kinds arise, by verse 83?
options: From an error in the basti
optionExplain: Age is not named in verse 83.
No meal is named in verse 83.
Water is not named in verse 83.
Right: बस्तिविभ्रमात्: from an error (vibhrama) in the basti.
questions.explain: बस्ति-विभ्रमात् is ablative: the cause from which the mishaps arise.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 83 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Line 1 gives the mishaps and their cause; line 2 the treatment.
questions.rule: नानाप्रकार = of various kinds; व्यापद् = mishap; विभ्रम = error; अवस्था = condition; साधन = treatment.

questions.q: Put these phrases of verse 83 in the verse's order.
questions.explain: Of various kinds arise mishaps, from an error in the basti; of those one should do the treatment.
questions.rule: नानाप्रकारा · जायंते · व्यापदो · बस्तिविभ्रमात् ‖ … तासां कुर्वीत साधनं.
questions.teaches: Verse 83: mishaps of various kinds arise from an error in the basti; one should carry out their treatment.

questions.q: Before बस्तिविभ्रमात्, the printed व्यापदो stands for which form?
optionExplain: Right: -अः → -ओ before a voiced sound (ब): व्यापदः + बस्ति… → व्यापदो बस्ति…
Final -आ stays -आ before ब; it does not become -ओ.
Final म् before ब becomes anusvāra: व्यापदं.
Final -ए stays -ए before a consonant.
questions.explain: व्यापदः (mishaps, nom. pl.): -अः turns into -ओ before the voiced ब.

questions.q: A basti has gone wrong and a mishap appears. How should it be treated, by verse 83?
options: By giving the same basti again
optionExplain: The verse ties the treatment to the condition, not one remedy.
Right: यथावस्थम्: according to the condition (avasthā).
No repeat of the basti is stated.
तासां कुर्वीत साधनम्: their treatment should be done.
questions.explain: यथा-अवस्थम् = as the condition is; the treatment follows it.

questions.q: Like यथावस्थम् (according to the condition), what does the new word यथाकालम् mean?
optionExplain: That would be अकाले; यथा- means 'according to'.
That would be कालात् पूर्वम्; यथा- means 'according to'.
Right: यथा + X (adverb) = according to X; काल = time.
That would be सर्वकालम् or सदा.
questions.explain: यथा-X-म् = according to X (as in यथाबलम्, 05.06.157).
questions.teaches: यथावस्थम् in verse 83 = यथा + अवस्था: 'according to the condition'.

questions.q: What is the name of the chapter closed by unit 84?
optionExplain: Bastikalpa is the fourth chapter.
Siddhabastikalpa is the fifth chapter.
Snehavyāpatsiddhi is the seventh chapter.
Right: बस्तिव्यापत्सिद्धिर्नाम: named Bastivyāpatsiddhi.
questions.explain: The colophon names the chapter: the success concerning the mishaps of basti.

questions.q: Put the words of unit 84 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Thus, Bastivyāpatsiddhi, named, the sixth, chapter.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 84 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The words of the colophon, with the two members of the chapter's name.
questions.rule: इति = thus; व्यापद् = mishap; सिद्धि = success; षष्ठ = sixth; अध्याय = chapter.
questions.teaches: Unit 84: the sixth chapter, Bastivyāpatsiddhi = success concerning the mishaps (vyāpad) of basti.

questions.q: Which split of सिद्धिर्नाम is right?
optionExplain: Right: -इः → -इर् before a voiced sound (न): सिद्धिः + नाम → सिद्धिर्नाम.
म् before न becomes anusvāra: सिद्धिं नाम.
Long ई before न stays ई; no र् appears.
र्नाम is not a word; the र् comes from the visarga.
questions.explain: सिद्धिः (success) + नाम (named): a visarga after इ becomes र् before a voiced sound.

questions.q: The colophon calls this the ____ (sixth) chapter. Type it in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: षष्ठोऽध्यायः = षष्ठः (sixth) + अध्यायः (chapter).
questions.teaches: Unit 84 names the chapter Bastivyāpatsiddhi and calls it the sixth (षष्ठ) chapter.

questions.q: षष्ठः + अध्यायः gives षष्ठोऽध्यायः. How do the new words अष्टमः + अध्यायः join?
optionExplain: That gap is for -अः before a vowel other than अ.
Right: Same rule: -अः + अ- → -ओऽ-, the avagraha marking the lost अ.
-अः does not lengthen to -आ before अ.
ए would belong to a locative अष्टमे, not to अष्टमः.
questions.explain: -अः before अ: ओ, and ऽ for the swallowed अ.
questions.teaches: -अः + अ- → -ओऽ-: षष्ठः + अध्यायः = षष्ठोऽध्यायः in unit 84.

questions.q: The chapter speaks of the mishaps (व्यापद्) of what?
options: Of madana, the foremost emetic fruit
Of the seasons and the daily diet
optionExplain: No emetic drug is named in this line.
Seasons and diet are not the subject named here.
Right: स्नेहव्यापदिकाम्: concerning the mishaps of sneha (oil or fat).
The line names sneha, not the physician.
questions.explain: स्नेह-व्यापद्-इका: relating to the mishaps of the unctuous substance (sneha).
questions.rule: स्नेहव्यापदिकां सिद्धिम् = the accomplishment concerning the mishaps of sneha.

questions.q: Put the words of the formula in the order of the text.
questions.explain: The line runs: now, therefore, concerning the mishaps of sneha, the accomplishment, we shall explain.

questions.q: Match each word of the formula to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words carry the whole announcement of the chapter.
questions.rule: स्नेह = unctuous substance; व्यापद् = mishap; सिद्धि = accomplishment; व्याख्यास्यामः = we shall explain.
questions.teaches: sneha is the unctuous substance (oil or fat); vyāpad is a mishap; the chapter is about mishaps of sneha.

questions.q: Which is the right split of the first word, अथातः?
optionExplain: तः is not a word here; the parts are अथ (now) and अतः (therefore).
The second part begins with short अ (अतः), not आ.
अथ ends in -अ and has no visarga.
Right: अ + अ gives आ: अथ + अतः = अथातः.
questions.explain: अथ (now) + अतः (therefore) = अथातः.

questions.q: Which word of the formula shows that the explaining is still to come?
optionExplain: Right: -स्यामः is the first person plural future: 'we shall explain'.
अथ means 'now'; it opens the formula but is no verb.
सिद्धिम् is the object, 'the accomplishment'.
This word names the subject, the mishaps of sneha.
questions.explain: Only the verb carries time; its ending -स्यामः is future.

questions.q: Like व्याख्यास्यामः, which form of √दा means we shall give?
optionExplain: This is 'we give', the present.
Right: -स्यामः is the 'we shall' ending, as in व्याख्यास्यामः.
This is 'we gave', a past form.
This is 'we should give', the optative.
questions.explain: The first person plural future ends in -स्यामः (or -ष्यामः).
questions.teaches: The first person plural future ends in -स्यामः / -ष्यामः (व्याख्यास्यामः, दास्यामः): 'we shall ...'.

questions.q: In which procedure does the verse place the sevenfold mishaps?
optionExplain: nirūha is not named in this verse; it says स्नेहबस्ति.
Emesis is not mentioned here.
Right: स्नेहबस्तौ: in the unctuous enema.
Purgation is not mentioned here.
questions.explain: स्नेहबस्तौ = in the unctuous enema (sneha-basti).
questions.rule: स्नेहबस्तौ ... सप्तधा व्यापदः = in the unctuous enema, the mishaps are sevenfold.

questions.q: Put the coverers in the order the verse names them.
questions.explain: The compound runs: wind, Pitta, Kapha, over-eating, accumulation of stool.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words name the coverers and the covering itself.
questions.rule: मरुत् = wind; अत्यशन = over-eating; विट्चय = accumulation of stool; आवृति = covering.
questions.teaches: The mishaps arise from a covering (āvṛti) of the sneha by wind, Pitta, Kapha, over-eating or stool.

questions.q: Which is the right split of कफात्यशन?
optionExplain: These pieces are not words.
अत्य and शन are not the words; they are अति and अशन.
Inside a compound कफ has no visarga.
Right: अ + अ → आ (कफाति), then इ + अ → य (अत्यशन).
questions.explain: कफ (Kapha) + अति (excessive) + अशन (eating).
questions.rule: अ + अ → आ; इ + अ → य.

questions.q: Which of these does the verse name as coverers in the unctuous enema? Choose all that apply.
optionExplain: Right: पित्त is named.
Not named in this verse.
Right: विट्चय is named.
Not named in this verse.
Right: अत्यशन is named.
questions.explain: The verse names wind, Pitta, Kapha, over-eating and stool; blood and urine are not among them.
questions.rule: Coverers: मरुत्, पित्त, कफ, अत्यशन, विट्चय.

questions.q: Join a new example, अति + अन्न (excess of food), as one word. Which is right?
optionExplain: Right: इ before a different vowel becomes य्: अति + अन्न = अत्यन्न, as अति + अशन = अत्यशन.
इ + अ does not give ई.
The इ does not simply drop.
The अ of अन्न stays short.
questions.explain: Same rule as अति + अशन = अत्यशन.
questions.teaches: Final इ before a different vowel becomes य् (अति + अशन = अत्यशन; अति + अन्न = अत्यन्न).

questions.q: With Pitta, which quality of the sneha does the unit name?
optionExplain: मृदु goes with Kapha.
Right: पित्तेऽत्युष्णः: in Pitta, very hot.
शीत goes with Vāta in excess.
गुरु goes with over-eating.
questions.explain: पित्ते अत्युष्णः = very hot in Pitta.

questions.q: Match each cause to the quality the unit pairs with it.
questions.explain: The unit gives one quality for each of the five causes.
questions.rule: वात: शीत/अल्प · पित्त: अत्युष्ण · कफ: मृदु · अतिभुक्त: गुरु · वर्चःसंचय: अल्पबल.

questions.q: Put the five causes in the order the unit gives them.
questions.explain: Vāta, Pitta, Kapha, over-eating, stool: the same order as the coverers of unit 2.
questions.teaches: The causes keep the order of unit 2: Vāta, Pitta, Kapha, over-eating, accumulation of stool.

questions.q: Which is the right split of शीतो ऽल्पो?
optionExplain: शीतो is not a stem; it is शीतः changed by sandhi.
There is no उ here; the ओ comes from अः.
Right: अः before short अ becomes ओ and the अ is dropped (ऽ): शीतोऽल्पः.
म् before a vowel stays म् (शीतमल्पम्), it does not give ओ.
questions.explain: शीतः (cold) + अल्पः (little); the second ओ (अल्पो) is the same change before वा.

questions.q: A student links 'mild' (मृदु) with Vāta. Which cause does the unit actually pair with मृदु?
optionExplain: Vāta in excess has 'cold or little'.
Over-eating has 'heavy'.
Accumulated stool has 'of little strength'.
Right: कफे मृदुः: mild in Kapha.
questions.explain: कफे मृदुः = mild in Kapha.

questions.q: Like पित्ते (in Pitta), which form of शरीर means in the body?
optionExplain: Right: An -अ stem's locative singular ends in -ए, like वाते, पित्ते, कफे.
This is the nominative/accusative, 'the body'.
This is the instrumental, 'by the body'.
This is the genitive, 'of the body'.
questions.explain: वाते, पित्ते, कफे are locatives in -ए: 'in / when'.
questions.teaches: The locative singular of an -अ stem ends in -ए (वाते, पित्ते, कफे, शरीरे): 'in, when'.

questions.q: What does the unit say the covered sneha does not do?
options: It does not get warm enough
It does not stay in the body
It does not mix with the food
optionExplain: Warmth is not mentioned in line 1.
Right: नायाति = न आयाति, 'does not come'; 'out' is understood.
The trouble is the opposite: it does not come.
Mixing is not mentioned.
questions.explain: दत्तः ... आवृतः स्नेहः न आयाति = the given sneha, covered, does not come (out).
questions.section: वायु से आवृत स्नेह और उपचार

questions.q: Match each word of line 1 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words make up the statement of the mishap.
questions.rule: दत्तः = given; आवृतः = covered; आयाति = comes; अभिभवात् = from overpowering.
questions.section: वायु से आवृत स्नेह और उपचार

questions.q: Put the signs of line 2 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The compound runs: stiffness, weakness of the thighs, distension, fever, pain, aching of the limbs.
questions.rule: स्तम्भ · ऊरुसदन · आध्मान · ज्वर · शूल · अङ्गमर्द.
questions.teaches: The signs of line 2 in order: stiffness, weakness of the thighs, distension, fever, pain, aching of the limbs.
questions.section: वायु से आवृत स्नेह और उपचार

questions.q: Which is the right split of नायात्यभिभवादपि?
optionExplain: यात्य and दपि are not words.
The verb is आयाति, with long आ.
Right: अ + आ → आ; इ + अ → य; त् → द् before a vowel.
नाय is not a word; the parts are न and आयाति.
questions.explain: न (not) + आयाति (comes) + अभिभवात् (from overpowering) + अपि (also).
questions.rule: अ + आ → आ; इ + अ → य; त् + vowel → द्.
questions.section: वायु से आवृत स्नेह और उपचार

questions.q: Which sign in line 2 means distension of the belly?
optionExplain: This is weakness (sinking) of the thighs.
This is stiffness.
This is aching of the limbs.
Right: आध्मान = distension of the belly (bloating; standard).
questions.explain: आध्मान is the bloating of the abdomen.
questions.section: वायु से आवृत स्नेह और उपचार

questions.q: Like दत्तः (given, from √दा), which past participle of √पा means drunk?
optionExplain: Right: A past participle in -त means 'done': दत्तः 'given', पीतः 'drunk'.
This is 'he drinks', the present.
This is the noun 'drinking'.
This is 'he will drink', the future.
questions.explain: दत्तः and आवृतः are past participles: 'given', 'covered'.
questions.teaches: Past participles in -त say what has been done (दत्तः given, आवृतः covered, पीतः drunk).
questions.section: वायु से आवृत स्नेह और उपचार

questions.q: With flank pain and twisting, by what does the unit say the sneha is covered?
optionExplain: Covering by Pitta comes in unit 8.
Right: विद्याद् वायुना स्नेहावृतम्: know the sneha covered by Vāyu.
Covering by Kapha comes in unit 9.
Covering by stool is not in this unit.
questions.explain: वायुना = by Vāyu; the sneha is covered (आवृत).
questions.rule: पार्श्वरुज् + वेष्टन → वायु से आवृत स्नेह.
questions.section: वायु से आवृत स्नेह और उपचार

questions.q: Put the four qualities of the remedy in the order of line 2.
questions.explain: The compound runs: unctuous, sour, salty, hot.
questions.section: वायु से आवृत स्नेह और उपचार

questions.q: Match each word of line 1 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words give the signs and the conclusion drawn from them.
questions.rule: पार्श्वरुज् = flank pain; वेष्टन = twisting; विद्यात् = one should know; वायुना = by Vāyu.
questions.teaches: Flank pain and twisting complete the signs by which the sneha is known to be covered by Vāyu.
questions.section: वायु से आवृत स्नेह और उपचार

questions.q: Which is the right split of विद्याद्वायुना?
optionExplain: द्वायुना is not a word.
The verb ends in a consonant, -त्.
Right: त् becomes द् before a voiced sound such as व.
A visarga after आ would drop before व, not become द्.
questions.explain: विद्यात् (one should know) + वायुना (by Vāyu).
questions.rule: त् → द् before a voiced consonant.
questions.section: वायु से आवृत स्नेह और उपचार

questions.q: The sneha is covered by Vāyu. Which set of qualities does line 2 give for the remedy?
optionExplain: Sweet and bitter are not named in this unit.
These tastes are not named in this unit.
Line 2 says unctuous and hot, the opposite of cold and dry.
Right: स्निग्धाम्ललवणोष्णैः.
questions.explain: स्निग्ध-अम्ल-लवण-उष्ण: unctuous, sour, salty, hot.
questions.section: वायु से आवृत स्नेह और उपचार

questions.q: Like विद्यात् (one should know), which form of √दा means one should give?
optionExplain: Right: The optative 'one should' of these roots ends in -यात्: विद्यात्, दद्यात्.
This is 'he gives', the present.
This is 'given', a past participle.
This is 'he will give', the future.
questions.explain: विद्यात् is a 3rd person singular optative: 'one should know'.
questions.teaches: The 3rd person singular optative of roots such as √विद् and √दा ends in -यात् (विद्यात्, दद्यात्): 'one should'.
questions.section: वायु से आवृत स्नेह और उपचार

questions.q: With which kind of enema does the unit say to expel the covered sneha?
optionExplain: The oil enema comes in unit 7.
Right: निरूहैः निर्हरेत्: expel with nirūhas.
No such enema is named here.
Nothing nasal is named here.
questions.explain: निरूहैः = with decoction enemas (nirūha).
questions.section: वायु से आवृत स्नेह और उपचार

questions.q: Put the five ingredients of the compound in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The compound runs: sour gruel, surā, kola, horse gram, barley; then साधित (prepared).
questions.section: वायु से आवृत स्नेह और उपचार

questions.q: Match each ingredient to its meaning on the card.
questions.explain: sauvīraka, kulattha and yava are standard identifications; kola is probable.
questions.rule: सौवीरक = sour gruel; कुलत्थ = horse gram; यव = barley; कोल = probably jujube.
questions.teaches: The nirūhas are prepared with sour gruel, surā, kola (probably jujube), horse gram and barley.
questions.section: वायु से आवृत स्नेह और उपचार

questions.q: What does समूत्रैः add to the nirūhas?
optionExplain: Honey is not named; मूत्र is urine.
Sour gruel is सौवीरक, a different word.
Right: स-मूत्र: 'together with urine'.
स- means 'with'; 'without' would be a- or nir-.
questions.explain: समूत्रैः = with urine (स + मूत्र).
questions.section: वायु से आवृत स्नेह और उपचार

questions.q: A sneha covered by Vāyu will not come out. Which of these does the unit name among the nirūha ingredients?
optionExplain: Milk is not named in this unit.
Sesame oil is not named in this unit.
Ghee is not named in this unit.
Right: कुलत्थ (horse gram; standard) is in the compound सौवीरक-सुरा-कोल-कुलत्थ-यव-साधितैः.
questions.explain: The nirūhas are prepared with sour gruel, surā, kola, horse gram and barley, with urine and the five roots.
questions.rule: वायु-आवृत स्नेह → सौवीरक, सुरा, कोल, कुलत्थ, यव से साधित निरूह.
questions.section: वायु से आवृत स्नेह और उपचार

questions.q: Like समूत्र (together with urine), which compound means together with oil?
optionExplain: Right: स- + noun = 'together with': स + तैल = सतैल.
अ- means 'without'.
This means 'oil and urine'.
This means 'born of oil'.
questions.explain: समूत्र = स + मूत्र, 'with urine'.
questions.teaches: स- before a noun makes a compound 'together with it' (समूत्र with urine, सतैल with oil).
questions.section: वायु से आवृत स्नेह और उपचार

questions.q: When does the unit say to give the oil enema (anuvāsana)?
options: At dawn, before taking any food
optionExplain: सायम् is evening, and भुक्ते means after eating.
Right: सायं भुक्ते: in the evening, when one has eaten.
The unit says evening and after eating.
Sleep is not named; सायम् is evening.
questions.explain: सायम् = in the evening; भुक्ते = when (one) has eaten.
questions.section: वायु से आवृत स्नेह और उपचार

questions.q: Match each word of line 1 to its meaning.
pairs: one should give an oil enema
questions.explain: These words give the time, the condition, the act and the means.
questions.rule: सायम् = evening; भुक्ते = having eaten; अनुवासयेत् = give an anuvāsana; तैलाभ्याम् = with two oils.
questions.section: वायु से आवृत स्नेह और उपचार

questions.q: Put these signs of line 2 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: After thirst and burning (print तृडदाह, read तृड्दाह) the compound runs: redness, bewilderment, discolouration, tamaka, fever.
questions.rule: (तृट् · दाह ·) राग · संमोह · वैवर्ण्य · तमक · ज्वर.
questions.teaches: Line 2 lists thirst, burning, redness, bewilderment, discolouration, tamaka and fever; unit 8 ties them to Pitta.
questions.section: वायु से आवृत स्नेह और उपचार

questions.q: ताभ्याम् ... तैलाभ्याम् is dual. What does the dual tell here?
optionExplain: The dual counts the oils, not the uses.
Many would be plural (तैलैः).
Right: -आभ्याम् is the dual instrumental: 'with those two oils'.
Urine is not named in this line.
questions.explain: ताभ्याम् तैलाभ्याम् = with those two oils.
questions.section: वायु से आवृत स्नेह और उपचार

questions.q: In the list of line 2, what does वैवर्ण्य mean?
optionExplain: That is संमोह.
That is राग.
That is दाह, burning.
Right: वैवर्ण्य = loss of normal colour, discolouration.
questions.explain: वैवर्ण्य comes from वि-वर्ण, 'off-colour'.
questions.section: वायु से आवृत स्नेह और उपचार

questions.q: Like अनुवासयेत् (one should give an oil enema), which form of √पा means one should make him drink?
optionExplain: Right: A causative optative ends in -अयेत्: अनुवासयेत्, पाययेत्.
This is 'one should drink', not 'make drink'.
This is 'he makes drink', the present.
This is 'drunk', a past participle.
questions.explain: अनुवासयेत् is the causative optative: 'one should cause to be given an oil enema'.
questions.teaches: A causative optative ends in -अयेत् (अनुवासयेत्, पाययेत्): 'one should make (it) happen'.
questions.section: वायु से आवृत स्नेह और उपचार

questions.q: With enemas of which tastes is the Pitta-covered sneha removed?
optionExplain: Sour and salty belong to the Vāyu remedy (unit 5).
Right: स्वादुतिक्तैः बस्तिभिः: with sweet and bitter enemas.
These are not named in this unit.
These are not named in this unit.
questions.explain: स्वादु = sweet; तिक्त = bitter.
questions.section: पित्त, कफ, अतिभोजन से आवृत स्नेह

questions.q: Put these signs of line 2 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The compound runs: drowsiness, (cold, fever,) lassitude, praseka, aversion, heaviness.
questions.section: पित्त, कफ, अतिभोजन से आवृत स्नेह

questions.q: Match each word of line 1 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Line 1 gives the diagnosis and then the remedy.
questions.rule: विद्यात् = know; पित्तावृतम् = covered by Pitta; बस्तिभिः = with enemas; हरेत् = remove.
questions.teaches: Line 1: know the sneha as covered by Pitta, and remove it with sweet and bitter enemas.
questions.section: पित्त, कफ, अतिभोजन से आवृत स्नेह

questions.q: Which is the right split of स्वादुतिक्तैस्तम्?
optionExplain: स्तम् is not a word here; the pronoun is तम्.
These pieces are not words.
Right: A visarga becomes स् before त: -ऐः + तम् = -ऐस्तम्.
The adjective is instrumental plural, agreeing with बस्तिभिः.
questions.explain: स्वादुतिक्तैः (with sweet and bitter) + तम् (it).
questions.section: पित्त, कफ, अतिभोजन से आवृत स्नेह

questions.q: After an unctuous enema there are redness, bewilderment and discolouration (unit 7). What does this unit then say to do?
options: Give a nirūha with urine and with barley
Give the two oils in the evening
Wait and give nothing more at all
Remove it with sweet and bitter enemas
optionExplain: That is the Vāyu remedy of unit 6.
That is the Vāyu remedy of unit 7.
The unit says to remove it (हरेत्).
Right: These are the signs of the Pitta covering; its remedy is स्वादुतिक्त बस्ति.
questions.explain: विद्यात् पित्तावृतम् ... स्वादुतिक्तैः तं बस्तिभिः हरेत्.
questions.section: पित्त, कफ, अतिभोजन से आवृत स्नेह

questions.q: Join a new example, रसैः + तु, as one word. Which is right?
optionExplain: Right: Visarga becomes स् before त, as in स्वादुतिक्तैस्तम्.
र् comes before a voiced sound, but त is voiceless.
The visarga does not simply drop here.
ष् comes before ट, not before त.
questions.explain: Same rule as स्वादुतिक्तैः + तम् = स्वादुतिक्तैस्तम्.
questions.teaches: A visarga before त becomes स् (स्वादुतिक्तैः + तम् = स्वादुतिक्तैस्तम्; रसैः + तु = रसैस्तु).
questions.section: पित्त, कफ, अतिभोजन से आवृत स्नेह

questions.q: With fainting and exhaustion, by what does the unit say the sneha is covered?
optionExplain: Covering by Vāyu was in unit 5.
Right: श्लेष्मणा स्नेहावृतम्: the sneha covered by Kapha.
Covering by Pitta was in unit 8.
Stool is not named in this unit.
questions.explain: श्लेष्मन् is a word for Kapha; श्लेष्मणा = by Kapha.
questions.rule: मूर्च्छा + ग्लानि → कफ से आवृत स्नेह.
questions.section: पित्त, कफ, अतिभोजन से आवृत स्नेह

questions.q: Put these words of line 2 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Line 2 runs: astringent, bitter, pungent; prepared with surā and urine.
questions.section: पित्त, कफ, अतिभोजन से आवृत स्नेह

questions.q: Match each word of line 2 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Three tastes, and the word for how the enemas are made.
questions.rule: कषाय = astringent; तिक्त = bitter; कटुक = pungent; उपसाधित = prepared.
questions.teaches: The Kapha remedy begins with astringent, bitter and pungent (things), prepared with surā and urine.
questions.section: पित्त, कफ, अतिभोजन से आवृत स्नेह

questions.q: Which is the right split of विद्याच्छ्लेष्मणा?
optionExplain: च्छ्लेष्मणा is not a word.
विद्याच् is not a word; the verb is विद्यात्.
Right: त् + श gives च्छ: विद्यात् + श्लेष्मणा = विद्याच्छ्लेष्मणा.
The word is श्लेष्मन्; the छ comes from श by sandhi.
questions.explain: विद्यात् (one should know) + श्लेष्मणा (by Kapha).
questions.section: पित्त, कफ, अतिभोजन से आवृत स्नेह

questions.q: Here कषाय stands beside तिक्त and कटुक. Which sense does the card give it?
optionExplain: That is the preparation sense; here it qualifies substances with other tastes.
No colour is meant here.
The enemas are named in unit 10 (बस्तिभिः).
Right: Beside two tastes, कषाय is the taste astringent (कसैला).
questions.explain: कषाय-तिक्त-कटुक: astringent, bitter, pungent.
questions.rule: कषाय as taste = astringent (कसैला); as preparation = decoction.
questions.section: पित्त, कफ, अतिभोजन से आवृत स्नेह

questions.q: Join a new example, तत् + शरीरम् (that body), as one word. Which is right?
optionExplain: Right: त् + श gives च्छ, as in विद्याच्छ्लेष्मणा.
त् → द् happens before voiced sounds; श is voiceless.
Here the sandhi is not left undone; त् + श → च्छ.
त् → ज् happens before voiced ज/झ; here श gives च्छ.
questions.explain: Same rule as विद्यात् + श्लेष्मणा = विद्याच्छ्लेष्मणा.
questions.teaches: त् before श becomes च्, and the श usually becomes छ (विद्यात् + श्लेष्मणा = विद्याच्छ्लेष्मणा; तत् + शरीरम् = तच्छरीरम्).
questions.section: पित्त, कफ, अतिभोजन से आवृत स्नेह

questions.q: Which word of line 1 says what is to be done with the sneha?
optionExplain: This is 'with enemas', the means.
Right: विनिर्हरेत् = one should expel completely.
This is 'with sour (things)'.
This is 'joined with', describing the enemas.
questions.explain: The verb of line 1 is विनिर्हरेत्, an optative: 'one should expel completely'.
questions.section: पित्त, कफ, अतिभोजन से आवृत स्नेह

questions.q: Put these signs of line 2 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The compound runs: vomiting, fainting, aversion, exhaustion, pain, sleep, and then aching of the limbs.
questions.rule: छर्दि · मूर्च्छा · अरुचि · ग्लानि · शूल · निद्रा (· अङ्गमर्दन).
questions.section: पित्त, कफ, अतिभोजन से आवृत स्नेह

questions.q: Match each sign of line 2 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four of the signs that begin the list of covering by over-eating.
questions.rule: छर्दि = vomiting; अरुचि = aversion; ग्लानि = exhaustion; निद्रा = sleep.
questions.teaches: Line 2 lists vomiting, fainting, aversion, exhaustion, pain, sleep and aching of the limbs; unit 11 ties them to over-eating.
questions.section: पित्त, कफ, अतिभोजन से आवृत स्नेह

questions.q: Which is the right split of साम्लैर्बस्तिभिः?
optionExplain: र्बस्तिभिः is not a word.
अस्तिभिः is not the word; it is बस्तिभिः.
Right: A visarga after ऐ becomes र् before a voiced sound such as ब.
The adjective is instrumental plural, agreeing with बस्तिभिः.
questions.explain: साम्लैः (with sour) + बस्तिभिः (with enemas).
questions.rule: Visarga (after a vowel other than अ/आ) + voiced → र्.
questions.section: पित्त, कफ, अतिभोजन से आवृत स्नेह

questions.q: Fainting and exhaustion show a Kapha covering (unit 9). With which enemas does this unit expel it?
options: Enemas that are sweet and bitter
Nirūhas with barley and with horse gram
The two oils, given in the evening
Enemas with fruit, oil and sour things
optionExplain: That is the Pitta remedy of unit 8.
That is the Vāyu remedy of unit 6.
That is the Vāyu remedy of unit 7.
Right: फलतैलयुतैः साम्लैः बस्तिभिः.
questions.explain: Kapha covering → enemas joined with fruit and oil, with sour things.
questions.section: पित्त, कफ, अतिभोजन से आवृत स्नेह

questions.q: Like स + अम्ल = साम्ल (with sour), join स + अग्नि (with fire). Which is right?
optionExplain: Right: अ + अ gives आ: स + अग्नि = साग्नि, as स + अम्ल = साम्ल.
The two अ do not shrink to one short अ.
ए comes from अ + इ, not अ + अ.
व् comes from उ, not from अ.
questions.explain: Same rule as साम्ल.
questions.teaches: स- before a word beginning with अ gives सा- (स + अम्ल = साम्ल; स + अग्नि = साग्नि).
questions.section: पित्त, कफ, अतिभोजन से आवृत स्नेह

questions.q: What does आम mean on this card?
options: A kind of sour fermented gruel
optionExplain: In Hindi आम is also mango, but here it is the undigested state.
Right: आम here is the raw, undigested state, not the fruit.
That is सौवीरक, in unit 6.
That is अनुवासन, in unit 7.
questions.explain: आमलिङ्गैः = by the signs of āma (the raw, undigested state).
questions.section: पित्त, कफ, अतिभोजन से आवृत स्नेह

questions.q: Put these words of the unit in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Line 1 gives the signs and the diagnosis; line 2 the pungents, the powders and the digestive.
questions.rule: आमलिङ्गैः · विद्यात् · अत्यशनावृतम् · कटूनाम् · चूर्णैः · पाचनम्.
questions.section: पित्त, कफ, अतिभोजन से आवृत स्नेह

questions.q: Match each word of the unit to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words carry the diagnosis and the first remedy.
questions.rule: अत्यशन = over-eating; पाचन = digestive; चूर्ण = powder; लवण = salt.
questions.teaches: For the sneha covered by over-eating, the first remedy is a digestive of decoctions and powders of pungents and salts.
questions.section: पित्त, कफ, अतिभोजन से आवृत स्नेह

questions.q: Which is the right split of विद्यादत्यशनावृतम्?
optionExplain: दत्य and शन are not words.
अत्य, शना and वृतम् are not the words here.
Right: त् → द् before a vowel; इ + अ → य; अ + आ → आ.
Inside the compound अशन has no visarga.
questions.explain: विद्यात् (one should know) + अति-अशन-आवृतम् (covered by over-eating).
questions.rule: त् + vowel → द्; इ + अ → य; अ + आ → आ.
questions.section: पित्त, कफ, अतिभोजन से आवृत स्नेह

questions.q: The sneha is covered by over-eating. What does line 2 give for it?
options: Sweet and bitter enemas, with nothing given before them
An oil enema in the evening after food
Nirūhas with sour gruel and with urine
A digestive (pācana) of pungents and salts
optionExplain: That is the Pitta remedy of unit 8.
That is the Vāyu remedy of unit 7.
That is the Vāyu remedy of unit 6.
Right: कटूनां लवणानां च ... पाचनम्: a digestive of pungent things and salts, as powders and (probably) decoctions.
questions.explain: Over-eating covering → first a digestive (pācana).
questions.section: पित्त, कफ, अतिभोजन से आवृत स्नेह

questions.q: Like कटूनाम् (of the pungent ones), which form of बस्ति means of the enemas?
optionExplain: Right: The genitive plural of an -इ/-उ stem lengthens the vowel and adds -नाम्: कटूनाम्, बस्तीनाम्.
This is 'with enemas', the instrumental.
This is 'in the enema', the locative singular.
This is 'enemas', the nominative plural.
questions.explain: कटूनाम् = कटु + genitive plural -ऊनाम्.
questions.teaches: The genitive plural of -इ and -उ stems ends in -ईनाम् / -ऊनाम् (कटूनाम्, बस्तीनाम्): 'of the ...'.
questions.section: पित्त, कफ, अतिभोजन से आवृत स्नेह

questions.q: What does मृदुविरेकः mean?
optionExplain: विरेक is purgation, and मृदु is mild, not strong.
Right: मृदु = mild, विरेक = purgation: a karmadhāraya.
The oil enema is अनुवासन, not विरेक.
The digestive (पाचन) is in verse 11.
questions.explain: मृदु-विरेकः = mild purgation, named beside the digestive of verse 11.

questions.q: Put these words of line 1 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Line 1: a mild purgation; and everything there prescribed for āma is beneficial.

questions.q: Match each clear sign word of line 2 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are the sure parts of the list; the stretch after 'wind' is unreadable.
questions.rule: विट् = stool; गुरुत्व = heaviness; आध्मान = distension; हृद्ग्रह = seizing of the heart.
questions.teaches: Line 2 begins the signs of the sneha covered by stool: stool, urine, wind, heaviness, distension, hṛdgraha.

questions.q: Which is the right split of तत्रामविहितम्?
optionExplain: Neither तत्रा nor मविहितम् is a word.
A final म् does not vanish before a vowel.
Right: अ + आ → आ: तत्र + आम → तत्राम.
त् before र would turn to द्: तद्राम, not तत्राम.
questions.explain: तत्र (there) + आम-विहितम् (prescribed for āma).

questions.q: A sneha is covered by over-eating; verse 11 named a digestive. What does this verse add?
options: A sharp enema with arka-leaf oil
Nirūha cooked with urine, śyāmā, trivṛt
Enemas that are sweet and bitter
A mild purgation and the āma measures
optionExplain: That is the treatment of verse 19, for unripe sneha.
That is verse 16, for the sneha that runs upward.
That is verse 8, for the Pitta covering.
Right: मृदुविरेकः सर्वं च तत्रामविहितं हितम्.
questions.explain: Over-eating covering: the digestive (verse 11), and also mild purgation and all that is prescribed for āma.

questions.q: Like मृदु + विरेक = मृदुविरेक (a mild purgation), what does मृदुबस्ति mean?
optionExplain: Right: Adjective first, noun second (karmadhāraya): मृदु बस्ति = a mild enema.
That would be a dvandva of two nouns; मृदु here describes बस्ति.
Nothing in the compound names a person.
There is no negative in the compound.
questions.explain: मृदु describes the noun that follows it, as in मृदुविरेक.
questions.teaches: In a karmadhāraya the first member describes the second: मृदुविरेक = mild purgation, मृदुबस्ति = mild enema.

questions.q: In विडावृतम्, what covers the sneha?
optionExplain: The card says viḍ here is stool, not the drug name.
Right: विट् + आवृतम्: covered by stool (विट्).
The wind covering was verses 5 and 6.
The Kapha covering was verses 9 and 10.
questions.explain: विडावृत = viṭ-āvṛta, covered by stool.

questions.q: Put these phrases in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Diagnosis first, then the means: sneha and sweating, enemas, nirūhas cooked with śyāmā and bilva, with anuvāsanas.
questions.rule: ज्ञात्वा · स्नेहस्वेदैः · सबस्तिभिः · श्यामाबिल्वादिसिद्धैः · निरूहैः · सानुवासनैः.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: The means named for the stool-covered sneha.
questions.rule: स्वेद = sweating; निरूह = decoction enema; अनुवासन = oil enema; सिद्ध = cooked.
questions.teaches: The stool-covered sneha is met with sneha and sweating, enemas, and nirūhas with anuvāsanas.

questions.q: What does ज्ञात्वा tell us?
options: One should know: an order to the reader
Having known: first know, then treat
To know: the purpose of the treatment
optionExplain: That is the optative विद्यात्, as in verse 11.
That would be the participle ज्ञात, not ज्ञात्वा.
Right: -त्वा is the absolutive: the knowing comes before the treatment.
That would be the infinitive ज्ञातुम्.
questions.explain: ज्ञात्वा = having known (absolutive of √ज्ञा).

questions.q: A sneha enema stays in with heaviness and distension, the signs of verse 12. Which means does this verse name?
options: A digestive of pungent and salt decoctions and powders
Enemas with fruit, oil and sour things
Actions that destroy vomiting, for the sneha at the throat
Sneha and sweating, enemas, nirūhas with anuvāsanas
optionExplain: That is verse 11, for the over-eating covering.
That is verse 10, for the Kapha covering.
That is verse 17, for the sneha coming up.
Right: स्नेहस्वेदैः सबस्तिभिः ... निरूहैः सानुवासनैः.
questions.explain: Signs of verse 12 → stool covering → the means of this verse.

questions.q: Like सबस्तिभिः (together with enemas), what does सतैलः, said of a nirūha, mean?
optionExplain: Right: स- = 'with' at the head of a bahuvrīhi: स-तैल = having oil with it.
Without oil would need a negative such as निस्- or अ-.
स- adds a companion; it does not say 'only'.
A hundred is शत, not the prefix स-.
questions.explain: स- + noun = together with that noun (सबस्ति, सानुवासन).
questions.teaches: The prefix स- makes a bahuvrīhi 'together with X': सबस्ति, सानुवासन, सतैल.

questions.q: What does निर्हरेत् mean?
optionExplain: Retaining is the opposite of निर्-हृ, taking out.
Right: निर्हरेत् is the optative of निर्-√हृ: one should take out, expel.
Cooking is सिद्ध / साधित, not निर्हरेत्.
That would be पाययेत्.
questions.explain: निर्हरेद्विधिना = निर्हरेत् (one should expel) + विधिना (by the rule).

questions.q: Put these words in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Line 1 finishes the removal; line 2 lists the three persons.
questions.rule: निर्हरेत् · विधिना · सम्यक् · उदावर्तहरेण · अभुक्ते · शूनपायौ · पेयामात्राशितस्य.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Line 2 names three persons; line 1 says the removal follows the rule.
questions.rule: अभुक्त = not having eaten; शूनपायु = swollen anus; पेया = thin gruel; विधि = rule.
questions.teaches: Line 2 lists the persons in whom the next case arises: the unfed, the one with a swollen anus, and the one fed only peyā.

questions.q: Which is the right split of निर्हरेद्विधिना?
optionExplain: द्विधिना is not a word.
A vowel-final word would leave no द्: it would read निर्हरेत विधिना.
Right: त् → द् before the voiced व.
इधिना is not a word; the word is विधिना.
questions.explain: निर्हरेत् (one should expel) + विधिना (by the rule).

questions.q: Which persons does line 2 name?
options: One who has eaten only thin gruel
One who has eaten heavy food
optionExplain: Fever is not named in this line.
Right: शूनपायौ.
Right: पेयामात्राशितस्य.
Not named; heavy (गुरु) sneha after over-eating was verse 3.
Right: अभुक्ते.
questions.explain: अभुक्ते शूनपायौ वा पेयामात्राशितस्य वा: three persons.

questions.q: Like अभुक्ते (in one who has not eaten), which form means in one who has eaten?
optionExplain: This is the genitive: of one who has eaten.
This is the instrumental: by one who has eaten.
This is nominative/accusative neuter or accusative masculine, not the locative.
Right: Drop the negative अ-: भुक्ते, locative singular, as in verse 7 (सायं भुक्ते).
questions.explain: अ- negates; -ए marks the locative singular of an -अ stem.
questions.rule: अ-भुक्ते = in one not having eaten; भुक्ते = in one having eaten.
questions.teaches: The prefix अ- negates a participle (अभुक्त = not having eaten), and the locative in -ए says 'in such a person'.

questions.q: Where is the sneha placed (प्रणिहितः) in line 1?
optionExplain: Right: गुदे = in the anus (locative).
The mouth is not named in line 1.
The nose is not named in line 1.
No skin application is named here.
questions.explain: गुदे प्रणिहितः स्नेहः = the sneha placed in the anus.

questions.q: Put these words of line 1 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Line 1: in the anus, placed, the sneha, with force, runs, not covered.
questions.rule: गुदे · प्रणिहितः · स्नेहः · वेगात् · धावति · अनावृतः.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Line 1 says how the sneha moves; line 2 opens with the direction.
questions.rule: वेगात् = by force; धावति = rushes; अनावृत = not covered; ऊर्ध्वम् = upward.
questions.teaches: An uncovered sneha, placed in the anus of the persons of verse 14, rushes with force, upward.

questions.q: Which is the right split of वेगाद्धावत्यनावृतः?
optionExplain: वेगा and द्धावति are not words.
Right: त् + ध → द्ध; इ + अ → य.
हावति is not the verb; the verb is धावति.
वेगद् and धावत्य are not words.
questions.explain: वेगात् (by force) + धावति (runs) + अनावृतः (not covered).
questions.rule: त् + ध → द्ध; इ + अ → य.

questions.q: A sneha enema is given to one who has not eaten, so nothing covers it. What does line 1 say happens?
options: It stays and coats the anus
It comes out with the stool
It is digested in the belly
optionExplain: Coating the anus is said of the unripe sneha, verse 18.
Line 1 says nothing of stool.
Right: वेगाद्धावत्यनावृतः: not covered, it runs with force.
Line 1 says it runs, not that it is digested.
questions.explain: Uncovered sneha in the persons of verse 14 → it rushes with force.
questions.rule: अनावृत स्नेह → वेग से दौड़ता है.

questions.q: Like अन् + आवृत = अनावृत (not covered), what is अन् + आहार (no food)?
optionExplain: The long आ of आहार must stay.
That is अन्न + आहार, food-eating, a different word.
ओ would come from अ + उ, not from अन् + आ.
Right: अन्- before a vowel joins straight on: अन् + आ → अना.
questions.explain: अन्- is the negative before a vowel: अनावृत, अनाहार.
questions.rule: अ- before a consonant, अन्- before a vowel.
questions.teaches: The negative is अ- before a consonant (अभुक्त) and अन्- before a vowel (अनावृत, अनाहार).

questions.q: What kind of enema does this verse say should be given (देयः स्यात्)?
options: A nirūha, together with an anuvāsana
An anuvāsana alone in the evening
A mild purgation with āma measures
A sharp enema with arka-leaf oil
optionExplain: Right: देयः स्यान्निरूहः सानुवासनः.
The verse joins a nirūha with the anuvāsana.
That is verse 12, for the over-eating covering.
That is verse 19, for unripe sneha.
questions.explain: निरूहः सानुवासनः = a decoction enema together with an oil enema.

questions.q: Put the ingredients in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: First what it is cooked with (urine, śyāmā, trivṛt), then what it has (yava, kola, kulattha).
questions.rule: मूत्र · श्यामा · त्रिवृत् ‖ यव · कोल · कुलत्थ.

questions.q: Match each ingredient to its rendering on the card.
questions.explain: Trivṛt is Operculina turpethum (standard); kola is probably jujube; kulattha horse gram; yava barley.
questions.rule: त्रिवृत् = turpeth; कोल = probably jujube; कुलत्थ = horse gram; यव = barley.
questions.teaches: The nirūha for the upward-running sneha is cooked with urine, śyāmā and trivṛt and has yava, kola and kulattha.

questions.q: Which is the right split of स्यान्निरूहः?
optionExplain: न्निरूहः is not a word.
Right: त् + न → न्न: the त् becomes the nasal before न.
इरूहः is not a word; the word is निरूहः.
अ + अ would give आ, and अनिरूह is not in the verse.
questions.explain: स्यात् (should be) + निरूहः (a decoction enema).

questions.q: A physician prepares the nirūha of this verse. Which of these does the verse say it has (-वान्)?
optionExplain: Right: कोल is in the same compound.
Right: यव is in यवकोलकुलत्थवान्.
Not here: बिल्व is in verse 13.
Not here: सौवीरक is in verse 6.
Right: कुलत्थ closes the compound before -वान्.
questions.explain: यव-कोल-कुलत्थ-वान् = having yava, kola and kulattha.

questions.q: Like यवकोलकुलत्थवान् (having yava, kola and kulattha), what does तैलवान् mean?
optionExplain: -वत् adds possession, not lack.
-वत् does not name an agent.
Right: The suffix -वत् (nominative -वान्) means 'having, possessing'.
Cooked would be सिद्ध, as in तत्सिद्धतैल.
questions.explain: -वान् = having: यवकोलकुलत्थवान्, तैलवान्.
questions.teaches: The possessive suffix -वत्, masculine nominative -वान्, means 'having': तैलवान् = having oil.

questions.q: What should one bring about for the sneha coming from the throat?
options: Its mixing with the next meal
optionExplain: The verse says turning back, not expulsion upward.
Cooking with urine is the nirūha of verse 16.
No meal is named in this verse.
Right: तस्य कुर्यान्निवर्तनम्: one should bring about its turning back.
questions.explain: निवर्तनम् = turning back.

questions.q: Put these words in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: From the throat, of (it) coming ... with anti-vomiting actions, its, one should do, turning back.
questions.rule: कण्ठात् · आगच्छतः · छर्दिघ्नीभिः · क्रियाभिः · तस्य · कुर्यात् · निवर्तनम्.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: The clear words of the remedy for the sneha coming up from the throat.
questions.rule: कण्ठ = throat; छर्दि = vomiting; क्रिया = action; निवर्तन = turning back.
questions.teaches: For the sneha coming from the throat the aim is its turning back, with actions that destroy vomiting among the means.

questions.q: Which word says that the actions are meant to stop vomiting?
optionExplain: Right: छर्दि-घ्नीभिः = destroying vomiting, describing क्रियाभिः.
This means 'with actions', not which kind.
This is the aim, turning back.
This is 'of (it) coming'.
questions.explain: छर्दिघ्नी (f., agreeing with क्रिया) = that destroys vomiting.

questions.q: The sneha of an enema is coming up from the throat. Which means does line 2 name for turning it back?
options: Enemas that are sweet and bitter
Nirūhas cooked with bilva and śyāmā
optionExplain: That is verse 8, for the Pitta covering.
Right: छर्दिघ्नीभिः क्रियाभिश्च.
That is verse 11, for the over-eating covering.
That is verse 13, for the stool covering.
