A fraction would be अष्टमांश.
questions.explain: Number + -क = a group of that many: पञ्चक, अष्टक.
questions.teaches: पञ्चक = a group of five (number + -क makes a group).

questions.q: What does अनुवासयेत् ask the physician to do?
optionExplain: The decoction enema (nirūha) was given before.
Right: अनुवासयेत् = should give anuvāsana, an oil enema.
A suppository is फलवर्ति (unit 51).
The broth is the meal, given before the anuvāsana.
questions.explain: ततोऽनुवासयेत् = then one should give anuvāsana.

questions.q: Put the steps of line 1 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: After nirūha, a meal with dhanva-rasa, then anuvāsana with nikumbha oil.

questions.q: Match each item to what the card says of it.
questions.explain: Line 1 gives the meal and the oil; line 2 names drugs of the next formula.
questions.rule: धन्वरस = probably dry-land meat broth; निकुम्भतैल = oil for anuvāsana; बला = country mallow; कृतमालक = Indian laburnum.
questions.teaches: After nirūha: a meal with dhanva-rasa, then anuvāsana with nikumbha oil.

questions.q: Which split is right for ततोऽनुवासयेत्?
optionExplain: अ + अ would give आ: ततानुवासयेत्.
नुवासयेत् is not a word.
Right: -अः + अ → -ओऽ (the अ is marked by ऽ).
म् before a vowel would give ततमनुवासयेत्.
questions.explain: ततः (then) + अनुवासयेत् (should give an oil enema).

questions.q: From कृतमालकात् फलम्, which part of kṛtamālaka is taken?
optionExplain: मूल is not said with कृतमालक.
Bark is not named in the verse.
Leaves are not named in the verse.
Right: कृतमालकात् फलम् = the fruit from kṛtamālaka.
questions.explain: Ablative of source: कृतमालकात् (from kṛtamālaka) फलम् (fruit).
questions.rule: Ablative + part = the part from that plant.

questions.q: Like कृतमालकात् फलम् (the fruit from kṛtamālaka), what does a new phrase बिल्वात् मूलम् mean?
optionExplain: Right: Ablative of source: बिल्वात् = from bilva; मूलम् = root.
And would need च, and both in the same case.
For would need the dative बिल्वाय.
In would need the locative बिल्वे.
questions.explain: Ablative + part = the part taken from that plant.
questions.teaches: The ablative names the source of a part: कृतमालकात् फलम् = the fruit from kṛtamālaka.

questions.q: In what are barley and horse gram boiled?
optionExplain: Urine belongs to the list of verse 52.
Right: पचेज्जले = should boil in water (जले).
Milk is not named in this verse.
Oil is added with ghee later; the boiling is in water.
questions.explain: यवान्कुलत्थांश्च पचेज्जले.

questions.q: Match each drug to the name the card gives.
questions.explain: Barley and horse gram are boiled in water; musta and indrayava go into the paste.
questions.rule: यव = barley; कुलत्थ = horse gram; मुस्त = nut-grass; इन्द्रयव = kurchi seed; जल = water.

questions.q: Put the gifts of this rasa in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: बल-पुष्टि-वर्ण-दः: giving strength, nourishment and complexion.
questions.teaches: The rasa gives strength, nourishment and complexion (बलपुष्टिवर्णदः).

questions.q: Which split is right for पचेज्जले?
optionExplain: ज्जले is not a word; the word is जले.
A visarga after ए before ज would give पचेर्जले.
Right: त् + ज → ज्ज.
No change would happen: पचेतजले.
questions.explain: पचेत् (should boil) + जले (in water).

questions.q: What does कल्कवान् (having a paste) describe?
optionExplain: जले is locative; कल्कवान् is nominative.
यवान् is accusative plural; कल्कवान् is nominative singular.
Rock salt is named only in line 2.
Right: रसः ... कल्कवान्: the rasa has a paste; both masculine nominative.
questions.explain: रसः समुस्तपाठेन्द्रयवैश्च कल्कवान्: the rasa, with musta, pāṭhā and indrayava, has a paste.
questions.rule: Agreement shows what an adjective describes.

questions.q: Like बलपुष्टिवर्णद (giving strength, nourishment, complexion), what does a new compound सुखद mean?
optionExplain: Right: -द at the end of a compound = giving.
Taking away would be -हर or -घ्न.
Born of would be -ज.
Without would be निः- or अ- in front.
questions.explain: Noun + -द = giving that noun.
questions.teaches: -द at the end of a compound means 'giving': बलपुष्टिवर्णद, सुखद.

questions.q: For whom does line 2 say these bastis are beneficial?
optionExplain: The aged are named in unit 56, not here.
Right: शिशोर्हितः = beneficial for a child (शिशु).
No pregnant woman is named in the verse.
Strength is not the subject of line 2.
questions.explain: शिशोः हितः = beneficial for a child.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
pairs: to be given as oil enema
questions.explain: Line 1: what is to be given as anuvāsana, prepared with madhuka ... or śatāhvayā. Line 2: for a child.
questions.rule: अनुवास्य = to be given as oil enema; साधित = prepared; अथवा = or; शिशु = child.

questions.q: What does अलवणः say about the rasa in a child's nirūhaṇa?
optionExplain: Five salts are in the formula of verse 52.
Rock salt is in the formula of verse 54.
Right: अ-लवण = without salt.
अ- negates लवण: no salt.
questions.explain: निरूहणे च अलवणः: and in nirūhaṇa, the one without salt.
questions.teaches: For a child: in anuvāsana the rasa with jīvanīya drugs; in nirūhaṇa the rasa without salt.

questions.q: Put these parts of line 2 in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: With jīvanīya, the rasa in anuvāsana; in nirūhaṇa, and without salt; beneficial for a child.

questions.q: A child is to be treated with bastis. Which pairings does line 2 call beneficial?
options: Anuvāsana: the rasa with jīvanīya drugs
Nirūhaṇa: the rasa with five salts
optionExplain: Right: निरूहणे चालवणः.
Nikumbha oil belongs to verse 53; line 2 does not name it.
Right: सजीवनीयस्तु रसोऽनुवासने.
Without salt is said of the nirūhaṇa, not the anuvāsana.
Line 2 says the opposite: without salt.
questions.explain: Anuvāsana → with jīvanīya; nirūhaṇa → without salt.
questions.rule: Child: anuvāsana with jīvanīya rasa; nirūhaṇa without salt.

questions.q: Like निरूहणे (in the decoction enema, locative -ए), what does a new form वमने mean?
optionExplain: By would be the instrumental वमनेन.
From would be the ablative वमनात्.
Of would be the genitive वमनस्य.
Right: -ए is the locative singular of an अ-stem: in, during.
questions.explain: अ-stem locative singular -ए = in: अनुवासने, निरूहणे, वमने.
questions.teaches: अनुवासने, निरूहणे are locatives: in the oil enema, in the decoction enema.

questions.q: In what, says unit 56, does nothing else match nirūha basti?
optionExplain: Right: आश्वङ्गबलाभिवर्धनम् = quickly increasing the strength of the limbs.
The head and eyes are not named here.
Cooling is not named here.
Wounds are not named here.
questions.explain: न चान्यदाश्वङ्गबलाभिवर्धनं निरूहबस्तेः.
questions.rule: Nirūha basti = the quick increaser of strength.

questions.q: Put these parts of unit 56 in their order.
questions.explain: Not any other quick increaser of bodily strength than nirūha basti; beneficial to those neither child nor aged.
questions.rule: न च अन्यत् · आश्वङ्गबलाभिवर्धनम् · निरूहबस्तेः · अशिशुवृद्धयोः · हितम्.

questions.q: Match each member to its meaning.
questions.explain: आशु-अङ्ग-बल-अभिवर्धनम् = quickly increasing the strength of the limbs.
questions.rule: आशु = quick; अङ्ग = limb; बल = strength; अभिवर्धन = increasing; अन्यत् = other.
questions.teaches: No other quick increaser of bodily strength exists than nirūha basti.

questions.q: Which split is right for आश्वङ्ग?
optionExplain: अ + अ would give आ: आश्वाङ्ग.
Right: उ → व् before an unlike vowel: आशु + अङ्ग → आश्वङ्ग.
Neither आश् nor वङ्ग is the word here.
इ before अ would give य्: आश्यङ्ग.
questions.explain: आशु (quick) + अङ्ग (limb).

questions.q: What does the ablative निरूहबस्तेः mean with अन्यत्?
optionExplain: Together with would need सह and the instrumental.
Before would need पूर्वम् or प्राक्.
Right: अन्यत् + ablative = other than.
Nothing is made from the basti here.
questions.explain: न च अन्यत् ... निरूहबस्तेः: nothing other than nirūha basti.

questions.q: Like अन्यत् निरूहबस्तेः (other than nirūha basti), what does a new phrase अन्यत् घृतात् mean?
optionExplain: अन्यत् is not a comparative; it means other.
Mixed with would need the instrumental.
Alone would need एव or केवल.
Right: अन्यत् + ablative = other than: other than ghee.
questions.explain: अन्यत् + ablative = other than (not comparison).
questions.teaches: अन्यत् with an ablative means 'other than': अन्यत् निरूहबस्तेः.

questions.q: Which number is this chapter?
optionExplain: Right: सप्तमः = seventh.
Sixth would be षष्ठः.
Eighth would be अष्टमः.
Seventieth would be सप्ततितमः; सप्तम is seventh.
questions.explain: सप्तमोऽध्यायः = the seventh chapter.

questions.q: Match each word of the colophon to its meaning.
questions.explain: स्नेहव्यापत्सिद्धिर्नाम सप्तमोऽध्यायः.
questions.rule: स्नेह = oleation; व्यापत् = complication; सिद्धि = cure; सप्तम = seventh; अध्याय = chapter.

questions.q: Put the members of the chapter title in their order.
questions.explain: स्नेह-व्यापत्-सिद्धि: cure of the complications of oleation.
questions.teaches: The title Sneha-vyāpat-siddhi = cure (siddhi) of the complications (vyāpad) of oleation (sneha).

questions.q: Which split is right for सप्तमोऽध्यायः?
optionExplain: अ + अ would give आ: सप्तमाध्यायः.
Right: -अः + अ → -ओऽ.
ध्यायः is not the word here.
म् before a vowel would give सप्तममध्यायः.
questions.explain: सप्तमः (seventh) + अध्यायः (chapter).

questions.q: Which topic does the chapter title name?
options: Cure of the complications of oleation
optionExplain: Cooking oils is not what the title says.
The title names स्नेह, not वमन.
Right: स्नेह-व्यापत्-सिद्धि: cure of what goes wrong with oleation.
The title names no drugs or seasons.
questions.explain: सिद्धि = cure; व्यापत् = complication; स्नेह = oleation.
questions.rule: Read a tat-puruṣa title from the last member back.

questions.q: Like स्नेहव्यापत्सिद्धिः, what would a new title वमनव्यापत्सिद्धिः mean?
options: Emesis as a cure for complications
Cure of the complications of emesis
optionExplain: The last member सिद्धि is the head: it is a cure, not complications.
व्यापत् means complication, not 'without trouble'.
वमन is the first member, qualifying the rest, not the cure itself.
Right: Read from the end: cure (सिद्धि) of complications (व्यापत्) of emesis (वमन).
questions.explain: In a tat-puruṣa the last member is the head; the earlier ones qualify it.
questions.rule: Tat-puruṣa: the last member is the head.
questions.teaches: Sneha-vyāpat-siddhi is a tat-puruṣa: the last member (siddhi, cure) is the head.

questions.q: What does unit 1 say the chapter will explain?
optionExplain: Right: भेषजकल्पम् = the preparation (kalpa) of medicines (bheṣaja).
The patient is not named in the formula.
Diseases are not named in the formula.
Seasons are not the subject of this line.
questions.explain: अथातो भेषजकल्पं व्याख्यास्यामः = now, therefore, we shall explain the preparation of medicines.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 1 to its meaning.
questions.explain: अथ + अतः open the line; भेषज-कल्प is its subject.
questions.rule: अथ = now; अतः = therefore; भेषज = medicine; कल्प = preparation.

questions.q: Put the words of unit 1 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Opening word, subject, verb: अथातो, भेषजकल्पं, व्याख्यास्यामः.
questions.teaches: The opening formula runs: now-therefore, the subject (accusative), we shall explain.

questions.q: Which is the right split of अथातो?
optionExplain: Neither अथा nor तो is a word of the card.
Right: अ + अ → आ (अथ + अ = अथा-); अतः before the voiced भ of भेषज becomes अतो.
तो is not a word; the second word is अतः.
अथात् and ओ are not words here.
questions.explain: अथातो = अथ (now) + अतः (therefore).
questions.rule: अ + अ → आ; अः before a voiced consonant → ओ.

questions.q: According to the note on the card, what does the chapter go on to treat?
options: Surgery, bandaging and the removal of foreign darts
Daily routine, sleep and the seasons
Land, collection, storage and five forms of preparation
Pulse, tongue and the examination of urine
optionExplain: None of these is named in the note.
These are not named in the note.
Right: The note lists exactly these as the chapter's later topics.
These are not named in the note.
questions.explain: The note: the chapter goes on to land, collection, storage and the five forms of preparation.
questions.rule: भेषजकल्प: भूमि → संग्रह → भण्डारण → पाँच तैयारियाँ (टिप्पणी).

questions.q: Like व्याख्यास्यामः (we shall explain), which form means we shall do (√कृ)?
optionExplain: This is the present: we do.
This is the 3rd person singular: he will do.
This is a past form: (they) did.
Right: 1st person plural future: stem करिष्य- + -आमः, like व्याख्यास्य- + -आमः.
questions.explain: व्याख्यास्यामः is 1 pl. future; the same ending -(इ)ष्यामः / -स्यामः gives करिष्यामः.
questions.teaches: The 1st person plural future ends in -स्यामः / -ष्यामः: व्याख्यास्यामः (we shall explain), करिष्यामः (we shall do).

questions.q: What name does unit 2 give to its whole description?
options: The special examination of the drug
optionExplain: Right: सामान्यतो भूमिपरीक्षा = the examination of land in general.
विशेषतः opens unit 3; unit 2 says सामान्यतः, of land.
Collection is not the subject of this line.
The physician is not named.
questions.explain: The unit closes: इति सामान्यतो भूमिपरीक्षा, thus (is) the general examination of land.
questions.rule: सामान्यतः = in general; भूमिपरीक्षा = examination of land.

questions.q: Match each word describing the land to its meaning.
questions.explain: All four are locatives describing the land.
questions.rule: जांगले = in jāṅgala; समे = level; शुचौ = clean; अनुपहते = not harmed.

questions.q: Put the four things the land is frequented by in the order of the text.
questions.explain: शिशिरातपपवनसलिलसेविते: cold, sunshine, wind, water.
questions.teaches: The land is frequented, in due season, by cold, sunshine, wind and water, in that order.

questions.q: Which is the right split of प्रदक्षिणोदके?
optionExplain: दके is not a word; the second member is उदक, water.
Right: अ + उ → ओ: प्रदक्षिण + उदके = प्रदक्षिणोदके, with water to the right.
A visarga after अ before उ would drop and leave a gap, not give ओ.
प्रदक्षिणोद and के are not words; the second member is उदक, water.
questions.explain: प्रदक्षिण (to the right) + उदक (water): with water to the right.

questions.q: Which two must the land be free from, according to unit 2?
optionExplain: No: black is one of the good soil qualities.
No: the land is spread with kuśa, not free from it.
Right: ऊषर is in the same 'free from' compound.
Right: वल्मीक is in आराम-वल्मीक-ऊषर-विरहिते.
questions.explain: विरहित = devoid of: garden, anthill and saline soil; the land is spread with kuśa and has black soil.
questions.rule: विरहिते: आराम · वल्मीक · ऊषर; आस्तीर्णे: कुश · रोहिष.

questions.q: Join a new example, शीत + उदकम् (cool water), as one word. Which is right?
optionExplain: ऊ needs उ + उ, not अ + उ.
औ comes from अ + औ or अ + ओ, not अ + उ.
Right: अ + उ → ओ, as in प्रदक्षिण + उदके = प्रदक्षिणोदके.
व् comes from उ before a vowel, not from अ + उ.
questions.explain: Same rule as प्रदक्षिणोदके.
questions.teaches: Final अ + initial उ join as ओ: प्रदक्षिण + उदके = प्रदक्षिणोदके; शीत + उदकम् = शीतोदकम्.

questions.q: What does unit 3 say this land abounds in?
optionExplain: Unit 3 names no element; it says only स्वगुण.
Fire is named in unit 5.
Space is named in unit 7.
Right: स्वगुणभूयिष्ठा = most abundant in its own (स्व) quality (गुण).
questions.explain: The unit says only स्व-गुण, its own quality; the element is not named.
questions.rule: स्वगुणभूयिष्ठा = abounding in its own quality.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 3 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four feminine adjectives of the land.
questions.rule: अश्मवती = stony; स्थिरा = firm; गुर्वी = heavy; श्यामा = dark.

questions.q: Put these words of unit 3 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Stony, firm, heavy, dark, then the grass, then trees and crops.
questions.rule: अश्मवती · स्थिरा · गुर्वी · श्यामा · कृशस्थूलतृणा · वृक्षसस्यप्राया.
questions.teaches: Unit 3 lists the land's qualities: stony, firm, heavy, dark, thin-and-thick grass, mostly trees and crops.

questions.q: Which is the right split of विशेषतस्त्वश्मवती?
optionExplain: Right: Visarga → स् before त; उ before a different vowel → व्: तु + अश्मवती = त्वश्मवती.
स्तु is not a word; the स् comes from the visarga.
ओ + अ would give -ोऽ, not त्व.
त्व and श्मवती are not the words of the card.
questions.explain: विशेषतः (in particular) + तु (but, and) + अश्मवती (stony).
questions.rule: ः → स् before त; उ + different vowel → व्.

questions.q: Does unit 3 itself name the element whose quality this land abounds in?
options: Yes; it names stone as the element
optionExplain: पृथिवी does not occur in unit 3.
Right: The note says the element is not named; earth is inferred, not stated.
अम्बु (water) does not occur in unit 3.
अश्मवती (stony) is a quality, not an element of the series.
questions.explain: स्वगुण = its own quality; the card treats 'earth' as an inference only.
questions.rule: Unit 3: element not named; earth type inferred.

questions.q: Like गुर्वी (heavy, feminine of गुरु), which phrase means a light land (लघु)?
optionExplain: This is the masculine form; भूमि is feminine.
There is no vowel between घ and व in the feminine.
Right: An adjective in -उ makes its feminine in -वी: गुरु → गुर्वी, लघु → लघ्वी.
-वः is a plural ending, not a feminine singular.
questions.explain: गुर्वी agrees with the feminine भूमि; लघ्वी is built the same way.
questions.teaches: Adjectives in -उ make the feminine in -वी and agree with a feminine noun: गुर्वी भूमिः, लघ्वी भूमिः.

questions.q: What colour does unit 4 give the land?
optionExplain: Dark is said in units 3 and 7, not in unit 4.
Ash-colour belongs to unit 6.
That is unit 5.
Right: शुक्ला = white, one of the clear words of the unit.
questions.explain: Unit 4: स्निग्धा, शीतला ... शुक्ला.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 4 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are the clear qualities of the land and its leaves.
questions.rule: स्निग्धा = unctuous; शीतला = cool; शुक्ला = white; कोमल = tender.

questions.q: Put the members of the compound स्निग्धतृणसस्यकोमलदलप्राया in their order.
questions.explain: Unctuous grass, crops, tender leaves: स्निग्ध · तृण · सस्य · कोमल · दल, then प्राया (mostly).
questions.teaches: The land is mostly (प्राया) covered with unctuous grass, crops and tender leaves, in that order.

questions.q: In unit 4, which word means cool, as distinct from स्निग्धा (unctuous)?
optionExplain: Right: शीतला = cool, the second word of the unit.
शुक्ला means white.
स्निग्धा means unctuous, smooth.
श्यामा means dark; it is not in unit 4.
questions.explain: Unit 4 opens स्निग्धा (unctuous), शीतला (cool), and ends शुक्ला (white).
questions.rule: शीतला = cool; स्निग्धा = unctuous; शुक्ला = white.

questions.q: Which two qualities belong to the land of unit 4?
optionExplain: No: stony is unit 3.
Right: शुक्ला is near the end of the unit.
No: रूक्षा is unit 6.
Right: शीतला is the second word.
questions.explain: Unit 4: unctuous, cool, (water near), unctuous grass, crops and tender leaves, white.

questions.q: Which phrase means a white cow (धेनु, f.), agreeing like शुक्ला (भूमिः)?
optionExplain: शुक्लः is masculine; धेनु is feminine.
Right: An -अ adjective takes -आ in the feminine singular: शुक्ल → शुक्ला.
शुक्लम् is neuter.
शुक्लाः is plural; धेनुः is singular.
questions.explain: शुक्ला agrees with the understood feminine भूमिः; the same form goes with धेनुः.
questions.teaches: An -अ adjective with a feminine singular noun ends in -आ: शुक्ला भूमिः, शुक्ला धेनुः.

questions.q: Which quality does the land of unit 5 abound in?
optionExplain: Unit 5 names अग्नि, not अम्बु.
Wind is the type of unit 6.
Right: अग्निगुणभूयिष्ठा = most abundant in the quality of fire.
Space is the type of unit 7.
questions.explain: The last word of unit 5 names fire.
questions.rule: अग्निगुणभूयिष्ठा = abounding in the quality of fire.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 5 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words describe the land, its flowers and its trees.
questions.rule: नानावर्णा = various colours; वृक्ष = trees; प्रविरल = very sparse; प्ररोह = growth.

questions.q: Put the words of unit 5 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Colours, flowers, trees, then the fire quality.
questions.teaches: Unit 5 runs: various colours, light flowers, very sparse pale trees, abounding in fire.

questions.q: How does the card render पाण्डु in unit 5?
optionExplain: The note rejects 'yellow' for पाण्डु.
Dark is श्यामा, in units 3 and 7.
White is शुक्ला, in unit 4.
Right: The note: पाण्डु is 'pale', not 'yellow'.
questions.explain: प्रविरल-पाण्डु-वृक्ष-प्ररोहा = with a very sparse growth of pale trees.

questions.q: Which two describe the land of unit 5?
options: with great trees at its edges
optionExplain: Right: नानावर्णा.
No: white is unit 4.
No: that is unit 7.
Right: प्रविरल-पाण्डु-वृक्ष-प्ररोहा.
questions.explain: Unit 5: various colours, light flowers, very sparse pale trees, fire.

questions.q: Like नानावर्णा (having various colours), what does an invented नानापुष्पा लता mean?
optionExplain: Right: नाना + noun + -आ is a bahuvrīhi describing the creeper: having various flowers.
The compound describes one creeper; it is not a list.
Nothing in नाना means 'without'.
नाना means various, and the noun is लता, a creeper.
questions.explain: नानावर्णा (भूमिः) = a land having various colours; नानापुष्पा लता = a creeper having various flowers.
questions.teaches: A bahuvrīhi like नाना-वर्णा describes its noun: 'having various X' (नानावर्णा भूमिः, नानापुष्पा लता).

questions.q: Which quality does the land of unit 6 abound in?
optionExplain: Fire is unit 5.
Right: अनिलगुणभूयिष्ठा = most abundant in the quality of wind.
Space is unit 7.
Unit 6 names अनिल, not अम्बु.
questions.explain: The last word of unit 6 names wind (अनिल).

questions.q: Match each word of unit 6 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Colour, dryness and the little rasa of the growth.
questions.rule: रासभ = donkey; भस्म = ash; रूक्षा = dry; अल्प = little.

questions.q: Put the words of unit 6 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Colour, dryness, the surface, the growth, then the wind quality.
questions.teaches: Unit 6 runs: donkey-and-ash colour, dry, (slight, hollow, saline), growth of little rasa, wind.

questions.q: What colour does unit 6 give the land?
options: Golden, like the good soil of unit 2
The colour of a donkey and of ash
optionExplain: Golden soil is praised in unit 2.
White is unit 4.
Right: रासभ-भस्म-वर्णा = of the colour of a donkey and ash.
Various colours is unit 5.
questions.explain: Each land type has its own colour; unit 6 is donkey and ash.

questions.q: What does unit 6 say about the growth (प्ररोह) on this land?
options: It has rasa that is indistinct
optionExplain: अल्प means little, not abundant.
Indistinct (अव्यक्त) rasa is said of water in unit 7.
Sweet is said of the soil in unit 2.
Right: अल्प-रस-प्ररोहा = with a growth of little taste or sap.
questions.explain: अल्प = little; रस = taste, sap; प्ररोह = growth.

questions.q: Like भस्मवर्णा (ash-coloured), what does an invented दुग्धवर्णा भूमिः mean?
optionExplain: Right: X-वर्णा describes the noun as having the colour of X.
-वर्णा names a colour, not contents.
Nothing in -वर्णा means giving.
-वर्णा means having the colour; it does not deny colour.
questions.explain: रासभभस्मवर्णा = donkey-and-ash-coloured; दुग्धवर्णा = milk-coloured.
questions.rule: X-वर्णा (f.) = having the colour of X.
questions.teaches: A compound ending in -वर्णा means 'having the colour of X': भस्मवर्णा, दुग्धवर्णा.

questions.q: Which quality does the land of unit 7 abound in?
optionExplain: Wind is unit 6.
Right: आकाशगुणभूयिष्ठा = most abundant in the quality of space.
Fire is unit 5.
स्वगुण is the phrase of unit 3.
questions.explain: The last word of unit 7 names space (ākāśa).

questions.q: Match each word of unit 7 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are the clear words of the unit.
questions.rule: समा = level; अव्यक्त = indistinct; जल = water; श्यामा = dark.

questions.q: Put these words of unit 7 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Level, the water, the trees, dark, then the quality of space.
questions.teaches: Unit 7 runs (after soft and having pits): level, water of indistinct taste, great trees, dark, space.

questions.q: What does unit 7 say about the taste (रस) of its water?
optionExplain: Sweetness is said of the soil in unit 2, not of this water.
Neither salt nor clarity is named in unit 7.
Right: अव्यक्त-रस-जला = with water of indistinct taste.
Little (अल्प) rasa is said of the growth in unit 6.
questions.explain: अव्यक्त = not manifest, indistinct.

questions.q: Units 3 and 7 both call the land dark (श्यामा). What marks the land of unit 7?
options: It has thin and thick grass
It is mostly trees and crops
It is level and abounds in space
optionExplain: अश्मवती and गुर्वी are unit 3.
कृशस्थूलतृणा is unit 3.
वृक्षसस्यप्राया is unit 3.
Right: समा and आकाशगुणभूयिष्ठा are words of unit 7.
questions.explain: Same colour, different land: unit 3 is stony and heavy; unit 7 is level and of the space type.

questions.q: Like अव्यक्त (a- + व्यक्त, not manifest), what does an invented अशुद्ध mean?
optionExplain: Right: The prefix अ- negates: अ + शुद्ध = not clean, as अ + व्यक्त = not manifest.
अ- does not intensify.
अ- does not mean 'again'.
There is no word for water in अशुद्ध.
questions.explain: अव्यक्त = not manifest, indistinct; the same अ- gives अशुद्ध, not clean.
questions.teaches: The negative prefix अ- before a consonant means 'not': अव्यक्त (indistinct), अशुद्ध (not clean).

questions.q: In which lands does unit 8 place the praised purgatives?
options: Lands abounding in fire, wind and space
Lands of water and earth qualities
Lands endowed with all the qualities
optionExplain: These yield emetics, in verse 9.
Right: अम्बु-पृथिवी-गुण-भूयिष्ठासु भूमिषु: in lands abounding in the qualities of water and earth.
These yield pacifying ones, in unit 10.
These yield both-way ones, in verse 9.
questions.explain: Unit 8 joins water-and-earth lands with purgative and nourishing (ones).

questions.q: Match each word of unit 8 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The place, the growth and the two uses.
questions.rule: विरेचनानि = purgatives; बृंहणानि = nourishing; भूमिषु = in lands; जातानि = born.

questions.q: Put these words of unit 8 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Which lands, lands, grown there, purgative, nourishing, are praised.
questions.rule: अंबुपृथिवीगुणभूयिष्ठासु · भूमिषु · जातानि · विरेचनानि · बृंहणानि · शस्यंते.
questions.teaches: Unit 8 runs: in lands abounding in water and earth, (ones) grown are praised as purgative and nourishing.

questions.q: Which is the right split of तत्रांबु-?
optionExplain: बु is not a word; the member is अम्बु, water.
तत्र is an indeclinable with no -म्.
Right: अ + अ → आ: तत्र + अम्बु = तत्राम्बु (print: तत्रांबु, anusvara for म्).
तत्र ends in a short अ in the word split.
questions.explain: तत्र (among these) + अम्बु (water).

questions.q: Does unit 8 itself say that its water and earth lands are those of units 3 and 4?
options: Yes; it repeats the words of unit 3
Yes; it calls them stony and white
optionExplain: The unit does not refer to other units.
None of unit 3's words occur in unit 8.
Stony and white are not in unit 8.
Right: The note says the correspondence is inferred, not stated.
questions.explain: Unit 8 names only 'water and earth qualities'; the link to units 3 and 4 is the card's inference.

questions.q: Like भूमिषु (in lands, from भूमि), which form means in rivers (नदी, f.)?
optionExplain: Right: Locative plural of an -ई / -इ feminine ends in -षु: भूमिषु, नदीषु.
This is the locative singular: in a river.
This is the instrumental plural: by rivers.
This is the nominative plural: rivers.
questions.explain: भूमिषु = in lands (loc. pl.); नदीषु is built the same way.
questions.teaches: The locative plural of feminines in -इ / -ई ends in -षु: भूमिषु (in lands), नदीषु (in rivers).

questions.q: What does verse 9 assign to lands abounding in fire, wind and space?
optionExplain: Purgatives come from water-and-earth lands, unit 8.
Right: अनलानिलाकाशगुणभूयिष्ठासु वमनानि.
Pacifying ones come from space lands, unit 10.
Nourishing ones are in unit 8.
questions.explain: Fire, wind and space lands: vamana.

questions.q: Put the words of verse 9 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Land, then use; land, then use.

questions.q: Match each word of verse 9 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Two elements of the first land, and the two uses of the verse.
questions.rule: अनल = fire; अनिल = wind; वमनानि = for vomiting; उभयतोभागानि = both-way.
questions.teaches: अनल (fire) and अनिल (wind) are different words; the verse joins fire-wind-space lands with vamana and all-quality lands with ubhayatobhāga.

questions.q: From which lands come the both-way (उभयतोभाग) ones?
options: Lands of fire, wind and space
optionExplain: These give vomiting ones (वमन).
These give purgative and nourishing ones, unit 8.
Right: सर्वगुणयुक्तासु उभयतोभागानि.
These give pacifying ones, unit 10.
questions.explain: All qualities joined: both-way.

questions.q: Verse 9 has no verb. Where do 'born' and 'are praised' come from?
optionExplain: Unit 10 is also elliptical; it takes the verb from unit 8 too.
Unit 11's verb is भवन्ति (become).
That is a noun-like adjective, not a verb.
Right: The note: जातानि and प्रशस्यन्ते carry over from unit 8.
questions.explain: Unit 8 supplies जातानि (born) and the verb 'are praised'.

questions.q: Join a new example, जल + अनिल (water and wind), as one word. Which is right?
optionExplain: Right: अ + अ → आ, as in अनल + अनिल = अनलानिल.
ए comes from अ + इ, not अ + अ.
ओ comes from अ + उ, not अ + अ.
य् comes from इ before a vowel.
questions.explain: Same rule as अनल + अनिल = अनलानिल.
questions.teaches: Final अ + initial अ join as आ: अनल + अनिल = अनलानिल; जल + अनिल = जलानिल.

questions.q: What does unit 10 assign to lands abounding in the quality of space?
optionExplain: Vomiting ones come from fire-wind-space lands, verse 9.
Right: आकाशगुणभूयिष्ठासु शमनानि.
Purgatives come from water-and-earth lands, unit 8.
Both-way ones come from lands of all qualities.
questions.explain: Space alone: pacifying.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 10 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The compound and the use.
questions.rule: आकाश = space; गुण = quality; भूयिष्ठ = most abundant; शमनानि = pacifying.

questions.q: आकाशगुणभूयिष्ठासु ____ (pacifying ones). Type it in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: शमनानि = pacifying (ones), neuter plural like वमनानि and विरेचनानि.
questions.teaches: Lands abounding in space yield pacifying (शमन) ones.

questions.q: How does the card explain शमन?
optionExplain: The note rules out purgative.
The note rules out emetic.
Right: The note: śamana = pacifying, palliative (not purgative or emetic).
Nourishing is बृंहण, unit 8.
questions.explain: शमन = pacifying; विरेचन, वमन, बृंहण are other uses.

questions.q: Space occurs in verse 9 and unit 10. How do they differ?
options: Verse 9: alone, pacifying; unit 10: with fire, emetics
Unit 10 repeats verse 9 word for word
Verse 9: with fire and wind, emetics; unit 10: alone, pacifying
optionExplain: This reverses the two verses.
Purgatives are from water-and-earth lands.
Unit 10 names only space and śamana.
Right: Verse 9 joins space with fire and wind; unit 10 names space alone.
questions.explain: अनल-अनिल-आकाश → वमन (9); आकाश अकेला → शमन (10).
questions.rule: आकाश के साथ अग्नि-वायु: वमन; अकेला आकाश: शमन.

questions.q: Which phrase means in clean lands, agreeing like आकाशगुणभूयिष्ठासु (भूमिषु)?
optionExplain: Right: A feminine -आ adjective in the locative plural ends in -आसु.
-एषु is the masculine/neuter locative plural.
शुद्धाः is nominative, not locative.
-आयाम् is the locative singular.
questions.explain: भूयिष्ठासु agrees with the feminine plural locative भूमिषु; शुद्धासु does too.
questions.teaches: An adjective with a feminine locative plural noun ends in -आसु: भूयिष्ठासु भूमिषु, शुद्धासु भूमिषु.

questions.q: What does unit 11 say the medicines become?
optionExplain: Nothing in the unit means weaker.
Right: बलवत्तमानि = most powerful.
Pacifying is unit 10's word.
Storage is not named in unit 11.
questions.explain: एवं बलवत्तमानि भवन्ति = thus (they) become the most powerful.

questions.q: Put the words of unit 11 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Thus, most powerful, become.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 11 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The whole unit is three words.
questions.rule: एवम् = thus; बलवत्तमानि = most powerful; भवन्ति = become.
questions.teaches: एवं बलवत्तमानि भवन्ति: thus (they) become the most powerful.

questions.q: Unit 2 has बलवत्तरैः and unit 11 has बलवत्तमानि. How do they differ?
optionExplain: This reverses the two suffixes.
The card glosses them differently: stronger / most powerful.
Right: बलवत्तर is the comparative (unit 2: stronger trees); बलवत्तम is the superlative.
Neither suffix means weak.
questions.explain: बलवत्-तर = stronger; बलवत्-तम = most powerful.

questions.q: What is the unstated subject of भवन्ति in unit 11?
optionExplain: Lands (भूमि) are feminine; बलवत्तमानि is neuter.
Those trees are masculine (द्रुमैः) and are harmful neighbours.
Physicians are not named.
Right: The note: the subject is the medicines, understood.
questions.explain: बलवत्तमानि is neuter plural, matching the medicines (भेषजानि) of unit 2.
questions.rule: Subject of भवन्ति = medicines (n. pl.), understood.

questions.q: Like बलवत्तम (most powerful, from बलवत्), which word means lightest (from लघु)?
optionExplain: Right: -तम makes the superlative: लघु + तम = lightest.
-तर makes the comparative: lighter.
-ता makes an abstract noun: lightness.
-त्व also makes an abstract noun.
questions.explain: बलवत् + तम = most powerful; लघु + तम = lightest.
questions.teaches: The suffix -तम forms the superlative ('most'), -तर the comparative ('more'): बलवत्तम, लघुतम; बलवत्तर, लघुतर.

questions.q: What does कालजानि say about the good herbs of unit 12?
options: They are cut at night time
They are born in due season
They are grown in a garden
They are kept for a long time
optionExplain: Nothing in the unit is about cutting or night.
Right: काल-जानि = born (ज) in (their) time (काल), in season.
A garden is not named in unit 12.
Keeping is not the sense of कालज.
questions.explain: कालजानि = born in their time, the first quality the unit names.
questions.section: औषधि के गुण और ग्रहण की ऋतु

questions.q: Match each member of उपगतसंपूर्णप्रमाणरसवीर्यगंधानि to its meaning.
questions.explain: The herbs have attained (उपगत) complete (सम्पूर्ण) measure, taste, potency and smell.
questions.rule: प्रमाण = measure; रस = taste; वीर्य = potency; गन्ध = smell.
questions.section: औषधि के गुण और ग्रहण की ऋतु

questions.q: Put the four things the herbs have fully attained in the order of unit 12.
questions.explain: उपगत-सम्पूर्ण-प्रमाण-रस-वीर्य-गन्धानि: measure, taste, potency, smell.
questions.teaches: A good herb has attained full measure, taste (rasa), potency (vīrya) and smell, in that order of the text.
questions.section: औषधि के गुण और ग्रहण की ऋतु

questions.q: Which is the right split of कालजान्युपगत-?
optionExplain: युपगत is not a word; the य् comes from the final इ.
न्युपगत is not a word; कालजानि is the n. nom. pl.
Right: इ before a different vowel becomes य्: कालजानि + उपगत = कालजान्युपगत.
Neither कालजान्यु nor पगत is a word.
questions.explain: कालजानि (born in season) + उपगत (attained).
questions.rule: इ + a different vowel → य् + that vowel.
questions.section: औषधि के गुण और ग्रहण की ऋतु

questions.q: Unit 12 opens a relative clause with यानि (which ...). Where does the card say it is taken up?
options: In the same line, by तत्र
It is never taken up at all
In the last line of the chapter
In the next line, by तेषाम्
optionExplain: तत्र (there, among these) opens unit 12; it does not answer यानि.
The note says the clause continues into the next line.
The note points to line 05.08.14, the very next line.
Right: The note: 'yāni ... sthitāni' continues into line 05.08.14, which begins तेषाम् (of these).
questions.explain: यानि (which) ... तेषाम् (of these): the relative clause of unit 12 is answered in line 05.08.14.
questions.rule: यानि … तेषाम्: relative and correlative across two units.
questions.section: औषधि के गुण और ग्रहण की ऋतु

questions.q: Join a new pair the same way: इति + उक्तम् (thus said). Which is right?
optionExplain: Right: इ before a different vowel becomes य्, as in कालजानि + उपगत = कालजान्युपगत.
ऊ would need उ + उ; here इ meets उ.
ए comes from अ + इ, not from इ + उ.
In close sandhi इ does not stay before a different vowel.
questions.explain: Same rule as कालजान्युपगत.
questions.teaches: Final इ before a different vowel becomes य्: कालजानि + उपगत = कालजान्युपगत; इति + उक्तम् = इत्युक्तम्.
questions.section: औषधि के गुण और ग्रहण की ऋतु

questions.q: In which two seasons does unit 13 say branch and leaf are to be taken?
optionExplain: Summer (ग्रीष्म) and the cold season come in unit 14, with roots.
Right: वर्षा-वसन्तयोः = in the rainy season and in spring.
Autumn and winter come in units 15 and 16.
Spring is right, but the other season is वर्षा, rain.
questions.explain: शाखापलाशम् … वर्षावसन्तयोर्ग्राह्यम्.
questions.section: औषधि के गुण और ग्रहण की ऋतु

questions.q: Match each word of unit 13 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The recently grown branch and leaf are to be taken.
questions.rule: शाखा = branch; पलाश = leaf; अचिर = recently; ग्राह्य = to be taken.
questions.section: औषधि के गुण और ग्रहण की ऋतु

questions.q: Put the words of unit 13 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Of these, branch and leaf, recently grown, in rain and spring, to be taken.
questions.teaches: Unit 13 runs: of these, the branch and leaf, recently grown, in the rainy season and spring, are to be taken.
questions.section: औषधि के गुण और ग्रहण की ऋतु

questions.q: Which is the right split of वर्षावसंतयोर्ग्राह्यं?
optionExplain: र्ग्राह्यम् is not a word; the र् comes from the visarga.
That would read -योरग्राह्यं, and it would mean 'not to be taken'.
Right: A visarga after ओ becomes र् before a voiced sound such as ग.
योर्ग्राह्यम् is not a word; -योः is the ending of the dual.
questions.explain: वर्षावसन्तयोः (in rain and spring) + ग्राह्यम् (to be taken).
questions.rule: Visarga after a vowel other than अ/आ, before a voiced sound → र्.
questions.section: औषधि के गुण और ग्रहण की ऋतु

questions.q: A gatherer wants freshly grown leaves of a good herb. When should he take them, by unit 13?
options: In summer, when roots are taken
In winter, when the sāra is taken
In autumn, with the bark and tuber
In the rainy season or spring
optionExplain: In unit 14 summer is the season for roots, not leaves.
Winter (hemanta) is the season of the sāra, unit 16.
Autumn is given for bark, tuber and milk in unit 15.
Right: Recently grown branch and leaf are to be taken in varṣā and vasanta.
questions.explain: Branch and leaf: वर्षा and वसन्त.
questions.section: औषधि के गुण और ग्रहण की ऋतु

questions.q: Like वर्षावसन्तयोः (in rain and spring), which form means in hemanta and śiśira?
optionExplain: Right: A dvandva of two seasons takes the locative dual ending -योः, as वर्षावसन्तयोः does.
-एषु is the locative plural, used for three or more.
-ए is the locative singular: one season only.
-आभ्याम् is a dual ending, but not the locative one.
questions.explain: Two seasons joined: dual; 'in' them: locative; so -योः.
questions.teaches: A dvandva of two items takes dual endings; the locative dual of an a-stem ends in -योः (वर्षावसन्तयोः, हेमन्तशिशिरयोः).
questions.section: औषधि के गुण और ग्रहण की ऋतु

questions.q: What does unit 14 say is to be taken in summer?
optionExplain: Bark belongs to autumn, unit 15.
Right: ग्रीष्मे मूलानि = in summer, the roots.
Flowers go by their own season, unit 17.
The sāra belongs to winter, unit 16.
questions.explain: ग्रीष्मे (in summer) मूलानि (roots).
questions.section: औषधि के गुण और ग्रहण की ऋतु

questions.q: Match each word of unit 14 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Summer for roots, or the cold season.
questions.rule: ग्रीष्मे = in summer; मूलानि = roots; शिशिरे = in the cold season; वा = or.
questions.section: औषधि के गुण और ग्रहण की ऋतु

questions.q: Put the words of unit 14 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Summer, roots, cold season, or, of those whose leaves have fallen and sprouted.
questions.teaches: Unit 14: in summer the roots; or in śiśira, of those whose leaves have fallen and sprouted.
questions.section: औषधि के गुण और ग्रहण की ऋतु

questions.q: Which season does unit 14 give as the alternative (वा) to summer?
optionExplain: वर्षा is named in unit 13, for branch and leaf.
शरद् is named in unit 15, for bark, tuber and milk.
Right: शिशिरे वा = or in the cold season.
वसन्त is named in unit 13, with वर्षा.
questions.explain: The only other season in unit 14 is शिशिर.
questions.section: औषधि के गुण और ग्रहण की ऋतु

questions.q: Unit 14 has no verb. How is 'to be taken' supplied, according to the card?
options: It is stated at the end of unit 14
It is given in the next line as a verb
It is not needed; the unit is a question
It is carried over from line 05.08.14
optionExplain: Unit 14 ends with शीर्णप्ररूढपर्णानाम्, a genitive, not a verb.
The card points back to line 05.08.14, not forward.
The unit is a statement of what is taken when.
Right: The note: grāhya (to be taken) is carried over from the previous line, where ग्राह्यम् stands.
questions.explain: Elliptical line: ग्राह्य is understood from unit 13.
questions.rule: No verb in unit 14: ग्राह्य carried over.
questions.section: औषधि के गुण और ग्रहण की ऋतु

questions.q: Like ग्रीष्मे (in summer, from ग्रीष्म), which form means 'in spring' (वसन्त)?
optionExplain: Right: An a-stem makes its locative singular in -ए: ग्रीष्म → ग्रीष्मे, वसन्त → वसन्ते.
This is the nominative: spring (as subject).
This is the accusative.
This is the ablative: from spring.
questions.explain: ग्रीष्मे and शिशिरे are both a-stem locatives in -ए.
questions.teaches: The locative singular of an a-stem ends in -ए and means 'in, at': ग्रीष्मे, शिशिरे, वसन्ते.
questions.section: औषधि के गुण और ग्रहण की ऋतु

questions.q: In which season does unit 15 place bark, tuber and milk?
optionExplain: Summer is for roots, unit 14.
Right: शरदि = in autumn.
Winter is for the sāra, unit 16.
Spring, with rain, is for branch and leaf, unit 13.
questions.explain: शरदि त्वक्कन्दक्षीराणि.
questions.section: औषधि के गुण और ग्रहण की ऋतु

questions.q: Match each member of the compound in unit 15 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Three members of the dvandva त्वक्-कन्द-क्षीराणि.
questions.rule: त्वक् = bark; कन्द = tuber; क्षीर = milk.
questions.section: औषधि के गुण और ग्रहण की ऋतु

questions.q: Put the three things of unit 15 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: त्वक्-कन्द-क्षीराणि: bark, tuber, milk.
questions.teaches: Autumn's list runs bark, tuber, milk (त्वक्, कन्द, क्षीर).
questions.section: औषधि के गुण और ग्रहण की ऋतु

questions.q: Which of these is NOT in the autumn list of unit 15?
optionExplain: Bark is the first item of the autumn list.
Tuber is the second item of the autumn list.
Right: Roots belong to summer in unit 14; autumn has bark, tuber and milk.
Milk is the third item of the autumn list.
questions.explain: शरद्: त्वक्, कन्द, क्षीर; not मूल.
questions.section: औषधि के गुण और ग्रहण की ऋतु

questions.q: What does the card say क्षीर most probably means in this plant context?
options: Cow's milk added to the herb
The water in which it is boiled
optionExplain: The note reads it of the plant itself, not of added milk.
Fruit and its juice are not in unit 15.
Boiling is not mentioned in unit 15.
Right: The note: in a plant context kṣīra probably means the milky latex; this is probable, not stated.
questions.explain: क्षीर = milk; of a plant, probably its milky sap.
questions.section: औषधि के गुण और ग्रहण की ऋतु

questions.q: Like शरदि (in autumn, from शरद्), which form means in misfortune (from आपद्)?
optionExplain: Right: A consonant stem makes its locative singular in -इ: शरद् → शरदि, आपद् → आपदि.
-ए is the dative singular of a consonant stem.
-आ is the instrumental singular.
-सु is the locative plural, not singular.
questions.explain: Same ending as शरदि.
questions.teaches: A stem ending in a consonant takes -इ in the locative singular: शरद् → शरदि, आपद् → आपदि, दिश् → दिशि.
questions.section: औषधि के गुण और ग्रहण की ऋतु

questions.q: What does unit 16 say is to be taken in hemanta?
optionExplain: Young branch and leaf go with rain and spring, unit 13.
Right: हेमन्ते साराणि = in winter, the sāra (core).
Tubers go with autumn, unit 15.
Fruit goes by its own season, unit 17.
questions.explain: The whole unit: हेमन्ते साराणि.
questions.section: औषधि के गुण और ग्रहण की ऋतु

questions.q: In winter (hemanta) the ____ is taken (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: सार = essence, core; probably the heartwood.
questions.teaches: हेमन्ते साराणि: winter is the season of the sāra.
questions.section: औषधि के गुण और ग्रहण की ऋतु

questions.q: Which two meanings of सार does the card give?
optionExplain: No: milky sap is the probable sense of क्षीर, unit 15.
No: bark is त्वक्, unit 15.
Right: the usual sense for a woody plant, marked probable.
Right: the plain sense of सार given in the data.
questions.explain: सार = essence, core; for a woody plant probably heartwood.
questions.teaches: सार means essence or core; for a woody plant it is probably the heartwood (marked probable).
questions.section: औषधि के गुण और ग्रहण की ऋतु

questions.q: Which season is हेमन्त in the card's rendering?
optionExplain: Spring is वसन्त, unit 13.
Autumn is शरद्, unit 15.
Right: हेमन्ते = in winter (hemanta).
Summer is ग्रीष्म, unit 14.
questions.explain: हेमन्त = winter.
questions.rule: हेमन्त = winter; शिशिर = the cold season.
questions.section: औषधि के गुण और ग्रहण की ऋतु

questions.q: A gatherer wants the inner core of a woody herb. Which season does unit 16 give?
optionExplain: Varṣā, with spring, is for branch and leaf.
Grīṣma, summer, is for roots.
Śarad, autumn, is for bark, tuber and milk.
Right: हेमन्ते साराणि: the sāra (core) is taken in hemanta.
questions.explain: Core (sāra) → hemanta.
questions.section: औषधि के गुण और ग्रहण की ऋतु

questions.q: साराणि has ण because of the र before it. Which neuter plural is spelt rightly by the same rule?
optionExplain: Right: ष before the न in the same word turns it to ण, as र does in साराणि (no ch/t/l/s sound between).
ष stands before the न, so the न must become ण.
फल has no र or ष, so the न stays: फलानि.
मूल has no र or ष, so the न stays: मूलानि (unit 14).
questions.explain: साराणि, क्षीराणि, पुष्पाणि: ण after र/ष; फलानि, मूलानि: न.
questions.rule: र, ऋ or ष earlier in the word turns a following न into ण.
questions.teaches: न becomes ण after र, ऋ or ष in the same word unless a palatal, cerebral, dental, ल, श or स stands between: साराणि, पुष्पाणि but मूलानि, फलानि.
questions.section: औषधि के गुण और ग्रहण की ऋतु

questions.q: What does unit 17 say about fruit and flower?
options: They are always taken in summer
They are taken according to the season
They are never to be gathered
They are taken only in the rainy season
optionExplain: No single season is named; yathartu means by the season.
Right: यथर्तु = according to the season (yathā ṛtu).
The unit lists them among the things taken.
No single season is named for fruit and flower.
questions.explain: यथर्तु-फल-पुष्पम्: fruit and flower according to the season.
questions.section: औषधि के गुण और ग्रहण की ऋतु

questions.q: Match each member of the compound of unit 17 to its meaning.
questions.explain: यथा + ऋतु + फल + पुष्प.
questions.rule: यथा = according to; ऋतु = season; फल = fruit; पुष्प = flower.
questions.section: औषधि के गुण और ग्रहण की ऋतु

questions.q: Put the members of यथर्तुफलपुष्पम् in their order.
questions.explain: यथा-ऋतु (according to season), then फल (fruit), then पुष्प (flower).
questions.teaches: The compound runs यथा-ऋतु-फल-पुष्प: according to the season, fruit and flower.
questions.section: औषधि के गुण और ग्रहण की ऋतु

questions.q: Which is the right split of यथर्तु?
optionExplain: र्तु is not a word; the र् comes from ऋ.
यथर् is not a word, and तु (but) does not fit.
Right: आ + ऋ → अर्: यथा + ऋतु = यथर्तु.
Neither यथर्त nor उ is a word here.
questions.explain: यथा (according to) + ऋतु (season).
questions.section: औषधि के गुण और ग्रहण की ऋतु

questions.q: A herb flowers only in one season. When does unit 17 say its flower is taken?
optionExplain: Hemanta is given for the sāra, not for flowers.
Summer is given for roots, not for flowers.
Autumn is given for bark, tuber and milk.
Right: यथर्तु: each according to its season.
questions.explain: Fruit and flower are taken by their own season.
questions.section: औषधि के गुण और ग्रहण की ऋतु

questions.q: Join a new pair the same way: महा + ऋषिः (great sage). Which is right?
optionExplain: Right: आ + ऋ → अर्, as in यथा + ऋतु = यथर्तु.
The long आ does not stay; आ + ऋ gives अर्.
In close sandhi the vowels do not stand side by side.
ए comes from अ/आ + इ, not from आ + ऋ.
questions.explain: Same rule as यथर्तु.
questions.teaches: अ or आ before ऋ joins as अर्: यथा + ऋतु = यथर्तु; महा + ऋषिः = महर्षिः.
questions.section: औषधि के गुण और ग्रहण की ऋतु

questions.q: What does unit 18 lead into?
optionExplain: The chapter goes on; this line opens a view.
Right: अन्ये पुनराहुः = others, again, say; the view follows in the next line.
Measures are not what the next line gives.
No sage or story is named.
questions.explain: The line introduces what others say, in line 05.08.20.
questions.section: औषधि के गुण और ग्रहण की ऋतु

questions.q: Match each word of unit 18 to its meaning.
questions.explain: These three words are the whole unit.
questions.rule: अन्ये = others; पुनर् = again; आहुः = they say.
questions.section: औषधि के गुण और ग्रहण की ऋतु

questions.q: Put the words of unit 18 in their order.
questions.explain: Others, again, say.
questions.teaches: The formula runs subject, particle, verb: अन्ये पुनर् आहुः (others, again, say).
questions.section: औषधि के गुण और ग्रहण की ऋतु

questions.q: Which is the right split of पुनराहुः?
optionExplain: Neither पुनरा nor हुः is a word.
पुन is not a word, and राहु does not fit the sense.
Right: पुनर् keeps its र् before a vowel: पुनर् + आहुः = पुनराहुः.
पुनो is not a form; the word is पुनर्.
questions.explain: पुनर् (again) + आहुः (they say).
questions.rule: पुनर्: र् stays before a vowel.
questions.section: औषधि के गुण और ग्रहण की ऋतु

questions.q: Does unit 18 itself state the view of the others?
options: Yes; it says roots are taken in winter
Yes; it rejects the seasons of unit 13
Yes; it says all parts are taken in spring
No; the view comes in the next line
optionExplain: No season or part is named in unit 18.
Unit 18 neither states nor rejects anything.
No season is named in unit 18.
Right: The note: the line leaves the content to the next unit (verse 19).
questions.explain: Unit 18 is only an introduction.
questions.section: औषधि के गुण और ग्रहण की ऋतु

questions.q: Join a new pair the same way: पुनर् + अपि (again also). Which is right?
optionExplain: Right: र् of पुनर् stays and joins the following vowel, as in पुनराहुः.
That pattern belongs to a visarga after अ, not to पुनर्.
A visarga cannot stand before a vowel and join it.
The र् is not dropped before a vowel.
questions.explain: Same as पुनराहुः.
questions.teaches: पुनर् keeps its र् before a vowel or voiced sound: पुनराहुः, पुनरपि.
questions.section: औषधि के गुण और ग्रहण की ऋतु

questions.q: By verse 19, in which seasons are saumya (gentle) medicines taken?
optionExplain: Those are for the āgneya (fiery) ones.
Right: सौम्यानि औषधानि सौम्येषु ऋतुषु: gentle medicines in the gentle seasons.
The verse matches each kind to its own kind of season.
The verse names no particular season.
questions.explain: Like with like: saumya in saumya, āgneya in āgneya.
questions.rule: सौम्य → सौम्य ऋतु; आग्नेय → आग्नेय ऋतु.
questions.section: औषधि के गुण और ग्रहण की ऋतु

questions.q: Match each word of verse 19 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Two kinds of medicine, and the result of matching them to the season.
questions.rule: सौम्य = gentle; आग्नेय = fiery; अव्यापन्न = unspoiled; आपूर्णतर = fuller.
questions.section: औषधि के गुण और ग्रहण की ऋतु

questions.q: Put these phrases of verse 19 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Gentle medicines, in gentle seasons; fiery in fiery; thus unspoiled; with fuller rasa and vīrya they become.
questions.rule: सौम्यान्यौषधानि · सौम्येष्वृतुषु · आग्नेयान्याग्नेयेषु · एवमव्यापन्नानि · आपूर्णतररसवीर्याणि भवन्ति.
questions.teaches: Verse 19 gives the rule (saumya in saumya, āgneya in āgneya), then its result (unspoiled, fuller rasa and vīrya).
questions.section: औषधि के गुण और ग्रहण की ऋतु

questions.q: Which is the right split of सौम्यान्यौषधानि?
optionExplain: यौषधानि is not a word; the य् comes from the final इ.
न्यौषधानि is not a word; सौम्यानि is n. nom. pl.
Right: इ before a different vowel becomes य्: सौम्यानि + औषधानि = सौम्यान्यौषधानि.
सौम्यान्य is not a form of सौम्य.
questions.explain: सौम्यानि (gentle) + औषधानि (medicines).
questions.section: औषधि के गुण और ग्रहण की ऋतु

questions.q: Which two results of gathering by the matching season does verse 19 state?
options: their rasa and vīrya are fuller
they need no cooking at all
optionExplain: Right: आपूर्णतर-रस-वीर्याणि, with fuller taste and potency.
Right: अव्यापन्नानि, unspoiled.
No: keeping time is not in verse 19.
No: cooking is not mentioned.
questions.explain: एवम् अव्यापन्नानि आपूर्णतररसवीर्याणि भवन्ति: thus they become unspoiled, fuller in rasa and vīrya.
questions.section: औषधि के गुण और ग्रहण की ऋतु

questions.q: Like आपूर्णतर (fuller, from आपूर्ण), which word means lighter (from लघु)?
optionExplain: -तम makes the superlative: lightest.
-त्व makes an abstract noun: lightness.
-वत् means 'like' or 'having', not 'more'.
Right: -तर makes the comparative: आपूर्ण → आपूर्णतर, लघु → लघुतर.
questions.explain: Same suffix as आपूर्णतर.
questions.teaches: The suffix -तर forms a comparative ('more ...'): आपूर्णतर (fuller), लघुतर (lighter); -तम forms the superlative.
questions.section: औषधि के गुण और ग्रहण की ऋतु

questions.q: What colour are the gatherer's clothes in unit 20?
optionExplain: Right: शुक्लवासाः = clothed in white (शुक्ल).
Red clothes are not named.
Yellow clothes are not named.
Dark clothes are not named.
questions.explain: शुक्ल-वासाः: one whose clothes are white.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 20 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Three words describe the gatherer; the verb comes last.
questions.rule: शुचिः = clean; शुक्लवासाः = in white clothes; कृतोपवासः = having fasted; गृह्णीयात् = he should take.

questions.q: Put those whom the gatherer worships in the order of unit 20.
questions.explain: संपूज्य देवताम् अश्विनौ गोब्राह्मणान् च: the deity, the two Aśvins, cows and brahmins.
questions.teaches: The text names those he worships in this order: the deity, the two Aśvins, cows and brahmins (देवताम् अश्विनौ may also be one apposition).

questions.q: Which is the right split of कृतोपवासः?
optionExplain: पवासः is not a word; the second member is उपवास.
Right: अ + उ → ओ: कृत + उपवासः = कृतोपवासः, one who has done a fast.
A visarga after अ before उ would drop and leave a gap, not give ओ.
ओपवास is not a word; ओ comes from अ + उ.
questions.explain: कृत (done) + उपवास (fast): one who has fasted.

questions.q: Which two does unit 20 state about the gatherer?
options: he has eaten a full meal
optionExplain: No: he has fasted.
No: no time of day is named.
Right: शुचिः, clean.
Right: कृतोपवासः, one who has fasted.
questions.explain: कृतोपवासः and शुचिः describe the gatherer.

questions.q: Like गृह्णीयात् (he should take, optative), which form means he should give (√दा)?
optionExplain: This is the present: he gives.
This is the future: he will give.
Right: The optative 3rd singular in -यात् says what one should do: गृह्णीयात्, दद्यात्.
This is the absolutive: having given.
questions.explain: गृह्णीयात् and दद्यात् are both 3 sg. optative.
questions.teaches: The optative (विधिलिङ्) 3rd singular states a rule, 'he should': गृह्णीयात् (should take), दद्यात् (should give).

questions.q: In what are the stored medicines hung, according to unit 21?
optionExplain: The floor is not named; they are hung up.
Water is one of the things kept away.
They are kept in houses.
Right: शिक्येषु आसज्य = having hung (them) in slings.
questions.explain: शिक्येष्वासज्य स्थापयेत्: he should keep them hung in slings.

questions.q: Put the storage steps of unit 21 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Having taken, having placed in a vessel, having hung in slings, he should keep.

questions.q: Put the first six things the medicines must be kept from in the order of unit 21.
questions.explain: अग्नि-सलिल-उपस्वेद-धूम-रजो-मूषिक-चतुष्पाद-आदि: fire, water, steam, smoke, dust, mice (then quadrupeds).
questions.rule: अग्नि · सलिल · उपस्वेद · धूम · रजः · मूषिक.
questions.teaches: The medicines are kept out of reach of fire, water, steam, smoke, dust, mice, quadrupeds and the like.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 21 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Vessel, house, sling: where the medicines go; steam: one thing kept away.
questions.rule: भाजन = vessel; आगार = house; शिक्य = sling; उपस्वेद = steam, moisture.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT among the things the stored medicines must be kept from?
optionExplain: Right: Moonlight is not named; the list is fire, water, steam, smoke, dust, mice, quadrupeds.
धूम (smoke) is in the list.
मूषिक (mice) is in the list.
रजः (dust) is in the list.
questions.explain: अनभिगमनीयानि: not to be reached by fire, water, steam, smoke, dust, mice, quadrupeds and so on.
questions.rule: Kept from: अग्नि, सलिल, उपस्वेद, धूम, रजः, मूषिक, चतुष्पाद.

questions.q: गृहीत्वा has no prefix; संस्थाप्य has सम्. With the prefix आ-, which absolutive of √दा is right?
optionExplain: -त्वा is used without a prefix; with आ- it becomes -य.
Right: With a prefix the absolutive takes -य (ल्यप्), not -त्वा: सम् + स्थाप्य, आ + दाय.
There is no such form; and a prefixed verb takes -य.
That has a noun ending; the absolutive is आदाय.
questions.explain: गृहीत्वा (no prefix, -त्वा) versus संस्थाप्य (prefix, -य).
questions.teaches: The absolutive is -त्वा without a prefix (गृहीत्वा) and -य with one (संस्थाप्य, आसज्य, आदाय).

questions.q: What does unit 22 tell him to do with those (तानि) that are with milk?
optionExplain: Nothing is thrown away in this line.
Burning is not in this line.
Right: उपकल्पयेत् = he should prepare, arrange.
Burying is not in this line.
questions.explain: तानि सक्षीराणि उपकल्पयेत्: he should prepare those with milk.

questions.q: Match each piece of unit 22 to its meaning.
questions.explain: स-क्षीराणि = with milk; तानि = those; the verb is optative.
questions.rule: तानि = those; स- = with; क्षीर = milk; उपकल्पयेत् = should prepare.

questions.q: In सक्षीर, the word meaning milk is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: स (with) + क्षीर (milk) = सक्षीर, with milk.
questions.teaches: क्षीर = milk; in a plant context probably milky sap.

questions.q: Does unit 22 decide whether सक्षीर means milky plants or 'together with milk'?
options: Yes; it says milky plants only
Yes; it says cow's milk only
Yes; it says milk is forbidden
No; the line leaves it open
optionExplain: The line does not decide this.
The line does not name any animal or milk source.
Nothing is forbidden; स- means with.
Right: The note: whether it means milky plants or together with milk is not decided by the line.
questions.explain: Both readings are kept open on the card.

questions.q: In which grammatical form is उपकल्पयेत्, according to the data?
optionExplain: Right: The gram label: 3 sg. opt. caus. upa-√kḷp: he should prepare.
A 3rd plural present would end in -न्ति.
An absolutive with a prefix would end in -य.
A past participle would end in -त; this ends in -येत्.
questions.explain: -येत् is the optative of a causative (-अय-) stem: he should prepare.

questions.q: Like सक्षीर (with milk), which word means with fruit?
optionExplain: अ- means 'without': fruitless.
Right: स- in front of a noun means 'with': स + क्षीर, स + फल.
वि- here means without: fruitless.
निस्- means 'without': fruitless.
questions.explain: Same pattern as सक्षीर.
questions.teaches: स- before a noun makes a bahuvrīhi 'having, with X': सक्षीर (with milk), सफल (with fruit).

questions.q: What does verse 23 call pippalī, viḍaṅga, jaggery, honey and ghee?
optionExplain: नव (fresh) is not the word of verse 23.
No taste is named in this list.
Right: पुराणानि तु = but old (ones).
Cooking is not named here.
questions.explain: पुराणानि तु पिप्पलीविडंगगुडमधुघृतानि.

questions.q: Match each item of verse 23 to its meaning.
questions.explain: The five items of the dvandva; pippalī and viḍaṅga are standard identifications.
questions.rule: पिप्पली = long pepper; विडङ्ग = Embelia ribes; गुड = jaggery; मधु = honey; घृत = ghee.

questions.q: Put the five old items of verse 23 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: पिप्पली-विडङ्ग-गुड-मधु-घृतानि.
questions.teaches: The old ones: pippalī, viḍaṅga, jaggery, honey, ghee, in that order.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT in the list of old things in verse 23?
optionExplain: मधु is the fourth item.
गुड is the third item.
घृत is the fifth item.
Right: सैन्धव is not named; the list is pippalī, viḍaṅga, jaggery, honey, ghee.
questions.explain: Five items: पिप्पली, विडङ्ग, गुड, मधु, घृत.
questions.rule: Old: पिप्पली · विडङ्ग · गुड · मधु · घृत.

questions.q: What does तु do at the start of the second line of verse 23?
options: It sets the old ones apart
optionExplain: Right: तु = but: the old ones are contrasted with what came before.
That is अपि च (unit 24), not तु.
Therefore is अतः, not तु.
That is इति, not तु.
questions.explain: पुराणानि तु: but old (ones).

questions.q: पुराणानि agrees with a neuter plural list. Which phrase rightly says old honey (मधु, neuter, one)?
optionExplain: -आनि is plural; मधु here is one thing.
Right: Neuter singular nominative: पुराणम् (पुराणं) agrees with मधु.
-अः is masculine; मधु is neuter.
-आ is feminine; मधु is neuter.
questions.explain: An adjective takes the gender, number and case of its noun.
questions.teaches: An adjective agrees with its noun in gender, number and case: पुराणानि …घृतानि (n. pl.), पुराणं मधु (n. sg.).

questions.q: What does unit 24 (अपि च) do?
options: It closes the topic of storage
It asks the reader a question
optionExplain: It adds more; it does not close.
No drug is named in these two particles.
Right: अपि च = and further; a further list follows.
अपि च is not a question.
questions.explain: The note: it introduces a further list (lines 05.08.28 and 29).

questions.q: What does अपि mean in unit 24?
optionExplain: That is तु.
That is अथ.
That is इति or एवम्.
Right: अपि = also, further.
questions.explain: अपि (also) + च (and) = and further.

questions.q: The particle meaning 'and' in अपि च is ____ (type it in Devanagari or in English letters, e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: च = and; अपि = also.
questions.teaches: In अपि च, च means 'and' and अपि means 'also'.

questions.q: Which two are true of unit 24?
options: it gives a measure of a drug
it leads into a further list
it is made of two particles
it names a season for gathering
optionExplain: No: no measure is given.
Right: the list of lines 05.08.28 and 29 follows.
Right: अपि and च.
No: no season is named.
questions.explain: अपि च: two particles that lead on.

questions.q: Which of these comes in the list that अपि च introduces?
optionExplain: Right: The next line begins क्षीरं … ग्राह्यं: milk is to be taken.
The vessel was named in unit 21, before अपि च.
Deep roots were named in unit 12.
Bark in autumn was named in unit 15.
questions.explain: After अपि च comes क्षीरं … ग्राह्यं (line 05.08.28).

questions.q: In a new sentence, रामः अपि गच्छति, what does अपि add?
optionExplain: Not would be न.
Right: अपि = also, as in अपि च (and further).
Again would be पुनर्.
Then would be अथ or ततः.
questions.explain: अपि marks 'also, even'.
questions.teaches: अपि means 'also, further': अपि च (and further), रामः अपि गच्छति (Rāma also goes).

questions.q: What is the first thing verse 25 says is to be taken?
optionExplain: Ghee was in verse 23's old list, not here.
Honey was in verse 23's old list.
Right: क्षीरं … ग्राह्यं = milk is to be taken.
Bark is a plant part, unit 15.
questions.explain: The verse opens: क्षीरं … ग्राह्यं.
questions.rule: क्षीर = milk; ग्राह्य = to be taken.

questions.q: Match each clear word of verse 25 to its meaning.
questions.explain: Milk is to be taken; disease-free; of those having age and strength.
questions.rule: क्षीरम् = milk; ग्राह्यम् = to be taken; नीरुजम् = disease-free; बल = strength.

questions.q: Put these clear words of verse 25 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Line 1: क्षीरं … ग्राह्यं … नीरुजं; line 2 opens वयोबलवतां.
questions.teaches: Verse 25: milk is to be taken ... disease-free; then, of those having age and strength ...

questions.q: Which is the right split of वयोबलवतां?
optionExplain: वलवताम् is not a word; the second member is बलवताम्, of those having strength.
उबलवताम् is not a word; ओ here comes from अः.
ओबलवताम् is not a word.
Right: अः before a voiced sound such as ब becomes ओ: वयः + बलवताम् = वयोबलवताम्.
questions.explain: वयस् (age) + बलवत् (strong): of those having age and strength.

questions.q: Does verse 25 name the animal whose milk, dung and urine are meant?
options: No; the animal is not named
optionExplain: Right: The note: the animal is not named in the line.
No animal name occurs in verse 25.
No animal name occurs in verse 25.
No animal name occurs in verse 25.
questions.explain: Only qualities are given (disease-free; age and strength); no animal is named.

questions.q: Like ग्राह्यम् (to be taken, from √ग्रह्), which word means to be done (√कृ)?
optionExplain: This is the past participle: done.
Right: The gerundive in -य says what is to be done: ग्राह्य, कार्य.
This is the absolutive: having done.
This is the present: he does.
questions.explain: ग्राह्य and कार्य are both gerundives (to be ...).
questions.teaches: The gerundive in -य states what is to be done: ग्राह्यम् (to be taken), कार्यम् (to be done).

questions.q: What does पञ्चविधः say about the kaṣāya of medicines in verse 26?
options: It is of one kind only
It has five drugs in it
optionExplain: पञ्च means five, not one.
विध is a kind, not a time of taking.
Right: पञ्च-विधः = having five (पञ्च) kinds (विध).
The five are kinds of preparation, not five drugs.
questions.explain: पञ्चविधः … कषायः: the preparation of medicines is fivefold.

questions.q: Match each form named in verse 26 to its meaning on the card.
questions.explain: Niryāsa is defined as svarasa in line 05.08.33; śīta and phāṇṭa are defined in lines 05.08.42 and 05.08.43.
questions.rule: निर्यास = juice; कल्क = paste; शीत = cold; फाण्ट = hot.

questions.q: Put the words of the first line of verse 26 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: पञ्चविधस्तु भेषजानां कषायः कल्प्यः: fivefold, of medicines, the kaṣāya, is to be prepared.
questions.teaches: Verse 26 opens: the kaṣāya of medicines is to be prepared (कल्प्यः) in five kinds (पञ्चविधः).

questions.q: Which is the right split of फांटश्च in verse 26?
optionExplain: श्च is not a word; the श् comes from the visarga.
That would print फाण्टं च; the form is m. nom. sg. फाण्टः.
A plural would print फाण्टाश्च, with आ.
Right: A visarga before च becomes श्: फाण्टः + च = फाण्टश्च.
questions.explain: फाण्टः (hot infusion) + च (and).

questions.q: A physician presses the fresh juice out of a herb. Which of the five forms of verse 26 has he made?
optionExplain: Right: The card: niryāsa is the svarasa, the herb's own expressed juice (line 05.08.33).
Kalka is a paste ground with a stone or the teeth, not pressed juice.
Phāṇṭa is made in hot water, not by pressing juice out.
Śīta is soaked in cold water overnight, not pressed out.
questions.explain: Pressed juice = niryāsa (svarasa).

questions.q: Join a new pair the same way as फाण्टः + च: रसः + च (and the juice). Which is right?
optionExplain: ओ comes before a voiced sound; च is unvoiced.
Right: A visarga before च becomes श्, as in फाण्टः + च = फाण्टश्च.
स् comes before त / थ; before च the visarga becomes श्.
च्च comes from a final त्, as in -आत् + च; here there is a visarga.
questions.explain: Same rule as फाण्टश्च.
questions.teaches: A visarga before च becomes श्: फाण्टः + च = फाण्टश्च; रसः + च = रसश्च.

questions.q: In unit 27, what does बलिनः mean?
optionExplain: Weak would be दुर्बल or अबल; बलिन् has strength.
Bitter is a taste (तिक्त), not बलिन्.
Right: बलिनः = strong (m. nom. pl. of बलिन्, from बल, strength).
Nothing in बलिन् means ready.
questions.explain: बलिनः = strong ones.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 27 to its meaning.
pairs: in the order of the preceding
questions.explain: ते यथापूर्वं बलिनः: they are strong in the order of precedence.
questions.rule: ते = they; यथापूर्वम् = by precedence; बलिनः = strong.

questions.q: Put the words of unit 27 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: ते यथापूर्वं बलिनः.
questions.teaches: Unit 27 runs: they (the five forms), in the order of the preceding, are strong.

questions.q: To what does ते refer in unit 27, by the card?
options: The physicians who prepare the forms
The herbs gathered in each season
The pots of copper, iron and clay
The five forms named in line 05.08.31
optionExplain: No person is named; बलिनः describes the five forms.
The gathering lines come earlier; ते takes up the five forms.
The pots come later, in line 05.08.38.
Right: The note: 'te' refers to the five forms of line 05.08.31.
questions.explain: ते = niryāsa, kalka, niryūha, śīta, phāṇṭa.
questions.rule: ते takes up the list just given.

questions.q: On the usual sense the card gives for यथापूर्वम्, which of these two is the stronger: kalka or phāṇṭa?
options: Kalka, as it stands earlier in the list
Phāṇṭa, as it stands later in the list
Both are equal, as the line says
Neither, as both are weak forms
optionExplain: Right: Kalka is second in the list, phāṇṭa fifth; the earlier is taken as stronger.
On the usual sense the earlier, not the later, is stronger.
The line ranks them by precedence; it does not make them equal.
बलिनः calls the forms strong, in order.
questions.explain: यथापूर्वम्: niryāsa, kalka, niryūha, śīta, phāṇṭa, from stronger to less strong (usual sense).
questions.rule: Earlier in the list = stronger (usual sense).

questions.q: बलिनः is the m. nom. plural of बलिन् (strong). Which form says of one form: it is strong?
optionExplain: बलिनः is plural (or gen./abl. sg.), not nom. sg.
Right: The m. nom. singular of an -इन् stem ends in -ई: बलिन् → बली.
बलिना is the instrumental singular, 'by the strong one'.
बलिनम् is the accusative singular.
questions.explain: बलिन्: nom. sg. बली, nom. pl. बलिनः.
questions.teaches: An -इन् stem like बलिन् (strong) has nom. sg. बली and nom. pl. बलिनः (as in ते बलिनः).

questions.q: What is niryāsa, by unit 28?
options: The gum oozing from a tree
A paste ground on a stone
The own juice of a fresh herb
optionExplain: The card: in this chapter niryāsa is the juice, not gum.
That is kalka, unit 29.
Right: स्वरसो निर्यासः: the svarasa (own juice) is niryāsa.
That is the powder of unit 30.
questions.explain: निर्यास = स्वरस, expressed juice.

questions.q: Match each step word of unit 28 to its meaning.
questions.explain: समुद्धृत-प्रक्षालित-क्षुण्णस्य तान्तव-निष्पीडितस्य: pulled up, washed, crushed, pressed out through a cloth.

questions.q: Put the steps of making niryāsa in the order of unit 28.
questions.explain: सद्यः समुद्धृत → प्रक्षालित → क्षुण्ण → तान्तवनिष्पीडित → स्वरसो निर्यासः.
questions.rule: Pull up · wash · crush · press through cloth · juice.
questions.teaches: Niryāsa: the herb is freshly pulled up, washed, crushed and pressed out through a cloth; its own juice is niryāsa.

questions.q: Which is the right split of स्वरसो निर्यासः?
optionExplain: That would print स्वरसं निर्यासः.
A dual in -औ would stay स्वरसौ in print.
सो is not a word here; स्वरस is one word.
Right: अः before a voiced sound such as न becomes ओ: स्वरसः + निर्यासः = स्वरसो निर्यासः.
questions.explain: स्वरसः (own juice) + निर्यासः.

questions.q: Unit 28 calls the juice ____ (own juice) niryāsa. Type it in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: स्वरसो निर्यासः: the svarasa is niryāsa.
questions.teaches: Niryāsa in this chapter is the svarasa, the herb's own juice pressed through a cloth.

questions.q: Join a new pair by the rule of स्वरसो निर्यासः: कल्कः + भवति (it is a paste). Which is right?
optionExplain: Right: अः before a voiced sound (भ) becomes ओ, as in स्वरसो निर्यासः.
स् comes before त / थ, not before भ.
र् comes after a vowel other than अ / आ; here it is अः.
The visarga drops before a vowel other than अ, not before भ.
questions.explain: Same rule as स्वरसो.
questions.teaches: अः before a voiced consonant becomes ओ: स्वरसः + निर्यासः = स्वरसो निर्यासः; कल्कः + भवति = कल्को भवति.

questions.q: With what is kalka ground, by unit 29?
options: Through a fine cloth and then a sieve
With a stone, the teeth and so on
With a ladle on a gentle fire
In hot water, and then strained
optionExplain: Cloth comes in units 28 and 30, not in the kalka line.
Right: उपल-दशन-आदि-पिष्टः: ground with stone (उपल), teeth (दशन) and so on.
The ladle and fire belong to the decoction, unit 34.
Hot water belongs to phāṇṭa, unit 37.
questions.explain: उपल = stone; दशन = tooth; पिष्ट = ground.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 29 to its meaning.
questions.explain: उपलदशनादिपिष्टस्तु कल्कः: (that) ground with stone, teeth and so on is kalka.
questions.rule: उपल = stone; दशन = tooth; पिष्ट = ground; कल्क = paste.

questions.q: Put the members of उपलदशनादिपिष्टः in the order of the text.
questions.explain: उपल-दशन-आदि-पिष्टः: stone, teeth, and so on, ground.
questions.teaches: The compound उपल-दशन-आदि-पिष्टः means 'ground with stone, teeth and so on'; ground = पिष्ट.

questions.q: Which is the right split of पिष्टस्तु?
optionExplain: स्तु is not a word; the स् comes from the visarga.
That would print पिष्टं तु.
Right: A visarga before त becomes स्: पिष्टः + तु = पिष्टस्तु.
A plural would print पिष्टास्तु, with आ.
questions.explain: पिष्टः (ground) + तु (but).

questions.q: A medicine is ground on a grinding stone into a mass. Which form of unit 29 is that?
optionExplain: Niryāsa is juice pressed out through a cloth, unit 28.
Niryūha is the decoction cooked in water, unit 32.
Śīta is soaked in cold water overnight, unit 37.
Right: Ground with a stone (उपल) and so on = kalka.
questions.explain: Ground on stone = kalka.

questions.q: Join by the rule of पिष्टस्तु: स्वरसः + तत्र (the juice, there). Which is right?
optionExplain: Right: A visarga before त becomes स्, as in पिष्टः + तु = पिष्टस्तु.
ओ comes before a voiced sound; त is unvoiced.
श् comes before च / छ, not before त.
त्त would come from a final त्; here there is a visarga.
questions.explain: Same rule as पिष्टस्तु.
questions.teaches: A visarga before त becomes स्: पिष्टः + तु = पिष्टस्तु; स्वरसः + तत्र = स्वरसस्तत्र.

questions.q: What does चूर्ण mean in unit 30?
optionExplain: Juice is रस / स्वरस, unit 28.
Right: चूर्णः = powder (cūrṇa).
Paste is कल्क, unit 29.
No oil is named in unit 30.
questions.explain: चूर्ण = powder.

questions.q: Match each member of सूक्ष्मतान्तवच्युतचूर्णः to its meaning.
questions.explain: A powder fallen through a fine cloth.
questions.rule: सूक्ष्म = fine; तान्तव = cloth; च्युत = fallen; चूर्ण = powder.

questions.q: Put the members of the compound of unit 30 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: सूक्ष्म-तान्तव-च्युत-चूर्णः.
questions.teaches: Unit 30 is one compound: fine (सूक्ष्म) cloth (तान्तव) fallen-through (च्युत) powder (चूर्ण).

questions.q: तान्तव also occurs in unit 28. What passes through the cloth there, and what in unit 30?
options: Powder in unit 28, juice in unit 30
Water in unit 28, juice in unit 30
Juice in unit 28, powder in unit 30
Paste in both of the two units
optionExplain: The other way round: juice is pressed in 28, powder sifted in 30.
Unit 28 presses the herb's own juice, and 30 gives a powder.
Right: Unit 28: तान्तवनिष्पीडित, juice pressed through cloth; unit 30: तान्तवच्युत, powder fallen through cloth.
Paste (कल्क) is ground with stone, unit 29; no cloth.
questions.explain: तान्तव = cloth: juice pressed through (28), powder fallen through (30).

questions.q: A dried herb is pounded and shaken through a fine cloth. Which word of unit 30 names what falls through?
optionExplain: स्वरस is the pressed juice of unit 28.
कल्क is the ground paste of unit 29.
क्वाथ is the decoction of unit 32.
Right: The thing fallen (च्युत) through the fine cloth is the powder (चूर्ण).
questions.explain: What falls through fine cloth = चूर्ण.

questions.q: Read a new phrase built like unit 30: सूक्ष्मतान्तवच्युतं जलम्. What does it mean?
options: Water that has fallen through a fine cloth
Water that is poured out over a fine cloth
A fine cloth that has fallen into water
Water in which fine powder has fallen
optionExplain: Right: The same compound pattern: fine-cloth-fallen-through, now describing water (जलम्).
च्युत is 'fallen through', not 'poured over'.
जलम् is the noun described; the cloth is the means.
No powder is named; च्युत describes the water.
questions.explain: सूक्ष्म-तान्तव-च्युत + noun = (noun) fallen through a fine cloth.
questions.rule: The last member names the thing; the first members describe it.
questions.teaches: In a descriptive compound the earlier members qualify what follows: सूक्ष्मतान्तवच्युत = fallen through a fine cloth.

questions.q: What does unit 31 conclude about तस्य (of that, probably the powder) and kalka?
options: It is not different from kalka
It is made from kalka by drying
optionExplain: Strength is the topic of unit 27, not of this line.
Right: कल्कात् + अभेदः = non-difference from kalka.
The line says the opposite: no difference.
The line gives no making of powder from kalka.
questions.explain: कल्कादभेदः: no difference from kalka.

questions.q: Match each word of unit 31 to its meaning.
questions.explain: तस्य … आशुतोपयोगाच्च कल्कादभेदः: of that, because of quick use, no difference from kalka.
questions.rule: तस्य = of that; आशुता = quickness; उपयोग = use; अभेद = non-difference.

questions.q: Put these words of unit 31 in the order of the text.
questions.explain: तस्य … आशुतोपयोगाच्च कल्कादभेदः: of that … and because of quick use, no difference from kalka.
questions.teaches: Unit 31 opens with तस्य (of that), gives its reasons in the ablative (one is quick use, आशुतोपयोगात्) and ends: no difference from kalka.

questions.q: Which is the right split of the printed कल्कादभेदः?
optionExplain: That would print कल्काद्भेदः, with no vowel after द्; it would also mean 'difference'.
दभेद is not a word; कल्कात् is the ablative 'from kalka'.
Right: त् before a vowel becomes द्; the अ after द is the अ of अभेदः: non-difference.
अः + अ gives कल्कोऽभेदः, not कल्कादभेदः.
questions.explain: कल्कात् (from kalka) + अभेदः (non-difference).
questions.rule: Final त् before a vowel → द्.

questions.q: Which reason does unit 31 give for तस्य (of that, probably the powder) being no different from kalka?
options: It is pressed out through a cloth
It is boiled with milk and the like first
It is kept overnight in cold water
It is put to use quickly
optionExplain: Pressing through cloth makes the juice of unit 28.
Milk comes in the decoction line 05.08.41.
Overnight soaking makes śīta, line 05.08.42.
Right: आशुता-उपयोगात्: because of quickness (आशुता) of use (उपयोग).
questions.explain: One stated reason: quick use (आशुता-उपयोगात्).
